body.text: śrīmadarcaṭaviracitā
body.translated_text: Composed by the illustrious <s>Arcaṭa</s>

body.text: || hetubinduṭīkā ||
body.translated_text: || <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> (Commentary on the Drop of Reason) ||

body.text: || namaḥ sarvajñāya ||
body.translated_text: || Homage to the Omniscient One ||

body.text: jinamanaskāreṇa maṅgalam |
body.translated_text: Auspicious invocation through salutation to the <s>Jina</s> (Victor).

children.text: yaḥ sañjātamahākṛpo vyasaninaṃ trātuṃ samagraṃ janam,
children.translated_text: He who, having arisen with great compassion to save all people who are afflicted,
having accumulated the vast cause consisting of merit and knowledge, with fatigue dispelled,
having resorted to the mountain of the arising of [the most pure wisdom] that pervades all objects of knowledge,
the sun among <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) who dispels the darkness of delusion in the world — him I salute with bowed head. || 1 ||

body.text: dharmakīrtivacasāṃ sarasatamatvakhyāpanam |
body.translated_text: Declaring the supreme eloquence of the words of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>.

children.translated_text: Indeed, it is excellent to chew again what has already been chewed among the works of <s>Dharmakīrti</s>;

children.text: niṣpīḍitāpi mṛdvī[kā nanu svādaṃ jahā]ti kim? || 2 ||
children.translated_text: does a grape, even when squeezed dry, [forsake its] flavor? || 2 ||

body.text: svalāghavaṃ prakhyāpya granthavivaraṇapratijñā |
body.translated_text: Having declared his own inadequacy, the promise to explain the treatise.

children.translated_text: Where one whose intellect weighs the whole world on the scale of the path of reasoning could prevail, where are his profound words, and where am I with my dull mind? || 3 ||

children.text: jayet tasya kva gambhīrā giro 'haṃ jaḍadhīḥ kva ca? || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, there are some who are even duller in understanding than I;
[for their sake], this <s>Hetubindu</s> (Drop of Reason) is analyzed by me as well. || 4 ||
[Explaining the purpose of the opening statement.]

body.text: ādivākyasya prayojanaprakaṭanam |
body.translated_text:
With "<s>parokṣe</s>" (regarding what is imperceptible) and so forth, he states the purpose at the commencement of the treatise.
Some say that this is for the sake of prompting the engagement of the audience.

body.text:
"parokṣe"- tyādinā prakaraṇārambhe prayojanamāha |
tacca śrotṛjanapravṛttyartham iti kecit |
body.translated_text: As it has been said—

body.text: taduktam[m-
body.translated_text: "Until the purpose of any [treatise] whatsoever or of any action

children.translated_text: has been stated, why should anyone undertake it?"

children.text: yāvat prayojanaṃ noktaṃ tāvat tat kena gṛhyatām ||"
children.translated_text: This is not correct. Because, when one demonstrates that 'this is the purpose of this treatise,' [one must first] ascertain the treatise's instrumentality toward that particular purpose, and since engagement is impossible without such means,

body.text: iti | tadayuktam | yato 'sya prakaraṇasyedaṃ prayojanamiti [pradarśane prayo]janaviśeṣaṃ prati upāyatāṃ prakaraṇasya niścityānupāye pravṛttyasambhavāt (

children.translated_text: it is argued that the statement of purpose is meaningful because discerning persons, desiring that goal, [would then engage in hearing the treatise] and so forth. But this is not correct. For the engagement of discerning persons who desire a purpose occurs through their ascertainment of the existence of that means toward that purpose — just as farmers and others [ascertain] the existence of seeds and such as means to crops, having determined the nature of seeds and such by distinguishing them from non-seeds. Otherwise, for those desiring a goal but uncertain of the means, their status as discerning persons would be compromised in their engagement. But regarding the goal, since the operation of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is impossible, even without certainty, those who have discerned the means, when there is no impossibility of the causal connection and qualification, think 'this is capable of producing the desired result' — [and through such engagement based on] estimation, their status as discerning persons would not be compromised.

children.text: ) prekṣāvatāṃ tadarthitayā pra[karaṇaśravaṇādau pravṛttiḥ] syāditi tadabhidhānasyārthavattā varṇyate | na caitad yuktam | yataḥ prekṣāvatāṃ pravṛttiḥ prayojanārthināṃ tadupāye tadbhāvaniścayāt | yathā kṛṣīva[lādīnāṃ sasyā]dyupāye bījādāvabījādivivekenāvadhṛtabījādibhāvānām | anyathā hyaniścitopāyānāmupeyārthināṃ pravṛttau prekṣāvattaiva hīyeta | upeye tu [pramā]ṇavyāpārāsambhavādaniścaye 'pi vivecitopāyāḥ pratibandhavaikalyayorasambhave ‘yogyametadvivakṣitaṃ kāryaṃ niṣpādayitum'; iti saṃ[bhāvanayā pravṛttau] prekṣāvattāto na hīyeran |
children.translated_text: And certainty comes only from <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition). But the statement of purpose has no validity as a <s>pramāṇa</s>, because verbal testimonies have no causal connection with external objects. Even [granting its validity] regarding the speaker's intention, since there is no invariable conformity with how things actually are, there is no certainty from that about the treatise's instrumentality toward a particular purpose. For those who express a certain thing with a certain intention about a certain object do not necessarily act in accordance with that — because in the world, since those with the intention to deceive are seen to state one thing and do another, there is universal distrust everywhere.

body.translated_text: Hbṭ 2

body.text: niścayaśca pramāṇādeva | na ca prayojanavākyasya prāmāṇyamasti, śābdānāṃ bahirarthe pratibandhābhāvāt | vivakṣāyāṃ [tasya prāmāṇye 'pi yathā] vastupravṛttiniyamābhāvāt na tataḥ prakaraṇasya prayojanavise(śe)ṣaṃ prati upāyatāniścayaḥ samasti | na hi ye yathā yamarthaṃ vivakṣanti te tathaiva tamanu[tiṣṭhanti vi]saṃvādanābhiprāyāṇāmanyathābhidhāyānyathāpravṛttidarśanālloke sarvatrānāśvāsāt |
body.translated_text: If it be said that the presentation of a particular purpose generates [doubt] regarding the treatise's instrumentality toward that purpose, and therefore engagement to ascertain that is appropriate, just as a farmer's engagement to ascertain seeds and such — no, because the doubt about the treatise's instrumentality toward a particular purpose exists even [before] that statement. In the absence of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) that would establish or refute it, such doubt is logically inevitable. And since treatises aimed at training in inference and such are observed, doubt of the form 'Is this treatise's purpose the training in <s>anumāna</s> (inference), or something else, or nothing at all?' — such doubt, arising prior to the statement, cannot be prevented by anyone. Moreover, when engagement is possible for one who wishes to know 'Is this purposeless, or purposeful, [or purposeful with] the purpose we maintain?' — the presentation of a statement of purpose is entirely superfluous.

body.text: prayojanaviśeṣopanyāsāt prakaraṇasya tadupāyatā[viṣaye saṃśayaḥ ja]nyate tatastadbhāvanirdhāraṇāya kṛṣīvalāderiva bījādyavadhṛtaye pravṛttiryukteti cet; na, prayojanaviśeṣopāyatāsaṃśayasya tadabhidhā[nāt prāgapi] bhāvāt | tatsādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāve tasya nyāyaprāptatvāt | anumānādivyutpattyarthānāṃ ca prakaraṇānāṃ darśanāt kimasyānumā[navyutpādanaṃ pra]yojanamanyaddhā, na vā kiñcidapītyevaṃrūpaśca saṃśayaḥ prāk pravartamānaḥ kena nivāryeta | api ca kimidaṃ niṣprayojanam, uta prayojana[vat, athāsmadabhima]tena vā prayojanena tadvaditi jijñāsoḥ pravṛttisambhave vyartha eva prayojanavākyopanyāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, 'a statement that lacks purpose, or its subject matter, is not undertaken by a discerning person to perform or to communicate — just as the statement about ten pomegranates, or the

body.text: tasmād ‘yat prayojanarahitaṃ vākyam, tadartho vā, na tat prekṣāvatārabhyate kartuṃ pratipādayituṃ vā | tadyathā (

children.translated_text: examination of a crow's teeth. [And if this] treatise or its subject matter is purposeless' — for one who objects through <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader), the presentation of the statement of purpose at the beginning is for the sake of refuting that unestablished charge.

children.text: ) daśadāḍimādivākyaṃ kākadanta[parīkṣā ca | niṣprayojanaṃ cedaṃ] prakaraṇaṃ tadartho vā'; iti vyāpakānupalabdhyā pratyavatiṣṭhamānasya tadasiddhatodbhāvanārthamādau prayojanavākyopanyāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Consideration of the purpose of both the treatise and its subject matter.]

body.translated_text: Hbṭ 3

body.text: prakaraṇatadabhidheyayoḥ prayojanacintā |
body.translated_text: There, by the statement "for the sake of generating that," he himself states the purpose of this treatise. For the purpose of a statement is the cognition of its respective subject matter. And that exists here, because from the mutual connection of words and subsidiary sentences, the composite meaning is understood. Thus: <s>anumāna</s> (inference) is what is expounded in this treatise, and that is the subject matter — due to the connection of the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>) with inference itself. Although <s>anumāna</s> (inference) is [subsidiary]

in the apprehension of imperceptible objects, nevertheless, because linguistic usage follows the speaker's intention, it is referred to by the word 'that.' Otherwise, how could there be any connection with the principal subject? Because words have no natural connection [with objects]. And through "<s>pakṣadharma</s>" (property of the thesis-subject) and so forth, it is indeed inference that is being expounded. Its <s>vyutpatti</s> (correct understanding) — the cognition of its [undistorted true] nature — is the purpose of this treatise, because that is what is to be accomplished. And precisely for this reason, to indicate the treatise's function as directed toward training in inference, he uses the causative form: "for the purpose of generating that (<s>tadvyutpādanārtham</s>)." And thus the relationship between the treatise and its purpose, characterized as means and end, is also stated. Although by linguistic usage the treatise's function directed toward [training in inference] has primacy, nevertheless in reality it is the <s>vyutpatti</s> (understanding) itself that has primacy, because that is what is to be accomplished. And the other is secondary because it serves as a means to that. Therefore, it is the <s>vyutpatti</s> (correct understanding) of inference alone that is apprehended as the purpose, not the treatise's function.

body.text: tatra "tadyutpādanārtham" iti vākyena svayamasya prakaraṇasya prayojanamāha | yathāsvamabhidheyapratītirhi vākyasya prayojanam | taccehāsti padānāmavāntaravākyānāṃ ca parasparasaṃsargāt samāsārthapratīteḥ | tathā hi- anumānamatra prakaraṇe vyutpādyata iti tad abhidheyam | tasyaiva tacchabdena sambandhāt | yadyapi parokṣārthapratipattau gu[ṇabhūtamanu]mānaṃ tathāpi vakturabhiprāyānuvidhāyitayā śabdavṛtteḥ tacchabdena parāmṛśyate | anyathā pradhānasaṃsparso(rśo)pi kathaṃ syāt? | śabdānāṃ sva[bhāvataḥ] sambaddhā(ndhā)yogāt | "pakṣadharma" ityādinā cānumānasyaiva vyutpādanāt | tasya vyutpatti [raviparītasvarū]papratītirasya prakaraṇasya prayojanam, tatsādhyatvāt | ata eva cānumānavyutpattiviṣayaṃ prakaraṇa[vyāpāraṃ pratipāda]yituṃ ṇicā nirdiśati- "tadvayutpādanārtham" iti | tataśca prakaraṇaprayojanayoḥ sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇaḥ sambandho 'pyukto bhavati | yadyapi śabdavṛttenā[numānavyutpattivi]ṣayasya prakaraṇavyāpārasya prādhānyaṃ tathāpi vastuvṛttena vyutpattereva pradhānatā tasyāstatsādhyatvāt | itarasya ca tadupāyatvenāpradhānatvāt | tasmādanumānavyutpatti reva prayojanatayā pratīyate na prakaraṇavyāpāra iti |
body.translated_text: By "because apprehension of imperceptible objects [depends on inference]," he states the purpose of the treatise's subject matter, namely the definition of <s>anumāna</s> (inference). For a discerning person does not engage merely because a statement has the result of conveying its own meaning, but rather when the subject matter treated therein is useful for human goals. And that exists here, because the apprehension — the ascertainment — of what is imperceptible, for that, <s>anumāna</s> (inference) — the <s>trirūpaliṅga</s> (triple-characterized logical mark) — is the cause, through the figurative transfer of the effect-term to the cause. To show that it is achievable by no other means, and to refute opposing doctrines,

body.text: "parokṣārthaprati[patteḥ amumānāśraya]tvāt" ityanena tu prakaraṇārthasyānumānalakṣaṇasya prayojanamāha | na hi vākyasya svārthapratītilakṣaṇaṃ phalamastītyetā[vataiva prekṣāvān prava]rtate 'pi tu tadabhidheyārthasya puruṣārthopayogitve sati | taccehāsti yataḥ parokṣārthasya yā pratipattiḥ- niścayaḥ- tasyā anumā[naṃ- trirūpaliṅgam] kāraṇe kāryopacārāt | ananyopāyasādhyatāṃ darśayituṃ paramatanirāsārtham (

children.translated_text: it is the foundation — the cause — parsing it generally as 'that whose foundation is inference.' [Then,] when the specific question arises 'of what is inference the foundation?' — although the feminine gender is understood from the grammatical connection with the word <s>parokṣārthapratipattiḥ</s> (apprehension of imperceptible objects), nevertheless, since that was not present in the mind at the time of word-formation, it is extrinsic and does not trigger the feminine suffix — just as in 'this woman is a <s>brāhmaṇī</s>' or 'this handful is for sowing.'

children.text: ) āśrayaḥ- kāraṇam, anumānamāśrayo yasyeti sāmānyena vigṛhya | [tadanu ca] kasyānumānāśrayatvāditi viśeṣāpekṣāyām-yadyapi parokṣārthapratipattiśabdasambandhe strītvaṃ gamyate tathāpi tat padasaṃskāravelāyāṃ buddhyasaṃnihitatvāt bahiraṅgamiti na strīpratyayanimittaṃ yathā bhūtamiyaṃ brāhmaṇī, āvapanamiyamuṣṭriketi |
children.translated_text: [Indicating that all imperceptible cognition is inferential precisely because it arises from logical marks.]

body.translated_text: Hbṭ 4

body.text: sarvaparokṣapratīterliṅgajatvādevānumānatvasūcanam |
body.translated_text: And by this it is stated that all valid apprehension of imperceptible objects, since apprehension thereof is impossible from anything else, depends solely on the <s>trirūpaliṅga</s> (triple-characterized logical mark) — because of the restrictive particle 'eva' in 'precisely because of dependence on inference.' [Therefore,]

for verbal testimony and other means of cognition, if they are valid, they must be inferential in nature; otherwise the absurd consequence would follow that they too need to be expounded here, since the reason would be the same.

body.text: anena ca sarvā parokṣā[rtha]pratipattiḥ pramāṇabhūtā, anyasmāt tatpratipattyayogāt, trirūpaliṅgāśrayaivetyuktaṃ bhavati anumānāśrayatvādeveti avadhāraṇāt | [tataśca śabdādī]nāṃ sati prāmāṇye 'numānatā, anyathā teṣāmapi vyutpādyatāprasaṅgo nimittasya samānatvāt |
body.translated_text: Thus: all valid apprehension of imperceptible objects is not independent — because, having no causal connection with its object, it cannot invariably correspond with it, and because <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is defined by non-deceptiveness. Even if cognition could arise from something else, since there would be the absurd consequence of cognition of everything from everything — it would generate cognition everywhere even without connection to the property-possessor — because there would be no difference of proximity or remoteness. And such a thing can only be the <s>trirūpaliṅga</s> (triple-characterized logical mark). Therefore all apprehension of imperceptible objects, being born from the triple-characterized mark, does not differ from <s>anumāna</s> (inference). And this meaning is shown through the connection with the context: "a <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject) pervaded by that portion is the <s>hetu</s> (logical reason)" — of what? — of the apprehension of imperceptible objects — because the restrictive sense establishes that only a <s>pakṣadharma</s> that is pervaded by that portion is the <s>hetu</s> (reason) for apprehending imperceptible objects.

body.text: tathā hi- sarvā parokṣārthapratipattiḥ pra[māṇabhūtā], na svatantrā bhavati | tasyāḥ svārthapratibandhābhāvena niyamena tatsaṃvādāyogāt | avisaṃvādalakṣaṇatvācca pramāṇasya | anyato 'pi [yadi syā]t sarvataḥ sarvapratipattiprasaṅgāt dharmyasambandhe 'pi sarvatra pratītiṃ janayet, pratyāsattiviprakarṣābhāvāt | evambhūtaśca trirūpa[liṅgamevārtho bhava]tīti sarvā parokṣārthapratipattistrirūpaliṅgajatvenānumānāt na bhidyata iti | eṣa cārthaḥ "pakṣadharmastadaṃśena vyāpto hetuḥ", kasya?, parokṣā[rthapratipatte]riti prakṛtena saṃbandhād darśitaḥ, pakṣadharma eva tadaṃśena vyāpta eva ca parokṣārthapratipatterheturityavadhāraṇāt |
body.translated_text: [Establishing that only <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) is real, not <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal)]

body.text: svalakṣaṇasyaiva vastutvaṃ na sāmānyasyeti sthāpanam
body.translated_text: The word 'artha' (object) in 'apprehension of imperceptible objects' is used to show that even the validity of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) pertains to <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular). For 'artha' (object) is that which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>), and it is <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) alone that has such a nature. For this very reason he will say: "because the establishment of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) is grounded in real entities (<s>vastu</s>)." Otherwise, one who seeks causal efficacy would not engage on the basis of inference toward that object.

body.text: arthagrahaṇaṃ tu parokṣārthapratipatteritya[numā]nasyāpi svalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ prāmāṇyaṃ darśayitum | arthakriyāsamartho hyarthaḥ, svalakṣaṇaṃ caivamātmakam | ata eva- "vastvadhiṣṭhānatvāt pramāṇavyavasthāyāḥ"- [iti va]kṣyati | anyathānumānāt tatra pravṛttirna syādarthakriyārthinaḥ |
body.translated_text: Even though <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) is not a real entity, since that causal efficacy consists merely in cognition, and since that cognition is established as produced by it — for a <s>jāti</s> (universal) is not employed in burning, cooking, and such; only <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) is useful there. If it be said that engagement toward that occurs due to its connection with the particular — no, because something permanent, being incapable of contributing anything, has no connection with anything. And even granting a connection, how can there be engagement toward one thing based on the cognition of another? — due to the absurd consequence of overextension. If it be said that engagement toward that occurs through error, due to the conviction of one who has not discerned the subtlety of <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — then let there be mere error alone; what need is there for <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) as a hidden presupposition? If it be said that error cannot arise without a basis — those very particulars, [producing a common effect], are the basis of the error. For the cognition of a universal has the form of similarity in color and shape. But <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) does not have that form — so how can it be the basis of error? For error is accepted by others as grounded in similarity. And it is the particulars themselves, [distinguished from those of dissimilar] classes, that constitute the nature of the cognition appearing as a universal — therefore they alone are the basis of error, because the exclusion from what is not of that form exists in them. But for a real <s>sāmānya</s> (universal), since connection [with particulars] is impossible, its presence in them is untenable.

body.text: sāmānyasyāvastutve 'pi jñānamātralakṣaṇatvāt tadarthakriyāyāḥ tasyāśca tadu[tpādya]tvena siddhatvāt | na hi jātirdāhapākādāvupayujyate, svalakṣaṇasyaiva tatropayogāt | tatsambandhāt tatra pravṛttiriti cet; na, nityasyānupakāra[katvena] kenacitsambandhābhāvāt | satyapi ca sambandhe kathamanyapratipattāvanyatra pravṛttiḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | samavāyasya sūkṣmatvenānavasitavivekasyāvasāyād bhrāntyā tatra pravṛttiriti cet; evaṃ tarhi bhrāntimātramevāstu, kimantargaḍunā sāmānyena? | nirbbījabhrāntyayogāditi cet; tā eva vyaktayastadekakā[ryakāriṇyo bhrānterbījam] | varṇākṛtisamānākāraṃ hi sāmānyajñānam | na ca sāmānyaṃ tadrūpam, tat kathaṃ tad bhrānterbbījam | sādṛśyanibandhanā hi bhrāntiriṣyate paraiḥ | vyaktaya eva cā[samānajā]tīyavyāvṛttāḥ sāmānyākārajñānasvarūpāstatastā eva bhrāntibījam, atadrūpavyāvṛttestāsu bhāvāt | vastubhūtasya tu sāmānyasya sambandha[āsaṃbhave]na tāsu bhāvāyogācca |
body.translated_text: Those who conceive <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) as identical with the particulars have thereby already accepted that the validity of <s>anumāna</s> (inference) pertains to <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular). But it must be considered how a <s>sāmānya</s> (universal) that is identical with <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (the particular) appears in inference. And no form of <s>sāmānya</s> (the universal) other than the form of the particulars is accepted, for that would lead to the absurd consequence of adopting the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> position. ...

body.text: yaistu vyaktyātmakameva sāmānyaṃ kalpitaṃ taiḥ svalakṣaṇaviṣayamanumānasya prāmāṇyamabhyupagatameva bhavati | svalakṣaṇātmakaṃ tu sāmānyaṃ kathamanumāne pratibhāsate iti cintyam | na ca vyaktirūpamapāsyāparaṃ sāmānyasya rūpamiṣyate, vaiśeṣikadarśanopagamaprasaṅgāt | ...........................................................................................................
body.translated_text: [1. General examination of <s>hetu</s> (the logical reason).]

body.text: 1. hetoḥ sāmānyanirūpaṇam |
body.translated_text: 1. Discussion of how the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is pervaded by the three characteristics.

body.text: 1. hetostritvena vyāptiḥ kathaṃ phaliteti carcā |
body.translated_text: ...has been stated. There, since <s>kārya</s> (effect) and <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature) function as provers of positive assertion, they have no role when negation is to be proved. From <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) too, there is no ascertainment of the absence of other reasons, because it is established in four forms: non-apprehension of <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), of <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause), of <s>vyāpaka</s> (the pervader), and the positive cognition of what is contradictory. Non-apprehension of <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature) — which is the cognition of something else that shares equal eligibility and is associated with a single cognition — is accepted as the basis for the convention of absence. And no other reason is posited as absolutely non-existent in the manner described; for if it existed, its negation would apply only to a particular place, time, etc., not as absolute non-existence. The non-apprehension of <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause) and <s>vyāpaka</s> (the pervader) occur when the relationship of effect-cause and pervaded-pervader is established. But when the absolute non-existence of another reason is accepted, this mode is not possible — so how will they establish its absence? Contradiction too is understood from the absence of something whose complete cause is present when the other thing exists — thus the apprehension of what is contradictory is also impossible. Or, if it were possible, how could the non-apprehension of cause and such establish absolute negation? Anticipating this objection, he says: "<s>hetvābhāsāḥ</s> (pseudo-reasons) are other than those." "Other than those" — other than the threefold <s>hetu</s> (reason) — are the "<s>hetvābhāsāḥ</s> (pseudo-reasons)" — because the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is precisely threefold.

body.text: .............hi kathitam | tatra kāryasvabhāvayorvidhisādhanatvānna pratiṣedhe sādhye vyāpāraḥ | anupalabdhito 'pi na hetvantarābhāvaniścayo yataḥ sā caturddhāvasthitā svabhāva[kāraṇa]vyāpakānupalabdhayo viruddha vidhiśceti | tulyayogyatārūpasyaikajñānasaṃsargiṇaḥ svabhāvānupalabdhiranyopalabdhirūpā abhāvavyavahāraheturiṣyate | na [ca hetvan]taramatyantābhāvatayopagatamanukrāntarūpam, yadi hi syāddeśādiniṣedha evāsya syāt nātyantābhāvaḥ | kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhī tu siddhe kārya[kāraṇa]vyāpyavyāpakabhāve bhavataḥ | na ca hetvantaretyantāsattayāṅgīkṛte prakāro 'yaṃ sambhavati | tat kathaṃ te tadabhāvaṃ gamayiṣyataḥ | virodho 'pyavikala[kāraṇasya] bhavato 'nyabhāve 'bhāvādavagamyata iti viruddhopalabdhirapyasambhavinī | sambhave vā kāraṇānupalabdhyādīnāṃ kathamatyantaniṣedhaḥ? ityāśaṅkayāha- "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare" iti | "tataḥ" trividhāddhetoḥ "apare" anye "hetvābhāsāḥ" yatastatastridhaiva sa iti |
body.translated_text: ...has been stated. There, since <s>kārya</s> (effect) and <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature) function as provers of positive assertion (<s>vidhi</s>), they have no role when negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) is to be proved. From <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) too there is no ascertainment of the absence of other reasons, since it [too] is established in four forms: the non-apprehensions of <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature), of <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause), and of <s>vyāpaka</s> (the pervader), and the positive cognition of what is contradictory (<s>viruddhavidhi</s>). The non-apprehension of <s>svabhāva</s> (essential nature) — which is of the nature of the apprehension of something else that shares equal eligibility (<s>tulyayogyatā</s>) and is associated with a single cognition — is accepted as the basis for the convention of absence. And no other reason that is admitted to be absolutely non-existent has the form here described; for if it existed, only the negation [of it] with respect to place and the like would obtain for it, not absolute non-existence. But the non-apprehensions of <s>kāraṇa</s> (cause) and <s>vyāpaka</s> (the pervader) operate [only] when the relations of effect-cause and pervaded-pervader are [already] established. And when another reason is admitted to be absolutely non-existent, this mode is not possible — so how will those two [non-apprehensions] make known its absence? Contradiction too is understood from the absence of something whose cause is complete and present when the other thing exists; hence the apprehension of what is contradictory (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>) is also impossible [here]. Or, if [these] be possible, how could the non-apprehension of cause and the rest [yield] absolute negation? Anticipating this doubt he says: "<s>hetvābhāsās tato 'pare</s>" ('the pseudo-reasons are other than those'). "Than those" — than the threefold <s>hetu</s> (reason) — "the others" (<s>apare</s>) are the "<s>hetvābhāsāḥ</s>" (pseudo-reasons), because [the reason] is precisely threefold, owing to that [restriction].

children.text: ) eva pratipannaḥ | tadātmaniyatapratibhāsajñānādeva tadviparītasyānyatayā tadābhāsatāpratīteḥ, parasparamitaretararūpābhāva[niśca]yāt | tatra trividhahetuvyatirikteṣvartheṣu hetvābhāsatvamupalabhyamānaṃ svaviruddhaṃ hetutvaṃ nirākaroti | te ca hetutrayabāhyā arthā nātyantāsatta[yopa]gatā nāpi hetutvaṃ teṣu niṣidhyamānaṃ, kevalaṃ vyāmohāt hetutvamanyatra prasiddhameva tatrāropitamāśaṅkitaṃ vā tadviruddhopalambhādapasāryate | tat kimucyate- "[atyantāsaṃbha]vinaḥ kathaṃ virodhaḥ" iti | na ca sahānavasthānalakṣaṇa eva virodho yena tannyāyaḥ sarvatropavarṇyeta | nāpi yad yatra pratiṣidhyate tasya tatraiva viro[dhaḥ prati]pattavyo yena "kathamasataḥ kenacid virodhagatiḥ?" iti codyeta | na hi nātra śītasparśo 'gneriti sādhyadharmiṇyeva śītasparśasyāgninā virodha[saṃba]ndho (?) yathā tu asyānyatra pratītavirodhasyāgninā sādhyadharmiṇi niṣedhaḥ tathā hetvābhāsatvopalambhād hetutrayabāhyeṣvartheṣu hetutvanirāsaḥ | [atyantāsa]to 'pi ca lākṣaṇiko virodhaḥ pratīyate yathā kṣaṇikatvenākṣaṇikatvasya tasya vastuni kvacidapyasambhavāt, bhāvena vā yadvadabhāvasya sarva[śaktivirahala]lakṣaṇasyetyalaṃ durmativiṣpanditeṣvatyādareṇeti sthitametat- tritve hetutvaṃ niyamyamānaṃ [tadviparyayasyā] 'pi ca vyāptau satyāṃ tatra niyataṃ bhavatītyabhiprāyavatā viparyayavyāptiṃ pradarśayitumidamuktam- "hetvābhāsa(sā)stato 'pare" iti |
children.translated_text: because the cognition of what is contrary to that [<s>hetu</s>] as something other [than <s>hetu</s>] — and thus its character as a <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (pseudo-reason) — is understood from the very cognition whose appearance is determined by the nature of that [<s>hetu</s>], since there is mutual ascertainment of the absence of each other's nature. Among these, the <s>hetvābhāsatva</s> (pseudo-reason character) observed in objects other than the threefold <s>hetu</s> removes the <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood) that is contrary to it. And those objects outside the three <s>hetus</s> are not [rejected as] utterly non-existent, nor is <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood) being denied where it [genuinely] exists in them; rather, <s>hetutva</s> that is well-known elsewhere has merely been superimposed or suspected in those [objects] due to confusion, and it is removed by the apprehension of what is contrary to it. So why is it said, 'How can there be contradiction with what is utterly impossible?' For contradiction is not defined solely as non-co-existence, such that this principle could be applied everywhere. Nor should one hold that whatever is negated somewhere is in contradiction with that very locus, such that the objection 'How can something non-existent have a relation of contradiction with anything?' would arise. For when it is said 'cold-touch does not belong to fire here,' the relation of contradiction of cold-touch with fire is not in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (subject of proof) alone; rather, just as the negation of fire in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> [proceeds from] its contradiction established elsewhere, so too the removal of <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood) in objects outside the three <s>hetus</s> [proceeds] from the apprehension of <s>hetvābhāsatva</s> (pseudo-reason character). Moreover, even for what is utterly non-existent, a figurative contradiction is perceived — just as non-momentariness is [contradicted] by momentariness because it is impossible anywhere in real entities; or as non-existence, characterized by the complete absence of all capacities, [is contradicted] by existence. Enough with excessive attention to the gyrations of the dull-witted! Thus it is established that when <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood) is restricted to the three kinds, and the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the converse is also present, [<s>hetutva</s>] is restricted to those [three] alone. With this intent — to demonstrate the converse <s>vyāpti</s> — it was stated: '<s>hetvābhāsās tato 'pare</s>' ('the rest are pseudo-reasons').

body.translated_text: The thought is as follows: Here, when something is restricted to a certain locus, that restriction is established through the converse — namely, through the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the opposite of that locus by the opposite [of what is restricted]. For example, when the restriction of <s>sattva</s> (existence) to momentary things is stated as 'whatever exists is momentary alone,' it is established through the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the opposite of the momentary — i.e., the non-momentary — by the opposite of <s>sattva</s>, i.e., non-existence. Likewise here too, when <s>hetu</s> (reason) is restricted to the three kinds, it is established through the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of what falls outside the three — i.e., [any] object [beyond the threefold classification] — by the converse of <s>hetu</s>, namely <s>hetvābhāsatva</s> (the character of being a pseudo-reason), so that [<s>hetu</s>] is restricted to the three alone. Therefore, he demonstrates the <s>hetvābhāsatā</s> (pseudo-reason character) of objects other than the threefold <s>hetu</s>. Hence, 'by the apprehension of what is contrary to the nature [of <s>hetu</s>], the ascertainment of the absence of <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood) in objects other than <s>kārya</s> (effect), <s>svabhāva</s> (identity), and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension).' And the contradiction between <s>hetu</s> (reason) and <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (pseudo-reason), being of the nature of mutual exclusion, is understood at the very time of apprehending the definition of <s>hetu</s>,

children.translated_text: And thus he will say: 'It [<s>avinābhāva</s>] does not exist in anything other than the threefold <s>hetu</s> — it is said to be restricted to that alone.' And the deficiency of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance), being pervaded by the general property of <s>hetvābhāsatva</s> (pseudo-reason character) — namely <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished), <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), and <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) — is ascertained in cases like <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) and so forth. Thus, when <s>hetvābhāsatva</s> is what is to be proved, the deficiency of <s>avinābhāva</s> serves as a <s>svabhāva-hetu</s> (reason based on identity).

body.translated_text: Here the following [objection] might arise: The <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of the opposite of the momentary by the converse of <s>sattva</s> (existence) was ascertained by the force of a <s>bādhaka-pramāṇa</s> (invalidating cognition). But here, by what <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) is the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of objects outside the threefold classification by <s>hetvābhāsatva</s> (pseudo-reason character) ascertained? To this he says: 'because of the restriction of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance).' The meaning is: even when <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of being a property of the thesis-subject) is present in an object that is taken to be, or suspected to be, a logical mark beyond the threefold <s>hetu</s>, there is absence of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance).

body.text: avinābhāvavaikalyaṃ ca trividhahetuvyatiriktatvādeva [tadanyeṣāṃ] [vyāpa]kānupalabdhitaḥ siddham | tathā hi- tādātmyatadutpattibhyāmavinābhāvo vyāptaḥ, tayostatrāvaśyaṃbhāvāt | tasya ca tayoreva bhāvādatatsvabhāvasyātadutpatteśca [tadanāyattata]yā tadavyabhicāraniyamābhāvāt | taduktam-
body.translated_text: And the deficiency of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) is established through the <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader) of those other [than the threefold <s>hetu</s>], precisely because they differ from the threefold <s>hetu</s>. For <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) is pervaded by <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) and <s>tadutpatti</s> (causal origination), since these two necessarily obtain wherever it does. And because [<s>avinābhāva</s>] exists only through those two, what is not of the nature of either and does not originate from either — being independent of them — has no restriction of non-deviation from them. As has been stated:

the restriction of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) [arises] — from non-observation [of exceptions], not merely from observation.

children.translated_text: even when the relation of product and producer does not hold, or in the case of <s>tādātmya</s> (identity), [the claim that] <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) is through that alone and not through anything else — if to this one replies: 'The answer is to be given through the essential natures of things themselves, which are simply so — we are not responsible for them, we are merely observers' — then that essential nature of things would be accidental, and so it could fail to obtain for anything. For without a cause, restriction to a particular place, time, and substance is not justified. For that [nature] would either be brought to some [locus] or not, and for whatever is either dependent or independent on something somewhere. Otherwise, in the absence of a distinguishing factor, what would prevent existence in places, times, and substances other than the designated ones, given the absence of distinction? Therefore, whatever is seen to be invariably concomitant with whatever, those who inquire into the nature of reality must specify the cause of its non-deviation — one should not simply rest on stretching one's legs [i.e., being lazy]. And that cause of non-deviation is not possible other than as stated [i.e., <s>tādātmya</s> and <s>tadutpatti</s>]; therefore, those lacking it do not partake of the definition of <s>hetu</s> (reason). And thus he says:

body.translated_text: For indeed, even the <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) of <s>rasa</s> (taste) and the like with <s>rūpa</s> (form) and the like is not intrinsic, but operates through non-deviation from their own cause; hence origination from that cause alone is the basis of <s>avinābhāva</s>. Otherwise, if <s>avinābhāva</s> were postulated for what is not dependent on that [cause], or not dependent on its cause, then everything would have <s>avinābhāva</s> with everything, since there would be no distinction. If one says that the <s>avinābhāva</s> of <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>rasa</s> (taste), and so on is due to the cause of co-inherence in a single object — well, <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) too is described as [obtaining] between what is supported and its support. And that relation of support and supported cannot be established through mere non-contribution to each other's nature, [for] that would lead to an undesired consequence; therefore co-inherence in a single object must be understood as dependence on a single causal complex. Or else, another real relation is impossible — as the author of the treatise [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] has explained in detail in the Examination of Relations (<s>Sambandhaparīkṣā</s>), so it should be ascertained from there. body.translated_text: Here the formal argument is: Whatever does not have <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) or <s>tadutpatti</s> (causal origination) with something is not invariably concomitant with it — like <s>prameyatva</s> (knowability) and the like with <s>anityatva</s> (impermanence) and the like. And objects that differ from <s>svabhāva</s> (identity) and <s>kārya</s> (effect) do not have <s>tādātmya</s> or <s>tadutpatti</s> with anything — this is the <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader). As for <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the essential nature), it is subsumed under the <s>svabhāva-hetu</s> (reason based on identity), so its <s>pratibandha</s> (necessary connection) is of the nature of <s>tādātmya</s> (identity) alone. And <s>vyāpaka-anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the pervader) and <s>kāraṇa-anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the cause) establish the cessation of the pervaded and the effect respectively, precisely by virtue of the necessary connection characterized by <s>tādātmya</s> and <s>tadutpatti</s>.

children.text: ) vyāpta eveti sambandhaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam? | "avinābhāvaniyamāt" | avinābhāvasya- vyāpteḥ | trividha eva pakṣadharme niyamāt | trividhasya ca pakṣadharmasyāvinābhāvaniyamāt | tena ca [sva]bhāvakāryānupalambhātmakatrividhapakṣadharmavyatiriktā na tadaṃśena vyāptā iti | trividhaśca kāryasvabhāvānupalabdhirūpaḥ pakṣadharmastadaṃśena vyāpta eveti na tasyāhetutvamityuktaṃ bhavati | tatastrividhahetubāhyeṣvavi[nābhā]bāddhetuvyavahāraṃ kurvantaḥ, trividhe ca hetāvavinābhāvasyāvaśyambhāvā[bhāvā]dahetutvamācakṣāṇā nirastā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: this is the connection. What is the reason? 'Because of the restriction of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance).' Of <s>avinābhāva</s> — that is, of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion): because of its restriction to the threefold <s>pakṣadharma</s> alone. And because of the restriction of <s>avinābhāva</s> to the threefold <s>pakṣadharma</s>. Therefore, [<s>pakṣadharmas</s>] other than the threefold one consisting of <s>svabhāva</s> (identity), <s>kārya</s> (effect), and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) are not pervaded by its component. And the threefold <s>pakṣadharma</s>, having the form of <s>kārya</s>, <s>svabhāva</s>, and <s>anupalabdhi</s>, is indeed pervaded by its component — thus it is stated that it does not lack <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood). Therefore, those who apply the designation '<s>hetu</s>' to [objects] outside the threefold <s>hetu</s> despite the absence of <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance), and those who declare that the threefold <s>hetu</s> lacks <s>hetutva</s> because <s>avinābhāva</s> is not necessarily present [in it] — both are refuted.

body.translated_text: Alternatively, '<s>tridhaiva saḥ</s>' — that <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject) is of exactly three kinds, designated as <s>svabhāva</s> (identity), <s>kārya</s> (effect), and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension), pervaded by its component [i.e., the threefold <s>hetu</s>], and no other. That threefold [<s>pakṣadharma</s>] is pervaded by its component alone —

body.text: 4. hetvābhāsalakṣaṇānabhidhānepi tatsūcanam |
body.translated_text: 4. The indication of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (pseudo-reason) even without stating its definition.

body.text: tatraitat syāt- hetvābhāsānamapi [lakṣaṇam]bhidhānīyaṃ tatra śiṣyāṇāṃ hetuvyavahāranivṛttaya ityāha "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare" iti | "tataḥ" pakṣadharmastadaṃśena vyāpta iti hetulakṣaṇād "apare" a[nye ta]lakṣaṇavikalā hetvābhāsā gamyanta eveti na tallakṣaṇamucyate | tathā hi- "pakṣadharmaḥ" ityukte yatra pakṣadharmatā nāsti na sa hetuḥ | "tadaṃśena vyāptaḥ" iti vacane yatra tadaṃśavyāptiviraho viparyayavyāptervyāpakasya vā tatrāvaśyambhāvābhāvāt, te heturūpavikalatayā "hetvābhāsāḥ" asiddhaviruddhānaikāntikā gamyanta eva | tathā hi- yallakṣaṇo yo 'rthaḥ śiṣyasya vyutpāditaḥ tallakṣaṇavirahite na tadvayavahāraṃ svayameva pravartayiṣyati a[tadrūpa]parihāreṇaiva tadrūpapratipatteriti na tatra yatnaḥ phalavān bhavati | yattvanyatra hetvābhāsavyutpādanaṃ tanmandabuddhīnadhikṛtya | idaṃ tu prakaraṇaṃ vipulamatīnuddiśya praṇītam "saṃkṣepataḥ" iti vacanāt | ta eva hi saṃkṣepoktaṃ yathāvadavagantuṃ kṣamāḥ na mandamatayaḥ, teṣāṃ vistarābhidhānamantareṇa yathāvadarthapratipatterabhāvāt | ata evārthākṣiptopanyāsapūrvakameva hetvābhāsalakṣaṇaṃ tatropavarṇitamiti | tadatra vyākhyāne hetulakṣaṇaṃ 1 hetusaṃkhyāniyamaḥ 2 (

children.text: ) tasya ca trividhasya hetutvāvadhāraṇaṃ 3 tadubhayakāraṇaṃ 4 śliṣṭanirddeśā[khyānaṃ 5] hetvābhāsalakṣaṇānabhidhānakāraṇaṃ 6 ceti ṣaḍarthāḥ śloke 'tra nirdiṣṭā iti |
children.translated_text: the ascertainment of the <s>hetutva</s> (reason-hood) of the threefold [<s>hetu</s>] [3], the cause of both [4], the explanation of the compact formulation [5], and the reason for not stating the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> [6] — these are the six topics indicated in this verse.

body.translated_text: Here the following [objection] might arise: The definition of <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (pseudo-reasons) too should be stated, so that students may cease applying the designation '<s>hetu</s>' to them. To this he says: '<s>hetvābhāsās tato 'pare</s>' ('the rest are pseudo-reasons'). From 'tataḥ' — from the definition of <s>hetu</s> as '<s>pakṣadharma</s> pervaded by its component' — 'apare' — others that lack that definition are understood to be <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (pseudo-reasons), and so their definition need not be separately stated. For when '<s>pakṣadharmaḥ</s>' is stated, whatever lacks <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (the property of being a property of the thesis-subject) is not a <s>hetu</s>. By the statement 'pervaded by its component,' wherever there is absence of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) by that component — because of the absence of the necessary occurrence of the <s>vyāpaka</s> (pervader) or of the converse <s>vyāpti</s> — those, being deficient in the form of <s>hetu</s>, are understood to be <s>hetvābhāsas</s>: <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished), <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), and <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive). For when a student has been instructed about an object having a certain definition, he will not himself apply that designation to what lacks that definition, since the apprehension of that nature arises precisely through the exclusion of what is not of that nature — so no effort [to separately define pseudo-reasons] is fruitful there. The instruction on <s>hetvābhāsas</s> given elsewhere [in other treatises] is intended for those of dull intellect. But this treatise is composed for those of vast intellect, as indicated by the word '<s>saṃkṣepataḥ</s>' ('in brief'). For only they are capable of properly understanding what is stated in brief, not those of dull intellect, since without detailed exposition they cannot properly comprehend the meaning. For this very reason, the definition of <s>hetvābhāsa</s> is described there [in other works] only after presenting what is implied by the meaning. Thus, in this commentary, the verse indicates six topics: the definition of <s>hetu</s> [1], the numerical restriction of <s>hetus</s> [2],

body.text: kiñca- idamapi sādhu dṛśyate- "tridhaiva" kāryasvabhāvānupalabdhi[bheda]bhinnaḥ sa hetuḥ | tathā, tridhaiva pakṣadharmānvayavyatirekarūpabhedāt "triprakāra eva" trirūpa eva | tadaṃśavyāptivacanenānvayavyatirekayorabhidhānāt | nābādhitaviṣayatvādirūpāntarayogyapi sa hetuḥ | kutaḥ? yataḥ "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare" "tataḥ" trividhāt svabhā[vā]deḥ, pakṣadharmādirūpatrayayogino vā "apare" anye saṃyogyādayo 'bādhitaviṣayatvādivyatiriktarūpavanto vā | kasmād? | avinābhāvasya atraiva trividha eva trirūpa eva ca hetau niyamādanyatra svabhāvādivyatirikta(kte) rūpāntarasambhavini vā avinābhāvābhāvādityarthaḥ | na hi svabhāvādivya[ti]rikte pratibandhanibandhanasyāvinābhāvasya saṃbhavaḥ tadvati vā rūpāntarasya | yathā cā(ca) satyevāvinābhāve rūpāntarasya na sambhavastathā "ṣaḍlakṣaṇa" ityādinā vakṣyati |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the following also appears sound: '<s>tridhaiva</s>' — that <s>hetu</s> (reason) is differentiated into the types of <s>kārya</s> (effect), <s>svabhāva</s> (identity), and <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension). And likewise, '<s>tridhaiva</s>' — '<s>triprakāra eva</s>' means 'having exactly three aspects,' since it is of three forms on account of the distinction between the aspects of <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject), <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance), and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance). This is because the statement about <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) by its component expresses both <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>. That <s>hetu</s> is not also fit for additional aspects such as having an uncontradicted domain, etc. Why? Because '<s>hetvābhāsās tato 'pare</s>' — 'tataḥ' means from the threefold <s>svabhāva</s> and the rest; or from [the <s>hetu</s>] possessing the three aspects of <s>pakṣadharma</s> and so on; 'apare' means others such as conjunction and the like, or those possessing aspects other than having an uncontradicted domain, etc. For what reason? Because <s>avinābhāva</s> (invariable concomitance) is restricted to just this — the threefold and three-aspected <s>hetu</s> alone — and elsewhere, in what differs from <s>svabhāva</s> and the rest, or in what admits of additional aspects, there is absence of <s>avinābhāva</s>. For there is no possibility of <s>avinābhāva</s>, which is grounded in <s>pratibandha</s> (necessary connection), in what differs from <s>svabhāva</s> and the rest, or of additional aspects in what possesses it. And that when <s>avinābhāva</s> is present there is no possibility of additional aspects — this he will state with the passage beginning '<s>ṣaḍlakṣaṇa</s>' ('six characteristics').

body.text: 5. diṅnāgānusāreṇa pakṣaśabdasya dharmimātraparatvam |
body.translated_text: 5. The term <s>pakṣa</s> refers to the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) alone, following <s>Diṅnāga</s>.

body.text: "pakṣadharmaḥ" ityatra hetulakṣaṇe 'pi kriyamāṇe yadi samudāyaḥ pakṣe(kṣo) gṛhyate yo 'numānaviṣayastadā sarvo heturasiddhaḥ, siddhau vānumānavaiyarthyamityāha "pakṣo dharmī" iti | kathaṃ punaḥ samudāyavacanaḥ pakṣaśabdo dharmimātre vartata iti cet? "avayave samudāyopacārāt" | pakṣākhyasya hi samudāyasya dvāvavayavau dharmī dharmaśca | tadatra dharmimātre samudāyopacārāt pakṣaśabdo vartate | tadekadeśatvaṃ ca samudāyopacāranimittamiti na sādhyadharmiṇo 'nyatra tatprasaṅgaḥ | taduktam-
body.translated_text: Even when the definition of <s>hetu</s> is being formulated as '<s>pakṣadharmaḥ</s>' (property of the thesis-subject), if <s>pakṣa</s> is taken as the aggregate — i.e., as the entire object of inference — then every <s>hetu</s> would be <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished), or if it were established, inference would be pointless. Therefore he says: '<s>pakṣo dharmī</s>' ('the <s>pakṣa</s> is the <s>dharmin</s>'). But how does the word <s>pakṣa</s>, which denotes the aggregate, apply to the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) alone? 'Through the figurative application of the aggregate term to a part.' For the aggregate called <s>pakṣa</s> has two parts: the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) and the <s>dharma</s> (property). Here, through figurative application of the aggregate to the <s>dharmin</s> alone, the word <s>pakṣa</s> functions [to mean <s>dharmin</s>]. And since being a part of the aggregate is the basis for the figurative application, there is no unwanted extension of this [usage] to anything other than the <s>sādhya-dharmin</s> (the subject to be proven). As has been stated:

body.text:
"samudāyasya sādhyatvāt dharmamātre [ca]dharmiṇi |
amukhye 'pyekadeśatvāt sādhyatvamupacaryate || "iti |
body.translated_text: 'Since the aggregate is what is to be proved, and the <s>dharmin</s> alone — though not the primary [referent] — is figuratively said to be what is to be proved, because it is a part [of the aggregate].'

body.text: 6. diṅnāgavyākhyāne īśvarasenākṣepastatuddhāraśca |
body.translated_text: 6. <s>Īśvarasena</s>'s objection to <s>Diṅnāga</s>'s explanation, and its resolution.

body.text: tadetadācāryīyaṃ vyākhyānamīśvarasenenākṣiptaṃ parihartuṃ pūrvapakṣayannāha "prayo[jane]" tyādinā |
body.translated_text: This explanation following the master [<s>Diṅnāga</s>] was objected to by <s>Īśvarasena</s>. In order to refute [that objection], he first presents the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opposing position), saying '<s>prayojane</s>' and so forth.

body.text: "narte, prayojanādiṣṭraṃ(ṣṭaṃ) mukhyaśabdārthalaṅghanam |"
body.translated_text: '[This is] not [correct], [because] the overriding of the primary meaning of a word, directed by purpose [alone, is inadmissible].'

body.text: ityasati prayojane nopacāro yuktaḥ | tato dharmidharma ityevāstviti paraḥ | "na" prayojanābhāvaḥ | kutaḥ? sarvaścāsau vivādāśrayo 'nyo vā dharmī yastasya pratiṣedho 'rthaḥ prayojanaṃ yasyopacārasya tadbhāvastasmāt "sarvadharmidharmapratiṣedhārthatvādupacārasya" iti prayojanābhāvādityasiddho hetuḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, in the absence of a purpose, figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is not appropriate. Therefore, the opponent says: let it just be "property-of-the-property-bearer" (<s>dharmidharma</s>). "No" — the absence of purpose [is itself] unestablished. Why? Because the purpose of that figurative usage is the negation of every subject of dispute (<s>vivādāśraya</s>) or any other property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>); therefore [the objection] "because of the absence of purpose of the figurative usage" is an unestablished reason, since it [i.e., the purpose in the form of] the negation of all property-bearer-properties does exist.

body.text: ka evaṃ sati guṇaḥ? iti cedāha "evaṃ hi" upacāre sati "cākṣuṣatvādi" ādigrahaṇāt ‘kākasya kārṣṇyāt'; ityādi vyadhikaraṇāsiddhaṃ "parihṛtaṃ" hetutvena nirastaṃ "bhavati" | dharmidharma iti tu sāmānye [nābhi]dhānāt teṣāmapi hetutā syāditi |
body.translated_text: If one asks: what then is the advantage in this case? — he says: "For thus" — when there is figurative usage, "being visual (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>) and so forth" — by the word "and so forth" [including examples like] "because of the blackness of the crow" — what is "unestablished in a different locus" (<s>vyadhikaraṇāsiddha</s>) "is eliminated" — is removed as a reason — "that is the case." But if [the formulation were] "property of the property-bearer," then since the designation would be in terms of the universal [alone], even those [pseudo-reasons] could [appear to] have the status of reasons.

body.text: asatyupacāre dharmigrahaṇādapyetat sidhyati | tato 'narthaka evopacāra ityāha paraḥ- "dharmavacanenāpi" na kevalaṃ dha[rmiva]canena | "dharmyāśrayasiddhau" dharmiṇa āśrayaṇamāśrayaḥ parigrahastasya siddhistasyāṃ satyām | kiṃ punarddharmasya dharmyākṣepanimittamiti cet? "parā[śrayatvā]t"- dharmiparatantratvāt "dharmasya" avaśyamasau dharmiṇamākṣipati | tato dharmivacanamatiricyamānaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ sādhyadharmiṇameva pratipādayati, [na dharmimātram] | syānmatam- dharmigrahaṇād viśiṣṭo 'tra dharmī kaścidabhipreta iti gamyeta | sa tu sādhyadharmīti kutaḥ? ityāha- "pratyāsatte"rnyāyāt | pratyāsattiścātra dharmi[vacanasāmarthyāda]bhipreteti gamyate | vyāptau tu nyāye dharmavacanenāpi dharmimātrākṣepat dharmigrahaṇavaiyarthyam | pratyāsannatā ca sādhyadharmiṇa eva, tatra prathamaṃ (

children.text: ) he[tūpa]darśanāt | na pratyāsatteḥ sādhyadharmiparigrahaḥ | kutaḥ? | "dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇo 'pi" na kevalaṃ sādhyadharmiṇaḥ pratyāsatteḥ | kadācid vyāptidarśanapūrvake prayoge dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇyapi prathamaṃ hetusadbhāvopadarśanāt |
children.translated_text: The inclusion of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (thesis-subject) is not [established] from proximity. Why? "Because even of the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> (example-subject)" — not only of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> — there is proximity; since sometimes, in a formulation preceded by the observation of pervasion, the existence of the reason is first shown in the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> (example-subject) as well.

body.translated_text: Even without figurative usage, this [elimination] could be achieved merely by mentioning the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). Therefore the opponent says this is purposeless figurative usage: "even by the mention of the property" — not merely by the mention of the property-bearer. "When the inclusion of the property-bearer is established" — the inclusion (<s>āśraya</s>) of the property-bearer, i.e., [its] acceptance; when that is established. What, then, is the reason for the property implying the property-bearer? "Because of [the property's] dependence on another" — because the property is dependent on the property-bearer, it necessarily implies the property-bearer. Therefore, the mention of the property-bearer, being surplus, indicates precisely the specific property-bearer that is the subject to be proved (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>), not just any property-bearer. One might think: from the mention of the property-bearer, it would be understood that some specific property-bearer is intended here. But how [do we know] that it is the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (the property-bearer in the thesis)? He says: by the principle of "proximity" (<s>pratyāsatti</s>). And proximity here is understood from the force of the mention of the property-bearer. But if, by the principle of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), even the mention of the property alone implies any property-bearer, then the mention of the property-bearer would be pointless. And proximity pertains to the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> alone, since the reason is first presented there.

body.text: yadi na pratyāsatteḥ sādhyadharmisiddhiḥ pāriśeṣyāt tarhi bhaviṣyati | yataḥ "tadaṃśavyāptyā" hetubhūtayā "dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi" dharmasya satva(ttva)siddheḥ | nahi dṛṣṭāntamantareṇa hetoḥ sādhyena vyāptiḥ pradarśayituṃ śakyata iti manyate | tato dharmigrahaṇādvayatiricyamānāt sādhyadharmiṇa eva parigrahaḥ | "tadaṃśena" iti ca tacchabdena dharmavacanākṣipto dharmī sambhantsyata iti tatsambandhanārthamapi dharmigrahaṇaṃ nāśaṅkanīyam | yatra prayojanāntaraṃ na sambhavati sa pāriśeṣyaviṣayaḥ, dharmivacanasya tvanyadapi prayojanaṃ sambhāvyate | tat kutaḥ pāriśeṣyāt "dharmivacanāt sādhyadharmiparigrahaḥ"? iti manyamānaḥ siddhāntavādyāha- "siddhe tadaṃśavyāptyā dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi satva(ttve) punarddharmiṇo vacanaṃ dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇa eva yo dharmaḥ sa heturiti niyamārthamāśaṅkayeta | tataśca cākṣuṣatvādaya eva hetavaḥ syuḥ, na kṛtakatvādaya iti aniṣṭameva syāt tasmādupacāraḥ kartavyaḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: If the establishment of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> is not from proximity, then it will be by elimination (<s>pāriśeṣya</s>). Because "through the pervasion of that aspect" (<s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s>) — which constitutes the reason — "the existence [of the property] in the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> (example-subject) is [already] established." For he thinks that the pervasion of the reason with the property to be proved cannot be demonstrated without an example. Therefore, from the mention of the property-bearer, which is surplus, only the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (thesis-subject) is to be accepted. And by the word "that" (<s>tad</s>) in "of that aspect" — lest one suspect that the mention of the property-bearer is for the purpose of connecting with the property-bearer implied by the mention of the property — [that suspicion is dispelled]. What is the domain of elimination is that where no other purpose is possible; but for the mention of the property-bearer, another purpose is also conceivable. Therefore, the proponent of the established view (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), thinking "how can the acceptance of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> be from elimination, from the mention of the property-bearer?" says: "When the existence [of the reason] in the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> (example-subject) is already established through the pervasion of that aspect, the further mention of the property-bearer might be suspected to be for the purpose of restriction (<s>niyama</s>) — [namely,] that only that property which belongs to the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> is a valid reason. And in that case, only visual character (<s>cākṣuṣatva</s>) and the like would be reasons, not being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and the like — which would be an undesirable consequence. Therefore, figurative usage must be employed."

body.text: kiṃ punastarkaśāstra dṛṣṭaṃ kvacit niyamārthavacanamitya āha- "dṛṣṭaṃ sajātīya eva" ityādi | "tatra yaḥ san sajātīye-" [nyāyamukha 7] ityatrācāryīye hetulakṣaṇe ‘sajātīya e[va] satva(ttva)mi'tyavadhāraṇena siddhe 'pi hetorvyatireke | kutra? | sādhyābhāve | yadetat "asaṃstadatyaye" [nyāyamukha 7] iti asatva(ttva)vacanaṃ tanniyamārthamācāryeṇa vyākhyāta[m a]satyeva nāstitā yathā syāt nānyatra na viruddha iti | tathehāpi dharmivacanaṃ tatraiva bhāvaniyamārthamāśaṅkayeta | kadā? siddhe 'pi dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi [sa]tve(ttve) | kutaḥ? tadaṃśavyāptivacanāt | (

children.text: ) kva bhāvaniyamārtham? "[ta]traiva" dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi, sati cāśaṅkāsambhave | kutaḥ? | pāriśeṣyāt sādhyadharmiparigrahaḥ | nanu apakṣadharmasyāhetutvāt na niyamārthatāśaṅkā | tathā hi- sādhyadharmeṇa vyāpto 'pi dharmo yadi kvacid dharmiṇyupalabhyeta tadā tatraiva svavyāpakapratītiṃ janayet nānyatra [pratyā]sattiviprakarṣābhyāṃ yathākramam | anupalavdhastu kvacid dharmiṇi kathaṃ gamakaḥ? | tathābhāve vā sarvatra svavyāpakaṃ gamayet pratyāsattiviprakarṣābhāvāde[vetyata] āha- "tasmāt sāmarthyāt" ityādi | yadidamanantaraṃ sāmarthyaṃ samupavarṇitam āsmāt sāmarthyādarthasya sādhyadharmiparigrahalakṣaṇasya bhavati pratīti[rpa]ṭudhiyāṃ śrotṛṇām, kintvaśabdakamarthaṃ svayamanusaratāṃ pratipattigauravaṃ syāt | tadupacāramātrāt svayamaśabdakārthābhyūharahitād dharmidharma ityane [na pa]kṣadharma iti "samānanirddeśāt [pratipattigauravaṃ ca] parihṛtaṃ bhavati |" "pratipattigauravaṃ ca" iti ‘ca'śabdenaitadāha- ye paropadeśamākāṅkṣanti tairayamartho lakṣaṇa[vaca]nād boddhavya iti |
children.translated_text: Where is it for the purpose of restricting the occurrence? "In that very [example-subject]" — in the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s>, when the possibility of such a suspicion exists. Why? By elimination, the acceptance of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> [follows]. But [one might object:] since a property not belonging to the thesis-subject (<s>apakṣadharma</s>) is not a valid reason, the suspicion of restriction does not arise. That is to say: even if a property is pervaded by the property to be proved, if it is apprehended in some property-bearer, then it would generate the cognition of its pervader only there, not elsewhere — [respectively] due to proximity and remoteness. But how can [a property] that is not apprehended in any property-bearer be indicative? Or, in the absence of such [differential proximity], it would indicate its pervader everywhere, since there would be no proximity or remoteness — therefore he says: "Therefore, from that capacity" and so on. This capacity that has been described immediately [before] — from this capacity, the apprehension of the meaning characterized as the acceptance of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> arises for listeners of sharp intellect; however, for those who must work out the unspoken meaning on their own, there would be difficulty in comprehension. From the mere figurative usage [of <s>pakṣadharma</s>], which by itself is devoid of the effort of inferring the unspoken meaning, and from the uniform expression (<s>samānanirdeśa</s>) [of <s>pakṣadharma</s>] rather than <s>dharmidharma</s>, "the difficulty of comprehension is also eliminated." And by the word "also" (<s>ca</s>) in "and the difficulty of comprehension," he states this: those who require instruction from another should understand this meaning from the definitional statement.

body.translated_text: Is a statement for the purpose of restriction ever observed in the science of logic? He says: "It is observed — in the <s>sajātīya</s> (homogeneous) alone" and so on. In the <s>Ācārya</s>'s (<s>Dignāga</s>'s) definition of the reason in [the <s>Nyāyamukha</s>]: "that which, being present in the homogeneous alone" [<s>Nyāyamukha</s> 7] — even though the exclusion (<s>vyatireka</s>) of the reason is already established by the restrictive particle "alone" in "existence in the homogeneous alone" — where? — in the absence of the property to be proved — the statement of non-existence "and non-existence in their absence" [<s>Nyāyamukha</s> 7] was explained by the <s>Ācārya</s> as being for the purpose of restriction: that the non-existence should be only in that [absence of the <s>sādhya</s>], and not elsewhere, [i.e.,] not in what is contrary [to the <s>sādhya</s>]. Likewise here too, the mention of the property-bearer might be suspected to be for the purpose of restricting the occurrence to that [subject] alone. When? Even though the existence [of the reason] in the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> (example-subject) is already established. Why? Because of the statement of pervasion of that aspect.

body.text: yathālakṣaṇaṃ pratīterapakṣadharmo na heturiti kutaḥ? iyamāśaṅkā | tatasteṣāṃ lakṣaṇānusāriṇāṃ niyamāśaṅkāparihārārthaṃ copacārakara[ṇami]ti |
body.translated_text: How is it that according to the definition, a property not belonging to the thesis-subject (<s>apakṣadharma</s>) is not a reason? This is the objection. Therefore, for the sake of removing the suspicion of restriction for those who follow the definition, the figurative usage is also made.

body.text: 7. pakṣadharma ityatra niyamavyavasthā |
body.translated_text: 7. Regarding the expression <s>pakṣadharma</s>, the determination of the restriction.

body.text: iha vyavacchedaphalatvāt śabdaprayogasyāvaśyamevāvadhārayitavyam | ṣaṣṭhīsamāsācca pakṣadharma ityatra nānyaḥ samāsaḥ sambhavati | tathā ca pakṣasyaiva dharma [i]tyevamavadhāraṇāt tadaṃśavyāptirvirudhyata iti viruddhalakṣaṇatāmudbhāvayannāha "pakṣasya dharmatve tvaṃ(taṃ) pakṣaṃ viśeṣaṇamanyato vyavacchedakamapekṣata" iti "tadviśeṣaṇāpekṣasya" dharmasya "anyatra" pakṣīkṛtādanyasmin sapakṣe "ananuvṛttiḥ" | tathā hi- yaḥ pakṣeṇa viśeṣyate sa pakṣasyaiva bhavati nānya[sya] | yathā- yo devadattasya putraḥ sa tasyaiva putro na yajñadattasyāpi | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 15.

children.text: ) tato 'nyatrānanuvṛtteḥ "asādhāraṇatā"- sādhāraṇatā na syāt | tadaṃ śavyāptivirodha [i]ti yāvat | sādhāraṇatāyāstva(yāśca) tadaṃśavyāptyā pratipādanāt | tato yadi pakṣadharmo na ta[daṃśe]na vyāptiḥ, atha tadaṃśavyāptirna pakṣadharma iti vyāhataṃ lakṣaṇamiti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of non-occurrence elsewhere, there would be "uncommonness" (<s>asādhāraṇatā</s>) — i.e., there would be no commonness (<s>sādhāraṇatā</s>). That is to say: a contradiction with the pervasion of that aspect (<s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s>). For commonness [of the reason with the homogeneous instances] is established through the pervasion of that aspect. Therefore, if [the reason is] a <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis-subject), then there would be no pervasion of that aspect; and if there is pervasion of that aspect, then it would not be a <s>pakṣadharma</s> — thus the definition would be self-contradictory.

body.translated_text: Here, since the purpose of the use of the word is exclusion, it must necessarily be determined. And since the compound <s>pakṣadharma</s> is a genitive compound (<s>ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa</s>), no other compound [analysis] is possible there. And thus, since the determination is "a property of the thesis-subject alone" (<s>pakṣasyaiva dharma</s>), the pervasion of that aspect (<s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s>) would be contradicted — bringing out the fault of a self-contradictory definition, he says: "When [it means] being a property of the thesis-subject, that thesis-subject, as a qualifier, requires exclusion from other [loci]" — of the property "that requires such qualification by the thesis-subject, [there is] non-occurrence elsewhere" — in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homogeneous instance) which is other than what has been made the thesis-subject. That is to say: what is qualified by the thesis-subject belongs to the thesis-subject alone, not to another; just as a son of <s>Devadatta</s> is the son of him alone, not also of <s>Yajñadatta</s>.

body.text: nanu ca tadaṃśavyāptirnāma sādhyadharmasya vyāpakasya tatra hetau sati tadādhāradharmiṇi bhāva, eva, vyāpyasya vā hetostatraiva vyāpake sādhyadharme satyeva bhāva iti svasādhyāvinābhāvalakṣaṇā vakṣyate | na cānayāvaśyaṃ pakṣīkṛtādanyatra vṛttirākṣipyate, yato lakṣaṇavyāghāta āśaṅkyeta | tathā hi- tatraiva pakṣīkṛte satyeva sādhyadharme heturvartamānastadaṃśavyāptiṃ pratipadyata eva | yaiva cāsya sādhyadharmiṇi svasādhyāvinābhāvitā saiva gamakatve nibandhanaṃ nānyadharmiṇi | sa ca svasādhyāvinābhāvaḥ pratibandhasādhakapramāṇanibandhanaḥ, na sapakṣe kvacid bahulaṃ vā sahabhāvamātradarśananibandhanaḥ | na hi lohalekhyaṃ vajram pārthivatvāt kāṣṭhādivat iti tadanyatra pārthivatvasya lohalekhyatāvinābhāvo 'pi tathābhāvo bhavati | yadi ca pakṣīkṛtādanyatraiva vyāptirādarśayitavyeti niyamastadā satvaṃ(ttvaṃ) kathaṃ kṣaṇikatāṃ bhāveṣu pratipādayet? | yo hi sakalapadārthavyāpinīmākṣa(nīṃ kṣa)ṇīkatāmicchati taṃ prati kasyacit [sa]pakṣasyaivābhāvāt | yadapi kaiścit jvālādeḥ kṣaṇikatvamabhyupagamyate tadapi na pratyakṣataḥ, kṣaṇavivekasyātisūkṣmatayānupalakṣaṇāt | anyatraiva ca vyāptirādarśanīyā na sādhyadharmiṇyapīti ko 'yaṃ nyāyaḥ? | evaṃ hi kālpanikatvaṃ hetulakṣaṇasya pratipannaṃ syāt, na vastubalapravṛttatvam, tasmāt svasādhyapratibandhād hetustena vyāptaḥ sidhyati | sa ca viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā sādhyadharmiṇyapi sidhyatīti na kiñcidanyatrānuvṛttyapekṣayā | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 16.

children.text: ) ata evānyatroktam- "yat kvacid dṛṣṭaṃ tasya yatra pratibandhaḥ tadvidaḥ tasya tad gamakaṃ tatreti vastugatiḥ" iti |
children.translated_text: For this very reason, it has been stated elsewhere: "That which is observed somewhere — for one who knows the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) of that with something — that is indicative of that [something] there. This is the nature of things."

body.translated_text: Now, the pervasion of that aspect (<s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s>) means: when the pervading property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) exists in the property-bearer where the reason is present, or when the pervaded reason exists only where the pervading property to be proved exists — it will be stated as having the character of invariable concomitance with its own provable property (<s>svasādhyāvinābhāva</s>). And by this [definition], the occurrence [of the reason] elsewhere — i.e., other than the thesis-subject — is not necessarily implied, so that a contradiction with the definition would be suspected. That is to say: even when the reason is present in that very thesis-subject, if the property to be proved is present, it indeed possesses the pervasion of that aspect. And it is precisely its invariable concomitance with its own provable property in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (thesis-subject) that is the basis for its being indicative, not [its occurrence] in another property-bearer. And that invariable concomitance with its own provable property (<s>svasādhyāvinābhāva</s>) is grounded in a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) that establishes the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), not grounded merely in the observation of co-occurrence in some or many <s>sapakṣa</s> (homogeneous instances). For [consider:] "A diamond is scratchable by iron, because it is made of earth, like wood and the like" — even though earthiness is invariably concomitant with scratchability-by-iron elsewhere, it is not so [in the case of diamond]. And if there were a rule that pervasion must be demonstrated exclusively elsewhere than the thesis-subject, then how could "existence" (<s>sattva</s>) demonstrate momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatā</s>) in all entities? For one who holds that momentariness pervades all objects, there is no <s>sapakṣa</s> (homogeneous instance) at all. And even when some [opponents] accept the momentariness of a flame and the like, that too is not [established] from direct perception, since the discrimination of moments is too subtle to be observed. And what principle dictates that pervasion must be demonstrated exclusively elsewhere and not also in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (thesis-subject)? For in that case, the definition of a reason would be understood as fabricated, not as proceeding from the force of reality. Therefore, the reason is established as pervaded by [the <s>sādhya</s>] through the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) with its own provable property. And that [necessary connection] is established, in the case of the contrary, through the operation of a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> (<s>bādhaka</s>), even in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> itself — so there is no dependence whatsoever on occurrence elsewhere.

body.text: yadapi "anumeye 'tha tattalye sadbhāvaḥ-" ityādi lakṣaṇaṃ tatrāpi sādhyadharmavāneva sapakṣa ucyate | tataḥ satyeva sādhyadharme vāstītyevaṃparametat | tataśca taddharmaṇaḥ sādhyadharmiṇo 'pi vāstavaṃ sapakṣatvaṃ na vyāvartate | sādhyatveneṣṭatayecchāvyavasthitalakṣaṇena pakṣatvena tasya nirākartumaśakyatvāt | tasmāt tadaṃśavyāptivacanena svasādhyāvinābhāvitvasya pratibandhanibandhanasyānyathā tadayogādabhidhānānnāvaśya manyatra vṛttirākṣipteti, kathamidamāśaṅkitam? | satyam, naivedamāśaṅkanīyam, yadi sarvasya hetoḥ pakṣīkṛte eva dharmiṇi svasādhyapratibandhaḥ pramāṇato niścetuṃ śakyeta | yathā sattvalakṣaṇasya svabhāvahetoḥ kṣaṇikatāyāṃ sādhyāyāṃ tādātmyaṃ viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā | kāryahetostu pa[kṣīkṛtadharmiṇā | kasyacit svabhāvahetoḥ] pratyakṣānupalambhasādhanaḥ pratibandhaḥ kathaṃ parokṣe sādhyadharme gṛhyeta? | tasmāt tasyānyatraiva [prasiddhiriti tadviśeṣaṇāpekṣasya tatra apekṣaṇāt anya]trānanuvṛtteḥ asādhāraṇatā sambhavamātreṇāśaṅkitā | tadā hyanyatrāvartamānaḥ sādhyaviparīta[vyatireka]...........................................................tadubhayabahirbhāvāyogāt taddharmiṇaḥ sādhyavṛttivyavacchedābhyāṃ sarvasaṃgrahāt tatra saṃśayahetu[rbhavati | syānmatam- kvacidāśraye sattāyāḥ prākpravṛttapūrvagṛhī]tavismṛtapratibandhasādhakapramāṇasmṛtaye 'nyatra vṛttirapekṣaṇīyā | etat pariharati | "na" ityādi | [nānyatrānanubhavattiḥ | kutaḥ? children.text: ) ayogo 'samba]ndhaḥ tavdyavacchedena viśeṣaṇāt pakṣasya | na hyanyayogavyavacchedenaiva viśeṣaṇaṃ bhavati | [kintu ayogavyavacchedenāpi | yatra dharmiṇi dha]rmasya sadbhāvaḥ saṃdihyate tatrāyogavyavacchedasya nyāyaprāptatvāt | atra ca dṛṣṭāntaḥ["yathā caitro dharnurdhara iti" | caitre hi dhanurdhara]tvaṃ saṃdihyate kimasti nāsti iti | tataścaitro dhanurddhara iti tatsadbhāvapratipādikā śrutīḥ [pakṣāntaramadhanurdharatvaṃ śroturāśaṅkopasthāpitaṃ] nirākarotītyayogavyavacchedo 'tra nyāyaprāptaḥ | parābhimatavyavacchedanirācikīrṣayāha- ["na, anyayogavyavacchedena viśeṣaṇāt" anyatrānanuvṛttera]sādhāraṇateti sambandhaḥ | atrāpi dṛṣṭānto "yathā pārtho dhanurddhara iti" | sāmānyaśabdo 'pyayaṃ dha[nurdharaśabdaḥ prakaraṇasāmarthyādinā prakṛṣṭaguṇavṛttiḥ | iha pārthe] hi dhanurddharatvaṃ siddhameveti nāyogāśaṅkā | [tādṛ]śaṃ tu sātiśayaṃ kimanyatrāsti nāstītyanyayoga [śaṅkāyāṃ śrotuḥ yadā pārtho dhanurdhara iti ucya]te tadānyayogavyavacchedo nyāyaprāptaḥ, pratipādyāśaṅkopasthāpitayoreva pakṣayoḥ para[sparaṃ virodhāt ekanirdeśena anyayogavyavacchedasya] nyāyabalāyātatvāt | tadiha pakṣe 'styayaṃ dharmo na veti saṃśītau [pakṣadharma ityukte pakṣasya dharma eva nādharmaḥ | dharmaśca āśritatvādviśeṣaṇaṃ tenāyogo vya]vacchidyate nānyayogastadaṃśavyāptyā tasya pratipādita[tvena dṛṣṭānte saṃdehābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: ) is the exclusion of non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>)], because the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is qualified by the exclusion of that [property]. For qualification does not occur only through exclusion of alternative connection (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>), [but also through exclusion of non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>)]. Where the existence of a [particular] property (<s>dharma</s>) in the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) is doubted, there the exclusion of non-connection is logically obtained. And here the example is ["as when one says '<s>Caitra</s> is an archer.' For regarding <s>Caitra</s>], archerhood is doubted — does he have it or not? Therefore, the statement '<s>Caitra</s> is an archer,' which establishes that existence, [rejects the alternative of non-archerhood, which was raised by the hearer's doubt] — thus the exclusion of non-connection is logically obtained here. Wishing to reject the exclusion accepted by the opponent, he says — ["No, because qualification is through exclusion of alternative connection (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>)," meaning non-occurrence elsewhere] is uncommonness — this is the connection. Here too the example is "as when one says '<s>Pārtha</s> is an archer.'" This word 'archer' (<s>dhanurdhara</s>), though a common term, [by the force of context etc., applies to one of preeminent quality. For regarding <s>Pārtha</s>], archerhood is already established, so there is no doubt of non-connection. [But such] surpassing [archerhood] — whether it exists elsewhere or not — when there is doubt of alternative connection, [when it is said '<s>Pārtha</s> is an archer,'] then the exclusion of alternative connection is logically obtained, because of the mutual opposition of the two alternatives [presented for establishment and raised by doubt], and because the exclusion of alternative connection [is logically entailed] by the indication of one. Therefore here, when there is doubt whether this property exists in the <s>pakṣa</s> or not, [when 'property of the thesis' is stated, it is the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> and not its absence. And since the property qualifies by virtue of being attributed, the exclusion of non-connection] is effected, not the exclusion of alternative connection, because that has already been established through <s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s> (pervasion by that portion), [since there is no doubt in the example].

body.translated_text: As for the definition "existence in the subject of inference or in what is homogeneous with it" and so on — there too, the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homogeneous instance) is said to be precisely that which possesses the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>). Therefore, [the expression "existence"] has the ultimate sense: "only when the property to be proved exists." And thus, the actual status of the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (thesis-subject) as a homogeneous instance, possessing that property [i.e., the <s>sādhyadharma</s>], is not excluded — because it cannot be excluded by the status of thesis-subjecthood, which is defined as being desired as the locus of what is to be proved. Therefore, since the statement of pervasion-of-that-aspect (<s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s>) denotes the invariable concomitance with one's own provable property, grounded in necessary connection — and since otherwise that [pervasion] would be impossible — the occurrence elsewhere is not necessarily implied. How then was this objection raised? True, this objection should indeed not be raised, if the necessary connection of every reason with its own provable property in the thesis-subject alone could be ascertained by a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Just as, for the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) characterized by existence (<s>sattva</s>), the identity [of existence and momentariness] when momentariness is the property to be proved [is established] through the operation of a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> in the case of the contrary. But for the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) [established with respect to a thesis-subject], how can the necessary connection, whose proof is direct perception and non-apprehension, be grasped regarding a supersensory property to be proved? Therefore, its establishment is only elsewhere [i.e., in the example]. And the suspicion of uncommonness was raised merely as a possibility — [namely,] that since the property that requires the thesis-subject as its qualifier would, due to its being so restricted, not occur elsewhere, [there would be uncommonness] ... [and] because of the impossibility of being outside both [the thesis-subject and the contrary], from the exclusion of [both] occurrence and non-occurrence [of the property] in the property-bearer of that [property to be proved], and from the comprehensive inclusion [of all property-bearers in one or the other], it would be a reason for doubt there. One might think: for [remembering] a <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the necessary connection — [a <s>pramāṇa</s>] previously operative, previously grasped, and [now] forgotten — [pertaining to] the existence [of the reason] in some locus, occurrence elsewhere is to be expected. He refutes this: "No" and so on. [There is no non-occurrence elsewhere. Why?

body.text: "tadaṃśaḥ" taddharma iti] | tacchabdena pakṣaḥ parāmṛśyate na dharmaḥ, dharmasya dharmāsambhavāt | aṃśaśca dharmo naikadeśaḥ, pakṣa[śabdena dharmimātravacanāt | na tadaṃśaḥ tasya eka]deśābhāvāditi |
body.translated_text: "That portion" (<s>tadaṃśa</s>) means 'a property of that' (<s>taddharma</s>)]. By the word 'that' (<s>tad</s>), the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) is referred to, not the property (<s>dharma</s>), because a property cannot have a [further] property. And 'portion' (<s>aṃśa</s>) means property, not a part; because the word '<s>pakṣa</s>' [denotes merely the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>). It is not a portion of that, since that] has no such part.

body.text: 8. vyāptervyāpyavyāpakobhayadharmatvam |
body.translated_text: 8. <s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion) has the character of being a property of both the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) and the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>).
