children.text: ) yatra dharmiṇi vyāpyamasti tatra sarvatra bhāva eva vyāpakasya svagato dharmo vyāptiḥ | tata[śca vyāpyabhāvāpekṣayā vyāpyasyaiva vyāptatāpratītiḥ] | na tvevamavadhāryate | vyāpakasyaiva tatra bhāva iti | hetvabhāvaprasaṅgādavyāpakasyāpi mūrtatvādestatra bhāvāt | nāpi ‘tatraive'ti prayatnānantarīyakatvāderahetutāpatteḥ | sādhāraṇaśca hetuḥ syāt | nityatvasya prameyeṣveva bhāvāt | yadā tu vyāpyadharmatā(rmatayā) vivakṣā vyāptestadā vyāpyasya vā gamakasya tatraiva vyāpake gamye sati | ytatra dharmiṇi vyāpako 'sti tatraiva bhāvo, na tadabhāve 'pi vyāptiriti | atrāpi vyāpyasyaiva tatra bhāva ityavadhāraṇaṃ hetvabhāvaprasaktereva nāśritam, avyāpyasyāpi tatra bhāvāt | nāpi vyāpyasya tatra bhāva eveti sapakṣaikadeśavṛtterahetutvaprāpteḥ | sādhāraṇasya [ca] hetutvaṃ syāt | prameyatvasya nityeṣvavaśyaṃbhāvāditi | vyāpyavyāpakadharmatāsaṃvarṇanaṃ tu vyāpterubhayatra tulyadharmatayaikākārā pratītiḥ saṃyogivat mā bhūditi pradarśanārtham | tathā hi- pūrvatrāyogavyavacchedenāvadhāraṇam uttaratrānyayogavyavacchedeneti kuta ubhayatraikākāratā vyāpteḥ? | taduktam-
children.translated_text: ) Where the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) exists in a property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>), there in every case the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) certainly exists — this inherent property is <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). And thus, [the cognition of pervasion belongs to the pervaded alone, in dependence on the existence of the pervaded]. But it is not determined in this way — that only the pervader exists there — because there would be the absurd consequence of the absence of the reason (<s>hetu</s>), since even what is not a pervader, such as corporeality (<s>mūrtatva</s>), also exists there. Nor [is it determined] as 'only there,' because there would be the absurd consequence that things like being immediately preceded by effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) would not be a reason. And the reason would be common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>), because permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) exists only among knowable things (<s>prameya</s>). But when the intention is that <s>vyāpti</s> is a property of the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>), then the pervaded, which is the means of cognition (<s>gamaka</s>), exists only there — in the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>), which is the object to be cognized (<s>gamya</s>). Where the pervader exists in a property-possessor, only there does [the pervaded] exist, and pervasion does not hold even in the absence of that [pervader]. Here too, the restriction 'only there does the pervaded exist' is not relied upon, due to the very absurd consequence of the absence of the reason, since even what is not pervaded also exists there. Nor [is it restricted as] 'the pervaded exists only there,' because there would be the absurd consequence that what occurs in only a part of the similar cases (<s>sapakṣaikadeśavṛtti</s>) would not be a reason. And a common [reason] (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) would become a [valid] reason, because knowability (<s>prameyatva</s>) necessarily exists among permanent things. The description in terms of the properties of pervaded and pervader is, however, for the purpose of showing that the cognition of pervasion should not have a single form equally in both [directions], like a conjoined thing (<s>saṃyogin</s>). For thus — in the former case the restriction is through exclusion of non-connection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>), in the latter through exclusion of alternative connection (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>) — so how could the pervasion have a single form in both cases? As has been stated —

body.translated_text: The <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) of that existing <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis) — is cognized [through the property of being both the pervaded and the pervader]. When it is intended as a property of the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>), then it belongs to the pervader, which is the object to be inferred (<s>gamya</s>). Here, the seventh case ending (<s>saptamī</s>) has the primary sense of the object, not the sense of a locus, because properties [do not have further] properties. Thus the meaning is — (

body.text:
"liṅge liṅgī bhavatyeva liṅginyevetarat punaḥ |
niyamasya viparyāse 'sambandho liṅgaliṅginoḥ ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "The mark (<s>liṅga</s>) certainly exists in what possesses the mark (<s>liṅgin</s>), and what possesses the mark certainly has the other [i.e., the mark]; but if the restriction is reversed, the connection between mark and mark-possessor is lost."

body.text: etenācāryeṇa saṃyogabalāt gamakatve yo doṣa uktaḥ-
body.translated_text: By this, the defect stated by the master (<s>ācārya</s>) [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] regarding the capacity to indicate through the force of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) —

body.text:
"na ca kenacidaṃśena na saṃyogī hutāśanaḥ |
dhūmo vā sarvathā tena prāptaṃ dhūmāt prakāśanam ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "Fire is not in no respect conjoined [with smoke], nor is smoke in every respect [conjoined with fire]; therefore, the inference of illumination from smoke would follow."

body.text: sa iha nāvataratītyākhyātaṃ bhavati | tathā hi- saṃyogasya ubhayatrāviśeṣāt eṣa prasaṅgo na tu vyāpteḥ | na hi yādṛśī (

children.text: ) vyāpakadharma vyāptiḥ tādṛśyeva vyāpyadharma iti | tathā cāha-
children.translated_text: ) is not the same as the <s>vyāpti</s> that is a property of the pervaded. And thus he says —

body.translated_text: It is declared that this [defect] does not arise here. For thus — since conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is indiscriminate in both [directions], this absurd consequence follows; but not so with <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). For the <s>vyāpti</s> that is a property of the pervader (

body.text:
"sambandho yadyapi dviṣṭhaḥ sahabhāvyaṅgaliṅginoḥ |
ādhārādheyavad vṛttistasya saṃyogivanna tu ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "Although the relation subsists in both [terms] — the co-existent and the mark-possessor — its operation is like that of container and contained, not like that of a conjoined thing."

body.text: tena vyāpako vyāpyo na bhavati vyāpyaśca [na] vyāpaka iti | "tadaṃśena vyāpto hetuḥ" iti vacanāt na saṃyogipakṣokto doṣaḥ | nāpyubhayorgamyagamakatāprasaṅgaḥ, yathoktād hetulakṣaṇād vyāpakasyaiva gamyatvapratīteḥ, vyāpyasyaiva gamakatāsampratyayāditi |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>) is not the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>), and the pervaded is [not] the pervader. Because of the statement "the reason is pervaded by that portion (<s>tadaṃśa</s>)," the defect stated under the conjunction view does not apply. Nor is there the absurd consequence that both would be the object of inference (<s>gamya</s>) and the means of inference (<s>gamaka</s>), because from the definition of reason as stated, only the pervader is cognized as the object of inference, and only the pervaded is understood as the means of inference.

body.text: 9. vyāpteranvayavyatirekarūpayossūcanam |
body.translated_text: 9. Indication that <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) has the forms of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

body.text: yadi tarhi "pakṣadharmastadaṃśena vyāptaḥ" ityetaddhetulakṣaṇaṃ tataḥ pakṣadharmatvaṃ tadaṃśavyāptiśceti dvirūpo hetuḥ syāt, anyatra ca trirūpa uktaḥ tat kathaṃ na vyāghātaḥ? ityāha "etena" tadaṃśavyāptivacanena "anvayo vyatireko vā uktaḥ" veditavya iti sambandhaḥ | anvayavyatirekarūpatvād vyāpteriti bhāvaḥ | tathā hi- ya eva yenānvito yannivṛttau ca nivartate sa eva tene vyāpta ucyate iti tadātmakatvād vyāptervyāptivacanenānvayavyatirekābhidhānam | tato vyāptivacanena rūpadvayābhidhānāt na vyāghāta iti |
body.translated_text: If indeed "the <s>pakṣadharma</s> (property of the thesis) pervaded by that portion" is the definition of a reason (<s>hetu</s>), then the reason would have two forms — being a property of the thesis and pervasion by that portion — while elsewhere it is stated as having three forms (<s>trirūpa</s>); so how is there no contradiction? To this he says: "by this" — by the statement of <s>tadaṃśavyāpti</s> (pervasion by that portion) — "positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) or negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is stated" — this is to be understood as the connection. The sense is: because <s>vyāpti</s> has the nature of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>. For thus — that which is positively concomitant with something and which ceases when that ceases, that alone is said to be pervaded by it — and since <s>vyāpti</s> is identical with this, the statement of pervasion is a statement of both <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>. Therefore, since the statement of pervasion expresses both forms, there is no contradiction.

body.text: 10. vyāpteḥ pratyakṣeṇānumānena vā niścayaḥ |
body.translated_text: 10. <s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is ascertained by perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) or by inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

body.text: tau ca jñapakahetvadhikārāt niścitau | "niścayaśca tayornaikenaiva pramāṇena api tu yathāsvam |" yasya yad ātmīyaṃ pramāṇaṃ niścāyakaṃ tena | yasya ca yat niścāyakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tad uttaratra vakṣyati |
body.translated_text: And these two [<s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>] are ascertained, since we are in the section dealing with the indicative reason (<s>jñāpakahetu</s>). "And the ascertainment of these two is not by a single means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) alone, but rather by the appropriate one for each." Whichever has its own appropriate means of valid cognition that ascertains it, by that [it is ascertained]. And which has which ascertaining means of valid cognition — that will be stated later.

body.text: "anvayo vyatirako vā" iti tulyakakṣatāsūcanārtho ‘vāśabdaḥ | tena sādharmyavaidharmyavatoḥ prayogayorekenaiva dvitīyagatervidhipratiṣedharūpatayā vyāvṛttibhede 'pi paramārthatastādātmyāt nobhayopadarśanamiti sūcitaṃ bhavati | vyatireko hi sādhyanivṛttau liṅgasya nivṛttidharmakatvaṃ svabhāvabhūto dharma ityanvayarūpatā vastuto 'sya na virudhyate | "pakṣadharmaśca" | kiṃ? | "yathāsvaṃ pramāṇena niścitaḥ" (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 20

children.text: ) ukta iti sambandhaḥ | niścayaprasaṅgena so 'pyatra pratipādyate, niścitasya gamakatvāmākhyātum | .................................................................................... iti pradarśanārtho ‘vāśabdaḥ | "pratyakṣeṇa ca svayaṃ svalakṣaṇākāratve 'pyanantarasāmānyavikalpajananāt prasiddhiḥ" upacārato niścaya ucyate- pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasyānadhigatārthādhigantṛtvābhāvaṃ darśayituṃ | tena yadyapi sāmānyarūpaṃ liṅgamavasthāpyate tathāpi svalakṣaṇapratītireva tadvyavasthānibandhanamiti pratyakṣataḥ pakṣadharmasya sādhyadharmiṇi prasiddhirucyate | etaccānantarameva vyaktīkariṣyate | "anumānato vā sādhyadharmiṇi pakṣadharmasya prasiddhi" rniścayaḥ | pramāṇaphalabhedācca "anumānataḥ" anumānena niścaya iti āha | "atrodāharaṇe" yathākramaṃ "yathā pradeśe dhūmasya" dhūmasāmānyasya pratyakṣato niścayaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: ) — this is the stated connection. By occasion of [discussing] ascertainment, that too is explained here, in order to declare the indicative capacity of what has been ascertained. ........................................................................... The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) is for the purpose of illustration. "And through perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), although it has the form of a particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) by its own nature, it generates the immediately subsequent universal concept (<s>sāmānyavikalpa</s>), [hence] it is well-known" — the ascertainment is spoken of figuratively (<s>upacāra</s>) — to show that the conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) that arises subsequent to perception does not cognize a previously uncognized object. Therefore, although the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is established in its universal form (<s>sāmānyarūpa</s>), nevertheless it is the perception of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) alone that is the basis for that establishment — thus the well-known status (<s>prasiddhi</s>) of the <s>pakṣadharma</s> in the subject to be proved (<s>sādhyadharmin</s>) is said to be from perception. And this will be clarified immediately after. "Or from inference (<s>anumāna</s>), the well-known status" — i.e., the ascertainment — "of the <s>pakṣadharma</s> in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s>." And due to the distinction between the means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and its result (<s>phala</s>), he says "from inference" meaning 'by inference.' "Here, as examples" — respectively — "such as the [ascertainment] of smoke in a location" — the ascertainment of smoke-in-general through perception.

body.translated_text: The word 'or' (<s>vā</s>) in "positive concomitance or negative concomitance" is for the purpose of indicating their equal status. By this it is indicated that, of the two formulations involving similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), through one alone the other is reached, and although there is a difference in the mode of exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) as having the form of positive rule (<s>vidhi</s>) and negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>), in ultimate reality, due to their identity, it is not necessary to demonstrate both. For negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) — the property of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) ceasing upon the cessation of the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) — is an inherent property, and thus its nature as positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is not in actual conflict with it. "And the property of the thesis (<s>pakṣadharma</s>)" — what about it? — "is ascertained by the appropriate means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>)" (

body.text: 11. uddayotakaramataṃ nirasya deśādyapekṣakāryahetorgamakatvoktiḥ |
body.translated_text: 11. Having refuted the view of <s>Uddyotakara</s>, a statement of the indicative capacity of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) depending on location etc.

body.text: yastu manyate- ‘yaḥ pradeśo 'gnisambandhī so 'pratyakṣo yastu pratyakṣo nabhobhāgarūpa ālokādyātmā dhūmavattayā dṛśyamāno na so 'gnimān ataḥ kathaṃ pradeśe dhūmasya pratyakṣataḥ prasiddhiḥ | tasmād dhūma eva dharmī yuktaḥ | sāgnirayaṃ dhūmaḥ dhūmatvāt ityevaṃ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ'; iti- tasyāpi sāgneḥ dhūmāvayavasyāpratyakṣatvāt, paridṛśyamānasya corddhavabhāgavartino 'gninā sahāvṛtteḥ, kathaṃ dhūmasāmānyasya sādhyadharmiṇi pratyakṣataḥ prasiddhiḥ? | dhūmāvayavī pratyakṣa iti cet; na, avayavavyatirekeṇa tasyābhāvāt | lokādhyavasāyatastasyaikatve vā pradeśasyāpi tāvataḥ (

children.text: ) kalpitamekatvaṃ na nivāryate | pradeśe eva ca loko 'gni pratipadyate, na dhūme | deśakālādyapekṣayaiva ca kāryaheturgamakaḥ | yadāha-
children.translated_text: ) constructed unity of the location also cannot be denied. And it is in the location that the world cognizes fire, not in smoke. And the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) is indicative only with reference to location, time, etc. As he says —

body.translated_text: But one who thinks — 'The location that is connected with fire is imperceptible, while what is perceptible, being of the nature of a portion of the sky, of the nature of light, etc., being seen as possessing smoke, is not possessed of fire; so how is there the well-known status of smoke in a location through perception? Therefore, smoke alone is the proper property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>). This smoke possesses fire, because of its smoke-nature — thus should be the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof' — even for him, since the portion of smoke that is with fire is imperceptible, and since the upper portion that is seen does not co-occur with fire, how can there be the well-known status of smoke-in-general in the subject to be proved through perception? If [one says] the smoke-whole (<s>dhūmāvayavin</s>) is perceptible — no, because in the absence of the parts, that [whole] does not exist. Or, if its unity is [accepted] based on common worldly understanding, then the likewise (

children.translated_text: "Even with regard to a contrary effect, dependence on location, time, etc. is accepted;
otherwise [the reason] would be deviating — like ashes being a means of proving [the existence of] heat."

body.text: iti |

children.translated_text: "Therefore, with regard to proving fire dependent on location etc., through [the location's] being apprehended as possessing smoke,
the status of the location as the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) is not contradicted."

body.text:
yathā balākāvato vṛkṣāderddeśādyapekṣayā jalasādhanatvamiti |
"śabde vā kṛtakatvasya" pratyayabhedabhiditvādinānumāneneti |
body.translated_text: Just as, from a location possessing herons, trees, etc., with reference to location etc., there is the capacity to prove [the existence of] water. "Or, of produced-ness (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) in the case of sound" — through inference, by means of the diversity of cognitions etc.

body.text: 12. nirvikalpaṃ kathaṃ sāmānyagrāhīti kumārilākṣepasyottaram |
body.translated_text: 12. <s>Kumārila</s>'s objection — how can <s>nirvikalpa</s> (non-conceptual perception) grasp universals — and the reply to it.

body.text: atra yathopavarṇitaṃ pratyakṣataḥ pakṣadharmasya sādhyadharmiṇi prasiddhāvabhiprāyamapratipadyamānaḥ kumārilaḥ- ‘kathaṃ pratyakṣeṇa(ṇā)vikalpena sāmānyātmano liṅgasya dhūmādeḥ svarūpagra[haṇa]mapi tāvad yujyate, dharmiṇo vā kuta eva tatsambandhagrahaṇam'- iti pratyavatasthe | tena hi "pratyakṣapūrvakatvāccānumānāderddharmaṃ pratyanimittatvam" ityetad bhāṣyam-
body.translated_text: Here, not understanding the intended meaning regarding the well-known status of the <s>pakṣadharma</s> in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> through perception as described above, <s>Kumārila</s> objected: 'How can perception, being non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>), even grasp the essential nature of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) such as smoke, which is of the nature of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>)? And even less so [can it grasp] the connection of that with the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>).' For he, [citing] the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) that "because inference etc. are preceded by perception, there is no uncaused [cognition] with respect to a property" —

children.translated_text: "How can inference etc. be preceded by perception,
when the non-conceptual sensory cognition is incapable of producing memory?

body.text: na cāvikalpyaliṅgasya dharmisambandhayostathā |
body.translated_text: And there is no apprehension of the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), which is not conceptualized, nor likewise of the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) and their connection,

body.text: gṛhītiḥ"
body.translated_text: " [thus] having raised the objection —

body.text: ityākṣipya-

children.translated_text: "As for the [alleged] non-apprehension by perception of the mark etc. due to its being non-conceptual,
that is not accepted [by us], since even conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is beneficial to the real nature of objects.
There is first a perceptual cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) that is non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>),
similar to the cognition of infants, mutes, etc., arising from the pure object alone.
Then subsequently, the cognition by which the object is determined
through properties such as universal class (<s>jāti</s>) etc. — that too is accepted as being perceptual."

body.text: iti bruvatā- ‘saugatānāmevāyaṃ liṅgadharmitatsambandhāgrahaṇalakṣaṇo doṣo yeṣāmavikalpakameva pratyakṣaṃ, nāsmākaṃ savikalpamapi pratyakṣamicchatām'; ityuktaṃ bhavati | tatastadupavarṇitadoṣapratividhānāyāha- "sadhūmaṃ hi" ityādi | ayamatra samudāyārthaḥ- pratyakṣaṃ hi purovasthitamauttarādharyeṇa dhūmapradeśādikaṃ vidhirūpeṇa dhūmādisvalakṣaṇaṃ sakalasajātīyavijātīyavyāvṛttaṃ ca svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ sarvāsāmarthamātrāṇāṃ parasparamasaṃkīrṇarūpatvāt tatsāmarthyabhāviyathāsthānamanukurvatpāścāttyavidhipratiṣedhavikalpadvayaṃ janayati yena dhūmapradeśākhyau dharmadharmiṇau tayoścauttarādharyam ‘evametat nānyathā iti vikalpayati | yathānubhavamabhyāsapāṭavādipratyayāntarasahakāriṇāṃ vikalpānāmudayāt | tato dharmadharmiṇoḥ svarūpaniścayaḥ sambandhaniścayaśca pratyakṣanibandhanaḥ sampadyate | tathā hi- ayameva dhūmapradeśayoḥ sambandhasya niścayo yaḥ ‘atrāyam'; ityadhyavasāyaḥ | sa cāvikalpenāpi pratyakṣeṇa yathoktena prakāreṇa sampādita eva | na cauttarādharyāvasthitād vastudvayādanya eva kaścidādhā[rādhe]yabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ yataḥ tasya pratyakṣeṇānanubhūtatvāt paścāda(d) vikalpanaṃ syāt | vastubhūtasya tasyānyatra niṣedhāt | tasmādayaṃ tadeva tathāvasthitamarthadvayamāśritya kalpanāsamāropita eva | tena sambandhaḥ sambandhīti bhedāntarapratikṣepāpratikṣepābhyāṃ dharmadharmitayā vyavahāro loke na tu pāramārthikaḥ | sāmānyavyavahāro 'pi vijātīyavyāvṛttāneva bhāvānāsṛ(śri)tya kalpanāsamāropita eva pratanyate | teṣāmeva bhinnānāmapyanubhavadvāreṇa vijātīyavyāvṛttatayā prakṛtyaivaikākāraparāmarśapratyayahetutvāt | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: By saying thus — 'This defect of not apprehending the relation between the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) belongs only to the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>), for whom perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is exclusively non-conceptual (<s>avikalpaka</s>), not to us who accept conceptual perception (<s>savikalpaka pratyakṣa</s>) as well' — this is what is stated. Therefore, to address that objection, he says "<s>sadhūmam</s> (smoke-possessing)" and so forth. Here the composite meaning is as follows: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), directly apprehending the smoke and place etc. situated before one in a vertical relation, generates — through its capacity, in accordance with each thing's position — the subsequent pair of conceptual cognitions (<s>vikalpa</s>), namely positive determination (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>) and negative determination (<s>pratiṣedhavikalpa</s>), which grasps the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of smoke etc. in its positive form and as excluded from all homogeneous and heterogeneous things, since all things, being established in their own natures, have mutually unmixed forms. By this, one conceptualizes the property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) called smoke and place, and their vertical relation, as 'it is exactly thus and not otherwise.' This is because conceptual cognitions arise in accordance with experience, assisted by other conditions such as proficiency through repeated practice. From this, the ascertainment of the intrinsic nature of property and property-bearer, and the ascertainment of their relation, are accomplished on the basis of perception. For indeed, the ascertainment of the relation of smoke and place is precisely the determination 'this is here.' And that has already been accomplished by perception, even though non-conceptual, in the manner described. There is no relation characterized by the supported-supporter relationship that is anything other than the two real entities situated in vertical relation, because since that has not been experienced by perception, its subsequent conceptualization would be impossible. Because such a real entity [as a separate relation] is negated elsewhere. Therefore, this [relation] is merely a conceptual superimposition (<s>kalpanāsamāropita</s>) based on that very pair of objects situated in that manner. Hence, the distinction of property and property-bearer through the acceptance and non-acceptance of other distinctions in relation (<s>sambandha</s>) and relata (<s>sambandhin</s>) is a conventional usage in the world, not ultimately real. The convention of universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) too is a mere conceptual superimposition operating based on things that are excluded from heterogeneous things (<s>vijātīyavyāvṛtta</s>). For those very things, though different, through the channel of experience, by their very nature of being excluded from heterogeneous things, serve as causes of a cognition that apprehends them under a single form. And thus he says —

children.translated_text: "Certain things, though different, are determined by their own nature, like sense faculties and the like,
to accomplish a single purpose, based on the cognition whose object is a single reflective apprehension (<s>ekapratyavamarśa</s>)."

body.text: tataḥ sāmānyavi[kalpajananadvārā] tatpratibhāsino dhūmākārasya vijātīyavyāvṛ[ttarūpasya sāmānyarūpatayā] pratyakṣeṇaiva gṛhītatvāt | na hi vijātīyavyāvṛttirvyāvṛttādanyaiva kācid yasyāḥ pratyakṣeṇāgrahaṇaṃ syāt | tasmād yathāparidṛṣṭaṃ dhūmādisvalakṣaṇamevānyato vyāvṛ[ttātmanā vi]kalpyata iti pratipatradhyavasāyavaśāt smṛtireva | dvividho vikalpaḥ pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvī vastutaḥ punarnirviṣaya eva | tato yadāha- sāmānyasyānanubhūtatayā-
body.translated_text: Therefore, since the smoke-form that appears in the universal-cognition (<s>sāmānyavikalpa</s>), having the nature of exclusion from heterogeneous things (<s>vijātīyavyāvṛtti</s>) and thus the form of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), has already been grasped by perception itself — for exclusion from heterogeneous things is nothing other than what is excluded, such that there could be non-apprehension of it by perception — therefore, the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of smoke etc., just as it was perceived, is what is conceptualized as excluded from others (<s>anyato vyāvṛtta</s>), and hence, by the determination of the cognizer, it is merely memory (<s>smṛti</s>). Conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is of two kinds: that which arises subsequent to perception (<s>pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvin</s>), and that which is in reality entirely without an object. Therefore, when it is said — since the universal has not been experienced —

children.translated_text: "Whoever would say that this cognition of non-difference is a memory (<s>smārta</s>),
for him there must surely be the capacity to remember even the son of a barren woman!"

body.text: iti tadapyapāstamiti ||
body.translated_text: — that too is refuted.

body.text: 13. anumiteḥ sāmānyaviṣayatve 'navastheti kumārilākṣepasyottaram |
body.translated_text: 13. Response to <s>Kumārila</s>'s objection of infinite regress if inference has universals as its objects.

body.text: athavāparaṃ kumārilenābhihitam- "svalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ pratyakṣaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayamanumānam" iti vacanāt dhūmādisāmānyamanumānagrāhyameva | tatra cānavasthā liṅgagrāhiṇo 'pyanumānasya tadanyaliṅgabalenotpatteḥ | tasya ca sāmānyarūpatayā tadanyānumānamānaviṣayatvāt tathā tadanyasyāpīti kasyacidekasyāpi liṅginaḥ pratipattiḥ yugasahasrairapi na sambhavati | kimaṅga punarekena puruṣāyuṣkeṇeti | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, another point raised by <s>Kumārila</s>: From the statement 'perception has particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object, inference has universals (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object,' the universal of smoke etc. is grasped only by inference. And in that case there is an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>), because even the inference that grasps the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) arises through the force of another logical mark; and since that too, being of the nature of a universal, is the object of yet another inference, and so on for that other one as well — the cognition of even a single property-possessor (<s>liṅgin</s>) is not possible even in thousands of world-ages, let alone within a single human lifespan. And thus he says —

children.translated_text: "The universal cannot be cognized without inference,
and inference does not operate without a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>).
No one accepts that a non-universal can serve as a logical mark,
and no logical mark that is not apprehended can illuminate anything.
The cognition of that [mark] too must come through another inference,
and its arising must come from a logical mark accompanied by universal-cognition.
That too has the nature of inference, and its arising is from a logical mark,
which in turn must be known through yet another inference — thus in this construction,
because of the infinity of logical marks, property-possessors, and inferences, even with respect to a single property-possessor,
cognition is not attained even in thousands of world-ages."

body.text: ityāśaṅkayāha "sadhūmaṃ hi" ityādi | evaṃ manyate | yasyānumānantareṇa sāmānyaṃ na pratīyate bhavatu tasyāyaṃ doṣaḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 24

children.text: ) asmākaṃ tu pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvināpi vikalpena prakṛtivibhramāt sāmānyaṃ pratīyate | liṅgavikalpasya ca svalakṣaṇadarśanāśrayatvāt paramparayā vastupratibandhādavisaṃvādakatvam, maṇiprabhāyāmiva maṇibhrānteḥ | kāryahetutvamapi vikalpāvabhāsino dhūmasāmānyasya liṅgatayāvasthāpyamānasya kāryadarśanāśrayatayā tadadhyavasāyācca | na hi dhūmasvalakṣaṇasya liṅgatāvasthāpayituṃ yuktā, tasyāsādhāraṇasya sapakṣe vṛttyabhāvāt, tadaṃśavyāptyayogāt, sādhyasādhanasaṃkalpe vastudarśanāsambhavācceti |
children.translated_text: ) But for us, the universal is cognized even by a conceptual cognition that arises subsequent to perception (<s>pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvin vikalpa</s>), through a natural error (<s>prakṛtivibhrama</s>). And since the inferential conceptual cognition of the logical mark is grounded in the perception of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇadarśana</s>), it is non-deceptive (<s>avisaṃvādaka</s>) through indirect connection with reality — like the error regarding a jewel in the luster of a jewel. The property of being an effect (<s>kāryahetutva</s>) also [belongs to it], because the smoke-universal appearing in the conceptual cognition, when established as a logical mark, is grounded in the perception of the effect and through the determination of that. For it is not proper to establish the particular of smoke as the logical mark, since being unique (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), it has no occurrence in the similar cases (<s>sapakṣa</s>), because there is no possibility of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of its parts, and because perception of both the probandum and probans together is impossible.

body.translated_text: To this objection he says "<s>sadhūmam</s> (smoke-possessing)" and so forth. He thinks thus: Let this defect belong to one for whom the universal is not cognized without another inference. (

body.text: yattūktam ‘sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣamanumānam‘ iti tatra naivamavadhāryate- sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayamanumānameveti | pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasyāpi tadviṣayatvāt tadanyasya ca vikalpasya | kintu sāmānyalakṣaṇaviṣayamevānumānamityavadhāryate svalakṣaṇaviṣayatvaniṣedhārthamiti | tatra saha dhūmena vartata iti "sadhūmaḥ" | pakṣadharmatāpratipadanārthamevamuktam | vidhivikalpasya caitadeva bījam | taṃ "sadhūmaṃ pradeśaṃ dṛṣṭavataḥ" pratyakṣeṇeti sambandhaḥ | kīdṛśam "arthāntaraviviktarūpam" arthāntaraiḥ sajātīyavijātīyairviviktamasaṅkīrṇaṃ rūpamasyeti vigrahaḥ | sarvabhāvānāṃ svasvabhāvavyavasthiteḥ svabhāvasāṅkaryābhāvāt | anyathā sarvasya sarvatropayogādatiprasaṅgaḥ | anena pratiṣedhavikalpasya nimittamākhyātam, sāmānyotprekṣāyāśca bījam | taduktam-
body.translated_text: As for what was said — 'inference has universals as its object' — this should not be understood as meaning that inference alone has universals as its object, since universals are also the objects of conceptual cognitions arising subsequent to perception, and of other conceptual cognitions as well. Rather, it should be understood as 'inference has exclusively universals as its object,' with the purpose of negating that it has particulars as its object. In that [root text], 'existing together with smoke' means <s>sadhūma</s>. This is stated to indicate the establishment of the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>). And this itself is the seed of the positive determination (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>). "Having seen the smoke-possessing place" — the connection is 'by perception.' Of what kind? "Having a form distinct from other things" — the compound means: whose form is distinct, i.e. unmixed, from other things both homogeneous and heterogeneous. Because all entities are established in their own natures, there is no confusion of natures; otherwise, since everything would be useful for everything, there would be over-extension. By this, the cause of the negative determination (<s>pratiṣedhavikalpa</s>) is indicated, as well as the seed of the supposition of universals (<s>sāmānyotprekṣā</s>). Thus it is said —

body.text: "itaretarabhedo 'ntya(sya) bījaṃ saṃjñā yadarthikā" iti |
body.translated_text: "The mutual difference of the latter is the seed; the designation is for that purpose."

body.text: tathā hi- arthāntaravyāvṛttiṃ parasparavyāvṛttānāmapi samānāmutpaśyato bhinnameṣāṃ rūpaṃ tirodhāyābhinnaṃ svabhāvamāropayantī kalpanotpadyate | "asādhāraṇātmanā" iti arthāntaravyāvṛttena svabhāvena | na tu yathā kumārilo manyate- ‘arthāntaraviveko 'bhāvapramāṇagrāhyo na pratyakṣāvaseyaḥ'; iti | nahi vastubalabhāvinā pratyakṣeṇa anyathādarśanasambhavo bhrāntatāprasaṅgāt | tenātmanā (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 25

children.text: ) dṛṣṭavataḥ sataḥ puṃso 'nantaraṃ "smārtaṃ liṅgajñānamutpadyate" iti sambandhaḥ | smṛtireva "smārtam" | liṅgapratibhāsi jñānaṃ "liṅgajñānam" | anena pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvini vikalpe yatsāmānyamābhāti tasya līṅgavyavasthāmāha |
children.translated_text: ) of the person who has seen [things thus], subsequently "a memory-based inferential cognition (<s>smārta liṅgajñāna</s>) arises" — this is the syntactic connection. Memory itself is what is meant by "memory-based" (<s>smārta</s>). A cognition in which the logical mark appears is called "inferential cognition" (<s>liṅgajñāna</s>). By this, he states the establishment of what appears as a universal in the conceptual cognition arising subsequent to perception as the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>).

body.translated_text: For indeed — when one perceives the exclusion from heterogeneous things even among things that are mutually different yet similar, a conceptual cognition arises that, concealing their different forms, superimposes a non-different nature upon them. "With a unique nature (<s>asādhāraṇātman</s>)" means with a nature that is excluded from other things. But not as <s>Kumārila</s> holds — 'the distinction from other things is grasped by the means of knowledge of absence (<s>abhāvapramāṇa</s>), not ascertainable by perception.' For it is impossible for perception, which arises from the force of the real object, to see things otherwise, since that would entail its being erroneous. With that nature, (

What is its object in the ultimate sense? "Having as its ultimate object the difference as perceived (<s>yathādṛṣṭabhedaparamārthaviṣayam</s>)".............................................................................

body.text: 14. darśanavidhipratiṣedhavikalpeṣu prāmāṇyāprāmāṇyavyavasthā |
body.translated_text: 14. The determination of validity and invalidity among perception (<s>darśana</s>), positive determination (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>), and negative determination (<s>pratiṣedhavikalpa</s>).

body.text: da
body.translated_text: He begins the investigation of which among perception, positive determination, and negative determination are valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) and which are not. "Among those" — among perception, positive determination, and negative determination. The first of those, which is —

body.text: rśanavidhipratiṣedhavikalpānāṃ pramāṇāpramāṇacintāmārabhate | "tatra" teṣu darśanavidhipratiṣedhavikalpeṣu | tadādyaṃ yadetat-
"asti hyālocanājñānaṃ prathamam-" iti
body.translated_text: "There is first the apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) —" thus,

body.text: ādau vikalpapravṛtterbhavamiti "ādyam" ākhyātam "asādhāraṇaviṣayam" svalakṣaṇaviṣayaṃ darśanaṃ tad "eva" pramāṇaṃ na vidhipratiṣedhavikalpāvapi | tasyaiva pramāṇalakṣaṇayogāditarayośca tadasambhavāt | tathā hi- anadhigataviṣayatvamarthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatvaṃ ca pramāṇalakṣaṇam | tad darśanasyaivāsti |
body.translated_text: what is designated as "first," being prior to the operation of conceptual cognition, and "having a unique object" — i.e., having the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) as its object — that perception (<s>darśana</s>) alone is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), not the positive and negative determinations. Because only perception possesses the defining characteristics of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, while the other two lack them. For the defining characteristics of a <s>pramāṇa</s> are: having a previously unapprehended object, and having an object that is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsādhana</s>). Only perception has these.

body.text: tatra "ādyam" ityapūrvārthavijñānatvamākhyātam "asādhāraṇaviṣayam" iti arthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatvam | svalakṣaṇasyaivārthakriyāsādhanatvāt |
body.translated_text: There, "first" indicates its nature as a cognition of a novel object; "having a unique object" indicates its having an object capable of causal efficacy — because only the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) is capable of causal efficacy.

body.text: 15. pratiṣedhavikalpasyāprāmāṇyasthāpanam |
body.translated_text: 15. Establishing the invalidity of the negative determination (<s>pratiṣedhavikalpa</s>).

body.text: tatra pratiṣedhavikalpasya tāvat pratyakṣagṛhītārthaviṣayatayā smṛtitvaṃ pratipādayannāha- "tasmin" asādhāraṇe "tathābhūte" arthāntarairasaṅkīrṇarūpe "darśanena" asaṅkīrṇarūpasāmarthyabhāvinā "dṛṣṭe" adhigate "sati" | tathā hi- vyatiriktamapi bhāvāṃśādabhāvāṃśamicchatā bhāvāṃśaḥ svabhāvenāsaṅkīrṇarūpaḥ kalpanīyaḥ, anyathā sa evābhāvāṃśo na sidhyet | na ca svabhāvenāsaṅkīrṇarūpatāyāmasatyāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 26

children.text: ) pṛthagbhūtābhāvāṃśasadbhāve 'pi sā yuktimatī, svahetubalāyātasya saṅkīrṇarūpasyākiñcitkarābhāvāṃśasambhave 'pi tyāgāyogāt | na ca tenaiva tadvināśanam, vināśahetvayogasya pratipādayiṣyamāṇatvāt | tena saṅkīrṇarūpavināśane ca varaṃ svahetoreva svabhāvato 'saṅkīrṇarūpāṇāmudayo 'stu kiṃ parivrāḍmodakanyāyopagamena? | tasmāt svabhāvata eva bhāvānāṃ pararūpavikalatvamabhāvāṃśaḥ nānyaḥ | sa ca tathābhūto darśanena gṛhīta eva | tasmiṃstathābhūte dṛṣṭe "sa" padārtho "yena" vastunā "asādhāraṇaḥ" samānasvabhāvo na bhavati tadrūpavikalasvabhāvatvāt "tadasādhāraṇatāṃ" tena tenātadrūpeṇāsamānasvabhāvatāṃ etadeva vyanakti | "tataḥ" arthāntarād "bhedaṃ" vailakṣaṇyamanyarūpamidaṃ na bhavatīti "abhilapantī" abhimukhayantī dṛṣṭavailakṣaṇye pravartamānatayā "smṛtirutpannā pratyakṣabalena" | yadi tu liṅgabalenotpadyeta vyavacchedaviṣayāpi smṛtirna syāditi bhāvaḥ | kiṃ viṣayā? | "atadvyāvṛttiviṣayā |" tacchabdena darśanaviṣayasya vastunaḥ parāmarśaḥ kṛtaḥ | na tat atat vijātīyam | atasmād vyāvṛttiḥ atavdyāvṛttiḥ | sā viṣayo yasyāḥ sā tathā | athādṛṣṭa evārthāntarebhyo bhedo mayāpi kalpyate iti pratipatra (ttara) dhyavasāyāccaivamuktam | parāmarthato nirviṣayatvāt | sā "na pramāṇaṃ" nābhāvapramāṇaphalamityarthaḥ | na hi smṛtijanakatvena pramāṇatā yuktā | kasmāt na pramāṇam? | yathādṛṣṭasyākāro 'bhyāsapāṭavādipratyayāntarasāpekṣo viśeṣastasya grahaṇāt | na hi dṛṣṭimityeva vikalpena gṛhyate, darśanāviśeṣāt sarvākāreṣu vikalpodayaprasaṅgāt, api tu kaścidevābhyāsādipratyayāpekṣa ityākāragrahaṇenācaṣṭe |
children.translated_text: ) because one cannot abandon what has a mixed form arising from the force of its own cause, even though a causally inefficacious absence-aspect may be present in it. Nor can that [absence-aspect] destroy it, because the means of destruction will be explained later. And if the mixed form is to be destroyed, it is better that things of unmixed form arise from their own causes by their very nature — why resort to the logic of the renunciant and the sweetmeat? Therefore, the absence-aspect of entities is nothing other than the lack of the form of other things, which belongs to them by their very nature. And that, being of such a nature, has already been grasped by perception. When that of such a nature has been seen, "that" entity, "with which" thing it "is not of the same nature" (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) — because of having a nature lacking that form — "its dissimilarity with that" (<s>tadasādhāraṇatā</s>), i.e. its not being of the same nature as this or that which is of a different form — this is what he explains. "From that" — from other things — the difference, the distinctness — "declaring" (<s>abhilapantī</s>), i.e. bringing to the fore, that 'this is not of that form' — "memory arises by the force of perception" — operating with respect to the perceived distinctness. If it were to arise through the force of logical marks, then even the cognition having exclusion as its object would not be [mere] memory — this is the purport. What is its object? "Having as its object the exclusion from that" (<s>atadvyāvṛttiviṣayā</s>). By the word 'that,' reference is made to the object of perception, the real entity. What is not that is the heterogeneous. Exclusion from that which is not-that is <s>atadvyāvṛtti</s>. That which has this as its object is so described. Moreover, it is said thus because of the determination of the cognizer that 'even I conceptualize the difference from other things that was not [separately] perceived.' Ultimately, because it is without a [real] object. That "is not a valid means of knowledge" — meaning it is not the result of absence as a means of valid knowledge (<s>abhāvapramāṇaphala</s>). For it is not proper that being a cause of memory constitutes validity. Why is it not a valid means of knowledge? Because it grasps a particular aspect — a specialization dependent on other conditions such as proficiency through repeated practice — of the form as perceived. For it is not the case that everything perceived is conceptualized, since if there were no distinction in perception, conceptual cognition would arise with respect to all forms. Rather, [conceptual cognition] is dependent on conditions such as repeated practice — this is what is indicated by 'grasping of a [particular] form.'

body.translated_text: There, to demonstrate that the negative determination, having as its object what has already been apprehended by perception, is [merely] memory, he says: "When that" unique thing, "being of such a nature" — having a form unmixed with other things — "has been seen" — apprehended — "by perception" — which arises from the capacity of the unmixed form — "that being the case." For indeed, even one who accepts the absence-aspect as distinct from the existence-aspect of an entity must maintain that the existence-aspect is of unmixed form by its own nature; otherwise, the absence-aspect itself would not be established. And even when a separately existing absence-aspect is present, without the unmixed nature, it would not be reasonable, (

body.text: bhavatu yathādṛṣṭākāragrahaṇam | pramāṇaṃ tu kasmānna bhavatīti parasya taduktapramāṇalakṣaṇavirahaṃ darśayannāha- "prāg" (

children.text: ) ālocanājñānodayakāle "asādhāraṇam" assaṅkīrṇarūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā asādhāraṇamarthāntararūpaṃ na bhavatīti "abhilapataḥ" vikalpayataḥ "pratiṣedhavikalpasyāpūrvārthādhigamābhāvād" apūrvārthavijñānatāvirahāt | apūrvārthavijñānaṃ ca pramāṇaṃ bhavatocyata iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) — at the time of the arising of apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) — having seen the "unique" — of unmixed form — and then "declaring" — conceptualizing — that the unique thing does not have the form of other things, "the negative determination lacks the apprehension of a novel object" — because it lacks the nature of being a cognition of a previously unapprehended object. And a cognition of a previously unapprehended object is what is called a valid means of knowledge by you — this is the purport.

body.translated_text: Granted that there is grasping of the form as perceived. But why is it not a valid means of knowledge? To show that it lacks the defining characteristic of a valid means of knowledge as stated by the opponent, he says: "Prior to" (

body.text: 16. vidhivikalpasyāsyaprāmāṇyavyavasthāpanam |
body.translated_text: 16. Establishing the invalidity of the positive determination (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>).

body.text: yadyuktena prakāreṇa pratiṣedhavikalpo na pramāṇaṃ, vidhivikalpastarhi pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | nahi tasyāpūrvārthavijñānatvābhāvaḥ sambhavati | tatpratibhāsino 'nugatasya sāmānyākārasyāsādhāraṇarūpāvalambinā darśanenānadhigamāt tat kuto 'syāprāmāṇyam | taduktam-
body.translated_text: If, by the reasoning stated, the negative determination is not a valid means of knowledge, then the positive determination should be a valid means of knowledge. For it is not possible that it lacks the nature of being a cognition of a novel object, since the universal-form (<s>sāmānyākāra</s>) that appears in it, being a concomitant [of the particular], has not been apprehended by perception (<s>darśana</s>) which is grounded in the unique form (<s>asādhāraṇarūpa</s>). So whence comes its invalidity? Thus it is said —

body.text: "tataḥ paraṃ punarvastu"
body.translated_text: "Then again, the real entity —"

body.text: ityādi | tadetat kumarilavacanamāśaṅkya vidhivikalpasyāpi prāmāṇyamanupa(mapa)nudannāha- "arthakriyāsādhanasya" svalakṣaṇasya "ālocanājñānena darśanādadṛṣṭasya punastatsādhanasya" arthakriyāsādhanasya svabhāvasya "vikalpenāpratipatteḥ vidhivikalpo na pramāṇam" | yadyapi tenānadhigataṃ sāmānyamadhigamyata iti varṇyate tathāpi tad arthakriyāsādhanaṃ na bhavati iti tadadhigantā taimirikādijñānaprakhyo vidhivikalpo na pramāṇam |
body.translated_text: and so forth. Having raised this statement of <s>Kumārila</s> as an objection, while not refuting the validity of the positive determination (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>) either, he says — "Of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular), which is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsādhana</s>), by the apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) — perception (<s>darśana</s>) — having been seen, and of that which is again capable of causal efficacy, its own nature, not being apprehended by conceptual cognition, the positive determination is not a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)." Although it is described that the universal, which has not been apprehended by that [perception], is apprehended [by the positive determination], nevertheless since that is not capable of causal efficacy, the positive determination that apprehends it, resembling the cognition of one with an eye-disease etc., is not a valid means of knowledge.
