children.translated_text: ) — this is a dissimilarity example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>). Just as, even when the property-bearer called 'place' (<s>pradeśa</s>), which is capable of causal efficacy, has been apprehended by perception, the fire — which is capable of causal efficacy but has not been apprehended, being imperceptible and not in the form of a universal — cannot be cognized in the form of the particular, so too the positive determination does not apprehend what is capable of causal efficacy in the form of a universal when it has not been apprehended, since that has already been apprehended by the apprehensive cognition itself. Being thus, it is merely memory, and hence not a valid means of knowledge.

body.translated_text: is determined by a cognition" — thus it is said. There, by the phrase 'again the real entity,' it is stated that the very entity that is the object of non-conceptual perception (<s>nirvikalpaka pratyakṣa</s>), qualified by genus etc., is determined by conceptual cognition. And since that has already been apprehended by non-conceptual cognition itself, there is no validity [in the positive determination] with respect to it; and since genus, being incapable of causal efficacy, even when apprehended though previously unapprehended, has no validity — just like the cognition of hair-like floaters etc. For this very reason, since there is no contact of the sense faculties with a universal devoid of the capacity for causal efficacy, perceptual status too is impossible [for it]. By the particle 'ca,' a cumulation of the previously stated reason — namely, because it is memory — is indicated. Its nature as memory will be demonstrated further on. "Like inference" (

body.text: 17. arthakriyāsādhanaviṣayajñānasyaiva prāmāṇyasamarthanam |
body.translated_text: 17. Establishing that only cognition having a causally efficacious object is a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>).

body.text: "arthakriyāsādhanaviṣayameva pramāṇam" netaraditi kuta etat? iti cet "arthakriyārthī hi" puruṣo yasmāt hitāhitaprāptiparihārārthī "sarvo" na kākatālīyanyāyena kaścideva, "prekṣāvān" buddhipurvakārī "pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ vā" pramāṇādeva sarvadā pravarta(rte)ya apramāṇāt mā kadācit, vipralambhasambhavād, "ubhayamanveṣate" na vyasanitayā | tato 'yamarthakriyāsādhanaviṣayameva pramāṇaṃ bravīti, tasyārthakriyāsādhane pravṛttyaṅgatvāt | netarat, tadviparītatvāt | tathāhi- pramāṇamavisaṃvādakamapratārakamucyate loke 'pi | yaccārthakriyāsādhanamanadhigacchanna tatra pravartayati, kuta eva tat prāpayet tat kathamavisaṃvādakatayā prekṣāpūrvakārī pramāṇamācakṣīta? |
body.translated_text: "Only that which has a causally efficacious object is a valid means of knowledge" — and nothing else: whence is this? To this he replies: "For every" person, not just some one by the logic of the crow and the palm fruit, "who is purposeful" — who acts with deliberation — "seeks" both "a valid means of knowledge and an invalid one" — [seeking] always to proceed from valid knowledge alone and never from invalid knowledge, due to the possibility of being deceived — not out of compulsion. Therefore, he declares that only what has a causally efficacious object is a valid means of knowledge, since that is the basis for activity toward causal efficacy. Not the other, since it is the opposite of that. For thus — a <s>pramāṇa</s> is called non-deceptive and non-misleading even in common usage. And that which does not apprehend what is capable of causal efficacy does not direct one toward it — how then could it bring about that [result]? How then could one who acts with deliberation call it a valid means of knowledge on the ground of its being non-deceptive?

body.text: 18. sāmānyasya vistareṇāvastutvasādhanam |
body.translated_text: 18. Establishing in detail the unreality of the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>).

body.text: yadyevaṃ sāmānyamapyarthakriyāsādhanameva tatastadviṣayo vidhivikalpaḥ pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ced āha- "na ca"naiva "sāmānyaṃ kāñcit" tatsādhyatayopagatāmabhinnajñānābhidhānalakṣaṇāmanyāṃ vā vyaktisādhyām "arthakriyāmupakalpayati" | kīdṛśam?, "svalakṣaṇapratipatteḥ" vyaktipratipatterālocanājñānasaṃjñitāyā "urddham" uttarakālaṃ "tatsāmarthyotpannavikalpavijñānagrāhyam" iti | tacchabdena svalakṣaṇapratipattiḥ sambadhyate | ‘tataḥ paraṃ punarvastu'; ityādi parairabhidhānādevaṃ bravīti darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya pratyakṣapramāṇatāṃ nirākartum | sarvameva tu sāmānyaṃ na kāñcidarthakriyāmupakalpayati | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 29

children.text: ) yat tu sāmānyamanumānavikalpagrāhyaṃ tat kāraṇavyāpakasambaddhaliṅganiścayadvārāyātaṃ sambaddhasambandhādanadhigatārthakriyāsādhanaviṣayāmarthakriyāmupakalpayatīti tadviṣayo vikalpaḥ pramāṇam | idaṃ tu naivam, adhigatatvādarthakriyāsādhanasyālocanājñāneneti | atrodāharaṇam "yathā- nīlaṃ dṛṣṭvā nīlamiti jñāne" pratibhāsamānamiti śeṣaḥ | na sāmānyaṃ kāñcidarthakriyāmupakalpayatīti prakṛtena sambandhaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) However, the universal that is grasped by inferential conceptual cognition, having come through the channel of the ascertainment of a logical mark connected with the pervader of the cause, brings about causal efficacy with respect to what is capable of causal efficacy yet not previously apprehended, through the connection with what is connected. Therefore, the conceptual cognition having that as its object is a valid means of knowledge. But this [positive determination arising from perception] is not like that, because what is capable of causal efficacy has already been apprehended by the apprehensive cognition. Here the example is: "Just as, having seen blue, in the cognition 'it is blue'" — the remainder is 'what appears [therein].' The universal does not bring about any causal efficacy — this is the connection with the main topic.

body.translated_text: If so, then the universal too is capable of causal efficacy, and therefore the positive determination having it as its object should be a valid means of knowledge — if one objects thus, he says: "The universal does not at all bring about any" causal efficacy — whether one accepted as accomplishable by it, characterized by non-differentiated cognition and designation, or any other accomplishable by individuals. Of what kind? "Graspable by the conceptual cognition generated by the capacity of that, after" — i.e. subsequent to — "the apprehension of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>)" — the apprehensive cognition. The word 'that' connects with the apprehension of the particular. 'Then again, the real entity' — he speaks thus following the statement of others, in order to refute the status of the conceptual cognition that arises subsequent to perception as a perceptual valid means of knowledge. But in fact, every universal does not bring about any causal efficacy whatsoever. (

body.text: nanu ca liṅgavikalpapratibhāsi sāmānyaṃ prakṛtam tat kimanyadudāhriyate? | sarvasya darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya paropagatāṃ pratyakṣapramāṇatāṃ tulyanyāyatayā nirākartum | kāṃpunarnīlamiti vikalpajñāne darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvini pratibhāsamānaṃ sāmānyamarthakriyāṃ nopakalpayati? | yadi vyaktisādhyām; tadānyo 'pi padārtho 'nyadīyāmarthakriyāṃ nopakalpayatīti tasyāpyanarthakriyāsādhanatvādavastutvaprasaṅgaḥ | atha svasādhyām; tadasiddham, abhinnajñānābhidhānalakṣaṇāyāḥ svasādhyāyāḥ karaṇādityāśaṅkayāha- "tadeva hi" yat tadālocanājñāne nopalabdhaṃ "nīlasvalakṣaṇam" nīlavyaktiḥ "tathāvidhasādhyārthakriyākāri" | tathāvidhaśabdena sāmānyamatrābhipretam, tādṛśaparyāyatvādasya, sādhāraṇarūpasya ca tādṛśatvāt | tena tathāvidhasādhyāṃ nīlasāmānyasādhyāmabhinnajñānābhidhānalakṣaṇāmarthakriyāṃ kartuṃ śīlamasya svalakṣaṇasyeti tat tathoktam |
body.translated_text: But is not the universal that appears in the inferential conceptual cognition the main topic? So why is another example cited? In order to refute, by parity of reasoning, the perceptual validity accepted by others for every conceptual cognition that arises subsequent to perception. What universal, appearing in the post-perceptual conceptual cognition 'blue,' does not bring about causal efficacy? If one says: that accomplishable by individuals — then any other entity too does not bring about the causal efficacy belonging to another, and hence, due to its incapacity for causal efficacy, there would be the unwanted consequence of its being unreal. If one says: that accomplishable by itself — then that is unestablished, because it [the particular] does accomplish its own causal efficacy characterized by non-differentiated cognition and designation — anticipating this objection, he says: "For that very" blue particular (<s>nīlasvalakṣaṇa</s>), which was not apprehended in the apprehensive cognition, is "productive of causal efficacy of that kind." By the word 'of that kind' (<s>tathāvidha</s>), the universal is intended here, this being a synonym for 'of such a nature,' and the common form being of such a nature. Thus, the particular has the disposition to produce the causal efficacy accomplishable by the blue-universal — characterized by non-differentiated cognition and designation. Therefore it is so stated.

body.text: evaṃ manyate- yathā bhinnā api vyaktayaḥ kayācit pratyāsattyā tadekakāryapratiniyamalakṣaṇayā tadekamabhinnaṃ sāmānyamupakurvanti, tadaparasāmānyayogamantareṇāpi, anyathānavasthāprasaṅgāt, tathābhinnajñānābhidhānātmikāmapyarthakriyāṃ sādhayiṣyanti | kimapramāṇakena pramāṇabādhitena ca sāmānyenopagatena? | tathā hi- anumānādike jñāne yathāvidhamasyāspaṣṭaṃ rūpaṃ pratibhāsate na tathāvidhaṃ vyaktiṣu dṛśyamānāsupalakṣayāmaḥ | ekameva hi vyaktidarśanakāle spaṣṭaṃ nīlādirūpaṃ vibhāvayāmaḥ | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 30

children.text: ) tat kathamadṛṣṭakalpanayātmānaṃ svayameva vipralabhemahi? | vyaktirūpasaṃsargād ayogolakavanhivadavibhāvanamiti cet; na, sarvatra bhedābhedavyavasthāyā abhāvaprasaṅgāt | asyottarasyānyatrāpi sulabhatvāt | na ca sāmānyasya dve rūpe staḥ spaṣṭamaspaṣṭaṃ ca, yenaikena darśane pratibhāseta anyenānumānādijñāne, padārthadvayopagamaprasaṅgāt, pratibhāsabhedasyaiva sarvatra bhāvabhedavyavasthānibandhanatvāt, sāmānyasyāparasāmānyaprasakterniḥsāmānyasya cāsyopagamāt |
children.translated_text: ) So how could we deceive ourselves by imagining something never seen? If one says: because of its intermixture with the individual form, it is not discerned, like fire mixed with gold — no, because in that case the distinction between identity and difference would be impossible everywhere. Since the answer to this is readily available elsewhere as well. Nor does the universal have two forms — clear and unclear — such that it would appear by one in perception and by the other in inferential cognition, because that would entail accepting two entities; because the difference in appearance is everywhere the ground for establishing the difference in reality; and because the universal would require another universal [to explain its unity], while it is accepted as having no further universal above it.

body.translated_text: He thinks thus: Just as individuals, though different, support that single non-different universal through some proximity — characterized by the invariable restriction of that one effect — even without the mediation of another higher universal, since otherwise there would be infinite regress; so too they will accomplish the causal efficacy characterized by non-differentiated cognition and designation. What need is there of a universal that is unestablished by any valid means of knowledge and is contradicted by valid knowledge? For thus — the indistinct form that appears in inferential and other cognitions is not observed as being of the same kind in the individuals when they are perceived. For at the time of perceiving an individual, we discern only the single clear form of blue etc. (

body.text: 19. kumāriloktadvayātmakabuddhernirasanam |
body.translated_text: 19. Refutation of <s>Kumārila</s>'s claim that cognition has a dual nature.

body.text: etenaitadapi nirastam yadāha-
body.translated_text: By this, the following is also refuted, which he says —

children.translated_text: "With respect to all entities, cognition arises

children.text: jāyate dvayātmakatvena vinā sā ca na yujyate ||"
children.translated_text: having the nature of both exclusion and inclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s> and <s>anugama</s>), and without being of dual nature, it is not tenable."
"And here, neither of the two is an error; nor is it accepted as figurative,
because cognition is always firm; error belongs to those who propound error."

body.text: iti | yato yadīndriyabuddhimabhipretyocyate; tadāsiddham, aspaṣṭasya nīlādyākārasya spaṣṭanīlādyābhāsāyāṃ tatrānupalakṣaṇāt, spaṣṭasyāpi ca dvitīyasyānuyāyinaḥ | tadbhāve ca vyaktidvayāntarālamapyāpnuvataḥ kathaṃ tadanugamaḥ? | vyāptau(vyaktau) copalabhyasya sataḥ tatrānupalakṣaṇaṃ kutaḥ? | nahi tasya vyaktāvyaktarūpasambhavaḥ, ekatvāt | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: Thus. Now, if this is said with reference to sensory cognition, then it is unestablished — because the indistinct blue-like form is not observed as such in the cognition that clearly manifests blue etc., and because even a second clear [universal form], if it were a constant accompaniment, would extend to the interval between two individuals — how then could it be a concomitant? And how could what exists and is perceived in the individual not be observed therein? For it is impossible for it to have both a manifest and unmanifest form, since it is one. And thus he says —

children.translated_text: "If <s>jāti</s> (genus), being in one individual and being non-different, were all-pervading,
it should be seen everywhere — [and it would not depend on individuals]."

body.text: iti | ekatrāpi ca vyaktāvupalabhyamānāyāṃ sakalatrailokyavyāpi rūpaṃ sakalasvāśrayavyāpi vā dṛśyeta? | na hyekasyāḥ kiñcid dṛṣṭamadṛṣṭaṃ vā nāma kṣaṇikatādivad | dṛṣṭāyāmapyekatraivāśraye darśanāvasāyo na sarvatreti cet; na, vikalpena taddarśanābhyupagamāt | na hi niścayaviṣayīkṛtaṃ cāniścitaṃ ceti yuktam | tataḥ sarvagatarūpadarśane sarvārthānāṃ darśanaprasaṅgaḥ | na hi taddarśane (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 31

children.text: ) tatsahacāriṇa upalabhyasya tadabhinnasvabhāvasya cānupalambho yuktaḥ | tataḥ kathamindriyabuddherdvyātmakatā? |
children.translated_text: ) it is not reasonable that what accompanies it, what is to be perceived, and what is of the same nature as it, should remain unperceived. Therefore, how can sensory cognition have a dual nature?

body.translated_text: And when it is perceived even in a single individual, should its form pervading the entire triple world, or pervading all its substrates, be seen? For it is not the case that something of one nature is partly seen and partly unseen, unlike momentariness etc. If one says: even when seen, the perception terminates in just one substrate, not everywhere — no, because it is accepted that the universal is seen by conceptual cognition [as pervading all]. For it is not proper that something is both ascertained and unascertained at the same time. Therefore, if the all-pervading form is seen, there would be the unwanted consequence of seeing all objects. For when that is seen, (

body.text: athānumānādibuddhim; tasyāmapi svalakṣaṇāpratibhāsanāt kuto dvayātmakatvam? | na hi tāsu sāmānyagrāhiṇīṣvaspaṣṭo vyaktyākāra iva lakṣyamāṇaḥ svalakṣaṇapratibhāsaḥ | tadabhāve 'pi tāsāṃ bhavāt | ākārāntareṇa ca svajñāne[']pratibhāsanāt anekākārāyogād ekasya, apratiprasaṅgācca | tasmānneyaṃ bhinnārthagrāhiṇyabhinnā sāmānyabuddhiḥ pratibhāti svalakṣaṇodbhavā satī | kintvanādivitatha vikalpābhyāsavāsanājanitā satī tathāvabhāsate | dṛḍhatvaṃ ca buddhernāvināśitvam, kṣaṇikatvābhyupagamāt kintvabādhyamānatvam | na cāsyāstat sambhavati, leśato bādhakasyoktatvāt | vistaratastu syāvdādabhaṅgād yathāvasaramihaiva tatra tatra vidhāsyamānād bādhakamavadhāryam | tasmād yathā vyaktayaḥ sāmānyāntaramantareṇa tadekamupakurvanti tathābhinnajñānābhidhāne api pravartayiṣyantīti tadeva nīlasvalakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyasādhyatvopagatārthakriyākāri |
body.translated_text: If [one says this refers to] inferential and other cognition — even in that, since the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) does not appear, whence the dual nature? For in those cognitions that grasp the universal, no appearance of the particular is discerned as an indistinct individual-form. Because those cognitions exist even without it. And because, since something does not appear in its own cognition under a different form, a single thing cannot have multiple forms; and because there would be the consequence of non-apprehension [if it had another form]. Therefore, this cognition of universals, grasping different objects, does not appear as non-different, being born from the particular. Rather, being generated by the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of beginninglessly false habitual conceptualization, it merely appears so. And the 'firmness' of cognition does not mean its indestructibility — since momentariness is accepted — but rather its being unrefuted. And that is not possible for it, since refuting evidence has been stated at least in part. In detail, the refuting evidence should be ascertained from the refutation of the 'syād' etc. [arguments], which will be set forth in appropriate places herein. Therefore, just as individuals support that single [universal] without the mediation of another universal, so too they will produce non-differentiated cognition and designation. Thus, that very blue particular (<s>nīlasvalakṣaṇa</s>) is productive of the causal efficacy accepted as accomplishable by the universal.

body.text: 20. kumāriladattasya doṣasya saugatabuddhyabādhakatvadarśanam |
body.translated_text: 20. Showing that the defect alleged by <s>Kumārila</s> does not refute Buddhist cognition.

body.text: yastu-
body.translated_text: Now, he who —

children.translated_text: "If the universal is not accepted as something different, then what controls its application?
Why is the cognition 'cow' not restricted even without <s>gotva</s> (cowness)?
Just as there is occurrence and non-occurrence in certain things despite equal difference,
so too cognition will be without a cause, even without <s>gotva</s> etc."

body.text: iti pūrvapakṣayitvā-
body.translated_text: — having stated the objection thus —

children.translated_text: "For without an object, the arising of cognitions is not accepted.
They accept the universal as something other than the particular; therefore that [universal] is certainly [real].

children.text: tā hi tena vinotpannā mithyā syurviṣayādṛte |
children.translated_text: For those [cognitions], arising without that [universal], would be false, being without an object.

children.text: na tvanyena vinā vṛttiḥ sāmānyasyeha duṣyati ||"
children.translated_text: But the operation of the universal without something else is not vitiated here."

body.text: iti mithyātvaprasaṅgadoṣa ukto nāsau tathāgatasamayanayāvadātabuddhīn bādhate | sāmānyabuddhīnāṃ bādhakapratyayanibandhanasya mithyātvasyopagatatvāt | tathā hi-
body.translated_text: Thus, the defect of the consequence of falsity has been stated. But that does not refute those whose intellects are purified by the system of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Buddha). Because the falsity of universal-cognitions, grounded in refuting cognition, is already accepted [by them]. For thus —

children.translated_text: "Why does <s>gotva</s> (cowness) belong only to what possesses a dewlap etc.? Because it is of that nature.
And why is it of that nature? Let it be understood: from its own nature."

body.text: iti vacanāt ‘vyaktisvabhāvaṃ ca sāmānyam | na cāsādhāraṇam vyaktyudayavināśayordhyā(yośca) nodayavyayayogi'; ityuyuktam, viruddhadharmādhyāsato bhedaprasaṅgāditi | āha ca-
body.translated_text: Because of this statement, 'the universal is of the nature of the individual; and it is not unique, nor does it undergo origination and destruction along with the origination and destruction of the individual' — this is untenable, because the superimposition of contradictory properties would entail difference. And he says —

children.translated_text: "If identity of nature is accepted for <s>jāti</s> (genus), then at the birth of an individual, it is unborn;
and at its destruction, it is undestroyed — by whom is this accepted? And would not non-continuity follow likewise?
If unborn at the birth of an individual, it has not come from another substrate;

children.text: prāgāsīnna ca taddeśe sā tayā saṅgatā katham? ||
children.translated_text: it did not previously exist in that place — so how is it conjoined with that [individual]?

children.text: vyaktināśe na cennaṣṭā gatā vyaktyantaraṃ na ca |
children.translated_text: If not destroyed at the destruction of an individual, it has not gone to another individual;

children.text: tacchūnye na sthitā deśe sā jātiḥ kveti kathyatām ||
children.translated_text: nor does it remain in a place devoid of that — so where is that <s>jāti</s>, let it be told!

body.text:
vyakterjanmādiyoge 'pi yadi jāteḥ sa neṣyate |
tādātmyaṃ kathamiṣṭaṃ syādanupaplutacetasām ||" iti |
body.translated_text: If, even though the individual undergoes birth etc., that is not accepted for <s>jāti</s>, then how could identity of nature be accepted by those of unimpaired minds?"

body.text: 21. nīlavikalpasyāprāmāṇyasamarthanam |
body.translated_text: 21. Establishing the invalidity of the conceptual cognition of blue.

body.text: yadi nīlasvalakṣaṇameva sāmānyasādhyārthakriyākāri tadeva tarhyadhigacchan vikalpaḥ pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatītyāha- "tacca" nīlakhalakṣaṇam | "tenātmanā" nīlasādhyārthakriyākāriṇā svabhāvena "dṛṣṭameva" ālocanāpratyayena | tato niṣpāditakriye karmaṇyaviṣeṣādhāyi vikalpajñānaṃ kathaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt? | atha matam- sāmānyameva tarhyadhigacchan nīlavikalpaḥ pramāṇamastu | tacca sāmānyamarthakriyākāri | yato nīlasādhyāmevārthakriyāṃ nīlena saha sambhūya kariṣyati | vyaktisvabhāvānyeva hi sāmānyānītyāha- "na ca" naiva "tat svalakṣaṇagrahaṇottarakālabhāvino" nīlavyaktidarśanottarakālaṃ bhavanaśīlasya | liṅgagrahaṇottarakālabhāvinastu pūrvoktena prakāreṇa vyaktisādhyārthakriyā sāmānyasya kalpitasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 33.

children.text: ) vyavasthāpayituṃ śakyata iti bhāvaḥ | "nīlavikalpasya viṣayeṇa" nīlasāmānyena "nīlasādhyārthakriyā" rañjanādikā "kriyate" | tasya vyaktisvābhāvyāyoge sati kalpitarūpasya tadasambhavāt | na ca nityasvabhāvatāmābibhrāṇena nīlavikalpasya viṣayeṇa nīlasādhyānyā vārthakriyā kriyate | kramayaugapadyavirodhāditi manyate |
children.translated_text: — this is the intended meaning. "By the object of the blue <s>vikalpa</s>" — i.e., by the blue universal — "the <s>arthakriyā</s> achievable through blue" — such as coloring and the like — "is accomplished." This is because, given the impossibility [of the universal] having the nature of a particular, and since it has a constructed form, that [<s>arthakriyā</s>] is impossible for it. Nor does the object of the blue <s>vikalpa</s>, bearing the nature of being permanent, accomplish any <s>arthakriyā</s> other than that achievable through blue — because of the contradiction between sequence and simultaneity. This is the view.

body.translated_text: If it is the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of blue alone that accomplishes the <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) that is the purpose to be achieved through the universal, then the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) that apprehends that very [particular] would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) — to address this he says: "And that" — the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of blue — "in that very nature" — in its nature as blue, capable of accomplishing <s>arthakriyā</s> — "has already been seen" — by the apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanāpratyaya</s>). Therefore, how could the conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpajñāna</s>), which contributes nothing new to the object whose purpose has already been accomplished, be a <s>pramāṇa</s>? Now one might think: then let the blue <s>vikalpa</s>, apprehending the universal alone, be a <s>pramāṇa</s>; and let that universal be causally efficacious, since it will accomplish the very <s>arthakriyā</s> achievable by blue, by combining with the blue [particular]. For universals are nothing other than the natures of the particulars themselves — he says: "And not" — it is certainly not the case — "that" [universal], which "comes into being after the apprehension of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>" — which has the nature of arising after the perception of the blue particular. But for [the universal] that arises after the apprehension of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), by the manner previously stated, the <s>arthakriyā</s> achievable through the particular can be established for the constructed [universal]

body.text: 22. mīmāṃsakasaṃmatapramāṇalakṣaṇe doṣadarśanam |
body.translated_text: 22. Exposing the defect in the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>.

body.text: tadevaṃ ‘nīlaṃ dṛṣṭvā nīlam'; iti jñāne pratibhasamānaṃ sāmānyaṃ na kāñcidarthakriyāmupakalpayatīti prasādhya anarthakriyākāriviṣayasyāpi vikalpasya pratyakṣapṛṣṭhabhāvinaḥ prāmāṇyaprasaṅgādativyāptiriti "tatrāpūrvārthavijñānam" iti pramāṇalakṣaṇe mīmāṃsakairviśeṣaṇamupādeyamiti darśayannāha- "tasmād" yata evamanarthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatayā darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya prāmāṇyamayuktam tasmādasmadabhimataṃ "pramāṇamavisaṃvādi jñānam" iti pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ vyudasya "anadhigatārthaviṣayaṃ pramāṇam", "tatrāpūrvārthavijñānaṃ pramāṇam" "iti api" etasminnapyāhopuruṣikayānyasmiṃ(smin) "pramāṇalakṣaṇe" kriyamāṇe "ativyāptiparihārāya viśeṣaṇīyaṃ" viśeṣaṇamupādeyam | kathaṃ viśeṣaṇīyam "anadhigate svalakṣaṇe iti" | anena hi viśeṣaṇenānumānavikalpasya ca prāmāṇyaṃ sidhyati, ālocanājñānapṛṣṭhabhāvinaśca vikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ vyudasyata iti sarvaṃ sustham |
body.translated_text: Having thus established that the universal appearing in the cognition "[seeing] blue, [one cognizes] blue" does not bring about any <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy), and since there would be the unwanted consequence (<s>ativyāpti</s>, over-extension) that even the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) following perception, whose object does not accomplish <s>arthakriyā</s>, would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> — showing that in the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>, "knowledge of a previously unknown object" (<s>apūrvārthavijñāna</s>), a qualifier must be adopted, he says: "Therefore" — since, as explained, the validity of a <s>vikalpa</s> following perception is inappropriate because its object cannot accomplish <s>arthakriyā</s> — therefore, setting aside our own accepted definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> as "non-deceptive cognition" (<s>avisaṃvādi jñāna</s>), "even in" this other "definition of <s>pramāṇa</s>" being formulated with great effort — [namely,] "a <s>pramāṇa</s> has as its object something not [previously] apprehended" or "knowledge of a previously unknown object is <s>pramāṇa</s>" — "a qualifier must be added for the removal of over-extension." How should it be qualified? "With respect to a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) not [previously] apprehended." For by this qualifier, the validity of inferential <s>vikalpa</s> is established, while the validity of <s>vikalpa</s> following apprehensive perception is rejected — and thus all is well.

body.text: tadevaṃ vidhivikalpasyānarthakriyāsādhanaviṣayatayānadhigatasāmānyadhigame 'pi prāmāṇyaṃ nirākṛtya caśabdasamuccitaṃ smṛtitvaṃ pratiṣedhavikalpena sādhāraṇamaprāmāṇyakāraṇaṃ darśayannāha- "adhigate tu svalakṣaṇe" ālocanājñānena "tatsāmarthyajanmā" svalakṣaṇādhigamabalabhāvī "vikalpastadanukārī" sākṣādanutpatterddarśanasaṃskārādheyavaśaccāspa(cca spa)ṣṭanīlasvalakṣaṇākārānukārī dṛśyavikalpyayoścaikīkaraṇādevamucyate | vastutastu (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 34.

children.text: ) na kiñcidasāvanukaroti | "sa smṛtireva" | kutaḥ? "kāryatastadviṣayatvāt" na paramārthataḥ | kāryamatra svalakṣaṇe puruṣasya pravartanam, tadadhyavasāyaśca | yataśca kāryataḥ tadviṣayatvāt smṛtirevāto "na pramāṇam" darśanabalotpanno vikalpaḥ | tathā hi- smṛterapyanubhūtasvalakṣaṇāṃśaviṣayāyā na paramārthatastadviṣayatvam | svalakṣaṇasyendriyabuddhāviva sphuṭarūpatayā smṛtāvapratibhāsanāt | kintu yathoktāt kāryata eva | tacca vidhivikalpe 'pi samānamiti kathamasau smṛtirna syāditi |
children.translated_text: it does not imitate anything at all. "It is simply <s>smṛti</s> (memory)." Why? "Because of being [directed to] that object by way of its effect" (<s>kāryataḥ</s>) — not in the ultimate sense. The "effect" (<s>kārya</s>) here is the person's engagement with the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, and the determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) regarding it. And since it is [directed to] that object by way of effect, it is simply memory; therefore "it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>" — the <s>vikalpa</s> arising from the force of perception. That is to say: even for memory, which has as its object an aspect of the previously experienced <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, there is no ultimate [directedness to] that object — because the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, in its vivid form as in sensory cognition, does not appear in memory. Rather, [it is directed to it] only by way of effect, as stated. And that is equally the case for positive <s>vikalpa</s> — so how could it not be memory?

body.translated_text: Having thus rejected the validity of positive <s>vikalpa</s> (<s>vidhivikalpa</s>) — because its object cannot accomplish <s>arthakriyā</s> — even though it apprehends a universal not previously apprehended, he now shows, using the word "and" (<s>ca</s>) to introduce a cumulative [reason], that the character of being memory (<s>smṛtitva</s>), which is common to both positive and negative <s>vikalpa</s>, is a [further] cause of invalidity. He says: "But when the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) has been apprehended" — by the apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) — "born from the power of that" — arising by the force of the apprehension of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> — "the <s>vikalpa</s> imitates that" — it is said to imitate the appearance of the vivid <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> of blue, since it does not directly arise [from the object] but is dependent on the impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by the perception; this is said because of the identification of the seen and the conceptualized. But in reality

body.text: 23. anumānasya vidhivikalpavailakṣaṇyena prāmāṇyasamarthanam |
body.translated_text: 23. Establishing the validity of inference through its dissimilarity from positive <s>vikalpa</s>.

body.text: tatraitat syāt- nanvanumānavikalpaḥ smṛtirūpo 'pi pramāṇamiṣyate | tathā hi- yadevānagnivyāvṛttaṃ vastumātraṃ mahānasādāvanubhūtamāsīt tadeva pradeśaviśeṣe dhūmadarśanāt smaryate | tadvad vidhivikalpo 'pi pramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha- "anadhigata"sya "vastu"no "rūpa"sya "anadhigateriti" | evammanyate- yat mahānasādāvanagnivyāvṛttaṃ vastumātraṃ prāganubhūtaṃ na tat taddeśādisambandhitayaivānumānavikalpena smaryate kintu yatra pradeśe prāgananubhūtaṃ tatsambandhitayā | tataḥ sādhyadharmidṛṣṭāntadharmigrāhidarśanadvayānadhigatasyānagnivyāvṛttasya vasturūpasyāyogavyavacchedenādhigamād yuktamasya prāmāṇyam | na tu darśanapṛṣṭhabhāvino vikalpasya, tadviparītatvāditi |
body.translated_text: Here one might object: but the inferential <s>vikalpa</s>, even though it has the nature of memory, is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s>. For: the bare real thing (<s>vastumātra</s>), excluded from non-fire, that was previously experienced in the kitchen and the like — that very thing is remembered upon seeing smoke in a particular location. In the same way, positive <s>vikalpa</s> too will be a <s>pramāṇa</s>. To this he says: "Because of the non-apprehension" of the "form" of a "real thing" (<s>vastu</s>) "not [previously] apprehended." He thinks thus: the bare real thing excluded from non-fire that was previously experienced in the kitchen — that is not remembered by the inferential <s>vikalpa</s> as connected with that very place and so forth; rather, [it is remembered] as connected with a location where it was not previously experienced. Therefore, since the form of the real thing not apprehended by the two perceptions — which grasp the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (thesis-subject) and the <s>dṛṣṭāntadharmin</s> (example-subject) — is apprehended through the exclusion of the impossible, its validity is appropriate. But not [the validity] of a <s>vikalpa</s> following perception, because it is the opposite of that.

body.text: 24. pramāṇavyavasthāyāḥ vastvadhiṣṭhānatvaṃ, svalakṣaṇasyaiva ca vastutvam |
body.translated_text: 24. The grounding of the <s>pramāṇa</s> system in reality (<s>vastu</s>), and that only the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) is real.

body.text: yadi nāmānadhigataṃ vasturūpaṃ nādhigacchati, pramāṇaṃ tu kasmānna bhavatīti ced āha- "vastvadhiṣṭhānatvāt" ityādi | vastvadhiṣṭhānatvaṃ ca "pramāṇavyavasthāyāḥ" pramāṇavyāpāraviṣayamabhipretyocyate nālambanalakṣaṇam, anyathānumānasya parikalpitasāmānyālambanatayā vastvadhiṣṭhānatvābhāvādavyāpinī pramāṇavyavasthā syād | yadi vastvadhiṣṭhānā pramāṇavyavasthā kathaṃ viprakṛṣṭaviṣayāyā (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 35.

children.text: ) anupalabdheḥ prāmāṇyam iti cet; tatrāpi pradhānādivikalpasyaiva bhāvānupādānatayā sādhyatvāt tasyā api vastvadhiṣṭhānatāstyevetyadoṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: have validity? Even there, since the <s>vikalpa</s> of the principal entity (<s>pradhāna</s>) and the like — through the non-apprehension of a [present] entity — is what is to be proved, that [non-apprehension] too has grounding in reality, so there is no fault.

body.translated_text: If [one objects:] even granted that it does not apprehend an unapprehended real form, why is it not a <s>pramāṇa</s>? He says: "Because the system of <s>pramāṇas</s> is grounded in reality" (<s>vastvadhiṣṭhāna</s>) and so on. And "grounded in reality" in "of the system of <s>pramāṇas</s>" is said with reference to the domain of <s>pramāṇa</s>-operation, not in the sense of the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>); otherwise, since inference has a constructed universal as its object-support, the system of <s>pramāṇas</s> would lack grounding in reality and thus be of insufficient scope (<s>avyāpin</s>). If the <s>pramāṇa</s> system is grounded in reality, how can <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), whose object is remote,

body.text: atha vastvadhiṣṭhānaiva pramāṇavyavastheti kuta etad? ityāha- "arthakriyāyāṃ" sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇāyāṃ yad "yogyaṃ" śaktaṃ "tadviṣayatvāt tadarthinām" arthakriyārthināṃ "pravṛtteḥ" prāptityāgalakṣaṇāyāḥ | yadi nāmarthakriyāyogye tadarthināṃ pravṛttistathāpi kathaṃ vastvadhiṣṭhānā pramāṇavyavasthā?, arthakriyāyogyādhiṣṭhānā hi tathā sati syāt iti cet; āha- "arthakriyā"yāṃ yad "yogyaṃ" ta"llakṣaṇa"meva "hi vastu" | tato 'rthakriyāyogyādhiṣṭhānatvena vastvadhiṣṭhānatvaṃ kathaṃ na syāt iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, how [do we know] that the <s>pramāṇa</s> system is grounded in reality? He says: "Because engagement" (<s>pravṛtti</s>) — characterized by obtaining and avoiding — "of those who desire [the result]" — of those who desire <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) — "is directed toward that which is 'capable' — i.e., potent — 'in [bringing about] <s>arthakriyā</s>'" — [an efficacy] characterized by pleasure and pain. If one objects: granted that the engagement of those who desire the result is toward what is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s>, how does this make the <s>pramāṇa</s> system grounded in reality? For in that case, it would be grounded in what is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> [rather than in reality per se]. He says: "That which is 'capable' 'in <s>arthakriyā</s>' — that, having 'that characteristic,' 'is indeed reality' (<s>vastu</s>)." Therefore, since grounding in what is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s> is [the same as] grounding in reality, how could [the system] not be grounded in reality? — this is the import.

body.text: idaṃ ca vastvāśrayeṇa pramāṇavyavasthāpratipādanamanadhigate svalakṣaṇa ityukte kadācit paro brūyāt- vastumātranibandhanā hi pramāṇavyavasthā na svalakṣaṇāśrayaiva | tato yadyapyanadhigataṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ nādhigacchati tathāpyanadhigatavasturūpamadhigacchato vikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti tadasiddhatodbhāvanārthamuktam- "anadhigatavasturūpe"tyādi | tadasiddhatodbhāvane cānadhigatavasturūpādhigantureva prāmānyaṃ netarasyeti kutaḥ? iti paryanuyoge "arthakriyāyogye"tyādi uktam | tathā ca vastuviṣayamapi prāmāṇyaṃ bruvatā svalakṣaṇaviṣayamevoktaṃ bhavati, tasyaivārthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvāt, sāmānyasya ca tadviparītatvāt iti manyate |
body.translated_text: This demonstration of the <s>pramāṇa</s> system through its grounding in reality, when it has been stated "with respect to a <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> not apprehended," [is given because] the opponent might at some point say: the <s>pramāṇa</s> system is grounded merely in reality (<s>vastu</s>) in general, not exclusively in the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular). Therefore, even if the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> not apprehended is not apprehended [by vikalpa], the <s>vikalpa</s> that apprehends an unapprehended real form (<s>vasturūpa</s>) will have validity. This [passage about reality-grounding] is stated for the purpose of bringing out the unestablished nature of that [objection]. And in bringing out the unestablished nature [of the claim], [the question arises:] why is validity only for that which apprehends an unapprehended real form, and not for the other? In response to this inquiry, "that which is capable of <s>arthakriyā</s>" and so on was stated. And thus, one who asserts validity with respect to reality has in fact asserted it with respect to the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone — because only that [<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>] has the characteristic of being capable of <s>arthakriyā</s>, while the universal is the opposite of that. This is the view.

body.text: punarapyanubhavottarakālabhāvino nīlavikalpasya prāmāṇyamapanetumupacayahetumāha- "tato 'pi" yathoktād vikalpād na kevalaṃ nīlasvalakṣaṇānubhavād "vastunyeva" svalakṣaṇa eva "tadadhyavasāyena" svalakṣaṇādhyavasāyena anyathā tatra pravṛttyayogāt "puruṣasya pravṛtte" adhigate svalakṣaṇe tatsāmarthyajanmā vikalpo na pramāṇamiti sambandhaḥ | pūrvamanadhigatavasturūpānadhigateraprāmāṇyamuktam | adhunā tvadhigatasyaivādhigamāditi vidhipratiṣedharūpatayopapattyorbhedaḥ | (

Alternatively, what was stated as "because of being [directed to] that object by way of its effect" (<s>kāryataḥ</s>) is here clarified by way of a cumulative reason.

body.translated_text: Again, in order to further remove the validity of the blue <s>vikalpa</s> that arises after experience, he states a cumulative reason: "Moreover, from that" — from the <s>vikalpa</s> as described — not merely from the experience of the blue <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> — "[the person's] engagement being toward the real thing alone" — toward the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone — "through the determination of that" — through the determination of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>, since engagement would otherwise be impossible — "when the person has engaged" — when the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> has been apprehended, the <s>vikalpa</s> born from the power of that is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>: this is the connection. Previously, the non-validity was stated as being due to the non-apprehension of an unapprehended real form. But now [it is stated] as being due to the apprehension of what has already been apprehended — this is the difference, in the form of [two] positive and negative justifications.

body.text: 25. vikalpasya darśanāt pṛthakpramāṇyābhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: 25. The absence of separate validity of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) distinct from perception.

body.text: yadi nāma tadadhyavasāyena vastunyeva puruṣasya pravṛttistathāpyanadhigatasāmānyagrāhiṇo 'sya darśanāt pṛthak prāmāṇyaṃ kimiti neṣyate? iti cet; āha- "pravṛttau" svalakṣaṇa eva satyāṃ "pratyakṣeṇa" ālocanājñānākhyena "abhinnayogakṣematvāt" | yogaḥ aprāptasya viṣayasya paricchedalakṣaṇā prāptiḥ, kṣemaḥ tadarthakriyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇaṃ paripālanam | abhinnau yogakṣemāvasyeti sa tathoktaḥ | tatra vikalpasya nirvikalpapratyakṣeṇābhinno yogaḥ svalakṣaṇādhyavasāyataḥ | abhinnaḥ kṣema ālocanāvijñānādiva vikalpādapi svalakṣaṇa eva pravṛtteḥ | ayamasyābhiprāyaḥ- yadi vikalpo nirvikalpacetasaḥ prameyāntaraviṣayastadā tatraiva puruṣaṃ pravartayatu tatsādhyāmarthakriyāmadhigantum | naiva vā pravartayet, tadviṣayatvābhimatasya sāmānyasyābhinnajñānalakṣaṇāyā evārthakriyāyā upagamād vikalpodayādeva ca tatsiddheḥ | nahi nīlānubhavāt prameyāntaraviṣayāḥ pītādipratyayāḥ puruṣaṃ nīlavastuni pravartayanti, sādhitārthakriyā vā kvacidapīti | tasmādālocanājñānānaivāyaṃ prameyāntaraviṣayaḥ | viśeṣeṇa yaireva vyākhyāyate-
body.translated_text: If [one objects:] even granted that the person's engagement is toward the real thing alone through the determination of that, why is the separate validity of this [<s>vikalpa</s>], which apprehends an unapprehended universal, not accepted — given its distinctness from perception? He says: "When engagement" is toward the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone, "because of having undifferentiated acquisition-and-preservation (<s>yogakṣema</s>) with perception" — i.e., with the apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>). <s>Yoga</s> (acquisition) is the attainment characterized by the determination of an object not previously reached; <s>kṣema</s> (preservation) is the protection characterized by the accomplishment of <s>arthakriyā</s> regarding that object. One for whom acquisition and preservation are undifferentiated [from perception] is so described. Therein, the <s>vikalpa</s>'s acquisition is undifferentiated from that of <s>nirvikalpaka</s> (non-conceptual) perception, because of [its] determination of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s>. Its preservation is undifferentiated [from perception] because, just as from apprehensive cognition, engagement from <s>vikalpa</s> too is toward the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> alone. His intent is this: if <s>vikalpa</s> had as its object a <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) different from that of non-conceptual cognition, then let it prompt the person toward that very [different object], to attain the <s>arthakriyā</s> achievable through it. Or else let it not prompt at all — since the universal, which is held to be its object, is acknowledged to have an <s>arthakriyā</s> characterized as nothing other than cognition itself, and since that [cognition-as-arthakriyā] is accomplished by the mere arising of the <s>vikalpa</s>. For cognitions of yellow and the like, which have objects different from the <s>prameya</s> [of blue experience], do not prompt a person toward a blue object, nor do they accomplish any <s>arthakriyā</s> [with respect to blue]. Therefore, this [<s>vikalpa</s>] does not have a <s>prameya</s> different from that of apprehensive cognition. Especially those who explain:

body.text:
"nirvikalpakabodhena dvayātmakasyāpi vastunaḥ |
grahaṇam"
body.translated_text: "Through non-conceptual cognition, the apprehension of an object that is of dual nature"

body.text: iti | tato nīladarśanasyaiva nirvikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ yuktam, na tadabhinnopayogasya smṛteriva vikalpasyāpi darśanāt pṛthageva | anyathā niṣphalāṃ pramāṇāntarakalpanāṃ kurvataḥ smṛticchādveṣaprayatnādi pramāṇamanuṣajyata iti pramāṇānāmiyattā viśīryeteti |
body.translated_text: — [maintain this]. Therefore, it is the validity of the perception of blue alone — being non-conceptual — that is appropriate, not the separate [validity] of the <s>vikalpa</s> that has the same utility, just as with memory, distinct from perception. Otherwise, one who fabricates a fruitless postulation of an additional <s>pramāṇa</s> would be followed by [the need to accept as <s>pramāṇas</s>] memory, desire, aversion, effort, and the like — and thus the definite number of <s>pramāṇas</s> would be destroyed.

body.text: 26. dhārāvāhikajñāneṣu yogitaditarāpekṣayā prāmāṇyāprāmāṇye |
body.translated_text: 26. Regarding streaming cognitions: validity and invalidity with respect to <s>Yogins</s> and others.

body.text: yadaikasminneva nīlādivastuni dhārāvāhīnīndriyajñānānyutpadyante tadā pūrveṇābhinnayogakṣematvād uttareṣāmindriyajñānānāmaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ | na caivam, ato 'nekānta iti pramāṇasaṃplavavādī darśayannāha- "pūrvapratyakṣakṣaṇena" ityādi | etat pariharati- "na", uttareṣāṃ prāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ | kutaḥ? | "nānāyogakṣematvāt" | tathā hi- pratikṣaṇaṃ viṣayaparicchedalakṣaṇo yogaḥ, tadarthakriyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇaśca kṣemaḥ paripālanarūpo bhidyate | tato vipakṣe vṛttyabhāvāt na heturanaikāntikaḥ | kadā nānāyogakṣematvam? | "kṣaṇaviśeṣasādhyārthavāñchāyām" | yadā kṣaṇaviśeṣasādhye 'rthe hitāhitalakṣaṇe vāñchā prāptiparihārecchā yogināṃ paropakāramuddiśya bhavati kasyacit kathañcit kvacidupayogāt tadā | yathā darśanamārge duḥkhe dharmajñānakṣāntirddamānāmanuśayānāṃ vāsanāṃ nirodhayati, tadviruddhāśayotpādanāt | duḥkhe dharmajñānaṃ kleśaviviktatālakṣaṇāṃ nirvāṇaprāptimutpādayati, anuśayaviruddhāśayadārḍhyotpādanāt | tat eṣāṃ grāhakāṇi paracittajñānāni pṛthageva pramāṇāni | parahitādhānadīkṣāvatāṃ ca samastavastuvistaravyāpijñānālokāvabhāsitāntarātmanāṃ bhagavatāṃ kaścidevārthakṣaṇaḥ kasyacideva parārthasyānugrāhako biabandhako veti sarvabhāvān pratikṣaṇaṃ vīkṣamāṇānāmadhyakṣacetasāṃ tadviṣayakṣaṇānāṃ bhinnārthakriyāsūpayogato nānāyogakṣematvāt | tad yadi pratikṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇavivekadarśino 'dhikṛtyocyate tadā bhinnopayogitayā pṛthak prāmāṇyāt nānekāntaḥ | atha sarvapadārtheṣvekatvādhyavasāyinaḥ sāṃvyavahārikān puruṣānabhipretyocyate tadā sakalameva (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 38.

children.text: ) nīlasantānamekamarthaṃ sthirarūpaṃ tatsādhyāṃ cārthakriyāmekātmikāmadhyavasyantīti prāmāṇyamapyuttareṣāmaniṣṭameveti kuto 'nekāntaḥ? iti darśayannāha- "sādhāraṇe hi" iti | tatsantānavartināṃ sarvakṣaṇānāmekatvenādhyavasitānāṃ vyavahartṛbhiryat sādhāraṇaṃ pratikṣaṇamanyānyakāraṇatayā vibhinnamapi paramārthato viparyāsādekatāyābhiniviṣṭaṃ rañjanādikaṃ nīlādikakārtyaṃ tatra "na teṣām" uktareṣāṃ jñānakṣaṇānāṃ "sāmarthya" syārthaprāpaṇaśakte"rbhedaḥ" | pūrvapratyakṣakṣaṇaviṣaya eva tebhyo 'pi pravṛtterādyasyaiva tatra prāmāṇyam | tathā hi- arthakriyārthināṃ tatsādhanaprāpaṇasamarthe jñāne pramāṇavyavahāraṃ kurvatāmaviklavadhiyāmarthakriyāsādhanabhedādeva prāmāṇyabhedavyavahāro jñāneṣu yuktaḥ anyathā smṛtyāderapi prāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ kathamapākriyeta?, ādriyeta vā niṣphalā pramāṇavyavasthā prekṣāvatā iti? |
children.translated_text: ) the blue continuum as a single object, as having a stable form, and the <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) to be accomplished by it as having a single nature — thus the validity of the subsequent [cognitions] too is undesired. So whence comes the non-exclusiveness? Showing this, he says "<s>sādhāraṇe hi</s> (for with respect to the common)" and so forth. With respect to what is common (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) to all the momentary instances belonging to that continuum, which are determined as one by the transactors — [namely] the blue-colored activity such as dyeing etc., which, though in reality distinct at each moment due to being caused by different causes, is clung to as unitary through the error [of cognizers] — "among them" (<s>na teṣām</s>), among the aforementioned cognition-moments, there is no "difference" in "capacity" (<s>sāmarthya</s>), i.e. in the power to bring about the object. Since activity arises from those [later cognitions] too only with respect to the object of the first perceptual moment, validity belongs only to the first [cognition] with respect to that [object]. For indeed — when those who desire <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) engage in the convention of calling a cognition a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) insofar as it is capable of bringing about the means of accomplishing that [causal efficacy], it is proper for those of undisturbed intellect that the convention of distinguishing validity among cognitions should be based on the difference in means of accomplishing <s>arthakriyā</s>. Otherwise, how could the consequence that even memory (<s>smṛti</s>) etc. would be valid be refuted? Or would a discerning person care about a fruitless establishment of valid means of knowledge?

body.translated_text: When streaming sensory cognitions arise with respect to one and the same object such as blue, there would be the unwanted consequence that the later sensory cognitions lack validity — because of having undifferentiated acquisition-and-preservation (<s>abhinnayogakṣematva</s>) with the earlier one. And since this is not the case, [there would be] inconclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>) — showing this, the advocate of the dissolution of all <s>pramāṇas</s> (<s>pramāṇasaṃplavavādin</s>) says: "By the earlier perceptual moment" and so on. He resolves this: "No" — there is no unwanted consequence of the later [cognitions] lacking validity. Why? "Because of differentiated acquisition-and-preservation" (<s>nānāyogakṣematva</s>). That is to say: at each moment, both the acquisition — characterized by the determination of the object — and the preservation — characterized by the accomplishment of <s>arthakriyā</s> with respect to that object, having the form of protection — are differentiated. Therefore, since the reason [cited by the opponent] does not occur in the counter-instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>), the reason is not inconclusive. When is there differentiated acquisition-and-preservation? "When there is desire for a result achievable in a specific moment." When there is desire — the wish to obtain or avoid — regarding a result characterized as beneficial or harmful that is achievable in a specific moment, [this obtains] for <s>Yogins</s> who act for the benefit of others, since [each moment] has some use for someone in some way. For example, on the path of insight (<s>darśanamārga</s>), the <s>dharmajñānakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance through knowledge of dharma) regarding suffering arrests the latent dispositions (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the latent afflictions (<s>anuśaya</s>), through the production of a mental disposition contrary to them. The <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharma) regarding suffering produces the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) characterized by freedom from afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), through the production of firmness in the mental disposition contrary to the latent afflictions. The cognitions of others' minds that apprehend these [moments] are separately valid <s>pramāṇas</s>. And for the Blessed Ones (<s>Bhagavat</s>, i.e., Buddhas), who have undertaken the vow of establishing others' welfare, whose inner being is illuminated by the light of knowledge pervading the expanse of all things — since some particular moment of purpose either benefits or binds some particular [being's] welfare — for those whose perceptual minds observe all existents at every moment, because of the differentiated <s>arthakriyā</s> of the moments [of cognition] directed toward those [objects], there is differentiated acquisition-and-preservation. Therefore, if [the statement] is made with reference to those who perceive the discrimination of moments at every instant, then because of differentiated utility, there is separate validity [for each moment], and so there is no inconclusiveness. But if [the statement] is made with reference to ordinary persons engaged in conventional [cognition], who determine unity with respect to all objects, then the entire

body.text: keṣāmiva sādhāraṇe kārye na sāmarthyabhedaḥ? ityāha- "aparāpare" ca te "dhūmā"śca taiḥ "pramitā"śca te "sannikṛṣṭāgraya"śca teṣviva tadviṣayāṇamiva "anumānajñānāmagnimātrasādhye 'rthe" sandhukṣaṇādike vāñchite tadarthakriyāsādhanaprāpaṇavyaktibhedābhāvāt yathā prāmāṇyabhedo na yukto viduṣāṃ tathātrāpi | yadā tu pañcatapastaptukāmo bhavati tadāparāparadhūmapramitasannikṛṣṭāgniviṣayāṇāmapyanumānānāṃ sāmarthyabhedāt prāmāṇyamanivāritameva |
body.translated_text: With respect to what kind of common effect is there no difference in capacity? He says: "The successive" — and those "smokes" — and those "cognized" by them — and those "having fire as their proximate [object]" — just as among the inferential cognitions (<s>anumānajñāna</s>) whose object is those [successive smokes cognized with fire as proximate], "with respect to an object accomplishable by fire alone" — such as the desired [activity of] kindling etc. — because there is no difference in the manifestation of the means of accomplishing that <s>arthakriyā</s>, just as a difference in validity is not warranted for the learned, so too here. But when one desires to perform the five-fire austerity (<s>pañcatapas</s>), even among the inferences whose object is fire proximate to successively cognized smokes, validity is indeed unrestricted due to the difference in capacity.

body.text: 27. vikalpaprāmāṇyanirāsasya phalitārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 27. The implication of the refutation of the validity of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>).

body.text: tadevaṃ ‘yathā nīlaṃ dṛṣṭvā nīlamiti jñān(m)'; ityudāharaṇe nīlavikalpasya prāmāṇyaṃ nirākṛtya prakṛte yojayannāha- "etena" nīlasvalakṣaṇadarśanottarakālabhāvino nīlavikalpasya prāmāṇyanirākaraṇena |
body.translated_text: Thus, having refuted the validity of the blue-<s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition of blue) in the example 'having seen blue, the cognition "it is blue",' he now applies this to the main topic, saying: "By this" — by the refutation of the validity of the blue-<s>vikalpa</s> that arises subsequent to the perception of the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) of blue —

body.text: "tanneṣṭatvād vikalpasyārtharūpopakāriṇaḥ |"
body.translated_text: "Because the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) that assists the real nature of objects is not accepted by them [as valid]."

The prior perception itself, which has the <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particular) as its object — what the opponent calls apprehensive cognition (<s>ālocanājñāna</s>) — that is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), but not the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual cognition) that arises subsequent to it, by the reasoning stated above. body.translated_text: 28. Indicating the primacy of inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.translated_text: ) From the declaration that "perception itself is the <s>pramāṇa</s>," it is indicated that the <s>pramāṇa</s> itself is the result (<s>phala</s>), because it has the nature of apprehension of the object. Likewise, because it will be stated that its application is twofold, inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) will be discussed, because it has the nature of stating the triple-characterized logical mark (<s>trirūpaliṅga</s>). And in brief, the elucidation of inference too is intended. Since all this belongs to inference alone, why was it said "for the purpose of elucidating inference"?

body.translated_text: If so, why was it said "this is undertaken for the purpose of elucidating inference (<s>anumāna</s>)" and not 'for the purpose of elucidating valid cognition (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) in general'? The dispute with the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> and others regarding the subject matter is also resolved here. For the apprehension of imperceptible objects, inference [alone is the] basis. Why? Because it has been stated that only a <s>hetu</s> (logical reason) that is a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) and is pervaded in that aspect is the cause of such [apprehension], and nothing else — therefore all valid cognition concerning imperceptible objects is subsumed under inference. Thus, in brief, the dispute with the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> regarding valid cognition is resolved. Likewise, because of the understanding that the pervaded aspect is what is to be inferred, by the statement of pervasion of that aspect, it is declared that inference has universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) as its object, not particulars (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), because the particular is unique (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>), and because what is unique cannot be a pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>), and because [the particular] is not an object of conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>). By stating "there, the first of those has a unique object (<s>asādhāraṇaviṣaya</s>)," perception alone is declared to have <s>svalakṣaṇa</s> (particulars) as its object. (

body.text: satyam, prādhānyāt tu tadgrahaṇam | tatā hi- pradhānapuruṣārthopayoginastattvasya caturāryasatyalakṣaṇasyānumānata eva niścayāt tasya prādhānyam | tathā pratyakṣe 'pi viṣaye vivādasambhave, nānumānādanyannirṇayanibandhanam ityato 'pyasya prādhānyam | pravartakatvācca prādhānyamasya | tathā hi- yadanubhūtaphalaṃ sukhaduḥkhasādhanam, anubhūyamānaphalaṃ vā dṛśyamānaṃ tatpravṛttiviṣayo nispannatvāt phalasya | tasmād yadanāgataphalaṃ sukhaduḥkhasādhanaṃ pratyakṣamapi tatrāpyanumānameva pravartakam | na hi tasyānāgate sukhaduḥkhe prati yogyatāṃ pratyakṣaṃ nirddhārayati, phalasya parokṣatvāt | taduktam- " na hyapratyakṣe kārye kāraṇabhāvagatiḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: True, but that term is used because of [inference's] primacy. For indeed — because the ascertainment of reality (<s>tattva</s>) characterized by the four noble truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>), which serves the chief human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>), comes from inference alone, inference has primacy. Likewise, even in a matter that is perceptible, when a dispute arises, there is no other basis for resolution than inference — hence too its primacy. And its primacy is due to its being the motivator of action (<s>pravartaka</s>). For indeed — that which has an already-experienced result, being a means to pleasure or pain, or that which has a presently-experienced result that is being perceived — action toward that is possible because the result is already accomplished. Therefore, even for that which is perceptible but has a future result as a means to pleasure or pain, inference alone is what motivates action even there. For perception does not determine its capacity with respect to future pleasure or pain, because the result is imperceptible. As it is said: "For there is no cognition of the causal relation with respect to an imperceptible effect."

body.text: tasmāt pūrvānubhūtasukhaduḥkhasādhanasādharmyāt pratyakṣaviṣayasyāpi vastuno 'nāgataphalayogyatāniścayaḥ na pratyakṣataḥ | tathā cāha- "tadyathādṛṣṭasādharmyāt tathāprasādhitaṃ nānumeyatāmatipatati" iti | kathaṃ tarhi dvayorapi pravartakatvam? "na hyābhyāmarthaṃ paricchidya pravartamāno 'rthakriyāyāṃ visaṃvādyate" ityuktam | sukhaduḥkhasādhanasya jalānalādeḥ svarūpasya pratyakṣataḥ prasiddheḥ, phalamanāgataṃ prati yogyatāyā anumānata ityubhayorapi pravartakatvam | samyagjñānapūrvakatvaṃ ca hitāhitaprāptiparihārayoraktam na tvanāgataphalaṃ prati yogyatāyāḥ pratyakṣato 'niścayāt | na hyarvāgdarśināṃ bhāviphalayogyatāyāstato niścayaḥ, tataḥ prādhānyādanumānagrahaṇamityalamativistareṇeti |
body.translated_text: Therefore, even for a perceptible thing, the ascertainment of its capacity for a future result is not from perception, but from its similarity to previously experienced means of pleasure and pain. And thus he says: "That which has not been established through the similarity of what has been observed does not transcend the status of being something to be inferred." How then is the motivating capacity of both [perception and inference]? It is said: "One who, having ascertained the object through both of these, engages in action, is not deceived in <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy)." Since the intrinsic nature of what is a means to pleasure or pain — water, fire, etc. — is established through perception, and the capacity for a future result is [established] through inference, both have the power to motivate action. And it is said that correct cognition (<s>samyagjñāna</s>) as a prerequisite pertains to the attainment and avoidance of what is beneficial and harmful, but not to the ascertainment of capacity for a future result from perception, since those who do not see beyond [the present] do not have certainty of the capacity for a future result from perception. Therefore, inference is mentioned because of its primacy — enough with excessive elaboration.

body.text: 29. svabhāvahetāvanvayaniścayaḥ svapramāṇāyattaḥ |
body.translated_text: 29. The ascertainment of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) in the case of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-reason) depends on its own means of valid cognition.

body.text: tatra svabhāvakāryānupalambhānāṃ pakṣadharmaniścayastulyopāyasādhyatayābhedenaivoktaḥ anvayavyatirekaniścayasya tu bhinnopāyasādhyatayā bhedenaiva nirddeśaḥ kārya iti svabhāvahetau tāvadanvayaniścayaṃ svapramāṇanibandhanaṃ darśayannāha- "anvayaniścayo 'pi" na kevalaṃ pakṣadharmaniścaya uktaḥ kintvanvayaniścayo 'pi "svabhāvahetau" ucyata iti śeṣaḥ | "sādhanadharma" sya yad "bhāvamātraṃ" sattāmātraṃ mugdarādinimittantarānapekṣaṃ tasya "anubandho" anugamanaṃ vyāptiḥ tasya "siddhiḥ" yā sa svabhāvahetāvanvayaniścayaḥ | kasya sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandhasiddhiḥ? | "sādhyadharmasya" sādhyaścāsau asiddhatvāt dharmadharmisamudayaikadeśatvāt dharmaśceti tathoktaḥ | yatra yatra sādhanadharmasya bhāvaḥ tatra tatra sādhyadharmasyāpi nimittāntarānapekṣo bhava ityetasyārthasya siddhiḥ svabhāvahetāvanvayaniścayaḥ | kathaṃ punaḥ sādhyadharmaḥ sādhanadharmabhāvamātramanubadhnāti |? "tadbhāvatayā" sa sādhanadharmo bhāvaḥ- svabhāvo yasya tasya bhāvatayā tadbhāvatayā | yo hi sādhanadharmaḥ sādhyadharmasya svabhāvaḥ sa kathaṃ taṃ nānubadhnīyāt, nīrūpatvaprasaṅgāt? |
body.translated_text: There, the ascertainment of the thesis-property (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) for the <s>svabhāva</s> (nature), <s>kārya</s> (effect), and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension) [reasons] has been stated without differentiation, since the means of accomplishment are the same. But the ascertainment of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) is presented with differentiation, since the means of accomplishment are different. Showing the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-reason) first, as depending on its own means of valid cognition, he says: "The ascertainment of positive concomitance too" — not only has the ascertainment of the thesis-property been stated, but the ascertainment of positive concomitance too "in the case of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>" — is stated, this is the remainder. What is the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>? It is the establishment of the "concomitance" (<s>anubandha</s>) — the invariable accompaniment, the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) — of the "<s>sādhyadharma</s>" (property to be proved) with "the mere existence" (<s>bhāvamātra</s>) — mere being, independent of any other cause such as a pestle etc. — of the "<s>sādhanadharma</s>" (proving property). Of whom is this establishment of concomitance with the mere existence of the proving property? Of the "<s>sādhyadharma</s>" — which is called thus because it is to be proved (<s>asiddha</s>) and because it is a part of the aggregate of property and property-bearer. The meaning is: the establishment of the fact that wherever there is the existence of the proving property, there too is the existence of the property to be proved, independent of any other cause — this is the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>. But how does the property to be proved accompany the mere existence of the proving property? "By virtue of being its nature" (<s>tadbhāvatayā</s>) — by virtue of being the nature, i.e. the essential being, of that proving property. For the proving property that is the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of the property to be proved — how could it fail to accompany it, since [otherwise] there would be the absurd consequence of [the thing] being without any nature at all?

body.text: 30. svabhāvahetāvaikyepi sādhyasādhanabhāvavyavasthā |
body.translated_text: 30. The establishment of the <s>sādhya-sādhana</s> (probandum-probans) relationship even when there is identity in the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-reason).

body.text: nanu tatsvabhāvatve bhedābhāvāt kathaṃ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ? ityāha- "vastutaḥ" paramārthataḥ | sādhyasādhanasaṃkalpakāle tu paramparayā tattadvayāvṛttapadārthanibandhanāyāṃ kalpanābuddhau bhedena pratibhāsanāt sādhyasādhanabhāvo na vihanyate | na hyasau pāramārthikaṃ sādhyasādhanadharmayorddharmiṇaśca kṛtakatvādau bhedamavalambate, sambandhābhāvena sādhyasādhanabhāvāyogāt |
body.translated_text: Objection: If it is of that nature, then since there is no difference, how can there be a <s>sādhya-sādhana</s> (probandum-probans) relationship? He says: "In reality" (<s>vastutaḥ</s>) — in the ultimate sense. But at the time of the supposition of probandum and probans, since in the conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanābuddhi</s>) — which is ultimately grounded in the exclusion of the referents of both those [terms] — they appear as different, the probandum-probans relationship is not undermined. For that [relationship] does not depend on an ultimate difference between the probandum-property, the probans-property, and the property-bearer in being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) etc., since in the absence of a [real] relation, the probandum-probans relationship would be impossible.

children.text: ) sambandhābhāvasya tadavasthatvāt, sambandhāntarakalpanāyāṃ cānavasthāprasaṅgāt | samavāyād vṛttikalpanāyāṃ ca kṛtakatvādayo nityābhimateṣvapyātmādiṣu varteran | ya eva hi kṛtakatvādeḥ śabde samavāyo yabdalāt tatraiva tad vartate sa eva nityābhimateṣvapi, tasyaikatvenopagatatvāt ityātmādau vṛttiḥ kṛtakatvādeḥ kena nivāryeta? | atha ‘ya evābhūtvā bhavanadharmā bhūtvā cābhavanadharmāsthirarūpo bhāvaḥ tatraiva kṛtakatvādayo dharmā vartante '; iti vyavasthāpyate | saiva tarhyabhūtvā bhavanasvabhāvatā bhūtasya cāsthirasvabhāvatā tadviparītarūpasamāropavyavacchedaviṣayāyāḥ kalpanābuddhernibandhanaṃ kiṃ neṣyate? | tayaiva paramārthābhedavatorddharmayoḥ sādhyadharmiṇi vṛtteḥ kimantarālagaḍunā kṛtakatvādinā vyatirekavatā upagatena? | tathā hi- na sattāmātreṇa kṛtakatvādayo dharmāḥ sādhyadharmapratipattinibandhanam, teṣāṃ sadā sannihitatvenānavarataṃ taddharmapratītiprasaṅgāt, kintu vikalpapratibhāsina eva | sa ca vikalpaḥ svapratibhāsinamevakāraṃ bahīrūpatayādhyavasitamanusaran kṛtakānityādirūpatāṃ vastunaḥ pratipadyate, paramārthato 'saṃsparśe 'pi tadrūpasya, paramparayā tadupādānatvāt | vyatiriktāstu dharmāstudutpattinimittamātratayā parikalpyante, tad varaṃ yadeva tatkalpanānnibandhanaṃ tadeva tathāvidhavikalpaprasavanimittamastu, tasyāvaśyamabhyupagamanīyatvāt, tadabhyupagame ca caritārthā vyatirekavanto dharmā ityalaṃ tatkalpanayā | avaśyaṃ ca vyatiriktānityatādvāreṇāpi vastuna evānavasthāyinamātmānaṃ pratipadyate, tadanurūpārthakṛ(kri)yārthitayā pravṛtteḥ, anyathā vyatiriktānityatayā nityatvāt tadavagamārthitvenāyamanityasādhyārthakriyārthī nityaṃ śabdādikamāśaṅkamānaḥ kimanityatāvicāraṃ prati āhītāsthaḥ? | (
children.translated_text: ) because the absence of relation remains in the same predicament [as before], and because positing yet another relation would lead to an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). And if activity is to be postulated through <s>samavāya</s>, then being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) etc. would be present even in things regarded as eternal, such as the <s>ātman</s> (self) etc. For indeed, the very same <s>samavāya</s> that [is supposed to connect] being-produced etc. with sound — since [you hold] that it is present there because of <s>samavāya</s> — that same [<s>samavāya</s>] would be present in things regarded as eternal too, since it is accepted as being unitary. So what would prevent being-produced etc. from being present in the <s>ātman</s> etc.? If it is maintained: 'Being-produced and other properties are present only in that entity which has the characteristic of coming into being after not having been, and of not persisting after having come into being — i.e. in an impermanent entity' — then why not accept that very nature of coming into being after not having existed, and the impermanent nature of what has come into being, as the basis for the conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanābuddhi</s>) that operates by excluding the superimposition of a contrary nature? Given that the activity of the two properties in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (property-bearer to be proved) is [established] by that very [nature] which is ultimately non-different, what is the use of the intermediary fiction of being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) etc., which is accepted as something distinct? For indeed — the properties such as being-produced are not the basis of apprehending the property to be proved merely by their existence, since as they are always present, there would be the absurd consequence of unceasing apprehension of that property; rather, only insofar as they appear in conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>). And that conceptual cognition, pursuing the form appearing in itself as though it were external, determines the being-produced-and-impermanent nature of the real entity, even though that form is ultimately untouched [by reality], because it is indirectly derived from it. Distinct properties are postulated merely as the cause of origination. It is better, then, that whatever is the basis of that conceptual construction be itself the cause of the arising of such conceptual cognition, since it must necessarily be accepted; and once that is accepted, the distinct properties have served their purpose — so enough with postulating them. And necessarily, even through the channel of a distinct impermanence, one apprehends the transient nature of the entity itself, because action is undertaken in accordance with the <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) corresponding to that. Otherwise, since due to distinct impermanence [the thing itself would be] permanent, one who desires the <s>arthakriyā</s> that is the purpose of proving impermanence, suspecting that sound etc. is permanent — why would he be unconcerned about investigating impermanence? body.text: ye 'pi jaiminīyā manyante- ‘yeṣāmatyantavyatirekavanto dharmāḥ teṣāmevāyaṃ naiyāyikādīnāṃ doṣaḥ, asmākaṃ tu kathañcid bhedābhedavatāṃ dharmāṇāṃ tatsvabhāvatayā naiṣa doṣaḥ'; iti; teṣāmapi vastutaḥ sādhanadharmarūpatopagame sādhyadharmasya, kathañcid bhedābhyupagame na kiñcit phalamutpaśyāmaḥ, sādhyasādhanabhāvasya kalpitabhedadvāreṇāpyupapatteḥ | na caikātmye kathañcidapi bhedo yuktaḥ, ekasmāt svabhāvādabhedāt | tato 'pi tayoḥ kathañcid bhedābhedau sta eveti cet; na, anavasthāprasaṅgāt | tathā hi- dharmayostadekasvabhāvādapi bhedavatostena svabhāvena kathañcidabhedanimittamabhinno 'paraḥ svabhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ, tathā tenāpyaparaḥ ityanantaiva bhinnābhinnasvabhāvaparamparā syāt | na ca kalpanābuddhāvanantobhayarūpasvabhāvaparamparā pratibhāsata iti kimiti tatkalpanayātmānaṃ vipralabhante bhavantaḥ? | kathañcit ca bhedopagamāt kathaṃ bhedapakṣabhāvināṃ doṣāṇāmanavasaraḥ? | yaṃ cātmānaṃ purodhāya ‘imau dharmau, ayaṃ dharmī'; iti vyavasthāpyate yadi tena bhedastadā bheda eveti kuto 'nekāntavādaḥ? | athābhedaḥ; tadā ‘ayaṃ sādhanadharmaḥ, ayaṃ sādhyadharmaḥ, dharmī cāyam'; iti kathaṃ pāramārthikaṃ tṛ(tri)tayaṃ sidhyet? | tasmāt tattatpararūpavyāvṛttisamāśrayāyāṃ kalpanābuddhau bhedavatāmiva dharmadharmiṇāṃ pratibhāsanāt sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ | tanmātrānubandhastu vastutaḥ tattatsvabhāvatayaiva yuktaḥ iti manyamānena "vastutastadbhāvatayā" ityuktam |
body.translated_text: Those <s>Jaiminīya</s>s who think: 'This fault of the <s>Naiyāyika</s>s and others applies only to those whose properties are absolutely distinct; but for us, whose properties are somehow both different and non-different (<s>bhedābheda</s>), this fault does not arise since they are of that nature (<s>tatsvabhāvatā</s>)' — even for them, when they accept in reality that the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) has the nature of the proving property (<s>sādhanadharma</s>), we see no purpose in admitting some kind of difference, since the relation of provable and prover (<s>sādhyasādhanabhāva</s>) is established even through a posited distinction. Nor is any kind of difference justified when there is identity, since from one nature there is non-difference. If [one objects] that from that very [nature] there somehow exist both difference and non-difference of those two — no, because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>). For thus: even if the two properties have one nature, yet being different, through that nature another nature must be posited as the ground of their somehow being non-different; and likewise through that [nature] yet another — so there would be an endless series of distinct and non-distinct natures. And since no endless series of natures of both kinds appears in conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanābuddhi</s>), why do you deceive yourselves by imagining it? And since difference is admitted in some way, how is there no occasion for the faults that attend the position of difference? If the self (<s>ātman</s>) — putting which forward one establishes 'these are the properties, this is the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>)' — is different [from them], then it is simply difference, so whence the doctrine of non-exclusiveness (<s>anekāntavāda</s>)? But if [there is] non-difference, then how could the threefold [distinction] — 'this is the proving property, this is the property to be proved, and this is the property-bearer' — be established in ultimate reality? Therefore, since in conceptual cognition (<s>kalpanābuddhi</s>), which depends on exclusion from what is other than each respective [entity], properties and property-bearers appear as if different, there is the relation of provable and prover (<s>sādhyasādhanabhāva</s>). But the invariable connection with the mere existence of the proving property is in reality justified only by being of the nature of each respective [entity] — thinking thus, he said "in reality, by being of that nature" (<s>vastutastadbhāvatayā</s>).

body.text: 31. bādhakapramāṇādeva svabhāvahetau sādhyasādhanatādātmyam |
body.translated_text: 31. In the case of <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential reason), the identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) of what is to be proved and the prover is [established
only through <s>bādhakapramāṇa</s> (countervailing evidence).]

body.text: kā punarasau vastutastadbhāvatā yayā hetubhūtayā sādhyadharmasya sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandhaḥ sidhyati? ityāha- "sā" vastutastadbhāvatā "sādhya"sya "viparyayo" vipakṣaḥ tatra, "hetoḥ" yad "bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ" tadviparītadharmapratyavasthāpakam, yena bādhyamāno hetustatra na pravartate, viruddhayorekatra sahabhāvāsambhavāt, tasya yā "vṛtti" pravṛttiḥ "bādhakapramāṇavṛttiḥ" tatsādhyatvācca vastutastadbhāvatāyāḥ sā bādhakapramāṇavṛttiruktā | tasyāṃ hi satyāṃ vipakṣāt nivṛtto hetuḥ sādhyadharmavatyeva dharmiṇi vartate iti sādhyadharmasyānarthāntarasya sādhanadharmasvabhāvatā sidhyati | "tayā ca" vastutastadbhāvatayā sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandhaḥ sādhyadharmasya sidhyatīti "anvayaniścayaḥ" ‘yatra yatra sādhanadharmastatra tatra sādhyadharmaḥ'; ityevaṃrūpo jāyate |
body.translated_text: What then is this 'being of that nature in reality' (<s>vastutastadbhāvatā</s>), which, serving as the reason, establishes the invariable connection of the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) with the mere existence of the proving property (<s>sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandha</s>)? To this he says: That 'being of that nature in reality' — the opposite of the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), i.e., the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar instance), therein, the <s>bādhakapramāṇa</s> (countervailing evidence) regarding the <s>hetu</s> (reason), which establishes the opposite property — by which the reason, being contradicted, does not operate there, since the co-presence of contradictory [properties] in one [locus] is impossible — its operation (<s>vṛtti</s>), i.e., functioning, is the 'operation of countervailing evidence' (<s>bādhakapramāṇavṛtti</s>); and since 'being of that nature in reality' is established by that, that operation of countervailing evidence is stated. For when that obtains, the reason, excluded from the <s>vipakṣa</s>, operates only in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) that possesses the property to be proved, and thus the nature of the property to be proved — which is nothing other [than the proving property] — as being of the nature of the proving property is established. "And through that" 'being of that nature in reality,' the invariable connection of the property to be proved with the mere existence of the proving property is established — thus the "ascertainment of positive concomitance" (<s>anvayaniścaya</s>) of the form 'wherever there is the proving property, there is the property to be proved' arises.

body.text: atrodāharaṇaṃ "yathā- yat sat tat kṣaṇikameva |" avadhāraṇena vyāptimāha | sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandhasya caitadrūpamākhyātaṃ, nimittāntaramantareṇa sat ityeva kṛtvā kṣaṇikamityupadarśanāt | sa ca vastutastadbhāvatayā sidhyatīti tatsiddhyupāyaṃ bādhakapramāṇavṛttiṃ darśayati- "akṣaṇikatve" kṣaṇikaviparyaye sati "artha kriyāvirodhāt" arthasya- kāryasya kriyā- niṣpattistasyā virodhāt "tallakṣaṇaṃ" sārthakriyā lakṣaṇaṃ yasya "vastutvasya" arthakriyāsāmarthyātmana, tattathoktam | arthakriyayā hi tatsāmarthyarūpaṃ vastutvaṃ lakṣyate | "tad" evaṃvidhaṃ vastutvaṃ "hīyate" nivartate, tadviparyayarūpasyāsattvasyākarṣaṇāt | etacca bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ vyāpakānupalabdhirūpamuttaratrāvasaraprāptaṃ svayameva vakṣyati | tadanayā bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā sādhyadharmasya vastutaḥ sādhanadharmasvabhāvatā sidhyati | tayā ca vastutastadbhāvatayā sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānubandha iti |
body.translated_text: Here the example is: "Whatever is real (<s>sat</s>) is momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>) alone." By the emphatic particle he states the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion). And this is declared as the form of the invariable connection with the mere existence of the proving property, since without any other ground, merely by being real, momentariness is shown. And since that is established through 'being of that nature in reality,' he shows the means of establishing it, namely the operation of countervailing evidence: "In the case of non-momentariness" — when there is the opposite of momentariness — "because of the contradiction with causal efficacy" (<s>arthakriyāvirodha</s>), i.e., because of the contradiction with the accomplishment of an effect (<s>artha</s> = <s>kārya</s>) — "that characterized" means that whose characteristic is causal efficacy — "of realness" (<s>vastutva</s>), i.e., of that whose nature is the capacity for causal efficacy — that is so stated. For realness, whose nature is such capacity, is characterized by causal efficacy. "That" realness of such a kind "is negated" (<s>hīyate</s>), ceases, because the opposite — unrealness — is drawn in. And this countervailing evidence, which has the form of non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>), he will himself explain later when the occasion arises. Thus, through this operation of countervailing evidence, the nature of the property to be proved as being in reality of the nature of the proving property is established. And through that 'being of that nature in reality,' there is the invariable connection with the mere existence of the proving property.

body.text: 32. kāryahetāvanvayaniścayanirūpaṇam |
body.translated_text: 32. Determination of positive concomitance (<s>anvayaniścaya</s>) in the case of <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-reason).
