body.text: evaṃ svabhāvahetau viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tādātmyasiddhito 'nvayaniścayaṃ pratipādya koryahetau pratipādapannāha- "kāryahetau" anvayaniścayaḥ iti prakṛtam | kaḥ punarasau kāryakāraṇayorbhāvaḥ? | "kāryatvaṃ" "kāraṇatvaṃ" ca | tasya yā "siddhiḥ" pratītiḥ sā kāryahetāvanvayaniścayaḥ | yathā ca kāryakāṃraṇabhāvasiddhirbhavati tathopadarśayannāha- "yathā" ityādi | yathāśabda upadarśanārthaḥ | "idaṃ" dhūmādikam "asya" agneḥ "upalambhe" sati "upalabhyata" iti sambandhaḥ | anena kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau pratyakṣavyāpāramāha | na ca kevalaṃ pratyakṣaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvamasandigdhaṃ sādhayati, kintu prākpravṛttānupalambhasahāyamiti darśayitumāha- "upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptamānupalabdham" iti | yadi tad dhūmādikamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ satsvanyai(nye)ṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu dṛśyātmakaṃ sat nopalabdhaṃ bhavati agnyādisāmagrīsannidhānāt prāk tādātmyādisāmagryāmupalabhyamānāyāmupalabhyamānaṃ tatkāryaṃ sidhyati | na tūpalambhapratyayāntaravaikalyādanupajātopalabdhiyogyarūpaṃ sat, taddeśasannihitamapyanupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatayāgnyādisāmagrīsannidhānāt prāganupalabdhamiti | upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya cānupalambhe nāgnyādisāmagrīsannidhānāt prāganyata āgamanaṃ, taddeśakālasaṃnnihitāt katakuṭyā derutpattiḥ, taddeśe cāsannidhānamiti, tritayamapākriyate | etāvadbhiśca prakārairatatkāryatā bhavantī bhavet | tato 'nupalambhenātatkāryatāśaṅkānirāsād tadbhāve bhāvagrāhipratyakṣanibandhanaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'sandigdhaḥ sidhyati |
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated the ascertainment of positive concomitance (<s>anvayaniścaya</s>) for <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential reason) through the establishment of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) by the operation of countervailing evidence in the opposite case, he now explains it for <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-reason): "In the case of <s>kāryahetu</s>" — the ascertainment of positive concomitance is the topic under discussion. What then is this relation of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>)? "Effect-ness" (<s>kāryatva</s>) and "cause-ness" (<s>kāraṇatva</s>). Its "establishment" (<s>siddhi</s>), i.e., cognition, is the ascertainment of positive concomitance in the case of <s>kāryahetu</s>. Showing how the establishment of the cause-effect relation occurs, he says: "As" and so forth. The word 'as' (<s>yathā</s>) is for the purpose of illustration. "This" — smoke and so on — "of this" — of fire — "when apprehended" (<s>upalambhe sati</s>) — "is apprehended" — such is the construction. By this he states the role of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) in establishing the cause-effect relation. And it is not perception alone that establishes the cause-effect relation without doubt, but rather [perception] assisted by prior non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) — to show this he says: "not apprehended [though] having fulfilled the conditions for apprehension" (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptam anupalabdham</s>). If that smoke and so on, having fulfilled the conditions for apprehension — being of a perceptible nature when the other conditions of apprehension are present — is not apprehended prior to the presence of the assemblage of [causes] such as fire, then when such an assemblage of [causes like] identity and so on is apprehended, that which is apprehended is established as an effect. But it is not the case that [something] whose perceptible form has not arisen due to the absence of other conditions of apprehension, even though present in that location, is [regarded as] not apprehended prior to the presence of the fire-assemblage by having fulfilled the conditions for non-apprehension. And by the non-apprehension of what has fulfilled the conditions for apprehension, three [alternative explanations] are eliminated: [the smoke's] coming from elsewhere prior to the presence of the fire-assemblage, its arising from a wall etc. present in that place and time, and its not being present in that place. By these [three] ways, it could be non-effect-ness. Therefore, through non-apprehension, by the removal of the doubt of non-effect-ness, the cause-effect relation, which is grounded in perception that grasps existence in the presence [of the cause] and [established] in the presence of that [cause], is established beyond doubt.

body.text: na cāgnīndhanādibhāve niyatasannidheradṛśyātmanaḥ kutaścit dhūmasya bhāvaḥ syāt ityāśaṅkanīyam | agnīndhanādibhedānuvidhānād dhūmasya | candanāgurukarpūrakeśorṇādīndhanabhede tadanurūpabhedasyāsya darśanādalpamahadindhanavikārakāriṇaścāgnestadanurūpasya | na cāgnīndhanādisannidhāvadṛśyātmano niyatasannidhānatā yuktā, (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 46

children.text: ) pratibandhābhāvāt | pratibandhe vā tatkāryatā tatkāraṇatā vā syāt | tatkāryatve, nāgnīndhanasamparkānantaraṃ dhūmajanma syāt, tadbhāvābhāvānuvidhānādeva cāsyāpi tatkāryatvam | tacca dhūme 'pi samānam | nāpīndhanādikāraṇatvam adṛśyātmanaḥ, indhanādeḥ svahetoreva vṛkṣāderbhāvadarśanāt | tatrāpi tathābhāvakalpanāyāṃ tadevottaraṃ vācyam | punaścodye sa eva parihāro 'navasthā ca | etenaikasāmagryadhīnatāpi pratyuktā | tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānādeva ca dhūmasya tat kāraṇaṃ kalpeta | taccāgnyādāvapi tulyam | tadapi tatra kāraṇamastu iti cet; na, agnayādibhāve 'vaśyambhāvino 'nyasyāpi kāraṇatvakalpanāyāṃ nimittābhāvāt, kāryavyatirekanibandhanatvāt kāraṇabhāvakalpanāyāḥ | yathā agnīndhanā derevānyatarābhāve abhavataḥ | bhavatu vānyasyāpi tadbhāve niyatasannidheḥ kāraṇatā | na tu tāvatāgnyādeḥ kāraṇatvahāniḥ, yato dhūmadarśanāt tanniścayena pravṛttau tadvisaṃvādaḥ syāt | nahi sarvasattvakarmādhipatyajanitatve 'pi jagadvaicitryasya dṛṣṭakāraṇahānitastatkāryadarśanād vā pravṛttānāṃ atatprāptirityalamatiprasaṅgena |
children.translated_text: because there is no causal restriction (<s>pratibandha</s>). Or if there were a restriction, it would be either an effect-ness of that [entity with respect to fire etc.] or a cause-ness of that [entity with respect to fire etc.]. If it were an effect, then the birth of smoke would not occur immediately after the contact of fire and fuel, since this [smoke] too would be an effect of that [invisible entity] precisely because it conforms to the presence and absence of that. And the same [argument] applies to smoke as well. Nor is an invisible entity the cause of fuel and so on, since fuel and the like are seen to arise from their own causes such as trees. If such a state were imagined even there, the same reply must be given. And upon further objection, the same refutation [applies], and there is infinite regress. By this, dependence on a single assemblage is also answered. And since smoke conforms to the positive and negative concomitance of that [fire etc.], that [fire etc.] would be posited as the cause. But the same applies to fire and so on [with respect to the invisible entity]. Let that also be a cause there — if so, no, because there is no ground for positing the cause-ness of yet another [entity] that must exist whenever fire and so on exist, since the positing of cause-ness is grounded in the absence of the effect [in the absence of the cause]. Just as in the absence of either fire or fuel, [smoke] does not exist. Or even if some other [entity] that is invariably present when that [fire etc. is present] were [admitted as] a cause, still there is no loss of the cause-ness of fire and so on, such that there would be error for one who, upon seeing smoke, proceeds with certainty about that [fire]. For even if the diversity of the world is produced under the dominion of the <s>karma</s> of all beings, those who proceed upon seeing an effect of an observed cause do not fail to attain that [cause] due to the loss of the observed cause — but enough of this digression.

body.translated_text: Nor should one suspect that in the state of fire, fuel, and so on, smoke might arise from some invisible entity that is invariably present. For smoke conforms to the varieties of fire, fuel, and so on — since we observe its corresponding variation with differences in fuel such as sandalwood, aloe, camphor, hair, and wool, and [we observe] the fire that transforms small and large fuel [producing] a corresponding [smoke]. Nor is it reasonable that an invisible entity is invariably present in the proximity of fire, fuel, and so on,

body.text: kiṃrūpaḥ punarasau kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'nupalambhasahāyapratyakṣanibandhana ityāha- "tadbhāve bhāvaḥ tadabhāve 'bhāvaśca" iti | ya eva hi kāraṇābhimatasya bhāve bhāva eva | kāryatvenābhimatasya bhāvaḥ | "tadabhāve" kāraṇatvābhimatasyābhāve "abhāva eva" kāryatvenābhimatasyābhāvaśca | sa eva kāryakāraṇābhāvo nānyaḥ |
body.translated_text: What then is the nature of this cause-effect relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) that is grounded in perception assisted by non-apprehension? He says: "Existence in the presence of that, and absence in the absence of that." For it is precisely [this]: the existence of what is regarded as the effect occurs only in the presence of what is regarded as the cause; "in the absence of that" — in the absence of what is regarded as the cause — "only absence" — the absence of what is regarded as the effect. That alone is the cause-effect relation, nothing else.

body.text: sa hi tābhyāmanyo bhavan svabhāvato 'pratipannakāryakāraṇarūpayorvā bhaved, yadvā svabhāvenaiva kāryakāraṇātmanoḥ | yadyādyaḥ pakṣaḥ tadā sarvatraivākāryaka(kā)raṇabhūte 'pi vastuni bhavet tanniyamakāraṇābhāvāt | tataḥ sarvaṃ sarvasya kāryaṃ syāt | (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 47

children.text: ) svabhāvena cātadrūpasyānyayoge 'pi na tadrūpatā | nahi bhāvāḥ pratiniyatarūpatyāgenānyayoge 'pi rūpāntaramābhajante, yato nānyayogasteṣāṃ pūrvarūpaṃ nāśayati vināśahetvayogād vakṣyamāṇakāt | nāpyapūrvamutpādayati tasya tato 'rthāntaratvaprasaṅgāt | nahi teṣu niṣpanneṣvaniṣpanno bhinnahetuko vā tatsvabhāvo yuktaḥ | ayaṃ hi bhedo bhedaheturvā viruddhadharmādhyāsaḥ kāraṇa bhedaśca tataścet na bhedaḥ, anyanimittābhāvāt ekaṃ dravyaṃ viśvaṃ syāt ityādi prasajyeta | pratibhāsabhedo 'pi hi itaretarābhāvarūpatayā viruddhadharmādhyāsatāṃ nātikrāmati | tataśca pūrvake vastunī tadavasthe eveti na tayoranyayoge 'pi kāryakāraṇarūpatāpattiḥ |
children.translated_text: And if something not of that nature [i.e., not cause-effect] is conjoined with another, it does not [thereby] become of that nature. For entities do not acquire a different nature by abandoning their own determinate nature even when conjoined with others, since conjunction with another does not destroy their prior nature, due to the absence of a cause of destruction, as will be explained. Nor does it produce a new [nature], since that [new nature] would be something entirely different from it. For it is not reasonable that when those [entities] have already arisen, a nature belonging to them [could be] unarisen or having a different cause. For this difference, or the cause of difference, is the superimposition of contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s>) and difference of cause. If from that there is no difference [because these are absent], then since there is no other ground, one substance would be the universe — and so on would follow as absurd consequences. Even the difference in appearance, insofar as it consists in mutual absence, does not go beyond the superimposition of contradictory properties. Therefore the prior entities remain in exactly the same state, and thus even when conjoined with another, there is no arising of the cause-effect nature in them.

body.translated_text: For if it were something other than those two, it would either belong to [things] whose cause-effect nature is not [already] established by their own nature, or it would belong to [things] that are by their very nature of the nature of cause and effect. If the first alternative [is taken], then it would apply everywhere, even to things that are not in a cause-effect relation, since there is no ground for restricting it. Then everything would be the effect of everything.

body.text: atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ, tadā svabhāvata eva tayoḥ kāryakāraṇarūpatvādanyastadbhāvaḥ kathaṃ na vaiyarthyamanubhavet? | kāryakāraṇavuddhī api tadbhāvabhāvitvamātranibandhane nārthāntaranimitte, tasyopapalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya kāryakāraṇarūpavivekinā rūpāntareṇāpratibhāsanāt | tathāvidhasyāpi grahaṇakalpanāyāmatiprasaṅgaḥ | anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatāyāṃ kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvabuddhī tannibandhane? | nahi tad arthāntaraṃ svasattāmātreṇa tabduddhī pravartayati | sadā sannihitatvenāsya tayoḥ sarvadodayaprasaṅgāt | na ca viśeṣaṇamagṛhītaṃ viśeṣye svaviśiṣṭapratyayanibandhanamityayuktāsyānupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatā | na ca dṛṣṭasyāpyanupalakṣaṇaṃ yuktam, kāryakāraṇabuddhyostannibandhanatopagamāt | na hi yannimito yo 'nyatrātabduddhibhāji tabdyavasāyaḥ sa tadanupalakṣaṇe yuktaḥ | devadatte daṇḍivyavasāyavad daṇḍānupalakṣaṇe | na cārthāntarasya kāryakāraṇābhyāṃ sambandho ghaṭate, sambandhāntarakalpanāyāmanavasthāprasakteḥ | kāryakāraṇabhāvābhyupagame kāryakāraṇābhyāmasahabhāvitā sadbhāvasya | tataśca kāryakāraṇakāle tasyāsannidhānāt kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabuddhihetutā? | (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 48

children.text: ) niruddhayoradhyāhṛtya tatpratyayakalpanāyāṃ ca kalpitaviṣaya eva kāryakāraṇatādhyavasāyaḥ syāt na vastuviṣayaḥ | sa ca viśiṣṭabhāvābhāvanibandhano 'bhyupagata eveti kimarthāntarakalpanayā? | kalpitaviṣayatve tavdhyavasāyasya, tasyā vaiyarthyāt kāryakāraṇayoścāyaugapadyāt | hani tābhyāmasau janyate, pratyekajanyaśca kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ? | yadā ca kāraṇena janyate tadā kiṃ svakāryasahito janyate, atha kevalaḥ? | kevalo 'pi kiṃ svakāryāt prāg, atha paścāt? | yadi svakāryasahitastudubhayoranyata eva bhāvāt parasparamasambandha iti kāryasambandhitāsya hīyeta | atha kevalaḥ svakāryāt prāk; tadā kṣaṇikatayā kāraṇasya tameva janayitvā dhvaṃsāt kathaṃ svakāryakrīyā? | tasyāṃ cāsatyāṃ kathaṃ tadapekṣamasya kāraṇatvam? | tasmiṃścāsati kathamakāraṇena kāryakāraṇasambandho janyate? | atha svakāryaṃ kṛtvā paścājjanyeta tadāpi svakāryakāle eva vinaṣṭatvād asatastaduttarakālabhāvikāryakāraṇabhāvajananaṃ kutaḥ? | tadbhāvaśca sambandha ucyate |
children.translated_text: — and when [the two] that have ceased are supplied [by imagination], the determination of the causal relation in the construction of the cognition of those [supplied entities] would pertain only to a constructed object, not to a real object. And that [causal relation] is acknowledged to be grounded in the specific presence and absence [of the entities] — so what is the point of postulating something additional? Given that the determination pertains to a constructed object, that [postulation] would be pointless, and because the cause and effect are not simultaneous. For [if one asks:] is it produced by both of them, and if produced by each individually, how can there be a causal relation? And when it is produced by the cause, is it produced together with its own effect, or alone? If alone, is it before its own effect or after? If together with its own effect — then since both [cause and effect] exist at the same [time but] in alternation, they would be mutually unrelated, and thus its connection with the effect would be lost. But if alone and before its own effect — then, since the cause, being momentary, perishes after producing only that [effect], how can it perform its own effect-operation? And in the absence of that [operation], how can its being a cause, which depends on that [operation], hold? And in the absence of that [causal status], how can a causal relation be produced by what is not a cause? But if it were produced after performing its own effect — even then, having perished at the very time of its own effect, whence could the non-existent produce a causal relation pertaining to a subsequent time? And that [relation of] being-of-that is called the connection.

body.translated_text: If [one takes] the second alternative, then since those two are of cause-effect nature by their very nature, how would a separate 'being of that nature' (<s>tadbhāva</s>) not be rendered purposeless? The cognitions of cause and effect too would be grounded merely in the occurrence of 'being of that nature,' not occasioned by anything else, since that [separate entity], though fulfilling the conditions for apprehension, does not appear with a form that discriminates the cause-effect nature. And if the apprehension of even such [an entity] were imagined, there would be absurd over-extension. If it has fulfilled the conditions for non-apprehension, how could the cognitions of cause and effect be grounded in it? For that separate entity does not produce those cognitions merely by its own existence, since because it is always present, those [cognitions] would absurdly arise at all times. And it is not reasonable that it has fulfilled the conditions for non-apprehension, since a qualifier that is not grasped is the ground for the cognition qualified by itself regarding the qualificand. Nor is the non-characterization of what is perceived reasonable, given that the cognitions of cause and effect are accepted as grounded in it. For whatever is the ground for a certain cognition in something — [to say] that it is uncharacterized in what does not bear that cognition is not reasonable — like the ascertainment of 'possessing a staff' regarding <s>Devadatta</s> [not being reasonable] when the staff is uncharacterized. Nor can a relation of the separate entity with cause and effect be established, since in imagining another relation there would be the absurd consequence of infinite regress. If a cause-effect relation [of the separate entity with cause and effect] is accepted, then it cannot coexist with cause and effect. And therefore, since it is not present at the time of cause and effect, how can it be the ground for the cognitions of cause and effect?

body.text: ....................................................................................................................................................................................... janyatāyāṃ vā yadi samagrāḥ svarūpata eva tāṃ janayanti kārye ka eṣāṃ śaktivyāghātaḥ? yato 'nyatra kalpyate | tatrāpyaparasāmagrīyogāpekṣāyāṃ cānavasthāprasaṅgaḥ | tataḥ samagrā eva janakāḥ |
body.translated_text: ... Or in [the case of] production — if the aggregate [of conditions] by their own nature alone produces it, what obstruction of their capacity [is there] with respect to the effect? Such that [the capacity] must be postulated elsewhere. And even there, if [the effect] depends on a connection with another aggregate, there would be an infinite regress. Therefore, the aggregate alone are the producers.

body.text: teṣāṃ ca kāraṇatvamekaikāpāye kāryavyatirekataḥ samunnīyata ityāha- "satsvapyanyeṣu" tatsāmagryantargateṣu "hetuṣu" janakeṣu (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 49.

children.text: ) pratyekaṃ teṣāṃ vyañjanakatvād "asyābhāve" janakatvena nirddhāryamāṇatayā vivakṣitasyābhāve "na bhavati" ityanenānupalambhasya viṣaya uktaḥ | pratyakṣavṛttistu pūrvoktaivānupalambharahitā tadbhāve bhāvagrāhiṇī saṃbandhyate |
children.translated_text: — since each of them individually has the capacity to manifest [the effect] — "in the absence of this" — i.e., in the absence of the one that is intended to be determined as a producer — "it does not exist" — by this, the object of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) has been stated. And the perceptual operation is precisely as stated before — devoid of non-apprehension, grasping the presence [of the effect] when [the cause] is present — and is connected [with the causal determination].

body.translated_text: And their causal status is ascertained from the absence of the effect when each one individually is removed — he says: "Even when the other" causes included within that aggregate "are present"

body.text: tathā cāyamapi tadbhāve bhāvaḥ tadabhāve 'bhāvaśca kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ kiṃsādhanaḥ? ityāha- "pratyakṣānupalambhasādhanaḥ" pratyakṣapūrvako 'nupalambhaḥ tavdivikrānyapadārthagrāhipratyakṣātmakaḥ sādhanamasyeti "pratyakṣānupalambhasādhanaḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ" | yastvanupalambhasāpekṣeṇa pratyakṣeṇa sādhyata iti prāguktaḥ so 'nupalambhapūrvakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ sādhanamasyeti anupalambhapratyakṣasādhana iti vaktavyaḥ | "tasya" kāryakāraṇabhāvasyānvayavyatirekātmanaḥ "siddhiḥ" niścayo "yathoktābhyāṃ" pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryahetāvanvayaniścaya iti sambandhate |
body.translated_text: And thus, what is the means of establishing this causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) — namely, presence when [the cause] is present and absence when [the cause] is absent? He says: "Established through perception and non-apprehension" (<s>pratyakṣānupalambhasādhana</s>) — non-apprehension preceded by perception, having as its means the perception that grasps the other entities distinct from that [cause]; thus the causal relation is "established through perception and non-apprehension." But what is to be established by perception conjoined with non-apprehension

body.text: nanu cānvayaniścayo nāma kāryahetoḥ sarvatra kāryasya bhavataḥ svakāraṇasattayānugamanamityevamavasāyaḥ tat kathaṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhirevāsāvucyate? ityāśaṅkya kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinibandhanatvādanvayaniścayasya kāraṇe kāryopacārādananyopāyasādhyatāṃ darśayitum, darśanamātranibandhanaṃ ye tamicchanti tanmataniṣedhārthamasāvevamukta iti darśayannāha- "kāryakāraṇabhāva eva hi" kāryakāraṇabhāve satyeva ‘hiḥ'; yasmāt "arthāntarasya" sādhyād vyatiriktasya, yastvavyatiriktaḥ tasya viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tādātmyaniścayādevānvayaniścaya iti pūrvamuktamevetyarthāntaragrahaṇam | tasyārthāntarasya "evaṃ syāt" | katham? | ‘yatra nāma kvacid dhūmaḥ tatrāvaśyamagniḥ'; iti niyamena ‘agneḥ tatra bhāvaḥ'; ityevaṃrūpo 'nvayaniścayaḥ | yastvakāryakāraṇabhāve 'pi rasasyārthāntarasya rūpeṇānvayaniścayaḥ sa ekasāmagryadhīnatayā tasya svakāraṇāvyabhicāradvāraka evetyadoṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: — one might object: the determination of positive concomitance (<s>anvayaniścaya</s>) of the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>) means the determination that the effect of everything, being [what it is], follows the existence of its own cause. How then can this very [determination] be called the establishment of the causal relation? Anticipating this objection, in order to show that the determination of positive concomitance, being grounded in the establishment of the causal relation, is due to the figurative designation of the effect upon the cause and is not achievable by any other means — to show this to those who, relying merely on observation, consider that [positive concomitance is established otherwise]

body.text: atha yadi nāma kāryamagnerdhūmastathāpi kimiti yatrāsau tatrāvaśyamagnirbhavati yataḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinibandhano 'nvayaniścaya ucyata ityāha- "agneḥ bhāve eva" sattāyāmeva ‘hiḥ'; yasmāt "bhāvaḥ" sattā dhūmasya "kāryatvamiti" | tasmāt kāryakāraṇabhāve satyeva yathokto 'nvayaniścaya iti | yadi hi yatra dhūmastatrāvaśyamagnirna syāt tadāgnimantareṇāpyasya bhāvād agnibhāva eva bhāvalakṣaṇaṃ kāryatvaṃ hīyeta |
body.translated_text: — now, even if smoke is an effect of fire, why must fire necessarily exist wherever smoke exists, such that the determination of positive concomitance is said to be grounded in the establishment of the causal relation? He says: "Only in the presence of fire" — only when it exists — "smoke [exists]"; because "the existence" — the being — of smoke "is [due to its being] an effect" (<s>kāryatvam</s>). Therefore, only when the causal relation obtains does the determination of positive concomitance as described [hold]. For if

body.text: 33. anupalabdhāvanvayaniścayopāyakathanam |
body.translated_text: 33. Statement of the means for the determination of positive concomitance in the case of non-apprehension.

body.text: idānīmanupalabdhāvanvayaniścayamāha- "anupalabdhāvapi" na kevalaṃ svabhāvakāryaheto(tvo)ranvayaniścaya uktaḥ kintvanupalabdhāvapyanvayaniścaya ucyate | kiṃrūpo 'sau? ityāha- "asadvyavahārasya" sādhyadharmasya yogyatāyāśca sādhyatvāt tadyogyatāsavdyavahāro 'bhipretaḥ, tasya, upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya yā "anupalabdhiḥ" tadanyopalabdhirūpā ta"nmātre" nimittāntarānapekṣaṇī, yā "vṛttiḥ" pravṛttirasavdyavahārasya tasyāḥ "sādhanaṃ" siddhiḥ anupalabdhavanvayaniścayaḥ | kutaḥ punarasavdyavahārasya tanmātre vṛttirbhavati? ityāha- "nimittāntarābhāvopadarśanāt" iti | yadā hyasavdyavahārasya yathoktānupaladbhivyatiriktaṃ buddhivyapadeśārthakriyāvirahādikaṃ nimittaṃ na bhavatīti sādhyate tadā yathoktānupalabdhimātre 'sya vṛttiḥ siddhā bhavati | tathā(tayā) cānupalabdhāvanvayaniścayaḥ | anyathā hi nimittāntarāpekṣāśaṅkāyāṃ satyāmapi yathoktānupalabdhau nāvaśyamasavdyavahārasya bhāva iti kuto 'nvayaniścayaḥ syāt? | nimittāntarābhāvastu vistarato vādanyāya ukta iti tata evāvadhāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now he states the determination of positive concomitance in the case of non-apprehension: "In the case of non-apprehension too" — not only has the determination of positive concomitance been stated for the essential-nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) and the effect-reason (<s>kāryahetu</s>), but it is also stated for non-apprehension. What is its form? He says: "Of the convention of non-existence" (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>) — i.e., of the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>); and since the capacity [for being perceived] is also what is to be proved, the convention of non-existence accompanied by that capacity is intended — of that, when it has attained the conditions for being perceived (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>)

body.text: athavā savdyavahārasya yannimittamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya sattvam tad asavdyavahāranimittādanyatvāt nimittāntaraṃ tatrānupalabdherabhāva upadarśyate yena pramāṇena tadevamuktam, tena, sati vastuni tasyā asambhavaniścayād anupalabdhāvanvayaniścayaḥ | tacca tavdyatirekacintāyāṃ darśayiṣyāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: — alternatively, the cause of the convention of existence being something other than the cause of the convention of non-existence — i.e., the existence of [the object] that has attained the conditions for being perceived is a different occasioning cause — the absence [of such existence] is shown there through non-apprehension. By whatever <s>pramāṇa</s> this is stated, by that very [<s>pramāṇa</s>], since it is ascertained that [the convention of non-existence] is impossible when the real thing is present, the determination of positive concomitance in the case of non-apprehension [is established]. And this we shall demonstrate in the consideration of its negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

body.text: tadevaṃ trayāṇāmapi hetūnāṃ yathāsvaṃ pramāṇenānvayaniścaya uktaḥ | svabhāvahetau viparyaye bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tādātmyasiddhinibandhanatvāt, kāryahetau pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinimittatvāt, anupalabdhau nimittāntarābhāvaprasādhakapramāṇastadabhavasiddhihetutvācceti |
body.translated_text: Thus, the determination of positive concomitance for all three types of reasons has been stated, each through its own respective <s>pramāṇa</s>. For the essential-nature reason, because it is grounded in the establishment of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) through the operation of a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> in the case of the contrary; for the effect-reason, because it is occasioned by the establishment of the causal relation through perception and non-apprehension; and for non-apprehension, because it is the means of establishing the absence [of the object] through a <s>pramāṇa</s> that demonstrates the absence of any other occasioning cause.

body.text: 34. kāryasvabhāvayorvyatirekaniścayopāyakathanam |
body.translated_text: 34. Statement of the means for the determination of negative concomitance for the effect-reason and the essential-nature reason.

body.text: samprati trayāṇāmapi hetūnāṃ svasvapramānanibandhanaṃ vyatirekaniścayaṃ pratipādayitukāma āha- "vyatirekaniścayo 'pi" na kevalamanvayaniścayo yathāsvaṃ pramāṇanibandhanastayoruktaḥ api tu "vyatirekaniścayo 'pi kāryasvabhāvahetvo" ryathāsvaṃ pramāṇanimitta ucyate |
body.translated_text: Now, wishing to teach the determination of negative concomitance (<s>vyatirekaniścaya</s>) for all three types of reasons, each grounded in its own respective <s>pramāṇa</s>, he says: "The determination of negative concomitance too" — not only the determination of positive concomitance of these [three reasons], grounded in its respective <s>pramāṇa</s>, has been stated — "but also the determination of negative concomitance of the effect-reason and the essential-nature reason" is stated as occasioned by their respective <s>pramāṇas</s>.

body.text: kaḥ punarasau? "sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasiddhiḥ" | yāvatadātmaka[tadātmakau hetū kāraṇavyāpakarūpasādhyasya sādhakau] sādhyābhāve cābhāvasiddhistayoḥ | kena pramāṇena? | "kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhibhyāṃ" | kāryahetau kāraṇānupalabdhyā sādhyābhāve 'bhāvaniścayaḥ | svabhāvahetau vyāpakānupalabdhyā | kadā punaste anupalabdhī sādhike tasya bhavataḥ? | "kāryakāraṇavyāpyavyāpakabhāvasiddhau" pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau satyāṃ kāraṇānupalabdhiḥ kāryahetau sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasya sādhikā, viparyaye ca bādhakapramāṇavṛttyā tadbhāvatāsiddhitaḥ | vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasiddhau satyāṃ vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ svabhāvahetau sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasya sādhiketi | tadevaṃ bruvatā ubhayatra tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇapratibandhaniścayādeva dvayorapyanvayavyatirekayoḥ niścaya iti uktaṃ bhavati | ata evānyatra- "kāryakāraṇabhāvād vā" ityādi uktam | kīdṛśībhyām? "dṛśyaviṣayābhyāṃ" dṛśyo viṣayo yayoste tathokte | yadi kāraṇavyāpakāvupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptau bhavatastadā tadanupalabdhī sādhyābhāve 'bhāvaṃ sādhayata iti yāvat | kadā punastayoḥ dṛśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇamapekṣyate? ityāha- "uddiṣṭaviṣayasya" uddiṣṭaḥ- kathito viṣayaḥ- ādhāro vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntalakṣaṇo yasya sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasya tasyopadarśane kriyamāṇe | tatrāpi (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 52.

children.text: ) kasmād dṛśyaviṣayatāpekṣyate? iti cet āha- "anupalabdhi" ityādi | "anyathā" yadi dṛśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇamanupalabdhyornāpekṣyate | yadānupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptaṃ viṣayaṃ vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntarūpamupādatte tadānupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptau tatra kāraṇavyāpakāvapi bhavata iti "anupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyaḥ" kāraṇasya vyāpakasya vā "kvacid" viprakṛṣṭe viṣaye sumervādau "abhāvāsiddheḥ" kathamābhyāṃ sādhyābhāve 'bhāvasiddhiḥ syāt, kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhyorevāsiddhatvāt ityabhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: — why is the condition of having a perceptible object (<s>dṛśyaviṣayatā</s>) required? He says: "Non-apprehension" and so on. "Otherwise" — if the qualifier of having a perceptible object is not required for non-apprehension — when [the definition of non-apprehension] takes as its object the counter-example (<s>vaidharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) that has attained the conditions for being perceived, then the cause and the pervader would also be present there in what has attained the conditions for being perceived — [and so] the non-apprehension of the cause and the pervader, "of what has attained the conditions for being perceived"

body.translated_text: What then is this [determination]? "The establishment of absence when the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proved) is absent." Inasmuch as the two reasons — those having the nature of identity [with the <s>sādhya</s>] and [those having the nature of being an effect of it] — are provers of the <s>sādhya</s> which has the form of a cause or pervader, the establishment of [their] absence when the <s>sādhya</s> is absent [is what is meant]. By what <s>pramāṇa</s>? "Through the non-apprehension of the cause and of the pervader" (<s>kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). For the effect-reason, the determination of absence when the <s>sādhya</s> is absent is through the non-apprehension of the cause. For the essential-nature reason, through the non-apprehension of the pervader. But when

body.text: athānuddiṣṭaviṣayasyāpyabhāvasyopadarśane 'nupalabdhyorddaśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇaṃ kimitti nāpekṣyate? ityāha- "anuddiṣṭaviṣayam" anuddiṣṭo viṣayaḥ- vaidharmyadṛṣṭāntarūpo yasmin sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvakhyāpane tat "pratibandhamātrasiddhau" satyāṃ dṛśyaviṣayatāviśeṣaṇamantareṇāpi yasmāt "sidhyati iti" tasmāt "na tatra" anuddiṣṭaviṣaye "vyatirekasādhane" anupalabdhyo "rdṛśyaviṣaya tāviśeṣaṇamapekṣyate" aṅgīkriyate | tathā hi- aśeṣapadārthaparigraheṇa sāmānyenāpi bruvato yo yatra pratibaddhasvabhāvaḥ tādātmyatadutpattibhyāṃ sa tadabhāve 'vaśyameva na bhavatīti niḥsvabhāvatvāhetukatvaprasaṅgāt | taduktam-
body.translated_text: — but why is the qualifier of having a perceptible object not required for the demonstration of the absence of an object that has not been specified? He says: "Concerning an unspecified object" — the unspecified object is in the form of the counter-example in which the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is to be declared through the absence of the reason — that [demonstration] "when merely the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is established" — even without the qualifier of having a perceptible object — "is accomplished, therefore"

children.translated_text: "For the essential nature, the invariable concomitance, which follows mere existence,
— in the absence of that [essential nature], the absence of the entity itself would follow, due to non-difference."

body.text:
tathā- "kāryaṃ dhūmo hutabhujaḥ kāryadharmānuvṛttitaḥ |
sa bhavaṃstadabhāve 'pi hetumattāṃ vilaṅghyet ||" iti |
body.translated_text: Likewise: "Smoke is an effect of fire; due to its following the properties of an effect, if it exists, even in the absence of that [fire], it would transgress its status of having a cause."

body.text: tatastatra dṛśyaviṣayatāpekṣyamāṇānupakārikaiveti na tayā kiñciditi bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the condition of having a perceptible object, when required there [in the context of specified objects], is of no help [in the case of unspecified objects] — so nothing [further is needed] from that [condition]. This is the import.

body.text: "pratibandhamātrasiddhau" ityanena ye pratibandhaṃ hetorna varṇayanti kintvadarśanamātrādeva vyatirekamāhusteṣāṃ tadasambhavaṃ vca darśayati | tathā hi- asati pratibandhe yadi sarve sādhyavirahiṇo 'rthā dṛśyā bhavanti tadā teṣvanupalabdhasya sādhanasyābhāvaḥ śiṣyet | tadāha kumārilo 'pi-
body.translated_text: By [the phrase] "when merely the necessary connection is established" (<s>pratibandhamātrasiddhau</s>), he also shows the impossibility [of the position] of those who do not describe the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) as belonging to the reason, but assert negative concomitance merely from non-observation. That is to say: in the absence of a necessary connection, if all things devoid of the <s>sādhya</s> were perceptible, then the absence of the proving property that is not perceived among them would remain [as the only basis for negative concomitance]. Thus <s>Kumārila</s> too says:

body.text:
"gatvā gatvā tu tān deśān yadyartho nopalabhyate |
tadānyakāraṇābhāvādasannityavagamyate ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "Having gone and gone to those places, if the object is not perceived, then, from the absence of any other cause, it is understood to be non-existent."

body.text: deśādiviprakarṣitayā tvadṛśyatve satyapi tatra hetāvanupalambhamātrasya sambhavāt sandigdho 'sāva'śeṣe sādhyābhāve sādhanābhāvalakṣaṇo vyatirekaḥ tathāvidhasyaiva yatra yatra sādhyābhāvaḥ tatra tatra sādhanābhāva iti vīpsāpadābhyāmabhidhānāt | anvayaniścayo 'pi prākpratibandhanibandhana eva varṇitaḥ tatastenāpi pareṣāṃ darśananibandhanāmanvayasiddhimicchatāmabhāvo 'syāpi kathita eva, sarvārthānāṃ hetumatāṃ sādhyadharmavattayā draṣṭumaśakyatvādanumātṛbhiḥ | aśeṣadeśādiviṣayasya ca sādhyānugamasya yatra yatra hetuḥ tatra tatra sādhyam iti vīpsayā pratipādanāt | na ca katipayadeśādau sādhanadharmasya sādhyadharmeṇa sahabhāvasya bhūyo darśane 'pi vyāptiḥ sidhyati, asati pratibandhe kvacid bahulaṃ tathādṛṣṭānāmapyanyāthātvasyāpi sambhavāt, tadasambhave bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: However, when there is invisibility due to remoteness in space etc., since the mere non-apprehension of the reason (<s>hetu</s>) in that case is possible [even when it exists], the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) — characterized by the absence of the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) in the totality of cases where the probandum (<s>sādhya</s>) is absent — is doubtful, because it is expressed by the distributive words 'wherever there is absence of the probandum, there is absence of the means of proof.' The ascertainment of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) too has been described as based on the prior [ascertainment of] necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>). Therefore, by this as well, the impossibility for those opponents who wish to establish positive concomitance on the basis of observation has already been stated, since it is impossible for inferring subjects to observe all things that possess causes as possessing the probandum-property. And because the concomitance of the probandum with respect to all places etc. is conveyed by the distributive expression 'wherever there is the reason, there is the probandum.' Nor is pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) established even through repeated observation of the co-existence of the reason-property with the probandum-property in several places etc., because in the absence of necessary connection, even things frequently observed together could turn out otherwise somewhere, and because in the absence of that possibility, there is no refuting evidence.

body.text: 35. anupalabdhau vyatirekaniścayopāyākathanam |
body.translated_text: 35. Explanation of the means of ascertaining negative concomitance in non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>).

body.text: anupalabdhimadhikṛtyādhunāha- "vyatirekaniścayo 'nupaladhau" ucyata iti śeṣaḥ | kimātmako 'sau? ityāha "upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptād" vidyamānopalambhapratyayāntarād dṛśyasvabhāvācca "sataḥ" vidyamānāt sādhyābhāvarūpād "anupalambhasya" tadviviktopalambhātmano yo 'bhāvaḥ sato yadgrāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tadbhāvalakṣaṇastasya "darśanaṃ" darśyate- pratyāyyate 'neneti darśanam upadarśakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tadātmako 'nupalabdhau vyatirekaniścayaḥ | taddhetutvācca tat pramāṇaṃ tathocyate | yadi hi sannihitānyopalambhapratyayo dṛśyasvabhāvo bhāvo vidyamāno 'pi nopalabhyeta kathamasau (
body.translated_text: Now, with regard to non-apprehension, he says: "The ascertainment of negative concomitance in non-apprehension" — the remainder is 'is stated.' Of what nature is it? He says: "From something that has fulfilled the conditions for apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>)" — from something that has the other conditions for apprehension of an existent thing present, and has a perceptible nature — "of an existent" — of something that exists, having the form of absence of the probandum — "the non-apprehension" — whose nature is apprehension devoid of that [object]; the absence of that which exists, and the perception that grasps it, whose nature consists in its existence — its "perception" (<s>darśana</s>) means: that by which it is shown — the demonstrating means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Such is the ascertainment of negative concomitance in non-apprehension. And because it is the cause of that, the means of valid knowledge is so called. For if a thing having a perceptible nature, even though existing, with the other conditions for apprehension present, were not apprehended, how could it (

body.text: Hbṭ 54
body.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 54

body.text: ) dṛśyasvabhāvaḥ syāt? | yo hi satsvanyeṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavati sa eva dṛśyasvabhāva ākhyāyate | tasmāt tathāvidhe sannihite 'vaśyaṃ pratyakṣavṛttyā bhavitavyam, anyathāsya na kadācidapi pratyakṣatā syāt, viśeṣābhāvāditi | prayogaḥ- yad yanmātranimittaṃ tatsmin sati niyamena bhavati | tad yathā- bījādisāmagrīmātranimitto 'ṅkuraḥ | yathoktopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptatāmātranimittaṃ ca sati vastuni tathāvidhe pratyakṣamiti svabhāvahetuḥ | [ete]na pramāṇena svabhāvānupalabdhau sādhyābhāve 'bhāvalakṣaṇo vyatireko niścīyate | etacca pramāṇamanvayaniścayasyāpi nimittam | anenaiva nimittāntare 'nupalabdherabhāvopadarśanāt | kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhyostu vakṣyamāṇayoḥ pratibandhadvayasidvyupāya evānvayavyatirekaniścayanibandhanam | sa ca kāryasvabhāvahetvorupadarśita eveti pṛthagnoktaḥ | tathā hi- kāraṇavyāpakayorabhāvaḥ kāryavyāpyābhāvābhyāmavaśyamanvitaḥ kāryavyāpyābhāvavyatireke ca tadbhāvalakṣaṇe 'vaśyaṃ vyatiricyate kāraṇavyāpakayorbhāvāt | anyathā kāryavyāpyayorahetukatvaniḥsvabhāvatāprasaṅgāditi na kiñcit pṛthagabhidhāneneti |
body.translated_text: ) be of perceptible nature? For that which, when the other conditions for apprehension are present, exists and is directly perceived — that alone is designated as being of perceptible nature. Therefore, when such [conditions] are present, there must necessarily be perceptual activity; otherwise, it would never be perceptible, due to the absence of any distinguishing feature. The formal argument is: whatever has as its sole cause a certain set of conditions necessarily exists when those conditions are present — for example, a sprout has as its sole cause the aggregate of seed etc. And perception necessarily occurs when a thing having the conditions for apprehension as described is present — this is an essential nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). By this means of valid knowledge, in the non-apprehension of the essential nature, the negative concomitance characterized by the absence [of the probandum] when the probandum is absent, is ascertained. And this means of valid knowledge is also the ground for the ascertainment of positive concomitance, since by this very ground, absence is shown through non-apprehension of other [relevant factors]. As for the non-apprehension of cause and pervader, which will be discussed later, the basis for the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance is the very means of establishing the two types of necessary connection. And that has already been shown in the case of the effect-reason and essential-nature-reason, so it is not stated separately. For thus: the absence of the cause and the pervader is necessarily accompanied by the absence of the effect and the pervaded; and in the absence of the negative concomitance of the effect and pervaded — i.e. when they are present — the cause and pervader must also be present, due to the existence of the cause and pervader. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence that the effect and pervaded are without cause or without essential nature. Therefore, nothing [further needs to be] stated separately.

body.text: 36. hetoḥ prakāratrayasya nāmanirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: 36. Designation of the three types of reason (<s>hetu</s>) by name.

body.text: tadetāvatā granthena "pakṣadharmastadaṃśena vyāpto hetuḥ" iti vyākhyātam | adhunā "tridhaiva saḥ" ityetad vyākhyātumāha- "etallakṣaṇaḥ" ‘pakṣadharmaḥ san yastadaṃśena vyāpto hetuḥ'; ityetallakṣaṇaṃ yasya sa etallakṣaṇaḥ | "tridhaiva saḥ" | ‘saḥ'; ityetasya vyākhyānaṃ "hetu"riti, | ‘tridhaiva'; ityasya vivaraṇaṃ "triprakāra eve" ti | tān hetūna svena svena nāmnā kīrtayati- "svabhāvaḥ kāryam anupalabdhiśceti" | "ca"kāro hetutvasamuccayārthaḥ | "iti" śabdaḥ samāptiṃ sūcayannavadhāraṇārthameva sphuṭayati | "yathā- anitye" kasmiṃścit śabdādau "sādhye satva(ttva)miti" svabhāvahetūpadarśanam, (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 55

children.text:
) "agnimati pradeśe" sādhye "dhūma iti" kāryahetoḥ pradarśanam, "abhāve ca" abhāvasya vyavahāre ca "upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiriti" anupalabdherupanyāsaḥ |
[37. trividhahetubāhyānāṃ hetvābhāsatve pramāṇopadarśanam |]
children.translated_text:
) "In a place possessing fire" being the probandum, "smoke" — this is the illustration of the effect-reason. "And in absence" — and in the convention of absence — "the non-apprehension of that which has fulfilled the conditions for apprehension" — this is the presentation of non-apprehension.
[37. Demonstrating through valid evidence that what falls outside the three types of reason is a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>).]

body.translated_text: Thus, by this much of the text, 'that which is a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) and is pervaded by a portion of that [probandum] is the reason' has been explained. Now, to explain 'it is of three kinds only,' he says: "Having this definition" — 'that which, being a property of the thesis-subject, is pervaded by a portion of that [probandum] — is the reason': that which has this as its definition has this definition. "It is of three kinds only." The explanation of 'it' is 'the reason'; the elucidation of 'of three kinds only' is "of exactly three types." He names those reasons by their respective names: "essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), effect (<s>kārya</s>), and non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>)." The particle 'ca' serves to aggregate the reasons. The word 'iti' signals completion and clarifies the restrictive sense. "For example: when impermanence" is the probandum in some [subject] like sound etc., "'being produced' (<s>sattva</s>)" — this is the illustration of the essential nature reason. (

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ trividha eva hetuḥ? ityāśaṅkaya trividhahetuvyatiriktānāmarthānāṃ hetvābhāsatayā hetuviruddhayā vyāptestriṣveva hetutvaṃ niyataṃ bhavatiti hetvābhāsatāṃ pramāṇavatīṃ tadvyatirekiṇāṃ darśayannāha- "atraiva" svabhāvakāryānupalabdhyākhye "trividhahetau avinābhāvasya niyamāditi" trividhahetuvyatirikteṣvartheṣvavinābhāvābhāvādityarthaḥ | tataścāvinābhāvavikalatvāt svabhāvakāryānupalabdhivyatirekiṇo 'rthā hetvābhāsāḥ prameyatvādivat ityuktaṃ bhavati | avinābhāvābhāvaśca trividhahetuvyatiriktatvādeva tādātmyatadutpattyoravinābhāvavyāpikayorabhāvād vyāpakānupalabdhito 'vagataḥ |
body.translated_text: Why is the reason of three types only? Anticipating this, showing that things other than the three types of reason are pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>), pervaded by being contrary to a valid reason, so that reason-hood is restricted to these three alone, and that this pseudo-reason status is supported by valid evidence, he says: "In these alone" — in the three types of reason called essential nature, effect, and non-apprehension — "because invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>) is restricted" — meaning, because invariable concomitance is absent in things other than the three types of reason. And therefore, since they lack invariable concomitance, things other than essential nature, effect, and non-apprehension are pseudo-reasons, like 'being knowable' (<s>prameyatva</s>) etc. — this is what is stated. And the absence of invariable concomitance is understood through the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>), namely from the absence of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and origination-from-that (<s>tadutpatti</s>), which pervade invariable concomitance, when there is something other than the three types of reason.

body.text: 38. avinābhāvanirūpaṇam |
body.translated_text: 38. Examination of invariable concomitance (<s>avinābhāva</s>).

body.text: atha ko 'yamavinābhāvaḥ? kasya cāsau? kathaṃ vātraiva niyata ucyate? ityata āha- "yathoktā vyāptiḥ vyāpakasya"- tatkāraṇatayā tadbhāvatayā ca | yatra tadvayāpyaṃ kāryaṃ svabhāvo vā sannihitastatra bhāva eva | "vyāpyasya vā"- kāryasya svabhāvasya vā | yatra tatkāraṇasvabhāvākhyaṃ vyāpakaṃ sannihitaṃ tatraiva dharmiṇi na tadabhāve 'pi bhāva iti yā vyāpakavyāpyadharmatayā vyāptiruktā sā "yathoktā vyāptiravinābhāvaḥ" | kasya? | "pakṣadharmasya" | sādhyadharmidharmasya | "sa" evaṃrūpo 'vinābhāvaḥ "tṛ(tri)vidhād" yathoktād hetoḥ "anyatraḥ" tadvyatirekiṇyarthe "nāsti" | yato 'tra ca tṛ(tri)vidhe 'sti tādātmyatadutpattyoravinābhāvena vyāptayorbhāvāt, kṛtakatvānityatvavadanayorvyāpyavyāpakabhāvāditi "tasmādatraiva" trividhe hetau tadanyatrābhāvamukhena "niyataḥ" ucyate | tadanena "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare" ityasya "avinābhāvaniyamāt" ityupapattisahitasyārthaḥ pradarśitaḥ | yathā ca trividhād hetoranyatrāvinābhāvo nāsti tathā prāgevoktam |
body.translated_text: Now, what is this invariable concomitance? Of what does it hold? And how is it said to be restricted to these alone? To this he says: "The pervasion as described, of the pervader" — by being its cause or by being of the same nature. Wherever its pervaded — the effect or essential nature — is present, there the pervader necessarily exists. "Or of the pervaded" — of the effect or essential nature. Wherever the pervader — called the cause or essential nature — is present, precisely in that property-bearer and not where it is absent. The pervasion that has been stated in terms of pervader and pervaded properties, that "pervasion as described is invariable concomitance." Of what? "Of the thesis-property" (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) — i.e. of the property of the subject of the probandum. "That" invariable concomitance of such a form "does not exist elsewhere" — in things other than that — "than the threefold" reason as described. Because it does exist in the threefold [reason], due to the existence of pervasion through invariable concomitance of identity and origination-from-that; because of the pervaded-pervader relation of these two, like 'being produced' and 'impermanence' — "therefore, in these alone" — in the threefold reason, stated negatively by its absence elsewhere — "it is restricted." By this, the meaning of 'the rest are pseudo-reasons,' together with the supporting reasoning 'because of the restriction of invariable concomitance,' has been demonstrated. And that invariable concomitance does not exist other than in the threefold reason — this has been stated earlier.

body.text: yadi vā svabhāvādanyo 'rtho 'rthāntaram, tacca kāryādapyanyat kāraṇamanubhayaṃ vā | anupalabdherapyanyad yathoktāyāḥ anupalabdhimātramupalabdhirvā pratiṣedhyasya tadanyasyāpi viruddhasyāviruddhasya vā | tatrārthāntaram yadyanantarakāryaṃ tasyārvāgdarśibhiḥ itaravivekena lakṣayitumaśakyatvāt aliṅgatvam | kāryadarśanāt vivekāvasāye 'pi sādhyasidyuttarakālabhāvī pakṣadharmatāvasāyo 'nvayānugamanaṃ ca vyarthaṃ | vyavahitakāryamapi kāraṇaṃ na kāryasya liṅgam, antarālapratibandhavaikalyasambhavena vyabhicārāt | taduktam-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, a thing other than essential nature is something different, and that is either a cause other than the effect, or neither of the two. And something other than non-apprehension as described is either mere non-apprehension, or apprehension — either of the thing to be negated, or of something other than that, whether contradictory or non-contradictory. In that case, if the different thing is an immediately subsequent effect, since it cannot be distinguished from the other by those who see only the proximate [cause], it is not a logical mark. Even if the distinction is ascertained through observation of the effect, the ascertainment of the thesis-property and the tracing of positive concomitance, which come after the establishment of the probandum, are pointless. Even a cause [related to] a remote effect is not a logical mark of the effect, because of deviation due to the possible deficiency of the intermediate necessary connection. As stated —

children.translated_text: "Since there is the possibility of the necessary connection being dependent on the transformation
of the aggregate, its power, and its result, there is inconclusiveness in the effect."

body.text: iti | yogyatānumāne tu nārthāntaraṃ liṅgam |
body.translated_text: And in an inference of capability, nothing other [than the three types] serves as a logical mark.

body.text: nāpyanubhayam, apratibandhena gamakatvāyogāt | kathaṃ kṛttikodayavijñānād rohiṇyāsattiklṛptiḥ? iti cet | nanu sāpi naivāsati pratibandhe yuktā viśeṣābhāvena sarvataḥ sarvapratītiprasaṅgāt ityuktatvāt | tasmānnakṣatracakrasya saṅkrāntihetureva kālavyavadhānena kaścit kalpayitavyaḥ, yathā bhūtasaṃkṣobhaḥ paścātkālabhāvino varṣasyeti hetudharmānumānena kāryaliṅgajaiva kalpayitavyā |
body.translated_text: Nor [can] what is neither [cause nor effect serve as a logical mark], because without necessary connection it cannot be probative. If one asks: how is the determination of <s>Rohiṇī</s>'s proximity established from the cognition of the rising of <s>Kṛttikā</s>? — Well, even that, without necessary connection, is not reasonable, because in the absence of a distinguishing feature, everything would follow from everything, as has been stated. Therefore, some cause of the revolution of the constellation-wheel must be posited, with temporal interval, just as the disturbance of elements [is posited as a cause] of subsequent rain — [the inference of constellational proximity] must be constructed as arising from an effect-mark through an inference of the reason-property.

body.text: anupalabdhimātramapi saṃśayahetuḥ, pramāṇanivṛttāvapyarthābhāvāsiddheḥ | upalabdhirapi pratiṣedhyasya kathamabhāvaṃ sādhayet?, abhrāntopalambhasyābhāvāyogāt | viruddhopalabdhistu pratiyogyabhāvaṃ sādhayati | kintu sa virodhastadbhāve satyanyānupalambhādeva siddha iti taddvāreṇānupalabdhireva prayuktā bhavati | anyathāniṣiddhopalabdherabhāvāsiddheḥ | aviruddhopalabdhiḥ punaḥ pratiṣedhe 'naikāntikī, sahabhāvasambhavādaviruddhānām | na cāparaḥ prakāraḥ sambhavatīti nāvinābhāvo 'nyatra vidyata iti |
body.translated_text: Mere non-apprehension too is a cause of doubt, since the absence of the object is not established even when the means of valid knowledge has ceased. How can apprehension of the thing to be negated establish absence? — because of the impossibility of undeluded apprehension [co-existing with] absence. But the apprehension of a contradictory [entity] does establish the absence of its counterpart. However, that contradiction is established only through the non-apprehension of the other when the first is present, so it is non-apprehension itself that is employed through that channel. Otherwise, from apprehension of something non-negated, absence would not be established. And apprehension of a non-contradictory [entity] is inconclusive with regard to negation, since non-contradictory things can co-exist. And no other type is possible — therefore, invariable concomitance does not exist elsewhere.

body.text: 2. svabhāvahetunirūpaṇam |
body.translated_text: 2. Examination of the essential nature reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>).

body.text: 1. svabhāvahetorlakṣaṇābhidhānam |
body.translated_text: 1. Statement of the definition of the essential nature reason.

body.text: idānīṃ svabhāvahetostāvallakṣaṇamāha- "tatra" hetutraye svabhāvahetostāvallakṣaṇamucyate | sādhyate yena tat sādhanam | taccāsau dharmaśca tasya bhāvastadbhāvaḥ | sa eva "sādhanadharmabhāvamātra"m | tasya "anvayaḥ" | sa yasyāsti sādhyadharmasyāvayave samudāyopacārāt, tasmin | "svabhāvo hetuḥ" | sādhyadharmasya śrutatvāt tasyaiva svabhāva iti gamyate | kathaṃ punarasau sādhyadharmasvabhāvo? yāvatā bhedena pratīyata ityata āha- "aparasmādaparasmācca" asato 'kṣaṇikācca yā "vyāvṛtti"stasyā yo "bhedaḥ" avadhibhedopakalpitastena hetubhūtena "sādhyadharmāt sādhanadharmasya" yo "bheda"stasmin "satyapi" "vastutaḥ" paramārthato "liṅgasvabhāva eva" sādhyadharmasvabhāva eva | tathā hi- ya evāsato vyāvṛttaḥ sa evākṣaṇikādapi | tata ekasmād dharmiṇo bhedābhāvāt sādhyasādhanadharmāvapi paramārthato naiva bhidyete iti |
body.translated_text: Now he states the definition of the essential nature reason: "Among those" — among the three types of reason, the definition of the essential nature reason is stated first. That by which something is proved is the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>). That is both a property (<s>dharma</s>) and the being of that [probandum] is its nature (<s>tadbhāva</s>). That alone is "the mere being of the proof-property" (<s>sādhanadharmabhāvamātra</s>). Its "concomitance" (<s>anvaya</s>) — [the probandum] in which it is present, i.e., in the part of the probandum-property, by figurative extension from the part to the whole — "the essential nature is the reason." Since the probandum-property has been mentioned, it is understood to be the essential nature of that very [probandum]. But how is it the essential nature of the probandum-property, given that it is cognized as different? To this he says: "From the other and from [yet] another" — the exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) from what is non-existent and from what is non-momentary — the "difference" constructed through the difference of limits — even when that difference of "the proof-property from the probandum-property" by that reason "exists, in reality" — ultimately — "it is of the very nature of the logical mark" — of the very nature of the probandum-property. For thus: that which is excluded from the non-existent is also excluded from the non-momentary. Therefore, since there is no difference from a single property-bearer, the probandum-property and proof-property are ultimately not at all different.

body.text: 2. paramatanirāsārthaṃ sādhyadharme sādhanadharmabhāvamātretyādiviśeṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: 2. The qualification 'mere being of the proof-property' etc. in the probandum-property, for the purpose of refuting the opposing position.

body.text: yadi vastuto liṅgisvabhāva eva sādhanadharmaḥ, tat kasmāt "sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānvayini" iti sādhyadharmo viśeṣyate? | yo hi yasya svabhāvaḥ sa kathaṃ tanmātrānvayī na syāt?, nīrūpatvaprasaṅgādatatsvabhāvatā vā ityata āha- hetuḥ svabhāvo yasya sādhyadharmasya tasmin "hetusvabhāve" "sādhyadharme" sati "anvayavyabhicārābhāvāt" sādhanadharmabhāvamātrasya yo 'nvayastasya vyabhicārābhāvāt | sambhave vyabhicāre ca viśeṣaṇaṃ yuktam | atra tu sambhava eva na vyabhicāra iti "viśeṣaṇamayuktameva | tathāpi" svabhavahetulakṣaṇe kriyamāṇe yadetat "sādhyadharmasya" "tanmātrānvayena" sādhanadharmabhāvamātrānugamanena viśeṣaṇaṃ "tat paramatāpekṣaṃ" naiyāyikādīnāṃ vipratipattestanmatāpekṣaṃ na tu svamatāpekṣam |
body.translated_text: If the proof-property is ultimately of the very nature of the property-possessor (<s>liṅgin</s>), then why is the probandum-property qualified as "concomitant with the mere being of the proof-property"? For how could that which is the essential nature of something not be concomitant with its mere being? — since otherwise it would have no form, or would not be of that nature. To this he says: For the probandum-property whose essential nature is the reason, in that "probandum-property having the reason as its essential nature," "because there is no deviation of the concomitance" — because there is no deviation of the concomitance of the mere being of the proof-property — when deviation is possible, the qualification would be appropriate. But here there is only the possibility [of concomitance], not deviation — so "the qualification is indeed inappropriate. Nevertheless," when formulating the definition of the essential nature reason, this qualification of "the probandum-property" "by concomitance with its mere being" — by following the mere being of the proof-property — "is made with reference to the opposing position" — due to the disagreement of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, it is with reference to their position, not one's own.

body.text: tāmeva paravipratipattiṃ darśayannāha- "pare hi" naiyāyikādayaḥ "arthāntaranimittaḥ" janakādarthādanyo yo 'rtho vegavaddravyayogādiḥ tannimittam | te hyevamāhuḥ- vegavaddravyayogādavayaveṣu karmāṇyutpadyante | tebhyo 'vayavavibhāgaḥ | tatastatsaṃyogavināśastadārabdhaṃ kāryadravye 'pi (kāryadravyamapi) naśyatīti | evamarthāntaraṃ nimittaṃ | tata eva "arthāntaranimittapekṣamāṇaṃ" kṛtakatvādibhāve 'pyabhāvād "atadbhāvamātrānvayinaṃ" tasya kṛtakatvādeḥ bhāvaḥ sattā saiva tanmātraṃ tasyānvayaḥ sa yasyāsti sādhyadharmasya anityatvalakṣaṇasya tadviparītam "api" kṛtakatvādeḥ "svabhāvamicchanti" yataḥ tato viśeṣaṇaṃ kṛtam | tena ca viśeṣaṇena tathāvidhasyārthāntaranimittasya vināśasyātatsvabhāvatāmāha lakṣaṇe viśeṣaṇakāraḥ | svasattāmātrabhāvinyeva svabhāvatvaṃ nānyatreti viśeṣaṇena sūcanāt |
body.translated_text: Showing that very disagreement of the opponents, he says: "For others" — the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others — [hold that destruction] "is caused by something other" — something different from the producing cause, such as the conjunction with a substance possessing velocity etc. — that is its cause. For they say thus: From the conjunction with a substance possessing velocity, motions (<s>karman</s>) arise in the atoms; from those, separation of atoms; from that, the destruction of their conjunction; and the composite substance produced from that also perishes. Thus, something other is the cause. Therefore, "requiring a cause that is something other" — since even when 'being produced' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) etc. is present, [destruction does] not [follow without the external cause], "they accept" the essential nature of 'being produced' etc. as "concomitant with the mere being of that, yet also" as having a "contrary" [nature] — the existence of the probandum-property of impermanence requires the mere existence of 'being produced' etc. as its concomitant, [but they hold that] the existence of that alone is insufficient. Therefore the qualification is made. And by that qualification, the author of the definition states the non-essential-nature of destruction caused by something other of that kind.

body.text: 3. hetumati vināśe sādhye kṛtakatvasya vyabhicāritvam |
body.translated_text: 3. The deviating character of 'being produced' when the probandum is destruction with a cause.

body.text: tathā, "tasmin" arthāntaranimitte sādhye "hetoḥ" kṛtakatvādeḥ vyabhicāramanaikāntikatāṃ cāha | atrodāharaṇaṃ "yathā hetumati vināśe" sādhye "kṛtakatvasya" hetoḥ "atatsvabhāvatā vyabhicāraśceti" |
body.translated_text: Likewise, he states the deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of the <s>hetu</s> such as <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced) — that is, its inconclusive character (<s>anaikāntikatā</s>) — when the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) is an <s>arthāntaranimitta</s> (extrinsic cause). Here, the example is: when the <s>sādhya</s> is destruction (<s>vināśa</s>) that is caused (<s>hetumati</s>), the deviation of the <s>hetu</s>, <s>kṛtakatva</s>, consists in its being "of a different nature" (<s>atatsvabhāvatā</s>).

body.text: nanu ca kṛtakatvasvabhāvatā anityatāyā bhedopagamāt neṣṭaiva paraistat kimucyate- "atadbhāvamātrānvayinamapi svabhāvamicchanti" iti? | evaṃ manyate- vyatiriktāvapi kṛtakatvānityatvākhyau dharmāvabhyupagacchadbhiravaśyam ‘abhūtvā bhavanaṃ bhūtvā cābhavanamanavasthāyisvabhāvatvam'; abhyupagantavyam, anyathātmādiṣvapi kṛtakatvānityatve viśeṣābhāvād bhavetām | tato yadeva‘abhūtvā bhavanaṃ bhūtvā ['bhavanaṃ] cānavasthāyitvam'; upādīyate bhāvasya tayoreva taddarśanabalotpannakṛtakatvāniyatvabhedāvabhāsikalpanādvāreṇa sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'stu, kiṃ vyatiriktadharmakalpanayā? | kalpayitvāpi vastvātmana evārthakriyānibandhanatayā tadarthibhiḥ cintyatvāt | taduktam-
body.translated_text: Objection: Since the opponents accept a difference between the nature of <s>kṛtakatva</s> (being produced) and <s>anityatā</s> (impermanence), they do not accept the identity of their natures. So why does [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] say "they accept a <s>svabhāva</s> (nature) that is concomitant with merely not being that"? The idea is as follows: Those who accept <s>kṛtakatva</s> and <s>anityatva</s> as distinct properties must necessarily accept that 'coming into being after not having existed, and ceasing to exist after having existed, constitutes having an unstable nature' (<s>anavasthāyisvabhāvatva</s>); otherwise, <s>kṛtakatva</s> and <s>anityatva</s> would apply to the <s>ātman</s> and the like as well, since there would be no distinguishing factor. Therefore, the very fact that an entity's 'coming into being after not having existed and [ceasing to exist after having existed constitute] its instability' is what is apprehended. Through the conceptual appearance of the distinction between <s>kṛtakatva</s> and <s>anityatva</s> — which arises from the force of perceiving just that — let the relation of <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and <s>sādhana</s> (probans) be established. What need is there for postulating distinct properties? Even if one postulates them, since it is the real nature of the thing itself that is the ground of causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>), those who desire that [efficacy] must reflect on that alone. As it has been said:

children.translated_text: "By those who do not deny the referents of words, [analyzing them] through the division into the existent and non-existent categories,
it is indeed the real thing itself that is examined here, [for] the arising of the result is invariably connected [to it].
For one who is capable of causal efficacy (<s>arthākriyā</s>), what [use] have those who desire that [efficacy] with [mere] modifications?
What [use] is the examination of a woman's beauty or ugliness for a eunuch (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>)?"

body.text: iti | tasmād dṛṣṭā api bhāvāḥ kenacidātmanā tadanyavyāvṛttena kathañcinniścitāḥ tadanyenāpyatadrūpavyāvṛttenātmanā bhrāntikāraṇasadbhāvādaniścīyamānāḥ, niścitāniścitayo rūpayoḥ pramāṇāntarataḥ pratibandhāvasāyāpurovartino 'numānato niścīyate iti anityatāsvabhāvabhūtasyaiva kṛtakatvasya vināśaṃ prati liṅgatā yuktā | tathā ca vināśasvabhāva eva kṛtakatvākhyo hetuḥ tairyathoktanyāyādiṣṭo bhavati | tasyātanmātrānvayitve 'rthāntaranimittatayā viśeṣaṇenātatsvabhāvatā kathyate |
body.translated_text: Therefore, although entities are perceived with a certain nature that is distinguished from everything else, they remain undetermined with respect to another nature — one that is excluded from what is not of that form — due to the presence of causes of error. The two aspects, the determined and the undetermined, are ascertained through <s>anumāna</s> (inference), which is preceded by the determination of the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) through another <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge). Thus it is proper that <s>kṛtakatva</s>, which is itself of the nature of <s>anityatā</s> (impermanence), serves as the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for destruction (<s>vināśa</s>). Accordingly, the <s>hetu</s> called <s>kṛtakatva</s> is itself of the nature of destruction, and is accepted by them [the opponents] according to the reasoning stated above. When it is concomitant with something beyond its own nature alone, its being of a different nature (<s>atatsvabhāvatā</s>) is declared by the qualifier <s>arthāntaranimiita</s> (extrinsic cause).

body.text: syānmatam- kṛtakatvena sākṣad hetumān vināśo 'numīyate tataḥ prākpradhvaṃsābhavaviśeṣaṇā sattā tatsamavāyo vānityatā vyavasthāpyate | ata evātmādiṣvanityatāprasaṅgābhāvaḥ | vināśa iti ca na bhāvābhāvaṃ pradhvaṃsalakṣaṇaṃ manyāmahe | kṛtakatvaṃ tu svakāraṇasattāsamavāyam | tasya viśeṣaṇena vināśo 'sva(śāsva)bhāvatākhyāpane na kiñcidaniṣṭamiti |
body.translated_text: One might think: Destruction that is caused (<s>hetumān vināśa</s>) is directly inferred through <s>kṛtakatva</s>, and prior to that, <s>anityatā</s> (impermanence) is established as <s>sattā</s> (existence) qualified by the <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (posterior absence), or as the <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) with that. Hence there is no unwanted consequence of impermanence applying to the <s>ātman</s> and the like. And by 'destruction' we do not mean the <s>pradhvaṃsa</s> (posterior absence), which is the absence of an entity. Rather, <s>kṛtakatva</s> is the <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) with the existence of its own cause. When the nature of destruction that is different from that [<s>kṛtakatva</s>] is declared through the qualifier, nothing undesirable follows.

body.text: tadayuktam, tathāvidhasya vināśasya hetumattāvirodhāt, svayameva caitadācāryo vakṣyati | na ca tenānumitena kiñcit, tasyārthakriyāsāmarthyavikalatvāt | sukhaduḥsvasādhane jñātvā yathārhaṃ pratipitsavo hi kiñcit parīkṣante na vyasanitayā | tasmādanenāsthirasvabhāvataiva bhāvasyānumātavyā | saiva ca hetumatī (

children.translated_text: Hbt 60

children.text: ) kalpanīyā | anyathā bhāvāvilakṣaṇasya pradhvaṃsābhāvasya mugdarāderudaye 'pi tasya bhāve 'nupayogāt sa bhāvastadavastha eveti kathaṃ tadviśeṣaṇā sattā tatsamavāyo vā anityatā syāt? | avicalitarūpasya ca bhāvasya mugdarādikṛtapradhvaṃsābhāvaviśeṣaṇau sattāsamavāyau yadyanityatā, kiṃ nātmāderapi? iti prasaṅga tadavastha eva | svakāraṇasamavāyo 'pi cābhūtvā bhavanamanicchato na sidhyati | abhūtvā bhavata eva ca yā sattā saiva kṛtakatvaṃ varṇyate | na ca sattāsamavāyayornityatayopagatayorniratiśayatvāt prākpradhvaṃsābhāvau viśeṣaṇaṃ yujyete | abhūtvā bhavanopagame ca tadeva kṛtakatvamasthirasvabhāvatā ca vināśo 'stu | kiṃ niṣphalayā apramāṇikayā pramāṇabadhitaya'rthāntarakalpanayā? | evaṃ kṛtakatvavināśayostādātmyopagamo 'vaśyambhāvī pareṣāmapi | tato vināśasyāsthāyitvalakṣaṇasyārthāntaranimittatopagame kṛtakatvasyātatsvabhāvatā viśeṣaṇena khyāpyate | tanniṣpattāvaniṣpannasya bhinnahetukasya ca tatsvabhāvatvāyogāt |
children.translated_text: For otherwise, since <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (posterior absence) — which is entirely unlike a positive entity — would exist even when a pestle and the like arise, and its presence would be of no consequence [to the pot], the entity would remain in the same state. How then could <s>anityatā</s> (impermanence) be <s>sattā</s> (existence) qualified by that [posterior absence], or <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) with it? And if the <s>sattā</s> and <s>samavāya</s> qualifying the entity — whose nature remains unchanged — with the <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> produced by a pestle and the like constitute <s>anityatā</s>, then why not also for the <s>ātman</s> and the like? — the same unwanted consequence remains. Moreover, <s>samavāya</s> with one's own cause does not hold for one who does not accept coming into being after not having existed (<s>abhūtvā bhavana</s>). And the very <s>sattā</s> that consists in coming into being after not having existed is what is described as <s>kṛtakatva</s>. Since <s>sattā</s> and <s>samavāya</s>, being accepted as permanent, are unlimited [in scope], <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> cannot properly qualify them. But if one accepts 'coming into being after not having existed,' then let that very <s>kṛtakatva</s> be the unstable nature, and let that be destruction (<s>vināśa</s>). What is the use of a fruitless, baseless postulation of something else that is contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition)? Thus, even for the opponents, the acceptance of the identity in nature (<s>tādātmya</s>) of <s>kṛtakatva</s> and <s>vināśa</s> is unavoidable. Therefore, when the <s>arthāntaranimiita</s> (extrinsic causation) of destruction — defined as instability (<s>asthāyitva</s>) — is accepted, the different nature (<s>atatsvabhāvatā</s>) of <s>kṛtakatva</s> is declared through the qualifier, because what has not come into being [at that point] and what has a different cause cannot be of the same nature as it.

body.translated_text: That is not correct, because such a destruction is not incompatible with being caused (<s>hetumattā</s>), and the <s>Ācārya</s> [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] himself will state this [later]. Moreover, nothing [useful] follows from what is inferred thereby, since it lacks the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>). For those who wish to act appropriately after knowing what conduces to happiness and suffering examine something [only] for a purpose, not out of mere idle curiosity. Therefore, what must be inferred for an entity is precisely its having an unstable nature (<s>asthirasvabhāvatā</s>). And that alone is to be understood as caused (<s>hetumatī</s>)

body.text: tathā, tasmin sādhye kṛtakatvasya vyabhicāraḥ | tathā hi- ye yatra hetvantarāpekṣiṇo na te tatrāvaśyambhāvinaḥ, yathā vāsasi rāgaḥ | hetvantarāpekṣī ca kṛtakeṣvapi bhāveṣu pradhvaṃsābhāva iti viruddhavyāptopalabdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Likewise, when that [caused destruction] is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), <s>kṛtakatva</s> deviates [from it]. For those [properties] that depend on an additional cause (<s>hetvantara</s>) in some locus are not invariably present there, just as dye [is not invariably present] in cloth. And <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (posterior absence) depends on an additional cause even in produced entities — this is an instance of the apprehension of a concomitance with the opposite (<s>viruddhavyāptopalabdhi</s>).

body.text: nanu vāsasi rāgasya parimitahetutvāt tasya ca svakāraṇāyattasannidhānatvāt tadāśrayasya ca vidhurapratyayopanipātenāsthiratayā nāvaśyambhavitā yuktaiva | na punarvināśasya, taddhetūnāmānantyādavaśyaṃ kasyacid ghaṭādiṣu sannidheḥ | na ca vināśasyāśrayaṃ prāk taddhetusannidheḥ kecidupaghnānti, yatastadabhāvād vināśo nārabhyeteti |
body.translated_text: Objection: Since the dye in cloth has a limited set of causes, and since its presence depends on the proximity of its own causes, and since its substratum is unstable due to the intervention of adverse conditions (<s>vidhura-pratyaya</s>), its non-invariable presence is indeed justified. But not so for destruction, since the causes of destruction are infinite and therefore some [cause] must necessarily be present in pots and the like. And no one destroys the substratum of destruction prior to the proximity of its cause, such that destruction would not arise due to the absence of that [substratum].

body.text: tadayuktam, yato yadyapi bahulaṃ vināśakāraṇāni santi tathāpi teṣāṃ svakaraṇāyattasannidhitvāt tathā tatkāraṇānāṃ ca sa nnihitānāmapi virodhināmapyānatyāt tadbhāve tacchaktipratibandhānnāvaśyaṃ hetavaḥ phalavanta iti kaścinna vinaśyedapīti vyabhicāro (

children.translated_text: Hbt 61

children.text: ) na nivartate | nanvayaṃ vāsasi rāgaḥ sāpekṣo 'pi yadi sarvatropalabhyeta tataḥ kimavaśyambhāvī na syāt? | syād, yadi tathopalabhyeta | sa tvanyathāpi gṛhyate | yadyevaṃ na tarhi sarvatropalabdhasya vināśasyānyathābhāvaśaṅkayā manasi kheda ādhātavyaḥ | kiṃ vā punarbhavān samastavastuvistaravyāpijñānālokaḥ?, yenaivaṃ vadati | tathābhāve vā kathamanumānavṛttirdṛṣṭe na vaiphalyamaśnuvīta? | kasyacit tu hetukṛtavināśadarśane 'pi hetvāyattajanmanamanyathāpi darśanād upajātāśaṅko deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭeṣu kathaṃ tathābhāvaṃ niścinvīta? | kṛtakamapi cāyaṃ bhavabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ vināśaṃ nityamupaiti, tadvināśopagame bhāvasyonmajjanaprasaṅgāt | na cāsya ghaṭāderiva vināśaheturupalabhyate kaściditi | taduktam-
children.translated_text: is not eliminated. [Objection:] If this dye in cloth, even though dependent [on other causes], were observed everywhere, then would it not be invariably present? It would, if it were observed thus. But it is also observed otherwise [i.e., absent in some cases]. [Response:] If so, then one should not trouble one's mind with the doubt that destruction, which is observed everywhere, might be otherwise. Or is your honor possessed of a cognition that illuminates the entire extent of all things, that you speak thus? And if [destruction] were thus [invariably present], how could the operation of inference in the observed domain not become futile? Yet even when destruction caused by some [external] agent is observed in some cases, one who sees that things born from causes also exist otherwise [i.e., persist] develops doubt — how could such a person ascertain that things distant in place, time, and nature are likewise [destroyed]? Moreover, this [entity], even though produced (<s>kṛtaka</s>), always undergoes destruction characterized by the cessation of its current state (<s>bhavābhāva</s>), since if one accepted the destruction of that [cessation] itself, the entity would resurface. And no cause of the destruction of this [cessation] is observed, unlike [the cause observed] for a pot and the like. As it has been said:

body.translated_text: That is not correct, because even though the causes of destruction are numerous, nevertheless, since their proximity depends on their own causes, and since even among those causes that are present there are also infinitely many obstructors, and since when those [obstructors] are present the capacity [of the destructive causes] is blocked, causes do not necessarily bear fruit — therefore someone might not be destroyed, and so the deviation

children.translated_text: "Just as causes that bring about destruction are observed in the case of pots and the like,
no such [cause] is [observed] for destruction [itself] — how then does it arise without a cause?"

body.text: iti | tataḥ kṛtakatva vināśe sādhye tenaiva vyabhicāraḥ kiṃ neṣyate? |
body.translated_text: Therefore, when destruction is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), why is the deviation of <s>kṛtakatva</s> with respect to it not accepted?

body.text: bhāvānāmayamaikāntika eva dharma iti cet, kutaḥ punaretadavasitam? | teṣāmanyathābhāvasyānupalambhāditi cet | nanvayamanupalambho bhavannapyātmāderanivartakaḥ sattāyāḥ, kathamanyatrānyathābhāvaṃ nivartayati? | tasyānumānenopalambhāditi yadyucyeta tadā tatrāpyanumāne vipakṣe vṛttimanupalambha eva hetoḥ kathaṃ nivartayati? iti yatkiñcidetat | tasmāt sādhūktam- ‘hetumati vināśe kṛtakatvasyāsvabhāvatāṃ vyabhicāraṃ cāha'; iti alamatijalpiteneti |
body.translated_text: If [one says]: 'This is an invariable property of entities' — on what basis is this ascertained? If [one says]: 'Because no instance of their being otherwise is apprehended' — but this non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), even while occurring, does not negate <s>sattā</s> (existence) of the <s>ātman</s> and the like; how then does it negate being otherwise in other cases? If one were to say: 'Because it is apprehended through inference (<s>anumāna</s>)' — then in that inference too, how does the mere non-apprehension of the <s>hetu</s>'s occurrence in the <s>vipakṣa</s> (dissimilar locus) negate [it]? All of this amounts to nothing. Therefore, it has been well said: 'He states the different nature (<s>asvabhāvatā</s>) of <s>kṛtakatva</s> with respect to caused destruction, and its deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>).' Enough of this excessive disputation.

body.text: 4. parārthānumāne sādharmyavaidharmyaprayogodāharaṇam |
body.translated_text: 4. Example of <s>sādharmya</s> (positive) and <s>vaidharmya</s> (negative) formulation in <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others).

body.text: idānīṃ yadyapi svārthānumānaṃ prakṛtaṃ tathāpi kaścit prayogadarśanābhyāsāt prayogabhaṅgayaiva pratipadyata iti svārthānumāne 'pi (

children.translated_text: Hbt 62

children.text: ) tatsvambhavāt prasaṅgena parārthānumānaṃ ca vyutpādayitumāha- "tasya" svabhāvahetoḥ "dvidhā" trailakṣaṇyapratipādako vacanodāhāraḥ "prayogaḥ" | tameva darśayati- samāno dharmo yasya tasya bhāvaḥ tena "sādhya(dha)rmyeṇaikaḥ" prayogaḥ | "aparo" visadṛśo dharmo yasya tasya bhāvaḥ tena "vaidharmyeṇa" |
children.translated_text: [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says, in order to teach <s>parārthānumāna</s> (inference for others) incidentally: "Of that" <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (identity reason), "the formal proof" (<s>prayoga</s>) — that is, the verbal illustration that demonstrates the three characteristics (<s>trailakṣaṇya</s>) — is "twofold." He shows this: one [proof] is "by <s>sādharmya</s>" — the state of having a common property (<s>samāna dharma</s>) [with the probandum]. "The other" is "by <s>vaidharmya</s>" — the state of having a dissimilar property.

body.translated_text: Now, although <s>svārthānumāna</s> (inference for oneself) is the present topic, nevertheless, since someone may understand [the matter] through the very form of a formal proof (<s>prayoga</s>) due to practice in observing formal proofs, and since that [formal proof format] naturally belongs to <s>svārthānumāna</s> as well,

body.text: yathākramamanayorudāharaṇamāha- "yathā yat sat" | yadyatsaditi vīpsāpradhāno yacchabdaḥ | "tat sarvam" iti tacchabdo 'pi vīpsāpradhāna eva | atra sarvagrahaṇena cāśeṣaparigrahād bahirvyāpternirāsaḥ | "yathā ghaṭādayaḥ" iti | yasya sattvakṣaṇikatvayoḥ pratibandhaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ ghaṭādau pravṛttaṃ taṃ prati tatra smṛtisamādhānārthaṃ dṛṣṭāntavacanaṃ na sādhyasiddhyartham | dṛṣṭāntamātrataḥ sādhyasiddherabhāvāt | na hyekasya tathā bhāve sarvastathā bhavati, atiprasaṅgāt | "saṃśca śabdaḥ" iti pakṣadharmopasaṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: He gives the example of these two in order. "Whatever exists" (<s>yathā yat sat</s>): the word <s>yad</s> ('whatever') has distributive force (<s>vīpsā</s>).
