"All that" (<s>tat sarvam</s>): the word <s>tad</s> ('that') likewise has distributive force. Here, by the inclusion of the word <s>sarva</s> ('all'), since everything without exception is encompassed, the [possibility of] external pervasion (<s>bahirvyāpti</s>) is precluded. "Such as pots and the like" (<s>yathā ghaṭādayaḥ</s>): the statement of the example is for the purpose of recollecting and focusing the mind of one for whom the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) establishing the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) between <s>sattva</s> (existence) and <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness) has operated in the case of pots and the like — it is not for the purpose of establishing the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). For the <s>sādhya</s> is not established merely from an example, since it is not the case that because one thing is so, everything is so — that would lead to overextension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). "And sound" (<s>saṃśca śabdaḥ</s>): this is the subsumption of the property of the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-locus) (<s>pakṣadharma</s>).

body.text: vaidharmyaprayogasyodāharaṇam- "tathā" ityādi | tathāśabdaḥ samuccaye | vaidharmyeṇa ca prayoga udāhriyate | atrāpi sarvagrahaṇaṃ vibhaktivipariṇāmena sambandhanīyam "kṣaṇikatvābhāve" sarvasmin "sattvā(ttvā)bhāvaḥ" iti |
body.translated_text: The example of the <s>vaidharmya</s> (negative) formulation: "Likewise" (<s>tathā</s>) and so forth. The word <s>tathā</s> indicates conjunction. And a proof by <s>vaidharmya</s> is illustrated. Here too, the word <s>sarva</s> ('all') should be connected with a change of case-ending: "In all that lacks <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness), there is absence of <s>sattva</s> (existence)."

body.text: prayogadvaye 'pi sarvagrahaṇasya phalaṃ darśayannāha- "sarvasmin sādhanadharmavati" dharmiṇi na dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇyeva "sādhyadharmasyo" pasaṃharaṇaṃ "upasaṃhāro" ḍhaukanaṃ tena yā "vyāptiḥ" ‘vyāpakasya tatra bhāva eva'; ityādirūpā tasyāḥ pradarśanaṃ pratipādanaṃ tadeva "lakṣaṇaṃ" yayoḥ tau tathoktau | tataśca ye sādhyadharmiṇaṃ parihṛtya bahirvyāptiṃ pradarśayanti te- yadyapi dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi sādhyadharmeṇa sādhanadharmo vyāptaḥ tāvatāsya sarvatra tathābhāvābhāvāt sādhyasiddhirayukteti- nirastā bhavanti | sarvatra vā sādhyadharmeṇa sādhanadharmasya vyāptiḥ tadbhāve, sā tathāvidhaiva kinna pradarśyate yenāsamarthā bahirvyāptirākhyāyate? | na hi ‘sa śyāmaḥ, tatputratvāt, paridṛśyamānaputravad'; iti tatputratvasya (

children.translated_text: Hbt 63

children.text: ) śyāmatvena sādhyād bahiḥ paridṛśyamānaputre vyāptipradarśane 'pi sādhyasiddhirbhavati | tasmād yaiva sarvopasaṃhāreṇa vyāptiḥ pramāṇasiddhapratibandhanibandhanā sādhyasiddhau samarthā saiva tatsmṛtaye pradarśanīyā | na ca sarvopasaṃhāreṇa vyāptipradarśane 'pi dharmaviśiṣṭo dharmyapi tadaiva pratīyate, yataḥ pakṣadharmopadarśanottarakālabhāvino 'numānasya smṛtitvaṃ syāt | tasyāḥ sādhyadharmiṇi sādhyadharmāvinābhūtasādhanadharmapratītinibandhanatvena tadupadarśanāt prāgasambhavāt | tatpūrvikāyāṃ ca vyāptau anantaraṃ viśeṣaviṣayamanumānaṃ kathaṃ smṛtiḥ syāt? iti |
children.translated_text: the <s>sādhya</s> is not established. Therefore, only that pervasion which, through universal subsumption, is grounded in an invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) established by <s>pramāṇa</s> and is capable of establishing the <s>sādhya</s> — that alone should be demonstrated for the purpose of recollecting it. Moreover, even when pervasion is demonstrated through universal subsumption, the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) qualified by the property is not cognized at that very moment, because the inference that occurs after the indication of the <s>pakṣadharma</s> (thesis-property) would [then] have the character of mere memory (<s>smṛti</s>). Since that [pervasion] has as its ground the cognition — in the <s>sādhya</s>'s property-bearer — of the <s>sādhana</s> property as inseparable from the <s>sādhya</s> property, it is impossible [to cognize the qualified <s>dharmin</s>] before demonstrating that [<s>pakṣadharma</s>]. And if the pervasion precedes [the <s>pakṣadharma</s>], how could the immediately subsequent inference concerning the particular [thesis] be [mere] memory?

body.translated_text: Showing the purpose of the word <s>sarva</s> ('all') in both forms of the proof, he says: The "subsumption" (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) — the bringing together — of the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (property to be proved) in "every [locus] possessing the <s>sādhana</s> (probans) property" — in every <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), not merely in the example — and the "pervasion" (<s>vyāpti</s>) thereby, which has the form 'the <s>vyāpaka</s> (pervader) is necessarily present there,' its demonstration, its establishment — that itself is the "characteristic" (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of those two [formulations], which are thus described. Therefore, those who, setting aside the <s>sādhya</s>'s property-bearer, demonstrate only external pervasion (<s>bahirvyāpti</s>) are refuted — for even though the <s>sādhana</s> property is pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s> property in the example-locus, the <s>sādhya</s> is not established merely from that, since such a relation does not hold everywhere. Or else, if the <s>sādhana</s> property is pervaded by the <s>sādhya</s> property everywhere where it is present, why is that very pervasion not demonstrated as such, so that the incapable external pervasion is [instead] proclaimed? For in the [proof]: 'He is dark-complexioned, because of being a son of that [dark man], like an observed son,' even when the pervasion of 'being a son of that one' with dark complexion is demonstrated externally in the observed son who is outside the <s>sādhya</s>,

body.text: 5. vaidharmyaprayoge 'pi vyāptipradarśanaṃ saṃgatam |
body.translated_text: 5. The demonstration of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is appropriate even in the <s>vaidharmya</s> (negative) formulation.

body.text: nanu ca sādharmyaprayogasya vyāptipradarśanalakṣaṇatvaṃ yuktam, sādhanadharme sati sādhyadharmasyavaśyāmbhāvitāpradarśanāt; vaidharmyaprayogasya tu katham? | tatra hi kevalaṃ sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvaḥ kathyate, na tu hetau sati sādhyasya bhāva eveti | naiṣa doṣaḥ | na hyatra sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvastuccharūpo darśyate, tasya heturūpatāvirodhāt | vastudharmo hi sattvādiko hetuḥ | tasyātmana evābhāvaḥ kathaṃ [hetusva]rūpaṃ bhaviṣyati, yatastrirūpo heturbhavet | kintu nivṛttau nivṛttidharmakatvaṃ svagato dharma upadarśyate vaidharmyaprayogeṇa, tathāvidhe ca sādhanadharme 'vaśyaṃtayā sādhyadharmasya bhāvaḥ pratīyata eva, anyathā tannivṛttau nivṛttidharmakatvasyaivāyogāditi na vyāptipradarśanalakṣaṇatvaṃ vaidharmyaprayogasya na yujyate |
body.translated_text: Objection: It is fitting that the <s>sādharmya</s> (positive) formulation has the characteristic of demonstrating pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), since it demonstrates the necessary presence of the <s>sādhya</s> property when the <s>sādhana</s> property is present. But how [is this so] for the <s>vaidharmya</s> (negative) formulation? For there, only the absence of the <s>hetu</s> in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is stated, not that the <s>sādhya</s> necessarily exists when the <s>hetu</s> exists. This is not a fault. For the absence of the <s>hetu</s> in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is not demonstrated here as a mere trifle, since that would be incompatible with its character as a reason (<s>hetu</s>). For a real property (<s>vastudharma</s>) such as existence (<s>sattva</s>) is the <s>hetu</s>. How could the mere absence of that nature itself be the essential character of the <s>hetu</s>, such that the <s>hetu</s> would be triple-characterized (<s>trirūpa</s>)? Rather, the <s>vaidharmya</s> formulation shows a property intrinsic to the <s>sādhana</s> — namely, its being such that when [the <s>sādhya</s>] ceases, it ceases. And when the <s>sādhana</s> property is of such a nature, the presence of the <s>sādhya</s> property is necessarily understood, since otherwise the very fact of ceasing when that ceases would be unjustified. Therefore, it is not the case that the <s>vaidharmya</s> formulation is unfit to have the characteristic of demonstrating pervasion.

body.text: 6. pratijñāprayogasya nairarthakyam |
body.translated_text: 6. The needlessness of the statement of the thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>) alongside the proof.

body.text: nanu dvividhe 'pi prayoge pratijñāprayogo nopadarśitaḥ tat kathaṃ tadarthāvagatiḥ?, tadarthapratyāyanāya ca sādhanaprayogo 'bhimataḥ ityata āha- "atra" anayoḥ prayogayoḥ "pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātrasāmarthyādeva" (

children.translated_text: Hbt 64

children.text: ) vakṣyamāṇakāt "pratijñārthasya" dharmadharmisamudāyalakṣaṇasya sādhyasya "pratīteḥ" hetoḥ "na" "pratījñāyāḥ prayoga upadarśitaḥ" | paraḥ sāmarthyamanavavudhyamāna āha- "apradarśite" vacanena "prameye" sādhye "kathaṃ" na kathañcit "tatpratītiḥ" pratijñārthapratītiḥ "iti" evaṃ "ced" yadi manyase tadā svārthānumānakāle "svayaṃ" paraṃ pratipādakamantareṇa "pratipattau" prameyasya "ka upadarśayitā"? naiva kaścit | svayameva tu sādhyavinābhūtasādhanadharmadarśanāt prameyaṃ pratipadyate tatha parārthānumāne 'pi tata eva tatpratītirastu kiṃ pratijñāvacanena? |
children.translated_text: ) From the forthcoming [statement] "of the thesis-meaning" — i.e., of the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) characterized by the aggregate of property and property-bearer — "because of the cognition" — i.e., from the <s>hetu</s> (reason) — "the statement of the thesis is not shown" to require a [separate] formulation. The opponent, not understanding the capacity [of the reason alone], says: "When the <s>prameya</s> (object to be proved), i.e., the <s>sādhya</s>, has not been indicated" by a verbal statement, "how" — in no way whatsoever — "can there be cognition of that" — cognition of the thesis-meaning — "thus" "if" you think so, then at the time of inference-for-oneself (<s>svārthānumāna</s>), "when one cognizes by oneself" without any external instructor, "who is the one who indicates" the <s>prameya</s>? No one at all. Rather, by oneself, merely from seeing the proving property that is inseparable from the <s>sādhya</s>, one cognizes the <s>prameya</s>. Likewise, in inference-for-others (<s>parārthānumāna</s>) too, let the cognition of that [<s>sādhya</s>] arise from that very [reason] alone — what is the need for a thesis-statement?

body.translated_text: Objection: In both types of proof, the statement of the thesis (<s>pratijñāprayoga</s>) has not been shown. How then is the understanding of its meaning [achieved]? And since the proof-statement is intended to convey its meaning — therefore [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says: "Here," in these two proofs, "by the mere force of the statement of the connection of the <s>pakṣadharma</s> (thesis-property)" alone,

body.text: yadi svayaṃpratipattikāle na kaścit prameyasyopadarśayitā kathaṃ tarhi tatpratipattiḥ? ityata āha- "pradeśasthaṃ" sādhyadharmiṇi sthitaṃ "dhūmaṃ" sādhanadharmaṃ "upalabdhavataḥ" pratyakṣeṇa dṛṣṭavataḥ sataḥ "tasya" dhūmasya "agninā" sādhyadharmeṇa pramāṇataḥ pratibandhaniścayabalāt prākpratipannāyāḥ "vyāpteḥ" avinābhāvasya "smaraṇe" sati "tatsāmarthyādeva" pakṣadharmagrahaṇavyāptigrahaṇasāmarthyādeva pratijñāprayogarahitād "agniratra iti" evaṃrūpā "pratijñārthapratītirbhavati" |
body.translated_text: If at the time of cognition-by-oneself no one indicates the <s>prameya</s>, then how is there cognition of it? To this he says: For one who has "perceived" — seen through perception — "smoke" — i.e., the proving property — "located at a place" — i.e., present in the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (the locus to be proved) — when there is "recollection" of the "pervasion" (<s>vyāpti</s>) — i.e., the invariable concomitance — of "that" smoke "with fire" — i.e., with the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (property to be proved) — [a pervasion] previously ascertained through a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) by the force of determining the necessary connection — "by that capacity alone" — by the capacity of apprehending the thesis-property and apprehending the pervasion alone, without the formulation of a thesis — there arises "cognition of the thesis-meaning in the form 'there is fire here.'"

body.text: syānmatam- tatrāpyasya karṇapiśācikādiḥ prameyaṃ kathayatyevetyata āha- "na ca" naiva "tatra" svārthanumānakāle "kaścit" karṇapiśācikadiradṛśyo "‘agniratra'- iti" evam "asmai" pratipatre(tre) prameyaṃ "nivedayati" kathayati | yadi bhavān satyavādī naivaṃ vaktumarhati | tathā hi- vayamapi pradeśasthadhūmadarśanāt tasyāgninā vyāptismaraṇasāpekṣādagniṃ pratipadyāmahe | na cāsmabhyaṃ kaścit nivedayati ‘agniratra'; iti, bhavati ca tatpratipattiḥ, tathā tadanyasyāpi sā yuktarūpaiveti |
body.translated_text: One might think: even there, some invisible agent like a <s>karṇapiśāca</s> (whispering demon) etc. tells him the <s>prameya</s>. To this he says: "And" indeed "no one" — no invisible being such as a <s>karṇapiśāca</s> etc. — "there" at the time of inference-for-oneself, "communicates" — tells — the <s>prameya</s> "to him" — to the cognizer — in the form "'there is fire here.'" If you are truthful, you should not speak thus. For consider: we too cognize fire from seeing smoke located at a place, dependent on the recollection of its pervasion with fire — and no one communicates to us 'there is fire here'; yet that cognition does occur. Likewise, for another person too, such [cognition] is perfectly reasonable.

body.text: yadyapi na kaścit nivedayati tathāpi svayameva prameyaṃ vyavasthāpya tatpratipattaye liṅgamanusariṣyatīti cet, āha- "nāpi" na kevalaṃ na kaścit nivedayati "svayamapi prāgeva" liṅgavyāpārāt na pratipadyate "kiñcid" agnyādikam | kasmāt? (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 65

children.text: ) iti cet, "pramāṇaṃ" hetum "antareṇa" vinā ‘agniratra" ityevaṃ pratīteḥ "nimittābhāvāt" | trirūpo hi hetuḥ parokṣārthapratīternimittam, tadabhāve sā kathaṃ bhavet? | atha liṅgamantareṇāpyevaṃ pratītirbhavatiti brūyāt tadā pratītāviṣyamāṇāyāṃ liṅgasya vaiyarthyam, tasyānumeyapratipattyarthatvāt, tena vinā tatpratipattau kathamasya niṣprayojanatā na syāt? |
children.translated_text: ) If so, [it is] "because there is no cause" for the cognition 'there is fire here' "without" — i.e., in the absence of — "a <s>pramāṇa</s>" — i.e., a <s>hetu</s> (reason). For indeed, a reason possessing the triple character is the cause of cognizing an imperceptible object; in its absence, how could that [cognition] occur? And if one were to say that such cognition occurs even without the logical mark, then when cognition is about to occur [anyway], the logical mark would be purposeless, since its purpose is the cognition of the inferable object — when that [cognition] occurs without it, how could [the logical mark] not be devoid of purpose?

body.translated_text: Even if no one communicates [the <s>prameya</s>], still, one might object that the person will first ascertain the <s>prameya</s> by himself and then seek the logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for the purpose of cognizing it. To this he says: "Not only" does no one communicate it, "but also one does not by oneself cognize" "anything" such as fire etc. "prior to" the operation of the logical mark. Why? (

body.text: atyantamūḍhatāṃ ca parasya darśayannāha- "svayameva" svatantra eva ‘agniratra'- iti vyavasthāpya | kathaṃ svatantro vyavasthāpayati? | "akasmāt" pramāṇamantareṇa vyavasthāpanāt "tatpratipattaye" nirnimittavyavasthāpitaprameyapratipattyarthaṃ "paścāt" "liṅgaṃ" tannimittam "anusaratīti ko 'yaṃ pratipatteḥ kramaḥ" paripāṭiḥ? | tathā hi- prathamaṃ liṅgānusaraṇam, tataḥ sādhyapratipattiriti vipaścitāṃ kramaḥ | ayaṃ tvapūrvo 'numātā yastadviparyayamāśrayata iti upahasati | yattalloke gīyate- śīro muṇḍayitvā nakṣatraṃ pṛcchatīti tattulyatvādasya kramasya | tasmāt pakṣadharmagrahaṇavyāptismaraṇasāmarthyādeva svayaṃ pratipadyate | tacca pratipādakaṃ kathitemaveti na kiñcit prameyanirddeśena |
body.translated_text: Showing the extreme foolishness of the opponent, he says: Having ascertained "by oneself" — independently — 'there is fire here,' how does one independently ascertain [this]? "Without any cause" — i.e., without a <s>pramāṇa</s> — having ascertained it, [and then] "for the purpose of cognizing that" — for the purpose of cognizing the <s>prameya</s> that was ascertained without any cause — "afterward" one "seeks the logical mark" — i.e., its cause — "what sort of order of cognition is this?" For indeed, the order of the wise is: first, the investigation of the logical mark, and then the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>. But this novel reasoner who resorts to the reverse — [the author] ridicules [him]. This order of his is like what is said in the world: 'Having shaved one's head, one asks about the auspicious constellation.' Therefore, by the capacity of apprehending the thesis-property and recollecting the pervasion alone, one cognizes by oneself. And that which instructs [others] has been explained as the statement [of the reason] — so nothing [is achieved] by indicating the <s>prameya</s> [separately].

body.text: yadi nāma svārthānumānakāle svayameva sādhyaṃ pratipadyate tad yuktameva, liṅgasyāpi tatra svayameva pratipatteḥ | parārthānumāne tu parato yathā liṅgaṃ pratyeti tathā prameyamapi parata eva pratyetavyam | ato yukta eva pratijñāprayoga ityata āha- "pareṇāpi" na kevalaṃ svayameva prāg vyavasthāpyamānaṃ plavate pareṇāpi vādinā "tat" prameyam "ucyamānaṃ plavat eva" tadvacanasya sandigdhārthabhidhāyakatayā sādhyaniścayānaṅgatvāt prameyagāmbhīryānavāgāhinaḥ paramparayāpyatatsambaddhasya vivakṣāmātranibandhanatayoparyevāvasthāpanāt | kasmāt plavate? iti cet, "upayogābhāvāt" nāsya sādhyapratītiṃ prati kaścidupayogaḥ, tatpratyāyanasamarthāsyānabhidhānāditi yāvat |
body.translated_text: If indeed at the time of inference-for-oneself one cognizes the <s>sādhya</s> by oneself, that is perfectly reasonable, since even the logical mark is cognized by oneself there. But in inference-for-others, just as the logical mark is cognized from another [person's statement], so too the <s>prameya</s> should be cognized from another alone. Therefore the formulation of the thesis is indeed appropriate — to this he says: "Even when stated by another" — not only does it float [i.e., fail to settle] when ascertained by oneself — even when stated by the proponent, "that" <s>prameya</s> "simply floats" — because the thesis-statement conveys a meaning that is doubtful, and thus is not conducive to the determination of the <s>sādhya</s>; because one who does not fathom the depth of the <s>prameya</s> — even indirectly, if unconnected with it — merely by the wish [of the speaker], it remains floating on the surface. Why does it float? "Because there is no use" — it has no use with respect to the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>, since what is capable of conveying that [<s>sādhya</s>] is not being stated — this is the meaning.

body.text: parastūpayogamātraṃ kadācid brūyād ityāśaṅkayāha- "viṣayopadarśanaṃ" hetoryo viṣayaḥ sādhyaṃ tadupadarśanaṃ pratijñāvacanasyopayogaḥ "cet matam" | atrāha "tenaiva" viṣayeṇa, "tāva"cchabdaḥ krame | viṣayasyopadarśyamānasyārthavattāyāṃ tadupadarśanaṃ pratijñāvacanasya prayojanaṃ bhavet | viṣayeṇaiva tu darśyamānena "ko 'rthaḥ" kiṃ prayojanam? |
body.translated_text: Anticipating that the opponent might sometimes claim some use [for the thesis-statement], he says: If it is "thought" that the use of the thesis-statement is "the indication of the domain" — i.e., showing what the <s>sādhya</s> is, which is the domain of the <s>hetu</s> — to this he replies: "By that very" domain — the word 'first' (<s>tāvat</s>) indicates sequence. If the domain being indicated were meaningful, then indicating it would be the purpose of the thesis-statement. But "what is the purpose" — what use is there — of the domain itself being indicated [when it accomplishes nothing]?

body.text: nanu sādhyapratītiḥ sādhyarmyavatprayogādipratītiśca viṣayopadarśanasyārthaḥ | tatastudupadarśanaṃ pratijñāvacanasya prayojanam | tathā hi- asati sādhyanirdeśe ‘yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityam'; ityukte ‘kimayaṃ sādharmyavāna prayogaḥ? uta vaidharmyavān?'; iti na jñāyeta | ubhayaṃ hyatrāśaṅkyate- kṛtakatvenānityatve sādhye sādharmyavān, nityatvenākṛtakatve vā vaidharmyavān iti | ‘anityaḥ śabdaḥ'; ‘akṛtako vā iti tu pratijñāvacane satyubhayamasandigdhamavagamyate | hetuviruddhānaikāntikapratītiśca na syāt | pratijñāpūrvake tu prayoge ‘anityaḥ śabdaḥ, kṛtakatvāt'; iti hetubhāvaḥ pratīyate, ‘nityaḥ, kṛtakatvāt'; iti viruddhatā, ‘pratyatnānantarīyakaḥ kṛtakatvāt'; ityanaikāntikatvam | hetośca trairūpyaṃ na gamyeta, tasya sādhyāpekṣayā vyavasthānāt | sati pratijñāvacane avayave samudāyopacārāt sādhyadharmī pakṣa iti tatra vṛttasya kṛtakatvasya pakṣadharmatvaṃ; sādhyadharmasāmānyena ca samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣa iti tatra vartamānasya sapakṣe sattvam; na sapakṣo 'sapakṣa iti sādhyadharmavirahiṇyavṛttasyāsapakṣe 'pyasattvaṃ pratīyeta ityāśaṅkayāha- "yadi pratīti" sādhyasya niścayalakṣaṇā sādharmyavatprayogādeśca svarūpāvadhāraṇātmikā | "anyathā" pratijñāvacanamantareṇa "na syāt tadā" yaduktaṃ sādhyasidhyarthaṃ sādharmyavatprayogādijñānārthaṃ ca viṣayopadarśanam iti tat "sarvaṃ śobheta" yāvatā svarthānumānakāle pratijñāvacanamantareṇāpi pakṣadharmagrahaṇa sambandhasmaraṇataḥ sādhyasiddhilakṣaṇā bhavatyeva pratītiḥ ityākhyātameva | tadvat parārthe 'pyanumāne bhaviṣyati | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 67

children.text: ) yata evaṃ "tasmāt" "eṣa" pratijñāprayogavādī yadā svayaṃ sādhyaṃ pratyeti tadā svayaṃ sādhyasya "pratītau" viṣaya upasthāpyate yena pratijñāvacanadvāreṇa puṃsā "kenacit" tena "vināpi" "pratiyan" sādhyaṃ niścinvan liṅgasāmarthyadeva | yadāsmābhiḥ pratipādyate tadā "asmān kāryiṇo dṛṣṭvā vyaktaṃ" pratijñāprayogalakṣaṇaṃ "mūlyaṃ mṛgayate" | ka iva? "parvabrāhmaṇa iva" | yathā dakṣiṇāmantareṇāpyanyadā aurdhvarathiko brāhmaṇo bhuñjāno 'nyadā śrāddhādiparvaṇyarthinaṃ śraddhāluṃ bravīti- yadi me ghṛtapūraṃ ghṛtapūraṃ prati rūpakaṃ dadāsi tato 'haṃ bhuñje nānyatheti | tena tulyo bhavānapīti |
children.translated_text: ) Since this is so, "therefore" "this" advocate of the thesis-formulation — when he himself cognizes the <s>sādhya</s>, the domain is presented "in [his] cognition" of the <s>sādhya</s> by himself — [yet] he, through the thesis-statement, "without" that "someone" [i.e., without needing any external indication], "cognizing" — determining the <s>sādhya</s> by the power of the logical mark alone — "seeing us as customers, evidently seeks a price" — i.e., a price in the form of the thesis-formulation. Like whom? "Like a festival-<s>brāhmaṇa</s>." Just as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who performs funeral rites (<s>aurdhvarathika</s>), who eats [at ceremonies] even without a fee at other times, on the occasion of a <s>śrāddha</s> (memorial rite) etc. says to the eager and faithful patron: 'If you give me one <s>rūpaka</s> (coin) per ghee-cake, then I will eat; not otherwise' — you are like him.

body.translated_text: But, one might object, the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s> and the cognition of the <s>sādharmyavat</s> formulation (positive formulation) etc. are the purpose of indicating the domain. From that, indicating the domain is the purpose of the thesis-statement. For consider: in the absence of stating the <s>sādhya</s>, when one says 'whatever is produced is impermanent,' [the question arises:] 'Is this a positive formulation (<s>sādharmyavat prayoga</s>)? Or a negative one (<s>vaidharmyavat</s>)?' — this cannot be known. For both can be suspected here: if impermanence is to be proved through being-produced, it is a positive formulation; or if non-production through permanence, a negative formulation. But when the thesis-statement is present — 'sound is impermanent' or 'non-produced' — both [the type of formulation and the <s>sādhya</s>] are understood without doubt. And the cognition of the <s>hetu</s> as contradictory or inconclusive would not arise [without it]. But in a formulation preceded by a thesis — 'sound is impermanent, because of being produced' — the status as a proper <s>hetu</s> is cognized; 'it is permanent, because of being produced' — contradictoriness; 'it arises immediately after effort, because of being produced' — inconclusiveness. And the triple character of the <s>hetu</s> could not be known, since it is determined relative to the <s>sādhya</s>. When the thesis-statement is present — by figurative transfer from the component to the aggregate — the <s>sādhyadharmin</s> (property-bearer) is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject), so the thesis-property status of being-produced, which obtains in it, [is understood]; and what has the same meaning as the general <s>sādhyadharma</s> is the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance), so the presence [of the <s>hetu</s>] in the <s>sapakṣa</s>; and what is not a <s>sapakṣa</s> is the <s>asapakṣa</s> (dissimilar instance), so the absence of what does not occur in what is devoid of the <s>sādhyadharma</s> in the <s>asapakṣa</s> too would be cognized — anticipating this objection, he says: "If the cognition" — i.e., the determination of the <s>sādhya</s>, and the apprehension of the nature of the positive formulation etc. — "would not be possible otherwise" — without the thesis-statement — "then all that would be fitting." However, since at the time of inference-for-oneself, even without the thesis-statement, from the apprehension of the thesis-property and the recollection of the relation, cognition in the form of the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> does indeed occur — this has already been explained. Likewise, in inference-for-others too it will be so. (

body.text: kiñca, yadapi bravīṣi- parārthānumānakāle yathā liṅgaṃ pareṇānabhidhīyamānaṃ na pratyeti pratipādyastathā sādhyamapīti | tadaitad yujyate yadyasau vādivacanamātreṇa liṅgamapi niścitya tadanusāreṇa sādhyamavagacchet, parapratītyarthinaśca tadā vayamapi pratijñāṃ kinna prayuñjmahe liṅgavacanarahitām? | asmadvacanasyaiva taṃ prati pramāṇatayā, tata evānumeyapratīteḥ, tadvacanasya caritārthatvāt | na caitadasti, yataḥ "asmadvacanādapi" na kevalaṃ svārthānumānakāle asmadvacanamantareṇa ityapiśabdaḥ | kintu yadāpyasmadvacanaṃ pravṛttaṃ tadāpi "naiva" asmadvacanāt "liṅgamapi pratyeti" kuta eva sādhyasiddhye 'nusariṣyati? | api tu svayamasya yadi talliṅgaṃ kutaścit pramāṇataḥ siddhaṃ bhavati "asmadvacanena tu" kevalaṃ tatra "smṛtisamādhānamātraṃ kriyate" | tadā svayaṃ siddhameva liṅgamanusṛtya sādhyaṃ pratyeti | nāsmadvacanāt pānīyamapi pibatīti | "tasmāt" "ko 'nayoḥ" pratijñāvacanāvacanātmikayoḥ "avasthayorviśeṣaḥ"?, ubhayatra svayaṃsiddhaliṅgasāmarthyādeva sādhyapratīterna kaścit | tataḥ svaparārthānumānayoḥ svayaṃsiddhaliṅgānusaraṇam, tataḥ sādhyapratītiṃ ca prati viśeṣābhāvāt pratijñopanyāsaḥ parārthānumāne 'pi vyartha eva | liṅgamapi hi tāvadatra nābhidhīyate yadi tat (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 68

children.text: ) pūrvaprasiddhaṃ svayamanusmaret kimaṅga punaḥ sandigdhārthābhidhāyakaṃ pratijñāvacanamupādīyate? |
children.translated_text: ) [logical mark] were previously established and one were to recollect it by oneself — how much less would the thesis-statement, which conveys a doubtful meaning, be adopted?

body.translated_text: Moreover, as for your claim that 'at the time of inference-for-others, just as the logical mark is not cognized by the person being instructed when not stated by another, so too the <s>sādhya</s>' — that would be valid only if he were to ascertain the logical mark merely by the proponent's statement and then, following that, cognize the <s>sādhya</s>. And if we are seeking the other's cognition, then why do we not formulate the thesis alone, without the statement of the logical mark? Since our statement alone would be a <s>pramāṇa</s> for him, and from that alone the cognition of the inferable [would follow], and his [own] statement would have served its purpose. But this is not so, because "even from our statement" — the word 'also' (<s>api</s>) means: not only at the time of inference-for-oneself without our statement [is it so], but even when our statement is employed — "the logical mark itself is not cognized" [merely from our statement] — how then will it serve to establish the <s>sādhya</s>? Rather, if that logical mark is established for him from some <s>pramāṇa</s> on its own, "by our statement, merely a recollection and focusing [of attention]" is brought about. Then, following the logical mark that is established on its own, one cognizes the <s>sādhya</s>. It is not as if he drinks even water from our statement. "Therefore" "what distinction is there between these two states" — the state with the thesis-statement and the state without it? In both cases, one cognizes the <s>sādhya</s> by the power of the logical mark that is established on its own — there is no [distinction] whatsoever. Hence, since there is no difference between inference-for-oneself and inference-for-others with respect to following the self-established logical mark and thence cognizing the <s>sādhya</s>, the presentation of the thesis is pointless even in inference-for-others. For indeed, even the logical mark is not stated here if that (

body.text: syānmatam- yadi nāma sādhyasiddhau pratijñāvacanasya nopayogastadartho 'sya prayogo mā bhūta, sādharmyatvatprayogādijñānārthaṃ tu tadupadānamavasthitameva, tasyānyathā pratītyabhāvāt ityata āha- "dṛṣṭā ca sādharmyavatprayogādeḥ pratijñāvacanamantarenāpi pratītiḥ," tatastadartho 'pi pratijñopanyāso na śobhate |
body.translated_text: One might think: even if the thesis-statement has no use for establishing the <s>sādhya</s>, let its formulation for that purpose not occur; but its adoption for the purpose of knowing the positive formulation (<s>sādharmyavatprayoga</s>) etc. remains in place, since those [formulations] cannot be cognized otherwise. To this he says: "And it has been shown that cognition of the positive formulation etc. is possible even without the thesis-statement" — therefore, the presentation of the thesis for that purpose too is not fitting.

body.text: kutaḥ punaḥ sādharmyavatprayogāderasati sādhyanirddeśe pratītiḥ? ityāha- pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātrāditi" | evaṃ manyate- naiva hi kaścit ‘yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityam" etāvanmātramabhidhīyāste, sādhananyūnatayaivāsya parājayāt, kintvavaśyaṃ hetordvarmiṇyupasaṃhāraṃ karotīti | tatra yadi ‘kṛtakaśca śabdaḥ'; iti brūyāt tadā sādhya(dha)rmyavatprayogapratītiḥ, atha ‘nityaśca'; ityabhidadhyāt tadā vaidharmyavata iti sambandhavacanapūrvakāt pakṣadharmavacanāt prayogadvayāvagatiḥ |
body.translated_text: From what source, then, is there cognition of the positive formulation etc. in the absence of stating the <s>sādhya</s>? He says: "From the mere statement of the thesis-property and the relation." The idea is as follows: indeed, no one merely states just 'whatever is produced is impermanent' [and stops there], since he would be defeated due to the incompleteness of the proof; rather, he necessarily makes the application of the <s>hetu</s> to the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer). There, if he says 'and sound is produced,' then the cognition of the positive formulation [arises]; but if he says 'and [sound] is permanent,' then [the cognition] of the negative formulation — thus, from the statement of the thesis-property preceded by the statement of the relation, the understanding of both types of formulation [is achieved].

body.text: hetuviruddhānaikāntikā api pakṣadharmavacanamātreṇa na pratīyante | yadā tu sambandhavacanamapi kriyate tadā kathamapratītiḥ? | tathā hi- ‘yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityam'; iti pakṣadharmavacane satyukte heturavagamyate, vidhiyamānenānūdyamānasya vyāpteḥ | ‘yatkṛtakaṃ tannityam'; ityabhidhāne viruddhaḥ, viparyayavyāpteḥ | ‘yat kṛtakaṃ tat prayatnānantarīyakam'; iti pradarśane vyabhicārādanaikāntikādhyavasāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: The <s>hetu</s> as contradictory or inconclusive too is not cognized merely from the statement of the thesis-property [alone]. But when the statement of the relation is also made, how can there be non-cognition? For consider: when the thesis-property statement is present and one says 'whatever is produced is impermanent,' the <s>hetu</s> is understood — because the pervasion of what is being legislated with what is being presupposed [is grasped]. When one says 'whatever is produced is permanent,' [it is understood as] contradictory, because of pervasion with the opposite. When one says 'whatever is produced is that which immediately follows effort,' [it is understood as] inconclusive, because of deviation.

body.text: trairūpyamapi hetorgamyata eva, yato vyāptipradarśanakāle vyāpako dharmaḥ sādhyatayāvagamyate | yatra ca vyāpyo dharmo dharmiṇyupasaṃhriyate sa vyāpakādharmaviśiṣṭatayāvagamyamānaḥ sādhyasamudāyaikadeśatayā pakṣa ityupasaṃhṛtasya vyāpyadharmasya pakṣadharmatvāvagatiḥ, sā ca vyāptiryatra dharmiṇyupadarśyate sa sādhyadharmasāmānyena samāno 'rthaḥ sapakṣaḥ pratīyata iti sapakṣe (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 69

children.text: ) sattvamavagamyate, sāmarthyācca vyāpakanivṛttau vyāpyanivṛttiryatrāvasīyate so 'sapakṣa ityasapakṣe 'pyasatva(ttva)mapi niścīyata iti, yadi pakṣādibhirapi jñātaiḥ kiñcitprayojanaṃ | na tu vyavahartaṇāṃ pakṣādisaṅketāpekṣā parokṣārthagatirbhavati | tathā hi- yat kvacid dṛṣṭaṃ tasya yatra pratibandhaḥ tadvidastasya tad gamakaṃ tatra iti hi loke vastugatirbhavati, na pakṣadisaṅketagrahaṇāpekṣā | tatra yatheṣṭaṃ śāstrakārā gamakarūpapratipattaye svasaṅketenānyathā vā lakṣaṇaṃ praṇayantu | na tu vyavahārakāle tadanusaraṇaṃ kvacidupayujyate | tatsaṅketapratipāditameva tu yathoktaṃ gamakaṃ rūpamupayogi vyavahartṝṇām | taccet pratipannaṃ tāvataiva sādhyasiddhiḥ sañjātā iti pakṣasapakṣādisaṅketāparijñāne 'pi na kiñcit plūyate | ata evācāryapādai ‘rtrāntarīyakārthadarśanaṃ tadvido 'numāna'; miti gamakarūpamātrameva pakṣādisaṅketānapekṣaṃ pratipāditam | svaprajñāparādhāstu tatrāpi kaiścidasanta eva doṣāḥ prakīrtyanta iti kimatra brūmaḥ? | "tasmāt" sādharmyavatprayogādijñānārthamapi pratijñāvacanaṃ pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātra eva yathoktena prakāreṇa pratīterayuktamiti "kastasya" pratijñāvacanasya "upayogaḥ" naivaṃ kaścit |
children.translated_text: — existence [in the <s>sapakṣa</s>] is understood, and the <s>asapakṣa</s> (heterogeneous instance) is that where the cessation of the pervaded is ascertained from the cessation of the pervader, by capacity — thus non-existence in the <s>asapakṣa</s> is also ascertained. [This holds] only if some purpose is served by knowing the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) and the like [as technical designations]. But the cognition of supersensory objects for those who engage in practice does not depend on the conventions of <s>pakṣa</s> and so on. For: "that which is observed somewhere — for one who knows the necessary connection of that with something — that is indicative of that there" — this is the way things work in the world, without dependence on grasping the conventions of <s>pakṣa</s> and so on. Let the authors of treatises, as they wish, compose definitions using their own conventions or otherwise, for the understanding of the form of the indicator. But following those [conventions] is never useful at the time of actual practice. What is useful for practitioners is precisely the form of the indicator as described, which is taught through those conventions. If that has been understood, the establishment of the <s>sādhya</s> has been accomplished just by that — so even when the conventions of <s>pakṣa</s>, <s>sapakṣa</s>, and so on are not fully known, nothing is lost. For this very reason, the Master (<s>Ācāryapāda</s>, i.e., <s>Dignāga</s>) taught only the form of the indicator, without dependence on the conventions of <s>pakṣa</s> and so on: "Inference, for one who knows it, is the seeing of a meaning connected with something else." But those who, through their own intellectual failings, proclaim non-existent faults even there — what can we say about that? "Therefore," even for the purpose of knowing the formulation in terms of agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>) and the like, the thesis-statement (<s>pratijñāvacana</s>), being nothing but a statement of the connection of the property to the thesis-subject, is inappropriate since cognition arises in the manner described [without it] — "what use is there" of that thesis-statement? None whatsoever.

body.translated_text: The triple character of the <s>hetu</s> too is indeed known, because at the time of demonstrating the pervasion, the pervading property is understood as the <s>sādhya</s>. And where the pervaded property is applied to the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), that [<s>dharmin</s>], being understood as qualified by a property other than the pervading one, is the <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis-subject) as a part of the <s>sādhya</s>-aggregate — thus the thesis-property status of the pervaded property that has been applied [is understood]. And where that pervasion is demonstrated in a <s>dharmin</s>, that which has the same meaning as the general <s>sādhyadharma</s> is understood as the <s>sapakṣa</s> (similar instance) — thus the presence [of the <s>hetu</s>] in the <s>sapakṣa</s> [is known]. And in the (

body.text: svayaṃ cāyaṃ vādī yena krameṇānumeyaṃ pratipannavāṃstamullaṅghya parapratipattaye kramāntaramāśrayan pravañcakatayā dhūrta eva pratīyate, na savdṛtta ityupadarśayannāha- "svaniścayavat" ityādi | yathātmano niścayasyotpādanaṃ kṛtaṃ tathaiva "anyeṣāmapi niścayotpādā(da)nāya" ca parahitanirataiḥ "sādhanamucyate", "tatra" etasmiṃ(smin) nyāye sati svayamayaṃ vādī "prameyasyopadarśanena" upadarśakena vacanena "vināpi" svārthānumānakāle "pratipadya" prameyaṃ "paraṃ" saṃśayitādikaṃ "pratipādayan" svapratipannaṃ prameyamavabodhayan "apūrvaṃ" svapratipattikāle pūrvaṃ yaḥ prameyapratipattau "kramaḥ" upāyo 'nubhūtastasmādanyam "āśrayata iti kimatra" kramāntarāśrayaṇe "kāraṇam"? naiva kiñcit paravyāmohanaṃ muktvā | tathā hi- yadi svapratipattikramaḥ (
