children.text: ) pratītinibandhanaṃ kiṃ tatparityāgena kramāntarāśrayaṇam?, kathaṃ tena svayaṃ pratipannavānasīti? | yata evaṃ "tasmānna prameyasya" sādhyasya "vacanena" pratijñākhyena "kiñcit prayojanam" | kutaḥ? | ‘anyathāpi'; vināpi tena "pratipatteḥ" sādhyapratīteḥ "utpatteri"tyupasaṃhāraḥ |
children.translated_text: — what grounds the cognition? Why abandon that and resort to a different procedure? How did he himself come to understand [the inference], if [the different procedure were needed]? Since this is so, "therefore, by stating" — through the thesis-statement — "the <s>prameya</s>" — the <s>sādhya</s> — "there is no purpose." Why? "Since cognition [arises] even otherwise" — even without it, the cognition of the <s>sādhya</s>

body.translated_text: And the proponent himself — who, having understood the object of inference through a certain process, bypasses that process and resorts to a different procedure for the sake of another's understanding — appears to be a cheat and a rogue, not a person of good conduct. Showing this, he says: "Just as for one's own determination" and so on. Just as the production of one's own determination was accomplished, "so too for others"

body.text: 7. upanayanigamanāderapi sādhanavākyānaṅgatvam |
body.translated_text: 7. The non-essentiality of application (<s>upanaya</s>), conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>), and the like to the proof-statement.

body.text: evaṃ pratijñāṃ sādhanavākyādapanīyāparamapyupanayanigamanādikaṃ paraparikalpitaṃ sādhanavākyādapanetumuktameva nyāyamatidiśannāha- "etena" anyathāpi pratipatterutpatteḥ'; iti nyāyena "upanayanigamanādikaṃ" ādigrahaṇāt saṃśayajijñāsādikaṃ "pratyuktaṃ" pratyākhyātam | tatra "udāharaṇāpekṣaḥ ‘tathā'; ityupasaṃhāro ‘na tathe'ti vā sādhyasyopanayaḥ", "pratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ pratijñā" iti tu pratijñāyāḥ | etenetyetadeva darśayati- "etāvataiva" pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātreṇaiva upanayādirahitena "sādhyapratīteḥ bhāvāt" utpatteriti |
body.translated_text: Having thus removed the thesis-statement from the proof-statement (<s>sādhanavākya</s>), extending the same principle already stated to remove the further [elements] — the application (<s>upanaya</s>), conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>), and the like, which are fabricated by others — from the proof-statement, he says: "By this" — by the principle that "cognition arises even otherwise" — "the application, conclusion, and so on" — by the word "and so on," [including] doubt, desire to know, and the like — "are answered."

body.text: atrodyo(ddyo)takaraḥ prāha- pratijñā tāvadviṣayanirddeśārthamavaśyakartavyā, yato lokaḥ prathamaṃ karma cchedyādikaṃ nirūpayati | tataḥ kuṭhārādikaṃ sādhanaṃ vyāpārayati | upanayenāpi yāvad dṛṣṭānte dṛṣṭasāmarthyo heturddharmiṇi nopasaṃhriyate tāvat kutaḥ sādhyapratītiḥ? | svārthānumānadṛṣṭaśca pratyavamarśapratyayārtho 'nena darśyate | tathā hi- svārthānumāne prathamaṃ pradeśe dhūmaṃ paśyati, tato ‘yatra yatrāhaṃ dhūmamadrākṣaṃ tatra tatrāgnimapi'; iti vyāptiṃ smarati | tato ‘dhūmaścātra'; iti punaḥ pratyavamṛśati, sa pratyavamarśārthaḥ parārthānumāne upanayenocyate | nigamanamapyavaśyābhidhānīyam, yato yadyapi pūrvaṃ anityaḥ śabda ityuktam, na tu tāvatāsya niścayo jātaḥ | samprati tu pramāṇabalāyāto 'rthaḥ tatsampratyayārthamanena nigamyate | aśeṣapramāṇavyāpāraścānenopasaṃhriyate | tathā hi- āgamaḥ pratijñā, heturanumānaṃ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 71.

children.text: ) dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratyakṣamupamānamupanayaḥ | tadetasya pramāṇacatuṣṭasyāpi vyāpāro nigamanenopasaṃhriyate- iti kathamasya na sāphalyam? ityetadāśaṅkayāha- "ḍiṇḍikarāgaṃ parityajya" ḍiṇḍikāḥ- nagnācāryāḥ te niṣphalamuparyupari nāmalekhane prasaktāḥ tatasteṣāmiva ‘pareṇokte tasyopari mayāvaśyamayuktatayā niṣphalamapyabhidhānīyam'; ityasthānābhiniveśaṃ tyaktvā "akṣiṇī nimīlya" bahirvikṣepamupasaṃhṛtya "cintaya tāvat"- "kimiyatā" pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātrakeṇa vākyena sādhyasya "pratītiḥ syāt na vā?" iti | yāvatā yāvāneva parārthānumāne 'rtho 'bhidhānīya ityasmābhiranujñāyate tāvānevānyūnānatiriktaḥ svārthānumāne 'pi pratītiheturdṛṣṭaḥ, tasya ka iha śaktervyāghātaḥ? yenāsau parārthānumāne 'pi pratītiṃ na kuryāt | "bhāve" pratīteḥ "kiṃ prapañcamālayā" pratijñopanayanigamanalakṣaṇayā, bālapratārakatadupayogopavarṇanalakṣaṇayā vā? | tathā hi- pratijñopanayanigamanaprayoge 'pi yadi pramāṇaniścitā svasādhyavyāptiḥ sādhanadharmasya na syāt, sādhyadharmiṇi vā sadbhāvastadāsya naiva pratītihetutā | tatsambhave tu pratijñādyabhāve 'pi svārthānumāna iva gamakarūpāvaikalyāt sā na nivāryata iti kimasthānanirbandhena iti? | nahi sādhyadharmākṣepaṇasāmarthyavirahe sādhanadharmasya vādivacanamātrāt sādhyaniścayo yuktaḥ, hetūpanyāsavairthyaprasaṅgāt, tasya tadākṣepasāmarthye vā pratijñāvacanasyeti |
children.translated_text: — the example is perception, comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is the application. And the operation of this fourfold <s>pramāṇa</s> is concluded by the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) — so how can it be without result? Anticipating this objection, he says: "Abandoning the attachment of the <s>Ḍiṇḍikas</s>" — the <s>Ḍiṇḍikas</s> are naked ascetics (<s>nagnācāryas</s>), who are engaged in the fruitless activity of writing names upon names, one on top of another; therefore

body.translated_text: Here <s>Uddyotakara</s> objects: The thesis-statement must necessarily be made for the purpose of indicating the subject matter, since people first determine the task — cutting and the like — and then apply the instrument — the axe and the like. Also, as long as the reason, whose capacity has been observed in the example, is not applied to the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) through the application (<s>upanaya</s>), so long

body.text: yatūktam ‘viṣayapradarśanāya pratijñā'; ityatra śāstrakṛtaiva dattamuttaram | yaśca sādhanaṃ prayukte tena ‘ahamanena sādhanenāmuṣmiṃ(ṣmin) sādhye pratītiṃ sādhayiṣyāmi'; iti karma nirūpyaiva tat prayuktamiti na laukikanyāyātikramaḥ, anyathā yadi sādhanād yasya sādhyapratītirupajāyate tenaiva karma nirūpaṇīyam kathaṃ tadabhāve svārthānumāne sādhyasiddhiḥ sādhananibandhanā (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 72.

children.text: ) syāt? | yaścāgnidhūmayoḥ sambandhaṃ cetasi vyavasthāpya ‘kvāgniḥ kvāgniḥ?'; ityagniṃ paryeṣate sa pradeśe dhūmadarśanamātrādevāgniṃ pratipadyata iti kathaṃ svārthānumāne pratyavamarśapratyayaḥ syāt? | atha kadācidasau dṛṣṭastatreti parārthe 'pyasyopādānaṃ tadā dadhyādikamapi bhuktvā kadācid dhūmādagniṃ pratipannavāniti kinna dadhibhojanāderapi kādācitkasyopādānam? |
children.translated_text: — would that be [possible]? And one who, having established in his mind the connection between fire and smoke, searches for fire [thinking] "where is fire, where is fire?" — he understands the existence of fire from the mere perception of smoke in a particular location; so how would there be a reflective judgment (<s>pratyavamarśapratyaya</s>) in inference-for-oneself? And if he was at some time seen there, then even in inference-for-another, his

body.translated_text: As for the statement that "the thesis is for the purpose of indicating the subject matter" — the author of the treatise (<s>śāstrakṛt</s>, i.e., <s>Dharmakīrti</s>) himself has already given the answer to that. And when one formulates a proof, one has already determined the task [mentally] — "I shall establish cognition of this <s>sādhya</s> by this proof" — and so the proof is formulated after the task has been determined; thus there is no transgression of worldly procedure. Otherwise, if the proof

body.text: yat punaruktam ‘āgamaḥ pratijñā'; iti, tatra yadi vādivacanamevāgamastadā tata eva sādhyasiddherhetvādyupadānamanarthakam | atha pratijñārthasyāgame pāṭhādāgamaḥ pratijñā, tadā na kvacidāgame paṭhyate atra pradeśe 'gniriti kathamāgamatvaṃ pratijñāyāḥ? |
body.translated_text: As for the further statement that "scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is the thesis" — if the proponent's own statement is scripture, then since the <s>sādhya</s> would be established from that alone, the presentation of the reason and the like would be purposeless. But if the thesis is scripture because the content of the thesis is found in scripture, then since it is not stated anywhere in scripture that "there is fire in this location," how can the thesis have the status of scripture?

body.text: ‘heturanumānam'; ityapyayuktam, na hi pakṣadharmatvamātraṃ hetuḥ, tasya trirūpatvāt | dṛṣṭānto 'pi na sarvaḥ pratyakṣa iti kathaṃ ‘dṛṣṭāntaḥ pratyakṣam'; bhavet? | upamānaṃ tu pramāṇameva na bhavati, kathaṃ tavdyāpāra upasaṃhriyeta nigamanena? | yadi cāvaśyaṃ dṛṣṭānte dṛṣṭasāmarthyo heturdvarmiṇyupaneyaḥ tadopanaya evāstu kiṃ ‘kṛtakatvāt'; iti pakṣadharmanirddeśena?, sa eva dṛṣṭasāmarthyaṃ hetumupasaṃhariṣyati pakṣadharmatāṃ ca darśayiṣyatīti na kiñcittena | tato yatra ca pratijñāyāḥ prathamata eva prayogo neṣyate tatra tasyāḥ punarvacanaṃ kuto nigamanaṃ bhaviṣyati? ityāha- "iti" tasmād "iyāneva" pakṣadharmasambandhavacanamātrātmakaḥ sādhanavākye "prayogo jyāyān" na pañcāvayavātmaka iti sthitam |
body.translated_text: "The reason is inference" — this too is incorrect, for the mere property of belonging to the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣadharmatva</s>) is not the reason, since the reason has three characteristics (<s>trirūpa</s>). Moreover, not every example is perceptible, so how can "the example is perception" hold? And comparison (<s>upamāna</s>) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all [for the Buddhists] — how can its operation be concluded by the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>)? If

body.text: 8. nyāyavākye hetudṛṣṭāntavacanayoḥ kramasyāniyamaḥ |
body.translated_text: 8. There is no fixed order of the statements of reason and example in the proof-sentence.

body.text: atra sādhanavākye na kevalaṃ pratijñādiprayogo na yuktaḥ paropagataḥ ‘pūrvaṃ hetuḥ prayoktavyaḥ paścād dṛṣṭāntaḥ'; iti kramaniyamo 'pi na kaścit | kutaḥ? sarvathā yadi pūrvaṃ hetuḥ paścād vyāptiḥ atha pūrvaṃ vyāptiḥ paścāt pakṣadharmaḥ prayujyate, tathāpi gamakatvāt |
body.translated_text: Here, in the proof-statement, not only is the formulation of the thesis and the like inappropriate, as accepted by the opponent, but the order-rule that "first the reason should be stated, then the example" is also not [valid]. Why? Because in every case — whether the reason is stated first and then the pervasion, or the pervasion first and then the property-of-the-thesis-subject — in either way

body.text: 9. hetostridhāprayogasya khaṇḍanam |
body.translated_text: 9. Refutation of the threefold formulation of the reason.

body.text: nanu tasya dvidhā prayoga ityayuktamuktam | yatastrividho hetuḥ- anvayī vyatirekī anvayavyatirekī ceti naiyāyikāḥ, tatastasya trighā prayogaḥ sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ ceti vaktavyamityata āha- "sambandhavacane 'pi" na kevalaṃ kramaniyamo na yuktaḥ kintu "artha bhedo 'pi na kaścid" ubhayatrāpi trirūpasadbhāvāta | tataḥ sarva eva heturanvayavyatirekī, na tvanvayī vyatirekī vā kaścidveturastīti bhāvaḥ | tat kutastrividhyaṃ prayogasya syāt? iti manyate | kutaḥ punararthabhedo nāstīti? cet, āha- "ubhayathā" sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca prayoge yadyapi vidhipratiṣedharūpatayā dharmabhedaḥ pratīyate tathāpi "tadbhāvasyaiva" sādhanadharmasya sādhyasvabhāvatāyāḥ eva sādharmyavaidharmyaprayogābhyāṃ "khyāpanāt" |
body.translated_text: Now, [one objects:] it is incorrect to say that the reason has a twofold formulation, since according to the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> the reason is threefold — positive-only (<s>anvayī</s>), negative-only (<s>vyatirekī</s>), and positive-and-negative (<s>anvayavyatirekī</s>) — and therefore it should be said that its formulation is threefold: through agreement (<s>sādharmya</s>), through difference (<s>vaidharmya</s>), and through both agreement and difference. To this he says: "Even in the statement of the relation" — not merely

body.text: nanu sādharmyaprayoge hetubhāve sādhyasya bhāvaḥ, vaidharmye ca sādhyābhāve hetvabhāvaḥ śabdādavagamyate, na tādātmyam | tat kimucyate ‘tadbhāvasyaiva khyāpanāt‘? ityata āha- "na hi" ityādi | yadi sādharmyaprayoge tadbhāvo nākṣipyeta tadā sādhanasya "atatsvabhāvasya bhāve" kimiti "ekāntena" avaśyantayā "sādhyasya bhāvaḥ?" | kādācitkastu bhavatu nāma? | ‘yat kṛtakaṃ tadanityam'; ityekāntabhāvaśca hetau sati sādhyasya vyāptyā sādharmyaprayoge 'bhidhīyate | sa ca tādātmyamantareṇānarthāntarasya na sambhavatīti sāmarthyāt tadākṣipati |
body.translated_text: Now, [one objects:] in the positive formulation (<s>sādharmyaprayoga</s>), the presence of the <s>sādhya</s> when the reason is present, and in the negative formulation (<s>vaidharmya</s>), the absence of the reason when the <s>sādhya</s> is absent — these are understood from the words [alone], not identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). So why is it said "because of the declaration of precisely that nature" (<s>tadbhāvasyaiva khyāpanāt</s>)? To this he says: "For not" and so on. If the positive formulation did not imply that nature [i.e., identity or necessary connection], then the proof

body.text: kathamivātatsvabhāvasya bhāve na ekāntenānyabhāva iti āha- "kṛtakatve"tyādi | yadi pratyatnānantarīyakatvamantareṇāpi kṛtakatvasya bhāvādatatsvabhāvatvam anityatve 'pyayameva vṛttāntaḥ | tataśca tādātmyavirahāt prayatnānantarīyakatvasyānityatvenānvayo na syāt, tannivṛttau vā nivṛttiriti kathaṃ tatastat (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 74.

children.text: ) pratīyate? | naiṣa doṣaḥ, prayatnānantarīyakapadārthasvabhāvasyaivānityatvasya tena sādhanāt, tatra ca tādātmyasadbhāvād anvayavyatirekāvanivāritau anityatvakṛtakatvamatrāpekṣayā tu tādātmyaviraho 'syābhihita iti |
children.translated_text: — is understood? This is not a fault, because it is precisely the impermanence that is the nature of the entity characterized as being immediately subsequent to effort (<s>pratyatnānantarīyaka</s>) that is proved by that [reason]; and since identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) does obtain there, positive and negative concomitance are irresistible. The absence of identity that has been stated [by the objector] is with reference to being-produced (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) [alone, independently of effort-dependence].

body.translated_text: How is it that in the presence of what is not of that nature, there is not necessarily the presence of something else? He says: "In the case of being-produced" (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and so on. If being-produced exists even without the characteristic of being immediately subsequent to effort (<s>pratyatnānantarīyakatva</s>), then it is not of the nature of that [effort-dependence]; and the same situation [obtains] for impermanence too. And thus, due to the absence of identity [between being-produced and impermanence independently of effort-dependence], the positive and negative concomitance of effort-dependence with impermanence

body.text: nanvagninivṛttāvatatsvabhāvasyāpi dhūmasya nivṛttirdṛṣṭānvayaścetyāha- "kāryasya" iti | anvayavyatirekayorhi pratibandho nibandhanam, tena tayoḥ vyāpteḥ, tadabhāve tayorapyabhāvāt | tatrārthāntarasya dhūmasyāgnau "tadutpattilakṣaṇaḥ pratibandho 'nvayavyatirekanimittama" stīti bhavetāṃ tau | yatra tvanarthāntarasya tāvucyete tatrāvaśyaṃ tādātmyena bhavitavyamityabhiprāyaḥ | atrodāharaṇam "yathā- anayoreva kṛtakatvaprayatnānantarīyakatvayorviparyayeṇa naikanivṛttāvanyanivṛttiḥ"- ‘yat pratyatnāntarīyakaṃ na bhavati tat kṛtakamapi na bhavati'; ityevaṃrūpā | yata evaṃ tasmadanvayavyatirekayoryathālakṣaṇaṃ hetubhāve sādhyasyāvaśyaṃ bhāvaḥ, sādhyābhāve ca hetoravaśyamabhāvaḥ ityeko 'pi sādharmyamukheṇa vaidharmyamukheṇa vā prayukto dvitīyamākṣipati, svavyāpakapratibandhākṣepāt, tasyāpi cetareṇa vyāpteḥ | tasmādubhayatra trairūpyapratīterekasya śabde(bda)to 'parasyārthata iti sambandhavacane 'pi prayoga eva vidhimukhena pratiṣedhamukhena vā bhidyate nārtha iti siddhaṃ tatastasya dvidhā prayogaḥ sādharmyeṇa vaidharmyeṇa ca | na tu sādharmyavaidharmyabhyāmapi, tadarthasyānyatareṇaiva prakāśanāt |
body.translated_text: But is it not the case that when fire ceases, smoke too, being of a non-identical nature, ceases, and [their] positive concomitance is observed? To this he says "of the effect." For necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) is the basis of positive and negative concomitance, and through it their pervasion holds; in its absence, both are absent. There, for smoke, which is a different entity from fire, "the necessary connection characterized by origination from that is the ground of positive and negative concomitance" — thus both [concomitances] would hold. But where [positive and negative concomitance] are stated for what is not a different entity, there the intention is that it must be through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>). Here the example is: "For instance, of these very two — 'being produced' (<s>kṛtakatva</s>) and 'being immediately preceded by effort' (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) — conversely, when one ceases, the other does not cease" — [in the form]: 'what is not immediately preceded by effort is also not produced.' Since this is so, in accordance with the definition of positive and negative concomitance, when the reason exists the probandum necessarily exists, and when the probandum is absent the reason is necessarily absent — thus even one [concomitance], whether employed through the similarity method or the dissimilarity method, implies the other, because it implies the necessary connection with its own pervader, and because that too is pervaded by the other. Therefore, since the triple character (<s>trairūpya</s>) is understood in both cases — one explicitly by words, the other by implication — even in the statement of the relation, only the formulation differs between the positive and negative modes, not the meaning. Thus it is established that its formulation is twofold: through similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>) and through dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>). But not through both similarity and dissimilarity together, since the purpose of both is accomplished by either one alone.

body.text: sarvo heturanvayavyatirekyeva vastuto na kaścidanvayī vyatirekī vā nāmetyetadupasaṃharannāha- "iti naikatrā" nvayamukhena vyatirekamukheṇa vā sādhanavākye "dvayo" ranvayavyatirekayoḥ "prayogaḥ" sākṣācchabdena pratipādanamiṣyate, "vaiyarthyāt" pratītapratyāyane prayojanābhāvāt |
body.translated_text: Concluding that every reason is in reality both positively and negatively concomitant, and none is exclusively positively or exclusively negatively concomitant, he says: "Therefore, in one" — in a probative statement, whether through the positive or negative mode — "the formulation" — the explicit verbal expression — "of both" positive and negative concomitance "is not accepted, because of redundancy" — because there is no purpose in expressing what is already understood.

body.text: tāmevārthato 'parasya pratītiṃ sphuṭayannāha- "tatsvabhāvatayā" ityādi | yadi tatsvabhāvatayā sādhyena hetoranvayaḥ sidhyati tata eva "tadabhāve 'bhāvo 'pi sidhyatyeva" | tatsvabhāvasya tadabhāve svayaṃ nairātmyena bhāvāyogāt | "tathā" tatsvabhāvatayā sādhyābhāve sādhanasyābhāva "siddhau" "ca" satyāṃ tata eva sādhyena hetoḥ "anvayasyāpi siddheriti" |
body.translated_text: Clarifying the very understanding by the other [concomitance] by implication, he says: "By virtue of being of that nature" and so forth. If the positive concomitance of the reason with the probandum is established by virtue of being of its nature, then from that very fact "the absence [of the reason] in the absence [of the probandum] is also established." Because what is of the nature of that cannot exist by itself, as selfless, when that is absent. "Likewise," when the absence of the means of proof in the absence of the probandum is "established" "by virtue of being of that nature," then from that very fact "the positive concomitance of the reason with the probandum is also established."

body.text: yaistu vyākhyāyate- "sādharmyavati prayoge tadabhāva eva vipakṣe hetorabhāvakhyātiryathā syāt nānyatra vipakṣe viruddhe vā hetvabhāvaprasaṅgāt viruddhata eva vyavacchedaprasaṅgācceti niyamakhyāpanārtho vyatirekaprayogaḥ" iti | sa tadartho 'pyayuktaḥ | kutaḥ? "anyaviruddhayorapi" na kevalaṃ tadabhāvasya "vipakṣatvāt" yasya hi- anya eva vipakṣo 'nyadharmayogī vānyo, na vivakṣitadharmānāśrayaḥ, viruddha eva vā sahānavasthānalakṣaṇenaiva virodhena, na parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatayāpi vipakṣaḥ- tasyānityatvādanyānātmādidharmavati arthe, kṛtakatvādivṛtteḥ, hetvabhāvaprasaṅgaḥ | auṣṇye ca sādhye 'gnilakṣaṇasya hetorviruddhādeva śītāt nānuṣṇaśītādapyanyato vyavacchedaprasaṅgāt naikāntenauṣṇyamagnirgrasayediti tasyāyaṃ doṣaḥ syāt | taṃ pratyācāryeṇoktam- yadyekasya vipakṣatvamiṣyate tadā tadabhāvasyaiveṣyatām, na viruddhasya anyasya vā, tasyānyatrāpi vivakṣitadharmānāśraye viruddhe ca bhāvāt, tadabhāvamantareṇa tayoranyaviruddhatvāyogāt | na tvasmākaṃ trividhamapi vipakṣamicchatām, vivakṣitadharmānāśrayaṃ cānyamiti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: But those who explain thus — "In a formulation with similarity, the negative concomitance formulation serves to indicate the restriction that the absence of the reason is only in the counter-thesis (<s>vipakṣa</s>), not elsewhere, because otherwise there would be the consequence of the reason's absence in other [similar] or contradictory [cases], and the consequence of exclusion only from the contradictory" — that purpose too is improper. Why? "Because the other and the contradictory too" — not only the absence of that [probandum] — "are counter-theses." For one whose counter-thesis is precisely what is other — possessing a different property, or simply different, not being the locus of the intended property — or precisely what is contradictory — through contradiction characterized only by the impossibility of co-existence, not through being characterized as established through mutual exclusion — for him, in an object possessing properties like non-self etc., which are other than impermanence, there would be the consequence of the reason such as 'being produced' being absent. And when heat is the probandum, there would be the consequence that the reason characterized as fire is excluded not only from the contradictory, cold, but also from what is neither hot nor cold — so fire would not invariably possess heat — this would be the defect. Against this, the master has said: if counter-thesis status is accepted for one alone, then let it be accepted only for the absence of that [probandum], not for the contradictory or the other, since those exist elsewhere too — in what is not the locus of the intended property and in the contradictory — and because without the absence of that [probandum], their being 'other' or 'contradictory' is impossible. But for us who accept all three as counter-theses, [the objection does not arise] — and what is 'other' is simply what is not the locus of the intended property — this is the purport.

body.text: 10. sattvasya kṣaṇikatvasvabhāvatāyāḥ samarthanam |
body.translated_text: 10. Establishing that existence (<s>sattva</s>) has momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) as its essential nature.

body.text: yadi svabhāvahetāvanvayavyatirekayoḥ sādhanadharmasya sādhyasvabhāvatā nibandhanamityanvayena vyatirekeṇa vā sādharmyevaidharmyavatoḥ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 76

children.text: ) prayogayorabhidhīyamānena tādātmyākṣepadvāreṇārthāditarākṣepa ucyate, tadā pramāṇasiddhaiva tatsvabhāvatā tayornibandhanaṃ na śabdamātrataḥ pratīyamānetyabhiprāyavānāha- "kathamidam" ityādi | "yene"ti sato naśvarasvabhāvatvena | satva(ttva)lakṣaṇasya hetoḥ kṣaṇikatvasvabhāvatveneti yāvat | pṛcchataścāyamabhiprāyaḥ- iha dvividhāḥ santaḥ- kṛtakāśca ghaṭādayaḥ akṛtakāścākāśādayaḥ | tatra ye tāvadakṛtakāste "sadakāraṇavat nityam" iti nityalakṣaṇayogādanityā eva na bhavanti kuta eva kṣaṇikāḥ? iti na satva(ttva)sya kṣaṇikatvasvabhāvatā | ye 'pi santaḥ kṛtakāsteṣāmapi mugdarādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyitayā vināśasya sahetukatvāt tadvetvasannidhāvavināśāt kṛtakātmano 'pi satva(ttva)sya kṣaṇikatvasvabhāvatā na samastyeveti nānvayavyatirekayoḥ sambhava iti | avaśyaṃ ca vināśo daṇḍādyanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyī, dṛṣṭatvāt | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: ) through the implication of identity, the other [concomitance] is implicitly stated — then that identity must be established by valid evidence, not merely understood from words alone. With this intention he says: "How is this" and so forth. "By which" — by its having a perishable nature as something existent. That is, by the reason characterized as existence (<s>sattva</s>) being of the nature of momentariness. And the intention of the questioner is this: Here, existing things are of two kinds — produced things like pots etc., and unproduced things like space etc. Among these, unproduced things, by virtue of conforming to the definition of permanence — 'what exists without a cause is permanent' — are simply not impermanent, let alone momentary. So existence does not have momentariness as its essential nature. And even produced things that exist, since their destruction has a cause, following the positive and negative concomitance of a club etc., and since there is no destruction in the absence of that cause, even existence characterized as 'produced' does not have momentariness as its essential nature at all. So there is no possibility of positive and negative concomitance. And destruction necessarily follows the positive and negative concomitance of a club etc., because it is observed. For thus —

body.translated_text: If in the essential nature reason, the essential nature of the proof-property being identical with the probandum is the basis of positive and negative concomitance — so that when stated through formulations with similarity or dissimilarity, (

children.translated_text: "Without the proximity of a cause of destruction such as a blow, fire-contact,

children.text: vinā saṃsargitāṃ yāti na vināśo ghaṭādibhiḥ ||"
children.translated_text: pots and the like do not undergo dissolution."

body.text: anyatrāpi cānvayavyatirekānuvidhānameva hetumattāvyavahāranivandhanamabhyupeyate saugatairapi, tadihāpyastīti kinna tavdyavahāraḥ pravartyatte? iti |
body.translated_text: And elsewhere too, it is accepted even by the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>) that conformity with positive and negative concomitance is the ground for the convention of being caused. Since that is present here too, why is that convention not applied?

body.text: nanu cānvayaniścayaṃ pratipādayatā bādhakapramāṇavṛttivaśāt tatsvabhāvatā pūrvameva pratipāditā ‘anvayaniścayo 'pi svabhāvahetau'; ityādivacanāt | tat kuto 'sya pūrvapakṣasyāvasaraḥ? | satyam, kintu pūrvācāryaiḥ kṛtakatvasya kṣaṇikatāyāṃ sādhyāyāṃ paraiḥ kṛtakānāmante 'vaśyaṃ hetunibandhanavināśopagamāt tadvetvayogapratipādanenānapekṣā vināśaṃ prati viparyaye bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ tādātmyaprasādhakamuktaṃ tat prasaṅgamukhena kṛtakalkṣaṇasyaiva sattvasya tadātmatāṃ gamayati nānyasya iti darśayitum | arthakriyāvirodhalakṣaṇaṃ tu sarvasya sattvasya iti vastumātreṇa (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 77

children.text: ) prāguktamapi vipañcayituṃ pūrvapakṣopanyāsaḥ | akṛtakalakṣaṇaṃ tu sattvaṃ na sambhavatyeva, niyāmakaṃ hetumantareṇa deśakālasvabhāvaniyamāyogāt | tataḥ pūrvācāryairna tasyaikāṅgavaikalyādeva "sadakāraṇavat nityam" iti nityatāsambhava iti na tadātmatāṃ prati yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ | śāstrakārastu sāmānyena sattvasya kṣaṇikasvabhāvatāṃ, kṛtakalakṣaṇasya api ca, deśakālasvabhāvaviprakṛṣṭasyāpi vastusthityaiva tadātmatām arthakriyāvirodhena, na paropagatāvaśyambhāvivināśasyāhetukatayā viśeṣābhāvāt utpannamātrasyābhāvaprasaṅgena pratipādayiṣyati |
children.translated_text: ) the objection is presented in order to elaborate what was said earlier. But existence characterized as 'unproduced' is simply impossible, since without a determining cause, restriction in space, time, and nature is impossible. Therefore, the earlier masters, since it [unproduced existence] fails due to the deficiency of one factor alone — namely, because permanence is impossible for 'what exists without a cause is permanent' — did not make an effort regarding its identity [with momentariness]. But the author of the treatise will demonstrate, generally, the momentary nature of existence, and also of what is characterized as produced, and the identity even of what is remote in space, time, and nature, by the very reality of the thing, through incompatibility with causal efficacy — not through the opponent's accepted [premise of] the causelessness of necessarily occurring destruction, since there is no distinguishing feature [between produced and unproduced on that basis], and through the consequence that what has just arisen would be absent.

body.translated_text: But has not the identity of nature been already established earlier, when demonstrating the ascertainment of positive concomitance, through the operation of refuting evidence? — as stated in 'the ascertainment of positive concomitance too, in the essential nature reason...' etc. So whence is there scope for this objection? True, but the earlier masters, since the opponents accept that for produced things there is necessarily destruction caused by something at the end, demonstrated the identity [of being produced and being impermanent] by establishing independence from that cause with respect to destruction, and stated the refuting evidence that establishes identity through the reductio method. That shows the identity only of existence characterized as 'produced,' not of anything else. But the identity characterized by incompatibility with causal efficacy belongs to all existence — and to show this through the mere reality [of things], (

body.text: 11. sahetukaṃ vināśaṃ nirasituṃ tasya bhāvasvabhāvatāyāḥ samalocanam |
body.translated_text: 11. Examination of the essential nature of destruction as belonging to the entity, in order to refute caused destruction.

body.text: tatra pūrvācāryoktaṃ ‘sarvasya sataḥ kṛtakasyavaśyamante hetukṛto vināśa iti'; yaḥ paririṣyate taṃ pratyanapekṣatvaṃ khyāpayitumupakramate "vināśahetvayogāditi" |
body.translated_text: There, what was stated by the earlier masters — 'for everything that exists and is produced, there is necessarily destruction caused by something at the end' — against the one who maintains this, he begins to proclaim its independence [from causes], saying "because there is no cause of destruction."

body.text: yadi tarhi nāśasya heturnāsti, sa teṣāṃ kṛtakānāṃ satāmavaśyambhāvī vināśaḥ kutaḥ? | na hyākasmikaḥ kaścitsvabhāvo yukta ityāha- "svabhāvata eva" | bhavatyasmāt kāryam iti bhāvaśabdo hetuvacanaḥ | tena svahetubhya eva "naśvarāḥ" naśanaśīlāḥ, sūcyagre sarṣapā ivānavasthāyinaḥ svātmani "bhāvā jāyante" | "naiṣāṃ" kṛtakalakṣaṇānāṃ satāṃ bhāvānāṃ "svahetubhyo niṣpannānāṃ" "anyataḥ" abhighātāde "rvināśotpattiḥ" | kutaḥ? "tasyā" bhighātāgnisaṃyogādestaddhetutayopagatasya "asāmarthyāt" | tathāhi- agnisaṃyogādikāle tritayaṃ lakṣayāmaḥ | tadeva kāṣṭhādikaṃ vināśyam, aṅgārādikamavasthāntaram, kāṣṭhādinivṛttilakṣaṇaṃ cābhāvaṃ tuccharūpaṃ, nāparaṃ yatrāgnisaṃyogādervyāparaḥ cintyeta | etāvatyāṃ ca vastugatau na kvacidatra vināśahetauḥ sāmarthyaṃ yujyate | yato "nahi vināśaheturbhāva" syendhanādeḥ svahetubhyaḥ sthirarūpasyotpannasya "svabhāvamevā" sthirātmatālakṣaṇaṃ "karoti" | kutaḥ? "tasye"ndhanādeḥ "svahetubhya" eva "nirvṛtteḥ" | nahi sthirātmano (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 78

children.text: ) nirvṛttasyānyathābhāvaḥ tadātmā śakyate kartum, tasya hetvantarāt paścād bhavto 'rthāntaratvaprasaṅgāt, tasyaivānyathātvāyogāt, tatra hetuvyāpārasya kalpayitumaśakyatvāt |
children.translated_text: ) its becoming otherwise cannot be made to be of that same nature, because there would be the consequence of its being a different entity, arising subsequently from another cause; because it is impossible for that very thing to become otherwise; and because it is impossible to conceive of the operation of a cause upon it.

body.translated_text: If there is no cause of destruction, then whence is that necessarily occurring destruction of those produced existing things? For no nature without a cause is reasonable. To this he says: "From their very nature." The word <s>bhāva</s> (existence) here denotes cause, in the sense that effects arise from it. Thus, "from their own causes alone," things "are born" as "perishable" — having the disposition to perish, unstable in their own being like mustard seeds on the tip of a needle. "Of these" existing things characterized as produced, "having been produced from their own causes," there is no "arising of destruction from something else" — from a blow etc. Why? "Because of the incapacity of that" — of the blow, fire-contact, etc. accepted as its cause. For thus: at the time of fire-contact etc., we observe three things — the very thing to be destroyed, such as firewood; a different state such as embers; and absence characterized by the cessation of firewood etc., which has an insubstantial form. There is nothing else where the operation of fire-contact etc. could be conceived. And in this extent of the reality of things, the capacity of the cause of destruction is not tenable anywhere. Because "the cause of destruction does not produce the very nature" — characterized by stable selfhood — "of the entity" such as firewood, which has arisen with a stable form from its own causes. Why? "Because of its" — firewood's — "having been produced from its own causes alone." For of what has been produced with a stable nature, (

body.text: athavā tritaye samīkṣyamāṇe yat tāvat vināśyaṃ kāṣṭhādi na tatsvabhāvamevāgnisaṃyogādirvināśahetuḥ karoti tasya svahetubhya eva nirvṛtteriti |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, when examining the three things [at the time of destruction], the fire-contact etc. does not make the very nature of the thing to be destroyed — firewood etc. — into a cause of destruction, because it [the firewood] has been produced from its own causes alone.

body.text: 12. kumārileṣṭabhāvāntarasvabhāvapakṣasya samālocanam
body.translated_text: 12. Examination of <s>Kumārila</s>'s accepted position that [destruction
has the nature of a different state (<s>bhāvāntara</s>).]

body.text: kumārilastu manyate- nāgnisaṃyogādinā bhāvasvabhāva eva kriyate kintvindhanādeḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvaḥ | sa cendhanādirūpavikalamaṅgārādikamuttaraṃ bhāvāntarameva | taduktam-
body.translated_text: But <s>Kumārila</s> thinks: Fire-contact etc. does not produce the very nature of the entity; rather, [it produces] the <s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s> (posterior absence) of firewood etc. And that [posterior absence] is precisely a different subsequent state (<s>bhāvāntara</s>) such as embers, lacking the form of firewood etc. As stated —

body.text: "nāstitā payaso daghni pradhvaṃsābhāvalakṣaṇam ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "The non-existence of milk in curd is of the nature of posterior absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>)."

body.text: tathāvidhasya cābhāvasya hetumattopagamo naiva virudhyate | tathā cāha kaścit-
body.translated_text: And the acceptance that such absence has a cause is not at all contradictory. And thus someone says —

body.text:
"bhāvāntaravinirmukto bhāvo 'trānupalambhavat |
abhāvaḥ sammatastasya hetoḥ kinna samudbhavaḥ? ||" iti |
body.translated_text:
"Absence, free from a different state, is accepted here as like non-apprehension.
Why should it not arise from a cause?"

body.text: tadetat kaumārilaṃ darśanamapanudannāha- "nāpi" ityādi | yadyuttaraṃ kāryātmakaṃ "bhāvāntarameva" abhāvastadāgnisaṃyogādayo 'ṅga(ṅgā)rādijanmani vyāpṛ(pri)yanta itīṣṭamevāsmākam, kintu "bhāvāntarakaraṇe" abhyupagamyamāne 'gnyādīnāmindhanādāvavyāpārāt tadavasthamevendhanādikam | tataśca yathāgnisaṃyogāt prāg indhanāderupalabdhiḥ anyā ca tatsādhyārthakriyā tathāṅgārādyutpattāvapyupalabdhyādeḥ prasaṅgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Refuting this <s>Kumārila</s>'s view, he says: "Nor" and so forth. If the subsequent "different state" having the nature of an effect "is itself" the absence, then fire-contact etc. operate in the production of embers etc. — this is indeed accepted by us. But "when the production of a different state" is accepted, since fire etc. have no operation upon firewood etc., firewood etc. remain in the same state. And therefore, just as firewood etc. are perceived before fire-contact and have other causal efficacies accomplishable by them, so too even after the arising of embers etc., there would be the consequence of perception etc. [of the firewood].

body.text: nanu bhāvāntarasya pradhvansā(dhvaṃsā)bhāvarūpatāyāṃ tadutpattāvindhanādīnāṃ pradhvastatvādasatāṃ kathaṃ tathopalabdhyādiprasaṅgaḥ? | satyam, evaṃ manyate- sarvasyendhanāderanyasya gavāderapi tathābhāvo mā bhūt ityaṅgārādeḥ dhvaṃsavyavasthāyāṃ nibandhanamabhidhānīyam | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hbṭ</s> 79

children.text: ) tasmiṃ(smin) sati tannivṛttiriti cet, aho vacanakauśalam yato nivṛttestucchasvabhāvatānaṅgīkaraṇāt tadeva bhāvāntaramaṅgārādikaṃ nivṛttiṃ brūṣe | tadayamarthaḥ sampannaḥ aṅgārādibhāve 'ṅgārādibhāvādaṅgārādikaṃ dhvaṃsaḥ kāṣṭhāderiti | na cāṅgārādibhāve tadbhāvaḥ svātmani hetubhāvāyogāt | agnyādibhyaśca tadutpādavacanādindhanādyupamarddenāṅgārādibhāvāt asya dhvaṃsaṃrūpateti cet | ko 'yamupamarddo nāma? | yadi nivṛttiḥ sāṅgārādilakṣaṇaiveti na pūrvasmād viśiṣyate | tasmāt svarasato nivartate kāṣṭhādiḥ, agnyādibhyastvaṅgārādijanma ityeva bhadrakam, anyathā kāṣṭhāde"stathopalabdhyādiprasaṅgaḥ" kathaṃ na syāt? |
children.translated_text: ) If one says: 'when that [embers] exists, firewood ceases' — ah, what verbal cleverness! Since you do not accept that cessation has an insubstantial nature, you call that very different state — embers etc. — the cessation. Then this meaning follows: the destruction of firewood consists in the existence of embers, because of the existence of embers. But the existence of embers is not [caused] by the existence of embers, since self-causation is impossible. If one says: because of the statement that they [embers] are produced from fire etc., and because embers come into being through the destruction of firewood etc., therefore [embers have] the nature of destruction — what then is this 'destruction'? If it is cessation, then since that is characterized precisely by [the arising of] embers etc., it does not differ from the former [position]. Therefore, firewood etc. cease by their own nature, while from fire etc. there is the birth of embers etc. — this alone is the right view. Otherwise, how could there not be "the consequence of perception etc. of firewood"?

body.translated_text: But if the different state has the nature of posterior absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>), then since at its arising firewood etc. are destroyed and non-existent, how can there be the consequence of their perception etc.? True. He thinks thus: let it not be the case that everything — firewood as well as other things like cows — undergoes such [destruction]. So the basis for the determination that [specifically] embers etc. constitute the destruction [of firewood] must be stated. (

body.text: api ca- yadi bhāvāntaraṃ pradhvaṃsābhāvo ya ete 'nupajātavikārāḥ pradīpabuddhyādayo dhvaṃsante teṣāṃ katarad bhāvāntaraṃ pradhvanso(dhvaṃso) vyavasthāpyate? | te 'pyavyaktatāmātmabhāvaṃ ca vikārameva dhvaṃsaṃ samalambanta iti cet | na, pradīpāderbhāvarūpāvyaktatābhāve pramāṇābhāvāt | yadi hi śaktirūpatāpattiravyaktatā tadā śakteḥ kāryadarśanonnīyamānarūpatvāt tadabhāve kathaṃ pradīpādayaḥ śaktyātmanāvasthitāḥ kalperan? | athopalabdhiyogyatāvikalātmatāpattiravyaktiḥ; atrāpi tadātmanāvasthitau naiva pramāṇamasti | na cāpramāṇakamādriyante vaco vipaścitaḥ | ātmanaścāsattvāt kathaṃ tadbhāvo buddhyādīnāṃ vikāraḥ pariṇāmaśca? | anyatra vihitapratikriyatvāt neha pratanyata ityalaṃ prasaṅgena |
body.translated_text: Moreover — if destruction-absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>) were a different entity (<s>bhāvāntara</s>), then for these [things] such as a lamp, cognition, and the like, which are destroyed without having undergone any transformation — which different entity is to be determined as their destruction? If [you say:] they too resort to [the state of] non-manifestation (<s>avyaktatā</s>) and the state of [returning to their] own nature, and [that] the transformation itself is the destruction — no, because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for the non-manifestation of a lamp and the like in the form of a positive entity. For if non-manifestation (<s>avyakti</s>) means the transformation into the form of a capacity (<s>śakti</s>), then since capacity has a form that is inferred from the observation of effects, in the absence of [such effects] how could a lamp and the like be postulated as existing in the form of a capacity? Or if non-manifestation means the transformation into the state of being fit for perception but devoid [of manifestation] — even for that, there is absolutely no <s>pramāṇa</s> for its existence in such a form. And the wise do not give credence to assertions lacking <s>pramāṇa</s>. And since there is no [permanent] self, how can cognition and the like have a modification or transformation that is a state of that [self]? Since the counter-argument to this has been provided elsewhere, it is not elaborated here — enough with this digression.

body.text: syānmatam- bhāvāntareṇāṅgārādināvṛtatvāt indhanādestathopalabdhyādayo na bhavantītyata āha- "nāpi" ityādi | svabhāvāntaram "anyasye"ndhanāderā"varaṇamapi"na"yujyeta" "tadavasthe" avicalita rūpe "tasminni"ndhanādau sa"tyāvaraṇasyāpi" na kevalamanupalabdhyāde"rayogāt" |
body.translated_text: One might think: the non-perception and the like of fuel and so forth do not occur because they are covered by a different entity, such as embers and the like. To this he says: "Nor" and so on. The covering of "another [thing]" — namely fuel and the like — by "a different nature" — "would also not be appropriate" — "when that" — the fuel and the like — "remains in the same state" — with its form unchanged; because "not only of non-perception and the like" but "of the covering too there would be impossibility."

body.text: 13. bhāvābhāvapakṣasyāpi samālocanam |
body.translated_text: 13. Examination of the position that [destruction is
both a positive entity and a non-entity.]

body.text: na kevalaṃ bhāvasvabhāvo bhāvāntaraṃ vā vināśahetunā na kriyate bhāvābhāvo 'pi na kriyata ityāha- "nāpi" ityādi | kutaḥ? iti cet, "abhāvasya vidhinā" paryudāsena vivakṣitādbhāvāda"nya"tayā kāryatvo"pagame" kriyamāṇe kimindhanādirūpa evāsau? athārthāntaram? iti "vyatirekāvyatirekāvikalpānatikramāt" | tatra cokta eva doṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Not only is [destruction] not produced as something of the nature of a positive entity or as a different entity by a cause of destruction, but even the non-existence of a positive entity (<s>bhāvābhāva</s>) is not produced — he says: "Nor" and so on. Why? "Because of the impossibility of going beyond the alternatives of difference and non-difference" — when [destruction as] the non-existence of a positive entity is conceived by the method of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) as being other than a positive entity, and its status as an effect is being postulated — is it of the very form of fuel and the like, or is it something entirely different? "From the impossibility of going beyond the alternatives of difference and non-difference." And in either case, the fault already stated [applies].

body.text: nanu prasajyapratiṣedhātmā tuccharūpo 'sāvagnyādijanyo 'bhyupeyate | tadbhāve cendhanadināṃ naiḥsvābhāvyāt kutaḥ pūrvadoṣāvasaraḥ? | sa cāvaśyamagnyādibhāvābhāvānuvidhāyitayā tatkāryastadbhāvavyavahārasyānyatrāpi tannibandhanatvāt | taduktam-
body.translated_text: But [one might object:] it is accepted that [destruction], having the nature of a simple negation (<s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>) and being of insubstantial form, is produced by fire and the like. And in its presence, since fuel and the like have lost their own nature, where is the occasion for the previously stated fault? And it must necessarily follow the presence and absence of fire and the like, since it is their effect — because the convention of its existence is grounded in them even elsewhere. As has been stated:

children.translated_text: "An existent [thing], being within the range of cognition — in the presence of that [destructive cause], it is not perceived.

children.text: naśyan bhāvaḥ kathaṃ tasya na nāśaḥ kāryatāmiyat ||
children.translated_text: A positive entity that is perishing — how can its destruction not attain the status of being an effect [of the destructive cause]?

body.text:
prāgabhūtvā bhavan bhāvo hetubhyo jāyate yathā |
bhūtvāpi na bhavaṃstadvaddhetubhyo na bhavatyayam ||" iti |
body.translated_text: Just as a positive entity, not having existed before, comes into being from its causes, so too this [destruction], having existed [as the entity] and then not existing, comes into being from its causes."

body.text: ata āha- "bhāvapratiṣedhe"tyādi | ayamabhiprāyaḥ- yadyanapekṣitabhāvāntarasaṃsargaścyutimātrameva tuccharūpaṃ dhvaṃsaḥ tadā tatra kārakavyāpāro naiva sambhavati bhavanadharmiṇyeva tatsambhavāt | tasyāpyabhūtvā bhāvopagamāt kāryatā na virudhyata iti cet | na | bhavanadharmaṇo bhāvarūpatāprāpterabhāvatvahāneḥ | yato bhavatīti bhāvo bhaṇyate, nāparamaṅkurāderapi bhāvaśabdapravṛttinimittam | arthakriyāsāmarthyāmiti cet | sarvasāmarthyavirahiṇastarhyasya kathaṃ pratītiviṣayatā? | nahyakāraṇaṃ pratītiviṣayaḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | tadaviṣayasya vā kathaṃ hetumattāvagatiḥ? vastutā vā? | uemācyate ‘tuccharūpameva tad vastu'; iti | pratītijanakatve vā kathaṃ na sāmarthyasambandhitā? | saditipratyayāviṣayasya kathaṃ bhāvateti cet | kāryatāpyasya katham? | svahetubhāve bhāvāt iti cet | kathaṃ tarhi satparatyayāviṣayatā? | (

children.text: ) tathā hi- yadi svahetubhāve bhavatīti pratīyate sadityapi pratīyeta | yato 'stīti sad iti vadanti vidvāṃsaḥ | na cāsti, bhavati, bhāvaḥ, sanniti śabdānāmarthabhedaḥ paramārthataḥ kaścit | abhāvātmakatayaiva bhavatyasāviti cet | na | vyāhatatvāt, yato na bhavatītyabhāva ucyate sa kathaṃ bhavatīti vyapadiśyate? | pratiṣṭhitena kenacid rūpeṇa svajñānātmanyapratibhāsanāt na bhava iti cet | atyantaparokṣāṇāṃ cakṣurādīnāmabhāvatāprasaṅgaḥ | na | teṣāṃ jñānaheturūpatayā pratibhāsanāt iti cet | na | asyāpi bhavitṛrūpatayāvabhāsanāt | sarvarūpavivekasya ca kathaṃ bhūtyā sambandhaḥ? | kenacid rūpeṇonmajjanaṃ hi bhavanam | jñānaviṣayatayāsyāpi ca teddheturūpatayāvabhāsanasya tulyatvāt, ahetośca viṣayatvāyogāt | asmākaṃ tvabhāvabuddhyaḥ svavāsanāparipākānvayā nirviṣayā eva | abhāvasya ca bhavitṛtve kathaṃ praryudāsāt prasajyapratiṣedho bhidyeta | asadrūpasya vidhānena paryudāsāt sa bhidyata iti cet | na | asadrūpsya bhavanavirodhāt | bhavatīti hi bhūtyā sattayābhisambadhyate | tatra kathaṃ sadrūpasya vidhānam? | paryudāsa evaiko nañarthaśca syāt, sarvatra vidheḥ prādhānyāt | so 'pi vā na bhavet | yadi hi kiñcit kutaścit nivartyeta tadā tavdyatireki saṃspṛśyeta tatparyudāsena | tacca nāsti | sarvatra nivṛttirbhavati ityukte vastvantarasyaiva kasyacit vidhānāt | tathānena vastvantaramevoktaṃ syāt, na tayorvivekaḥ | aviveke ca na paryudāsaḥ | aprastutābhidhānaṃ ca syāt | bhāvanivṛttau prastutāyāṃ asadātmano vastvantarasyaiva vidhānāt | na cāsya svarūpeṇāsadātmakatvam, svarūpeṇāpyasataḥ kāryatvavirodhāt | pararūpeṇa tu sarvameva vastvasadātmakamiti nāsya ghaṭādeḥ kaścid viśeṣaḥ | bhavatu vāyamabhāvo 'gnyādibhyastadbhāve kimiti nopalabhyante kāṣṭhādayaḥ? | tathā hi- agnyādīnāmanyakriyāyāṃ caritārthatvādanivṛttā eva tebhyaḥ (

body.text: atraiva vyāptimādarśayati- "yo hi" ityādi | "na punaḥ tadbhāve" tatsvabhāvatve janakāt heto "rhetvantaramapekṣate |" "na hi prakāśādayaḥ" ityādinā dṛṣṭāntavivaraṇam | tadātmatāyā hetvantarānapekṣaṇena vyāptiṃ tādātmyasādhakena pramāṇena darśayati- "tadātmano" yo yasya svabhāvaḥ tatsvabhāvasya "tādātmyābhāve" hetvantaramapekṣamāṇasya svahetorniṣpannasyāpi tatsvabhāvatvābhāve "nairātmyasya" niḥsvabhāvatāyāḥ prasaṅgāt | "tadvat" prakāśādivat "na punaḥ" paścāt "tadātmatāyāṃ" asthitidharmātmatāyāṃ "hetvantaramapekṣata" iti pramāṇaphalam | "asthitidharmā cet" naśvarasvabhāvaścet | "svabhāvataḥ" svahetubhyo "niṣpanno" bhāva iti pakṣadharmopasaṃhāraḥ | viruddhvyāptopalabdhiśceyam, hetvantarāpekṣānapekṣayoḥ parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatayā virodhāt, hetvantarānapekṣayā ca tatsvābhāvatāyā vyāptatvāt |

[This shows that] due to the nature of being of that identity, there is no need for another cause, and [hence]

body.translated_text: And here, anticipating an opportunity for the opponent's objection, he says: "Like a seed and the like" and so on. With "It may be [objected]" he analyzes this very [point]: "Alone, they do not produce" — why? Because the capacity of water, earth, and the like — which is distinct from the seed's own cause — to produce sprouts and the like, [shows that seeds alone are insufficient];

body.text: 16. pratyakṣeṇa bādhāt na pratyabhijñayā sthiraikabhāvasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: 16. Because of sublation by perception, the permanent unitary existence is not established by recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>).

children.text: ) 'nekānto na syāt | na cāpramāṇaṃ pratyabhijñā, "tatrāpūrvārthavijñānam" ityādipramāṇalakṣaṇayogāt, satsamprayogeṇendriyāṇāṃ bhāvataśca pratyakṣameva pratyabhijñānam | na ca pratyakṣād gariṣṭhaṃ pramāṇamasti, yatastadviṣayasya bhedasiddhyā bādhāmanubhavadapramāṇametat syāt ityāśaṅkayāha- ‘ata eva'; janakatvājanakatvādeva viruddhadharmādhyāsāt ‘tayoravasthayoḥ'; janakājanakāvasthayoḥ bījādeḥ "vastubhedaḥ" svabhāvabhedo "niśceyaḥ"adhyavasātavyaḥ | yathā hi śālibījaṃ tadaṅkurajananasvabhāvaṃ tadbhāve śālyaṅkurabhāvadarśanāt pratyakṣato 'vagamyate, yavabījaṃ cātajjananasvabhāvam tadbhāve śālyaṅkurānupalabdhyā tadviviktayavabījagrāhipratyakṣarūpayā pratīyate tathātrāpyavasthādvaye śālibījasya tadaṅkuraviviktāviviktāvasthāgrāhipratyakṣabalādeva svāṅkurajanakājanakasvabhāvatā kinna niścīyate? | iṣyata evāvasthayorbhedo 'vasthāvatastvabheda iti cet | na | tasyāvasthārūpavivekinā rūpāntareṇa pratyakṣe pratibhāsanaprasaṅgāt | na hi yadanātmarūpavivekena svajñāne na pratibhāsane tasya pratyakṣatā yuktā | avasthā tadvatoḥ svabhāvabhedābhāvāt kathaṃ rūpāntareṇa pratibhāsanam? iti cet | nanvavasthābhyo 'navāptarūpabhedasyāvasthānāmivātmanastadbhede satyabhedo na saṅgacchate | tataścāsyāvasthānāmivātmabhedamanubhavataḥ kathamavasthātṛtvam? | avasthābhede 'pyabhinnarūpasya tathā vyavasthānāt kathañcidbhedasyāpi bhāvādadoṣa iti cet | yadi yamātmānaṃ purodhāya ‘ayamavasthātā, avasthāścemāḥ'; iti bhaṇyate tenāvasthātadvatorbhedastadā bheda eveti ‘kathañcit'; ityandhapadametat | tato 'sya pratyakṣatāyāṃ anātmarūpavivekinā rūpāntareṇāvabhāsanaprasaṅgo na nivartate | atha tenātmanābhedaḥ | avasthāvadbhedaprasaṅgo 'vasthātuḥ, tadvadavasthānāmabhedasya vā | tayorapi kathañcid bhedābhedāviti cet | tayostarhyavasthātadvadātmanorbhedavatoḥ kathañcidanimittaṃ rūpāntaramiṣṭaṃ syāt | (
children.translated_text: ) 'there would be no inconclusiveness.' Nor is <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition) not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), since it possesses the definition of <s>pramāṇa</s> stated as "cognition of a previously unknown object" and so forth; and because of the actual contact of the senses with a real [object], recognition is indeed <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). And there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> stronger than perception, so that through the establishment of difference in its object, this [recognition] would be a non-<s>pramāṇa</s> due to being contradicted by experience — anticipating this objection, he says 'ata eva' (for this very reason); precisely because of the superimposition of contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s>) — namely being productive and non-productive — 'of those two states' (<s>tayoravasthayoḥ</s>); of the productive and non-productive states of the seed and the like, "a difference of entities" (<s>vastubheda</s>) — a difference of essential nature — "is to be ascertained" — is to be determined. For just as a rice-seed is understood through perception to have the nature of producing a rice-sprout, from seeing the existence of the rice-sprout when it [the seed] is present, and a barley-seed is understood to have the nature of not producing that [rice-sprout], through non-apprehension of a rice-sprout when it [the barley-seed] is present — [this being understood] by means of perception that grasps the barley-seed as distinct from that [rice-sprout] — so here too, with regard to the two states of the rice-seed, why should not its nature of being productive and non-productive of its own sprout be ascertained precisely through the force of perception that grasps the states as distinct and non-distinct from that sprout? If [one says:] the difference of the states is accepted, but there is non-difference of the possessor of the states — no, because there would be the consequence that it appears in perception with a form other than [what is distinguished by] the distinction of the form of the state. For it is not reasonable that something is perceptible which does not appear in its own cognition through distinction from what is not its own nature. [If one asks:] since there is no difference of essential nature between the states and their possessor, how can there be appearance with a different form? — Well, for one whose distinction of form has not been obtained from the states, its non-difference when there is difference of those [states] is not coherent, just as [it would not be coherent] for the states themselves. And therefore, for one who experiences the difference of its own nature just like the difference of the states, how can it be the possessor of states? If [one says:] even when the states are different, because something of undifferentiated form is so established, since difference too exists in some manner, there is no fault — if the identity presupposed is such that one says 'this is the possessor of states, and these are the states,' then the difference between the states and their possessor is simply difference, and so 'in some manner' (<s>kathañcit</s>) is a blind word. Therefore, the consequence that it appears with a form other than [what is distinguished by] the distinction from what is not its own nature is not averted for its perceptibility. But if [one says:] by that nature there is non-difference — then there would be the consequence that the possessor of states [has] the difference of the possessor of states, or non-difference of the states like that [possessor]. If [one says:] of those two also there is somehow both difference and non-difference — then for those two, namely the possessor of states and the states, which are different, there would have to be accepted yet another form that is somehow without basis.
