children.text: ) tathā ca tasyāpi tābhyāṃ kathañcidbhedaḥ, anyathā tadekasvabhāvādatyantamabhedādavasthātadvatoḥ parasparamatyantaṃ bhedābhedau prasajyeyātām | rūpāntarasya kathañcidbhede tannibandhanamaparaṃ rūpam, tathāsyāpi tadanyad ityaparimitarūpataivaikaikasya vastunaḥ samāsajyeta | na cāparimitarūpapratibhāsi pratyakṣamanubhavāmaḥ | ananubhavantaśca kathaṃ tatkalpanayātmanaivātmānaṃ vipralabhemahi? | tasmādavasthārūpavivekenopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalambhād aparimitarūpatāprasaṅgācca kathañcidbhedābhedavato 'vasthāturasattvameva | tāścāvasthā janakājanakasvabhāvabhedavatyaḥ pratyakṣata evāvagamyanta iti tadekatvādhyavasāyi pratyabhijñānaṃ tabdādhāmanubhavat kathaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt?, yato bījādināmaṅkurādijananasvabhāvānāmapi tadātmatāyāṃ hetvantarāpekṣaṇāt prāktanasya hetoranaikāntikatā bhavet |
children.translated_text: ) And likewise, that [further form] too would have somehow a difference from those two; otherwise, since it would be of one nature with that, from absolute non-difference, absolute difference and non-difference between the states and their possessor would follow with respect to each other. And if there is somehow a difference of that further form, another form would be grounded on that, and likewise yet another different from this — and so an infinity of forms would attach to each and every entity. But we do not experience perception that manifests unlimited forms. And not experiencing [them], how would we deceive ourselves by ourselves through such imagination? Therefore, because that which has the characteristics of apprehension (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>) through distinction from the form of the state is not apprehended, and because of the consequence of unlimited forms, the possessor of states that has somehow both difference and non-difference is simply non-existent. And those states, which possess a difference of nature as productive and non-productive, are understood through perception alone — so how can recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>), which determines their unity, be a <s>pramāṇa</s> when it experiences contradiction [with perception]?, since even for seeds and the like that have the nature of producing sprouts, the dependence on other causes for their identity would render the former cause inconclusive.

body.translated_text: But [one objects:] by the perception that is recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), the unitary nature of seeds and the like is directly observed. Whence then this distinction characterized as "having the nature of producing" and "having the nature of not producing"? Since

body.text: bhavatu vāvasthātā kaścit, tasyāpyetadeva bhedaṃ sādhayati | tathā hi- "tayoḥ" janakājanakāvasthayoriti saptamīdvivacanametat tadā bhavati | tadayamartho- janakāvasthāyāmajanakāvasthāyāṃ ca "vastunaḥ" dharmilakṣaṇasya "bhedaḥ" svabhāvanānātvam "ata eva" janakājanakasvabhāvatvādeva pratyakṣāvasitāt "niśceyaḥ" niścayalakṣaṇastatra vyavahāraḥ kartavyaḥ, viṣayasya viruddhadharmādhyālasakṣaṇasya darśanāditi |
body.translated_text: Or let there be some possessor of states; even for that, this very [argument] establishes the difference. For thus — "of those two" — of the productive and non-productive states — this is a locative dual. Then the meaning is this: in the productive state and in the non-productive state, "of the entity" — of what is characterized as the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) — "difference" — diversity of essential nature — is "to be ascertained" from this very [fact] (<s>ata eva</s>) — precisely from the being productive and non-productive as ascertained through perception — "a determination" — a conventional practice in the form of ascertainment should be made there, because of seeing [in] the object the characteristic of superimposition of contradictory properties.

body.text: na ca śākyate vaktum- avasthā evāṅkurādijananasvabhāvā nāvasthātā iti | tasya sarvasāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇasyāsattvaprasaṅgāt | tato yad ekarūpatayā pratyabhijñānaṃ bhāveṣu tat pūrvottarakālayorjanakājanakasvabhāvabhedavyavasthāpakapratyakṣanibandhanāmanubhavadvādhāṃ kathamiva pramāṇaṃ syāt? | tatpratibhāsinaścābhinnarūpasyālīkatve 'kṣasamudbhavāmapi vṛttimanubhavato 'sya satsamprayogajatvābhāvāt taimirikādidhiyāmiva kutaḥ pratyakṣatā? | na cārthakriyānibandhanaṃ (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 86

children.text: ) rūpamapāsya bījāderaparaḥ paramārthataḥ svabhāvo 'sti, yasyādhigamāt pratyabhijñānaṃ pramāṇaṃ bhavet, arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvāt paramārthasataḥ | tasmāt sadṛśāparabhāvanibandhana evāyaṃ keśakadalīstambādiṣvivākārasāmyatāmātrāpahṛtahṛdayānāṃ bhrānta eva tattvādhyavasāyo mantavyaḥ | tataḥ sato 'pi pratikṣaṇaṃ bhedasyānupalakṣaṇaṃ bālānām | yadā tu vidhurapratyayopanipātād visadṛśāparabhāvaprasavaḥ tadāsya tattvādhyavasāyī pratyabhijñāpratyayo na bhūtimavalambate | na ca tadekākāraparāmarśapratyayajanakatvādaparaṃ sādṛśyam | bhedāviśeṣe 'pi ca svahetubalāyātaprakṛtivaśāt kecidevaikākāraparāmarśapratyayalakṣaṇāmarthajñānādilakṣaṇāṃ vārthakriyāṃ kurvanti nāpara iti vipañcitaṃ pramāṇavārtika eva śāstrakṛteti neha prapañcyate |
children.translated_text: ) — by the cognition of which recognition would be a <s>pramāṇa</s>, since what is ultimately real has the characteristic of causal efficacy. Therefore, this determination of identity — based merely on the production of a subsequent [entity that is merely] similar, just as in the case of hair, plantain-trunks, and the like — for those whose minds are carried away by mere similarity of appearance, should be regarded as simply an erroneous ascertainment of reality. Hence, even though difference exists at every moment, it is not noticed by the ignorant. But when, from the occurrence of dissimilar conditions, the production of a dissimilar subsequent [entity] occurs, then the recognition-cognition that ascertains identity does not take hold. Nor is there a further similarity [beyond what is] productive of a cognition that grasps [things as having] a single form. And although there is no distinction in difference [among momentary entities], some produce the particular causal function (<s>arthakriyā</s>) characterized by a cognition grasping a single form, or characterized by cognition of an object and the like, due to the nature brought about by the force of their own causes — while others do not — this has been elaborated in the <s>Pramāṇavārttika</s> itself by the author of the treatise (<s>śāstrakṛt</s>), and so is not expanded upon here.

body.translated_text: Nor can it be said that the states alone have the nature of producing sprouts and the like, not the possessor of states — because there would be the consequence that it, characterized by the absence of all capacity, is non-existent. Therefore, how can recognition, which [cognizes] entities as having a single form, be a <s>pramāṇa</s> when it experiences contradiction from perception that establishes the distinction of productive and non-productive natures at earlier and later times? And since the undifferentiated form that appears in it [recognition] is false, even though one experiences an occurrence arising from the senses, because of the absence of being born from actual contact [with reality], how can it be perceptual — just like the cognitions of one with an eye-disease (<s>taimirika</s>) and the like? Nor is there, in ultimate reality, any other essential nature of the seed and the like apart from the form grounded in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) (

body.text: 17. anumānenāpi pratyabhijñāyā bādhāt na tataḥ sthirabhāvasiddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: 17. Even through inference, since recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) is contradicted, the existence of a permanent entity is not established from it.

body.text: avaśyaṃ ca bījāderjanakājanakāvasthayorvastubhedo yathokto 'vagantavya iti darśayitumanamānamabhedasya bādhakamāha- "bhāvānāṃ" bījādīnāṃ svakāryajanako yaḥ "svabhāvaḥ" tasya teṣu satsu "anyathātvābhāvāt" kadācidajanakatvāsambhavāt "tatsvabhāvasya" aṅkurādijanakasvabhāvasya "paścādiva" salilādikāraṇasannidhāna iva "prāgapi" kuśūlādyavasthitikāle 'pi svakārya "jananaprasaṅgāt" | tathā hi- salilādisannidhāne 'pi bījādiḥ svarūpeṇaiva kāryaṃ karoti, na pararūpeṇa | yaścāsya tadākāryajanakaḥ svabhāvaḥ, sa cet prāgapyasti, ‘sa evāyam'; iti pratyabhijñāyāṃ puro 'vasthāyino janakasvabhāvasya prācyarūpābhedādhyavasāyāt, tataḥ kimiti prāgapi tatkāryaṃ na kuryāditi? | prayogaḥ- yad yadā yajjananasvabhāvaṃ tat tadā tajjanayatyeva | ajanakasya janakatvasvabhāvavirodhāt | anyasyāpi vā tatsvabhāvatāpatteḥ | yathā- tadeva bījādikaṃ salilādisannidhikāle | kuśūlādyavasthāsvapi cedaṃ bījādikaṃ svakāryajananasvabhāvameva (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 87

children.text: ) pratyabhijñayā vyavasthāpyata iti svabhāvahetuprasaṅgaḥ | na ca janayati | tasmānna tajjananasvabhāvamiti | viparyayaprayogaḥ- yad yadā yajjananasvabhāvaṃ nirvartyaṃ kāryaṃ na janayati na tat tadā tajjananasvabhāvam, tadyathā- śālyaṅkurajananasvabhāvanirvartyaṃ kāryamajanayat kodravabījam | na janayati ca salilādikāraṇasannidheḥ prāk tatkāryajananasvabhāvanirvartyaṃ svakāryaṃ bījādikamiti vyāpakānupalabdhiḥ | tato 'numānato 'pi bādhāmanubhavat pratyabhijñānaṃ kathaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt? |
children.translated_text: ) — then there is the consequence of a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (essential nature reason) [proving that it should produce the effect then too]. But it does not produce [it]. Therefore it does not have the nature of producing that [effect then]. The counter-argument: whatever, whenever, does not produce the effect to be accomplished that has the nature of producing something — that, at that time, does not have the nature of producing that; just as a <s>kodrava</s>-seed [does not produce] the effect to be accomplished that has the nature of producing a rice-sprout. And the seed and the like does not produce, before the proximity of water and other conditions, its own effect to be accomplished that has the nature of producing that effect — this is a case of non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). Therefore, how can recognition be a <s>pramāṇa</s> when it experiences contradiction even from inference?

body.translated_text: And it must necessarily be understood that there is a difference of entities between the productive and non-productive states of the seed and the like, as stated. To show this, he states an inference that contradicts non-difference: "Of entities" — of seeds and the like — the "essential nature" (<s>svabhāva</s>) that produces their own effect — since there is "no alteration" of that when they [the seeds] exist — since it is impossible for [the seed] to be sometimes non-productive — "of that which has that nature" — of that which has the nature of producing sprouts and the like — "just as afterwards" — just as in the proximity of water and other conditions — "even before" — even at the time of being stored in a granary and the like — there would be "the consequence of producing" its own effect. For even in the proximity of water and the like, the seed produces its effect by its own nature alone, not by another nature. And if that essential nature of it which is productive of that [particular] effect at that [later] time also exists before — because recognition determines the non-difference of the productive nature of the [presently] existing [seed] from its former form, [thinking] 'this is the very same one' — then why would it not produce that effect even before? The formal argument: whatever, whenever, has the nature of producing something, that, at that time, necessarily produces that; because non-productivity is contradictory to the nature of productivity; or because anything else too would have to be of that nature. For example: that very seed at the time of the proximity of water and the like. And if, even in the states of being in a granary and the like, this very seed is established by recognition as having the nature of producing its own effect (

body.text: nanu cānena bādhyamānasyānumānasyāprāmāṇyāt kathaṃ bādhakatvam? | aniścitapramāṇabhāvena kuto bādhā? | nāpi itaretarāśrayatvam | nahi pratyabhijñānasyāprāmāṇyādetadanumānaṃ pramāṇam, kintu svasādhyapratibandhāt | sa ca viparyaye bādhakapramāṇabalānniścita iti |
body.translated_text: Now [one objects:] since this inference, which is being contradicted, is itself not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, how can it be a contradicting [authority]? How can there be contradiction from something whose status as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is not established? Nor is there mutual dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>). For it is not the case that this inference is a <s>pramāṇa</s> because of the non-validity of recognition; rather, [it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>] because of the invariable connection with what is to be proved (<s>svasādhyapratibandha</s>). And that [invariable connection] is established through the force of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> in the case of the opposite [hypothesis].

body.text: 18. pratyakṣasyānumānāt garīyastvanirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: 18. Refutation of the claim that perception is stronger than inference.

body.text: na pratyakṣādanyad gariṣṭhaṃ pramāṇamiti cet | na | pratyabhijñāyāḥ pratyakṣatvāsiddheḥ | na hīyamanumānena pratyakṣātmikā satī bādhyata iti brūmahe | kiṃ kṛtaṃ ca pratyakṣasya garīyastvam? | tadvayarthasyāsambhave 'bhāvāt pramāṇamucyate taccānumānasyāpyarthapratibaddhaliṅgajanyatayā samānamiti nāsya kaścidviśeṣaḥ | yadi cānumānavirodhamaśnuvānāpi pratyabhijñā pramāṇaṃ tadākārasya sāmyāt tadekatāṃ pratiyatī nīletarakusumādeḥ [pratītiḥ] kiṃ na pramāṇam? | nahi kusumaphalādikāryadarśanonnīyamāno bhedaḥ pratyakṣatastathābhāvamanubhavati | vistarataśca pratyabhijñāprāmāṇyanirāsaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhāveva vihita ityāstāṃ tāvadiha |
body.translated_text: [One objects:] there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> stronger than perception — [we reply:] no, because it is not established that recognition is perceptual. For we do not say that this [recognition], being perceptual in nature, is contradicted by inference. And what makes perception stronger? In the absence of the impossibility of its object, it is called a <s>pramāṇa</s>, and that is equally [true] of inference too, since it arises from a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) that is invariably connected with the object — so there is no special distinction of this [perception over inference]. And if recognition is a <s>pramāṇa</s> even while being contradicted by inference, then, due to similarity of form, the [erroneous] cognition that apprehends as identical such things as a blue <s>Itaraka</s> flower [and something else] — why would [that cognition] not be a <s>pramāṇa</s>? For the difference that is inferred from seeing effects such as flowers and fruits does not so appear in direct perception. And the refutation of the validity of recognition has been extensively treated in the proof of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s>) itself — so let this suffice here.

body.text: "yataḥ evam" uktena prakāreṇa janakājanakāvasthayoḥ bījādervastubhedaḥ "tasmād yo 'ntyo 'vasthāviśeṣo" yadanantaraṃ aṅkurādikāryaprasavaḥ (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 88
) — "that alone has the nature of producing the sprout," because the nature of producing that [sprout] is of a form inferred from seeing the effect.

body.translated_text: "Since it is thus" — in the manner stated, there is a difference of entities between the productive and non-productive states of the seed and the like — "therefore, that final particular state" — immediately after which the production of effects such as sprouts [occurs] (

body.text: yadi tarhi sa evāṅkurajananasvabhāvaḥ, pūrvabhāvināmavasthābhedānāmatajjananasvabhāvatvāt kathaṃ teṣu tatkāraṇavyapadeśaḥ? aṅkurārthibhirvā tadupādānam? ityata āha- ‘pūrvabhāvinastu'; kuśūlādyavasthitikālabhāvinastu "avasthāviśeṣā aṅkukāraṇasyā"ntyasyāvasthāviśeṣasya "kāraṇāni" pratyayāntaropadhīyamānaviśeṣebhyaḥ paramparayā "tebhyastadutpatteḥ" | atasteṣūpacārataḥ kāraṇavyapadeśo 'ṅkurārthibhiścopādānam | yatastatsvabhāvasya bījāderjananaṃ na hetvantarāpekṣam, yajjānakamapekṣate na tasya tajjanasvabhāvatvam iti | "tasmānnānekānto" bījādivat ‘tatsvabhāvatvāt'; ityasya hetoḥ ityupasaṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: If, then, that alone has the nature of producing the sprout, since the preceding state-differences do not have the nature of producing that [sprout], how can there be the designation of 'cause' for them? Or the procurement of them by those desiring sprouts? To this he says: 'But the preceding ones' — but the particular states existing at the time of being stored in a granary and the like, "the particular states" that are "the causes of the cause of the sprout" — [they are] the causes of the final particular state — "because of the production of that from them" — in a series, through the distinctions supplied by other conditions (<s>pratyayāntara</s>). Therefore, the designation of 'cause' for them is figurative (<s>upacāra</s>), and the procurement [of them] by those desiring sprouts [is also figurative]. Since the production by the seed having that nature is not dependent on other causes — what depends on [other causes] for production does not have the nature of producing that [independently]. "Therefore there is no inconclusiveness" — this is the conclusion regarding the reason 'because of being of that nature' (<s>tatsvabhāvatvāt</s>) for seeds and the like.

body.text: tadevaṃ yadā tāvat pratyabhijñānaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇatayā sthairyasiddhaye parairūcyate bījādivadanekāntaṃ pratipādayitum, tadā tasyoktena prakāreṇa pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ bādhyamānatvāt tadātmatā nāstīti kutastata ekatā bhāvānām?, yato 'nekāntaḥ syāditi pratipāditam | yadā tu pratyabhijñāyamānatvāt pūrvāparakālayorekasvabhāvā bījādaya iti hetutayocyate paraiḥ, tadāyamasiddho hetuḥ | na ca sa pakṣe kvacid vartata ityāha- "kṣaṇikeṣu bhāveṣu" asmābhiriṣyamāṇeṣu "aikyābhāvā"diti sambandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, when opponents claim that recognition, as a perceptual <s>pramāṇa</s>, [serves] to establish permanence, in order to demonstrate inconclusiveness as in the case of seeds and the like, since [recognition] is contradicted by both perception and inference in the manner stated, its identity [with the earlier entity] does not exist — so whence would there be unity of entities from which inconclusiveness would follow? — this has been demonstrated. But when the opponents state as a reason that seeds and the like have one nature at earlier and later times because of being recognized, then this is an unestablished reason (<s>asiddha hetu</s>). And that [reason] does not obtain anywhere in the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) — he says: "because of the absence of unity in momentary entities" — in entities accepted by us as momentary — this is the connection.

body.text: 19. tatsvabhāvatvāt ityatra punarapi anekāntadoṣodvāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 19. Regarding 'because of being of that nature' (<s>tatsvabhāvatvāt</s>), once again the avenue of the fault of inconclusiveness.

body.text: atha yasyāpi kṣaṇikā bhāvāstasyāpi bījādīnāṃ pratikṣaṇamaikyābhāve 'pi viśeṣānupalakṣaṇādantyakṣaṇavat sarveṣāṃ janakasvabhāvānāmapi tadbhāvaṃ prati salilādyapekṣatvāt tadavasthamanaikāntikatvam ityāśaṅkayāha- "aparāparotpatteḥ" kṣaṇikairapi nānekāntaḥ, aparebhyo 'parebhyaśca pratyayebhyaḥ pratikṣaṇamutpatteḥ kṣaṇikānāṃ bhinnaśaktitvādantyakṣaṇavajjanakasvabhāvatāvirahāt kutastairapyanekāntaḥ syāt? | na hi kāraṇabhedopadhīyamānajanmanāṃ viśeṣānupalakṣaṇe 'pyabhinnasvabhāvatā yuktā, hetu (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 89

children.text: ) bhedānanuvidhāne 'hetukatāprasaṅgāt | tathā ca vakṣyati- ‘aparāparapratyayayogena pratikṣaṇaṃ bhinnaśaktayaḥ santanvantaḥ saṃskārā yadyapi kutaścit sāmyāt samānarūpāḥ pratīyante tathāpi bhinna eva eṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ, tena kiñcideva kasyacit kāraṇam'; iti |
children.translated_text: ) if [the effect] did not follow the differentiation of causes, there would be the consequence of non-causality. And thus he will say: 'The <s>saṃskāras</s> (dispositional formations), which have different capacities at every moment due to being associated with successively different conditions, even though they are apprehended as having the same form due to some similarity — nevertheless their essential nature is indeed different; therefore, only something particular is the cause of something particular.'

body.translated_text: Now [one objects:] even for one who [accepts that] entities are momentary, even though there is an absence of unity of seeds and the like at every moment, since the distinction is not noticed, all [moments] — like the final moment — have the nature of being productive; and since even their becoming that [i.e., producing the effect] depends on water and the like, the inconclusiveness remains the same. Anticipating this objection, he says: "Because of production from successively different [conditions]" — even by those who accept momentariness, there is no inconclusiveness, because of the production at every moment from successively different conditions; since momentary [entities] have different capacities, and like the final moment, [they all] lack the nature of being productive [on their own] — so how could there be inconclusiveness even for them? For it is not reasonable that things whose births are supplied by different causes have an undifferentiated nature, even when the distinction is not noticed, because (

body.text: yaduktaṃ ‘tatsvabhāvasya jananāt'; ityasyānekāntamudbhāvayannāha paraḥ- "te" bījakṣityādayaḥ "antyāḥ" ante bhavāḥ pratyekamaṅkurajanane ‘samarthāḥ'; khaṇḍaśaḥ kāraṇebhyaḥ kāryotpādābhāvād bhavadbhiriṣyanta iti "kinna janayanti pratyekam"? | tataścaiṣāmeka eva kaścidaṅkuraṃ janayati, tadanye tu tatsvabhāvā api na janayantīti ‘tatsvabhāvasya jananāt'; ityanekāntaḥ | tadvat kuśūlādyavasthā api bījādayo 'ṅkurādijananasvabhāvā api na jānayiṣyantīti tairanekāntaḥ tadavastha eveti manyate paraḥ |
body.translated_text: Regarding the statement 'because that which has that nature generates [the effect]' — raising a doubt of non-exclusiveness (<s>anekānta</s>) against this, the opponent says: "They" — seed, earth, etc. — "the final ones" — those existing at the end — are "capable" of generating the sprout individually; since you accept that the effect does not arise from causes piecemeal, "why do they not generate [it] individually?" And so one single [factor] among them generates the sprout, while the others, though having that very nature, do not generate — thus 'because that which has that nature generates' is subject to <s>anekānta</s> (non-exclusiveness). Likewise, even in the state of being in a granary etc., the seeds etc., though having the nature of generating sprouts etc., will not generate — so through them [too] there is <s>anekānta</s>, and the situation remains the same — so the opponent thinks.

body.text: atrāha- "iti" yadevaṃ tvaṃ manyase | pareṇa sāmānyenābhidhānāt sāmānyenaivottaramāha- "janayantyeva" "nātra" svakāryajanane "anyathābhāvaḥ" ajanakatvamāśaṅkanīyam | kutaḥ? "svabhāvasyāvaiparītyāt" | yai hi na janayeyurjananasvabhāvā eva na syuḥ | tatsvabhāvāśceṣyanta ityavaśyaṃ janayanti, tathā ca kuto 'naikāntaḥ? iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: To this he replies: "Thus" — since you think in this way. Since the opponent has stated [the objection] in general terms, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] gives a reply in equally general terms: "They do generate indeed"; "there is no" "being otherwise" — i.e., the state of being a non-generator — "to be suspected" regarding the generation of their own effect. Why? "Because there is no reversal of [their] nature." For if they did not generate, they would simply not have the nature of generators. And since they are accepted as having that nature, they necessarily generate — so whence the <s>anekānta</s>? This is the purport.

body.text: 20. ekekaiva samarthena kāryajanane pareṣāmanupayogamāśaṅkaya taduddhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 20. Anticipating the objection that the others are useless when each individual [factor
alone is capable of generating the effect, and its resolution.]

body.text: pratyekamantyānāṃ janakatve kāryasyaikena jananādapareṣāmupayogasya nirviṣayatvādajananameveti manyamāna āha paraḥ- "teṣu" antyeṣu "sahakāriṣu" saha- yugapat karaṇaśīleṣu "samarthasvabhāveṣu" tatkāryakriyāyogyeṣu abhyupagamyamāneṣu satsu "kāryasyaikenaiva janitatvāt ko 'parasyopayogaḥ?" naiva kaścit | tat kimucyate ‘janayantyeva'; iti? | etat pariharati- ‘na vai'; naiva "bhāvānāṃ" bījādīnāṃ kācit "prekṣāpūrvakāritā" buddhipūrvakāritā, "yataḥ" prekṣāpūrvakāritvāt ‘ayamasmāsvanyatama eko 'pi samarthaḥ kāryajanane, kimatrāsmābhiḥ kartavyam?'; ityālocya "apare nivarteran" audāsīnyaṃ (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 90

children.text: ) bhajamānāstatkāryajanane na vyāpriyeran | yasmāt "te" bījādayo bhāvāḥ "nirabhiprāyavyāpārāḥ" paryālocanāśūnyavyāpārā ekata utpadyamāne "kārye sarva eva vyāpriyante" | bhavanadharmaṇi ca kārye teṣāṃ prāgbhāva eva vyāpāraḥ | tadanyasyāyogāt | yadi hi vyāpṛtādanya eva vyāpāraḥ tadā tata eva kāryotpādād vyāpāravataḥ kārakatvameva hīyate |
children.translated_text: ) and not engage in the generation of that effect. Since "those" entities such as seeds etc. "have purposeless activity" — activity devoid of deliberation — when the "effect" is being produced from [them] collectively, "all of them indeed engage." And for an effect whose nature is to come into being, their activity is simply their prior existence (<s>prāgbhāva</s>). Because no other [activity] is tenable. For if the activity were something other than the [cause] that is active, then since the effect arises from that very [activity], the causal status of the one possessing the activity would itself be lost.

body.translated_text: Thinking that if each final [factor] individually has generative capacity, then since one alone generates the effect, the usefulness of the others has no scope and so they simply do not generate, the opponent says: "When these" final "cooperative factors" — those whose nature is to act simultaneously — "are accepted as having capable natures" — as fit for producing that effect — "since the effect is generated by just one alone, what is the use of the others?" None whatsoever. So why is it said 'they do generate indeed'? [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] resolves this: 'Not so'; indeed "entities" such as seeds etc. have no "deliberate agency" — no intellectually guided agency — "such that," on account of deliberate agency, [they would think] 'this one among us, even a single one, is capable of generating the effect — what need is there for us here?' — and having reflected thus, "the others would withdraw," adopting indifference (

body.text: tasyāsau vyāpāraḥ tatastasya kārakatvam iti cet | nanvevaṃ vyāpāropayogasya kāryānupayogini tatropacārāt pāramārthikamasya kārakatvaṃ hīyeta | kaścāsya vyāpāreṇa sambandhaḥ? | samavāyaścet | na | tasya prāgeva nirastatvāt | samavāyācca vyāpāravattve anyasyāpi tatkāryānupayoginastadbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ, samavāyasyeheti buddhihetorekatvena sarvatra samānatvāt | abhimatenaiva vyāpṛtena tabdyāpārotpādanāt nātiprasaṅgaḥ iti cet | nanu tena tadutpādanaṃ tatra samavāyodevocyate | sa ca sarvatra samānaḥ | yena ca pariśrameṇa vyāpāraṃ janayati tena kāryameva kinnotpādayati? yena vyavadhānamāśrīyate | yathā ca svasannidhimātrenaivāyaṃ vyāpāraṃ janayati na vyāpārāntareṇa, anavasthāprasaṅgāt, tathā tata eva kāryamapītyuktaprāyam |
body.translated_text: If [one says]: that is its activity, and from that comes its causal status — but then, since the usefulness of the activity does not contribute to the effect, and it is merely figuratively attributed there, its real causal status would be lost. And what is its connection with the activity? If [you say] <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — no, because that has already been refuted. And if something possesses activity through <s>samavāya</s>, then even something else that does not contribute to that effect would absurdly have that [activity] too, since <s>samavāya</s>, being unitary as the cause of the cognition 'this is here,' is the same everywhere. If [one says] there is no overextension because it is the very [cause] intended that, being active, produces that activity — but then, that production by it of that [activity] is precisely what is called <s>samavāya</s> with respect to it, and that is the same everywhere. And with whatever effort it generates the activity, why does it not generate the effect itself with that same [effort]? — since an intermediary is being resorted to. And just as this [cause] generates the activity by its mere proximity alone and not through another activity — because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress — so too the effect [arises] from that very [cause]. This has been essentially stated already.

body.text: tasmād bhāvini kārye prāgbhāva eva kāraṇasya vyāpāraḥ | sa ca sarveṣāmastīti sarva eva kāryotpattau vyāpriyanta iti vyapadiśyante |
body.translated_text: Therefore, for an effect that is about to come into being, the activity of the cause is simply [its] prior existence (<s>prāgbhāva</s>). And since all [causes] have that, all are said to be engaged in the production of the effect.

body.text: "tadapi kāryaṃ sarvebhya eva jāyate" sarveṣāṃ bhāva eva tadbhāvāt | na hi kāryasya kāraṇābhimatabhāva eva bhāvamantareṇāparaṃ janma | tathābhāve hi tatraiva kāraṇavyāpārāt kāryakriyaivaiṣāṃ na sambhavet | tataśca satsvapi kāraṇeṣu kathamasya bhāva upalabdhirvā syāt? | tatsambandhino janmanaḥ karaṇāt iti cet | na | asatā (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 91

children.text: ) tena sambandhāyogāt | svata eva sattve vā janmārthānupapatteḥ | janmakāle copalabhyasyātmanaḥ prāgapi bhāvāt tathopalabdhiprasaṅgaḥ, rūpāntareṇa bhāve natasya bhāvaḥ syāt | rūpabhedalakṣaṇatvād bhāvabhedasya | tasmādupalabhyātmano janmanaḥ prāganupalambhādasattvam | tato 'sya janmasambandhitā kutaḥ? | tasmāt kāryamevābhūtvā hetubhāve bhavatīti bhāva evāsya tato janmeti sarvebhyastat jāyate |
children.translated_text: ) is not tenable. Or if it has existence of its own accord, then birth would serve no purpose. And if the self that is apprehended at the time of birth also existed before, there would be the absurd consequence of apprehension [at that earlier time] too; and if it existed in a different form, then it would not be that [same] entity's existence, since difference of existence is defined by difference of form. Therefore, from the non-apprehension of the apprehended self prior to birth, [its] non-existence [is established]. So whence its connection with birth? Therefore, the effect, having not existed, comes into existence when the cause exists — thus its birth is simply its coming-into-existence from those [causes] — and so it arises from all of them.

body.translated_text: "That effect too arises from all [of them] together" — because its existence occurs only when all of them exist. For the effect has no other birth apart from the existence of what are accepted as its causes. For if it existed [independently], then since the causal activity would be directed there alone [at an already-existing thing], the causal operation of these [causes] would not be possible. And in that case, even though the causes exist, how could its existence or apprehension occur? If [one says]: because of the production of a birth connected with that — no, because connection with that which is non-existent (

body.text: nanvekasyāpi tajjanane sāmarthyāt apareṣāṃ tatra sannidhilakṣaṇo vyāpāro vyartha eveti na tatrapareṣāṃ bhāvaḥ saṅgacchata iti cedāha- "svahetoḥ" kṣitibījasalilādisāmagrīlakṣaṇasya "pariṇāmaḥ" kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣavataḥ pratikṣaṇamupadhīyamānātiśayasya kṣaṇāntarasya prasavaḥ, tataḥ "upanidhiḥ" kāryadeśe sannidhānaṃ "dharmo" yeṣāṃ te "tathābhavantaḥ" kāryadeśe sannidhīyamānāḥ "nopālambhamarhanti"- ‘ekasyāpyetatkāryakaraṇe samarthatvāt kimatra bhavantaḥ sannihitāḥ?'; iti na paryanuyogamarhanti | na hi tadaparasannidhimantareṇa tatraikasyāpi bhāva upapadyate | kutaḥ? "tatprakṛteḥ" tatprakṛtitvāt iti bhāvapradhāno nirddeśaḥ | kṣitibījasalilādisāmagrīpariṇāmajanyasvabhāvatvādekaikasya samarthasya tadabhāve kutaḥ kevalasya sambhavaḥ?, sāmagrīśabdavācyaiḥ kāraṇabhedaiḥ samarthasvasvalakṣaṇāntarārambhāt | tataśca pratikṣaṇamupadhīyamānātiśayasyotpādāt kevalānāṃ ca tajjananasvabhāvavaikalyāt tadaparapratyayayogajanyasvabhāvatvāt samarthajanakasya hetoḥ | etacca yathāvasaraṃ tatra tatra vyaktīkariṣyati | tasmād yatsāmagrījanyasvabhāvo yo bhāvaḥ sa tatraikābhāve 'pi kāraṇavaikalyānna sambhavatītyekasāmagrījanmanāṃ sahabhāvo niyataḥ | sarveṣāṃ teṣāṃ bhāva eva kāryasya bhāvāt sarva eva janayantīti ‘tatsvabhāvasya jananāt'; ityatra nānekāntaḥ iti |
body.translated_text: If [the objection is]: since even a single [factor] has the capacity to generate that [effect], the activity of the others, characterized by mere proximity, is pointless with respect to it, and so the existence of the others there is not coherent — to this he says: "The maturation" of "its own cause" — namely the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) characterized by earth, seed, water, etc. — that is, the production of a subsequent moment possessing a specific character conducive to the generation of the effect, with an excellence being progressively accumulated at each moment; and from that, "proximity" — being present at the location of the effect — is the "property" of these; "being in that state" — being present at the location of the effect — "they do not deserve reproach" — [one cannot say] 'since even one of you is capable of producing this effect, what are you doing present here?' — they do not deserve such censure. For without the proximity of those others, even a single one's existence there is not tenable. Why? "Because of its having that as its nature" (<s>tatprakṛti</s>) — the statement is made with the abstract noun [but means] 'because of having that nature.' Since each capable [factor], being of a nature born from the maturation of the aggregate of earth, seed, water, etc., how could it exist alone in the absence of that [aggregate]? — because the distinct individual [factors] designated by the word <s>sāmagrī</s> (aggregate) each initiate their own distinct particular [nature]. And therefore, since the excellence is progressively accumulated at each moment and arises [only so], and since individual [factors] alone lack the nature of generating that [effect] — because the capable generator-cause has a nature born from the conjunction with those other conditions — this will be made clear in the appropriate places. Therefore, whatever entity has a nature born from the aggregate, that entity, even in the absence of one [factor], does not occur due to deficiency of causes — thus the co-existence of things born from a single aggregate is invariable. Since the effect exists only when all of those exist, all of them generate [it] — so in 'because that which has that nature generates,' there is no <s>anekānta</s>.

body.text: yenābhiprāyeṇa ‘te 'ntyāḥ samarthāḥ kinna janayanti'; ityuktaṃ taṃ prakaṭayannāha- "samarthāḥ" ityādi | siddhāntavādyapi ‘janayantyeva'; iti yadabhiprāyavatoktaṃ tamādarśayati- "na, tatraiva" ityādi | etadeva vyācaṣṭe- "tasyaiva" ityādi | ayamabhiprāyaḥ- ‘idamatra samartham, idamasamartham'; iti pratyakṣānupalambhasādhanābhyāmanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vyavahriyate, anyanimittābhāvāt | tau cānvayavyatirekāvekatraiva kārye dṛśyete nāparāparatreti tasyaivaikasya janane samarthā gamyanta iti nāparaparajananam | te tu yadavasthā janayanto dṛśyante- kiṃ tajjananasvabhāvāstadaiva? āhosvit prāgapi? ityatra vivādaḥ | tatra prāgapi tatsvabhāvatve paścādiva prāgapi janaprasaṅga iti pratikṣaṇaṃ bheda ucyata iti |
body.translated_text: Revealing the intention behind the statement 'they, the final ones, being capable, why do they not generate [individually]?' he says: "capable" etc. Showing also the intention of the proponent who said 'they do generate indeed,' he says: "No, in that very [case]" etc. He explains just this: "of that very" etc. The purport is this: 'This is capable, this is incapable' — such [judgments] are made through positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) by means of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) as proofs, because there is no other basis. And those positive and negative concomitances are seen with respect to one and the same effect, not with respect to different effects successively — so they are understood as capable of generating that one single [effect], not of generating different things successively. But a dispute arises: in the state in which they are seen to generate — do they have the nature of generating that only at that time? Or also before? Regarding this, if they have that nature even before, there would be the absurd consequence of generation earlier just as later — hence difference at each moment is asserted.

body.text: 21. kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedaṃ svīkurvadbhiḥ kṣapaṇakajaiminīyairanekāntasyodbhāvanam |
body.translated_text: 21. The raising of <s>anekānta</s> (non-exclusiveness) by the <s>Kṣapaṇakas</s> and <s>Jaiminīyas</s>, who accept difference of effect from difference of cause.

body.text: punaranyathā kṣapaṇakajaiminīyā anekāntamudbhāvayanta āhuḥ- "bhinnaḥ" parasparavyāvṛttaḥ "svabhāvo" yeṣāṃ tebhyaścakṣurādibhyaḥ "sahakāribhyaḥ" yugapatkartṛbhyaḥ "ekasya" vijñānalakṣaṇasya "kāryasyotpattau" satyām, bahūni bhinnasvabhāvāni kāraṇāni kāryaṃ tvekamabhinnasvabhāvamiti "na kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedaḥ syāt" | tataścakṣurādayo na bhinnenātmanaikasya kāryasya janakā eṣṭavyāḥ | kintvabhinnameṣāmekakāryajanakaṃ sāmānyabhūtaṃ rūpamupeyaṃ yenābhinnaṃ kāryaṃ janayanti | tacca samagrāvasthāyāmeva tatkāryaṃ janayati na vyagrāvasthāyām | na caikaikābhāve tasyābhāvaḥ, sāmānyātmanaḥ kadācidabhāvavirodhāt | na ca tadāsyājanakasvabhāvatā, janakājanakarūpavataḥ samagretarāvasthayorbhedaprasaṅgāt | tathā ca sāmānyātmanā hāniḥ | tato yadasya samagreṣu cakṣurādiṣu janakaṃ rūpaṃ tadekaikābhāve 'pi vidyate na ca janayatīti ‘tatsvabhāvasya jananāt'; ityanekānta iti |
body.translated_text: Again, raising <s>anekānta</s> in another way, the <s>Kṣapaṇakas</s> and <s>Jaiminīyas</s> say: "When a single" effect characterized as <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) "arises from" cooperative factors (<s>sahakārin</s>) such as the eye etc. "whose natures are different" — mutually distinct — the causes are many and of different natures, but the effect is one and of undifferentiated nature, so "there should be no difference of effect from difference of cause." Therefore the eye-faculty and the rest should not be regarded as generators of a single effect through distinct natures. Rather, one should accept that they have an undifferentiated, generic form that generates one effect, by which they generate an undifferentiated effect. And that [generic form] generates that effect only in the state of completeness (<s>samagra</s>), not in an incomplete state. Nor is there absence of that [generic form] when one individual [factor] is absent, because something of a universal nature cannot ever be incompatible with existence. Nor is there non-generative nature of it [in the incomplete state], because there would be the absurd consequence of difference [in the generic form] between the complete and incomplete states, as it would have both generative and non-generative forms. And thus the universal nature would be lost. Therefore, that generative form which it has in the complete [set of] eye-faculty etc. is present even in the absence of one [factor], and yet does not generate — so 'because that which has that nature generates' is subject to <s>anekānta</s>.

body.text: 22. siddhāntavādīnā dūṣaṇodvāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 22. The opening of the refutation by the proponents.

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "na, yathāsvam" ityādi | evaṃ manyate- kiṃ punaridaṃ kāraṇamabhimataṃ bhavataḥ? | yadi pratyekaṃ cakṣurādikam; (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 93

children.text: ) tadayuktam | sāmagrījanyasvabhāvatvāt kāryasya, tasyā eva kāraṇatvāt | nanu tadavasthāyāṃ pratyekameva sāmagrīśabdavācyānāṃ jananasvabhāvatvābhyupagamāt pratyekameva cakṣurādikaṃ kāraṇam | yadyevaṃ ko 'yaṃ niyamo yadanekasmād bhavatānekena bhavitavyam viparyaye bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt, ekenaiva tat kāryaṃ kartavyamiti ca na niyamakāraṇamutpaśyāmaḥ | ekaṃ ca tatkāryaṃ karotīti kuto 'vasitam? | tadbhāve bhāvāt iti cet | anekatrāpi samānametat | taduktam- "tasyaiveikasya janane samarthāḥ nānyasya iti nāparāparajananam" iti | na cānekasmād bhavadanekaṃ prāpnoti | yato nāsmākaṃ bhavatāmiva kāraṇameva kāryātmatāmupaiti, yato 'nekapariṇateranekarūpatvāt kāryasyānekatā syāt | kintu apūrvameva keṣucit satsu bhavati | taccānekabhāva eva bhāvāt tatkāryamucyate tasya kuto 'nekatāprasaṅgaḥ? | yattvabhinnaṃ rūpaṃ janakamucyate tasyaikasthitāvapi bhāvāt tatkāryajananasvabhāvācca tataḥ kāryaprasavaprasaṅgaḥ, tadanyasannidhau tasya viśeṣābhāvāt tadāpi vāna janayet | tasmād yeṣuṃ bhāvābhāvavatsu kāryaṃ bhāvābhāvavad dṛṣṭaṃ ta eva viśeṣā janakā iti kuto 'nekāntaḥ? |
children.translated_text: ) that is untenable — because the effect has a nature born from the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>), and it is the aggregate itself that is the cause. [Objection:] But since in that state [of aggregation] we accept that each individual [factor] designated by the word <s>sāmagrī</s> has the nature of a generator, each individual factor such as the eye-faculty is indeed the cause. [Reply:] If so, what is this restriction that from many [causes] there must be many [effects]? — since there is no invalidating proof (<s>bādhaka-pramāṇa</s>) for the contrary, and we see no reason for the restriction that the effect must be produced by one alone. And how is it ascertained that one [factor] alone produces that effect? If [you say]: because there is existence [of the effect] when that exists — this is equally [true] of many [causes]. This has been stated: "they are understood as capable of generating that one single [effect], not of generating different things successively." Nor does it follow that because it arises from many, it must be many. For in our view, unlike yours, the cause does not itself become the nature of the effect, such that from the transformation of many, the effect would be many due to having many forms. Rather, something entirely new comes into being when certain [conditions] are present. And since it exists only when the many exist, it is called the effect of those — so whence the absurd consequence of multiplicity [of the effect]? As for saying that an undifferentiated form is the generator — since that exists even when one [factor] alone is present, and since it has the nature of generating that effect, there would be the absurd consequence of production of the effect from it [alone]; and in the proximity of the others, since there is no specific difference in it, it would either [generate] then too or not generate [at all]. Therefore, whatever specific [factors] in whose presence and absence the effect is seen to be present and absent — those very specifics are the generators. So whence the <s>anekānta</s>?

body.translated_text: The proponent says: "No, according to each one's own [nature]" etc. He thinks as follows: What then is the cause you have in mind? If it is each individual [factor] such as the eye-faculty etc. (

body.text: atha sāmagrīṃ kāraṇamāśrityocyate ‘na kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedaḥ syāditi', "tanna", "yathāsvaṃ" yasyāḥ sāmagryāḥya ātmīyaḥ svabhāvastadbhedena "tadviśeṣopayogataḥ" tasya- vijñānalakṣaṇasya kāryasya, viśeṣāḥ- sāmagrībhedād bhinnāḥ svabhāvāḥ, teṣūpayogataḥ tadupayogaiḥ bhinnasāmagrīvyāpāraiḥ kāryāḥ ye svabhāvaviśeṣāḥ- kāryāṇāṃviśiṣṭāḥ svabhāvāḥ teṣāmasaṅkarātparasparavyāvṛttarūpatvāt | sāmagrībhedād bhinnarūpataiva kāryāṇāmiti kathanna kāraṇabhedād kāryabhedaḥ syāt? | tathā hi- ekā sāmagrī manaskāratatsāgduṇyādilakṣaṇā, tato vikalpavijñānamātraṃ jāyate; aparā manaskārendriyamātralakṣaṇā, tato bhrāntendriyavijñānasambhavaḥ; tadanyā viṣayendriyamanaskārātmikā, tato 'pyabhrāntavijñānasambhūtiriti bhinnasāmagrījanmanāṃ kāryasvabhāvaviśeṣāṇāmasāṅkaryādastyeva (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 94

children.text:
) sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇabhedāt kāryāṇāṃ bheda iti |
nanu yadā viṣayendriyamanaskārebhyo vijñānasambhavaḥ tadā teṣāmupayogaviṣayasyaikatvāt kathamasāṅkaryam? | tathāvidhasya sāṅkaryasyeṣṭatvāt adoṣaḥ | taduktam- "tatraivaikatra sāmarthyāt" ityādi |
children.translated_text:
) difference of effects from difference of cause characterized as aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>).
But when consciousness arises from object, sense-faculty, and mental attention, since the scope of their contribution is one [and the same], how is there non-intermixture? [Reply:] There is no fault, because such intermixture is accepted. This has been stated: "Because of capacity directed at that one and the same [effect]" etc.

body.translated_text: If, taking recourse to the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) as the cause, it is said 'there should be no difference of effect from difference of cause,' "that is not so": "according to each one's own" — by the difference of the nature proper to each aggregate, "because of the contribution of the specific features of that [effect]" — of that effect characterized as <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), the specific features — the distinct natures produced by difference of aggregate — by their contributions, i.e., by the operations of distinct aggregates that produce them; the specific features of nature that are effects — the distinguished natures of the effects — because of their non-intermixture, because of their having mutually exclusive forms. Since the effects have distinct forms due to difference of aggregate, how could there be no difference of effect from difference of cause? For example: one aggregate, characterized by mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) and its favorable conditions etc., gives rise to merely conceptual consciousness (<s>vikalpa-vijñāna</s>); another, characterized by mental attention and sense-faculty alone, gives rise to erroneous sensory consciousness (<s>bhrānta-indriya-vijñāna</s>); yet another, consisting of object, sense-faculty, and mental attention, gives rise to non-erroneous consciousness (<s>abhrānta-vijñāna</s>) — since the specific features of the effects that are born from distinct aggregates are not intermixed, there is indeed (

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi teṣāṃ tajjanakatvam?, yadi tadbhedāt na bhidyate kāryam | kiṃ nu vai samagrāṇāmanyānyakāryajananena janakatvam yatastadabhāve tanna syāt | janakatvaṃ hyeṣāṃ tadbhāva eva kasyacid bhāvāt | tatraikasyānekasya vā bhāve teṣāmekānekajanakatvamucyate |
body.translated_text: But then how is their status as generators [established], if the effect is not differentiated by their differentiation? Is it that their generative status consists in the generation of mutually different effects by the complete [set], such that in its absence that [effect] would not occur? For their generative status is due to the existence of something when they exist. And therein, when one or many exist, they are said to be generators of one or many [effects].

body.text: 23. ekasāmagrījanyeṣvapi kāryeṣu bhedopapādanam |
body.translated_text: 23. Establishing difference even among effects born from a single aggregate.

body.text: nanvekasyāḥ sāmagryā anekasya bhāve sāmagryantarajanyebhyo bhavatu bhedaḥ, parasparatastu katham? | tadatadrūpahetujatvāddhi bhāvāstadatadrūpiṇa iṣyante | tatra yadā cakṣūrūpamanaskārebhyo vijñānajanma tadā cakṣūrūpakṣaṇayorapi bhāvād vijñānenābhinnahetujatvāt tayorvijñānātmatā, vijñānasya vā tadrūpatā kathaṃ na prasajyeta? | āha ca-
body.translated_text: But [one objects:] if from a single aggregate many [effects] arise, let there be a difference [of those effects] from [effects] produced by a different aggregate; but how [can there be] a difference among those [effects] themselves? For entities are held to be of a particular nature because they are born from causes of that particular nature. Now, when consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) is produced from the eye, form, and mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), then since the eye-moment and the form-moment also exist [in that aggregate], and consciousness would share the same causes with them, how would it not follow that those [eye and form moments] have the nature of consciousness, or that consciousness has their nature? And it has been said:

body.text:
"tadatadrūpiṇo bhāvāstadadrūpahetujāḥ |
tadrūpādi kimajñānaṃ vijñānābhinnahetujam ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "Entities that are of a particular nature are born from causes of that particular nature; is the unknown [entity] of such-and-such a nature, being born from causes undifferentiated from consciousness?"

body.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ | teṣāṃ yathāsvaṃ svabhāvabhedena nimittopādānatayā tadupayogāt | manaskāro hi vijñānasyopādānakāraṇam | cakṣuṣastu svavijñānajananayogyasya janamani sahakārikāraṇam | evamitaratrāpi yathāyogamvācyam | tato 'nyādaśī sāmagrī cakṣuḥkṣaṇasya janikā, anyādaśī ca vijñānāderiti tadvailakṣaṇyādeva kāryāṇāṃ vailakṣaṇyam |
body.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because those [causes] function according to their respective differences in nature, as efficient (<s>nimitta</s>) or material (<s>upādāna</s>) causes. For mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) is the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>) of consciousness. But the eye is a cooperative cause (<s>sahakārikāraṇa</s>) in the production of what is fit to generate its own consciousness. The same should be stated elsewhere as appropriate. Therefore, the aggregate that produces the eye-moment is of one kind, and the aggregate that produces consciousness and the like is of another kind — and from the very distinctness of the aggregates follows the distinctness of the effects.

children.text: ) tadbhāve vyabhicārāvyabhicārataśca | tathā hi- vijñānaṃ manaskārasya bodharūpatāmanukaroti, na cakṣurāderjarā(ḍā)dibhāvam | evamanyadapi pratyeyam | niyamena ca vijñānamātrabhāve samanantarapratyayasya vyāpāro na cakṣurādeḥ | cakṣuḥkṣaṇāntarodaye ca pūrvabhāvinaścakṣuṣo na svavijñānayogyatāhetoḥ samanantarapratyayasya | evaṃ rūpasyāpi vācyam | tasmādavasthābhede 'pi yad ekākāraparāmarṣa(rśa)pratyayanibandhanatayā svasantatipatitakāryaprasūtinimittaṃ tad upādānakāraṇaṃ yat santānāntare prāgavasthāpekṣaviśeṣodayanibandhanaṃ tat sahakārikāraṇam | sā ceyaṃ bhāvānāṃ svahetuparamparayātā prakṛtiryayā kiñcit kāryaṃ svasantānavyavasthānibandhanaṃ janayantyaparaṃ ca santānāntaravyapadeśanibandhanamiti tasyā eva sāmagryā avāntaraviśeṣakṛtatvāccakṣūrūpavijñānakṣaṇānāṃ parasparato vailakṣaṇyaṃ na virudhyate |
children.translated_text: — and from the deviation and non-deviation in the presence of that [factor]. That is to say: consciousness imitates the cognitive nature of mental attention, not the inert nature and the like of the eye and so forth. The same should be understood for other [cases] as well. And necessarily, when consciousness alone is present, it is the immediately preceding condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>) that operates, not the eye and the like. And when a subsequent eye-moment arises, it is the previous eye [that serves as the immediately preceding condition] for [the production of what is] fit to generate its own consciousness, not the immediately preceding condition [of consciousness]. The same should be said for form as well. Therefore, even when there is no difference in state, that which — by being the ground of a cognition grasping a single aspect — serves as the cause for the production of effects falling within its own continuum (<s>santāna</s>), that is the material cause (<s>upādānakāraṇa</s>); and that which serves as the ground for the arising of a distinctive state in dependence on a prior state in a different continuum, that is the cooperative cause (<s>sahakārikāraṇa</s>). And this very nature of entities — [arising] through the succession of their own causes — is the nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) by which [an entity] produces some effect that grounds the determination of its own continuum, and another [effect] that grounds the designation of a different continuum; and since the distinctness of the eye-moment, form-moment, and consciousness-moment from each other is due to the internal sub-distinctions of that very aggregate, there is no contradiction.

body.translated_text: One might object: since the positive and negative concomitance of all [the factors in the aggregate] follow together, whence this distinction — that here [mental attention] functions as a material cause, and elsewhere [the eye] as a cooperative cause? [The answer:] from the imitation and non-imitation of the cognitive nature (<s>bodharūpatā</s>) and so on,

body.text: 24. kāraṇānekatve 'pi kāryasyaikatvaṃ sāmagrībhede ca kāryabhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: 24. Even when causes are many, the effect is unitary; and when the aggregate differs, the effect differs.

body.text: tasmād yadi ‘kāraṇabhedāt'; kāraṇānekatvāt "kāryasya bhedaḥ" anekatvaṃ tadā pratibandhābhāvādanekāntaḥ | na ca tadabhyupagamyata iti na kācit kṣatiḥ |
body.translated_text: Therefore, if "from the difference of causes" — from the multiplicity of causes — "there is a difference" — multiplicity — "of the effect," then [the argument would be] inconclusive, due to the absence of necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>). And since this [multiplicity of effects from multiple causes] is not accepted [by us], there is no harm.

body.text: atha sāmagrīlakṣaṇasya kāraṇasya bhedaḥ sāmagryantarād vailakṣaṇyaṃ kāryasyāpi bhedo 'tatkāraṇebhyo bhinnasvabhāvatocyate | tadā tasyeha bhāvāt kathaṃ na kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedaḥ syāt? iti abhiprāyavatā ‘na'; kāraṇabhedāt kāryabhedo na syāt | kutaḥ? | "yathāsvam" ityādyabhihitam |
body.translated_text: But if the difference of the cause characterized as an aggregate — i.e., its distinctness from another aggregate — and the difference of the effect — i.e., its having a nature different from [effects] not born from those [same] causes — is what is being said, then since that [aggregate-difference] obtains here, how could there not be a difference of the effect from the difference of the cause? body.translated_text: 26. Refutation of the position, accepted by <s>Ahrīka</s> and others, of difference-and-non-difference of substance and mode (<s>dravyaparyāya</s>).

body.text: nanu ca mṛtsaṃsthānaviśeṣayorekasvabhāvatve 'pyahrīkādibhiḥ saṅkhayādibhedād bheda iṣyate tatkathamanekapratyayajanitasyaikatve etadudāharaṇam syāt? | sarvatraiva hi dravyaparyāyayoḥ saṅkhayāsaṃjñālakṣaṇakāryabhedād bhedo deśakālasvabhāvābhedāccābheda iṣyate, yathā ghaṭasya rūpādīnāṃ ca | tathā hi- eko ghaṭaḥ rūpādayo bahava iti saṅkhyābhedaḥ | ghaṭaḥ rūpādayaḥ iti saṃjñābhedaḥ | anuvṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dravyannityaṃ ca, vyāvṛttilakṣaṇā bhedāḥ kṣaṇikāśca; jaiminīyasya tu kecit kālāntarasthāyino 'pīti lakṣaṇabhedaḥ | ghaṭenodakāharaṇaṃ kriyate, rūpādībhiḥ punarvasturāga iti kāryabhedaḥ | evaṃ sarvatra dravyaparyāyoḥ saṅkhayādibhirbhedaḥ deśādibhistvabheda iti mṛtsaṃsthānayoḥ kathañcit bhedāt mṛtkulālābhyāṃ janitasya kāryasyānekatāstyeva | yathā tvekatā tathā tābhyāṃ tasya abhinnātmajanyataiveti yadanekakāraṇaṃ tadanekameva, yat punarekaṃ tat sahakāriṇāmabhinnarūpajanyatayaikakāraṇameveti na vyabhicāra iti |
body.translated_text: But [one objects:] even when the clay and the particular configuration are of one nature, the <s>Ahrīkas</s> (<s>Jainas</s>) and others hold that there is a difference due to the difference of number (<s>saṅkhyā</s>) and the like. So how can this be an example for the unity [of the effect] when produced from multiple causes? For everywhere, [they hold that] between substance (<s>dravya</s>) and mode (<s>paryāya</s>), there is a difference characterized by number, designation, and the like

When the difference in nature is not accepted [as real], the difference [based on number and the like] is unestablished any other way — since the production of a single effect from multiple [causes] is not contradicted. Or, if the difference in nature were accepted, then since the clay and configuration would be mutually non-identical, [they would be] unrelated to each other as specific modifications of configuration-nature and clay-nature, and thus

body.text: saṅkhyābhedastāvadasamarthaḥ, ekasminnapi dravye bahutvena vyavahāradarśanāt | yathā gurava iti | na ca bahuvacanasya niyamenādarśanād rūpādayo 'tra nimittam, rūpādinimittatve hi guruḥ iti na kadācidekavacanaṃ syāt | sambhavi dharmirūpamātramabhidheyatvena vivakṣitam iti cet | na | tasyaikatvena vivakṣāyāṃ kārtsnyagauravayorapratitiprasaṅgāt | brīhaya iti ca jātivacane dharmiṇo rūpādīnāṃ cānabhidhānāt na kiñciduttaram | ubhayarūpasya ca vastuno guruśabdavācyatvāt kathaṃ sambhavino dharmirūpasyaikatvena vivakṣā? | tataścaiko gururiti sāmānādhikaraṇyadarśanāt paryāyā apyekasaṃkhyāviṣayāḥ | te ca paryāyarūpeṇa bhidyante | tat kathaṃ saṃkhyābhedād bhedasiddhiḥ? iti |
body.translated_text: The difference of number, for a start, is incapable [of establishing real difference], since even in a single substance, usage in the plural number is observed — as in "the heavy ones" (<s>gurava</s>). And since the plural number is not invariably observed [to indicate real plurality], form and the like are not the ground [for it] here; for if form and the like were the ground, then the singular "the heavy one" (<s>guruḥ</s>) would never

body.text: saṃjñāpi saṅketanibandhanā | sa cecchāyattavṛttiriti kutastato 'rthabhedaḥ? | ekasminnapi ca saṃjñābhedadṛṣṭeḥ kathamasya bhedanimittatā? | yathā indraḥ śakraḥ purandaraḥ iti | atrāpi indanāt śakanāt dāraṇācca śaktibhedo gamyata iti cet | na | samastasya kāryakartṛtvāt | na hi śaktireva indati śankoti dārayati ca | kiṃ tarhi? | dharmirūpamapi, tayorekasvabhāvopagamāt, śaknotyādipadaistadvācināṃ sāmānādhikaraṇyadarśanācca | na cāskhalavdṛttipratyayaviṣayatvādupacārakalpanā yukteti | yeṣāṃ ca paryāyāṇāṃ na kācidarthānugamamātrā tatra kiṃ vaktavyam? |
body.translated_text: A name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) too is dependent on convention (<s>saṅketa</s>). And that [convention] operates dependently on volition (<s>icchā</s>). So how can a difference of meaning arise from that? Moreover, since differences in names are observed even for a single thing, how can [name-difference] be the basis of [real] difference? For instance: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Purandara</s>. If [one objects that] even here a difference in powers (<s>śakti</s>) is understood from the acts of 'gladdening' (indana), 'being able' (śakana), and 'destroying' (dāraṇa) — no, because the entire [entity] is the agent of [all] effects. For it is not the power alone that gladdens, is able, and destroys. Rather, the substance-nature (<s>dharmin</s>) too [does so], because the two [power and substance] are accepted as having a single nature, and because co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is observed between terms like 'is able' (śaknoti) etc. and words denoting that [substance]. Nor is it proper to postulate figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>), since [these terms] are objects of unhesitating cognition. And for those synonyms (<s>paryāya</s>) that have no semantic basis whatsoever — what is there to say?

body.text: lakṣaṇabhedo 'pyahetuḥ asiddhatvāt | nahyeko bhāvaḥ kvacidapyanvayī siddha iti | tathā hi- na kūṭasthanityatayā nityaṃ dravyamahrīkairiṣyate, (

children.text: ) pariṇāmanityatopagamāt | sā ca purvottarakṣaṇaprabandhavṛttyā | nahyasya paryāyāṇāmivocchedaḥ tadrūpeṇa, paryāyā eva paryāyarūpeṇa nirudhyante na tu dravyamiti nityamabhyupagamyate | na ceyaṃ kūṭasthanityatā vā dravye sambhavati, paryāyavyatiriktasya dravyasyāsiddheḥ tasyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya tadvivekānupalakṣaṇāt | paryāyeṣveva tulyarūpakāryakartṛṣu dravyābhimāno mandamatīnām | na punastat tato vilakṣaṇamupalakṣyate |
children.translated_text: because they accept permanence through transformation (<s>pariṇāma-nityatā</s>). And that [transformation-permanence] operates through a continuum (<s>prabandhavṛtti</s>) of prior and subsequent moments. For there is no destruction of it [the substance] in its own form, as there is of its modes (<s>paryāya</s>); rather, the modes alone are destroyed in their modal form, while the substance is not — thus it is held to be permanent. But neither immutable permanence (<s>kūṭastha-nityatā</s>) nor [transformation-permanence] is possible in substance, because a substance apart from its modes is unestablished — since that [substance], which meets the conditions for being perceivable (<s>upalabdhi-lakṣaṇa-prāpta</s>), is not perceived as distinct from them [the modes]. Rather, it is only with regard to modes that have similar forms and are agents of [similar] effects that the dull-witted develop the notion of 'substance'. But that [substance] is never perceived as having a nature distinct from those [modes].

body.translated_text: Difference in characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇabheda</s>) too is not a [valid] reason, because it is unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>). For a single entity that persists anywhere has never been established. To explain: the shameless ones (<s>ahrīka</s>, i.e., the Jains) do not hold that a permanent substance (<s>dravya</s>) is permanent in the sense of being immutable (<s>kūṭastha-nitya</s>),

body.text: kāryabhedastvasmān prati asiddha eva | rūpādīnāmeva keṣāñcit tatkāryakartṛtvāt | tathāpyabhyupagamyocyate- kāryaṃ hi dvividham | bhinnakālamabhinnakālaṃ ca | tatra pūrvaṃ bhavati bhedanivandhanam yadīha sambhavet | tattu na sambhavati dharmadharmiṇostulyakālatvāt | abhinnakālastu kāryabhede 'naikāntikaḥ, vibhaktapariṇāmeṣu paṭādiṣu sambhavāt | paṭādayo 'pi hi vibhaktapariṇāmā anekaṃ kāryaṃ kurvanto dṛṣṭāḥ | na ca dharmirūpeṇa bhidyante, ekasyānekakriyāvirodhābhāvācca | nahyatra kāraṇameva kāryātmatāmupaiti, yata ekasya kāraṇātmanaḥ ekakāryarūpatopagame tadanyarūpābhāvāt tadanyakāryātmatopagatirna syāt | kintvapūrvameva kasyacid bhāve prāgavidyamānaṃ bhavat tatkāryam | tatra viṣayendriyamanaskārāṇāmitaretaropadānāhitarūpabhedānāṃ sannidhau viśiṣṭasvetarakṣaṇabhāve pratyekaṃ tadbhāvābhāvānuvidhānādanekakriyopagamo na virudhyate | yatra ekakriyāyāmapi tasya tadbhāvabhāvitaiva nibandhanam | sā cānekakriyāyāmapi samāneti |
body.translated_text: Difference in effects (<s>kāryabheda</s>), however, is simply unestablished from our [Buddhist] standpoint, since only certain things such as color (<s>rūpa</s>) etc. are agents of those effects. Nevertheless, accepting [the opponent's position] for the sake of argument, we say: effects are of two kinds — occurring at different times and occurring at the same time. Of these, the first could serve as a basis for [establishing] difference, if it were possible here. But it is not possible, because the property (<s>dharma</s>) and the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) are simultaneous. And [the argument from] effects occurring at the same time is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because it is possible in things like cloth etc. that undergo differentiated transformation (<s>vibhakta-pariṇāma</s>). For things like cloth too, undergoing differentiated transformation, are observed to produce multiple effects. Yet they are not divided in their substance-nature, because there is no contradiction in a single entity performing multiple actions. For it is not that the cause itself becomes the effect-nature, such that if a single cause-nature assumed one effect-form, the absence of another form would prevent its assuming another effect-nature. Rather, something that was previously nonexistent, coming into being upon the existence of something, is an effect of that. In that case, when the sense-object, sense-faculty, and mental attention — whose forms have been differentiated by the modifications contributed by each to the others — are in proximity, due to the fact that in each distinct subsequent moment the [effect's] presence and absence follow upon the presence and absence of each [contributing factor], the admission of multiple effects is not contradictory. Even where there is a single effect, it is precisely the condition of being brought about by that [factor's] presence that serves as the basis. And that [condition] is the same even in [the case of] multiple effects.

body.text: nanu ca tatsannidhau vijñānalakṣaṇakāryasambhavāt tajjananasvabhāvataivaiṣāmavadhriyate, kāryasvabhāvāpekṣayā kāraṇasya janakarūpatāvasthānāt | tato vijñānajananasvabhāvebhyaḥ pratyekaṃ kathaṃ tadanyakāryasambhavaḥ? | (

children.text: ) tadbhāve vā teṣāṃ tadanyajananasvabhāvatā syāt | tataśca vijñānameva na kuryuḥ, tadaḥ yajananasvabhāvatvāt |
children.translated_text: Or if [such a different effect] exists, they would have the nature of generating something other [than cognition]. And in that case, they would not produce cognition at all, since they would have the nature of generating something other than that.

body.translated_text: But [the opponent objects:] since in the proximity of those [factors] an effect in the form of cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) arises, their nature as generators of just that is ascertained, because the generative nature of the cause is determined relative to the nature of the effect. So how, from those whose nature is to generate cognition, can a different effect individually arise?

body.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ, teṣāmanekakāryākriyāsvabhāvatvāt | tathā hi- te tadavasthāyāṃ pratyekaṃ viśiṣṭasajātīyetarakṣaṇajananātmakāḥ, teṣāṃ tatsattānantaryadarśanāt | tatra vijñānajananasvabhāvataiveti tasyājananasvabhāvatā vyavacchidyate tasyā eva pratiyogitvāt nānyajananasvabhāvatā | na cātasteṣāmanekātmatā syāt, ekasyaivātmātiśayasyānekakāryahetutvāt | na hi tadanyāpekṣayā viparyavyāvṛttimupādāyānekena śabdenābhidhīyamānaṃ vastu anekarūpatāṃ pratipadyate, prativiśiṣṭasyaikasyaivātmanastathābhidhānāt | yathā rūpaṃ sanidarśanaṃ sapratighamiti | nahyatra svabhāvabhedanibandhanā dhvanayaḥ, sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāvaprasaṅgāt | tannimittānāmekatra bhāvāt adoṣa iti cet | na | teṣāṃ tadekopakārānapekṣiṇāṃ tadayogāt | apekṣāyāṃ vā kathamekamanekakāryaṃ na syāt? | anekenaivātmanopayogāt iti cet | na | sāmānādhikaraṇyābhāvadoṣasya tādavasthyaprasaṅgāt | na ca nīlādīnāmātmabhedamadhyakṣamīkṣāmahe | nāpi kāryabhedādevātmabhedānumānam, pratibandhābhāvāt, tadāgrahakapramāṇābhāvāt | pratyakṣato 'nekakāryāṇāmapi bhāvānāmekātmatayaivopalakṣaṇāt pradīpādīnām | nānumānataḥ, tatrāpi viparyaye bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt | ekasyānekakriyānabhyupagame ca yo 'yaṃ rūparasagandhasparśaviśeṣāṇāṃ kvacit sahabhāvaniyamaḥ pramāṇaparidṛṣṭaḥ sa na syāt | bhinnanimittānāṃ sahabhāvaniyamāyogāt | tannimittānāmapi tadekakāraṇānāyattajanmanāṃ niyatasāhityāsambhavāt | tadekadharmisvabhāvatayaikatra sahabhāvaniyama iti cet | na | ekasyānekasvabhāvatāyā eva cintyatvāt | anekenaikasvabhāvatāṃ cānubhavataḥ tadvadanekatāyā durnivāratvāt anyathā dharmadharmiṇāṃ kathaṃ (

children.text: ) naikāntiko bhedaḥ? | tathā hi- yamātmānaṃ purodhāyāyaṃ dharmī paryāyāścaite iti vyavasthāpyate, yadi tasya bhedastadā bheda eveti |
children.translated_text: not be absolute? To explain: the self (<s>ātman</s>) that is put forward [as the basis] — saying 'this is the substance and these are the modes' — if there is a difference of that [self from the modes], then there is simply difference [and no unity].

body.translated_text: This is not a fault, because they have the nature of producing multiple effects. To explain: in that state, each of them individually has the nature of generating a distinct subsequent moment of the same kind (<s>sajātīya</s>), since the arising of that [subsequent moment] is observed immediately after the existence of those [factors]. Here, [when we say] 'their nature is just that of generating cognition,' what is excluded is the nature of not generating that [cognition], since that alone is the counter-correlate (<s>pratiyogin</s>) — not the nature of generating something else. Nor would this entail that they have multiple natures, because a single excellence of nature (<s>ātmātiśaya</s>) is the cause of multiple effects. For a real thing, being described by multiple words on the basis of exclusions (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) relative to different things, does not thereby acquire multiple natures, since one single nature with respect to each distinction is so described. Just as: 'color is visible (<s>sanidarśana</s>) and tangible (<s>sapratigha</s>).' For here the designations are not based on a difference of nature, since [otherwise] there would be an absence of co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>). If [one says] there is no fault because the bases of those [designations] exist in one [entity] — no, because those [bases], not requiring a single benefit from that [entity], cannot belong to it [as a unity]. Or if there is [such mutual] dependence, how could a single thing not have multiple effects? If [one says] it serves through multiple natures only — no, because the fault of absence of co-referentiality would remain as before. And we do not perceive through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) a difference of nature in blue (<s>nīla</s>) etc. Nor is there an inference of difference of nature from difference of effects, because of the absence of an invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), i.e., the absence of a means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that grasps that [connection]. Since through perception, things that produce multiple effects — like a lamp (<s>pradīpa</s>) etc. — are perceived as having a single nature. Nor [can it be established] through inference, because even there, there is no means of knowledge that would refute the contrary position. And if one does not accept that a single entity can perform multiple actions, then the observed invariable co-occurrence of specific forms of color, taste, smell, and touch in certain [entities], which is established by a means of knowledge, would be impossible. Because there can be no invariable co-occurrence of things with different causes. And even for the causes of those [qualities], since they arise dependently on a single cause, invariable co-existence would be impossible [without unity]. If [one says] the invariable co-occurrence in one [locus] is due to their being the nature of a single property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) — no, because precisely the single entity's having multiple natures is what is in question. And for one who experiences multiple things as having a single nature, the multiplicity [of those things] is equally difficult to deny, since otherwise how would the difference between properties (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>)

body.text: anekasyāpyekakāryatā na syāt | na hi parasparopādānakṛtopakārānapekṣā viṣayendriyamanaskārāḥ sahaikakāryārambhiṇo yuktāḥ | na caikameva kiñcit kvacit janayati | tataśca sarvatra kāryakāraṇabhāva evo 'tsīdet, anekasyaikasya caikānekakriyāvirahāt prakārāntarābhāvācca |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the production of a single effect by multiple [causes] would also be impossible. For sense-objects, sense-faculties, and mental attention, without requiring the assistance produced by each serving as the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of the others, are not fit to jointly initiate a single effect. And nothing ever generates a single [effect] entirely by itself. Consequently, the causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) everywhere would collapse, since multiple [things] having a single [effect] and a single [thing] having multiple effects would both be absent, and no alternative [explanation] exists.

body.text: nāpyehetukameva viśvam, deśakālaprakṛtiniyamāt | tasmādekasāmagryadhīnajanmanāmeva sahabhāvaniyamo bhāvānāmekakāryakriyāniyamo vā | tataśca svasantānakṣaṇamitaropādānaṃ ca yugapadupakurvataḥ kathamekasyānekakāryatā na syāt? | tataḥ kāthaṃ kāryabhedād bhedaḥ kalpyeta? | dravyaparyāyāṇāṃ caikasvabhāvatāmācakṣāṇa ekasyānekakāryatāṃ pratikṣipatīti kathaṃ nonmattaḥ?, svabhāvasyaiva vastutvāt, anyathā tasya niḥsvabhāvatāprasaṅgāt | ekasvabhāvatve ca dravyaparyāyāṇāṃ tatkāryabheda ekavastunibandhana eveti kāryabhedād bhedamabhidadhānaḥ sphuṭamahrīka evāyamityupekṣāmarhati |
body.translated_text: Nor is the universe without a cause (<s>ahetu</s>), because of the regularity of place, time, and nature (<s>deśakālasvabhāvaniyama</s>). Therefore, the invariable co-occurrence of things is due to their arising dependently on a single causal complex (<s>sāmagrī</s>), or [equivalently,] the regularity of producing a single effect. And so, for one that simultaneously contributes to [producing] a moment of its own continuum (<s>svasantānakṣaṇa</s>) and serves as the material cause of something else, how could a single entity not have multiple effects? How then could difference be postulated from difference of effects? Moreover, one who declares the identity of nature of substance (<s>dravya</s>) and modes (<s>paryāya</s>) yet rejects a single entity's having multiple effects — how is he not mad? — since the intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) alone is the real entity, and otherwise its lack of any nature would follow. And if substance and modes are of one nature, then the difference of their effects is grounded in a single entity alone. Thus one who asserts difference from difference of effects is plainly a shameless one (<s>ahrīka</s>, i.e., a Jain) and deserves to be disregarded.

body.text: 27. vaiśeṣikakṛto 'pyekasyānekakāryakāritvākṣepo na yuktaḥ |
body.translated_text: 27. The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s>'s objection too, that a single entity cannot produce multiple effects, is unjustified.

body.text: vaiśeṣiko 'pi dravyasyaikasya dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ samavāyikāraṇatāṃ bruvāṇaḥ karmaṇaścaikasya saṃyogavibhāgasaṃskāranimittatāmekasyānekakāryakriyāṃ pratikṣipan svakṛtāntakopenaiva pratihataḥ | na cātra śaktibhedo nibandhanam, yatastadekopakāranirapekṣāḥ kathametāḥ śaktayo niyatārthādhārāḥ?, na punaranavayavena vyaktīrvāśnuvīran? | tato yata evāsyātmātiśayādanekaśaktyupakāra (

children.translated_text: from that very same [nature] there is also the production of multiple effects — so enough with this overly lengthy discussion.

body.translated_text: The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> too, while asserting that a single substance (<s>dravya</s>) is the inherence-cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of [further] substance, quality (<s>guṇa</s>), and action (<s>karman</s>), and that a single action is the efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>) of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>), and <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) — is refuted by the very rebellion of his own doctrine when he rejects that a single entity can produce multiple effects. Nor can a difference of powers (<s>śakti</s>) serve as the basis [for the objection], for how can those powers, without requiring a single benefit from that [entity], have determinate objects as their substrate? Could they not pervade the individuals even without component parts? Therefore, from whatever excellence of nature (<s>ātmātiśaya</s>) there is the contribution of multiple powers,

body.text: 28. deśakālasvabhāvābhedasyābhedasādhakatvanirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: 28. Refutation of the establishment of non-difference from non-difference of place, time, and nature.

body.text: deśakālasvabhāvābhedādabhedastu yo 'bhyupagamyate so 'pyanupapanna eva | tathā hi- deśakālayorabhede 'pi rūparasagandhasparśāḥ paryāyarūpeṇa bhidyante tataḥ kathamabhedasiddhiḥ? | svabhāvo 'pi yadi dravyaparyāyayordvayorapi pratyekamanuvṛttivyāvṛttirūpatā; tadā padārthadvayaṃ syād ghaṭapaṭavad, na tvekaṃ dvirūpamiti kathantasmādabhedasiddhiḥ? | na cānuvṛttivyāvṛttī svabhāvo yuktaḥ, tayoranuvartamānavyāvartamānādhīnatvāt | tataścānuvartamānavyāvartamānayoḥ svabhāvo 'nyo vaktavyaḥ, na tu tayoranuvṛttivyāvṛttī eva svabhāvaḥ, bhāvatvena bhavitradhīnatvāt | nahi smṛtiḥ smartuḥ svabhāvo bhavati | anuvṛttivyāvṛttyośca svabhāvatve lakṣaṇāt svabhāvasya bhedo vaktavyaḥ | mṛdādirūpatā svabhāva iti cet | atrāpyabheda iti yadi sādṛśyamucyate; tad bheda eva sambhavati, sādṛśyasya sadṛśādhikaraṇatvāt | tataśca padārthadvayameva syāt na tvekaṃ dvirūpamiti | athaikyaṃ dvitīyarūparahitatābhedo 'ṅgīkriyate kathaṃ tarhi dvirūpatā? | rūpaśabdena hyatra svabhāvo 'bhidhīyate | tasya caikye kathaṃ dvīrūpatā? | vipratiṣiddhaṃ hyetat ekasvabhāvatā dvirūpatā ceti | atha punaḥ svabhāvata aikyaṃ nopeyate | kathaṃ tarhi sa eka ityucyate anekaḥ san? | na tāvadekakāraṇajanyatvāt, sarvatropādānanimittakāraṇabhedena hetubhedasiddheḥ | nāpyekakāryakartṛtvāt, ekasyāpi vibhaktapariṇāmāvibhaktapariṇāmakāryabhedābhyupagamāt | ekābhidhānābhidheyatvādapi naikatvam, ekasyāpyanekaparyāyasambhavāt | yogyatvācca viśvasya kṛtākṛtānāmekābhidhānābhidheyatvasya kvacidasambhavāt śaktibhedācca viṣayabhedaṃ brūvāṇaṃ prati abhihitam | nāpyekavijñānaviṣayatvādekam, ekatrāpyanekavijñānaprasūteḥ | tathā hi- śaśāṅkodayaṃ bahavo nirīkṣante tasya kathamekatvamabhyupagatam? | (

children.text: ) bahūnāṃ caikavijñānaviṣayatvasambhavāt nīlapītādīnāmekatāprasaṅgaḥ | sarvathedaṃ na kathañcidapi saṅgacchate yaduta ekasya dvairūpyamiti | vijñānaṃ tu nīlapraticchāyatayotpadyamānaṃ pītādipratibhāsavyavacchedena prativiśiṣṭaṃ khyāpyate, na punarasya bhāvato dve rūpe staḥ |
children.translated_text: And since many [things] can be the object of a single cognition, there would be the absurd consequence that blue, yellow, and other [colors] are identical. In no way whatsoever is this coherent — namely, that a single entity has two forms. Cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), however, arising as a reflection of blue, is made known as specific through the exclusion of the appearance of yellow etc. But it does not [thereby] actually have two forms.

body.translated_text: The non-difference that is accepted on the basis of non-difference of place, time, and nature (<s>deśakālasvabhāva</s>) is also untenable. To explain: even when place and time are non-different, color (<s>rūpa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), and touch (<s>sparśa</s>) differ in their modal form (<s>paryāya</s>) — so how is non-difference established? As for nature (<s>svabhāva</s>): if the nature of both substance (<s>dravya</s>) and mode (<s>paryāya</s>) individually consists in both persistence (<s>anuvṛtti</s>) and exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), then there would be two entities, like a pot and a cloth, and not a single thing with two forms — so how is non-difference established from that? Nor is it proper [to hold that] persistence and exclusion constitute the nature [of things], since they depend on the persisting and the excluded [entities respectively]. Consequently, a separate nature of the persisting and the excluded must be stated, and persistence and exclusion themselves cannot be the nature, because being an entity cannot depend on that which exists through it. For memory is not the nature of the rememberer. And if persistence and exclusion were the nature, then on account of [their being distinct] characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), a difference in nature would have to be acknowledged. If [one says] the nature is being of the form of clay etc. — here too, if by 'non-difference' one means similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>), then only difference is possible, since similarity belongs to [at least two] similar things as its substrate. And so there would be just two entities, not a single thing with two forms. If, on the other hand, unity is accepted as the absence of a second form, how then is there duality of form? For by 'form' (<s>rūpa</s>) here, nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is meant. And if that is one, how is there duality of form? For these are contradictory: having a single nature and having two forms. Now if, on the other hand, unity of nature is not accepted — then how is that [thing] called 'one' while being many? Not, firstly, because of being produced by a single cause, since in all cases difference of cause is established through the difference of material, efficient, and other causes. Nor because of producing a single effect, since even for a single [entity] a difference of effects is accepted in terms of differentiated and undifferentiated transformation. Nor is there unity because of being the referent of a single designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>), since even for one thing multiple synonyms are possible.
