And because it is possible for everything — whether [actually] designated or not — to be the referent of a single name, and because of the impossibility [of invariable co-occurrence] in some cases, this has already been addressed to one who asserts difference of objects from difference of powers. Nor is it one because of being the object of a single cognition, since from a single [object] multiple cognitions arise. For example: many people observe the rising of the moon — how is its unity accepted?

body.text: atha punardravyaparyāyayoḥ sammūrcchitatvāt narasiṃhavadekaṃ śabalarūpatvāt dvīrūpamucyate | tadayuktam, narasiṃgha[ha]sya śabalarūpatvāsiddheḥ | sa hyanekaparamāṇusaṅghātarūpaḥ, te ca paramāṇavaḥ pratyekaṃ narasiṃharūpā na bhavanti, ūrdhvabhāgastasya siṃharūpaḥ, adhobhāgastu nararūpaḥ, jātyantaraṃ ca sa eva narasiṃhābhyāṃ syāt, na śabalarūpaḥ | vicitraṃ hi rūpaṃ śabalamucyate | vicitratā ca nānāsvabhāvatāṃ | nānāsvābhāvye caikatvaṃ kutaḥ? iti kevalamanekatve 'pi bahuṣvekakāryadarśanāt senādivadekavyavahāradarśanakṛto 'yaṃ viparyāso jaḍamatīnām |
body.translated_text: If, however, [one argues that] substance and mode are fused together (<s>sammūrcchita</s>), and therefore — like <s>Narasiṃha</s> (the Man-Lion) — it is one [yet] is called 'two-formed' because of its variegated nature (<s>śabalarūpa</s>): that is unjustified, because the variegated nature of <s>Narasiṃha</s> is unestablished. For he is of the form of a collection of many atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), and those atoms individually do not have the form of <s>Narasiṃha</s>. The upper part has the form of a lion, and the lower part has the form of a man. And he would be a [third] species entirely different from both man and lion — not 'variegated.' For 'variegated' (<s>śabala</s>) means having a diverse form. And diversity means having multiple natures. And given multiple natures, whence unity? Thus, it is merely because, even in [actual] multiplicity, a single effect is observed in many [components], that the conventional usage of unity arises — like an army (<s>senā</s>) — and this is a confusion (<s>viparyāsa</s>) of the dull-witted.

body.text: tadevaṃ tāvat pratyakamahetutvaṃ deśakālasvabhāvānāmekatvaprasādhane | samuditānāmapi vyabhicāritvaṃ paryāyaiḥ | tathā hi paryāyā abhinnadeśakālasvabhāvāśca paryāyarūpeṇa ca bhidyante pūrvoktācca dharmadharmiṇorniṣedhānnobhayavādasambhava iti |
body.translated_text: Thus, so far, each of these — place, time, and nature — individually fails as a reason for establishing unity. And even taken together, they are deviant (<s>vyabhicārin</s>) due to the modes. To explain: the modes are non-different in place, time, and nature [from the substance], yet they differ in their modal form. And from the previously stated negation of [the distinction between] property and property-bearer, the position asserting both [unity and difference] is also impossible.

body.text: 29. dravyaparyāyānekāntavādakhaṇḍanam |
body.translated_text: 29. Refutation of the <s>anekāntavāda</s> (doctrine of non-absolutism) regarding substance and modes.

children.translated_text: And he [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:
"Because of being in the form of substance (<s>dravya</s>) and mode (<s>paryāya</s>), a thing supposedly has a dual nature.
Even though the two are of a single nature, difference [is claimed] on the basis of difference in names and the like. [verse 1]
The form of a thing that appears in sense-cognition (<s>indriyajñāna</s>) is the object [of perception];

children.text: śabdānāṃ naiva, tat kena saṃjñābhedād vibhinnatā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: but it is not the [object] of words. By what, then, is there difference from difference of names? [verse 2]
'Its ultimate identity is not [negated]' — on account of such statements, and
because that which is not engaged by words does not appear in the cognition of one whose senses are inactive, [verse 3]
the words [applied to] that object are of a conventionally constructed scope — like in the case of seeing.
If the difference of that [object] from difference of names were only of the constructed [level], [verse 4]

children.text: vyāvṛttibhedaḥ kaścit syād, vastuno na kathaṃcana |
children.translated_text: there might be some difference in exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>), but never of the real thing.
Nor is numerical difference (<s>saṃkhyābheda</s>) considered to be anything other [than what arises] from verbal difference. [verse 5]
From that too, only the difference of the conventionally constructed would somehow result,
'For those whose words are governed by reality' — and so on — but not [difference] of the real thing. [verse 6]
Non-destruction is called persistence (<s>anuvṛtti</s>), and exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) is called destruction.
If substance (<s>dravya</s>) is non-destructible [yet] the modes are destructible — are they of the same nature as that [substance]? [verse 7]
If they [the modes] are destroyed in their modal form, [yet are held to be] of the nature of substance —
If not, is there some other form of theirs? And if not, then how can there be destruction? || 8 ||
When the substance-nature persists and modes arise subsequently, being of that [substance's] nature,

children.text: viruddhadharmādhyāse 'pi, kena, bhūtaṃ ca kiṃ, yataḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: even with the superimposition of contradictory properties — by what [means]? And what has happened? Because || 9 ||
modes are conceived therein. If the nature of difference is accepted,

children.text: bhinnaṃ paryāyarūpaṃ hi dravyarūpād bhaved yadi || 10 ||
children.translated_text: then if the form of the mode is different from the form of the substance, || 10 ||

children.text: tadaitat syādabhede tu naitat saṃbadhyate vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: this would follow. But if there is non-difference, this statement does not apply.
It would follow that one thing is both born and unborn, both destroyed and undestroyed. || 11 ||
When the substance and mode are accepted as not having each other's nature,
then there is simply no difference between them through the difference of characteristics. || 12 ||
If the difference between them in essential nature would arise from the difference of effects,
then due to the non-difference of essential nature, there would be no non-difference when that is the case. || 13 ||

children.text: svabhāvasyaiva bhedena kiṃ bhedaśca na kīrtitaḥ? |
children.translated_text: Why is the difference not stated as being by the difference of essential nature itself?

children.text: na hi paścādbhavan bhedaḥ kāryāṇāṃ tasya bhedakaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: For a difference that arises subsequently through effects is not what differentiates it. || 14 ||
Because the essential nature too would be an effect, since a cause of destruction is impossible;

children.text: ekāntena vibhinne ca te syātāṃ vastunī sa ca || 15 ||
children.translated_text: and if absolutely different, those two would be [separate] entities, and that [substance] too. || 15 ||
By which of the two [would the third relate]? Because of the difference of a non-different [entity] from two different ones,
if a non-different [entity] is posited for the purpose of establishing the non-difference of those, || 16 ||
then yet another essential nature must be conceived for establishing its non-difference [with them],
and yet another essential nature — thus there would be infinite regress. || 17 ||
And infinite essential natures cannot appear in a cognition
that lacks the capacity for [cognizing] objects — therefore, such an acceptance cannot hold. || 18 ||
If non-difference from the non-different were invariable, then for the two different [modes],
difference itself would collapse, because of their inseparability from that [non-different substance]. || 19 ||
If non-difference is not abandoned, difference would be a product of mere conceptual construction;
or if that [construction] is not false, then the non-difference would have false content. || 20 ||
Since a single existence of things whose forms are mutual absence
is not caused by another absence, therefore a single thing cannot have two forms. || 21 ||
And modes, having the form of mutual absence, would not be different [from each other];
or if the substance is not destroyed at their destruction, how could it be otherwise? || 22 ||
Absolute permanence (<s>kūṭasthanityatā</s>) in the substance and momentary destruction in the modes —
why is this not accepted? If contradiction [is alleged], then the characteristic of difference is not accepted. || 23 ||
If that [identity of substance and mode] is accepted, then why is the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), which follows all individuals,

children.text: ekamiṣṭaṃ jananyā ca jāyāyāḥ kiṃ na caikatā? || 24 ||
children.translated_text: not accepted as one? And why is there not oneness of the mother and the born [daughter]? || 24 ||
And the defects stated regarding difference and non-difference — how would they not apply

children.text: pratyekaṃ ye prasajyante dvayorbhāve kathaṃ na te? || 25 ||
children.translated_text: when that [identity] is accepted? Those that apply individually — how would they not apply when both are present? || 25 ||
If <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery) is a cause of phlegm and <s>nāgara</s> (dry ginger) is a cause of bile,
then something born from their root that is different, called '<s>guḍanāgara</s>' [jaggery-ginger compound] — || 26 ||

children.text: madhuraṃ na hi sarvaṃ syāt kaphaheturyathā madhu |
children.translated_text: for not everything sweet would be a cause of phlegm, as honey [is],

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ vā pittajanakaṃ yathā māgadhikā matā || 27 ||
children.translated_text: nor [everything] pungent a generator of bile, as <s>māgadhikā</s> (long pepper) is considered. || 27 ||

children.text: pratyekaṃ yannidānaṃ yat svato miśraṃ tadātmakam |
children.translated_text: What causes what individually — [when] mixed, having that nature of its own,

children.text: kinna dṛṣṭam? yathā māṣaḥ snigdhoṣṇaḥ kaphapittakṛt || 28 ||
children.translated_text: is it not observed? Just as <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), being unctuous and hot, produces both phlegm and bile. || 28 ||
And effects would depend on capacities, not being grounded in qualities alone,
because those [capacities] are absent everywhere [uniformly] and belong to particular things only partially. || 29 ||

children.text: ye bhedābheda mātre tu doṣāḥ sambhavinaḥ katham? |
children.translated_text: The defects that apply to mere difference and non-difference — how

children.text: tatsadbhāve 'pi te na syuriti brūyād vicakṣaṇaḥ || 30 ||
children.translated_text: could a discerning person say that even when both are present, those [defects] would not arise? || 30 ||
The defect of the co-presence of contradictories — even its consequence would not arise [they say];
but when that [contradictory co-presence] exists, what is undesired, being of its nature, does not depart. || 31 ||

children.text: bhāgā eva ca bhāsante sanniviṣṭāstathā tathā |
children.translated_text: Only parts appear, arranged in this way and that,
but no possessor of parts that is without parts ever appears. || 32 ||
Those [parts], depending on mutual conditions, with forms thus established,
and by the capacity of actions (<s>karman</s>) too, existing without separation — || 33 ||
those entities that, through their arrangement, give pleasure and pain to living beings,
being produced by actions — from those very [actions] they are inseparable. || 34 ||
And they would be denoted by a single word in some sense, but they are not truly non-different;
and in the cognition of the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), the meaning of the word does not appear. || 35 ||

children.text: aspaṣṭarūpā gamyante śabdebhyo 'pi ta eva hi |
children.translated_text: They are understood from words too, but only with an indistinct form;
therefore, with what would the conception of their being both different and non-different be compatible? || 36 ||
And how is the connection of what is without parts with multiple separate spatial portions
accepted? If [you say] because of cognition — [we reply]: of one who experiences momentary destruction, || 37 ||
the modes that are cognized are considered to belong to what possesses permanence and bliss;
whence [is this known]? If through another means of valid knowledge, then here too, a refuting [cognition] is equivalent. || 38 ||
Because they are not other [than each other], difference and non-difference of those two would certainly be invariable;
or there would be a fixed difference between those two — property and property-bearer. || 39 ||

children.text: tayorapi bhaved bhedo yadi yenātmanā tayoḥ |
children.translated_text: If there would be a difference between those two as well, then by which nature of those two
is it that 'the mode is the substance'? If that is the nature by which there is difference, || 40 ||

children.text: bheda eva tathā ca syānnaivekasya dvirūpatā |
children.translated_text: then there is simply difference, and thus a single thing would not have two forms;
or there is nothing here other than the forms of substance and mode. || 41 ||
The essential nature by reason of which there would be the conception of their oneness —
if there is non-difference of those two, then the loss of their own identity would follow. || 42 ||

children.text: tasya bhedo 'pi tābhyāṃ ced yadi yenātmanā ca te |
children.translated_text: If its difference too from those two [is posited], and by whatever nature those two
are the property-bearer and property, and if something other than that too is different by that nature — || 43 ||
then there is simply difference; and if yet another is conceived beyond those,
for the purpose of establishing their non-difference, the consequence as before would follow. || 44 ||

body.text:
dharmitvaṃ tasya caivaṃ syāt tattantratvāt tadanyayoḥ |
na caivaṃ gamyate tena vādo 'yaṃ jālmakalpitaḥ || 45 ||"
body.translated_text: And property-bearer-hood of that [third entity] would be so, because of its dependence on those; and of the two others [likewise]. And since it is not understood thus, this argument is contrived by a rogue. || 45 ||"

body.text: ityalaṃ bahubhāṣitayā | tadevaṃ mṛtsaṃsthānayorekasvabhāvatve na kathañcidbhedasambhava iti sahakāriṇāmanekatve 'pi na kāryasyānekatvamityatra bhavatyetadudāharaṇamiti |
body.translated_text: Enough of excessive speech. Thus, when clay and shape have a single essential nature, difference is in no way possible; and even when the auxiliary causes are many, the unity of the effect [is maintained] — this serves as the example for that [thesis].

body.text: 30. dravyagunayorabhede vaiśeṣikakṛtapūrvapakṣasyollekhaḥ |
body.translated_text: 30. Mention of the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> objection regarding the non-difference of substance and quality.

body.text: atra vaiśeṣikamatamāśaṅkayāha- "anyadeva" ityādi | "saṃsthānaṃ" hyavayavasanniveśa ucyate | sa ca saṃyogalakṣaṇatvād guṇarūpaḥ | "tato" mṛddravyādasyānyatvaṃ dravyaguṇayorasaṃkīrṇasvabhāvatvāt | tena yadi mṛtpiṇḍasya mṛdātmatāyāṃ vyāpāraḥ kulālasya tatsaṃsthānaviśeṣe kathyate, tadā tayotyantabhedāt kāraṇānekatvāt kāryānekatvaṃ prāptamiti | siddhāntavādyāha- "uktamatra" iti | mṛtsaṃsthānayoḥ svabhāvabhede dūṣaṇamuktam "mṛtsaṃsthānayoraparasparātmatayā" (

children.text: ) ityādikamiti na saṃsthānasya mṛddravyādanyatvam | tato mṛtpiṇḍopādānāhitātiśayena tatkāryakṣaṇasahakāriṇā kulālena tadupādānopakṛtātmanā tatkāryakṣaṇasahakāriṇā mṛtpiṇḍena ca pratyekaṃ sakalameva mṛtsaṃsthānātmakaṃ kāryaṃ kriyata iti na kāraṇānekatve 'pyanekatvamasya | atraivopacayahetumāha- "api ca" ityādi | yat tad ghaṭagataṃ saṃsthānaṃ "yadi tata" mṛdo "bhinnaṃ syāt" tadā kulālaḥ pṛthageva kimiti na karoti? | nahi bhinnānāmāvaśyakamapṛthakkaraṇam, kulālaścānvayavyatirekābhyāṃ tasya saṃsthānasya guṇātmanaḥ kāraṇatayā gamyata iti "sa pṛthagapi" tat "kuryāt" | para āha- "gunasyetyādi | "dravyāśrayya'guṇavān saṃyogavibhāgeṣvakāraṇamanapekṣa" iti guṇalakṣaṇāt sarvadā guṇo dravyaparatantraḥ, sa kathaṃ kadācit pṛthak kriyeta? | vaiśeṣika eva bauddhīyaṃ codyamāśaṅkayāha- "tatsaṃsthāna" ityādi | yadi svabhāvenaiva tasya guṇātmanaḥ saṃsthānasya "kriyāvad guṇavad" ityādivacanādādhārasvabhāvaṃ tat mṛddravyaṃ, saṃsthānaṃ vā tathāvidhaṃ kapālādheyātmakaṃ tadā kimiti kulālavyāpāramapekṣate? | svata eva kiṃ na bhavati? iti codakābhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) and so forth — therefore configuration is not different from the substance, clay. Hence, by the potter, who is a cooperating cause of that effect-moment, endowed with the special capacity imparted by the clay-lump as material cause, and by the clay-lump itself, which is a cooperating cause of that effect-moment with a nature assisted by that material cause — by each of them individually, the entire effect consisting of clay-and-configuration is produced. Therefore, even though the causes are many, the effect is not many. Here he states the reason for the accumulation: "Moreover" and so forth. If that configuration present in the pot "were different from that" — from clay — then why does the potter not make it separately? For there is no necessity that different things cannot be produced separately, and the potter is understood through positive and negative concomitance as the cause of that configuration having the nature of a quality — so "he would produce" that "separately too." The opponent says: "Of a quality" and so forth. Since a quality is always dependent on substance — by the definition 'a quality resides in substance, is non-qualitied, and is not a cause in conjunctions and disjunctions, being independent' — how could it ever be produced separately? The <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> himself, anticipating the Buddhist objection, says: "Its configuration" and so forth. If by its very nature the configuration, being of the nature of a quality, and the substance of clay, being of the nature of a substrate, [are related] by the statement 'possessing action, possessing quality' etc., or if the configuration is of such a kind as to consist in what is placed upon potsherds — then why does it require the potter's operation? Why does it not arise of its own accord? — this is the intention of the objector.

body.translated_text: Anticipating the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> position here, he says: "Something else" and so forth. "Configuration" (<s>saṃsthāna</s>) refers to the arrangement of parts. And that, being of the nature of conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), is a quality (<s>guṇa</s>). "Therefore" — its difference from the substance, clay, is due to the unmixed natures of substance and quality. Hence, if the potter's operation is described as being upon the clay-substance in its clay-nature and upon the particular configuration, then since those two are entirely different, and since the causes are many, the effects too should be many. The proponent of the established position says: "It has been stated here." The refutation of the difference in nature of clay and configuration has been stated — "because clay and configuration are not of each other's nature" (

body.text: evaṃ codyamāśaṅkaya vaiśeṣikaḥ parihāramāha- "na, tataḥ" ityādi | yat tat mṛddravyaṃ pṛthubudhnodarādyākāraṃ ca saṃsthānaṃ tayoryaḥ sambandha ādhārādheyalakṣaṇaḥ tatra yā "yogyatā" tāṃ "dvayamapyetat kulālād" yataḥ pratilabhate tasmāt "kulālamapekṣate" kulālānapekṣāyāṃ doṣamāha- "anyathā" yadi tayoḥ parasparasambandhayogyatāyāṃ kulālāpekṣā na syāt tadā svabhāvata eva mṛtpiṇḍasya tathavidhasaṃsthānasambandhayogyatvaṃ bhavet | tasmiṃśca sati vastuna eva tatsaṃsthānasambandhayogyatālakṣaṇā dharmatāstīti kulālasannidheḥ prāgapi saṃsthānaviśeṣeṇa sambandhaḥ syāditi vaiśeṣikīyaścodyaparihāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Anticipating this objection, the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> states the reply: "No, because of that" and so forth. The clay-substance and the configuration with its form of wide-bottom-belly etc. — the relation between them characterized as substrate and superstratum — the "suitability" for that — "both of these obtain" that [suitability] "from the potter," and "therefore it requires the potter." He states the defect if the potter were not required: "Otherwise" — if there were no dependence on the potter for the suitability of their mutual relation — then the clay-lump would have by its very nature the suitability for the relation with such a configuration. And if that were the case, since the entity itself would have the property characterized as suitability for the relation with that configuration, even before the proximity of the potter there would be a relation with the particular configuration. This is the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> reply to the objection.

body.text: 31. dravyaguṇayorabhedasyopapādanam |
body.translated_text: 31. Establishing the non-difference of substance and quality.

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "evam" ityādi | yadi parasparasambandhayogyatāyāṃ kulālamapekṣate "evaṃ tarhi sā yogyatā mṛddravyasya kulālād bhavati iti" āpannam | na ca "anayoḥ" mṛddravyayogyatayoḥ svabhāvasya "bhedaḥ" nānātvam | yadi hi syāt tadā yogyatāyāḥ dravyāt pṛthakkaraṇaṃ "prāgvat prasajyeta" | atha yogyatāyā api yogyapāratantryādapṛthaksiddhiṃ brūyāt tadā tasyā api vastudharmatayaiva prāgapi samāveśo mā bhūditi dravyeṇa saha sambandhayogyatāyā anya yogyatā kulālād bhavatītyeṣṭavyā | sāpi pṛthakkaraṇaprasaṅgā[t] dravyād bhinnasvabhāvā nopagantavyā | pṛthakkaraṇaprasaṅge vā punaḥ sa eva parihāraḥ tadīyaḥ, punastadevottaram, ityanavasthāprasaṅgādavaśyāmabhinnasvabhāvatā kapālātmakamṛddravyayogyatayorabhyupagantavyā | kimevaṃ sati siddhaṃ bhavati? ityata āha- "asti tāvat" ityādi | mṛtpiṇḍakulālabhyāṃ kapāladravyasya saṃyogaviśeṣasambandhayogyasyārambhāt yadaikasvabhāvatve 'pyekasyānekapratyayopādheyaviśeṣatā tadā siddhaḥ āsmākīnaḥ pakṣaḥ | tataśca kimasmākaṃ mṛtsaṃsthānayorekasvabhāvatvasādhanāya atinirbbandhanena? | yadi yogyatāmapyāśrityānekapratyayajanyatve 'pyekatvāt nānātvaprasaṅgābhāvaḥ sidhyati kāryasya, na kiñcid dravyagunavādanirākaraṇeneha prayojanam, anyatraiva tannirākaraṇasya kṛtatvādityabhiprāyaḥ | nirbandhagrahaṇena ca mṛtsaṃsthānayoraparasparātmatayā saṃsthānamṛtsvabhāvaviśeṣābhyāṃ tayorapratibhāsanaprasaṅgāt ityanayopapattyā sādhitamevānayorekatvam, yuktyantarāṇāṃ sambhave 'pi tadabhidhānalakṣaṇo nirbbandho na kriyate, prakṛtasiddheranyathāpi bhāvādityācaṣṭe |
body.translated_text: The proponent of the established position says: "Thus" and so forth. If it requires the potter for the suitability of mutual relation, "then it follows that the suitability of the clay-substance comes from the potter." And there is no "difference" — no plurality — "of the essential nature of these two" — the clay-substance and the suitability. For if there were, "the separate production of the suitability from the substance would follow as before." If one were to say that the suitability too, because of the dependence of what is suitable, is established as inseparable [from substance] — then, for that [suitability] too, since it would be included even earlier as a property of the real entity, another suitability for the relation of the suitability with the substance must be accepted as coming from the potter. That too, due to the consequence of separate production, should not be accepted as having a different nature from the substance. Or if separate production is [again] consequent, the same reply of theirs [applies], and then the same response [from us], and thus, due to the consequence of infinite regress, the non-difference of nature of the potsherd-natured clay-substance and the suitability must necessarily be accepted. What is established when this is the case? To this he says: "There is indeed" and so forth. Since the potsherd-substance, suitable for the relation of a particular conjunction, is produced from the clay-lump and the potter — when even with a single essential nature, a single thing has distinctions contributed by multiple conditions — then our position is established. And therefore, what need is there for excessive insistence on proving the single essential nature of clay and configuration? If through the suitability too, even though produced from multiple conditions, there is no consequence of plurality because of unity — then there is no purpose here in refuting the substance-quality doctrine, since its refutation has been accomplished elsewhere. This is the intent. And by the word 'insistence,' [he indicates that] since the unity of clay and configuration has already been established by the reasoning that they are not of each other's nature and that the specific features of configuration and clay-nature would not appear [if they were different] — even though other arguments are possible, the insistence of stating them is not made, since the point at hand is established by other means as well.

body.text: 32. sāmagrībhede kāryabhedasya kāraṇabhede 'pi ca kāryasyaikyasyopasaṃhāraḥ |
body.translated_text: 32. Summary: difference of the effect from what is produced by a different aggregate, and unity of the effect even when the causes are multiple.

body.text: tadevaṃ sāmagrībhedāt sāmagryantarajanyebhyo bhedaḥ sahakāriṇāmanekatve 'pi ca kāryasyaikatvamaviruddhamiti pratipādya (

children.text: ) upasaṃharannāha- "tena sahakāriṇa" ityādi | yena- pratyayāntarapracaye tadvikalasāmagryāḥ sāmagryantaraṃ sampadyate, tacca pūrvasāmagrījanyād bhinnaṃ kāryāntarameva janayati ; ekasāmagrīvyapadeśaviṣayāṇāṃ ca sahakāriṇāmanekatve 'pyanekasyaikakriyavirodhābhāvāt tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhāyinaśca kāryasyaikasya darśanāt svabhāvata ekatvaṃ sādhitam- tena kāraṇena sahakaraṇaśīlā ekasāmagryantargatāḥ pratyayāḥ sāmagryantaraiḥ saha "naikopayogaviṣayāḥ" eka upayogasya viṣayo yeṣāṃ te na bhavanti, sāmagryantaraireva saha bhinnopayogaviṣayatvasya nyāyabalāt pratīteḥ | anena yat prāg vikalpitaṃ ‘yadi kāraṇaśabdena sāmagrī bhaṇyate tadā tadbhedādastyevātatsāmagrījanyebhyaḥ kāryasya bheda iuti kimucyate- na kāraṇabhedād bhedaḥ syāt'; iti etadudā haraṇopadarśitaṃ nigamitam | atha kāraṇaśabdena sāmagrīvyapadeśaviṣayāḥ sahakāriṇa ucyante tadā tadbhedādanekatvalakṣaṇāt kāryasyānekatvalakṣaṇo bhedo neṣyata eva, anekasyaikakriyāvirodhābhāvāt, ekasyānekata utpattidarśanācceti mṛtsaṃsthānayorekātmakatopadarśitaṃ nigamayati- ‘kāryasvabhāvasya'; mṛtsaṃsthānātmana ‘ekatve 'pi'; nānātvābhāve 'pi ‘vastutaḥ'; paramārthataḥ kalpanābuddhau mṛtsaṃsthānayorbhinnayoriva pratibhāsane 'pīti |
children.translated_text: ) Summarizing, he says: "By that cooperative cause" and so on. By which — through the accumulation of additional conditions — from an aggregate lacking that [condition], another aggregate comes into being, and that [new aggregate] produces an entirely different effect from what was produced by the prior aggregate; and although the <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes) that are the referents of the designation of a single aggregate are many, since there is no contradiction in many [causes] performing a single action, and since a single effect that follows the positive and negative concomitance of those [causes] is observed, their unity has been established by nature — by that reasoning, the conditions that habitually cooperate, being included within a single aggregate, are "not the objects of a single application" together with other aggregates — that is, those for whom one application is the object, they are not such [with respect to other aggregates], since it is understood by the force of reasoning that they have different applications only with respect to different aggregates. By this, what was previously hypothesized — 'if by the word cause the aggregate is meant, then from its difference there is indeed a difference of the effect from those not produced by that aggregate, so why is it said that there would be no difference from the difference of causes?' — this has been concluded as demonstrated through the example. Now, if by the word cause the <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes) that are the referents of the aggregate designation are meant, then from their difference characterized by multiplicity, a difference characterized by multiplicity of the effect is not accepted at all, because there is no contradiction in many [causes] performing a single action, and because the production of one [effect] from many [causes] is observed — this he concludes as demonstrated through showing the unity of clay and configuration: 'of the nature of the effect'; of the nature of clay-and-configuration, 'even when there is unity'; even when there is no multiplicity, 'in reality'; in the ultimate sense, even though in conceptual cognition clay and configuration appear as if different.

body.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated that there is difference from what is produced by a different aggregate, and that the unity of the effect is not contradicted even when the auxiliary causes are many, (

body.text: evam udāharaṇe sāmagrībhedāt kāryāṇāṃ bhedo naikasāmagrīviṣayapratyayabhedādanekatvaṃ kāryasyeti pratipādya prakṛte cakṣurādau yojayannāha- "yathā iho" dāharaṇe "kāraṇabhedaḥ" sāmagrībhedaḥ kulālavikalamṛtpiṇḍatatsahitasūtrādhikasāmagrītritayalakṣaṇo ‘bhinneṣu'; nānāsvabhāveṣu ‘viśeṣeṣu'; iṣṭakādicakrāvibhaktaghaṭatadvibhaktaghaṭalakṣaṇeṣūpayogā "nnaikakāryaḥ" kintu bhinnakārya eva, "tathā" tenaiva prakāreṇa cakṣurādibhyo vijñānasyotpattau sāmagryantarāt sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇabhedo 'nekakārya ityunneyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated in the example that the effects differ from the difference of aggregates, and that there is no multiplicity of the effect from the difference of conditions within a single aggregate, applying this to the case at hand — visual cognition and the like — he says: "Just as here" in the example, "the difference of causes" — the difference of aggregates, characterized by three aggregates: a lump of clay without a potter, that combined with a thread, and one with additional [factors] — has "application in distinct" — in those of different natures — "particulars" — characterized by bricks and the like, an undivided pot on a wheel, and a divided pot — "not as a single effect" but rather as different effects indeed, "likewise" in exactly the same manner, in the production of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) from the eye and the like, the difference of causes characterized as the difference of aggregates from another aggregate is to be inferred as producing multiple effects.

body.text: etadeva vibhajannāha- "tathāhi" ityādi | yā cakṣūrūparahitā samanantarapratyayākhyāvijñānalakṣaṇā pratyayāntarasāpekṣā sāmagrī, tato vijñānasya vikalpakasyetarasya vā tadupādeyatvena yā bodharūpatopalabdhā sā cakṣurvijñānasyāpi bhavati | "tasyaiva" cakṣurvijñānasya | kīdṛśasya? | "upalambhātmanaḥ sato bhavataḥ" jāyamānasya tadaiva tadekakāryapratiniyatasya cakṣurindriyasya sannidhānāt samanantarapratyayopādānopakṛtāt tato "rūpagrahaṇapratiniyamo" rūpākāratāpratiniyamaḥ, śabdādyākāravivekavata evaṃ (va) kāryasya cakṣuḥsahitasamanantarapratyayasāmagryāḥ janakatvād | "viṣayād" viṣayādhikāt samanantarapratyayādindriyācca "tena" viṣayeṇa "tulyarūpatā" na kevalaiva rūpapratibhāsitā bhrāntavijñānasyeveti viṣayendriyamanaskāralakṣaṇasāmagrīkāryamevaṃ pradarśitam | tadanyadekadvayajanyaṃ tu kāryaṃ svayambhūhyam | atrābhinnatve 'pi vastutaḥ "kāryasya" cakṣurvijñānalakṣaṇasya "kāraṇānāṃ" viṣāyendriyamanaskārāṇāṃ bhinnebhyaḥ svabhāvebhyaḥ kevalānāmeṣāṃ yaḥ svabhāvastato bhinnā evātajjanyebhyo vidhiśe (nyebhyo 'pi viśe)ṣā bodharūpatādilakṣaṇā "bhavanti" | atajjanyāpekṣayā caikātmakā api bahutvena nirdiṣṭāḥ | yata evam "iti" tasmāt na kāraṇabhede 'pi | yathaikasāmagryantargatapratyayabhede 'pyabhedo naivaṃ sāmagrīlakṣaṇakāraṇabhede 'pyabhedaḥ sāmagryantarajanyebhyaḥ "kāryaviśeṣasya" viśiṣṭasya kāryasyeti |
body.translated_text: Elaborating on this very point, he says: "For" and so on. That aggregate which lacks the eye and form, which is characterized by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) called the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> (immediately preceding condition), and which depends on additional conditions — from that, whatever cognition of <s>vijñāna</s>, whether conceptual or otherwise, is apprehended in the form of awareness as being to be grasped by it, that also belongs to visual consciousness. "Of that very" visual consciousness. Of what kind? "Of that which, being of the nature of apprehension, comes into being" — that is, being born — at that very moment, due to the proximity of the visual faculty which is exclusively determined to that single effect, and which is aided by the appropriation of the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> (immediately preceding condition), from that there is "the exclusive determination of the apprehension of form" — the exclusive determination of having the aspect of form, as distinct from the aspects of sound and the like, because the effect is produced by the aggregate of the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> combined with the eye. "From the object" — from what is additional to the object, namely the sense faculty and the <s>samanantarapratyaya</s> — "by that" object — "conformity of form" — not merely the appearance of form as in the case of erroneous consciousness — thus the effect of the aggregate characterized by object, sense faculty, and mental attention has been demonstrated. The effect produced by one or two [of these] alone is to be understood by oneself. Here, even though there is non-difference "of the effect" characterized as visual consciousness "in reality," from the causes — object, sense faculty, and mental attention — from the natures of these taken separately, their particular characteristics — such as being of the nature of awareness and the like — "are" indeed different from [effects] not produced by those [causes]. And in relation to what is not produced by those, even though they are of one nature, they are spoken of as many. Since it is thus, "therefore" even when the causes differ, just as there is no difference [of the effect] even when conditions within a single aggregate differ, so too there is no [difference of the aggregate-characterized] cause-effect; from the difference of aggregates [there is difference] "of the particular effect" — of the distinguished effect — from [effects] produced by other aggregates.

body.text: tena yaducyate- ‘yadi sahakāriṇāṃ bhede 'pyabhinnaṃ kāryaṃ bhavati sāmagrībhede 'pyabhinnamastu, atha sāmagrībhedād bhinnaṃ bhavati sahakāribhedādapi kimiti bhinnaṃ na bhavati viśeṣābhāvāt?'; iti tadapāstaṃ bhavati | tathā hi- parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayāt pratyayaviśeṣādekakāryoddeśenetaretarasantānopakārācca sahakāriṇāṃ pratiniyataśaktināmudayādekaṃ kāryaṃ samājāyate | sāmagryantarasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 112.

children.text: ) tu kāryāntaraprabhavaśaktinibandhanebhyo hetvantarebhyaḥ svabhāvabhedavato bhāvād bhinnakāryaprasūtiriti kuto viśeṣābhāvaḥ? |
children.translated_text: ) — because of the existence of [causes] differing in nature from other causes whose capacities are grounded in the production of a different effect — there is the generation of a different effect. So how can there be an absence of distinguishing features?

body.translated_text: Therefore, what is said — 'if the effect is undifferentiated even when the <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes) differ, let it be undifferentiated even when the aggregate differs; or if it is differentiated due to the difference of aggregates, why is it not differentiated due to the difference of cooperative causes, there being no distinguishing feature?' — that is refuted. For, due to the dependence on the mutual approach and the like of specific conditions, and due to the mutual assistance of [their] continua for the purpose of a single effect, from the arising of cooperative causes possessing exclusively determined capacities, a single effect is produced. But from another aggregate (

body.text: 33. janakatvamevādhāratvaṃ na tu sthāpakatvam |
body.translated_text: 33. Generation itself is the supporting relation, not stabilization.

body.text: nanu ca sarvaṃ kāryaṃ sādhāraṃ yathā upādāyarūpam | taddhi bhūtebhyo jāyamānaṃ tānyevāśrayata iti bhavadbhiriṣyate | tathānyadapi vijñānādikaṃ kāryam | ato 'nenāpi kiñcit kāraṇamāśrayaṇīyam | tasya ca kāraṇasya pūrvaṃ janakatvaṃ paścāt kāryaṃ pratyādhārabhāva eva, na jananam, tatastatsvabhāvasya jananādityanekāntaḥ tadavastha evetyata āha- "ta evaite" ye 'nantaramuktāḥ "kāraṇaśaktibhedāḥ" kāraṇānāṃ śaktiviśeṣāḥ | kīdṛśāḥ? "yathāsvaṃ" yeṣāṃ kāraṇaśaktibhedānāṃ sahakārilakṣaṇānāṃ yadātmīyaṃ sāmagryantarajanyāt prativiśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ tasya janane 'vyavadheyā vyavadhātuṃ pratibandhumaśakyā śaktiryeṣāṃ tadbhāvastayā " avyavadheyaśaktitayā" avaśyaṃ kāryakāriśaktitayā "pratyupasthitāḥ" udyuktāḥ santaḥ "sāmagrīkāryasya" ekapratyayajanitasya kasyacidabhāvāt sarvaṃ sāmagryā eva kāryamiti kṛtvā sāmagrīkāryasya svabhāvasthityāśraya ityucyante | kasmāt punaravyavadheyaśaktitā? "kṣaṇikatvāt" | nahi kṣaṇikasya śaktiḥ pratibanddhuṃ śakyate, svabhāvāntarotpādane yāvatpratibandhako vyāpriyate tāvat kṣaṇikasya svakāryaṃ kṛtvaiva nirodhāt |
body.translated_text: But [one objects:] every effect is dependent, just like <s>upādāyarūpa</s> (derivative form). For that [derivative form], being produced from the <s>bhūtas</s> (elements), rests upon those very [elements] — so you yourselves accept. Likewise, other effects too, such as <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) and the like. Therefore, by this [reasoning] too, some cause must be depended upon. And for that cause, the prior generation is one thing, and afterward the relation of being a support for the effect is something else — not generation — and therefore [the argument that] from [being of] that nature [follows] generation and so on, is inconclusive; [the situation] remains exactly as before. To this he says: "These very" — those just mentioned — "differences in the capacities of causes" — the particular powers of causes. Of what kind? "According to their own" — [those] whose capacity to generate their own particular effect, distinguished from what is produced by another aggregate, cannot be obstructed — that is, cannot be blocked — "with unobstructable capacity" — with the power of necessarily producing the effect — "being ready" — being engaged — they are said to be the support for the natural continuity of "the effect of the aggregate," since in the absence of any [effect] produced by a single condition alone, every effect is indeed the effect of the aggregate. Why is the capacity unobstructable? "Because of momentariness." For the capacity of what is momentary cannot be blocked, since by the time an obstructor engages in producing a different nature, the momentary [entity] has already ceased after producing its own effect.

body.text: kathaṃ punarasamānakālaṃ kāraṇamādhāro yujyate?, ityata āha- "tathā hi" ityādi | yasmāt "tat" vijñānalakṣaṇa kāryaṃ "tebhyaḥ" cakṣurādibhya "samastabhyo" bodharūpatayā tadanyasmāt tadajanyāt "prativiśiṣṭasvabhāvamekaṃ" khaṇḍaśaḥ kāryasyānutpādādekaikasmāt sakalasyaiva bhāvādekaṃ jātam, tasmāt te ādhārā ucyante | nahi janakādanya evopakārakaḥ | na cānupakāraka ādhāraḥ, (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 113.

children.text: ) atiprasaṅgāt | tato bhinnakālasyādhārabhāvo na virudhyate | yadapi bhūtānāmupādāyarūpaṃ pratyāśrayatvamucyate tadapi svadeśasyāsya janakatvameveti na kiñcit prāgjanakaṃ bhūtvā paścāt sthāpakatāmupaiti, yato 'nekāntaḥ syāditi |
children.translated_text: ) because of overextension. Therefore, the support-relation of what is of a different time is not contradicted. And what is said about the elements being the support for <s>upādāyarūpa</s> (derivative form) — that too is nothing but their being the generator of that [form] in that location. Nothing first serves as a generator and then assumes the role of a stabilizer, such that there would be inconclusiveness.

body.translated_text: But how is it appropriate for a cause that is not simultaneous [with its effect] to be its support? To this he says: "For" and so on. Because "that" effect characterized as <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), "from those" — the eye and the like — "from all of them together," possessing the nature of awareness, is "one, with a nature exclusively distinguished from" anything other than that, [anything] not produced by those — since the effect is not produced piecemeal, but since the entire [effect] arises from the complete [set of causes] — it is born as one. Therefore, they are called supports. For there is no benefactor other than the generator. Nor is a non-benefactor a support, (

body.text: 34. atiśayotpādanaṃ na sahakāritvaṃ kintu ekārthakāritvam |
body.translated_text: 34. The production of an enhancement is not cooperative causation; rather, it is the joint production of a single result.

body.text: punaranyathā tatsvabhāvasya jananādityanekāntodbhāvanaṃ parasyāśaṅkyāha- "apratirodhaśaktikeṣu" avidyamānaḥ pratirodhaḥpratibandho yasyāḥ śakteḥ sā yeṣām | apratirodhaśaktikatvaṃ cānantarakāryatvāt | ye hyutpannāḥ kālakṣepeṇa kāryaṃ kurvanti teṣāṃ syādapi śaktipratibandho, na tu ya udayānantarameva kāryaṃ kurvanti | anena kṣaṇakṣayiṇāmupaghātakābhāvamāha | anugrāhakavirahamapyāha- "anādheyaviśeṣeṣu" | taccānādheyaviśeṣatvaṃ "kṣaṇikeṣu" ityanenāha | nahi kṣanikānāṃ viśeṣa ādhātuṃ śakyate, viśeṣādhāyakena tatsahabhāvinā tadanantaraṃ tadutpādanāt | tadā ca tasya nirodhāt | teṣvevaṃvidheṣu "pratyayeṣu parasparaṃ kaḥ sahakārārthaḥ" yena sahakāriṇa ucyante? | nanvanādheyaviśeṣatvenaiva sahakāritvābhāvaḥ pratipādita iti kimarthamidamapratirodhaśaktikeṣviti? | nahi śaktipratirodhakaḥ sahakāri bhaṇyate | satyam | sarvathā tu tatrākiñcitkaratvajñāpanārthametaduktam | śaktipratibandhakāpanayanena copakāritvakalpanāṃ sahakāriṇāṃ nirasyati | tasmādatiśayādhāyinaḥ sahakāriṇo 'sambhavāt kṣaṇikānāṃ svahetumātrapratibaddhameva janakatvam | taccaivaṃvidhaṃ sarvadāsti | na ca kevalā janayantīti tatsvabhāvasya jananādityanekānta eveti manyate |
body.translated_text: Again, the opponent's objection — that from [being of] that nature [follows] generation and so on, hence inconclusiveness — he anticipates and says: "In those whose capacity is unobstructable" — those in whom there is no obstruction, no blocking, of capacity. And the unobstructability of capacity is because [the effect] is produced immediately. For those which, having arisen, produce an effect after a lapse of time — for them there might be an obstruction of capacity; but not for those which produce an effect immediately upon arising. By this he states the absence of destroyers for momentary entities. He also states the absence of enhancers: "In those to which no additional qualification can be imparted." And this impossibility of imparting additional qualification he states "because they are momentary." For no additional qualification can be imparted to momentary entities, since the qualifier that coexists with them produces [its effect] immediately after them. And at that point, the [momentary entity] has ceased. In the case of such conditions, "what is the purpose of cooperative causation among them" — on account of which they are called cooperative causes? Now, [one might say:] the absence of cooperative causation has been established by the very impossibility of imparting additional qualification; so what is the purpose of [saying] "in those whose capacity is unobstructable"? For an obstructor of capacity is not called a cooperative cause. True. But this is said in order to make known, in every way, that they are inefficacious in that regard. And by [showing] the removal of obstructors of capacity, he refutes the supposition of beneficial action on the part of cooperative causes. Therefore, since cooperative causes that impart enhancement are impossible for momentary entities, their generative capacity is exclusively dependent on their own causes alone. And such [generative capacity] of this kind exists always. And [the causes] do not generate alone — hence from [being of] that nature [follows] generation and so on: this is indeed inconclusive, so [the opponent] thinks.

body.text: etat pariharati- "na vai" naiva atiśayotpādanaṃ sahakriyā yatastadabhāvāt sahakāriṇo na syuḥ | kva punaratiśayotpādanaṃ sahakriyā pratyayānāṃ na bhavati? | "sarvatra" | nahi kvacidapi sahabhāvināmatiśyotpādanalakṣaṇā sahakriyā sambhavati | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 114.

children.text: ) kā tarhi sahakriyā? ityāha- "ekārthakaraṇam" ekakāryaniṣpādanaṃ yad "bahūnām" | "apiḥ" sambhāvanāyām | nyāyabalādevaṃvidhāmeva sarvatra sahakriyāṃ sambhāvayāmaḥ, nānyamiti | atrodāharaṇam- "yathā antyasya" anantarāṅkurādikāryasya "kāraṇakalāpasya" pratyayasāmagryā iti |
children.translated_text: ) What then is cooperative action? To this he says: "The joint production of a single result" — the accomplishment of a single effect — that which belongs "to many." The word "<s>api</s>" indicates possibility. By the force of reasoning alone we consider cooperative action to be of just this kind everywhere, and not otherwise. Here the example is: "Of the final" — of the immediately subsequent effect such as a sprout and the like — "causal assemblage" — the aggregate of conditions.

body.translated_text: He resolves this: "Not indeed" — not at all is the production of enhancement cooperative action, such that from its absence cooperative causes would not exist. Where then does the cooperative action of conditions, characterized as the production of enhancement, not occur? "Everywhere" — for nowhere at all is cooperative action characterized as the production of enhancement possible among coexisting [entities]. (

body.text: 35. ekakāryakāritvameva mukhyaṃ sahakāritvamitarattu gauṇam |
body.translated_text: 35. Joint production of a single effect is indeed the primary cooperative causation; the other is merely figurative.

body.text: syādetat- aupacārikametat sahakāritvam, atiśayotpādanameva tu mukhyam ityat āha- "tadeva" ekakāryakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ "mukhyaṃ sahakāritvam" nātiśayotpādanalakṣaṇam, tasyaiva gauṇatvāt | etaccottaratra vakṣyate | kuta etat? ityāha- "tasyaiva antyasya" vivakṣitakāryaṃ prati "kāraṇatvāt" | kāraṇasya ca sahakārivyapadeśaḥ nākāraṇasya | yataḥ saha- yugapat kurvantaḥ sahakāriṇa ucyante, antyaśca kāraṇakalāpa evaṃvidha iti | yathā cāntyasyaikārthakaraṇaṃ sahakāritvam evaṃ pūrvasyāpi kāraṇakalāpasyottarottaraviśiṣṭakṣaṇāntarārambhiṇa ityavaseyam, antyasyodāharaṇatayā nirddeśāt | tasmāt sarvaṃ kāryamaṅkurādikaṃ viśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vānekapratyayajanyamiti | sarvatraikārthakriyaiva copacīyamānāpacīyamānakāryakāriṇaḥ kāraṇakalāpasya sahakāritvam, na viśeṣotpādanamiti |
body.translated_text: One might say: this cooperative causation [defined as joint production] is merely figurative, while the production of enhancement is the primary [meaning]. To this he says: "That very" — characterized as the joint production of a single effect — is "the primary cooperative causation," not that characterized as the production of enhancement, since that [latter] is itself figurative. And this will be explained later. Whence is this? He says: "Because of the causality of that very final" [causal assemblage] with respect to the intended effect. And the designation 'cooperative cause' belongs to what is a cause, not to what is not a cause. Since those that act together — simultaneously — are called cooperative causes, and the final causal assemblage is of just this kind. And just as the joint production of a single result is the cooperative causation of the final [assemblage], so too it should be understood for the prior causal assemblage that initiates successively distinguished moments — since [the prior assemblage] is indicated as exemplified by the final one. Therefore, every effect — sprouts and the like — or [effects] characterized by particularity, is produced from multiple conditions. And everywhere, the cooperative causation of the causal assemblage that produces effects, whether increasing or decreasing, is just the joint production of a single result, not the production of a special feature.

body.text: syādetat- ekārthakaraṇamapi tatra sahakāritvamastu atiśayotpādanalakṣaṇamapītyata āha- "tatra ca" kṣaṇe 'ntye "viśeṣasya kartumaśakyatvāt" nātiśayotpādanamapi sahakāritvam | kuto viśeṣasya kartumaśakyatvam? ityata āha- "ekasya" anaṃśasya "svabhāvasyāvivekāt | na hi tatra ‘ayamanāhitātiśayo bhāgaḥ svahetubhyo jātaḥ, ayaṃ tu sahakāribhirāhitātiśayaḥ'; iti viveko 'sti | yadi nāmavivekaḥ, viśeṣastu kimiti na kriyate? ityata āha- "svabhāvāntarotpattilakṣaṇatvād viśeṣotpatteḥ", nirbhāge ca kutaḥ svabhāvāntarasya vyavasthā? |
body.translated_text: One might say: let there be cooperative causation in the form of joint production of a single result there, but also [cooperative causation] characterized as the production of enhancement. To this he says: "And there" — in the final moment — "because of the impossibility of producing a special feature" — the production of enhancement is also not cooperative causation. Whence the impossibility of producing a special feature? To this he says: "Because of the indivisibility of a single nature" — of what is without parts. For there [in the effect], there is no distinction such that 'this portion has arisen from its own causes without enhancement imparted, while this [portion] has enhancement imparted by cooperative causes.' If there is no [such] distinction, why then is the special feature not produced? To this he says: "Because the production of a special feature consists in the production of a different nature," and in what is without parts, how can there be the establishment of a different nature?

body.text: syānmatam- bhinnasvabhāva evāntyasya viśeṣo 'stu ityata āha- "bhavāntara"- ityādi | yadi bhāvāntaralakṣaṇo viśeṣo (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 115.

children.text: ) bhavet tadā tasyāntyatvameva hīyeta | hīyenāṃ (hīyatāṃ) ko doṣaḥ? iti cet; "tataśca" anantyatvāt "na sākṣāt kāraṇaṃ syāt" | yata evaṃ "tasmānna kāraṇasya" mukhyasya "sahakāribhyaḥ" sakāśād "viśeṣasyotpattiḥ" ityekārthakriyaiva sahakāritvamiti |
children.translated_text: ) then its very finality would be lost. Let it be lost — what is the fault? "And from that" — from [its] non-finality — "it would not be a direct cause." Since it is thus, "therefore there is no production of a special feature for the cause" — the primary [cause] — "from the cooperative causes." Thus, the joint production of a single result alone is cooperative causation.

body.translated_text: One might think: let the special feature of the final [moment] be of an entirely different nature. To this he says: "A different entity" and so on. If the special feature were characterized as a different entity, (

body.text: nanvasatyāṃ sahakāribhyo viśeṣotpattau kāryajanane sāmarthyameṣāṃ na yujyata ityata āha- "te samarthāḥ" ityādi | yadi hi te svabhāvenāsamarthā utpadyeran tadaiṣāṃ sahakāribhyaḥ sāmarthyotpattirabhyupagamyeta | yāvatā "te 'ntyāḥ svabhāvenaiva samarthāḥ pratyayāḥ sahitā jāyante" kṣaṇamātravilambino | "yeṣā"mekakṣaṇaniyatatvāt tataḥ "prākpaścātpṛthaktvabhāvo nāsti | yebhyaścānantarameva kāryamutpadyate" na kālāntareṇa "tatra" teṣvevaṃvidheṣu "ekārthakriyaiva sahakāritvam" nātiśayotpādanalakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: [The opponent thinks:] 'When there is no arising of a special [capacity] from the auxiliary causes, the capacity of these [causes] for producing the effect is not justified.' In response to this, he says: "They are capable" and so forth. For if they were produced as incapable by their own nature, then the arising of their capability from auxiliary causes would have to be accepted. However, "those final <s>pratyayas</s> (conditions) are capable by their very nature, and they arise together" — they are delayed only by a single moment. "Since these" are determined to a single moment, "there is no" prior, subsequent, or separate "existence" apart from that. "And from which the effect arises immediately" — not after another time — "in their case," for those of such a nature, "a single <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) alone constitutes <s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperating-cause-hood)," not one characterized by producing an additional capacity.

body.text: svabhāvataḥ sāmarthyasya bhāvavirodhāt, parasparataścānabhyupagamāt samarthasya janmaivāyuktamiti manvānaḥ paraḥ āha- "samarthaḥ kutaḥ" ityādi | siddhāntavādyāha- "svakāraṇebhyaḥ" iti | paramatāpekṣayā tu svabhāvata ityuktam | paro hyatyantasya (hyutpannasya) kāraṇasya sahakāribhyaḥ sāmarthyamicchatīti tanniṣedhaparaṃ svabhāvata iti vacanam | na tu svabhāvataḥ kiñcijjāyate, tasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: The opponent, thinking that the very birth of something capable is unjustified — because capability by nature contradicts [momentary] existence, and because capability [arising] from each other is not accepted — says: "Whence capable?" and so forth. The proponent of the established position says: "From their own causes." But the expression 'by nature' is said with reference to the opponent's position. For the opponent desires that the capability of a cause arises from auxiliary causes after it has been completely [produced]. The statement 'by nature' is intended to negate that. But nothing arises from its own nature [alone], because the absurd consequence of being without a cause would follow.

body.text: 36. kṣaṇikeṣvekārthakriyāniyamasya vyavasthāpanam |
body.translated_text: 36. Establishing the restriction of single <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) among momentary entities.

body.text: ekārthakriyāniyama eva kṣaṇikānāmayuktaḥ, kevalānāmapyaṃtyakṣaṇasarūpāṇāṃ darśanāt | tathāhi- ‘idamevaṃrūpaṃ naiva ca'; iti darśanādarśanābhyāṃ vibhajyate | tatra yādṛśaḥ kṣityādayastadanyapratyayasannidhāvupalabhyante tādṛśā eva kevalā api | tatastadanyasahitā iva kevalā api samarthamaṅkurajanane svaṃ svaṃ kṣaṇāntaramārabheran | tataḥ kevalasyāpyaṅkurādijananasvābhāvyādajananācca ‘tatsvabhāvasya jananāt'ityanekānta eveti manyamānaḥ para (

children.text: ) āha- "tāni" svakāraṇāni kṣitibījādīni "enaṃ" samartham "aparasya" anyasya pratyayasya "sannidhāna eva kiṃ" kasmāt "janayanti"? na kevalāni?, sahitānāmeva sarvadā sambhavāt iti cet āha- "kadācit" kasmiṃścit kāle "anyathāpi" kevalā api "syuḥ" bhaveyuḥ | tathā hi- dṛśyanta evādhyātmikabāhyāḥ kvacit kārye yādṛśā yatsahitāḥ tādṛśā eva tadrahitā apīti | janayantu kevalā api sambhavantaḥ samartham, ko doṣaḥ? iti cedāha- "tataśca" kevalānāmapi samarthajanakānāṃ sambhavāt "eko 'pi" na kevalamanekaḥ "kvaci" ddeśādau samarthaḥ utpannaḥ kṣitibījādoiraṅkurādikāryaṃ "janayet" yadi tatsvabhāvasyāvaśyaṃ janakatvam | na ca kevalo janayati tatsvabhāvasambhave 'pi tato 'nekāntaḥ iti paraḥ |
children.translated_text: ) says: "Those" — the own causes such as earth and seed — "this" capable [entity] — "in the proximity of another" condition — "why do they produce" [the effect]? Why not when alone? If [you say] because those accompanied [by auxiliaries] always exist — he says: "Sometimes" — at some time — "they may be otherwise too" — even alone. For indeed, internal and external [causes] are seen: in some effect, those that are of such a kind when accompanied by certain [auxiliaries] are exactly of such a kind even when devoid of them. Let even those that are alone produce the capable [effect], since they can exist — what is the fault? To this he says: "And consequently" — since even those that are alone can be capable producers — "even one alone" — not only many — "somewhere" in a particular place etc., having arisen capable, the earth-seed etc. "would produce" the effect such as a sprout, if what is of that nature necessarily produces. But [something] alone does not produce, even when that nature is present — therefore <s>anekānta</s> (inconclusiveness). This is the opponent's [position].

body.translated_text: The very restriction of a single <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) is unjustified for momentary entities, since even those that are alone are seen to be of the same form as the final moment. For indeed, 'this has such a form and not otherwise' — [a thing] is distinguished by being observed and not observed. In that case, just as earth-elements etc. are perceived in the proximity of other conditions of such a kind, exactly so are they even when alone. Therefore, just as when accompanied by those other [conditions], even when alone they should initiate their own respective subsequent moments, being capable of producing a sprout. Hence, since something of that nature produces and also does not produce [at different times], 'because it is of that nature, it produces' — this is merely an <s>anekānta</s> (inconclusive reason). Thinking thus, the opponent (

body.text: etat pariharannāha- "aparāpara- " ityādi | aparaiścāparaiśca kuśūlatadapanetṛpuruṣaprayatnapiṭakādiprakṣepakṣetranayanaprakiraṇādibhiḥ "pratyayai"ryo "yogaḥ" tena kāraṇena "pratikṣaṇaṃ bhinnaśaktayo" na kadācit pūrvāparakālabhāvina ekaśaktayaḥ aparāparapratyayayogalakṣaṇahetubhede 'pyabhinnaśaktitāyāmahetukatvaprasaṅgāt | anyatrāpi ca śāliyavabījādau śaktibhedasya hetubhedanibandhanatvāt |
body.translated_text: Refuting this, he says: "By successive" and so forth. By "successive conditions" — the granary, the man who removes [grain] from it, the effort, the placing in a basket, bringing to the field, scattering, and so forth — the "conjunction" with these is the reason why [the causes] have "capacities differing at each moment." They never have a single capacity existing across earlier and later times, because if the capacity were undifferentiated despite the difference of causes characterized by conjunction with successive conditions, the absurd consequence of being causeless would follow. And because in other cases too, such as rice, barley, and seeds, the difference of capacity is contingent upon the difference of causes.

body.text: "saṃskārāḥ" sametya sambhūya ca pratyayaiḥ kriyamāṇāḥ "santanvantaḥ" santānena bhavanto "yadyapi kutaścit sāmyād" varṇena saṃsthānena anyena vā kenacitprakāreṇa sādṛśyādekākaraparāmarśapratyayajananalakṣaṇāt samānaṃ rūpameṣāmiti "sarūpāḥ" sadṛśāḥ "pratīyante" pratyabhijñāyante "tathāpi" kṛtrimākṛtrimāṇāmiva maṇimuktādīnāmaparāparapratyayogalakṣaṇasāmagrībhedād "bhinna eva" visadṛśa eva na pratyabhijñānavaśādabhinnaḥ tulyarūpa "eṣāṃ" bījādīnāṃ "svabhāvaḥ" yata evaṃ "tena" bhinnasvabhāvatvena bhinnaśaktitayā vāparāparasāmagrījanyatvena kṣaṇānāṃ siddhyā "kiñcideva" kṣitibījādikaṃ "kasyaci"deva kāryasyāṅkurādestajjananasamarthasya (

children.text: ) vā "kāraṇam" | na sarvaṃ sarvasya | tathā ca vyagrāṇāṃ kṣitibījādīnāmaṅkurajananasvabhāvatā samarthakṣaṇajānanasvabhāvatā vā nāstyeveti tatsvabhāvasya jananādajanakasya cātatsvabhāvatvādityatra nānekāntaḥ yato yo yatsvabhāvaḥ sa svahetorevotpadyamānaḥ tādṛśo bhavati na punastadbhāve hetvantaramapekṣata ityatrānekāntaḥ syāditi | pratyabhijñānasya ca sarūpatāviṣayasya sāmagrībhedādanumitabhinnaśaktisvabhāvatvena bādhyamānatayā prāmāṇyābhāvāt na tataḥ sarūpatāsiddhiḥ kṣaṇakṣayiṇāmiti |
children.translated_text: ), not everything of everything. And thus, earth-seed etc., when occupied [with other functions], do not have the nature of producing a sprout, or the nature of producing a capable moment. Therefore, since what is of that nature produces, and what does not produce is not of that nature — here there is no <s>anekānta</s> (inconclusiveness). For whatever has whatever nature, being produced from its own cause alone, becomes of such a kind — it does not require another cause for that state. The <s>anekānta</s> would apply [only] here [if that were the case]. And since recognition, whose domain is similarity of form, is overridden by the different-capacity-nature inferred from the difference of aggregates, and thus lacks validity — similarity of form is not established from that [recognition] for things that perish every moment.

body.translated_text: "The <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions)," being produced by conditions through combination and accumulation, "continuing" — existing in a continuum — "although" due to some "similarity" — resemblance in color, shape, or some other aspect, which is characterized by producing a cognition that grasps them as one — "they are perceived as having the same form" (<s>sarūpa</s>), that is, they appear similar and are recognized [as the same], "nevertheless," just as artificial and natural gems, pearls, etc. [differ], due to the difference of the aggregate characterized by conjunction with successive conditions, "the nature of these" — of the seeds etc. — "is entirely different," not identical by force of recognition, but dissimilar. Since this is so, "therefore," by virtue of having different natures, different capacities, and being produced by successive aggregates — with the establishment of [distinct] moments — "only something specific" — a particular earth-seed etc. — is the "cause" of "some specific" effect — a sprout etc. — that is capable of producing it (

body.text: pūrvaṃ ca ‘ata evāna(eva ta)yoravasthayorvastubhedo niśceyaḥ ityādinā ekatvaviṣayaṃ pratyabhijñānaṃ nirastam | adhunā tu tulyasvabhāvatāviṣayamiti bhedaḥ | etadapi tatra ‘aparāparotpatteḥ'; ityanenoktameva | vipañcanārthaṃ tu punaḥ iha upanyastam |
body.translated_text: Previously, with the statement 'Therefore the real distinction between those two states must be ascertained' and so forth, recognition whose object is identity was refuted. But now, [recognition] whose object is similarity of nature [is refuted] — this is the difference. This too was already stated there by the [phrase] 'because of successive origination.' But it is presented here again for the purpose of elaboration.

body.text: 37. kṣaṇikeṣu hetuphalabhāvavyavasthāyāḥ kathanam |
body.translated_text: 37. Explaining the determination of the cause-effect relation among momentary entities.

body.text: kiñcideva kasyacit kāraṇam ityuktam tatra kiṃ kasya kāraṇamiti śakyaparicchedamapyādhyātmikeṣu tāvad darśayannāha- "tatra" ityādi | "tatra" teṣu pratikṣaṇaṃ śaktisvabhāveṣu kṣaṇikeṣu bhāveṣu | vyavadhānaṃ- vyavadhīyate yana, tadādiryeṣāṃ atidūrātyāsannatvādīnāṃ te 'vidyamānā yasmin deśe so 'vyavadhānādiḥ deśo yasya so 'vyavadhānādideśaḥ, rūpamindriyaṃ cādī yasya manaskārādeḥ sa rūpendriyādiḥ sa cāsau karaṇakalāpaśca sāmagrīlakṣaṇastathoktaḥ, avyavadhānādideśaścāsau rūpendriyadikāraṇakalāpaśca sa"vijñānajanane samartho hetuḥ" nānyaḥ, tadbhāva eva tasya bhāvāt, anyabhāve 'pi cābhāvāt, etanmātranibandhanatvācca samarthāsamarthavyavasthāyāḥ | "yasteṣā" mindriyādīnāṃ "parasparopasarpaṇasya" anyonyaḍhaukanasya | "ādi" grahaṇād vyavadhānāpanayanā.................................................................................................................... [sā]magryadhīnatvenāsaṃvāditi |
body.translated_text: It was said that only something specific is the cause of something specific. As to what is the cause of what — showing that this is determinable, at least in the case of internal [phenomena], he says: "Among those" and so forth. "Among those" — among entities that are momentary, having the nature of capacity at each moment. "Obstruction" (<s>vyavadhāna</s>) is that by which [something] is obstructed; those that begin with that, such as excessive distance and excessive proximity, are absent in a certain place — that is a place without obstruction etc.; <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>indriya</s> (sense faculty), and so forth belong to <s>manaskāra</s> (attention) etc. — that is what has form-and-sense-faculty etc.; and that is also the causal aggregate (<s>kāraṇakalāpa</s>), which is the defining characteristic of the <s>sāmagrī</s> (aggregate of conditions), and is so called; and the place without obstruction etc. that is also the causal aggregate of form-sense-faculty etc. — that is "the capable cause in the production of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)," and no other, because its existence obtains only when that [aggregate] exists, because it is absent even when something else exists, and because the determination of capable and incapable is contingent upon this alone. "The beginning of their" — of the sense faculties etc. — "mutual approach" — their coming together — the word "etc." includes the removal of obstruction .............................................................................................. [the <s>sāmagrī</s> (aggregate)] being dependent, it accords [with experience].

body.text: imamevaṃvidhaṃ hetuphalabhāvapratiniyamaṃ niravadyamādhyātmikeṣu darśitam anyatrāpyatidiśannāha- "anena nyāyena" ityādi | yo 'yamanantaraṃ hetuphalabhāvapratiniyame nyāya uktaḥ so 'nyatrāpi "sarvatra" draṣṭavyaḥ | sarvatreti vacanāt akṣaṇikeṣvapi pratītirmā bhūt ityāha- "pratikṣaṇam" ityādi | yāḥ kṣaṇe kṣaṇe 'nyāścānyāśca svabhāvabhedānvayinyaḥ śaktayo bhavanti tatrāyamekārthakriyāpratiniyamaḥ sahakāriṇāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ | na tu ye sthiraikasvabhāvā bhāvāḥ paraiḥ kalpyante teṣvapi | sthairyaṃ santānāśrayeṇāpi vyapadiśyetetyekagrahaṇam | kṣaṇe 'pyekatvamastīti sthiragrahaṇam |
body.translated_text: Having shown this faultless determination of the cause-effect relation in internal [phenomena], extending it to other cases as well, he says: "By this principle" and so forth. The principle that has just been stated regarding the determination of the cause-effect relation — that is to be "seen everywhere" in other cases as well. Lest from the word 'everywhere' [one think] the application extends even to non-momentary entities, he says: "At each moment" and so forth. The capacities that are different at each and every moment, following upon the difference of natures — it is with respect to those that this restriction of single <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) of the cooperating causes is to be seen; not with respect to those entities that are imagined by opponents as having a stable, single nature. Even stability may be designated on the basis of a continuum — hence the word 'single.' Even in a moment there is unity — hence the word 'stable.'

body.text: 38. akṣaṇike ekārthakriyākāritvasyābhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: 38. The absence of single-<s>arthakriyā</s>-causation in non-momentary entities.

body.text: kasmāt punaḥ sthiraikasvabhāveṣu neṣyate? ityāha- "svabhāva- " ityādi | kāmaṃ bhāvaḥ svayaṃ na bhavet | na tu svata eva svabhāvasyānyathātvaṃ sambhavati | tataśca sthiraḥ padārtho yadi kāryotpādanasamarthasvabhāvaḥ tato 'syākriyā nopapadyate iti sarvadaiva kuryāt | athāsamarthasvabhāvaḥ | tadāpi kriyānupapannā, sarvadaiva na kuryāditi bhāvaḥ | yattu kadācit karoti kadācinna ityetanna labhyate | tataścākṣaṇikānāṃ tatkāryakriyāsamarthasvabhāvatve sahitāsahitāvasthayorekarūpatvāt kevalānāmapi tatkāryakriyāprasaṅgena kuta ekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvaṃ sambhavet? |
body.translated_text: Why then is it not accepted for entities with a stable, single nature? To this he says: "Nature" and so forth. Granted, an entity may not exist by itself. But the alteration of nature from itself alone is not possible. Consequently, if a permanent thing has a nature capable of producing an effect, then its non-activity is not justified — so it should always act. If, on the other hand, it has a nature incapable [of producing an effect], then too activity is unjustified — it should never act. This is the point. But that it sometimes acts and sometimes does not — this cannot be maintained. Consequently, if non-momentary entities have a nature capable of producing that effect, then since their form is identical in both the accompanied and unaccompanied states, and since even when alone the absurd consequence of producing that effect [would follow], how could <s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperating-cause-hood) characterized by the restriction of single <s>arthakriyā</s> (causal efficacy) be possible?

body.text: atra para āha- "anyasahitaḥ" ityādi | yadyapi kevalasyapyakṣaṇikasya samarthaḥ svabhāvaḥ tathāpi anyasahitaḥ karoti na kevalaḥ | ayamapi hyasya svabhāvaḥ yad- ‘anyasahitena svakāryaṃ kartavyam na samarthasvabhāvenāpi satā kevalena'; iti |
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: "Accompanied by another" and so forth. Although even a non-momentary entity when alone has a capable nature, nevertheless it acts when accompanied by another, not when alone. For this too is its nature — that 'the own effect is to be performed when accompanied by another, not when alone, even though having a capable nature.'

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "kiṃ kevalasya" ityādi | anyasahitenaiva svakāryaṃ kartavyaṃ na kevalena ityetat kevalasyāsamarthasvabhāvatve yujyate nānyatheti manyamānasya praśnaḥ | parastvanavagatābhiprāya āha- "samartha" iti | kevalasyāpyakṣaṇikasya samartha eva svabhāvaḥ (

children.text: ) anyathāsyākṣaṇikataiva hīyeteti | siddhāntavādyāha- "kinna karoti" iti | nahi samarthasyākriyā, sahitasyāvasthāyāmiva yujyata iti sahitasyaiva kriyāmicchatā kevalasyāsamarthasvabhāvataivopagantavyā |
children.translated_text: ) — otherwise its very non-momentariness would be lost. The proponent of the established position says: "Why does it not act?" For the non-activity of what is capable is not justified, just as in the state of being accompanied. Therefore, one who accepts activity only for the accompanied state must accept that the solitary entity has an incapable nature.

body.translated_text: The proponent of the established position says: "Is the solitary one" and so forth. The question is posed by one who thinks that 'the own effect is to be performed only when accompanied by another, not when alone' is justified only if the solitary entity has an incapable nature, not otherwise. But the opponent, not having understood the intention, says: "Capable." Even when alone, the nature of the non-momentary entity is indeed capable (

body.text: atha matam- kevalasya yadi śiraśchidyate tathāpi na karotītyata āha "akurvan" ityādi | kāryānumeyaṃ hi sāmarthyaṃ na ca kevalasya kadācidapi kāryakriyāstīti kathaṃ sāmarthyaṃ kalpyate? | nāyaṃ niyamaḥ yat samarthasvabhāvenāvaśyameva kāryaṃ kartavyam, anyathāpi darśanāt iti manyamāna aha paraḥ- "kuvindādayaḥ" ityādi | siddhāntavādyapahasannāha "krīḍanaśīlaḥ" ityādi | devānāṃpriyaḥ ṛjuḥ mūrkho va sukhasaṃvarddhitatvāt ramaṇasvabhāvaḥ, krīḍanaṃ bāladharmaḥ, tatsādharmyeṇa prajñāvaikalyaṃ darśayati, sukhaidhitatvena śāstreṣvanabhiyogam | yo hyanabhiyukto durbuddhiśca sa "kṛtamapi" vastu vismaraṇaprakṛtitvāt punaḥ punaḥ "kārayatīti" punaḥ pratividhāpayati | kva punaretat prativihitam? ityāha- "tathāhi"- ityādi | ‘bījādivadanekāntaḥ'; ityanena prastāvena nirlloṭhitamevaitat |
body.translated_text: If [the opponent] thinks that even if the solitary entity's head were cut off, it still would not act — to this he says: "Not acting" and so forth. For capability is to be inferred from the effect, and since the solitary entity never at any time has activity producing an effect, how can capability be postulated? The opponent, thinking 'This is not a rule that one with a capable nature must necessarily produce an effect, since otherwise too is observed,' says: "Weavers and others" and so forth. The proponent of the established position, laughing [at this], says: "One of playful disposition" and so forth. A <s>devānāṃpriya</s> (simpleton) — one who is naive, a fool — being nurtured in comfort, is of a pleasure-loving nature; playfulness is a childish trait; by analogy with that, [the author] indicates a deficiency of wisdom, and by being raised in comfort, a lack of application to the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises). For one who is unapplied and dull-witted, being of a nature prone to forgetting, "makes [others] do again" — causes [them] to re-establish — what "has already been done." Where then was this already addressed? To this he says: "For indeed" and so forth. By the introduction 'like seed etc., [there is] <s>anekānta</s> (inconclusiveness),' this very [point] has already been thoroughly examined.

body.text: tadevamakṣaṇikasya samarthasvabhāvatve sahitasyaiva kāryakriyāsvabhāvatvavirodhāt kevalasyākriyānupapanneti pratipādyopasaṃharannāha- "tasmāt tatsvabhāvasya" kāryakriyāsamarthasya "anyathātvāsambhā(mbha)vāt" kadācidasamarthatvābhāvāt "taddharmaṇaḥ" kāryakriyādharmaṇaḥ tathābhāvaḥ kāryakriyā "antyāvasthāvat" sahitāvasthāyāmiva "anivāryaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, having demonstrated that if a non-momentary entity has a capable nature, then the non-activity of the solitary [entity] is unjustified since it contradicts that the accompanied [entity] alone has the nature of causal efficacy, he concludes by saying: "Therefore, since the alteration of what has that nature" — of what is capable of causal efficacy — "is impossible" — since there is no absence of capability at any time — "its property" — the property of causal efficacy — "that state" — causal activity — "is unavoidable, as in the final state" — just as in the accompanied state.

body.text: 39. mīmāṃsakasaṃmatasya bhāvasvabhāvarūpasāmarthyasya nirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: 39. Refutation of the capacity in the form of essential nature of an entity as accepted by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>.

body.text: syānmatam- kevalo 'yamakṣaṇiko 'samartha eva | tataḥ kevalo na karoti, sahitāvasthāyāṃ tvasya sāmarthyaṃ sahakāribhyo jāyate | tataḥ sahita eva karotītyata āha- "antyāvasthāyāṃ sāmarthyotpattau" kīdṛśasya "prāgasamarthasya" sataḥ "tasya sāmarthyasya" yasya tadupajāyate "tatsvabhāvatve" mīmāṃsakādibhiriṣyamāṇe | (

children.text: ) nahi teṣāṃ samarthasya sāmarthyasya ca svabhāvabhedo 'bhimataḥ | kathañcit tadbhede 'pi tatsvabhāvatayaiva pratīyamānatvāditi te manyante | "apūrvotpattireva sā" apūrvasyaiva vastunaḥ sā utpattiryā tatsvabhāvasya sāmarthyasya | nahyekasvabhāvatve sāmarthyamevāpūrvamupajātaṃ na samarthaḥ iti yuktam, tayoḥ svabhāvabhedaprasaṅgāt, viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedalakṣaṇatvāt |
children.translated_text: ) — for they do not accept a difference of essential nature between the capable [entity] and the capability. Even if there were somehow a difference, since it is cognized as being of that [entity's] nature — so they think. "That is the origination of something entirely new" — that origination which is of that-natured capability is indeed the origination of an entirely new entity. For if there is a single essential nature, it is not justified [to say] that only the capability has newly arisen but not the capable [entity], because the absurd consequence of a difference in their natures would follow, since the superimposition of contradictory properties is the defining characteristic of difference.

body.translated_text: One might think: this solitary non-momentary entity is indeed incapable. Therefore, when alone it does not act, but in the accompanied state, its capability arises from the auxiliary causes. Therefore, it acts only when accompanied. In response to this, he says: "When capability arises in the final state" — of such a kind that is "previously incapable" — "that capability" which arises — "if it is of that [entity's] own nature" — as maintained by <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s> and others (

body.text: nanu pratīyamāne eva sāmarthyatadvatorutpattyanutpattī ekasvabhāvatā ca kathaṃ ninhotuṃ śakyate? iti cet | na | apramāṇena pratīteḥ, anyathā pratītyanusāriṇā bhavatā dvicandrādayo 'pi na ninhotavyāḥ | bādhakapramāṇasambhavāt te 'panhūyanta iti cet | ihāpi vastuna ekasvabhāvasyotpattyanutpattī parasparaviruddhe bādhike kiṃ neṣyete? | vyavasthitasyaiva vajropalāderddharmiṇaḥ tatsvabhāvaṃ sāmarthyamutpannamiti ca purvāparakālayorapratibhāsamānavivekaḥ kathaṃ pratīyāt? |
body.translated_text: But how can the arising and non-arising of capacity and of what possesses it, and their single essential nature, be denied when they are actually cognized? If one objects thus — no, because that cognition is not based on a valid means of knowledge. Otherwise, you who follow cognition should not deny even double moons and the like. If one says: those are denied because of the possibility of a refuting means of valid knowledge — here too, arising and non-arising, which are mutually contradictory, are refuting cognitions for what has a single essential nature. Are they not accepted as such? And how could the distinction — which does not appear [between] the earlier and later times — be cognized, namely that the capacity, being of that nature, has arisen in the entity that was already established, such as a diamond or stone, as the property-bearer?

body.text: vijñānādikāryasyānutpattiyaugapadyodayaprasaṅgāt cakṣurādisānnidhye prāgasat tat sāmarthyamutpannaṃ kramavacceti niścaya iti cet | yadyevamekākāratayā pūrvāparakālayoradhikṛtaṃ pratyabhijñānamupajāyamānamapūrvasāmarthyapratibhāsaviviktopalādigrāhyapyanumānādarthāpattito vā bādhāmanubhavanna pramāṇamityupagataṃ syāt | tathā, utpattnutpattyorekasvabhāvatāyāṃ virodhāt samarthasyaivāpūrvasyotpattiḥ sadṛśāparabhavagrahakṛtaścārvāgdarśanānāmekatvavibhramo lūnapunarjjāteṣviva keśanakhādiṣviti kiṃ neṣyate? |
body.translated_text: If one says: because of the consequence of non-arising, simultaneity, or arising [at wrong times] of the effect such as cognition, the determination is that the capacity, being absent before the proximity of the eye etc., has arisen [only then] and is sequential — if so, then the recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) that arises as apprehending a single form at earlier and later times, even though it grasps stones etc. that are devoid of the appearance of a novel capacity and are knowable by inference or <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), experiences refutation and thus would be accepted as not being a valid means of knowledge. Likewise, since arising and non-arising are contradictory when they have a single essential nature, [should it not be accepted that] only what is capable and novel arises, and that the error of unity among those with ordinary perception is due to grasping a similar subsequent existence — like hair and nails that are cut and regrow?

body.text: 40. naiyāyikābhimatasya bhāvāsvabhāvarūpasāmarthyasya nirāsaḥ
body.translated_text: 40. Refutation of the <s>Naiyāyika</s>'s accepted capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) that is not of the entity's own nature.

body.text: atha sāmarthyaṃ sahakāripratyayasānnidhyalakṣaṇamevetyatatsvabhāvamiti nāpūrvotpattiprasaṅga iti naiyāyikādayo manyeran atrāha- "atatsvabhāvatve" sāmarthyasyeṣyamāṇe "sa" bījādiḥ padārthaḥ "prāgiva" tadrūpāparityāgāt "paścādapyakāraka eva" | (

children.text: ) kuta? | sāmarthyamityākhyā yasya padārthāntarasya sahakāripratyayasānnidhyalakṣaṇasya sa evātiśaya[śabda]vācya iti naiyāyikairabhyupagamāt | tata eva tadbhāvabhāvitvena kāryotpatteḥ | te 'pi sahakāriṇaḥ pratyayāḥ yadyakṣaṇikāḥ teṣvapyevaṃ prasaṅgo 'nivārita eveti kṣaṇikatevaikārtha[kriyā]pratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvamicchato 'bhyupeyā |
children.translated_text: ) Why? Because the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> accept that the entity designated by the name 'capacity,' which is another entity characterized as the proximity of auxiliary conditions, is what is to be denoted by the word 'special excellence' (<s>atiśaya</s>). Therefore, the production of the effect occurs through the existence of precisely that [auxiliary condition]. If those auxiliary conditions too are non-momentary, the same consequence applies to them as well, inescapably. Therefore, the cooperative causation characterized as restriction to a single causal efficacy must be accepted by one who holds momentariness.

body.translated_text: Now, if the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others think that capacity is merely the proximity of auxiliary conditions and thus is not of its [the cause's] own nature, so there is no consequence of novel arising — to this he says: "If the capacity is accepted as not of its own nature" — then "that" entity such as a seed "is non-productive even afterwards, just as before," since it has not relinquished that form. (

body.text: punarapyakṣaṇikānāmekārthakriyāpratiniyamaṃ nirākartumupacayahetumāha- "api ca" ityādi | yo 'sāvakṣaṇiko bhāvaḥ sakaleṣu sahakāriṣu svakāryaṃ karotītīṣyate, sa tadaiva tāvat kasmāt karoti? | yena hi kāraṇena tatkāryakriyāsvabhāvatvena tadā karoti tene(nai)va sthirasvabhāvatvāt prāgapi kuryāt, tataḥ kuto 'syaikārthakriyāpratiniyamaḥ? iti bhāvaḥ |
