body.translated_text: To state an additional reason for refuting the restriction to a single causal efficacy of non-momentary entities, he says: "Moreover" and so forth. That non-momentary entity which is accepted as producing its own effect when all auxiliary conditions are present — why does it produce [the effect] precisely at that time? For by the very reason that it produces [the effect] at that time through its nature of producing that effect, it should produce it earlier too, since it has a stable nature. So whence is the restriction to a single causal efficacy? — this is the purport.

body.text: "kā cānyā mṛgyate yuktiḥ yathā tad dṛśyate tathā" iti sarvatreyamapratihatā yuktiriti manyamānaḥ kumārilaḥ prāha- "kurvan dṛṣṭaḥ" ityādi | yatastadaiva kāryaṃ kurvam(n) dṛṣṭo mayā "tena darśanabalena karotīti brūmaḥ", kimatrānyayopapattyābhihitayā?, prāk tat kurvanna dṛṣṭaḥ tena na karotītyekārtha[kriyā]pratiniyamaḥ sidhyati akṣaṇikānāmapīti | bhāvo hi kāryaṃ karoti tajjananasvabhāvatayā na darśanabalenādṛṣṭasyāpi svakāryakaraṇāt ato nedamuttaraṃ sambadhyata ityupahasannāha- "aho mahāsamarthyam" ityādi | mahāprabhāvasya bhavato mahasāmarthyaṃ darśanam, yasmādetadbhāvān kāryakaraṇasvabhāvavikalānapi- yadi kāryakaraṇasvabhāvatvād bhāvāḥ kāryaṃ kuryuḥ tadaitadevottaraṃ kiṃ noktam?, yataḥ kāryakaraṇe darśanamuttarīkṛtamiti kṛtvā- "svabhāvamātreṇa" ātmasattāmātreṇa "nānāprakāreṣu vyāpāreṣu niyuṅkte" tat kathaṃ mahāsāmarthyaṃ na syāt? | na cātra me kācidakṣamā kintu "yadi nāma kiñcit" kāraṇaṃ "kathañcid" anādṛtasya vā vyākṣiptasya vā "atra bhavata" iti pūjāvacanam (

children.text: ) "darśanasya viṣayatāmatikrāmet" tadā "hanta" iti dainyodbhāvanametat, aprasavo dharmo 'sya tadidam- "aprasavadharmakaṃ" tato 'petasantānaṃ "syādi"ti iyamasmākaṃ cintā cittaṃ dunoti |
children.translated_text: ) "should transcend the domain of observation," then "alas" — this is an expression of distress — it would be "unproductive" — bereft of its continuum — "this is our worry that torments the mind."

body.translated_text: <s>Kumārila</s>, thinking 'what other reasoning need be sought? It is as it is observed' — this reasoning is undefeated everywhere — says: "It is observed producing" and so forth. Since it is "observed by me producing the effect at that very time, we say on the strength of that observation that it produces [it]." What use is some other reasoning? Before that, it is not observed producing, therefore it does not produce — thus the restriction to a single causal efficacy is established even for non-momentary entities. But an entity produces an effect through its nature of generating it, not through the force of observation, since even what is unseen produces its own effect. Therefore, this answer is not applicable — mocking [<s>Kumārila</s>] thus, he says: "What great power!" and so forth. Great is the power of your observation, possessor of great influence! Because of this existence [of your observation], even things lacking the nature of producing effects — for if entities produce effects through their nature of producing effects, then why was this same answer not given [from the start]? Since observation has been made the answer for effect-production — "by mere essential nature" — by mere self-existence — "[your observation] engages in various operations of diverse kinds." How could it not be of great power? And I have no impatience here, but "if perhaps some" reason "somehow" — whether neglected or distracted — "of your" — this is an honorific expression — (

body.text: para āha- "na vai vayam" ityādi | naiva vayaṃ kāryakaraṇasvabhāvarahitānāṃ "bhāvānāmasmaddarśanavaśāt kāryakriyāṃ brūmaḥ, kintu" svabhāvenaiva te bhāvāḥ tatkāryakaraṇasvabhāvāḥ, tataḥ svakāryaṃ kurvanti | "tān paśyantaḥ kevalaṃ jānīmahe" ta ete kārakasvabhāvā iti | darśanasya hi yathāvasthitavastuvijñāne vyāpāraḥ, nāvidyā(dya)mānasvabhāvakriyāyāmiti |
body.translated_text: The opponent says: "We do not" and so forth. We do not at all say that "entities" lacking the nature of producing effects "produce effects through the force of our observation. Rather," those entities are by their very nature of the nature of producing that effect, and therefore they produce their own effects. "We merely, seeing them, know" — that these are of productive nature. For observation functions in the cognition of things as they are, not in the creation of a non-existent nature.

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "satyam, idamapyasti" | kiṃ vayaṃ nyāyānurāgitayā nyāyyaṃ vacanamupalakṣayāmaḥ, uta bhavāneva sarvadā nyāyyavacanarahito 'pi kathañcinnyāyyamuktavān iti sañjātaparitoṣaḥ pṛcchati- kiṃ tad? ityāha- "svabhāvasteṣāṃ" bhāvānāṃ "kāryakriyādharmā" kāryakaraṇadharmā "tena" kāraṇena "samastāḥ" samagrāḥ pratyayāḥ sahakāriṇo yeṣāṃ teṣāmakṛtvā kāryaṃ "nopekṣāpattiḥ" naudāsīnyapratipattiḥ iti satyam- idamapyasti bhavato nyāyyaṃ vacanamiti, kintu idamasi praṣṭavyaḥ- "sau['kṣepa]kriyādharmā svabhāvaḥ kiṃ teṣāṃ tadaivāntyāvasthāyāṃ" samagrāvasthāyāṃ yadanantaraṃ kāryamutpadyate tadaiva "utpannaḥ? āhosvit prāgapi" parasparavirahāvasthāyāmapi "āsīt"? |
body.translated_text: The proponent of the established position says: "True, this too is [well said]." Are we the ones who, out of fondness for logic, notice a logical statement, or is it you yourself — who is always devoid of logical statements — who has somehow made a logical statement, generating satisfaction? He asks: what is it? He says: "The nature of those" entities "has the property of producing effects." "Therefore" — for that reason — there is no "lapsing into inaction" — no falling into indifference — for those who have "complete" — full — conditions, all auxiliary conditions. True — this too is a logical statement of yours, but you should be asked this: "Is the nature of prompt action (<s>akṣepakriyā</s>) — was it" of those entities "born only then, at the final state" — at the state of completeness, immediately after which the effect arises — "or did it also exist before" — even in the state of mutual separation?

body.text: tatra tadaivotpanne tatsvabhavatve 'pūrvotpattireva, atatsvabhāvatve so 'kāraka eveti prāguktadoṣabhayāt para āha- "āsīt" | kutaḥ? pracyutaśca utpannaśca pracyutotpannaḥ, tasya pratiṣedhaḥ "apracyuto 'nutpa(apracyutotpa)nnaḥ" sthira ekaḥ svabhāvo yeṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ teṣāṃ kasmiṃścit kāle "kasyacit" svabhāvasya tatropalabdhasya "abhāvavirodhāt" | kṣaṇikeṣveva hyekadā dṛṣṭaḥ svabhāvo 'nyadā na bhavet tadā tasyānyatvāt | nāpracyutānutpannapūrvāpararūpeṣu sthireṣu bhāveṣviti |
body.translated_text: There, if it arose only then, and if it is of that nature, there is novel arising [of a new entity]; if it is not of that nature, it remains non-productive — out of fear of these previously stated defects, the opponent says: "It existed." Why? Because entities "whose single stable nature is non-departed and non-arisen" — i.e. not newly arisen and not having departed — "cannot at any time lack" any essential nature that is perceived in them, "because of the contradiction with the absence" [of that nature]. For only in momentary things could a nature seen at one time not exist at another, since it would be different then. Not in stable entities whose earlier and later forms are non-departed and non-arisen.

body.text: atrāha- "tat kimidānīm" ityādi | syānmatam- naivedamanena vākyena sadṛśamasmadvākyamityāha- "ko vāsya" ityādi | yadyetadanena tulya na bhavati tadā sakalasahakāryavasthāyāḥ "prāgapi" ayam "akṣepakriyāsvabhāvaḥ" avilambitakāryakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ "kāryaṃ ca na karotī"tyasya bhāṣitasyārtho vaktavya iti |
body.translated_text: To this he says: "Then what now" and so forth. One might think that this statement of ours is not similar to his. To this he says: "What then of this" and so forth. If this is not equivalent to his [statement], then the meaning of this statement — that "even before" the state of complete auxiliary conditions, this [entity] "has the nature of prompt action" — the nature of undelayed effect-production — "and yet does not produce the effect" — must be explained.

body.text: naiyāyikāstu manyante- bhāvānāṃ sahakārisannidhānāsannidhānāpekṣayā kārakākārakasvabhāvavyavasthā, na svabhāvataḥ, tenāyamapracyutotpannasthiraikasvabhāvatve 'pi na prāgapi svakāryajananasvabhāvaḥ, kintu sannihitasakalasahakāripratyaya eveti | tanmatamāśaṅkamāna āha- "sahitaḥ" ityādi |
body.translated_text: The <s>Naiyāyikas</s> think: The determination of entities as productive and non-productive depends on the presence and absence of auxiliary conditions, not on their own nature. Therefore, even though having a stable, single, non-departed and non-arisen nature, it is not of the nature of producing its own effect before [the auxiliary conditions are present], but only when all auxiliary conditions are present. Anticipating their view, he says: "Together with" and so forth.

body.text: etannirasyati- "anyastarhi" ityādi | yadi nāma sahitasya svakāryajananasvabhāvatā, kevalasya ca tadviparītarūpatā, anyatvaṃ tu kasmādbhavati? ityata āha- "svabhāvabheda" ityādi | "svabhāva bheda eva hi bhāvabhedasya lakṣaṇam" | sa cet tatkāryajanakājanakarūpatayā bhidyate, śāliyavabījādīnāmiva kathamiva bhāvabhedo na syāt? | nahi svabhāvādanyo bhāvaḥ yatastadbhede 'pi na bhidyeta, niḥsvabhāvatāprasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: He refutes this: "Then it is different" and so forth. Even if it is of the nature of producing its own effect when accompanied [by auxiliary conditions], and of the opposite nature when alone — why would there be difference? To this he says: "Difference of nature" and so forth. "For difference of nature is the very definition of difference of entity." And if it differs in the form of being productive and non-productive of that effect — like seeds of rice, barley etc. — how could there not be a difference of entity? For there is no entity other than essential nature such that even when that [nature] differs, [the entity] would not differ — since that would entail being without any nature.

body.text: nanu coktaṃ svato janakājanakasvabhāvatāvirahāt pratyayāntarabhāvādyapekṣatvāt janakājanakarūpatāyāstadbhede 'pi kuto bhāvabhedaprasaṅgaḥ?, tasyāparāpekṣasvabhāvabhedalakṣaṇatvāt ityata āha- "nahi sa sāhitye 'pi" ityādi | tadaitaduttaraṃ bhāvatkaṃ sambadhyeta yadi bhāvo yo 'sau paraḥ sahakāritvābhimataḥ sannidhīyate tadrūpeṇa kartā syāt na svarūpeṇa | na caitadasti, tathābhāve hi paramārthataḥ sa eva paraḥ kartā syāt | tatra tu kartṛtvavyapadeśaḥ kalpanānirmita eva bhavet | na ca kalpanānuvidhāyinyo 'rthakriyāḥ | nahi māṇavako dahanopacārādādhīyate pāke | tataśca nāsyānupakāriṇo bhāvamapekṣeta kāryamiti tadrahitebhya eva (

children.text: ) sahakāribhyo bhavet | yadvā tebhyo 'pi na bhavet | teṣāmapi pararūpeṇa kartṛtve svayamakārakatvāt | tataḥ sarveṣāmevaṃ svayamakārakatve pararūpeṇāpyakārakatvāt sarvathā kārakoccheda eveti na kiñcit kutaścit jāyeta | tasmāt svarūpeṇaiva bhāvaḥ svakāryasya kartā na pararūpeṇeti nāsyottarasyāvakāśaḥ | tato 'nyaḥ sahito 'nyaśca kevalaḥ ityetadavicalameveti |
children.translated_text: ) without it. Or it would not arise even from them, since if they too are productive in the form of another, they themselves are non-productive. Therefore, when all are thus non-productive in themselves, and non-productive in the form of another as well, there is a complete elimination of productive agency in every way, so nothing would arise from anything. Therefore, an entity is the producer of its own effect in its own form alone, not in the form of another — so there is no scope for this answer. Hence, 'the one accompanied is different, and the one alone is different' — this remains unshaken.

body.translated_text: But it has been said that, since there is no nature of being productive or non-productive from its own side, and since the nature of being productive or non-productive depends on other conditions, how can there be the consequence of difference of entity even when that [nature] differs? — since [difference of entity] is defined as difference of nature independent of other things. To this he says: "For even in accompaniment, it is not" and so forth. This answer would be applicable if the entity — the other one accepted as the auxiliary — were the producer in that [other's] form, not in its own form. But this is not the case, for in that event, in ultimate reality, that other one alone would be the producer. And in that case, the designation of agency would be a mere conceptual construction. But causal efficacies do not follow conceptual constructions. For a boy is not employed in cooking through the figurative designation of being a fire. And therefore, the effect would not depend on the existence of a non-contributing entity, and would arise from the auxiliary conditions alone (

body.text: atha yena svarūpeṇāyaṃ janakastadasya sahitāsahitāvasthayoḥ sarvadāsti tadā svarūpaṃ ca svakāryajanakamasya sthirasvabhāvasya prāgapi sahitāvasthāyāstadeva yatsahitāvasthāyāmakṣepakriyāsvabhāvamiti tasmāt na kathaṃcit kāryakriyāvirāmaḥ | athavā kadācit paro brūyāt svahetubhirevāyaṃ pratyayāntarāpekṣaḥ svakāryajananasvabhāvo janita iti kevalo na karoti | na cāsya sahitāsahitāvasthayoḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ, pratyayāntarāpekṣasvakāryajananasvabhāvatāyāḥ sarvadā bhāvāt ityata āha- "nahi sa sāhitye 'pi" ityādi | svarūpeṇaivāsya kartṛtvāt tasya ca prāgapi bhāvāt pratyayāntarāpekṣāyāśca tato labhyasyātmātiśayasyābhāvenāyogāt upakāralakṣaṇatvādasya, anyathātiprasaṅgāt, kevalasya kāryakaraṇamanivāryamiti akurvataḥ kathaṃ sahitāvasthāyā na bhedaḥ syāt? iti bhāvaḥ | pratyayāntarāpekṣasvakāryakaraṇasvabhāva ityapi pararūpeṇākārakasya pratyayāntarasannidhānopalakṣitakāle kārakatvaṃ na prāgityayamarthaḥ | tataśca kadācit kāryakriyāsvabhāvo na sarvadā iti brūvatā kathaṃ sarvadā kāryajananasvabhāvatāsyoktā bhavati? | nanvevaṃ svabhāvabheda evāsya tadatatkālayoḥ samarthitaḥ syāt | tasmānnākṣaṇikānāmekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvamiti sthitam |
body.translated_text: Now, by whatever own form this [entity] is productive, that [form] always belongs to it in both the accompanied and unaccompanied states. Then its own form, being productive of its own effect, existed even before the accompanied state for this entity of stable nature — that very [form] which in the accompanied state has the nature of prompt action. Therefore, there is no cessation of effect-production under any circumstances. Or perhaps the opponent might say: this [entity] has been produced by its own causes as having a nature of producing its own effect only in dependence on other conditions, so when alone it does not produce. And there is no difference of essential nature between its accompanied and unaccompanied states, since the nature of producing its own effect in dependence on other conditions always exists. To this he says: "For even in accompaniment, it is not" and so forth. Since its productivity is in its own form alone, and since that [form] exists even before, and since the dependence on other conditions is impossible — because the self-excellence obtained from them is absent [for a stable entity], because this [cooperative causation] is of the nature of contributing [something new], and because otherwise there would be over-extension — the production of the effect by the one alone is inescapable. So how would there not be difference between its state when not producing [the effect] and the accompanied state? This is the purport. Even the expression 'having a nature of producing its own effect in dependence on other conditions' means that what is non-productive in the form of another is productive at the time marked by the proximity of another condition, not before. And therefore, one who says 'at some time it has the nature of producing effects, not always' — how has he stated that the nature of producing effects always belongs to it? Well, in that case, the difference of essential nature between those times [accompanied and unaccompanied] would itself be established. Therefore, it is established that for non-momentary entities, cooperative causation characterized by restriction to a single causal efficacy is impossible.

children.text: ) eva svabhāvato 'ntyāḥ pratyayāḥ saha jāyante kṣaṇikā yeṣāṃ prākpaścātpṛthagbhāvo nāsti'; ityatra | "sa kathamekakṣaṇabhāvī" ekasminnevāntye kṣaṇe bhavanaśīlaḥ "anyathā bhavet" antyakṣaṇāt prāk paścāt pṛthagvā bhavet? "yaśca" anyathā "bhavati sa" evāntyakṣaṇabhāvī sahakārisantānopakṛtasvabhāvo 'kṣepakriyādharmā "na bhavatīti nāyam" akṣaṇīkapakṣoditaḥ "prasaṅgaḥ" kṣaṇikapakṣe | kutaḥ? | "kārakākārakayoḥ" ityādi | kārako 'ntyaḥ akārakastadanyaḥ tayoryaḥ "svabhāvaḥ" sa bhinno 'pi bhedāvivakṣayaikatvenoktaḥ | tathā kārakasya yo heturupāntyaḥ, akārakasyāpi yo hetustadanyaḥ sa bhinno 'pyabhedavivakṣayaivaikatvenoktaḥ | tena kārakākārakayoryau svabhāvau tayorekatra dharmiṇi virodhāt | tathā tayoḥ svabhāvayorjanakau yau hetū- ekaḥ kārakasvabhāvajanako 'nyaścākārakasvabhāvajanakaḥ- tayorapyekatra dharmiṇi virodhāt, anyatve sati | akārakasvabhāvajanakahetorutpannasyākārakasya svabhāvasyānyatvāt "yaśca bhavati sa eva na bhavatīti nāyaṃ prasaṅga" iti |
children.translated_text: ) that arise together, being capable by their very nature, are momentary, and for them there is no separate existence before, after, or apart' — in this context. "How could that which exists only for a single moment" — having the disposition to exist only in the final moment — "be otherwise" — exist before or after or separately from the final moment? "And one who would be otherwise would not be" the very one existing only in the final moment, of a nature assisted by the continuum of auxiliary conditions and having the property of prompt action — "therefore this consequence" raised against the non-momentary position "does not apply" to the momentary position. Why? "Of the productive and non-productive" and so forth. The productive is the final [moment]; the non-productive is other than that. The "essential nature" of those two — though different, is stated as one through the intention of not emphasizing difference. Likewise, the cause of the productive — the penultimate [moment]; and the cause of the non-productive — what is other than that — though different, is stated as one through the very intention of non-difference. Therefore, of the productive and non-productive, the two essential natures are contradictory in a single property-bearer. Likewise, of the two causes that produce those two essential natures — one producing the productive nature and the other producing the non-productive nature — these too are contradictory in a single property-bearer, since they are different. Because the non-productive essential nature, produced from the cause that generates the non-productive nature, is different [from the productive one] — "therefore, one who exists [as non-productive] is the very one who does not exist [as productive]" — this consequence does not apply.

body.translated_text: 41. Refutation of the view that it is the effect itself that depends on auxiliary conditions.

children.text: ) tadātmanaḥ kāryasya sahitebhya eva bhāvādekārthakriyālakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvamakṣaṇikānāmapyupapadyata iti | siddhāntavādī pūrvadoṣānatikramamasya darśayannāha- "tasyāpi" evaṃvādinaḥ "kathaṃ sa" nityābhimato bhāvaḥ "kevalaḥ karotyeva" ‘akṣepakriyādharmaiva sa tasya svabhāvaḥ'; iti vacanāt | kāryaṃ ca sahitebhya eva bhavati, ‘sāmagrījanyasvabhāvatvāt tasya'; iti vacanāt | tasmāt kevalānna bhavatīti "tadavastho virodho" yaḥ pūrvamuktaḥ | tathāhi- yadyakṣepakriyādharmā tadāvaśyamanena kāryaṃ kartavyam na cedavaśyaṃ karoti kathamakṣepakriyāsvabhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: since the effect of that nature arises only from [causes] combined together, <s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperative causation) characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) would be possible even for non-momentary entities. The proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), showing that this [opponent] has not overcome the previously stated faults, says: "For him too" — the one who speaks thus — "how does that" entity, considered permanent, "alone actually produce [an effect]," since it was stated that 'the property of <s>akṣepakriyā</s> (compelling activity) is its very nature'? And the effect arises only from combined [causes], since it was stated that 'its nature is to be produced by an aggregate.' Therefore, it does not arise from [causes] alone — "the contradiction remains the same" as was stated before. For indeed, if its nature is <s>akṣepakriyā</s> (compelling activity), then it must necessarily produce the effect; and if it does not necessarily produce [it], how can its nature be <s>akṣepakriyā</s>?

body.translated_text: Another [opponent], however, has imagined in a different way that there is no restriction of <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) to collective [causes] alone. He presents that [view], beginning with "He who also thinks" and so on. For the nature of an entity is always the property of <s>akṣepakriyā</s> (compelling activity), and it is not as some say — that the establishment of entities as causal agents depends on the proximity of <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes), not from their own nature. For if they lack causal capacity from their own nature, there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all causal establishment, since causal capacity through another's nature would be impossible. An entity of such a nature never requires companionship in producing its own effect, because otherwise one [entity] accompanied [by others] and another [entity] alone would differ in having the natures of being a cause and not being a cause. If so, then since it always has that nature, why does it not always produce the effect? To this [it is replied]: Because the effect has a nature that depends on other conditions, even though [the cause] is always established as a generator, it does not arise from [that cause] alone. Therefore it is the effect itself that is at fault here, for even though [the cause] is established as a generator when alone, [the effect] still requires other conditions. Therefore,

body.text: akṣepeṇā kāryadarśanādakṣepakriyāsvabhāvatāvagamyate nānyathā iti parābhiprāyāśaṅkayāha- "na kevalaḥ" ityādi | naivaṃ mayoktaṃ kevalaḥ karotyeveti kintvakṣepakriyāsvabhāva iti | atrāha- "kathamidānīm" ityādi | yadi karotyeveti neṣyate kathamakṣepakriyāsvabhāva iti kathyate? | atha tathocyate tathā nanvetadevānena "vacasā paridīpitam" abhihitaṃ bhavati | kiṃ tat? | karotyeveti | sa eva hyakṣepakriyāsvabhāvo yaḥ karotyeva, yastu nāvaśyaṃ karoti sa kathaṃ tadrūpaḥ syat? | yadapyuktaṃ ‘kāryasyaivāyamaparādho yat tasmiṃ (smin) janakatayāvasthite pratyayāntarāṇyapekṣate'; iti tadapyayuktam, yataḥ "kāryaṃ" cāyamakṣaṇiko bhāvaḥ "kevalo 'pi samarthaḥ san paraṃ" pratyayāntaram "apekṣamāṇaṃ kathamupekṣeta?" naiva | anupekṣamāṇena kiṃ kartavyam? | āha- "paraṃ" pratyayāntaram "anādṛtya" tiraskṛtya etat kāryaṃ "prasahya" haṭhāt "kuryāt" | ka evaṃ satyasya guṇo bhavati? iti cet, āha- "evaṃ hi" paramanādṛtya haṭhāt svakāryaṃ "kurvatānena" kevalenāpi samarthena satā yat tadātmanaḥ kevalasyāpi "sāmarthyaṃ" tad "darśitaṃ" prakāśitaṃ bhavati | anyathānyasahitasyaiva karaṇāt kevalasya ca kadācidapyakaraṇāt na ‘ayaṃ kevalo 'pi samarthaḥ'; iti pareṣāṃ buddhiḥ syāt | tato 'yaṃ tiraskṛtaprabhāva iva kathaṃ bhrājeta? | tasmādayuktamucyate kāryaṃ pratyayāntarāpekṣamiti |
body.translated_text: [The opponent] suspects [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>'s] intent to be that <s>akṣepakriyā</s>-nature is understood from the observation of [compelling] activity, and not otherwise. [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] states [the opponent's objection], beginning with "Not alone" and so on: I did not say that [the cause] alone actually produces [the effect], but rather that its nature is <s>akṣepakriyā</s> (compelling activity). To this he replies, beginning with "How then": If it is not accepted that it actually produces [the effect], how is it said that its nature is <s>akṣepakriyā</s>? If it is said thus, then is not precisely this "illuminated by those words" — that is, expressed [by them]? What is that? That it actually produces [the effect]. For that which actually produces [the effect] is indeed of <s>akṣepakriyā</s>-nature, but how could that which does not necessarily produce [it] be of that nature? As for what was said — 'it is the fault of the effect itself that, even though [the cause] is established as a generator, [the effect] requires other conditions' — that too is unjustified, because "the effect" — and this non-momentary entity — "even when alone is capable, how could it disregard [the effect] that requires another" condition? It could not. What should be done by one that does not disregard [it]? He says: Disregarding "another" condition, it should "forcibly" produce this effect "by force." What virtue would there be in this? He says: "For thus," by "this" [entity] which, even when alone, is capable, "producing" its own effect forcibly without regard for another, "its capacity" — even when alone — "would be demonstrated," made manifest. Otherwise, since it only produces [effects] when accompanied by others and never produces when alone, others would not think 'this one is capable even when alone.' Then how would it shine forth, as though its power were obscured? Therefore it is wrong to say that the effect depends on other conditions.

body.text: kāryāpekṣayāpi virodhasya tādavasthyaṃ darśayannāha- "kāryaṃ param" ityādi | kāryasya parāpekṣāṃ brūvan kevalāt kāraṇādanutpattimasya kathayasi, ‘sa kevalo 'pi samarthaḥ'; itīdaṃ vadaṃstataḥ kevalādutpattiṃ kāryasya brūṣe | ete caikasyaiva kāryasya | tat evaikasmāt kāraṇādutpattyanutpattī parasparaviruddhe "kathamekatra" kāryākhye dharmiṇi "syātām?" viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedalakṣaṇatvāt | ekatra te brūvāṇo ‘mātā ca vandhyā ca'; ityanena sadṛśaṃ brūṣa iti na pūrvoktadoṣānmucyase, yata evamapi brūvāṇo viruddhameva brūte na ca lakṣayati "tat" tasmāt "ayam" akṣaṇikavādī kṣaṇikapakṣasyānavadyatayā tadvādināṃ nirddoṣatāsampatsu amarṣalakṣaṇerṣyā eva śalyaṃ antarduḥkhahetutvāt tena vitudyamānāni vyathyamānāni marmāṇi yasya so "'yamīrṣyāśalyavitudyamānamarmā" varāko 'svasthacittatayā viruddhābhidhānamapyalakṣayan "viklavam" ākulaṃ pūrvāparāsambaddhaṃ "vikrośati" viroditi "iti" kṛtvā asvasthacittavacaneṣvanādarāt taddoṣodbhāvanasya sutarāṃ duḥkhotpādanena kṣatakṣāraniṣekatulyatvāt "upekṣāmeva" vipaścitānāṃ (ścitāṃ) kṛpādhanānām "arhatīti" |
body.translated_text: Showing that the contradiction remains the same even from the perspective of the effect, he says, beginning with "The effect, another" and so on. In speaking of the effect's dependence on others, you are saying that it does not arise from the cause alone; in saying 'it is capable even when alone,' you are saying that the effect arises from that [cause] alone. And these [statements concern] one and the same effect. Therefore, arising and non-arising from one and the same cause are mutually contradictory — "how could they obtain in one and the same" entity called the effect? For the superimposition of contradictory properties is the mark of difference [i.e., incoherence]. One who asserts both of these regarding a single [entity] says something comparable to 'she is both a mother and barren.' Therefore you are not freed from the previously stated fault, since even in speaking thus one speaks contradictorily without realizing it. "Therefore this" proponent of non-momentariness, since the momentariness thesis is faultless and the proponents of momentariness possess freedom from defects, "has the thorn of envy" — characterized by resentment — because it is an inner cause of suffering, "his vital points pierced by it," the poor fellow, with his mind disturbed, failing to notice even his own contradictory statements, "cries out incoherently," in a confused manner, with statements unconnected to what precedes and follows. "Therefore," since his words are those of a disturbed mind and deserve no regard — for exposing their faults would only increase his suffering, like pouring salt on a wound — "he deserves only to be ignored" by the wise, who are rich in compassion.

body.text: tadevamakṣaṇikeṣu na kathañcidekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvaṃ sambhavatīti pratipādyopasaṃharannāha- "tasmādidam" ityādi | yeṣāṃ hi sthirarūpatayā pṛthagapi bhāvaḥ sambhavati teṣāmakṣaṇikānāṃ "pṛthak" kevalānāṃ "kāryakaraṇasambhavena" hetunā sahaiva kurvantīti sahakāritvaniyamāyogādidamekārthakriyālakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvaṃ kṣaṇikānāmeva | teṣāṃ svahetupariṇāmopanidhidharmāṇāṃ parasparopādānasahakāripratyayaikasāmagrījanyānāṃ pṛthagasambhavāt |
body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated that <s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperative causation) characterized as the restriction of <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) is in no way possible for non-momentary entities, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] concludes by saying, beginning with "Therefore this": For those non-momentary entities which, due to their enduring nature, can exist separately as well, "since it is possible for" them "to produce effects separately" when alone, there can be no restriction that they produce [effects] only together — therefore this <s>sahakāritva</s> characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> belongs only to momentary entities. For those [momentary entities], whose nature is determined by the maturation of their own causes and concurrent conditions, being produced by a single aggregate of mutually [dependent] substantial and cooperative conditions, cannot exist separately.

body.text: 42. kṣaṇīkapakṣe eva ekārthakriyārūpasahakāritvasya vyavasthā |
body.translated_text: 42. The establishment of <s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperative causation) in the form of <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) belongs only to the momentariness thesis.

children.text: ) ekārthakriyālakṣaṇameva sahakāritvaṃ sarvatra na kvacidatiśayotpādanaṃ sambhavati | yatra tu santānopakāreṇa pūrvapūrvapratyayebhyo viśiṣṭaviśiṣṭatarottarottarakṣaṇajanena bhāvāḥ sahakāriṇo vivakṣitakāryasya hetutāṃ pratipadyante- yathā taṇḍulādibhya odanādijanmani dahanodakādayaḥ, bījādibhyaścāṅkurādijanmani pṛthivyādayaḥ- tatra viśeṣotpādanaṃ pratyayānāṃ sahakriyocyate loke | santānāśrayeṇa pūrvakṣaṇebhyo dvitīyādiviśiṣṭakṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ santānākhyaṃ kāryamāśrṛ(śri)tya purvottarakṣaṇayorekatvādhyavasāyena tasyaivāyamatiśaya iti na dravyāśrayeṇa | aupacārikameva na tu pāramārthikam | pūrvapūrvakṣaṇebhyastu svahetupariṇāmopanidhidharmabhya uttarottaraviśeṣotpattau pūrvakāraṇakalāpasyaikārthakriyālakṣaṇameva tatra paramārthataḥ sahakāritvamiti na kācit kṣatiriti | kasmād dravyāśreyeṇātiśayotpādanaṃ neṣyate? | kṣaṇike dravye vastuni viśeṣasyānutpatteḥ tasyānantarakṣaṇabhāvarūpatvād |
children.translated_text: <s>Sahakāritva</s> (cooperative causation) characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) [applies] everywhere; nowhere does <s>atiśayotpādana</s> (production of an enhancement) obtain. Where, however, entities attain the status of being causes of the intended effect through <s>santānopakāra</s> (assistance to the continuum) — by generating successively more and more distinct moments from the preceding conditions — as, for example, fire, water, and the like in the production of cooked rice and so forth from raw rice grains, and earth and the like in the production of sprouts and so forth from seeds — there, the cooperative action of conditions is called in common parlance the production of a particular enhancement. Based on the continuum, the effect called a continuum, characterized by the second and subsequent distinct moments [arising] from the preceding moments, is spoken of [as enhanced] through the determination of identity between the earlier and later moments — 'this is an enhancement of that very [thing]' — but this is not based on [a single enduring] substance. It is merely conventional, not ultimate. However, from the preceding moments, which have the nature of maturation of their own causes and concurrent conditions, in the production of successively distinct [moments], the <s>sahakāritva</s> of the preceding causal aggregate is ultimately characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) even there — so there is no loss. Why is <s>atiśayotpādana</s> (production of an enhancement) not accepted as based on [a single enduring] substance? Because no enhancement arises in a momentary substance-entity, since that [enhancement] has the nature of the immediately subsequent moment.

body.translated_text: Now, <s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperative causation) characterized as <s>atiśayotpādana</s> (producing an enhancement) is also observed in entities. How then was it said earlier that 'nowhere is cooperative action the production of an enhancement; rather, it is simply the production of a single effect by many [causes]'? To this he says, beginning with "Where, however, through assistance to the continuum":

body.text: yadi tarhi kṣanike taṇḍulādidravye viśeṣo notpadyate, anantaramapyasau mā bhūt | tato yathā parasparato viśeṣamanāsādayanto 'pi kṣaṇikāḥ sahitā eva kurvanti na kevalāḥ, evamakṣaṇikā api | tenaiṣāmekārthakriyālakṣaṇameva sahakāritvaṃ bhaviṣyati | na ca śakyaṃ vaktum- yo yasya prāgakārakaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa paścādapīti | tathā hi- prabhāsvarādapavarakaṃ praviṣṭasyendriyamarthapratipattimakurvadapi paścāt kurvāṇamupalabhyate | taduktam-
body.translated_text: If, then, no enhancement arises in the momentary substance of rice grains and the like, then let it not arise in the immediately subsequent [moment] either. Therefore, just as momentary [entities], even though they do not obtain any enhancement from each other, produce [effects] only when combined and not alone, so too would non-momentary [entities]. Thus for these [non-momentary entities] too, <s>sahakāritva</s> will be characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect). Nor can it be said that whatever is by its own nature not a cause of something at first, is not a cause of it later either. For consider: the sense organ of one who has entered a dark room from a bright [place], though not producing cognition of objects [at first], is observed to produce [it] later. As it has been said:

body.text:
"na hi praviṣṭamātrāṇāmuṣṇād garbhagṛhādiṣu |
arthā na pratibhāntīti gṛhyante nendriyaiḥ punaḥ ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "For it is not the case that, for those who have just entered hot inner chambers and the like from a bright [place], objects do not appear — rather, they are [eventually] apprehended by the sense organs."

body.text: ata āha- "nahi taṇḍulādīnām" ityādi | viśeṣānutpattau sannidhānasyāpyasannidhānatulyatvāt dahanādibhāve 'pi taṇḍulādibhyo naudanajanma syāt | tathā prabhāsvarādapavarakaṃ praviṣṭasya yadīndriyaṃ svopakāribhyo 'tiśayaṃ krameṇa na pratipadyate tadā prāgiva paścādapyarthapratipattiṃ naiva janayet | tasmādyadasambhavi (

children.text: ) kāryaṃ yatra dṛśyate tasya tato 'nyatvameva, śālibījādiva kodravabījasyeti niratiśayādanyatvameva sātiśayatayā tatkāryakāriṇa iti | evaṃ tāvad yatra sahakāribhyaḥ krameṇa kāryaṃ bhavati tatrātiśayotpādanalakṣaṇamaupacārikaṃ sahakāritvamekārthakriyālakṣaṇameva tu mukhyaṃ tatrāpīti pratipāditam |
children.translated_text: where it is [subsequently] observed — that [later entity] is simply different from [the earlier one], just as a <s>kodrava</s> seed is different from a rice seed. That which produces the effect of that [intended result] by virtue of possessing an enhancement is simply different from [the entity] without enhancement. Thus, where the effect arises gradually from <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes), the conventional <s>sahakāritva</s> characterized as <s>atiśayotpādana</s> (production of an enhancement) has been shown to be, in its primary sense, none other than <s>sahakāritva</s> characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect).

body.translated_text: Therefore he says, beginning with "For of rice grains and the like": If no enhancement is produced, then since the mere proximity [of fire etc.] would be equivalent to non-proximity, even in the presence of fire and the like, cooked rice would not arise from rice grains and the like. Likewise, for one who has entered a dark room from a bright [place], if the sense organ does not gradually obtain an enhancement from its auxiliary [causes], then it would not produce cognition of objects later either, just as it did not before. Therefore, that effect which was impossible

body.text: yatra tvakṣepeṇaivārthasannidhimātreṇa sahakāriṇaḥ kāryaṃ kurvanti kiṃ tatrāpi santānāśrayamatiśayotpādanamasti? ityata āha- "akṣepakāriṣu" ityādi | ‘ye hyavyavadhānādideśā indriyādayaḥ svahetubhyo jātāsteṣvavilambitakāriṣu na viśeṣotpattiḥ parasparataḥ sambhavati, kṣaṇikatvāt'; ityuktaṃ prāk |
body.translated_text: Where, however, <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes) produce the effect immediately, merely through the proximity of the object, does <s>atiśayotpādana</s> (production of an enhancement) based on the continuum also obtain there? To this he says, beginning with "In the case of those that act immediately": 'For those [entities] such as sense organs and the like, which arise from their own causes in an unmediated location and act without delay — among these immediately-acting [entities], the production of an enhancement from each other is not possible, because they are momentary' — this was stated earlier.

body.text: yadi na viśeṣotpattiḥ tadā kathaṃ nirviśeṣā jñānasya kāraṇībhavanti? ityata āha- "tatra yathāsvaṃ" yasya ye ātmīyāḥ pratyayāḥ taiḥ, "parasparopasarpaṇavyavadhānādivirahāderāśrayabhūtairye jātāḥ" yogyaścāsāvatyāsannatvātiviprakarṣavirahād deśaśca sa ādiryasyāvyavahitadeśādeḥ tatrāvasthānamavasthā yeṣāṃ "te saha svabhāvaniṣpattyā" svabhāvaniṣpattirvidyata ityeva kṛtvā "jñānahetutāṃ pratipadyante" tatra kiṃ parasparato viśeṣotpattyā prārthitayā? | yadi hi svahetubhya eva parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayebhyaḥ svakāryajananakṣamā yogyadeśādyavasthānalakṣaṇaviśeṣayogino notpadyeran, tadaiṣāṃ parasparato viśeṣotpattiḥ prārthyeta, na tu svahetubhya eva tathāvidhānāmutpattau | yata evaṃ "iti" tasmāt "tatra"teṣu akṣepakāriṣvindriyādiṣu "ekārthakriyaiva" mukhyaṃ "sahakāritvaṃ" na santānāśrayeṇa vyavasthāpyamānamatiśayotpādanalakṣaṇaṃ gauṇamiti |
body.translated_text: If no enhancement is produced, then how do [entities] without enhancement become causes of cognition? To this he says: "There, each through its own" — that is, through its own conditions — "those that have arisen from bases such as mutual proximity, absence of obstruction, and so on" — where 'proximity' means an unmediated location and the like, consisting in the absence of excessive remoteness — "having the state of being situated there, they, through <s>svabhāvaniṣpatti</s> (natural production) — simply by virtue of the fact that natural production exists — "attain the status of being causes of cognition." What need is there for the production of an enhancement from each other? For if [entities] capable of generating their own effects, possessing the particular qualification of being situated in a suitable location and so forth, did not arise from their own causes — [causes] that serve as bases for mutual proximity and the like — then the production of an enhancement from each other would be sought. But not when such [entities] arise from their own causes in just that manner. Since this is so, "therefore, in those" immediately-acting [entities] such as sense organs and the like, "<s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) alone is the" primary "<s>sahakāritva</s> (cooperative causation)," not the secondary one characterized as <s>atiśayotpādana</s> (production of an enhancement) established on the basis of the continuum.

body.text: atha viśeṣotpādanalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvaṃ kathaṃ na vyavasthāpyate? | tadapi hi loke pratītatvād vyavasthāpanīyamevetyata āha- "yatra tu" kārye nāvyavadhānādideśopanipātamātreṇaivendriyādaya iva sahakāriṇaḥ pratyayatāṃ pratipadyante, kintu vivakṣitakāryotpādānuguṇaṃ (

children.text: ) pratikṣaṇaṃ prakṛṣyamāṇaṃ viśeṣamutpādayantaḥ "tatra" kālakṣepabhāvini kārye kartavye "hetusantāno"'parāparakṣaṇabhāvalakṣaṇa ātmātiśayāsādanārthaṃ sahakārīṇi pratyayāntarāṇyapekṣate, na tu tatsamānakālaḥ kāraṇakṣaṇa iti | "tata" stebhyaḥ kāraṇāntarebhyaḥ "svabhāvāntarasya" kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣaparamparālakṣaṇasya "pratilambhaḥ" santānasyaikatvenādhimuktasyocyate loke | paramārthatastu tatrāpi pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ pratyayakalāpa uttarottarakāryotpādānuguṇe viśiṣṭakṣaṇe pratiniyata ityekārthakriyālakṣaṇameva sahakāritvamanubhavati |
children.translated_text: "there," in the case of an effect that involves the passage of time, "the causal continuum" — characterized by the nature of successive moments — "requires" cooperative conditions, other conditions, for the purpose of attaining an enhancement of itself, but not the causal moment that is simultaneous with them. "From those" — from other conditions — "the obtaining of another nature" — characterized by a series of particular enhancements conducive to the production of the effect — is spoken of in common parlance as [an enhancement] of the continuum apprehended as a unity. But in ultimate reality, even there, each preceding causal aggregate is restricted to a particular distinct moment conducive to the production of the subsequent effect, and thus it undergoes <s>sahakāritva</s> characterized as <s>ekārthakriyā</s> (producing a single effect) alone.

body.translated_text: But how is <s>sahakāritva</s> characterized as <s>viśeṣotpādana</s> (production of a particular enhancement) not established [at all]? For since it too is recognized in common experience, it ought to be established. To this he says: "Where, however," the <s>sahakārins</s> such as sense organs and the like do not attain the status of being conditions merely through the immediate proximity of an unmediated location, as [they do] in [the case of entities] that act immediately; rather, producing an enhancement that is progressively intensified moment by moment in a manner conducive to the production of the intended effect,

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ svabhāvāntarapratilambhasteṣām?, yataḥ krameṇa kāryaṃ nirvartayantītyata āha- "tatra svarasataḥ" ityādi | "tatra" tasmin hetusantāne ye hetava upādānakāraṇākhyāḥ ye ca pratyayāḥ sahakārisaṃjñitāsteṣāṃ ye pūrve prathama upanipātakṣaṇāḥ teṣāṃ vināśahetvanapekṣitayā svarasato nivṛttau satyāṃ tebhya eva svarasato nivartamānebhyaḥ prathamakṣaṇebhyaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇena viśeṣeṇa viśiṣṭasya kṣaṇasyotpattiḥ tebhyo 'nuguṇataraviśeṣavatāṃ tṛtīyakṣaṇānāṃ tebhyonuguṇatamaviśeṣavatāṃ caturthakṣaṇānām; evaṃ yāvadatyantātiśayavānantyaḥ kāraṇakalāpo jātaḥ tataḥ kāryasyotpattiḥ ityevaṃ sahakāribhyaḥ svabhāvāntarapratilambhaḥ, kṣepavatī ca kāryotpattiriti |
body.translated_text: But how do they obtain a different nature, since they produce the effect gradually? To this he says: "There, spontaneously" and so on. "There" — in that causal continuum, those causes called <s>upādānakāraṇa</s> (material causes) and those conditions designated as <s>sahakārins</s> (cooperative causes) — of these, those which are prior, the first moments of occurrence — when their cessation occurs spontaneously, without depending on a cause of destruction, from those very [causes] that are spontaneously ceasing, from those first moments, a moment arises distinguished by a special feature conducive to the production of the effect; from those, third moments possessing a still more conducive special feature; from those, fourth moments possessing the most conducive special feature — thus, until a causal assemblage of the final [moment] possessing the utmost enhancement is produced, and from that the effect arises. In this way, there is the obtaining of a different nature from the cooperative causes, and the production of the effect involves a delay.

body.text: atra paraścodayannāha- "sahakāriṇaḥ" saha karaṇaśīlāt kāraṇāt, jātāvekavacanam, yat samutpannaviśeṣamanantaroktena prakāreṇa kāraṇaṃ antyasāmagrīkṣaṇalakṣaṇaṃ tato 'ṅkurādikāryotpattau iṣyamāṇāyāṃ tasyaiva viśeṣasyādyasya kāryotpādanānuguṇasya yaḥ krameṇābhivarddhamānaḥ kāryasya janaka iṣyate tasyaiva utpattirna syāt prathamakṣaṇopanipātināṃ parasparato viśeṣānāsādanāt kṣaṇānāmavivekāt anabhyupagamācca |
body.translated_text: Here, the opponent raises an objection and says: "From the cooperative cause" — from the cause that has the habit of acting together, singular used in the generic sense — that cause characterized as the moment of the final aggregate, in which a special feature has arisen in the manner just described — when the production of an effect such as a sprout and the like from that [cause] is accepted, the production of that very first special feature, conducive to the generation of the effect, which is accepted as the generator of the effect by gradually increasing — that very production would not occur, because the moments at the first occurrence do not obtain special features from one another, because the moments are indistinguishable, and because [such obtaining] is not accepted.

body.text: parasparato 'navāptaviśeṣā eva kāryotpādanānuguṇaṃ viśeṣamārapsyanta iti cedāha- "aviśiṣṭāda" viśiṣṭebhyaḥ parasparato "viśeṣasya" (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 131.

children.text: ) kāryotpādānuguṇasyotpattāviṣyamāṇāyāṃ "kāryasya" aṅkurādeḥ syāt, viśeṣābhāvādityabhiprāyaḥ | tataśca parasparato viśeṣotpādānapekṣiṇa eva sahakāriṇaḥ kāryaṃ kurvīran |
children.translated_text: ) — conducive to the production of the effect — if the production is accepted, "of the effect" — a sprout and the like — [it] would [arise immediately], because of the absence of [any] special feature — this is the intention. And therefore, the cooperative causes that depend on the mutual production of special features alone would produce the effect.

body.translated_text: If [one says:] those that have not obtained special features from one another will indeed acquire a special feature conducive to the production of the effect — to this he says: "From the undistinguished" — from those that are undistinguished from one another — "of a special feature" (

body.text: kimevaṃsati siddhaṃ bhavati? iti cet, āha- "tena" yena kṣaṇikā api parasparato viśeṣotpādānapekṣā eva svakāryaṃ kurvanti ekakāryapratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ ca sahakāritvaṃ pratipadyante tena kāraṇena "akṣaṇikānāmapi kāraṇatā syāt, apekṣaṇīyebhyaḥ svabhāvātiśayotpatiśca na syāt" ityakṣaṇikavādī kṣaṇikapakṣeṇa svapakṣasya sāmyamāpādayati | yadāha-
body.translated_text: What is established if this is so? If [one asks], he says: "By that" — by the fact that even momentary [entities] produce their own effects only in dependence on the mutual production of special features and enter into cooperative causation characterized as the exclusive determination of a single effect — by that reasoning, "there would be causality even for non-momentary entities, and there would be no production of an enhancement of nature from those upon which [they] depend" — thus the proponent of non-momentariness brings about parity of [his] own position with the position of momentariness. As he says:

children.translated_text: "Who would look good saying this, were it not for shamelessness,

children.text: ajñatā vā yataḥ sarvaṃ kṣaṇikeṣvapi tatsamam ||
children.translated_text: or ignorance? For all this is equally [applicable] to momentary [entities] too.
The conditions that are the causes of special features for them are in no way
applicable to [their] moments, because of [their] indistinguishability, just as in the case of permanent [entities]."

body.text: iti | tatraitat syāt prathamakṣaṇe 'pi kṣitibījādayaḥ parasparataḥ samutpannaviśeṣā eva sannidhīyante-
body.translated_text: Here one might [think]: even at the first moment, earth, seeds, and the like come together already possessing special features produced from one another —

body.text: "yena yasyābhisambandho dūrasthasyāpi tena saḥ |"
body.translated_text: "That which has connection with something, even though distant, has [connection] with that [thing]."

body.text: iti nyāyāddhi dūradeśavartināmapi hetuphalabhāvāt ityāśaṅkayāha- "atha sahakāriṇā" ityādi | sahakāriṇaḥ parasparasamparkavikalā api vastudharmatayaivānyonyamupakurvantīti śahakāriṇā kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajananāya kṛtaviśeṣa eva samparkakāla upatiṣṭheta, evaṃ satyanavasthā syāt | tathā hi- tadviśeṣotpattāvapyaparaḥ sahakārikṛto viśeṣo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ, tathā tadutpattāvapyanya iti |
body.translated_text: — since there is a cause-and-effect relationship even for things situated in distant places, by this principle. Anticipating this [objection], he says: "Now, by a cooperative cause" and so on. Even though the cooperative causes lack mutual contact, since by the very nature of reality they assist one another, [if one says] the cooperative cause would come to the time of contact already having been given a special feature for the purpose of generating a special feature conducive to the production of the effect — if so, there would be an infinite regress. For, the production of that special feature [would itself require further explanation].

body.text: atha naivaṃ sahakāriṇaḥ parasparasya kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣaṇimittamaparaṃ viśeṣaṃ kurvanti, svabhāvata eva tatra teṣāṃ yogyatvāt ityata āha- "na ca" ityādi | naiva hi sahakāriṇaḥ kṣitibījādayaḥ parasparasya kāryotpādānuguṇo yo viśeṣaḥ tadutpādane "nityaṃ" sarvakālaṃ yogyāvasthā "yena" yogyāvasthatvena "nityānuṣaktaḥ" nityānubaddhaḥ "eṣāṃ" kṣitibījādīnāṃ kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanako (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 132.

children.text: ) viśeṣaḥ syāt yataḥ ‘aviśiṣṭād viśeṣotpattau kāryasyāpi syāt'; ityetadapi parihriyeta |
children.translated_text: ) there would be [the production of] a special feature, since [then the objection] 'from the undistinguished, if a special feature arises, the effect too would [arise immediately]' would also be resolved.

body.translated_text: Now, if the cooperative causes do not in fact produce any additional special feature for one another conducive to the production of the effect, because they are naturally fit for that — to this he says: "Not" and so on. For the cooperative causes — earth, seeds, and the like — are not "always" — at all times — in a state of fitness for the production of the special feature conducive to the production of the effect for one another, "such that" — if they were in a state of fitness, (

body.text: kuta etad? ityāha- "tadupāya" ityādi | teṣāṃ kṣitibījādīnāmupāye- yogyadeśopanipāte kāryavyaktidarśanāt apāye ca- parasparasamparkavirāme kāryānutpattidarśanāt | yadi hi kāryotpādanuguṇaviśeṣotpādane sarvadā yogyāvasthāḥ syuḥ tadā so 'pi viśeṣaḥ sarvadā syat | tatastatparamparābhāvi kāryamiti tadupāyāpāyayoḥ kāryasyotpattyanutpattī na syātām | tasmānna sahakāriṇaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣotpādane yogyāvasthāḥ sarvadeti | yataḥ sahakāriṇā pṛthagavasthitenānavasthābhayāt kṛtaviśeṣo nopatiṣṭhate parasparataśca prathamasamparkakṣaṇabhāvināṃ nopeyate yujyate vā | tena kāraṇenādyo viśeṣaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇaḥ sahakāribhyaḥ samānakālatayā nirupakārasya kṣitibījādeḥ "notpadyate", utpadyate cāsau itīṣyate | tena samagrāvasthāvat sarveṣāṃ vyagrāvasthābhāvināmapi kṣaṇānāmaviśeṣāt tajjananasvabhāvatve 'pyajananāt samagrāvasthāyāmeva jananād | yathā kṣaṇikānāmekārthakriyāpratiniyamalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvaṃ tathā sthirasvabhāvānāmapi bhaviṣyatīti kṣinasarvopāyo 'kṣaṇikavādī sāmyamevātura iva bahumanyamānastatraiva bharaṃ kṛtavān |
body.translated_text: Whence is this? He says: "The means of that" and so on. Because of the observation that the effect-instance appears when the means of those — earth, seeds, and the like — [namely] the occurrence at a suitable location — [is present], and because of the observation that the effect does not arise when [those means] are absent — when the mutual contact ceases. For if they were always in a state of fitness for producing a special feature conducive to the production of the effect, then that special feature too would always exist. And consequently, the effect that is the eventual result of that [special feature] — [would arise] when the means [are present] and not otherwise.

body.text: siddhāntavādī bhaṅgyā paramupahasannāha- "nāsmākaṃ punaḥ punaḥ" ityādi | yadi punaḥ punarvacane 'pi lokasya nyāyapratītirbhavati śataśo 'pi brūmaḥ | kimaṅga punarddhau trīn vā vārān? | nahi parārthapravṛttānāmasmākaṃ punaḥ punarabhidhāne kaścidudvego bhavati | evaṃvādinaśca śāstrakṛtaḥ kvacit prakārāntareṇa tamevārthaṃ sphuṭīkurvato ye punaruktatāaprihārāya yatante sa teṣāmasthānapariśrama eva | yadi nodvego hanta tarhyucyatām ityata āha- "na viśeṣotpādanādeva" ityādi | naiva viśeṣotpādanāt sahakāriṇāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 133.

children.text: ) sahakāritvaṃ paramārthataḥ kvacit sambhavati, yataḥ prathamakṣaṇabhāvināṃ bījādīnāṃ tadabhāvāt kāryotpādānuguṇe viśeṣe kartavye sahakāritāvirahaḥ syāt | kintvekārthākriyaiva sahakāriṇāṃ pāramārthikaṃ sahakāritvaṃ pūrvoktābhiryuktibhiḥ sambhāvyate | sā ca prathamamasamparkabhājāmastyeveti kiṃ na sahakāriṇaḥ syuḥ? |
children.translated_text: ) — cooperative causation in the ultimate sense is possible in some cases, since for seeds and the like existing at the first moment, due to the absence of that [special feature], there would be an absence of cooperative causation in producing a special feature conducive to the production of the effect. However, the joint production of a single result alone is the ultimate cooperative causation of cooperative causes, as has been established by the previously stated arguments. And that [joint production] exists even for those that have not initially come into contact — so what is not [possible]?

body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis, indirectly mocking the opponent, says: "We do not [mind] saying again and again" and so on. If the understanding of logical principles arises for people even through repeated statement, we say it a hundred times. How much more [gladly] two or three times? For there is no weariness for us who engage for the sake of others in repeated exposition. And the author of the treatise, who speaks thus, [adopts] a certain manner in some places (

body.text: para āha- sāpyekārthakriyā na bhavet parasparato viśeṣarahitānām | yadi punaḥ parasparato viśeṣarahitānāmapi tadekārthakriyāṅgikriyate tadā pratyekaṃ tadavasthāyāṃ tadutpādanasāmarthyābhyupagamāt tadavasthāyāmiva pṛthagapi sā bhavet | tathāhi- te tadavasthāyāmapi parasparato nirviśeṣā eva kurvanti | teṣāṃ pṛthagapi tadviśeṣakriyā kathamiva na prasajyeta? | nahyeṣāṃ saṃhatāsaṃhatāvasthayoḥ kaścidviśeṣo 'stīti | bhavatu, ko doṣaḥ? iti cet; "tathā ca" kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣasya pṛthakkaraṇaprasaṅge sati "tasmād viśeṣād bhavanaśīlam" aṅkurādi "kāryamapi" viśeṣavat kevalāt sahakāriṇaḥ syāt iti cenmanyase, atrāpi sarvamuktamuttaram | tathā hi- saṃhatāsaṃhatāvasthayonnirviśeṣā eva kṣaṇakṣayiṇo bhāvā iti yaducyate tat kiṃ tāvadviśeṣamātrāpekṣayā? āhosvit kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanakaviśeṣāpekṣayā? | yadi prācyo vikalpaḥ tadayuktam | na hi kācid viśeṣamātrarahitāvasthā sambhavati, sarvadāparaparapratyayayoganibandhanasyāparāparaviśeṣasya bhāvāt | nahi kadācit kiṃcidekameva, ādhāracchāyātapavātaśītāderyathāsambhavaṃ bhāvāt | na ca tadbhāve 'pi tat tādṛśameva, kāraṇabhedāt | etāvattu syāt- kaścid viśeṣaḥ kvacit kārye 'nuguṇo na sarvaḥ sarvatreti | etacca prāgevoktamiti darśayannāha- "pratikṣaṇamaparāparaiḥ pratyayaiḥ" iti | ‘aparāparapratyayogena pratikṣaṇaṃ bhinnaśaktayaḥ saṃskārāḥ santanvanto yadyapi kutaścit sāmyāt sarūpāḥ pratīyante, tathāpi bhinna evaiṣāṃ svabhāvaḥ, tena kiñcideva kasyacit kāraṇam'; iti, ‘kṣaṇikeṣu (

children.text: ) bhāveṣvaparāparotpattairaikyābhāvāt'; iti cātra saṃkṣipyataramuktam | evaṃ ca 'nāsmākaṃ punaḥ punarvacana'; ityatra dviḥ punargrahaṇaṃ yujyate | yathā yena prakāreṇa bhāvasantāne viśeṣasyotpattiḥ [ta]dapyuktam ‘tatra svarasataḥ pūrvakṣaṇanirodhe tebhya eva viśiṣṭakṣaṇotpādād viśeṣotpattiḥ'; iti | atha kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanakaviśeṣāpekṣayā prāgvat prathamasamparkabhājaḥ parasparato nirviśeṣā ityabhimataṃ tadapyayuktam | yataḥ kāryotpādānuguṇasya viśeṣasya janakāḥ kṣitibījādayaḥ kīdṛśāḥ ye vyavadhānādirahitatvenopanipātinaḥ | tadbhāva eva tasya bhāvāt etāvanmātranibandhanatvācca janakaṃ vya(kavya)vasthāyāḥ | te ca tathāvidhāḥ sarvadā na bhavantīti kathaṃ pṛthagapi kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣārambha eṣāṃ syāt?, yataḥ kevalānāmapi kāryakriyā prasajyeta tad darśayati- yogyo deśo yeṣāṃ te yogyadeśāḥ, tadbhāvo yogyadeśatā, sā ādiryeṣāmavyavahitadeśatvādīnānavasthābhedānāṃ te tathoktāḥ, te ca te avasthābhedāśca tathoktāḥ | "yogyadeśatā a(tādya) vyavahitadeśatādayo" ye "avasthāviśeṣāḥ" kṣitibījādīnāmupajāyante te kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣalakṣaṇakāryakaraṇaśīlāḥ, naivaṃvidhāḥ sarvadā bījādaya iti kathameṣāṃ pṛthagapi tathāvidhaviśeṣārambhaḥ syāt? | etadapi prāgevoktam ‘tatra yo 'vyavadhānādideśo rūpendriyādikalāpaḥ sa vijñānajanane samartho hetuḥ'; iti vacanāt | tasya codāharaṇamātratvāt | ihāpi tatra yo 'vyavadhānādideśaḥ kṣitibījādikalāpaḥ sa kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanane samartho heturiti pratīyata eva | sa ca tathāvidhoviśeṣaḥ sarvadā na bhavati, tajjanakasya hetorabhāvāt | parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayasyaiva pratyayaviśeṣasya tadvetutvāt | etadapi pūrvamevoktamityāha- teṣāṃ ca kāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣa[janane] viśeṣavatāṃ yata utpattistadapyuktamasakṛdeva ‘yasteṣāṃ parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayaḥ pratyayaviśeṣaḥ sa taddhetujanane samartho hetuḥ'; iti | tathā ‘yathāsvaṃ pratyayaiḥ parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayairye (
children.translated_text: ) — because of the absence of unity among entities through the production of ever-successive [moments]'; and here this has been stated more concisely. And thus the double use of 'again' in 'we do not [mind] saying again and again' is appropriate. As for the manner in which the special feature arises in the continuum of an entity, that too has been stated: 'there, upon the spontaneous cessation of the prior moment, from those very [moments], through the production of a distinguished moment, there is the arising of a special feature.'

children.translated_text: ) — when the state of suitable location and the like has arisen, they, together with [their] natural development, attain the status of being causes of cognition'; by this [statement], since it is understood here as well. Therefore, although there is no special feature for these [entities] from one another, because of [its] impossibility, [a special feature] produced by their own causes — by whom can it be prevented? And when special features have arisen from their own causes, there is no expectation of that [special feature] from one another, since the arising of a special feature from one another is impossible.

body.translated_text: The opponent says: that joint production of a single result too would not occur for those that lack special features from one another. But if the joint production of a single result is accepted even for those lacking special features from one another, then, since the capacity for producing that [result] is acknowledged even in their [initial] state, it would occur individually in that very state as well. For, even in that state, they produce [the effect] while being without special features from one another.

body.text: kutaḥ punarayaṃ kāmacāro labhyate yadaṅkurādikāryaṃ sahakāriṇaḥ parasparasya kāryotpādānuguṇāṃ viśeṣaparamparāṃ janayantaḥ kurvanti, kāryotpādānuguṇaṃ tu viśeṣaṃ vyavadhānādirahitadeśopanipātamātreṇetyata āha- "kāryadvaividhyaṃ ca yasmāt tasmādevaṃ vibhajyate" | kathaṃ dvaividhyaṃ kāryāṇāmiti? ata āha- sahakāribhiravyavadhānādideśairanantaraṃ sañjanitāḥ parasparasya prāgavasthāpekṣaviśiṣṭakṣaṇabhāvalakṣaṇā ye viśeṣāstatparamparayā uttarottaraviśiṣṭaviśiṣṭatarādikṣaṇabhavarūpayā utpattirddharmo yasya tadātmakamekaṃ kāryam | anyacca tadviparītaṃ yat sahakārisannidhimātreṇa bhavati na parasparakṛtāṃ viśeṣaparamparāmapekṣate | atrodāharaṇam- "aṅkurādivat", ādigrahaṇādodanādivat | tathākṣepeṇa karaṇaśīlaṃ yadindriyaṃ tadvijñānādivacca | prabhāsvarādapavarakapraviṣṭendriyanirāsārthaṃ caitad viśeṣaṇam | kuta etad? iti cet ; kāryakāraṇayoḥ (

children.text: ) svabhāvabhedāt | kiṃciddhi kāryaṃ kāraṇasāmagrīsannidhimātrajanyasvabhāvam, tadanyattu tatpariṇāmāpekṣamiti | kāraṇamapi kiñcit svasannidhimātreṇa kāryajananasvabhāvaṃ svakāraṇebhya eva bhavati, yena parasparakṛtāṃ viśeṣaparamparāṃ svakāryakaraṇe nāpekṣate | anyattu tadviparītasvabhāvam | yathā kiñcideva śālyaṅkurajananasvabhāvam, tadviparītaṃ cāparam | śālyaṅkuraśca tabdījajanyasvabhāvo na yavādībījajanyasvabhāva iti na bhāvānāṃ svahetubalāyātāḥ pramāṇādhigatāḥ svabhāvāḥ paryanuyojyāḥ | ye tu yajjananasvabhāvāḥ pramāṇato 'dhigatāḥ te kiṃ sarvadaiva tatsvabhāvāḥ? āhosvit tadaiva? ityatra cintā pravartate | tatra sarvadā tatsvabhāvatve paścādiva prāgapi tatkāryakriyāprasaṅgena pararūpeṇākārakasya bhinnasvabhāvatā kārakākārakāvasthayoḥ śāliyavabījādīnāmiva tattvacintakairūcyate | sadṛśāparabhāvanibandhanaṃ caikatayā pratyabhijñānaṃ lūnapunarjāteṣviva keśanakhādiṣu ityatra virodhābhāvāditi | yadā ca taktāryakāraṇasvabhāvabhedāt kāryavdaividhyam, "tatrai"tasmiṃ(smin) sati "sahakāribhyaḥ" kṣitibījādibhyasteṣāṃ parasparasantānopakāramapekṣate yat kāraṇamantyāvasthāprāptaṃ tasya yat kāryamaṅkurādikaṃ tajjanmanimittaṃ "sahakāriṇāṃ" prathamakṣaṇāntaraṃ viśiṣṭadvitīyakṣaṇabhāvarūpo yo viśeṣaḥ kāryotpādānuguṇaḥ "ādyo" bhavati "sa teṣāṃ" sahakāriṇāṃ prathamasamparkabhājāṃ parasparakṛto yo viśeṣastajjanmā na bhavati parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayādeva pratyayaviśeṣāt tasya bhāvāt | tataḥ kāryotpādānuguṇādādyād viśeṣāt prathamakṣaṇopanipātibhiḥ sahakāribhiranyataḥ samāsāditaviśeṣaiḥ janitāt tatprabhṛti "ye viśeṣāḥ" prakṛṣyamāṇataduttarottarakṣaṇabhāvalakṣaṇā jāyante "te tajjanmānaḥ" sahakārikṛtaviśeṣajanmānaḥ | kutaḥ? "tatprakṛtitvāt" tasyādyasya viśeṣasya parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayāt pratyayaviśeṣādāsāditatadanukūlaviśeṣaiḥ sahakāribhiḥ parasparopakāranirapekṣairjanyasvabhāvatvāt, taduttareṣāṃ ca viśeṣāṇāṃ sahakārikṛtakāryotpādānuguṇaviśeṣajanyasvabhāvatvāt | (
children.translated_text: for some effects have a nature that is produced merely by the proximity of the complete causal assemblage (<s>kāraṇasāmagrī</s>), while others depend on the transformation of those [causes]. A cause, too, is of two kinds: some have a nature of producing effects merely by their own proximity and arise only from their own causes, whereby they do not depend on a series of specializations produced by each other for bringing about their own effect. Others have a nature contrary to that. Just as only certain [seeds] have the nature of producing a rice sprout, and others are contrary to that. And a rice sprout has the nature of being produced from a rice seed, not from a barley seed and the like — thus the intrinsic natures (<s>svabhāva</s>) of entities, which are established by their own causal power and ascertained by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), are not to be challenged. But those that are ascertained by valid cognition as having the nature of producing such-and-such — are they always of that nature? Or only at that [particular] time? Herein deliberation proceeds. If they were always of that nature, then since the production of that effect would absurdly follow even before [the appropriate conditions], just as after, the thinkers on reality say that the difference in intrinsic nature between the states of being an agent and a non-agent, like rice and barley seeds, is [explained by the fact that] one who does not act in the form of another has a different nature in the states of agency and non-agency. And recognition as identical is based on a similar subsequent existence, as with hair and nails that have been cut and regrown — here there is no contradiction. And when the twofold nature of effects follows from this difference in the intrinsic nature of causes and effects between cause and effect, "in that case," when this obtains, the cause that has reached its final state, depending on the mutual assistance of the continua of the cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>) such as earth and seed — for its effect, namely the sprout and the like, the cause of that birth, "the first" specialization of the cooperative conditions, having the form of a distinct second-momentary existence after the first moment, "is" conducive to the production of the effect. "That" is not born from the specialization produced by each other among those cooperative conditions that share the first contact, because that [first specialization] arises from a distinct condition (<s>pratyaya</s>) based only on mutual approach and the like. Then, from that first specialization conducive to the production of the effect, "the specializations that" arise thereafter, characterized by the successively intensified momentary existence, are "born from that" — born from the specialization produced by the cooperative conditions. Why? "Because of having that as their material cause (<s>prakṛti</s>)" — because those cooperative conditions, having acquired specializations favorable to that [effect] from a distinct condition based on the mutual approach of the first specialization, produce [effects] without depending on each other's mutual assistance; and because the subsequent specializations have the nature of being produced by the specialization conducive to the production of the effect that was brought about by the cooperative conditions.
