children.text: ) kāraṇasthasāmānyadharmairvinā bhavatām | tadevaṃ kāraṇasya sāmānyadharmā eva gamyā na viśeṣadharmāḥ, kāryasyāpi viśeṣadharmā eva gamakā na sāmānyadharmāḥ, tatkāryatvaniyamāt | ye tu kāraṇasya viśeṣadharmā yaistatkāryatvaniyamaḥ kāryamātrasya nāstīti na te gamyāḥ | ye ca kāryasya sāmānyadharmā dravyatvādayasteṣāmapi tatkāryatvaniyamābhāvādeva gamakatvaṃ nāstīti kāryakāraṇabhāvena gamakatve kutaḥ sarvathā gamyagamakabhāvaḥ pareṣāmiva prasajyeta? |
children.translated_text: ) — which exist even without the general properties residing in the cause. Thus, only the general properties of the cause are what is indicated, not the particular properties; and only the particular properties of the effect are the indicators, not the general properties — because of the invariable rule of being the effect of those. But those particular properties of the cause with respect to which mere effect has no invariable rule of being the effect — those are not indicated. And those general properties of the effect such as substance-hood and the like — since there is no invariable rule of being the effect of those either, they have no indicative function. So how can there be indicative function through the cause-effect relationship [for all properties]?

body.translated_text: Having thus examined the aspect belonging to the cause through the latter meaning, now examining the aspect belonging to the effect through the former meaning, he says: "And by those very" and so on. The effect too, by those very properties belonging to itself, is the indicator of the properties belonging to the cause — just as the particular forms such as smoke-hood, having pale leaves, and the like that come into being intermediately, do not exist without those general properties belonging to the cause. Here too, 'because of the invariable rule of being the effect of those' is to be supplied. Because of the invariable rule that those very particular properties belonging to the effect are effects with respect to the general properties belonging to the cause. For those particular properties belonging to the effect never exist without the general properties residing in the cause. Therefore, the invariable rule of being the effect belongs to those alone, and not to others such as substance-hood and the like (

body.text: 2. janyajanakabhāvasya sarvathā sattve 'pi gamyagamakabhāvasya na tathātvam |
body.translated_text: 2. Even though the producer-produced relationship exists in every respect, the indicated-indicator relationship is not the same way.

body.text: parasyāniṣṭhāpādanamāśaṅkayāha- "aṃśena" ityādi | yadi hi kāraṇasya sāmānyadharmā eva gamyāḥ kāryasyāpi viśeṣadharmā eva gamakāḥ tatkāryatvaniyamādiṣyante, hanta tarhyaśena janyajanakabhāvaḥ prāptaḥ | kāraṇasya sāmānyadharmā eva janakā na viśeṣadharmāḥ, kāryasyāpi viśeṣadharmā eva janyā na sāmānyadharmā iti syāt | sarvathā ca janyajanakabhāvo 'bhimata ityubhyupagamavirodhaḥ | etat pariharati- nāṃśena janyajanakabhāvaprasaṅgaḥ, niraṃśatvena vastunaḥ sarvātmanā tadabhyupagamāt, gamyagamakabhāvasyāpi sarvathābhimatatvāt | tadāha- "tajjanya" ityādi | yadi hi kāryasya taiḥ kāraṇagatairviśeṣadharmairjanyo yo viśeṣaḥ sa grahītuṃ śakyate, tadā tajjanyaviśeṣagrahaṇe 'bhimatatvāt kāraṇagataviśeṣadharmāṇāṃ gamyatvasya | tathā liṅgaviśeṣo dhūmatvādi upādhirviśeṣaṇaṃ yeṣāṃ dravyatvādīnāṃ sāmānyānāṃ kāryagatānāṃ teṣāṃ cābhimatatvāgdamakatvasya | tathā hi- agurudhūmagrahaṇe bhavatyeva tadagneranumānaṃ dhūmatvaviśeṣaṇena ca dravyatvādināgneranumānam | na hi sarvathā janyajanakabhāvo 'stītyeva tathaiva gamyagamakabhāvo bhavati, tasya jñānāpekṣatvāt | tathā hi- na sattāmātreṇa liṅgasya gamakatvam, tasya jñāpakatvāt | jñāpako hi svaniścayāpekṣo jñāpyamarthaṃ jñāpayati, nānyathā | kathaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 153.

children.text: ) tarhyuktaṃ "tadabhāve bhavataḥ tadutpattiniyama(mā)bhāvāt" iti |? | sarvathā janyajanakabhāvābhyupagame tadabhāve bhāvasyaivābhāvādityata āha- "aviśiṣṭa"- ityādi | yadi hi tajjanyaviśeṣa grahaṇarahitamaviśiṣṭaṃ kāryamātramupādīyate liṅgaviśeṣopādhirahitaṃ vā dravyādikaṃ tadā "aviśiṣṭasāmānyavivakṣāyāṃ" kāraṇagataviśeṣābhāve 'pi dhūmamātrasya bhāvāt tadaviśiṣṭasya ca dravyatvāderagnyabhāve 'pi bhāvād vyabhicāra iti sarvathā janyajanakabhāvo neṣyate, tadabhāvād gamyagamakabhāvaśca | na tu viśeṣavivakṣāyām, tatra vyabhicārābhāvāt | tathā hi- yadi nāmadhūmamātraṃ tārṇapārṇādiviśeṣābhāve bhavati, na tu tajjanyo viśeṣaḥ, sa yadi grahītuṃ śakyate, tadā viśeṣasya gamyatvamastyeva, niścitasyaiva liṅgatvāt | tathā yadyapi dravyatvasattvamātramagnyabhāve 'pi bhavati na tu dhūmātmakamiti tadviśiṣṭasyāvyabhicārād gamakatvamapi na vāryata iti |
children.translated_text: ) Then was it not stated: "because of the absence of the invariable rule of production from that, of that which exists in its absence"? If the producer-produced relationship is acknowledged in every respect, in the absence of that there would be the absence of the entity itself — to this he says: "Undistinguished" and so on. For if mere effect, devoid of the apprehension of the particular [properties] produced by that, is taken up in an undistinguished manner, or [if] substance-hood and the like, devoid of the qualification of a particular inferential mark, [are taken up] — then, "when the undistinguished generality is intended," even in the absence of the particular [property] belonging to the cause, since mere smoke exists, and since substance-hood and the like, which are undistinguished, exist even in the absence of fire,

body.translated_text: Anticipating the imposition of an undesired consequence on the opponent, he says: "Partially" and so on. For if only the general properties of the cause are said to be indicated and only the particular properties of the effect are said to be indicators, because of the invariable rule of being the effect of those — well then, the producer-produced relationship would be obtained only partially. Only the general properties of the cause would be producers, not the particular properties; and only the particular properties of the effect would be produced, not the general properties — this would follow. But the producer-produced relationship is accepted in every respect — so there would be a contradiction with what is acknowledged. He resolves this: not partially [is the producer-produced relationship limited].

body.text: 3. kāryakāraṇabhāvapratīteratidurlabhatvāśaṅkāyā nirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: 3. Removal of the apprehension that the cognition of the cause-effect relationship is extremely difficult to obtain.

body.text: atra parasya vacanāvakāśamāśaṅkayāha- "kasyacit" dhūmādeḥ "kadācit" kasmiṃścit kāle "kutaścit" agnyādeḥ "bhāve 'pi" sati "sarvo" dhūmādiḥ "tādṛśo" yādṛśa ekadāgnyāderbhavana dṛṣṭa tajjātīyaḥ, "tathāvidhajanmā" yathāvidhāt sa eko bhavan dṛṣṭaḥ tādṛśādeva janma yasya sa | "tathāvidhajanmetyetat kutaḥ" pramāṇādavasitam? yenocyate ‘kāryahetau kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhinibandhanāvanvayavyatirekau'; iti | tathāhi- yadi nāma pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ kasyaciddhūmasyāgnyādisāmagrīkāryatvamavagataṃ kimetāvatānyasyāpi tādṛśasya tādṛśakāryatā sidhyati, tatra tannibandhanayoḥ pratyakṣānupalambhayoravyāpārāt | yatraiva hi tayorvyāparastasyaiva tatkāryatā bhavatu, tadanyasya tu kimāyātam? yena tathavidhādasya janma syāt | evaṃ hi kasyāściddhūmavyakteragnyādijanyatā dṛṣṭeti kinna ghaṭāderapi sābhyupagamyate? anyatvena (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 154.

children.text: ) viśeṣābhāvāt | ka evaṃ sati doṣaḥ? iti cet ; tathā ca pramāṇābhāvena tathāvidhajanmatvāniścayādatādṛśādapi janmāśaṅkāyāṃ tādṛśasya dhūmāderagnyādinā'nvayavyatirekau na niścitāviti kutaḥ kāryahetorgamakatvam? | na hi yo 'sāveko deśakālāvasthāniyato 'gniviśeṣahetuko dhūmo 'dhigataḥ pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ tasyaivānvayavyatirekau pratipattavyau | tasya deśāntarādāvasambhavāt | kiṃ tarhi? | tādṛśasya sāmānyātmana eva liṅgatvāt tasya cātathāvidhādapi janmāśaṅkāyāṃ kutastathāvidhenānvayo vyatireko vā? | taduktam-
children.translated_text: ) — because of the absence of a distinguishing feature. What fault is there if this is so? And thus, because of the non-ascertainment of being born from such a kind [of cause] due to the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), when there is the apprehension that [it might be] born even from something unlike [the established cause], the positive and negative concomitance of such smoke and the like with fire and the like are not ascertained — so whence the indicative function of the effect-reason? For it is not the case that the positive and negative concomitance of that very smoke, known through perception and non-apprehension as being caused by a particular fire restricted to a specific place, time, and condition, are to be understood [only for that particular instance]. Since its occurrence from another place is not impossible. What then? [The concomitance is] of such a kind [of smoke in general].

body.translated_text: Here, anticipating the opportunity for the opponent's statement, he says: "Of some" — smoke and the like — "at some time" — at a certain time — "from some" — fire and the like — "even when there is existence," "every" — smoke and the like — "of such a kind" — of the same type as the one seen to arise from fire and the like on one occasion — "born from such" — that which was seen once [arising] from such [a cause], that very kind of birth belongs to it. "Whence is it [known] that it is born from such a kind [of cause]?" — from what <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) is this ascertained? Such that one says 'positive and negative concomitance are the basis for establishing the cause-effect relationship with respect to the cause of the effect.' Thus,

body.text:
"avasthādeśakālānāṃ bhedād bhinnāsu śaktiṣu |
bhāvānāmanumānena pratītiratidurllabhā ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "Given the difference of conditions, locations, and times, and the consequent difference of capacities among entities, the cognition through inference is extremely difficult to obtain" — thus [says the opponent].

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "na, atadbhāvinaḥ" ityādi | evaṃ manyate- ihaikadā dhūmāderagnyādisāmagrījanyatayā pratyākṣānupalambhābhyāṃ niścitarūpatve 'pi tādṛśasyātādṛśādapi bhāvaḥ samāśaṅkyate yathāparidṛṣṭādanyatvena | tatra yo 'sāvagnyādisāmagrījanyo dhūmaviśeṣa ekadā niścitastadapekṣayā yathānyo dhūmaviśeṣastādṛśo yo 'nyādṛśādapi- bhāvānāṃ vicitraśaktitayā- bhavediti śaṅkayate, tathā so 'pyekadāgnyādisāmagrījanyatayā niścitastadanyāpekṣayā tādṛśa eva | tatra yadi tadanyasya tādṛśasyātādṛśājjanma syāt tadā tādṛśasya svabhāvasya nāgnyādisāmagrījanyasvabhāvateti paridṛṣṭasyāpi dhūmasya nāgnyādisāmagrī kāraṇamityāyātam | tādṛśasya svabhāvasyāgnyādisāmagrīvilakṣaṇakāraṇajanyasvabhāvatvāt | tataścāgnyādisāmagryā akāraṇatvāt yo mayaikadā tato bhavan dṛṣṭo dhūmaḥ so 'pi na bhavet | nahi yad yasya kāraṇaṃ na bhavati tat tataḥ sakṛdapi jāyate, tasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgāditi | "atadbhāvinaḥ" iti tacchabdena vivakṣitamagnyādikāraṇaṃ parigṛhyate, na tat atat, tavdilakṣaṇaṃ atādṛśaṃ śakramurddhādikam, atasmād bhavituṃ śīlaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 155.

children.text: ) yasya tasyātadbhāvinastādṛśasya tallakṣaṇasya dhūmavastunaḥ "sakṛdapi" ekadāpi "tataḥ" agnyādeḥ "abhāvād" bhāvavirodhāt | bhavati ca tādṛśo 'gnyādisāmagrītaḥ tatastādṛśasya svabhāvasya tādṛśameva kāraṇamityavagamyate sakṛtpravṛttābhyāmeva pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāmiti kuto vyabhicārāśaṅkā? | tena yādṛśo dhūmo 'gnyādisāmagryā bhavan dṛṣṭaḥ sakṛt tādṛśasya tasya tajjanyasvabhāvatayā tādṛśādeva bhāvāt ‘yatra dhūmastatrāgnyādisāmagrī'; ityanvayavyatirekaniścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) — of that which does not exist in the absence of that — of such a smoke-entity of that character — "not even once" — not even at one time — "from that" — from fire and the like — "because of [its] absence" — because of the impossibility of existence [without fire]. And such [smoke] does arise from an aggregate of fire and the like; therefore it is understood that a nature of such a kind has a cause of just such a kind — through perception and non-apprehension operating even on a single occasion. So whence the suspicion of deviation? Therefore, whatever smoke is seen once to arise from an aggregate of fire and the like — of such [smoke], because of its nature of being produced by that, its existence is only from such [a cause],

body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis says: "No, of that which does not exist in the absence of that" and so on. He thinks thus: even when the nature of smoke and the like has been ascertained through perception and non-apprehension as being produced by an aggregate [of causes] such as fire and the like, the existence of such [smoke] even from something unlike [fire] is suspected — as being different from what has not been observed. Therein, that particular smoke which was once ascertained as produced by an aggregate of fire and the like — with respect to that, another particular smoke of such a kind that might also exist from something of a different kind — because of the varied capacities of entities — thus one suspects; and likewise, that [fire-aggregate] too, which once [produced smoke],

body.text: athavānyathā vyākhyāyate- iha pratyakṣānupalambhanibandhanā kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhiḥ prāguktā tannibandhanāvanvayavyatirekau pratipādayitum, taccāyuktam | tathā hi- "kasyacit" dhūmasyāgnyādisāmagryanantarabhāvina ādyasya "kadācit" prathamotpādakāle "kutaścid" agnyādisāmagryāḥ "bhāve 'pi" utpāde 'pi "sarvastādṛśo" yādṛśaḥ prathamakṣaṇabhāvī dhūmo dvitīyādikṣaṇeṣvapi tādṛśaḥ pratyakṣata eva tasya pūrvakṣaṇāvilakṣaṇatayā pratīteḥ | "tathāvidhajanmā" iti yathāvidhādagnīndhanasāmagrīlakṣaṇāt kāraṇādādyo dhūmakṣaṇa utpannastathāvidhājjanma yasya sa "tathāvidhajanmetyetat kutaḥ" naiva tasya dhūmāderabhāvāt | evaṃ ca yadyato dṛṣṭaṃ tasyānyato 'pi bhāvasya darśanāt sarvatrānāśvāsa iti manyamāna āha- "tathā ca" anagnito dhūmādapi dhūmasya bhāve śakramūrddhāderapi tasya bhāvāvirodhādagninā dhūmasya nanvayavyatirekāviti cenmanyase iti pūrvapakṣāśaṅkā |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, [this passage] is explained in another way: here, the establishment of the cause-effect relationship based on perception and non-apprehension was stated earlier. In order to demonstrate the positive and negative concomitance based on that, and [to show] that this [objection] is inappropriate — for: "of some" — of the first smoke that exists immediately after an aggregate of fire and the like — "at some time" — at the time of first arising — "from some" — from an aggregate of fire and the like — "even when there is existence" — even when there is production — "every one of such a kind" — a smoke that is of the same kind as the smoke existing at the first moment is of such a kind in the second and subsequent moments too, by direct perception itself, that [smoke] previously [known] —

body.text: taduktam-
body.translated_text: It has been said:

children.translated_text: "If [things are] momentary, how do entities have their existence dependent on something [else] in certain cases?
In the absence of the well-known cause, their existence from something else [is possible].

body.text:
ataścānagnito mād yathā dhūmasya sambhavaḥ |
śakramūrdvnastathā tasya kena vāryeta saṃbhavaḥ ||"iti |
body.translated_text: And therefore, just as the arising of smoke might be from something other than fire, likewise, who can prevent its arising from the head of <s>Indra</s>?" — thus [says the opponent].

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- nāgnīndhanasāmagrījanyo yādṛśo dhūmastādṛśa eva dhūmādapi bhavati kāraṇabhedena | kutaścit sāmyāt (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 156.

children.text: ) sarūpatayāvasīyamānasyāpyanyādṛśatvāt | tādṛśo hyagnīndhanasāmagrīkṣaṇāntarajanya ādya evāparaḥ kṣaṇastathā tadanya ādya evāparāgnīndhanasāmagrījanya iti tādṛśasya dhūmasya dhūmādasambhavāt na kvacidanāśvāsaḥ kāryaḥ | tathā yādṛśo dvitīyakṣaṇabhāvī prathamadhūmakṣaṇajanito dhūmakṣaṇastādṛśo 'paraprathamadhūmakṣaṇajanita eva dvitīyo dhūmakṣaṇo na tṛtīyādiḥ | evaṃ tṛtīyakṣaṇādiṣvapyaṅkurādiṣu ca sarvatra vācyam | kutaḥ punarayaṃ vibhāgaḥ? iti cet, āha- "atadbhāvinaḥ" atasmād- anagnīndhanādirūpād dhūmād bhavanaśīlasya prathamakṣaṇāvilakṣaṇasya dhūmasya "sakṛdapi" ekadāpi "tataḥ" agnyādisāmagryāḥ "abhāvāda" bhāvāyogād | yathā hi prathamakṣaṇāpekṣayā dvitīyastādṛśastathā tadapekṣayā prathamo 'pīti tādṛśatvāviśeṣāt tādṛśasyānagnito bhāve tādṛśo nāgnijanyasvabhāvaḥ iti sakṛdapi tato na bhavet | bhavan vā tajjanyasvabhāvatāmātmānastādṛśaḥ khyāpayatīti kuto 'nyādṛśād bhavet? tasmādanyādṛśād bhavannanyādṛśa eva tato na vyabhicāraḥ |
children.translated_text: ) even though [smoke] is ascertained as having the same form, it is of a different kind. For the first [smoke] that is of such a kind (<s>tādṛśa</s>) is indeed produced by a subsequent moment of the aggregate of fire and fuel, and the second one is likewise just the first [type] produced by another aggregate of fire and fuel. Since such smoke (<s>tādṛśa dhūma</s>) cannot arise from [other] smoke, there should be no cause for doubt anywhere. Similarly, the smoke-moment that exists at the second moment, produced by the first smoke-moment — one of such a kind (<s>tādṛśa</s>) — the second smoke-moment is produced only by another first smoke-moment, not by a third and so on. The same should be stated for the third moment and so on, and for sprouts and the like everywhere. If asked: whence then comes this distinction? — he says: "<s>atadbhāvinaḥ</s>" (of that which does not arise from that) — of smoke that is disposed to arise from that which is not of the form of fire-and-fuel and the like, which is dissimilar to the first moment, "even once" (<s>sakṛd api</s>), "from that" (<s>tataḥ</s>), i.e., from the aggregate of fire and the like, "because of the absence" (<s>abhāvāt</s>), i.e., because of the impossibility of arising. For just as the second [moment] is of such a kind (<s>tādṛśa</s>) relative to the first moment, so too the first is [of such a kind] relative to that [second]. Since there is no difference in being-of-such-a-kind (<s>tādṛśatva</s>), if what is of such a kind were to arise from something other than fire, then what is of such a kind would not have the nature of being fire-produced — hence it would not arise from that even once. Or, if it does arise, it would declare its own nature as having the nature of being produced by that — so how could it arise from something of a different kind? Therefore, arising from something of a different kind, it would be only of a different kind from that — hence there is no deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>).

body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis says: not [so]; whatever smoke is produced by an aggregate of fire and fuel — one of exactly such a kind does not arise even from smoke [itself], because of the difference of causes. Because of a certain similarity (

body.text: 4. bhinnakāraṇajanyānāṃ dhūmānāṃ atādṛśatve 'pi sādṛśyāt tādṛśatvābhimānaḥ |
body.translated_text: 4. Although smoke-instances produced by different causes are not of such a kind (<s>tādṛśa</s>), because of similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>) there is the false attribution of being of such a kind (<s>tādṛśatva</s>).

body.text: nanu sarveṣāṃ dhūmakṣāṇānāṃ kaṇṭhakṣaṇanākṣisrutikālīkaraṇādikāyāmarthakriyāyāmupayogāt kathaṃ tādṛśasvabhāvatā na syāt? | na, tasyā apyarthakriyāyāḥ kṣaṇabhedopadhīyamānarūpāyāḥ tādṛśatvābhāvāt tatrāpi tulyadoṣatvāt | kathaṃ tarhi loke sarvatra dhūmavyavahāraḥ iti cet; sadṛśāparabhāvanibandhanaikatvādhyavasāyavaśāt kṣaṇiarvyavahārāyogācca | sādṛśye sati kathaṃ na tādṛśatā? iti cet | tādṛśādanyatvāt sadṛśasya | tathā hi- gosadṛśo bhavati gavayaḥ na tu tādṛśaḥ, gorevāparasya tādṛśatvāt | paramārthenātādṛśe 'pi tādṛśābhimāno mandamatīnāṃ bhavan kathaṃ nivārtyet? | tathā hi- tattvādhyavasāyo 'pi tāvad- atasminnarvāgdṛśāṃ vinivārayituṃ na pāryate, kimaṅga punastādṛśatvādhyavasāyaḥ? yathoktam-
body.translated_text: Objection: since all smoke-moments are useful in causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) such as irritating the throat, making the eyes water, blackening, and so forth, how could they not have the nature of being of such a kind (<s>tādṛśa</s>)? No, because that causal efficacy too, whose form is constituted by the distinction of moments, lacks being-of-such-a-kind (<s>tādṛśatva</s>), there being the same fault there as well. If asked: then how is there the conventional usage of 'smoke' everywhere in the world? — [Reply:] it is due to the determination of unity based on the cognition of a subsequent [moment] similar [to the prior one], and because conventional usage regarding momentary things is not possible [otherwise]. If asked: given that there is similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>), how is there no being-of-such-a-kind (<s>tādṛśatā</s>)? — [Reply:] because what is similar (<s>sadṛśa</s>) is different from what is of such a kind (<s>tādṛśa</s>). For example, a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is similar to a cow (<s>go</s>), but not of such a kind, since being-of-such-a-kind belongs to another [individual] that is indeed a cow. In ultimate reality, even when something is not of such a kind, how could one prevent the false attribution of being-of-such-a-kind among those of dull intellect? For even the determination of reality (<s>tattvādhyavasāya</s>) — the superimposition upon what is not that — cannot be prevented among ordinary people; how much less then the determination of being-of-such-a-kind? As it has been said:

body.text:
"samānavarṇasaṃsthāne santāne 'tyatra jāyate |
atasmiṃstanmatiḥ puṃsāṃ kimutaikatra saṃtatau? ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "In a continuum where there is the same color and shape, even across different [continua], there arises in people the cognition of that in what is not that — how much more so within a single continuum?"

body.text: tattvacintakāstu tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇabhedāt tādṛśātādṛśatāṃ bhāvānāṃ anumanyante na tādṛśatām | tad yadyatādṛśādapi tadṛśo bhavet tadā tasya tajjanyaḥ svabhāva ityatadbhāvinaḥ sakṛdapi tato bhāvo na syāt | amumevārthaṃ samarthayamana āha- "parasparāpekṣayā" ityādi | kāraṇāpekṣayā hi janyasvabhāvaṃ kāryam, kāryāpekṣayā ca janakasvabhāvaṃ kāraṇam | yato hi kāraṇād yad bhavad dṛṣṭam tasya tajjanyasvabhāvaḥ, itarasya ca tajjanaka iti pratīyate | anyathā tasya tato bhāvāyogāt, itarasya ca tajjananāyogāt | yadi nāmaivaṃ tataḥ prakṛte kiṃ siddham? ityata āha- "tatra" etasmin nyāye sati "yadi dhūmo" yādṛśa ādyo 'gnyādisāmagrījanitastādṛśo dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvī "agnyādisāmagryā" agnīndhanādikāraṇakalāpāt tajjanakasvabhāvatayā nirddhāritā "danyato"'gnīndhanādisāmagrījanitādādyāddhūmakṣaṇād bhavet | tadā "tasya" tādṛśasya dhūmasvabhāvasya "tajjanyo"'gnyādisāmagrījanyaḥ "svabhāvo na bhavati" kintu dhūmajanya eveti kṛtvā sakṛdapi "tato"'gnyādisāmagrīto "na bhaveta" | tādṛśasya hi svabhāvasyānyato bhāve tajjanyasvabhāvatā, nāgnyādijanyasvabhāvateti kutaḥ sakṛdapi tato bhāvo yujyeta | atra dṛṣṭāntaḥ "arthāntaravad" iti | yathā hyarthāntaramatajjanyābhimatamanyato bhavat na tajjanyasvabhāvaṃ nāgnyādisāmagrījanyasvabhāvamiti sakṛdapi tato na bhavati tadvat tādṛśo dhūmo 'pīti tato bhavannanyādṛśa evāsāviti gamyate |
body.translated_text: But those who investigate reality (<s>tattvacintaka</s>) accept, based on the distinction of causes that are of such a kind and not of such a kind, that things are of such a kind and not of such a kind respectively — not that they are [all] of such a kind. Therefore, if what is of such a kind were to arise even from what is not of such a kind, then its nature would be 'produced by that' — and so what does not arise from that would never arise from that, not even once. Establishing this very point, he says: "<s>parasparāpekṣayā</s>" (with respect to each other) and so forth. For the effect has the nature of being produced relative to the cause, and the cause has the nature of being a producer relative to the effect. That which has been observed to arise from a certain cause — of that, the nature is 'produced by that'; and the other [i.e., the cause] is understood as 'the producer of that.' Otherwise, because the former could not arise from that, and the latter could not produce that. If this is so, then what is established with respect to the matter at hand? — To this he says: "<s>tatra</s>" (in that case) — given this principle, "if smoke" — of such a kind as the first [moment] produced by the aggregate of fire and the like — existing at the second and subsequent moments, "from the aggregate of fire and the like" (<s>agnyādisāmagrī</s>), i.e., from the causal complex of fire, fuel, and so forth, having the nature of being its producer — [if it] were to arise "from another" — from the first smoke-moment produced by the aggregate of fire, fuel, and the like — then "its" — of such a smoke-nature — the nature would "not be produced by the aggregate of fire and the like" (<s>tajjanya</s>), but rather would be produced by smoke only. Hence, not even once would it arise "from that" — from the aggregate of fire and the like. For if the nature of such a kind were to arise from another, its nature would be 'produced by that [other],' not 'produced by fire and the like' — so how could arising from that [fire-aggregate] be justified even once? Here the illustration is: "like something entirely different" (<s>arthāntaravat</s>). Just as something entirely different, considered not to be produced by that [fire-aggregate], arising from another, does not have the nature of being produced by that, nor the nature of being produced by the aggregate of fire and the like — and hence never arises from that — so too smoke of such a kind. Thus, if it arises from that [other source], it is understood to be only of a different kind.

body.text: syānmatam- agnyādisāmagryāsāvatajjanyasvabhāvo 'pi tādṛśo balājjanyate kastasya tapasvino 'parādhaḥ? ityata āha- "nāpi" na kevalaṃ svayamatajjanyasvabhāvatayā tato na bhavet, kintvagnyādisāmagryapi taṃ tādṛśaṃ dhūmaṃ- yādṛśo dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvī- (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 158

children.text: ) na janayet | kutaḥ? | atajjananasvabhāvatvāt | tādṛśasya hyanyato bhāve sa eva tajjananasvabhāvo nāgnyādisāmagrīti tajjananasvabhāvavikalā kathaṃ taṃ janayet? | atrāpyudāharaṇam- "sāmagryantaravaditi" | yathā sāmagryantaramatajjananasvabhāvābhimataṃ na janayati tadvadagnyādisāmagryapi | tathā hi- sā ātmīyaṃ svabhāvamanusṛtyaiva pravartate, tataḥ kuto 'sau sāmagrībalājjāyeta? |
children.translated_text: ) It would not produce [it]. Why? Because it lacks the nature of producing that. For if what is of such a kind were to arise from another, that very [other] would have the nature of producing it, not the aggregate of fire and the like. Being deficient in the nature of producing that, how could it [the fire-aggregate] produce it? Here too the illustration is: "like another aggregate" (<s>sāmagryantaravat</s>). Just as another aggregate, considered not to have the nature of producing that, does not produce [it], so too the aggregate of fire and the like. For that [aggregate] operates only in accordance with its own nature — so how could that [smoke] arise by the force of [another] aggregate?

body.translated_text: One might think: even though [the smoke] is not of the nature of being produced by the aggregate of fire and the like, it is produced as of such a kind by force — what offense has that ascetic committed? To this he says: "<s>nāpi</s>" (nor indeed) — not only would it not arise from that because it itself lacks the nature of being produced by that, but also the aggregate of fire and the like would not produce that smoke of such a kind — the kind that exists at the second and subsequent moments — (

body.text: 5. tādṛśātādṛśajanyatve kāryasyāpi tādṛśātādṛśatvam |
body.translated_text: 5. If the effect is produced by causes both of such a kind and not of such a kind, the effect too would be both of such a kind and not of such a kind.

body.text: syānmatam- agnyādisāmagrījanyasvabhāvo 'pi tādṛśo dhūmo dhūmajanyasvabhāvo 'pi yathā sa eva dhūma indhanajanyasvabhāvo 'gnijanyasvabhāvaścobhayato bhavati | tathā tādṛśo 'pi dhūma ubhayasāmagrījanyasvabhāvatayobhayato bhaviṣyatītyata āha- "na ca" naiva "dhūmasya" tādṛśasya "tadatajjanyaḥ" agnyādisāmagrījanyo dhūmajanyaśca "svabhāvo yuktaḥ" yuktyā saṅgataḥ | kutaḥ? "ekasvabhāvatvāt" tādṛśasya dhūmarūpasya bhedābhāvāt | nahi tasya kālabhede 'pi tādṛgrūpatā bhidyate | bhede hyanyādṛśasyānyādṛśādbhāve vivādāyogāt | tasya yadi tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇajanyatā syāt tatastādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvataiva syāt | tadeva darśayannāha- "dhūmādhūma"- ityādi | dhūmaśabdena yādṛśo 'gnyādisāmagrījanyastādṛśaḥ svabhāvo 'bhipretaḥ, adhūmaśabdenānyādṛśakāraṇajanyo dhūmajanito 'nyādṛśaḥ | tayośca tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇajanyatayaiva tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvatāvagantavyā vakṣyamāṇanītyā | tenāgnidhūmalakṣaṇāt "dhūmādhūmajananasvabhāvāt" tādṛśātādṛśajananasvabhāvāt tādṛśātādṛśatayāsya bhavato dhūmādhūma[svabhāva]stādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvaḥ syāt kutastādṛśa eva? | kuta etat? ityāha- "kāryasvabhāvānām" ityādi | kāryāṇāṃ hi ye svabhāvāḥ parasparāsaṃbhavinaḥ te parasparavilakṣaṇakāraṇasāmagrīsvabhāvakṛtā na svābhāvikā ahetukatvaprasaṅgāt | tatastādṛśātādṛśād bhavato dhūmasya tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvataiva syāt |
body.translated_text: One might think: just as that same smoke, though having the nature of being produced by fire, is also produced by fuel — and thus having the nature of being produced by both fire and fuel, it arises from both — so too, smoke of such a kind, having the nature of being produced by both aggregates, will arise from both. To this he says: "<s>na ca</s>" (nor indeed) — it is not at all "fitting" (<s>yukta</s>), i.e., logically coherent, that "the nature of such smoke" be "produced by both that and not-that" — produced by the aggregate of fire and the like and also produced by smoke. Why? "Because of having a single nature" (<s>ekasvabhāvatva</s>) — because the smoke-form of such a kind is without distinction. For even when there is a difference in time, its being-of-such-a-kind is not divided. If it were divided, there would be no dispute about something of a different kind arising from something of a different kind. If it had the nature of being produced by causes both of such a kind and not of such a kind, then it would have both a nature-of-such-a-kind and a nature-of-not-such-a-kind. Showing this very point, he says: "<s>dhūmādhūma</s>" and so forth. By the word 'smoke' (<s>dhūma</s>) is meant the nature of such a kind, produced by the aggregate of fire and the like; by the word 'non-smoke' (<s>adhūma</s>) is meant what is of a different kind, produced by a cause of a different kind, generated by smoke. And the being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind of those two is to be understood precisely through their being produced by causes of such a kind and of a different kind respectively, by the principle to be stated. Therefore, from what has the nature of producing both smoke and non-smoke — i.e., the nature of producing both what is of such a kind and what is of a different kind — since it [the effect] partakes of both, it would have the nature of both smoke and non-smoke (<s>dhūmādhūmasvabhāva</s>), i.e., both of such a kind and of a different kind — so how could it be exclusively of such a kind? Whence is this? He says: "<s>kāryasvabhāvānām</s>" and so forth. For the natures of effects that are mutually incompatible are brought about by mutually distinct causal aggregates — they are not intrinsic, since otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of being without a cause (<s>ahetuka</s>). Therefore, smoke arising from what is both of such a kind and of a different kind would have both a nature-of-such-a-kind and a nature-of-a-different-kind.

body.text: syānmatam- naiva tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvatāyāṃ tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇāpekṣā, kāryāṇāmutpattimātra eva kāraṇāpekṣaṇādityata āha- "akāraṇāpekṣaṇe ca" tādṛśātādṛśarūpatāyāṃ tādṛśātādṛśa- kāraṇānapekṣaṇe ca tādṛśātādṛśatāyāḥ "ahetukatvaprasaṅgāt" | na hi tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvayorabhūtvā bhāvavyatirekeṇānyā kācidutpattiḥ yatra tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvakāraṇanirapekṣāṇāmapi tadapekṣā syāt | tasmādutpattiśabdena tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvataivocyata iti | tatra kāraṇāpekṣopagame kathaṃ tādṛśātādṛśatāyāṃ kāraṇāpekṣā na syāt | tasmāt sāmagrīṇāṃ tādṛśātādṛśatvādeva kāryāṇāṃ tādṛśātādṛśasvabhāvavibhāga iti kuto 'nyādṛśāttādṛśasambhavaḥ? iti |
body.translated_text: One might think: there is no dependence on causes of such a kind and of a different kind for the being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind [of effects], since effects depend on causes only for their origination. To this he says: "<s>akāraṇāpekṣaṇe ca</s>" (and if there is no dependence on causes) — if there is no dependence on causes of such a kind and of a different kind for the being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind, then there would be "the absurd consequence of being without a cause" (<s>ahetukatva-prasaṅga</s>). For there is no origination of the natures of such a kind and of a different kind other than their coming-into-being from non-being — and it is with respect to that [coming-into-being] that even those not dependent on causes of such a kind and of a different kind would require that dependence. Therefore, by the word 'origination' is meant precisely the being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind. Given this, if one accepts dependence on causes [for origination], how could there not be dependence on causes for being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind? Therefore, it is precisely because of the being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind of the causal aggregates that there is the division of effects into having the nature of such a kind and having a nature of a different kind — so how could what is of such a kind arise from what is of a different kind?

body.text: yattūktaṃ ‘yathaiko dhūmo 'gnīndhanābhyāṃ vilakṣaṇābhyāṃ janyate tathaikalakṣaṇamapi kāryaṃ vilakṣaṇādapi sāmagryantarād bhaviṣyati'; iti | tadayuktam | yato nāsmābhirvilakṣaṇānāṃ janakatvaṃ vāryate janayantyeva paraspavilakṣaṇā api svahetupariṇāmopanidhidharmāṇastadavasthāniyatāḥ tadekaṃ kāryaṃ, tasya tu teṣāṃ ca parasparāpekṣayā janyajanakasvabhāvatāniyamāt tādṛśasya tādṛśādeva janmocyate nānyādṛśāt, tasyātajjananasvabhāvatvāt, tadabhāve 'pyanyato bhavatastadutpattiniyamābhāvāt | aniyame ca kāryakāraṇabhāvāyogāt | yadi tvagnirivendhanopādānopakṛtastadupādānopakṛtaṃ cendhanamiva tadavasthāniyatamatādṛśamapi dhūmādikaṃ tādṛśaṃ dhūmaṃ janayet pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ ca tathāvagamyeta tadāgnyādivat so 'pi tajjananasvabhāvatāniyamāt tādṛśajanakaḥ kena nānumanyeta | tadabhāve 'pi tu tādṛśasya bhāve tayorjanyajanakasvabhāvatāniyamābhāvāt kutaḥ kāryakāraṇatetyahetutaiva tādṛśasyānyādṛśād bhavataḥ syāt | yata evaṃ "tasmāt" so 'gnīndhanādisāmagrīviśeṣo mantavyo "yaḥ" ādya "dhūmajanano" nānyaḥ "sa" dhūma ādyo yaḥ "gnyādisāmagrīviśeṣeṇa" janito nānya a (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 160

children.text: ) iti kṛtvā kāryakāraṇayorevaṃ yathoktena nyāyena janyajanakarūpasya svabhāvasya niyamād yādṛśaṃ yasya kāraṇamekadā pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāmevāvadhāritaṃ "tadvijātīyāt" tato 'nyādṛśāt kāraṇāt "utpattiḥ" tādṛśasya kāryasya "na bhavati" anyādṛśasya eva na vāryata iti |
children.translated_text: ) — therefore, since the nature of being produced-and-producer between cause and effect is fixed in the manner stated, whatever has been ascertained once through perception and non-apprehension (<s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anupalambha</s>) as the cause of something, "from a cause of a different kind" (<s>tadvijātīyāt</s>), i.e., from a cause dissimilar to that, "the origination" of an effect of such a kind "does not occur" — while [the origination] of one of a different kind is not denied.

body.translated_text: As for what was said — 'just as a single smoke is produced by fire and fuel, which are dissimilar to each other, so too a single effect could arise even from another, dissimilar aggregate' — that is incorrect. For we do not deny that dissimilar things have productive capacity. Indeed, even things that are mutually dissimilar — possessing the properties of being transformations and proximate conditions of their own causes, being fixed in that state — do produce that single effect. However, since there is a fixed relationship of produced-and-producer nature between them, relative to each other, it is said that what is of such a kind arises only from what is of such a kind, not from what is of a different kind — because the latter lacks the nature of producing that, and because in its absence, there is no fixed rule that what arises from another should be its product. And without such a fixed rule, the relationship of cause and effect is not possible. But if fire, assisted by the material cause of fuel, and fuel, assisted by the material cause of that [fire] — as if in that fixed state — were to produce smoke and the like of such a kind even from what is not of such a kind, and if this were also ascertained through perception and non-apprehension (<s>pratyakṣa</s> and <s>anupalambha</s>), then just as with fire and the like, that [other cause] too, because of the fixed rule of having the nature of producing what is of such a kind, would be accepted as a producer of such a kind — who would deny it? But if what is of such a kind were to arise in the absence of that [cause], then since there would be no fixed rule of produced-and-producer nature between the two, how could there be a cause-and-effect relationship? — and so the arising of what is of such a kind from what is of a different kind would be without a cause. Since this is so, "therefore" that particular aggregate of fire, fuel, and the like is to be understood as "that which produces smoke" — not anything else — and "that" first smoke which is "produced by the particular aggregate of fire and the like" — not any other (

body.text: tadevaṃ tādṛśātādṛśakāraṇakṛtakatvaṃ tādṛśātādṛśakāryasvabhāvasya pratipādyopasaṃharannāha- "tat" tasmāt yādṛśaṃ kāryaṃ yādṛśāt kāraṇāt dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ niścitamekadā tat t"nna vyabhicarati" tādṛśamanyādṛśānna bhavati | yanaivaṃ "tena" kāraṇena "siddhe kāryakāraṇabhāve" tādṛśasya "kāryasya" tādṛśameva kāraṇamiti niścaye sati yathoditena nyāyena "kāryasya kāraṇena vyāptira"nvayavyatirekarūpā "siddhā" bhavati |
body.translated_text: Thus, establishing that the being-of-such-a-kind and being-of-a-different-kind of the nature of effects is brought about by the distinction between causes of such a kind and of a different kind, he concludes: "<s>tat</s>" (therefore) — whatever effect has been observed to arise from whatever cause, ascertained once through perception and non-apprehension, "it does not deviate" (<s>na vyabhicarati</s>) — such [an effect] does not arise from what is of a different kind. When thus "through that cause, the cause-and-effect relationship is established" — when there is the ascertainment that the cause of an effect of such a kind is only a cause of such a kind — then, by the principle stated, "the pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of the effect by the cause," in the form of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>), "is established."

body.text: "na vijātīyādutpattiriti" dṛṣṭakāraṇavijātīyāt kāraṇādanyādṛśānnotpattirityasamumarthamapratipadyamānaḥ kāryasya vijātīyāt kāraṇānnotpattirityayamatrārtho 'bhimata iti manvānaḥ paraścodayannāha- "nanu" svato "vijātīyādapi" kāraṇāt "kiñcit" kāryaṃ "bhavad dṛṣṭaṃ" tat kathaṃ na vijātīyādutpattirityasya na dṛṣṭavirodhaḥ syāt | kathaṃ yathā ityāha- "tad yathā gomayādeḥ" ādigrahaṇāt śṛṅgacandrakāntādeḥ " śālūkādi" ādigrahaṇāccharodakādi | tathā hi- gomayācchālūkasya bhāvaḥ śṛṅgāccharasya candrakāntādapāma | na ca gomayādikaṃ śālūkāderna vijātīyam tat kimucyate na vijātīyādutpattiḥ iti | siddhāntavādī parasya bhrāṃtatāṃ darśayannāha- "na vijātīyādutpattiḥ" iti | yato hi kāraṇād yad bhavad dṛṣṭaṃ tat tato 'nyādṛśānna bhavati ityayamatrārtho vivakṣitaḥ, na tu kāryavijātīyāditi | na ca tasya vyabhicāraḥ | tadāha- "tathāvidhameva hi" gomayādirūpaṃ "tādṛśaṃ" śālakādīnāmā "dinimittaṃ" śālūkādiprabandhasya ya ādiḥ prathama ārambhakṣaṇaḥ tasya kāraṇamiti kṛtvā śālūkādiprabandhasyāderna kāraṇābhedo (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 161

children.text: ) 'nyādṛśādutpattiḥ | sarvasya tadādergomayādinimittatvāt | yadā tu prabandhena pūrvakṣaṇanimittānāmuttarottarakṣaṇānāṃ santānenotpattilakṣaṇā vṛttirbhavati śarasya tadā śarādbhāvaḥ | tadevaṃ yasya prabandhādeḥ śṛṅgādibhyo bhāvo na tādṛśasya śarādeḥ yasya ca śārādestuduttarottarasya bhāvo na tādṛśasya śṛṅgāderiti na dṛṣṭakāraṇavijātīyāt kāraṇāt tādṛśasya sambhava iti kāryahetoranvayavyatirekaniścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) origination from what is of a different kind, for the beginning of the entire continuum of lotus roots and the like. Since all such beginnings have cow dung and the like as their cause. But when, through the continuum, there is the activity characterized by origination — where subsequent moments have prior moments as their causes — that is the arising of the arrow from [a prior moment of] the arrow [continuum]. Thus, that which is the beginning of a continuum that arises from horn and the like — what is of such a kind, such as the arrow and so forth, [does not arise from horn in the same way]; and that which arises as subsequent moment after subsequent moment [within the arrow continuum] — what is of such a kind does not arise from horn and the like. Hence, what is of such a kind does not arise from a cause of a different kind from the observed cause — and thus the ascertainment of positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) of the <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-reason) [is established].

body.translated_text: Misunderstanding the statement "there is no origination from what is of a different kind" — thinking that the meaning intended here is 'there is no origination of the effect from a cause of a different kind from the effect' rather than the actual meaning 'there is no origination from a cause of a different kind from the observed cause' — the opponent raises an objection, saying: "<s>nanu</s>" (but) — "something" — some effect — "is observed to arise even from a cause of a different kind" (<s>vijātīya</s>) from itself — so how would there not be a contradiction with observation in the statement 'there is no origination from what is of a different kind'? How so? He says: "for example, from cow dung and the like" — the word 'and the like' includes horn, moonstone, and so forth — "a lotus root (<s>śālūka</s>) and the like" — the word 'and the like' includes arrows, water, and so forth. For there is the arising of a lotus root from cow dung, of an arrow from horn, and of water from moonstone. And cow dung and the like are certainly of a different kind from lotus roots and the like — so why is it said 'there is no origination from what is of a different kind'? The proponent, showing the opponent's confusion, says: "there is no origination from what is of a different kind" — the meaning intended here is that whatever has been observed to arise from a certain cause does not arise from what is different from that [cause] — not that [it does not arise from what is] of a different kind from the effect. And there is no deviation from that [principle]. Therefore he says: "for it is precisely that kind of thing" — of the form of cow dung and the like — that is "the cause of the beginning" of things such as lotus roots and the like — the first moment of origination of the continuum of lotus roots and the like — and hence there is no difference of cause, [no] (

body.text: yadāpi śālūkādayaḥ pūrvapūrvasvajātinibandhanā anādisantānapravṛttā iṣyante tadāpi gomayādibhyaḥ keṣāñcidbhāve 'pi tādṛśatvābhāvānna vyabhicāra iti darśayannāha- "asti ca" ityādi | yasya śālūkasantānasya gomayādi kāraṇaṃ yasya ca sarvadā svajātinimittatvaṃ tayorgomayetarajanmanoḥ śālūkayorastyeva svabhāvabhedaḥ parasparamanyādṛśatvaṃ "rūpasyābhede 'pi" sati | tulyākāratve sati kathamanyādṛśatvam? iti cet, āha- "nahi" ityādi | yasmānnākāratulyataiva bhāvānāṃ "tattve" tādṛśatve nimittam yato gomayetarajanmanoḥ śālūkayorākārasāmyāt tādṛśatvameva syānna jātibhedaḥ | kuta etat? ityāha- "abhinnākārāṇāmapi" ityādi | yeṣāmapi hi samānākāratā keṣāñcidbhāvānāṃ teṣāmapi yata ākārādanyato viśeṣājjātibhedo dṛśyate tato nākārasāmyameva jātyekatve nibandhanam | tathā hi- ākārasāmye 'pi kvacit puṣpād bhedo dṛśyate nīletarakusumayoriva sūryayoḥ, kvacitphalāt bandhyetarayoriva karkoṭakyoḥ, kvacid rasād vanyetarayoriva trapuṣayoḥ, kvacid gandhād vṛkṣetaraprabhavayoriva campakayoḥ, kvacit prabhāvāt sparśopayogastraṃsinyoriva haritakyoriti | tasmādākārasāmyanibandhanaṃ yadyapi ‘tadevedam'; iti pratyabhijñānaṃ sajātīyatāṃ goamayetarajanmanoḥ śālakayorūpakalpayati tathāpi vilakṣaṇasāmagrījanyatayā tayorjātibheda evāvagantavyaḥ, naikajātitā | tata eva pratyabhijñānasya bhrāntatayā tatkalpitasya tādṛśatvasyālīkatvāt |
body.translated_text: Even when <s>śālūkas</s> (lotus roots) and the like are accepted as proceeding in a beginningless continuum grounded in their own respective prior kinds, even then, showing that despite the existence of some [lotus roots] arising from cow-dung and the like, there is no deviation because of the absence of being of such a kind, he says: "There is indeed" and so on. Between the <s>śālūka</s> continuum whose cause is cow-dung and the like, and that whose cause is always its own kind — between those two <s>śālūkas</s>, one born from cow-dung and the other [from its own kind], there is indeed a difference of nature, a mutual dissimilarity, "even when there is no difference of form." If [one asks:] when there is similarity of appearance, how can there be dissimilarity? He says: "For not" and so on. Because similarity of appearance alone is not the ground for the "suchness" — the being of such a kind — of entities, such that the similarity of appearance between <s>śālūkas</s> born from cow-dung and those born otherwise would entail being of the same kind rather than a difference of class. Whence this? He says: "Even of those with undifferentiated appearance" and so on. For even among entities that have identical appearance, a difference of class is observed due to some distinguishing feature other than appearance. For although the appearance is similar, in some cases a difference is observed from the flower — as between blue and other-colored <s>sūrya</s> (sunflower) plants; in some cases from the fruit — as between barren and fertile <s>karkoṭakī</s> (bitter gourd) plants; in some cases from the taste — as between wild and cultivated <s>trapuṣa</s> (cucumber) plants; in some cases from the fragrance — as between tree-born and otherwise-born <s>campaka</s> (magnolia) flowers; in some cases from the potency — as between those <s>harītakī</s> (chebulic myrobalan) fruits whose use is in touch and those that cause loosening. Therefore, although recognition based on similarity of appearance fabricates the same-class-ness of <s>śālūkas</s> born from cow-dung and those born otherwise through the judgment 'this is that very thing,' nevertheless, since they are produced by dissimilar aggregates, a difference of class alone is to be understood, not identity of class — precisely because recognition is erroneous and the 'being of such a kind' fabricated by it is unreal.

body.text: 6. vilakṣaṇasāmagryā avilakṣaṇakāryajanakatve doṣāḥ |
body.translated_text: 6. Faults in the production of an undifferentiated effect by a differentiated aggregate.

body.text: yadi punargomayetarādijanmanaḥ śālūkākāderagnidhūmādijanmano vā dhūmādeḥ pratyabhijñāvaśād vilakṣaṇasāmagrīnibandhanatve 'pi samānasvabhāvataiva syāt ko doṣaḥ syāt? ityata āha- "anyathā hi" ityādi | yadi hi yā svajāti [lakṣaṇapratyayāntarasahitā sāmagrī yā ca] svajātinirapekṣā gomayādirūpā śālūkādeḥ, dhūmasya vā yāgnīnadhanādilakṣaṇā yā ca śakramūrdvādisvabhāvā dhūmādyātmikā avi(kā tasyāḥ vi)lakṣaṇāyā api sāmagryā avilakṣaṇaṃ tādṛśameva kāryaṃ dhūmaśālūkādikamutpadyeta tadā na ‘kāraṇasya'; sāmagrīrūpasya "bhedābhedābhyāṃ" vailakṣaṇyāvailakṣaṇyābhyāṃ kāryasya "bhedābhedau" vailakṣaṇyāvailakṣaṇye tajjātīyavijātīyātmake syātāmiti kṛtvā "viśvasya" sakalasya padārtharāśeḥ "ahetukau bhedābhedau" sajātīyavijātīyatve syātām | tasmād yatra vilakṣaṇā sāmagrī tatra kutaścit sāmyāt sarūpatve 'pi vijātīyataiva kāryasyeti |
body.translated_text: But if, due to the force of recognition, the <s>śālūka</s> and the like born from cow-dung and the like, or smoke and the like born from fire and the like, were of identical nature despite being grounded in a dissimilar aggregate — what would be the fault? To this he says: "For otherwise" and so on. For if the aggregate that includes a condition characterized by its own kind and the aggregate characterized by cow-dung and the like that is independent of its own kind [produce the same result] for <s>śālūkas</s> and the like, or for smoke the aggregate characterized by fire, fuel, and the like and that [arising from] the head of <s>Indra</s> —

body.text: nanu dhūmendhanādisāmagrībhede 'pi dhūmasya na jātibhedamāmananti vidvāṃsaḥ, atadrūpaparāvṛtterubhayatra samānatvāt, naiṣa doṣaḥ, kṣaṇabhedāśrayasūkṣmāvāntarajātibhede 'pi sthūlasantānāśrayavijātīyavyāvṛtteḥ samānatvāt | śābaleyādyavāntarajātibhedepyagovyāvṛttinibandhanagojātivad gavāṃ sarvadhūmānāmekasantānavyavasthāvyu(pyu)pādānakāraṇakṣaṇabhede 'pyekākārapratyayanibandhanatayā samānatvāt | ādyasyendhanaprabhavasya katham? iti cet | na | indhanajātyanuvidhānāt sarvadhūmānām | tathā hi- agurukarpūracandanādijātibhedamanukurvantyeva taddhūmāḥ, kāsaśvāsādiharadravyanirmitavartibhedaṃ ca taddhūmāḥ, tadrasavīryavipākānuvidhānāt | na cākārānyatayā vijātīyatvam, yato nākāra'bhedabhedanibandhena sajātīyavijātīyatve | nahi śālyaṅkurādayaḥ (

children.translated_text: ) — they imitate the appearance of that seed and the like. And they do experience the belonging to that class, grounded in the exclusion from non-rice and the like. Therefore, fuel alone is their material cause; distinguished by the special feature imparted by the cooperative conditions such as fire and the like, it produces the smoke-effect and embers and the like, which are of different appearance. Enough with this overextension.

body.translated_text: But [one objects:] even when the aggregate of smoke, fuel, and the like differs, the learned do not acknowledge a difference of class for smoke, since the exclusion from what is not of that nature is the same in both cases. This is not a fault, [the response goes,] because even when there is a subtle sub-class difference based on momentary difference, the exclusion from what is of a different class based on the gross continuum is the same. Just as in the case of sub-class differences such as <s>Śābaleya</s> (piebald cow) and the like, the cow-class based on the exclusion from non-cow [remains the same], so too for all smokes — [even though there is] a difference in the moments of the material cause that serves to establish a single continuum —

body.text: nanu ca yadi nāma sāmagrībhede 'pi kāryasya bhedo na jātaḥ tadā kāraṇabhede satyapi tasyābhāvāt tasyāhetukatāstu, abhedasya tu kimāyātam? yenobhayorahetukatvamucyate ityata āha- "tathāhi" ityādi | yadā hi sāmagrībhede satyapi kāryasya bhedo na jāta iti tasyāhetukatvam- na hi hetau satyabhavataḥ kathañcidapi hetumattopapadyate- tadā yo 'pyasāvabhedaḥ kāryasya so 'pi sāmagryoḥ bhinnatvādasatyabhede jāta iti kutastasyāpi hetumattā? | yathā hi hetau satyabhavato na hetumattā tathā hetāvasatyapi bhavato hetumattā kutaḥ syāt? | hetubhedasyaivābhedanibandhanatvāt na iti cet; na tarhyayaṃ bhedaḥ kvacit padamābadhnīyāt, śālīkodravāderapi hetubhedasyābhedahetutvānnimittamantareṇa kalpanāyāṃ viśeṣābhāvāt | pratibhāsābhedasya ca kutaścid bhrāntinimittāt paramārthato bhede 'pyupalakṣaṇāt | syādetat- yo hyatādṛśādapi tādṛśodbhavamicchati tasya bhedābhedayorahetukatvamiṣṭameva bhāvā eva kevalaṃ hetumanta ityata āha- "tadvyatiriktaśca" ityādi | nahi bhedābhedavyatiriktaḥ kaścid bhāvānāṃ svabhāvo 'sti yastayorahetukatve 'pi hetumān syāt | tasya tābhyāmanyatve ‘asyemau bhedābhedau'; iti sambandhābhāvaprasaṅgāt, tadanyasambandhakalpanāyāmanavasthādoṣāt, ananyatve 'pi bhedābhedayorbhāvasvabhāvasya ca svātmanyevāvasthānāt anupakārācca kutaḥ sambandhitā? | upakārakalpanāyāṃ ca yadi bhāvasvabhāvaḥ svahetubhya eva na kutaścid bhinno 'bhinno vā samutpanna itīṣyate, tadā tadbhāve 'pi svabhāvānyathātvābhāvāt kuto bhinnābhinnatā bhāvasvabhāvasya syāt? | atha vyatiriktabhedābhedavaśād (

children.translated_text: ) — [if someone says] let a nature that apprehends both difference and non-difference [exist] — if those two [difference and non-difference] are themselves different, then the nature of the entity remains exactly as it was, and there would be no difference or non-difference of it from anything whatsoever in its own form. body.text: 1. vipratipattipradarśanapūrvakamanupalabdhessvarūpam |
body.translated_text: 1. The nature of non-apprehension, preceded by the demonstration of conflicting views.

body.text: tadevaṃ karyahetau yato yadbhavadṛṣṭaṃ sakṛt pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ tādṛśasya sarvasya tathāvidhādeva janma na tadvijātīyadityekasyā api kāryavyakteḥ kutaścid bhāvadarśane vyāptyānvayavyatirekasiddhiriti pratipāditam | anupalabdhau tu yathoktāyāṃ nimittāntarābhāvopadarśananibandhanayornānvayavyatirekayorvipratipattiḥ | svarūpa eva tu pare vipratipadyante | tathāhikecidupalabdhyabhāvamātramanupalabdhimabhāvasya prasajyapratiṣedhātmanaḥ pramāṇāntaratvena gamikāmicchanti īśvarasenaprabhṛtayaḥ, apare tu pratiṣedhyaviṣayajñānarūpeṇāpariṇāmamātmanaḥ tadanyavastuviṣayaṃ vijñānameva vābhāvasya gamakaṃ pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ pramāṇāntaramāhurmīmāṃsakāḥ | na hyanyavastuviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣānumānātmakamabhāvaṃ pratipadyate, tasya bhāvāṃśaviṣayatvāt, abhāvāṃśasya ca tato 'nyatvāt | abhāvāṃśe tu nāstīti jñānaṃ janayat tadabhāvapramāṇākhyāṃ labhate, yathendriyaṃ svaviṣayapratipattijanakatvena pratyakṣākhyām | tathānye anyabhāvalakṣaṇāṃ tajjñānalakṣaṇāṃ vānupalabdhimabhāvasyaiva sādhanamāhurnābhāvavyavahārasya, anupalabdherliṅgādādabhāvasiddhau svayameva tadvyavahārapravṛtteḥ | naiyāyikāstu nāstīti jñānameva kevalapradeśādigrāhijñānantarabhāvipratyakṣaṃ na pramāṇāntaramabhāvasya tuccharūpasya paricchedātmakamācakṣate tadevāsya ghaṭādeḥ pratiṣedhyasyānupalabdhiśabdena yadyucyate na kaścidvirodhaḥ iti | tadevamanupalabdhau bhedaṃ gatā buddhayaḥ prativādināmiti tannirāsārthamanupalabdhisvarūpaṃ tāvadupadarśayannāha- "upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya" ityādi | ‘upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptīḥ'; ‘upalambhapratyayāntarāṇāṃ samanantarādhipatipratyayasaṃjñitānāṃ sākalyam, ālambanapratyayasya svabhāvaviśeṣaśca | yaḥ svabhāvaḥ satsvanyeṣūpalambhapratyayeṣu san pratyakṣa eva bhavatī'tyevaṃrūpā śāstrakṛtānyatra (

children.text: ) vyākhyātā naiyāyikavipratipattinirāsārtham | te hyupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptiśabdena mahāttvānekadravyavattvarūpāṇi dravyāṇāmāhuḥ | "mahattvādanekadravyavattvād rūpāccopalabdhiḥ" iti vacanāt | evaṃ copalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiḥ satyapi vastuni sambhavatītyasadvyvahārasiddhāvanaikāntikītyācakṣate | na hi cākṣuṣasyāpi raśmermahattvānekadravyavattvarūpāṇyupalambhakāni bhavanti | na ca tāvatānupalambha'pyasavdyavahārastatra śakyate kartum | yadāha bhāṣyakāraḥ- ‘nānumānata upalabhyamānasya pratyakṣato 'nupalabdhirabhāve hetuḥ'; iti | indriyatvāt tvagādivat kila prāpyakāri cakṣurityanumānataścākṣuṣo raśmirupalabhyate tasya pratyakṣato 'nupalabdhiḥ kathamabhāvavyavahāraṃ sādhayet? iti | tadevamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānu palabdhimasavdyavahāre 'naikā ntikīmāhurnaiyāyikāḥ tannirāsamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpteraviparītarūpopadarśanena śāstrakāro 'bhyadhāt | yadā hyupalambhapratyayāntarasākalyaṃ svabhāvaviśeṣaśca yathokta upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptirucyate na mahattvādikaṃ tadā kuto vyabhicārāvakāśaḥ?, sati vastuni tasyā asambhavāt | mahattvādikaṃ tvasambhavādeva nopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptiśabdena vācyam | nahi rūpādivyatiriktaṃ dravyaṃ tatpratibhāsavivekinākārāntareṇa svajñāne pratibhāsate | na cāpratibhāsamānamanātmarūpavivekinā rūpeṇa pratyakṣatāmanubhavatyatiprasaṅgāt | tat kuto 'syāsato mahattvādisambhavaḥ? | na ca svarūpeṇāmahataḥ tatsambandhe 'pyasya mahattāsambhavaḥ | apararūpeṇa vā grahaṇe kathaṃ tadgrāhijñānamabhrāntam? | tato na mahattvaṃ dravyasyopalambhakaṃ rūpaṃ vā | tasyāpi svarūpeṇa grahaṇe dravyātmano 'tyantaparokṣatvāt | dravyarūpasya ca tadvivekenānupalakṣaṇānna tathā grāhakatvam | na ca mahattvaṃ rūpaṃ vā dravyodayakāle 'bhyupagamyate, yato dravyaṃ guṇasya samavāyikāraṇamiṣyate | tacca pratilabdhātmakameva tathātāmanubhavatīti prathame kṣaṇe dravyaṃ nirguṇameva | na cāsya dvitīye kṣaṇe prāktanarūpatyāgo 'sti rūpāntaraṃ vāvirbhavati yataḥ prāgapratipannādhārabhāvaṃ (
children.translated_text: for the purpose of refuting the disagreement of the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>. For they say that what is meant by the term <s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s> (fulfillment of the conditions for perception) with respect to substances is magnitude (<s>mahattva</s>), being composed of multiple substances (<s>anekadravyavatva</s>), and color (<s>rūpa</s>). Because of the statement: "Perception [arises] from magnitude, being composed of multiple substances, and color." And thus, the non-apprehension of that which has fulfilled the conditions for perception is possible even when the object exists — hence they declare it to be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) for establishing the convention of non-existence. For even a visual ray, though apprehensible by the eye, does not possess magnitude, being composed of multiple substances, and color as conditions of its apprehension. Yet the convention of non-existence cannot be applied to it merely through non-apprehension. As the author of the <s>Bhāṣya</s> [<s>Vātsyāyana</s>] says: 'The non-apprehension through direct perception of what is apprehended through inference is not a reason for [its] absence.' For the visual ray is apprehended through inference — since it is a sense faculty, like touch etc., the eye must operate through contact — and how could its non-apprehension through direct perception establish the convention of absence? Thus the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> declare that the non-apprehension of what has fulfilled the conditions for perception is inconclusive for [establishing] the convention of non-existence. The author of the treatise [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] refuted this by showing the correct form of <s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>. For when the completeness of the other conditions of apprehension and the specific nature as described are called <s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>, and not magnitude etc., then where is the scope for deviation? — since when the object exists, [non-apprehension fulfilling those conditions] is impossible. And magnitude etc., precisely because they are impossible [as real properties], should not be denoted by the term <s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>. For no substance apart from color etc. appears in its own cognition through a distinct aspect that discriminates its manifestation. And what does not appear [in cognition] does not experience perceptibility through a form that does not discriminate its own nature — because of the absurd consequence [of over-extension]. So how could magnitude etc. belong to what is non-existent? And even if a non-great [thing] is connected with that [magnitude], it cannot thereby become great. Or if it is grasped through another form, how can the cognition grasping it be non-erroneous? Therefore, neither magnitude nor color is the form that makes a substance perceptible. For if [color] were grasped in its own form, the substance-nature would be utterly imperceptible. And since substance-as-color is not discerned distinctly from it, it cannot serve as its apprehender in that way. Moreover, neither magnitude nor color is accepted at the time of the substance's arising, since substance is held to be the inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) of quality. And [a substance] that has already obtained its own nature experiences that status [as cause], so at the first moment the substance is without qualities. And at the second moment there is no abandonment of its prior form, nor does another form arise, such that having previously not attained the status of substratum

children.text: ) mahattvādiguṇapratibandhādādhāratāṃ yāyāt | na cājanaka ādhāraḥ | janakatve ca kṣaṇikatā, arthakriyāvirodhādakṣaṇikasya | tataḥ kutaḥ sāmavāyikāraṇasya sambhavaḥ?, yataḥ svotkalitaṃ kāryaṃ janayat tathā vyapadiśyate | na caitat kṣaṇikatve sambhavati akṣaṇikatve vā prāga'nādhārasya paścādādhārābhāvaḥ | samavāyikāraṇāsambhavādevānekadravyavattvamapyasmabhavi yasmādanekaṃ dravyamārambhakaṃ samavāyikāraṇātmanā yasya vidyate tadevaṃ vyapadiśyate | dravyābhavācca nānekadravyavattvaṃ | sattve 'pi mahattvāderneyamupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptirasmākamabhimatā | yā tvabhimā(ma)tā na tayopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhirasavdyavahārasiddhāvanaikāntikīti śāstrakāro darśayāmbabhūva "upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya" yā "anupalabdhiḥ" kāraṇasya vyāpakasya vā pratiṣedhyādanyasya sā "abhāvahetuḥ" kāryasya vyāpyasya ca "abhāvavyavahārahetuśca" | yā tu pratiṣedhyasyaivopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiḥ sābhāvavyavahārahetureveti vāśabdena darśayati | yā tvanupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhiḥ pratyakṣānumānanivṛttilakṣaṇā sā saṃśayahetuḥ pramāṇanivṛttāvapyarthābhāvāsiddheḥ, nimittābhāvāttu savdyavahārapratiṣedhaheturityavagantavyam |
children.translated_text: it would attain substratum-hood through the obstruction of qualities such as magnitude. And a non-producer is not a substratum. If it were a producer, then momentariness [would follow], since permanence contradicts causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). So how is an inherent cause (<s>samavāyikāraṇa</s>) possible — one that, producing the effect it has projected, is so designated? And this is not possible under momentariness; nor under non-momentariness, since what was previously not a substratum cannot later become a non-substratum. Due to the impossibility of an inherent cause, being composed of multiple substances (<s>anekadravyavatva</s>) is also impossible, since that which has multiple substances as its producers in the capacity of inherent cause is so designated. And since [such] substance does not exist, there is no being-composed-of-multiple-substances. Even if magnitude etc. existed, the <s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s> (fulfillment of perceptibility conditions) intended by us would not be [defined by] it. And with the <s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s> that is intended [by us], the non-apprehension of what has fulfilled the conditions for perception is not inconclusive for establishing the convention of non-existence — this is what the author of the treatise has shown. "The <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) of that which has fulfilled the conditions for perception (<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpta</s>)" — [the non-apprehension] of the cause or of the pervader, or of something other than what is to be negated — is "a reason for [establishing] absence (<s>abhāvahetu</s>)" of the effect or of the pervaded, "and a reason for the convention of absence (<s>abhāvavyavahārahetu</s>)." But that which is the non-apprehension of what is to be negated itself, having fulfilled the conditions for perception — that is a reason only for the convention of absence — this he shows with the word 'or' (<s>vā</s>). But the non-apprehension of what has not fulfilled the conditions for perception — characterized by the cessation of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference) — that is a cause of doubt, since even when the <s>pramāṇa</s> ceases, the absence of the object is not established. However, due to the absence of a ground [for assertion], it is a reason for prohibiting the positive convention — this should be understood.

body.translated_text: Thus, regarding <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-as-reason), it has been demonstrated that since whatever is observed to arise from something once through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) and <s>anupalambha</s> (non-apprehension), all such [things] of that kind originate only from that type and not from anything of a different kind — thus, even from a single instance of an effect being observed to arise from something, the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) through <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) is established. Regarding <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension) as described above, there is no disagreement about <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>, which are grounded in the demonstration of the absence of other causes. But opponents disagree about its very nature. For some, such as <s>Īśvarasena</s> and others, hold that <s>anupalabdhi</s> — which is merely the absence of apprehension, [serving as a means of knowing] absence (<s>abhāva</s>) whose nature is <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (implicative negation) — is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition). Others, the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, say that cognition of something other than the negated object — without transforming into a cognition having the negated object as its content — is the indicator of absence, and is a <s>pramāṇa</s> distinct from <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference). For cognition whose content is another object, being of the nature of perception or inference, does not apprehend absence, since it has the positive aspect of a thing as its object, and the absence-aspect is different from that. But when it generates the cognition 'it is not there' regarding the absence-aspect, it obtains the designation of <s>abhāvapramāṇa</s> (means of knowing absence), just as a sense faculty obtains the designation 'perception' by virtue of generating the apprehension of its own object. Similarly, others say that <s>anupalabdhi</s> — characterized by the existence of another entity, or characterized by the cognition thereof — is a means of establishing absence itself, not of the verbal convention of absence, since upon the establishment of absence through <s>anupalabdhi</s> as a logical mark, the convention [of absence] naturally follows. The <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, however, declare that the cognition 'it is not there' alone — which is a <s>pratyakṣa</s> (direct perception) arising after the cognition grasping merely the bare location etc. — is not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> but is a determiner of absence, which is of a negligible nature. If that very thing is called by the word <s>anupalabdhi</s> with reference to what is to be negated, such as a pot, there is no contradiction. Thus, the views of the opponents regarding <s>anupalabdhi</s> have diverged, and in order to refute them, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] first shows the nature of <s>anupalabdhi</s>, saying "<s>upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasya</s>" and so forth. '<s>Upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāpti</s>' [means]: 'the completeness of the conditions of apprehension designated as <s>samanantara</s> (immediately preceding) and <s>adhipati</s> (dominant) conditions, and the specific nature of the <s>ālambanapratyaya</s> (object-condition). That nature which, when the other conditions of apprehension are present, being [itself] present, would be directly perceived' — such is the definition explained by the author of the treatise elsewhere,

children.translated_text: the producership of anything other than the sense faculties etc. is not possible, since the relation of cause and effect is grounded in <s>anvaya</s> (co-presence) and <s>vyatireka</s> (co-absence), and these two — co-presence and co-absence — are not possible for anything other than the sense faculties etc., because when the sense faculties etc. are present, apprehension invariably occurs. For if, even when the sense faculties etc. are present, apprehension sometimes did not arise, then the non-arising of the effect even when all other causes are present would indicate the deficiency of another condition, and thus an additional cause beyond those would be postulated. But this is not the case. So how could the role of being a cause of apprehension's arising be accepted for the <s>ātman</s> (self)? — because of the absurd consequence [of over-extension]. As [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] says:

body.translated_text: Among those, first, those who hold that <s>anupalabdhi</s> is merely the absence of apprehension, or, because of the statement "or cognition regarding another object," that it is merely cognition of another object — in order to refute them, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>], wishing to show <s>anupalabdhi</s> as characterized by properties of the knower and the knowable, first shows <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension) as twofold, saying: "Here" — in the statement on <s>anupalabdhi</s>, the <s>upalabdhi</s> that is heard, being of the nature of an action, when it is considered from the standpoint of the agent — then, when "the property of the apprehender" is considered, "the cognition of the apprehender" — the cognition belonging to the one who apprehends — is called <s>upalabdhi</s>. And the 'one who apprehends' refers to the aggregate of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>indriya</s> (sense faculty), and <s>deha</s> (body) included in the preceding moment, which is the producer of apprehension. For the agent is said by others to be either the producer or the substratum of apprehension. But

body.translated_text: "When something invariably exists whenever [certain conditions] are present, if one postulates something else [as its cause], then since anything could be a cause of anything, there would be no fixed order among causes."

body.text: āśrayatvamapi janakasyaiveti tadapyātmano na sambhavati | sthāpakatvādāśraya iti cet; na, kṣaṇikatve sthiterabhāvādupalabdherakṣaṇikatve 'pi svayamevāvināśādavasthānāt | tathāhi- upalabdheravināśa eva sthitirucyate na pātābhāvaḥ tasyā gurutvābhāvāt "saṃyogābhāvena gurutvāt patanam" iti ca pareṣāṃ kṛtāntaḥ | samavāyādāśraya iti cet; nanu so 'pi ādhāryādhārabhūtānāmeveṣyate | na cāpatanadharmikāyā upalabdherādhāreṇa kiṃcit, samavāyāccāśrayatve 'nyasyāpi tadbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ, tasya sarvātmasu samānatvāt, ekatvenāsyopagamāt | kramayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhācca nāsyātmanaḥ sattvam, tato 'sya kuto janakatvam? āśrayatvaṃ vā? ityalaṃ kṣuṇṇakṣodīkaraṇeneti |
body.translated_text: Substratum-hood too belongs only to the producer, so that also is not possible for the <s>ātman</s> (self). If [one says] the substratum is so called because it supports — no, because in [the doctrine of] momentariness there is no persistence, and even if apprehension were non-momentary, it would remain on its own without being destroyed. For what is called the 'persistence' of apprehension is simply its non-destruction, not the absence of falling, since it has no heaviness — and the opponents' doctrine is: "falling occurs from heaviness in the absence of conjunction." If [one says] substratum-hood is through <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — but that too is accepted only for things that are container and contained. And for apprehension, which has no property of falling, what use is a substratum? Moreover, if substratum-hood were through inherence, then anything else could also have that status, since [inherence] is the same in all <s>ātmans</s>, because it is accepted as one [universal relation]. And because of the contradiction with causal efficacy through both succession and simultaneity, the existence of this <s>ātman</s> itself is not [established]. So how could it have producership? Or substratum-hood? Enough of grinding what is already ground.

body.text: evamupalabdhimādarśyānupalabdhimādarśayannāha- " tasmādupalabdhijñānādanyā" vastvantaraviṣayā "upalabdhiḥ" jñānātmikā "anupalabdhiḥ" | kathaṃ punarupalabdhirevānupalabdhirucyate? ityāha- "vivakṣite"tyādi | yathā bhakṣyābhakṣyaprakaraṇe vivakṣitād bhakṣyādanyatvād ‘abhakṣyo grāmyakukkuṭaḥ'; bhakṣyo 'pi san tadanyasya- ucyate | yathā ca sparśanīyāsparśanīyādhikāre vivakṣitāt sparśanīyādanyatvād ‘asparśanīyaścāṇḍālādiḥ'- tadanyasya sparśanīyo 'pi san- ucyate | (

children.text: ) tadvadupaladbhirevānupalabdhirmantavyā | nañaḥ pratiṣedhaviṣayatvāt kathaṃ bhāvaviṣayatā? iti cet, āha- "paryudāsavṛttyeti" | paryudāsena pratiṣedhyasyārthasya rvajanena yā viśiṣṭe 'rthe vṛttistayā , nañaḥ āgṛhītapratiṣedhasya bhāvaviṣayatā | yatra vidheḥ prādhānyaṃ pratiṣedho 'rthagṛhītaḥ vidhibhāksvapadena nocyate ekavākyatā ca tatra paryudāsavṛttitā | vidheśca prādhānyaṃ ‘vivakṣitopalabdheranyopalabdhirbhavati'; ityevaṃ vākyenānyopalabdhervidhānāt anyopalabdhisāmarthyādeva vivakṣitopalabdheḥ pratiṣedhaḥ pratīyate | vivakṣitopalabdheranivartane tadapekṣayānyasyā vidhānāyogāt svapadena nañā vidhibhāṅ nocyate | kiṃ tarhi? | anyaśabdena paryudāsāśrayeṇānyaśabdasyaiva vākye prayogāt anyā upalabdhiranupalabdhiriti | nañaśca subantena sāmarthyaṃ na tiṅantena ityekavākyatvaṃ ‘na upalabdhiranupalabdhiḥ'; iti | prasajyapratiṣedhaḥ punaretadviparīto mantavyaḥ | tatra hi pratiṣedhasya prādhānyaṃ vidhirarthād gamyate vākyabhedaḥ svapadena nañā pratiṣedhabhāk sambadhyate |
children.translated_text: In the same way, <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension) itself should be understood as <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension). If [one objects]: since the negative particle (<s>nañ</s>) has negation as its scope, how can it have a positive entity as its object? — he answers: "through the <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion) function." Through <s>paryudāsa</s>, by the inclusion of the meaning to be negated, the function that applies to a qualified meaning — through that [function], the negative particle, whose negation is contextually implied, has a positive entity as its object. Where the positive injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) is primary and the negation is contextually understood, [where] the negation is not expressed by its own word as subsidiary to the injunction, and [where] there is syntactic unity — there the <s>paryudāsa</s> function applies. And the primacy of the injunction [is established] because by the sentence 'the apprehension of something other than the intended apprehension occurs,' the other apprehension is positively enjoined, and the negation of the intended apprehension is understood solely through the force of the other apprehension. Since without the cessation of the intended apprehension, the injunction of another in relation to it would be pointless — [the negation] is not expressed by its own word, the negative particle, as subsidiary to the injunction. Rather, through the word 'other' (<s>anya</s>), which serves as the basis for <s>paryudāsa</s> — since the word 'other' itself is used in the sentence — 'other apprehension is non-apprehension.' And the negative particle has syntactic connection with a nominal form, not with a verbal form — thus the syntactic unity is: 'non-apprehension is non-apprehension.' <s>Prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation), on the other hand, should be understood as the opposite of this. For there the negation is primary, the injunction is understood from context, there is sentence-division, and by its own word the negative particle is connected with what partakes of negation.

body.translated_text: Having thus shown <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension), [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] now shows <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), saying: "Therefore, <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension) that is other than the cognition of apprehension" — having another object as its content, being of the nature of cognition — "is <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension)." But how can apprehension itself be called non-apprehension? To this he says: "<s>vivakṣita</s>" and so forth. Just as in the context of edible and inedible [foods], because of being other than the intended edible, 'a domestic fowl is inedible' — though it is itself edible, it is so called because of being other than that [intended edible]. And just as in the context of touchable and untouchable, because of being other than the intended touchable, 'a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> etc. is untouchable' — though he is himself touchable, being other than that [intended touchable], he is so called.

body.text: tadevaṃ jñātṛdharmalakṣaṇāmanupalabdhiṃ vyākhyāya jñeyadharmalakṣaṇāṃ pratipādayannāha- "upalabhyamānadharmatve" ityādi | yadā karmasthakriyāpekṣayopalabhyamānasya vastuno dharma upalabdhirvivakṣyate tadā viṣayasvabhāva upalabdhirmantavyā | kīdṛśo viṣayasvabhāvaḥ? ityāha- "svaviṣaye"tyādi | pratiṣedhyasya ghaṭāderyadātmaviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ tajjanane yā yogyata tallakṣaṇo viṣayasvabhāva upalabdhiśabdenocyate | yadi viṣayasvabhāva upalabdhiḥ, kathaṃ yogyatālakṣaṇaḥ? | tathā hi yogyatā dharmaḥ, dharmadharmiṇośca bheda eva ityata āha- "yogyatāyāḥ" ityādi | yogyatā hi paramārthato bhāvarūpaiva na vasturūpāda bhidyate, anyathā bhāvo yogya eva na syāt | yogyatāsyeti ca sambandhābhāvato na syāt | sambandhakalpanāyāmanavasthetyuktaprāyam |
body.translated_text: Having thus explained <s>anupalabdhi</s> characterized by a property of the knower (<s>jñātṛdharma</s>), [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] now teaches [<s>anupalabdhi</s>] characterized by a property of the knowable (<s>jñeyadharma</s>), saying: "<s>upalabhyamānadharmatve</s>" and so forth. When <s>upalabdhi</s> is intended as a property of the object being apprehended, considered from the standpoint of the action as it relates to the object (<s>karmastha</s>), then <s>upalabdhi</s> should be understood as the nature of the object (<s>viṣayasvabhāva</s>). What kind of object-nature? To this he says: "<s>svaviṣaye</s>" and so forth. The capacity (<s>yogyatā</s>) to produce the cognition whose content is the object itself — such as a pot etc. that is to be negated — that object-nature characterized [by such capacity] is called by the word <s>upalabdhi</s>. If object-nature is <s>upalabdhi</s>, how is it characterized by capacity? For capacity is a property, and there is indeed a difference between property and property-bearer — to this he says: "<s>yogyatāyāḥ</s>" and so forth. For capacity, in ultimate reality, is of the nature of a positive entity and does not differ from the nature of the thing; otherwise, the entity would not be capable at all. And 'it has capacity' — this relation would not hold due to the absence of a connection. And if a connection were postulated, there would be an infinite regress — this has been stated previously.

body.text: tadevamupalabherviṣayadharmatāṃ pratipādyānupalabdherapi pratipādayannāha- "tasmādanyaḥ" ityādi | "tasmāt" pratiṣedhyād ghaṭādeḥ (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 172
