children.text: ) svaviṣayajñānajananayogyād yo 'nya upalambhajananayogya eva na tadviparītaḥ svabhāvo ghaṭaviviktapradeśarūpaḥ sa eva cātrānupalabdhiśabdenocyate | prāktanameva nyāyamatrādiśannāha- "pūrvavaditi |" vivakṣitopalabdheranyatvādabhakṣyāsparśanīyavat paryudāsavṛtyeti | kathaṃ punarayaṃ naña anyārthavṛttiḥ sāmānyaśabdaḥ san ghaṭaviviktapradeśasya tajjñānasyaiva vā ghaṭaviviktasyānupalabdhitvaṃ paryudāsavṛttyā prakalpayati, na punaraviśeṣeṇa sarveṣāmevānyaśabdavācyānām? ityata āha- "yatra yasmin" ityādi | "yatra" deśe kāle 'vasthāyāṃ vāvyavadhānādilakṣaṇāyām, "yasmin" pradeśarūpādau "upalabhyamāne niyamena" avaśyaṃtayā "yasyānyasya" padārthasya ghaṭarūpāderupalabdhirbhavati "sa" ghaṭarūpādiḥ padārthaḥ "tatsaṃsṛṣṭaḥ" tena pradeśarūpādinā saṃsṛṣṭaḥ | kathamekasminnupalabhyamāne parasyāpi niyamopalabdhiḥ? iti cet, yogyatāyā aviśeṣāt | pradeśaghaṭayorhi svaviṣayavijñānajanane yogyatā tulyā | yadā hi pradeśarūpaṃ vyavadhānaviprakarṣādirahitaṃ vijñāne svākāraṃ samarpayati tadā ghaṭarūpamapi tatra tathāvidhaṃ svākāraṃ samarpayatyeva | yadi nāma yogyatā tasya tena tulyā svasvabhāvavyavasthitestu kathaṃ tatsaṃsṛṣṭatā? ityata āha- "ekajñānasaṃsargādi"ti | ekatra hi jñāne dvāvapi tau svākāradvāreṇa saṃsṛṣṭau na sākṣāt, tadvijñānaṃ padārthadvayākāramājāyamānaṃ tayorātmani saṃsargaṃ darśayati | kimiti punastat jñānaṃ padārthadvayākāramavaśyaṃ bhavati yatastayorjñānadvārakaḥ saṃsargaḥ? ityata āha- "tayoḥ satoḥ" ityādi | yāvetau tulyayogyatārūpau tau yadi santau bhavatastadā naivaikākāraniyatā pratipattirbhavati | kasmāt? asambhavāt | na hyeṣa sambhavo 'sti- yattulyayogyatārūpayoreka eva pratibhāseta nāpara iti | tathāhi- aviśiṣṭatvād yogyatāyāḥ kastatra svākāraṃ na samarpayet? | anubhavasiddhaṃ ca yugapadanekapratibhāsanam | na cānubhavaviruddhamācakṣāṇā viduṣāmavadheyavacaso bhavanti | ladhuvṛttitvād yaugapadyābhimāna iti cet; na, bādhakapratyayaviraheṇa (
children.translated_text: ) that which is other than what is capable of producing cognition of its own object — [that other] which is merely capable of producing apprehension, not the opposite of that — [namely] a nature which is the location devoid of the pot — that alone is here referred to by the word '<s>anupalabdhi</s>' (non-perception). Indicating the previously [established] reasoning here, he says: "as before." Because it is other than the intended apprehension, it is through <s>paryudāsa</s> (nominally bound exclusion), like [the injunction regarding] what is not to be eaten or touched. But how does this negative particle, being a general term functioning in the sense of 'other,' establish — through <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion) — the status of non-perception only for the location devoid of the pot, or only for the cognition of that [location] devoid of the pot, and not indiscriminately for all things expressible by the word 'other'? To this he says: "where, in which" and so on. "Where" — in the place, time, or condition characterized by the absence of obstruction and the like — "in which" — in the location and the like — "when [that] is being apprehended, necessarily" — with certainty — "of which other" — entity such as a pot — "there is apprehension, that" — entity such as a pot — "is conjoined with that" — is conjoined with that location and the like. How is it that when one is being apprehended, there is necessarily apprehension of the other as well? If so asked: because there is no distinction in capacity. For the location and the pot have equal capacity to produce cognition of their own objects. When the form of the location, free from obstruction, distance, and the like, imparts its own aspect to cognition, then the form of the pot too, being of such a nature there, necessarily imparts its own aspect [to cognition]. Even if its capacity is equal to that [of the location], how can there be conjunction with that, given that each is established in its own intrinsic nature? To this he says: "conjunction in a single cognition" and so on. For in a single cognition, both of those two are conjoined through the medium of their own aspects, not directly; that cognition, arising with the aspects of both objects, reveals their conjunction within itself. But why must that cognition necessarily have the aspects of both objects, such that their conjunction is mediated through cognition? To this he says: "when both of them exist" and so on. When these two, which are of the nature of equal capacity, exist, then there is never an apprehension restricted to a single aspect alone. Why? Because of impossibility. For there is no such possibility — that of two things of equal capacity, only one would appear and not the other. For thus: given that the capacity is undifferentiated, which one there would not impart its own aspect? And the simultaneous appearance of multiple [objects] is established by experience. And those who assert what contradicts experience are not persons whose words are to be heeded by the learned. If [one objects that] the impression of simultaneity is due to the rapid succession of [momentary cognitions] — no, because in the absence of a sublating cognition (
<s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 173.

children.text: ) bhrāntikalpanānupapatteḥ, sarvatra tathābhāvāprasaṅgāt | karaṇadharma evāyaṃ yadekasminneva karmaṇi kriyāṃ niṣpādayatinānekatra, karaṇaṃ cendriyaṃ tato nānekapratipattiheturiti cet, kathaṃ pradīpādiranekatra bahūnāṃ pratipattijanakaḥ? | kartṛbhedādadoṣa iti cet; kartrekatvāt tarhi kriyaikatra karmaṇīti kathaṃ ‘karaṇadharmaḥ'; ityādi vaco na plavate? | na ca pratikṣaṇaviśarāruṣu bhāveṣu paramārthataḥ kartṛkaraṇādibhāvo yuktaḥ kriyā vā kācit | na ca sarvakārakānvayavyatirekānuvidhāyini kārye kasyacidatiśayo 'sti yenāyaṃ kartā kā(ka)raṇaṃ cedamityādi parikalpyeta | tasmādaviśiṣṭayogyatayoḥ kuta ekarūpaniyatāyāḥ pratipatteḥ sambhavaḥ? iti siddha ekajñānasaṃsargaḥ | tulyayogyatārūpatvasya caitadeva liṅgam | na hyasati tulyayogyatārūpatve yugapadekendriyajanitajñānapratibhāsitā rūparasavat sambhavatīti |
children.translated_text: ) the supposition of error is untenable, and because the same consequence would apply everywhere. [If one argues:] 'It is a property of the instrument that it accomplishes action with respect to only one object, not many; and the instrument is the sense-faculty, therefore it is not the cause of multiple apprehensions' — [we reply:] then how does a lamp and the like produce apprehension of many things in many [locations]? If [one replies:] 'There is no fault because of the difference of agents' — then, since the agent is one, [and you say] the action is with respect to one object only, how does the statement 'it is a property of the instrument' stand? Such words do not hold up. Nor is the agent-instrument distinction ultimately tenable with respect to entities that perish at every moment, nor is there any action whatsoever. And in an effect that conforms to the presence and absence of all <s>kārakas</s> (case-relations), no one [factor] has any superiority by which one might construct [the designations] 'this is the agent, this is the instrument,' and so on. Therefore, given that the two have undifferentiated capacity, whence the possibility of an apprehension restricted to a single form? Thus the conjunction in a single cognition is established. And this itself is the mark of [their] being of the nature of equal capacity. For without being of the nature of equal capacity, simultaneous appearance in a cognition produced by a single sense-faculty would not be possible, as [it would not be possible] for form and taste [which are perceived by different faculties].

body.translated_text: Having thus taught that <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension) has the character of being a property of the object, [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] now teaches the same for <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension), saying: "<s>tasmādanyaḥ</s>" and so forth. "From that" — from what is to be negated, such as a pot etc.

body.text: tatra yeṣāṃ saugatānāmidaṃ darśanaṃ ‘ekāyatanasaṅgṛhīte 'nekatrāpyekamevendriyajñānamājāyate'; iti teṣāṃ mukhya evaikajñānasaṃsargaḥ | ye tu ‘tatrāpi pratyarthaṃ bhinnānyevaikendriyanimittānyekakālāni tadviṣayāṇāṃ yugapatsannihitānāṃ svajñāneṣu sāmarthyāviśeṣāt, ata evaikatayā loke 'dhyavasīyamānāni jñānānyupajāyante'; iti varṇayanti teṣāmekendriyajatvenaikāyatanaviṣayatvena caikakāleṣvekatvavyapadeśo loke tathādhyavasāyādaupacārikaḥ |
body.translated_text: Among those <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) who hold the view that 'with respect to multiple [objects] included in a single <s>āyatana</s> (sense-base), only a single sense-cognition arises' — for them, the conjunction in a single cognition is primary. But those who maintain that 'even there, for each object, distinct cognitions caused by a single sense-faculty arise simultaneously with respect to simultaneously present objects of that [faculty], due to the non-difference in their capacity; and for that very reason, these cognitions, being apprehended as one in the world, arise [appearing as one]' — for them, the designation of oneness with respect to [cognitions that are] simultaneous, by virtue of being produced by a single sense-faculty and having objects belonging to a single <s>āyatana</s>, is figurative, due to such apprehension in the world.

body.text: yadi nāmaikajñānasaṃsargāt tatsaṃsṛṣṭastathāpi sāmānyena sarvamanyamayaṃ nañ kinna pratipadayati? iti, ata āha- "tasmāt" ityādi | yasmādaviśiṣṭatvādyogyatāyā yathoktena prakāreṇaikatra jñāne dvayorapi saṃsargaḥ tasmādaviśiṣṭaṃ yogyatārūpaṃ yayoḥ tata evaikajñānasaṃsargiṇau tau tasmāt tayorevaṃrūpayoḥ "parasparāpekṣameva" na sarvānyapadārthāpekṣam "anyatvamiha" anupalabdhyadhikāre "abhipretam" | loke tu yadyapyaśeṣapadārthāntarāpekṣamanyatvaṃ nañā kvaciducyate vyāptinyāyasamāśrayāt, tathāpi tadiha na gṛhyate, (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 174.

children.text: ) "pratyāsatterāśrayaṇāt" ekajñānasaṃsargalakṣaṇā prattyāsattirāśrīyate nānyā, pramāṇacintādhikārāt anyathānupalabdhiranaikāntikyeva syāt | tasmāt tattvacintakaistathāvidhamanyatvamāśrayaṇīyam yadanupalabdheravyabhicāranibandhanam | tacca yathoktamevetyabhiprāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) "because proximity is resorted to" — the proximity characterized by conjunction in a single cognition is resorted to, not any other, because this is a section on the investigation of <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge); otherwise, <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception) would simply be inconclusive. Therefore, those who investigate reality should resort to that kind of otherness which is the ground for the non-deviation of <s>anupalabdhi</s>. And that is just as described — this is the intent.

body.translated_text: Even if [the location] is conjoined with that [pot] through conjunction in a single cognition, why does the negative particle not indicate all other [things] in general through [the word] 'other'? To this he says: "therefore" and so on. Since, due to the non-differentiation of capacity, there is conjunction of both in a single cognition in the manner described, therefore the two whose capacity-nature is undifferentiated — and who are therefore conjoined in a single cognition — of these two of such nature, "the otherness here" in the section on <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception) "is intended" "only with mutual reference," not with reference to all other entities. In the world, although otherness with reference to all other entities without exception is sometimes expressed by the negative particle, based on the principle of <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), nevertheless that is not adopted here (

body.text: tadevamekajñānasaṃsargāpekṣayānyatvaṃ pratipādyānupalabdhiṃ darśayannāha- "sa kevalaḥ" ityādi | sa eva yadā kevalaḥ pradeśo yathoktaghaṭāpekṣaya tasmādanya ucyate tadā ghaṭaviviktapradeśajñānaṃ vānupalabdhiḥ, na tu yathesvaraseno manyate upalabdhyabhāvamātramanupalabdhiriti, vakṣyamāṇadoṣāt; ghaṭaviviktapradeśasvabhāvo vā, na tu tadviviktajñānameva yathāha kumārilaḥ "vijñānaṃ vānyavastuni" iti | yathā hyanyavastuviṣayaṃ jñanamanubhūyamānaṃ pratiyogismaraṇāpekṣaṃ tadabhāvavyavahāranibandhanaṃ tathā tadviviktaḥ pradeśo 'pi | tathāhi- kasyacit pratipattuḥ ‘yataḥ kealapradeśākārameva jñānaṃ mayā saṃvedyate na tu ghaṭākāramapi tasmādatra ghaṭo nāsti'; iti evaṃ nāstitājñānamutpadyate; kasyacit tu ‘yataḥ kevalaḥ pradeśo 'yaṃ dṛśyate na tu ghaṭasahitaḥ tasmānnāstyatra ghaṭaḥ'; ityevam | tasmādubhayornāstitājñānajanmani tulyaṃ sāmarthyamiti dvayorapi anupalabdhivyavasthā yukteti | tatra yadā tajjñānaṃ tadā jñātṛdharmalakṣaṇānupalabdhiḥ kartṛsthakriyāpekṣayā, yadā tatsvabhāvastadā jñeyadharmalakṣaṇā karmasthakriyāpekṣayeti |
body.translated_text: Having thus explained otherness with reference to conjunction in a single cognition, he shows <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception), saying: "that alone" and so on. When that very location is said to be 'other' with reference to the aforementioned pot — that is, when it is alone — then the cognition of the location devoid of the pot is <s>anupalabdhi</s>, or [alternatively] the intrinsic nature of the location devoid of the pot [is <s>anupalabdhi</s>]; not, as <s>Īśvarasena</s> thinks, that the mere absence of apprehension is <s>anupalabdhi</s> — because of the fault to be stated later; nor that the cognition devoid of that [pot] alone [is <s>anupalabdhi</s>], as <s>Kumārila</s> says: "or the cognition regarding another object." For just as a cognition directed at another object, being experienced, requires the recollection of the counter-correlate and serves as the ground for the conventional usage of its absence — so too does the location devoid of that [pot]. For thus: for a certain perceiver, the knowledge of non-existence arises as follows — 'since only a cognition having the aspect of the bare location is apprehended by me, and not one having the aspect of a pot as well, therefore there is no pot here'; for another, however, [it arises] thus — 'since this bare location alone is seen, and not [a location] accompanied by a pot, therefore there is no pot here.' Therefore, since both have equal capacity in producing the cognition of non-existence, the characterization as <s>anupalabdhi</s> is appropriate for both. There, when it is the cognition [of the bare location], it is <s>anupalabdhi</s> characterized as a property of the knower, with reference to action residing in the agent; when it is the intrinsic nature [of the bare location], it is [<s>anupalabdhi</s>] characterized as a property of the knowable, with reference to action residing in the object.

body.text: evamanupalabdhiṃ paryudāsavṛttyā vyavasthāpya sādhyamasyā darśayannāha- "sā abhāvam" ityādi | sarvānyopalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptavivikte 'pi pradeśādau dṛśyamāne yatra ghaṭādau pratiyoginyarthitvādibhiḥ smṛtirasya bhavati tasyābhāvaṃ sādhayati, abhāvavyavahāraṃ vā | kāraṇavyāpakānupalabdhī abhāvamabhāvavyavahāraṃ ca sādhayataḥ | svabhāvānupalabdhistu abhāvyavahārameva | abhāvavyavahāraśca jñānābhidhānapravṛttilakṣaṇaḥ | tatra ‘nāstyatra ghaṭaḥ'; ityevamākāraṃ jñānam, evaṃvidhavastvabhidhāyakaṃ cābhidhānaṃ, niḥśaṅkasya ca tatra pradeśe gamanāgamanalakṣaṇā pravṛttiriti |
body.translated_text: Having thus established <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception) through <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion), he shows what it proves, saying: "it [establishes] absence" and so on. Even when a location and the like, devoid of all other things possessing the conditions for apprehension, is perceived — wherever there is recollection of the counter-correlate such as a pot through desire and the like — [non-perception] establishes the absence of that, or the conventional usage of absence. <s>Kāraṇānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of the cause) and <s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of the pervader) establish both absence and the conventional usage of absence. But <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of the intrinsic nature) [establishes] only the conventional usage of absence. And the conventional usage of absence is characterized by cognition, verbal expression, and purposive activity. There, the cognition has the form 'there is no pot here'; the verbal expression is that which denotes an object of such a kind; and the purposive activity is the action of going and coming in that location by one who is free from doubt.

body.text: atreśvarasena- kumārilayorvacanāvakāśamāśaṅkaya siddhāntavyavasthāmeva kurvatā tanmate niraste 'pyāhatya tanmatanirāsārthamāha- "kathamanyabhāva" ityādi | īśvaraseno hi manyate- kārya- svabhāvahetubhyāṃ bhāvarūpābhyāṃ anupalabdheḥ pṛthakkaraṇādavaśyamabhāvarūpatvamasyāḥ, anyathā pṛthakkaraṇamanarthakameva syāt | tvayā cānyasya pratiṣedhyaviviktasya pradeśādestajjñānasya vā bhāvarūpānupalabdhirākhyāyate tannūnamanyabhāvastadabhāvo yenaivamabhidhīyate | na caitad yujyate, bhāvābhāvayorvirodhādekātmatānupapatteriti |
body.translated_text: Having anticipated the occasion for the statements of <s>Īśvarasena</s> and <s>Kumārila</s>, and while establishing the final position itself — even though their views have already been refuted — in order to refute their views once again directly, he says: "how can the existence of the other" and so on. For <s>Īśvarasena</s> thinks: since <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception) is treated separately from the <s>kārya</s> (effect) and <s>svabhāva</s> (intrinsic nature) reasons, which are of the nature of positive entities, it must necessarily be of the nature of absence; otherwise, treating it separately would be pointless. And you describe <s>anupalabdhi</s> as being of a positive nature — [namely] the location devoid of the thing to be negated, or the cognition thereof — so surely the existence of the other must be the absence of that, by which it is so described. But this is not tenable, because a positive entity and an absence are contradictory, and their identity is untenable.

body.text: kumārilo 'pyevaṃ manyate- yeyaṃ jñātṛ- jñeyadharmalakṣaṇā dvidhānupalabdhirabhāvarūpā tvayocyate tasyā bhavatu nāstitājñānaṃ prati sādhanabhāvaḥ | kintu sa evānyasya pratiṣedhyaviviktasya vastunaḥ pratiṣedhyajñānādanyasya vā tajjñānasya yo bhāvo bhāvāṃśaḥ sa kathamabhāvaḥ? pratiṣedhasya tajjñānasya vā kathamabhāvāṃśaḥ? | naiva yujyate, dharmarūpatayā bhāvābhāvāṃśayorbhedāt | satyapi dharmirūpeṇābhede tayoścodbhavābhibhavābhyāṃ grahaṇāgrahaṇavyavastheti | yadāha-
body.translated_text: <s>Kumārila</s> too thinks thus: let this twofold <s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception) described by you as being of the nature of absence — characterized as a property of the knower and as a property of the knowable — have the status of being a means of establishing the cognition of non-existence. However, how can that very positive existence — the positive aspect — of the object devoid of the thing to be negated, or of the cognition of that [bare location] which is other than the cognition of the thing to be negated — how can that be absence? How can the negation, or the cognition thereof, have an absence-aspect? This is simply not tenable, because the positive aspect and the absence-aspect are different, being of the nature of [different] properties. Even though there is non-difference in the form of the property-bearer, there is the determination of apprehension and non-apprehension through [their respective] emergence and suppression. As he has said:

body.text:
"dharmayorbheda iṣṭo hi dharmyabhede 'pi naḥ sthite |
udbhavābhibhavātmatvād grahaṇaṃ cāvatiṣṭhate ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "For the difference of properties is accepted by us even when there is non-difference of the property-bearer. And apprehension is maintained through the nature of emergence and suppression."

body.text: uktottaratāmasya darśayannāha- "uktamuttaramatra"codye yathā "paryudāsavṛttyā apekṣātaḥ" | ‘pratiṣedhyaṃ tajjñānaṃ vā apekṣya tadvivikto 'rthastajjñānaṃ vābhāvo 'nupalabdhiścocyate'; iti īśvarasenasya prativacanam | na hi prasajyapratiṣedha evaiko nañarthaḥ kintu paryudāso 'pi | tato 'nyabhāvasyābhāvarūpatā na virudhyate, prasajyapratiṣedharūpatāpyanyabhāvasya yathā tathottaratra vakṣyate | svabhāvahetostvanulabdheḥ pṛthakkaraṇaṃ pratipatrabhiprāyavaśāt | pratipattā hi svabhāvahetau vastupratipattyadhyavasāyī | anupalabdhau tvabhāvapratipattyadhyavasāyī | paramārthatastu pratiṣedhyābhāvavyavahārayogyatā (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 176.

children.text: ) vastubhūtaiva pradeśasya sādhyata iti na svabhāvahetoḥ svabhāvānupalabdhirbhidyata iti |
children.translated_text: ) is itself of the nature of a positive entity belonging to the location — this is what is to be established. Therefore, <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-perception of the intrinsic nature) does not differ from the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (intrinsic nature reason).

body.translated_text: Showing that this has already been answered, he says: "the answer has been stated here" — to the objection — namely, "through <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion), by way of reference." 'Non-perception is called [so], and absence [is spoken of], with reference to — that is, in relation to — the thing to be negated or the cognition thereof, [while] the object devoid of that, or the cognition thereof [is what is actually denoted]' — this is the reply to <s>Īśvarasena</s>. For the <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (verbally bound negation) is not the only meaning of the negative particle; <s>paryudāsa</s> (nominally bound exclusion) is also [a meaning]. Therefore, the fact that the existence of the other is of the nature of absence is not contradictory; and that the existence of the other also has the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (verbally bound negation) will be stated later. As for the separate treatment of <s>anupalabdhi</s> from the <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (intrinsic nature reason) — that is due to the intention of the person to be instructed. For the person to be instructed, in the case of the <s>svabhāvahetu</s>, is one whose determination is directed toward the apprehension of a positive entity. But in the case of <s>anupalabdhi</s>, [the person to be instructed] is one whose determination is directed toward the apprehension of absence. In ultimate reality, however, the capacity for conventional usage regarding the absence of the thing to be negated (

body.text: yattu ‘anapekṣitārthāntarasaṃsargaṃ pratiṣedhamātramanupalabdhiḥ'; itīśvaraseno manyate tannirākurvannāha- "na pratiṣedhamātram" ityādi | kasmāt? ityāha- "tasya sādhanāsiddheḥ" ityādi | nahyabhāvasya sarvasāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇasya sādhanatvaṃ siddhihetutvaṃ sidhyati, sarvasāmarthyaviraharūpasya tadayogāt | hetutve vā kathaṃ na sāmarthyayogitā? bhāvarūpatā vā?, sāmarthyalakṣaṇatvād vastunaḥ | abhāvasya cānapekṣitasahakāriṇo anādheyātiśayatayā nāstīti jñānajanane nityaṃ tajjananaprasaṅgaḥ | tataśca sādhakatvāyogādabhāvavyavahāra eva na sidhyet | athavā tasya prasajyapratiṣedhātmana upalabdhyabhāvasya sādhanameva kiñcinna sidhyatīti | sa hyabhāvatvādapareṇopalabdhyabhāvena sādhyaḥ syāt, so 'pyapareṇetyanavasthānam | na cendriyavadajñātasya pratiṣedhajñānahetutā, sadā sannihitatvenānapekṣitasahakāriṇo nityaṃ tadudayaprasaṅgāt | idaṃ cārthadvayaṃ ‘kathamabhāvaḥ kasyacit pratipattiḥ, pratipattiheturvā? | tasyāpi kathaṃ pratipattiḥ'; ityatrāntare svayameva vipañcayiṣyati |
body.translated_text: As for [the view] that <s>Īśvarasena</s> holds — '<s>anupalabdhi</s> (non-perception) is mere negation without regard to conjunction with any other entity' — refuting that, he says: "not mere negation" and so on. Why? To this he says: "because its being a means of proof is not established" and so on. For it is not established that absence — characterized by the complete lack of all capacity — can serve as a means of proof, i.e., a cause of establishment, because what is of the nature of the complete lack of all capacity is incompatible with that [role]. Or if it has the status of a cause, how can it not have connection with capacity? Or [how can it not have] the nature of a positive entity? — because an entity is defined by [its] capacity. And since absence, requiring no auxiliary conditions, is devoid of any additional qualification, [if it were the cause of] the cognition 'it does not exist,' there would be the undesirable consequence that it would always produce that [cognition]. Consequently, since it is unfit to serve as a means of proof, the very conventional usage of absence would not be established. Alternatively: of that [absence] which is of the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (verbally bound negation), i.e., the mere absence of apprehension — nothing whatsoever is established as its means of proof. For that, being of the nature of absence, would have to be established by another absence of apprehension, and that by yet another — resulting in infinite regress. Nor can the unperceived [absence], like a sense-faculty, serve as the cause of the cognition of negation, because since it is always present and requires no auxiliary conditions, there would be the undesirable consequence that [the cognition of negation] would arise at all times. And these two points — 'how can there be apprehension of absence, or how can [absence] be a cause of apprehension? And of that [further absence] too, how would there be apprehension?' — he himself will elaborate upon in what follows.

body.text: kumārilasyāpyuttaramāha- "tasya" anyasya pratiyoginā vastvantareṇāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpasya | na hyasau vastvantaraiḥ saṃsṛṣṭasvabhāva ekarūpaḥ | tathātve hyabhāvāṃśo 'pi na kvacit sidhyet | tasyaivaṃvidhasya "bhāvasiddhireva" bhāvāṃśasiddhireva "aparasya" pratiyogino vastvantarasyābhāvasiddhirabhāvāṃśasya tvadabhimatasya siddhirastu bhāvāṃśasyaivābhāvāṃśarūpatopapatteriti manyate | tathā hi- abhāvāṃśo 'pi pararūpāsaṃsṛṣṭatayaivābhāva iti vyapadiśyate, anyathā tadayogāt | sā ca bhāvāṃśasyāpi samāneti sa evābhāvo 'stu tannimittasya samānatvāt kimanyenābhāvāṃśopagatena? | ata evāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpasyeti viśeṣaṇam | yata (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 177.

children.text: ) evam "iti" tasmād "anyabhāvo 'pi" anyasya vastuno bhāvo 'pi tvadabhimato bhāvāṃśo 'pi na kevalamabhāvāṃśastvanmatyābhāva iti vyapadiśyate 'smābhiḥ | tato bhāvāṃśasyābhāvarūpatā saṅgataiveti na kiñcid virudhyata iti |
children.translated_text: ) Thus, "therefore," "even the existence of another" — even the existence of another entity, even the positive aspect according to your view — not merely the negative aspect — is designated by us as absence according to your understanding. Therefore, the nature of the positive aspect as being of the form of absence is entirely consistent, and nothing is contradicted.

body.translated_text: He states the answer to <s>Kumārila</s> as well, saying: "of that" — of the other [entity] whose nature is not conjoined with another object, i.e., the counter-correlate. For that [entity] is not of a single nature conjoined with other objects. If it were so, then the absence-aspect too would not be established anywhere. "The very establishment of the positive existence" — the establishment of the positive aspect — "of that" which is of such a nature "is itself the establishment of the absence" of the other, i.e., the counter-correlate — the establishment of the absence-aspect as you conceive it — let it be [understood as] the very absence-aspect-nature of the positive aspect itself — this is what [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] holds. For thus: even the absence-aspect is designated as absence solely by virtue of being unconjoined with the form of the other; otherwise that [designation] would be impossible. And that [feature of being unconjoined] is the same for the positive aspect as well. Therefore, let that very [positive aspect] be the absence, since the ground for that [designation] is the same — what need is there for another [entity] possessing the absence-aspect? For this very reason, the qualification 'whose nature is not conjoined' [is used]. Since (

body.text: yaduktaṃ ‘jñātṛjñeyadharmalakṣaṇayā svabhāvānupalabdhyā abhāvavyavahāra eva sādhyate nābhāvaḥ'; iti tat paro vighaṭayituṃ, yaccoktaṃ ‘na pratiṣedhamātramanupalabdhiḥ, tasya sādhanāsiddheḥ'; iti dvitīye vyākhyāne pratiṣedhamātrasyānupalabdhi[ri]tyetasya sādhanaṃ darśayitumāha- "anyabhāvalakṣaṇa" ityādi | evaṃ manyate- loko hi kevalapradeśadarśanāt ghaṭābhāvameva prathamaṃ pratipadyate kevalapradeśajñānasaṃvedanadvāreṇa ghaṭajñānābhāvapratipattyā vā tato ghaṭābhāvasya vyavahāram | tena lokapratītyanusāreṇa pratiṣedhyādanyasya pradeśasya pratiṣedhyajñānādvā tajjñānasya yo bhāvastallakṣaṇo 'bhāvaḥ svayaṃ pramāṇenendriyapratyakṣeṇa svasaṃvedanapratyakṣeṇa ca siddho 'laṃ ghaṭābhāvaṃ sākṣāt pāramparyeṇa ca yathākramaṃ sādhayitum, sa ca ghaṭābhāvavyavahāramityevaṃ vyavasthāpayituṃ yuktam | na caivamapi vyavasthāpane [asma]tpakṣasya kācit kṣatiḥ | tathāhi- pāramparyeṇāpi yadanupalabdheḥ tvadabhyupagatāyāḥ siddhaṃ tat tata eva siddhaṃ bhavatīti pratiṣedhamātrasyānupalabdhitve tatsādhanapratipādane 'pi | ayamabhiprāyaḥ- yathā bhavato jñātṛjñeyadharmalakṣaṇā bhāvarūpā dvividhānupalabdhistathā mamāpi jñātṛjñeyadharmalakṣaṇopalabdhyabhāvo 'pyanupalabdhisaṃjñito dvividho bhaviṣyati | tatra jñeyadharmalakṣaṇenānyabhāvena pratyakṣasiddhena pratiṣedhyābhāvo jñeyadharmalakṣaṇopalabdhyabhāvarūpo 'nupalabdhisaṃjñitaḥ setsyati | jñātṛdharmalakṣaṇena cānyabhāvena kevalapradeśajñānātmanā svasaṃvedanasiddhena jñātṛdharmaḥ pratiṣedhyajñānābhāvarūpo 'nupalabdhisamākhyātaḥ setsyati | tataśca kuto 'navasthā yena sādhanāsiddhiḥ syāditi | tatra "anyabhāvalakṣaṇa" iti pratiṣedhyāt tajjñānācca yo 'nyo bhāvaḥ pratiṣedhyaviviktaḥ pradeśaḥ tajjñānaṃ ca tadātmako 'bhāvaḥ vivakṣitād bhāvāt pratiṣedhyād bhāvāt tajñānāccānyatvādanupalabdhitvena (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 178.

children.text: ) bhavato 'bhimataḥ svayaṃ svarūpeṇa pramāṇenendriyapratyakṣeṇa svasaṃvedanapratyakṣeṇa ca siddhaḥ saṃstasya pratiṣedhyasyābhāvavyavahāraṃ jñānābhidhānapravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ sādhayet "tatsiddhisiddho" vā tasyānyabhāvalakṣaṇasyābhāvasya yathoktasya siddhyā siddho vā tadabhāvastasya pratiṣedhyasya tajjñānasya vābhāva iti evamapīṣyamāṇe "na kaścid viśeṣaḥ" tvadabhimatānupalabdhito 'smadabhimatānupalabdheḥ tato 'smaddarśanaṃ kimiti pratikṣipyate? | nanvastyevaivamiṣyamāṇe viśeṣo 'nyabhāvalakṣaṇānupalabdhiritarayā vyavahitā tadabhāvavyavahāraṃ sādhayeditarā tu sākṣādityāha- sa viśeṣo nāsti yena viśeṣeṇānupalabdhyābhāvarūpayā vastusaṃsparśarahitayāsmadabhimatayābhāvavyavahārasiddheḥ virodhaḥ syāt | anyasya tu viśeṣasya sato 'pyabādhakatvādasatsamatvameva | yadapyuktaṃ- ‘tasya sādhanābhāvādabhāvavyavahārāsiddhiprasaṅgaḥ'; iti, tadapyasat, yataḥ sa eva tvadabhimato 'nyabhāvaḥ pratiṣedhyaviviktabhūtalātmakastadviṣayā copalabdhiranupalabdhitveneṣṭā bhavatastadabhāvasyānupalabdhitvenāsmanmatasya pratiṣedhyābhāvasya tadupalabdhyabhāvasya ca "kiṃ" kasmāt "na sādhanaṃ" liṅgam "iṣyate?" | tathā hi sati lokapratītiranusṛtā bhavati | "kiṃ punaḥ" kasmāt punaḥ "abhāvasya" dvividhasya "siddhireva tadabhāvasiddhiḥ" na tatsādhyā kācidanyā vidyata ityasmanmataniṣedhārthaṃ lokātikrāntamiṣyata iti pūrvapakṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) — acknowledged by you, itself established in its own form by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, namely sensory perception and self-awareness perception — would establish the conventional usage of absence of what is to be negated, characterized by the functioning of cognition and verbal expression; or, "established by the establishment of that" — by the establishment of that absence characterized as the existence of another, as described — what is established is the absence of that — the absence of what is to be negated or of the cognition of it. Even if it is accepted in this way, "there is no difference" between the non-apprehension as you conceive it and the non-apprehension as we conceive it.

body.translated_text: What was said — 'by <s>svabhāvānupalabdhi</s> (non-apprehension of the intrinsic nature) characterized by properties of the knower and the knowable, only the conventional usage of absence is established, not absence [itself]' — in order to dismantle that, and what was also said — 'non-apprehension is not mere negation, because of the non-establishment of the means of proof' — in order to show the proof of this [claim] that mere negation is non-apprehension, in the second interpretation, he says: "Characterized as the existence of another" and so on. He thinks thus: for ordinary people, from merely seeing a [bare] location, first understand the absence of a pot, either through the bare perception of the location or through the understanding of the absence of the cognition of the pot via the awareness of the cognition of the bare location, and then [proceed to] the conventional usage of the absence of the pot. Therefore, in accordance with ordinary understanding, absence characterized by the existence of the other — i.e., the location distinct from what is to be negated, or the cognition [of the location] distinct from the cognition of what is to be negated — is itself established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), namely sensory perception and self-awareness perception, and is sufficient to establish the absence of the pot directly and indirectly, respectively, as well as the conventional usage of the absence of the pot. It is appropriate to establish [things] in this way. Nor is there any harm to our position even with this establishment. For: whatever is established — even indirectly — by non-apprehension as you acknowledge it, that is established from that very [non-apprehension] — even when non-apprehension is [understood as] mere negation and even when the proof of that is demonstrated. The intention is this: just as for you there is a twofold non-apprehension characterized by properties of the knower and the knowable, which is of the nature of a positive entity, so too for me there will be a twofold [thing] designated as non-apprehension, which is the absence of apprehension characterized by properties of the knower and the knowable. Therein, by the existence of another characterized as a property of the knowable, which is established by perception, the absence of what is to be negated — which is of the form of the absence of apprehension characterized as a property of the knowable, designated as non-apprehension — will be established. And by the existence of another characterized as a property of the knower — being of the nature of the cognition of the bare location, established by self-awareness — the property of the knower, which is of the form of the absence of the cognition of what is to be negated, called non-apprehension, will be established. And therefore, whence the infinite regress such that there would be non-establishment of the means of proof? Therein, "characterized as the existence of another" means: the existence of another — distinct from what is to be negated and from the cognition of it — the location distinct from what is to be negated,

body.text: atrāha- "apṛthaksiddheranyabhāvāt" tadabhāvasya pṛthaksiddherabhāvāt kuto liṅgaliṅgitā | tathā "sambandhābhāvāccā" anyabhāvatadabhāva yorna liṅgaliṅgiteti | prathamaṃ tāvat kāraṇaṃ vivṛṇvannāha- "anyabhāvastadviviktadeśātmakastāvanna sādhanaṃ" liṅgaṃ pratiṣedhyābhāvasya, ‘tadupalabdhirapi tadabhāvasya na sādhanam'; iti paścād vakṣyate | tadarthameva tāvacchabdaḥ | kasmādanyabhāvo na sādhanam? ityāha- "yatsiddhau" yasya vastunaḥ siddhau pratītau "yasya" aparasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 179.

children.text: ) vastuno "na siddhi"rna pratītiḥ tadvastu tasya vastuno liṅgaṃ bhavatītyayaṃ liṅgaliṅginornyāyaḥ | tatrodāharaṇam- "dhūmāgnivaditi" | yathā- yadā dhūmapratītau nāgniḥ pratīyate tadā tayorlliṅgaliṅgibhāvo bhavati, na tu dhūmapratītikāla eva pratīyamāne 'gnau | yadi nāmaivaṃ tataḥ kim? ityata āha- "anyasya vastuno yo bhāvaḥ" svabhāva "tatsiddhyaiva" tatpratītyeva "tadabhāvaḥ" tasya pratiṣedhyasyābhāvaḥ "prasidhyati" pratīyateanyabhāvasyaiva tadabhāvātmakatvāt tatsiddhereva tatsiddhilakṣaṇatvāt |
children.translated_text: ) — "there is no cognition" — no awareness — of the entity; the entity of that thing becomes the inferential mark — this is the principle of the relation between inferential mark and what is marked. An example for that: "like smoke and fire." Just as: when fire is not cognized upon the cognition of smoke, then there is the relation of inferential mark and what is marked between them — but not when fire is cognized at the very time of the cognition of smoke. If this is so, then what [follows]? To this he says: "The existence of another entity" — [its] intrinsic nature — "by the establishment of that very" — by the cognition of that very [existence of another] — "the absence of that" — the absence of what is to be negated —

body.translated_text: Here [the opponent] says: "Because of the non-separate-establishment of the existence of another" — because of the absence of separate establishment of the absence of that [from the existence of another], whence is there the relation of inferential mark and what is marked? Likewise, "and because of the absence of a relation" between the existence of another and the absence of that — [they are] not [related as] inferential mark and what is marked. First, explaining the [first] reason, he says: "The existence of another, being of the nature of the location distinct from that, is first of all not a means of proof" — not an inferential mark — for the absence of what is to be negated. 'Nor is the apprehension of that a means of proof for the absence of that' — this will be stated later. The word <s>tāvat</s> is for that purpose. Why is the existence of another not a means of proof? He says:

body.text: naiyāyikāstu manyante- pratiṣedhyābhāvo hi prasajyapratiṣedhātmakastuccharūpastasya kathaṃ tadanyabhāvarūpatā?, bhāvābhāvayorvirodhāt | tataḥ kathaṃ tadanyabhāvasiddhyaiva tadabhāvasiddhiḥ syāt? ityata āha- "tasya" tadanyabhāvasya pradeśalakṣaṇasya tasmādanyena pratiṣedhyena ghaṭādinā "asaṃsṛṣṭarūpasya" rahitātmanaḥ kevalasya pratiṣedhyena śūnyātmanaḥ | anena kevalapradeśasyāpi prasajyapratiṣedhātmakatāmāha | kathaṃ bhāvasya tuccharūpatā svabhāvaḥ, virodhāt? iti cet; na, pararūpeṇa tasyāpi tuccharūpatvāt | yathā hyanapekṣitabhāvāntarasaṃsargaḥ prasajyapratiṣedhaḥ śūnyavikalpapratibhāsī pratiṣedhyena tuccharūpaḥ tadrūpavirahāt, tathā tadanyabhāvo 'pi pratiṣedhyāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpaḥ | tataḥ kathamasya pratiṣedhyena tuccharūpatā virudhyeta? | svarūpeṇa hyayamatuccharūpaḥ syānna pararūpeṇa, anyathā kathamasyānyabhāvatvaṃ parasya vā tatrābhāvaḥ syāt? | yo hi yadabhāvarūpo na bhavati sa evāsau bhavati, tatsvarūpavat | tataḥ sarvasya jagataḥ parasparātmatāprasaṅgaḥ | tasmāt sarvabhāvāḥ pararūpeṇa niḥsvabhāvāḥ svarūpeṇa rūpavattve 'pī tyanavadyam |
body.translated_text: But the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> think: the absence of what is to be negated is of the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation), a mere nothing — how can it have the nature of the existence of another, since positive existence and absence are contradictory? And therefore, how can the establishment of the absence of that be accomplished by the establishment of the existence of another? To this he says: "Of that" — of the existence of another, characterized as the location — "whose form is unsullied by" — devoid of, free from, empty of — "another" — the thing to be negated, such as a pot and the like. By this [it is shown that] even the bare location, [being devoid of the negated entity, shares] the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation).

body.text: kastarhi prasajyapratiṣedhatparyudāsasya bhedaḥ? | na kaścit, kevalamanapekṣitarūpāntaramabhāvamātraṃ prasajyapratiṣedha iti loke kathyate | rūpāntaraṃ tu pararūpaśanyaṃ paryudāsa iti | na tu rūpāntaraṃ pararūpatucchātmakaṃ na bhavati | anubhūyata eva ca rūpāntaraṃ tadrūpaśūnyatayā, (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 180.

children.text: ) kathaṃ tasya prasajyapratiṣedhātmatā na syāt pararūpeṇa? | sāmarthyāt tatastatpratītiriti cet; na, akāraṇapratītau sāmarthyāsambhavāt | tādātmyābhāve hi prasajyapratiṣedhasya paryudastāt pratītau tatkāraṇatve sati syāt pratipattiḥ nānyathā | tasya tadanyāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpasya yat tattvaṃ tasya pratiṣedhyatuccharūpatāyā vyavasthāpakaṃ pramāṇaṃ pratyakṣarūpam tata eva- na taduttarakālabhāvino ‘nāstīha ghaṭaḥ'; iti vikalpāt, tasya gṛhītagrāhitayā smṛtitvenāpramāṇatvāt- anyasya ghaṭādestatrāsato vyavacchedasyābhāvasya siddhestadabhāvātmakasyaiva pradeśasya tena grahaṇāt | dvividho hyayaṃ pradeśo ghaṭāsaṃsṛṣṭarūpsastavdyāvṛttarūpatayā tato 'nyo ghaṭavānapi, kevalaśca ghaṭaṃ prati apratipannādhārabhāvaḥ | tasya tadvivekena pratyakṣeṇa grahaṇe ghaṭādanyatvaṃ ghaṭavirahaśca gṛhīta eva bhavatīti na vastvasaṃkarasiddhyartham, ‘ihedaṃ nāsti'; ityevamarthaṃ ca pramāṇāntaramanveṣaṇīyam | vistarataścaitaduttaratra vakṣyata iti āstāṃ tāvat | yataścānyabhāvasiddhyaiva tadabhāva uktena nyāyena siddhyati tato nānyabhāvaḥ pratiṣedhyābhāvasya liṅgam |
children.translated_text: ) — how would it not have the nature of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation) by virtue of the other's form? If [one says:] from capacity, therefore there is the cognition of that [absence] — no, because capacity is impossible when the cognition has no cause. For in the absence of identity [between the existence of another and the absence of what is negated], the cognition of <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> from <s>paryudāsa</s> would [require] that [paryudāsa] be the cause of that cognition; otherwise there would be no understanding. Of that — of the existence of another unsullied by what is to be negated — the reality of which, the <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the nature of the nothingness of what is to be negated, is of the form of perception — from that very [perception] — not from a subsequent cognition of the form 'the pot does not exist here.'

body.translated_text: What then is the difference between <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s> (simple negation) and <s>paryudāsa</s> (exclusion)? There is none. It is merely that what is bare absence without reference to another form is conventionally called <s>prasajyapratiṣedha</s>. But another form that is empty of another's form is called <s>paryudāsa</s>. However, it is not the case that the other form, whose nature is the nothingness of another's form, does not exist. And the other form is indeed experienced as being empty of that form, (

body.text: dvitīyaṃ kāraṇaṃ vyācakṣāṇa āha- "sambandhābhāvācca" iti | anyabhāvatadabhāvayorna kaścit sambandho 'sti, tataḥ kuto liṅgaliṅgibhāvaḥ? iti | etacca kadocyate? | yadā tadabhāvarūpatānyabhāvasya parānabhyupagatāpekṣyate | tadanyabhāvāt pṛthageva tadabhāvastuccharūpa iṣyate paraiḥ | anyathoktena nyāyenānyabhāvasyaiva tadabhāvarūpatve tādātmyāt kathaṃ sambandhābhāvaḥ? | pratyakṣasiddhatā ca tadaiva, na pakṣāntareṇa abhihitā | "tacca tasya" ityādyasyaiva vivaraṇaṃ vyatirekamukhena "ekārthasamavāya" iti paradarśanenoktaṃ | pareṣāṃ hi naiyāyikādīnāṃ vyatiriktāveva kṛtakānityatvākhyau dharmāvekasminneva dharmiṇi samavetāviti kṛtakasyānityatvenaikasminnarthe dharmiṇi samavāyaḥ sambandhaḥ dhamasya veti (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 181.

children.text: ) sambandha evodāharaṇāntaram | atraikarthasamavāya iti saṃyogaḥ sa eva samavāyaśabdenoktaḥ | saṃyogasamavāyayoḥ kalpitatvād bhedena vyapadeśe 'nādarāt | pareṣāṃ tvagnidhūmau svāvayaveṣveva samavetāviti na tayorekārthasamavāya ādhārādheyabhāvo veti dhūmasyāgnerupari darśanāllaukikaḥ sambandha uktaḥ | "janyajanakabhāvo vā" iti pāramārthikaḥ sambandho 'bhihitaḥ, paramārthato 'gnerjanakatvāt itarasya ca janyatvāditi |
children.translated_text: ) — relation itself is another example. Here, "co-occurrence in a single locus" — that is, conjunction — that very [conjunction] is expressed by the word <s>samavāya</s> (inherence). Since both <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) are fabricated, there is no regard for designating [them] separately. But for the opponents, fire and smoke inhere in their own parts, so there is no co-occurrence in a single locus — [rather] there is the relation of container and contained — and thus, since smoke is observed above fire, the worldly relation is stated. "Or the producer-produced relationship" — the ultimate relation is stated, since fire is ultimately the producer and the other [smoke] is the produced.

body.translated_text: Explaining the second reason, he says: "And because of the absence of a relation." Between the existence of another and the absence of that, there is no relation whatsoever; therefore, whence the relation of inferential mark and what is marked? And when is this said? When the form-as-absence-of-that of the existence of another is considered with reference to what the opponent does not acknowledge. For the opponents accept the absence of that as a mere nothing, separate from the existence of another. Otherwise, by the principle stated [above], when the existence of another itself has the form of the absence of that, due to identity, how can there be an absence of relation? And its establishment by perception is at that very [moment], not [later].

body.text: nanu ceśvarasenena saha vicāraḥ prakrāntaḥ tat kimiti naiyāyikābhimasyāpi sambandhasyānyabhāvatadabhāvayorabhāva ucyate | satyam, prasaṅgena tu tanmatasyāpi niṣedhārthamuktam | pūrvaṃ hyanyabhāvagrāhipratyakṣasiddhatvāt pratiṣedhyābhāvasya na tadarthaṃ pratyakṣāntaraṃ ‘nāstīha ghaṭaḥ'; ityevamākāraṃ kalpanīyamiti prasaṅgataḥ kathitam | adhunā tu prasaṅgādidamucyate- yadānyabhāvagrāhipratyakṣasiddho 'yaṃ tadabhāvo na bhavati tadā pratyakṣāntaraṃ ‘nāsti iha ghaṭaḥ'; ityevamākāraṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvalakṣaṇāt sannikarṣādiṣṭaṃ bhavatā | na cāsati sambandhe 'nyabhāvatadabhāvayorviśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo yuktaḥ, atiprasaṅgāt | tataḥ kutastallakṣaṇāt sannikarṣāt tadabhāve pratyakṣaṃ bhavediti |
body.translated_text: But [one objects:] the discussion was undertaken with <s>Īśvarasena</s>; so why is the absence of the relation as conceived by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> also stated, for the existence of another and the absence of that? True, but it is stated incidentally for the purpose of refuting their view as well. For previously, it was stated incidentally that, because the absence of what is to be negated is established by the perception that grasps the existence of another, another perception of the form 'the pot does not exist here' need not be postulated for that purpose. But now, this is stated incidentally: when what is established by the perception that grasps the existence of another —

body.text: evaṃ sambandhasvarūpamākhyāya tasyehāsambhavamāha- "naivam" yathā kṛtakatvānityatvayoragnidhūmayorvaikārthasamavāyādilakṣaṇaḥ sambandho naivaṃ kaścid bhāvābhāvayoḥ sambandho yena "asya" tadabhāvasyānyabhāvaḥ sādhanaṃ syāt | yāvekatrārthe dharmirūpe pravartete tayorekārthasamavāyo bhavati | anyabhāvaśca pradeśākhyaḥ svāvayaveṣu yeṣu vartate na tatra ghaṭābhāvaḥ | evaṃ hi pradeśāvayaveṣu ghaṭo nāstīti syāt na pradeśe | na cāsya pradeśāvayavairārambhaḥ | te hi dravyātmāno dravyāntaramevārabhante | na ca ghaṭābhāvo dravyam | navaiva hi dravyāṇīṣyante | na ca kriyāvadādikaṃ dravyalakṣaṇaṃ tatrāsti | na ca guṇarūpatayā tatra vartate | caturviśatireva hi (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 182.

children.text: ) guṇā iṣyante | na cāyaṃ teṣāmanyatamaḥ | nāpi karmarūpatayapañcasu karmasvanantarbhāvāt tallakṣaṇavirahācca | "ekadravyam" ityādikaṃ hi tallakṣaṇam | na caitadabhāve sambhavatīti | nāpi sāmānyādirūpatayā, tadrupavirahādeva | nāpyanyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ saṃyogo 'gnidhūmayoriva, dravyayoreva tadabhyupagamāt | na ca tadabhāvo dravyamityuktam | nāpyādhāra(rā)dheyabhāvo, yataḥ so 'pi saṃyoganimitta ucyate ‘iha kuṇḍe badarāṇi'; iti | samavāyanimitto vā, ‘iha tantuṣu paṭaḥ'; iti | na cābhāvasyādravyātmanaḥ saṃyogaḥ samasti | nāpi samavāyaḥ, pañcānāmeva hi dravyādīnāṃ padārthānāṃ samavāyitvamiṣyate; na cābhāvaḥ pañcasvantarbhavatīti | na ca tadātmānupakāre satyādhāravyapadeśaḥ sambhavati | upakāre vā janyajanakabhavaḥ | na ca tadabhāvo janyaḥ, kāryatāprasaṅgāt | kāryatā cāsyāsambhavinī, yataḥ svakāraṇasamavāyaḥ, sattāsamavāyo vā kāryatocyate bhavadbhiḥ | anyabhāvastu pradeśākhyo 'sya na kāraṇam, trayāṇāmeva hi dravyaguṇakarmaṇāṃ dravyaṃ kāraṇamiṣṭam | na cābhāvo dravyādilakṣaṇaḥ iti | sattāsamavāye 'pi satpratyayaviṣayatā tadabhāvasya syāt, nābhāvapratyayaviṣayatā | pradeśābhāve 'pi ca ghaṭābhāvasambhavāt kutastatkāryatā | na cāsya prativiṣayaṃ bhedaḥ, ekākārajñānaviṣayatvāt | sambandhibhedād bhede vā sāmānyādiṣvapi tatprasaṅgaḥ | samavāyopyasyānantarameva nirasta iti kutaḥ svakāraṇasattāsamavāyarūpā kāryatā tadabhāvasya syāt? | etena janyajanakabhāvaḥ prayuktaḥ | tataḥ sarvathā sambandhābhāvānnānyabhāvaḥ tadabhāvasya sādhanamiti |
children.translated_text: ) qualities are accepted. And this is not any one of those. Nor as an action, because it is not included among the five actions, and because it lacks their defining characteristic. For the defining characteristic of [action] is 'residing in a single substance' and so on. And this is not possible in the case of absence. Nor in the form of a universal and the like, precisely because of the absence of that form. Nor is there conjunction between the existence of another and the absence of that, as between fire and smoke, since that [conjunction] is acknowledged only between substances. And it has been said that the absence of that is not a substance. Nor is there a container-contained relation, since that too is said to be occasioned by conjunction — as in 'there are jujubes in this vessel' — or by inherence — as in 'the cloth is in the threads.' And for absence, which is not of the nature of substance, there is no conjunction whatsoever. Nor is there inherence, for only the five categories — substance and the like — are accepted as possessing inherence; and absence is not included among the five. And without assistance to its nature, the designation of support is not possible. Or if there is assistance, there would be a producer-produced relationship. But the absence of that is not a product, because [otherwise there would be] the undesired consequence of being an effect. And the status of being an effect is impossible for it, since [you maintain that] the status of being an effect consists in inherence in one's own cause, or in inherence of existence. But the existence of another, called the location, is not its cause, for only substance is accepted as the cause of the three — substance, quality, and action. And absence is not characterized as substance and the like. And even in the case of the inherence of existence, the absence of that would be the object of the concept 'existent,' not the object of the concept 'absent.' And since the absence of the pot is possible even in the absence of the location, how can it be an effect of that [location]? And there is no differentiation of this [absence] for each counter-positive, being a single [absence].

body.translated_text: Having thus explained the nature of relation, he states its impossibility here: "Not so" — just as there is a relation characterized by co-occurrence in a single locus and the like between being produced and impermanence, or between fire and smoke, there is not such a relation between positive existence and absence, such that the existence of another could be a means of proof "for this" absence of that. When two [properties] operate in a single object of the nature of a property-bearer, there is co-occurrence of those two in a single locus. But the existence of another, called the location, operates in whatever parts of itself — the absence of the pot does not exist there [in those parts]. For it would then follow that the pot does not exist in the parts of the location, not in the location [as a whole]. And the absence [of the pot] is not produced by the parts of the location. For those [parts], being of the nature of substance, produce only another substance. And the absence of the pot is not a substance. For only nine substances are accepted. And the defining characteristics of substance, such as possessing action and the like, do not exist in it. Nor does it exist there as a quality. For only twenty-four (

body.text: paraḥ sambandhāntaraṃ darśayannāha- "asti viṣaye"tyādi | yathā hi artho viṣayaḥ śabdo viṣayīti tayorviṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ sambandhaḥ, evamanyabhāvatadabhāvayorviṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ sambandho bhaviṣyati | pradeśākhyenānyabhāvena ghaṭābhāvasya pratyāyanāditi pūrvapakṣāśaṅkā | śabdārthayoḥ sambandhaḥ syādityabhisambandhaḥ | (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 183.

children.text: ) kiṃ rūpaḥ? | "kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇaḥ" | kathaṃ punararthakāryatā śabdasya? | tatpratipādanābhiprāye sati arthapratipādanavivakṣāyāṃ satyāṃ tatprayogācchabdoccāraṇāt | tenārthena vivakṣāviparivartinā śabdasya kāryakāraṇalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ syāt | yadyapi ca śabdārthayoḥ buddhiparikalpitasāmānyarūpatā tathāpyarthapratibhāsinyā vivakṣayā śabdasāmānyotprekṣānibandhanasya śabdasvalakṣaṇasyotthāpanāt tanmukhena kāryakāraṇabhāva ucyate | "avinābhāvalakṣaṇo vā" iti paraprasiddhyocyate | paro hyavinābhāvalakṣaṇaḥ śabdārthayoḥ sambandha iti vyavaharati | tataḥ sambandhanivandhana pratipādyapratipādakarūpo viṣayaviṣayibhāvo yuktaḥ | tadabhāvānyabhāvayorapyevaṃ bhaviṣyatīti cet, āha- "ayaṃ ca" anantaroktaprakāraḥ "atra" tadabhāvānyabhāvayoḥ "na sambhavati" | nahi ghaṭābhāvapratipādanābhiprāye sati anyabhāvasya pradeśalakṣaṇasya prayogo niṣpattirbhavati, ghaṭābhāvapratipādanābhiprāyāt prāgapi pradeśasya svahetubhya eva niṣpatteḥ | satyapi tadabhiprāye 'nyabhāvasyābhāvācca | tataśca kathaṃ tayoḥ kāryakāraṇabhāvaḥ?, tadvārako 'vinābhāvo vā syāt? yato viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ kalpyeta |
children.translated_text: ) Of what form? "Characterized as cause and effect." But how is the word the effect of the referent? When there is the intention to communicate that [referent], when there is the desire to express the referent, from the employment of that [intention], from the utterance of the word. Therefore, with the referent that varies with the desire to express, the word would have a relation characterized as cause and effect. And although the word and the referent have the form of a universal fabricated by cognition, nevertheless, through the desire to express that produces an appearance of the referent, the production of the word-universal [occurs].

body.translated_text: The opponent, showing another relation, says: "There is, with respect to the object" and so on. Just as an object is a <s>viṣaya</s> (object-domain) and a word is a <s>viṣayin</s> (possessor of the object-domain), and the relation between them is the object-possessor relation — likewise, there will be an object-possessor relation between the existence of another and the absence of that. Because the absence of the pot is made known by the existence of another called the location — this is the prima facie supposition. There would be a relation between word and referent — thus is the connection. (

body.text: syānmatam- yathā śabdārthayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvanimitto viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ tathā anyabhāvatadabhāvayorapi ityetāvanmātreṇa śabdārthayordṛṣṭāntatetyata āha- "siddhe hi" ityādi | śabdārthayorhi kāryakāraṇabhāvanibandhanaḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ anyathārthāntaratve tadayogāt tathehāpi yadi tadabhāvānyabhāvayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ sidhyet tadā tanmukhena sādhyasādhanabhāvadvāreṇa viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ syāt | yāvatā sa eva sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'sati sambandhe kāryakāraṇabhāvādike na sidhyati, sarvasya sādhyasādhanatāprasakteḥ |
body.translated_text: One might think: just as between word and referent, the object-possessor relation is occasioned by the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof, so too between the existence of another and the absence of that — this much alone [establishes] word and referent as an example. To this he says: "For when established" and so on. For the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof between word and referent is grounded in the cause-effect relationship — otherwise, if they were different entities [without that relationship], that [proved-prover relation] would be inappropriate. Likewise here too, if the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof between the absence of that and the existence of another were to be established, then through that [relation],

body.text: kathamindriyaṃ svaviṣayasiddhinibandhanamiti cet; parasparopasarpaṇādyāśrayāt pratyayaviśeṣādindriyaviṣayayorekavijñānotpādanayorudayāt (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 184.

children.text: ) tathā vyapadeśaḥ, naivamiha, anyabhāvatadabhāvayostadayogāt | liṅgaliṅgibhāvalakṣaṇasya ca sādhyasādhanabhāvasya prakṛtatvāt, tasya ca sambandhamantareṇāyogāt |
children.translated_text: ) such a designation [is made]. But it is not so here, because that [relationship] is inappropriate for the existence of another and the absence of that. And since the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof, characterized as the relation of inferential mark and what is marked, is the topic under discussion, and since that [relation] is impossible without a [prior] relation.

body.translated_text: If [one asks:] how is the sense faculty the ground for the establishment of its own object? Due to the dependence on mutual approach and the like, from the arising of particular conditions — the sense faculty and the object — that produces a single cognition, (

body.text: naiva sambandhāntaranibandhano 'nyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'pi tu viṣayaviṣayibhāvanimitta eveti cet; āha- "anyathā" yadi sambandhāntaraṃ neṣyate kintu viṣayaviṣayibhāvāt sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ tasmācca viṣayaviṣayibhāvaḥ, tata itaretarāśrayamidaṃ syāt | tathā caikāsiddhau dvayorapyasiddhirbhavediti | kiñcānyabhāvācca liṅgabhūtādabhāvasya liṅginaḥ siddhāvanumitāviṣyamāṇāyāṃ asamudāyaśca sādhyaḥ syāt, anyabhāvena tadabhāvasya kevalasyaiva sādhanāt na kevalasambandhābhāvāt sādhyasādhanabhāvāyogaḥ | samudāyaśca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvāpanno dharmadharmilakṣaṇaḥ sādhyo ya iṣṭastadabhāvadoṣaśceti ‘ca'; śabdaḥ |
body.translated_text: If [one says:] the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof between the existence of another and the absence of that is not grounded in another relation at all, but rather is occasioned by the object-possessor relation itself — he says: "Otherwise" — if another relation is not accepted, but rather from the object-possessor relation there is the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof, and from that the object-possessor relation — then this would be a case of mutual dependence. And thus, if one is not established, neither would be established. Moreover, from the existence of another that is the inferential mark, the absence —

body.text: sarvatra samudāyasya sādhyatā naiveṣṭeti cet, āha- "tathā ca" dharmamātrasyāpi svatantrasya sādhyatopagame ‘ghaṭābhāvastadanyabhāvāt'; ityevaṃrūpe prayoge ghaṭasya sarvatra deśe sarvadā cābhāvaḥ prasajyeta | dharmiṇi hi kvaciddharmasya guṇabhūtasya sādhane tatraiva tatkāla eva ca bhāvo yukto nānyadeti sarvatra samudāya eva sādhyo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ na kevalo dharma iti |
body.translated_text: If [one says:] the aggregate is never accepted as what is to be proved — he says: "And thus" — even if the provability of a property alone, independently, is accepted, in a proof-statement of the form 'the absence of the pot, because of the existence of another' — the absence of the pot everywhere and always would follow as a consequence. For when a property that is a subordinate [attribute] is proved with respect to the property-bearer somewhere, its existence is appropriate only there and at that time, and not elsewhere — therefore, only the aggregate is to be accepted as what is to be proved, not [the property] alone.

body.text: atrāha paraḥ- nāsamudāyasya sādhyatā anyabhāvatadabhāvayorasambandho vā | kutaḥ? | "pradeśādi" ityādi | ‘iha pradeśe ghaṭo nāsti'; ityevaṃ ghaṭābhāvena pradeśādirdharmī viśeṣyate saghaṭāt pradeśāderbhedenāvasthāpyata iti tadviśeṣaṇatvaṃ prāptasādhyate na tu ghaṭo nāstītyevaṃ "kevalo" dharmiṇaḥ kasyacigduṇabhāvamanāpannaḥ | tato nāsamudāyasya sādhyateti kutastadbhāvī doṣaḥ? | "na ca" naivāsminpakṣe "liṅgasyā" nyabhāvātmano "liṅginaśca" pradeśādidharmilakṣaṇasya "asambandhadoṣaḥ prasajyate" | kuta? | "anyabhāvasya" ghaṭaviviktapradeśadilakṣaṇasya "pradeśādinā" dharmiṇā (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 185.

children.text: ) "sambandhāt" tadātmyasadbhāvāditi | tathā hi- śabdādidharmiṇā kṛtakatvādestādātmyalakṣaṇa eva sambandha iṣyate bhavatā | sa ihāstītyabhiprāyaḥ | tataśca ‘sambandhābhāvācca'; ityayuktamiti manyate |
children.translated_text: ) "because of the relation" — because of the existence of the relation of identity. For: you accept that between the property-bearer such as sound and the like and [its property] such as being produced, the relation is characterized as identity alone. That [relation] exists here [too] — this is the intention. And therefore, [the objection that] 'because of the absence of a relation' was inappropriate — so [the opponent] thinks.

body.translated_text: Here the opponent says: it is not the case that only the non-aggregate is what is to be proved, or that there is no relation between the existence of another and the absence of that. Why? "The location and the like" and so on. [The reasoning is:] 'In this location, the pot does not exist' — thus, by the absence of the pot, the location and the like are qualified as the property-bearer, being established as different from a location with a pot — and this qualifying function is what is being proved, not that 'the pot does not exist' as a "bare" [property] that has not attained the status of being subordinate to any property-bearer. Therefore, it is not the case that only a non-aggregate is what is to be proved.

body.text: siddhāntavādī tu sādhyadharmalakṣaṇasya liṅgino ghaṭābhāvākhyasyānyabhāvena liṅgena sambandhābhāvaḥ prāgukto na dharmiṇā tataḥ damuttaraṃ sāṃbadhyata iti manyamāno dharmiṇāpyanyabhāvākhyasya liṅgasya sambandhābhāvaṃ darśayannāha- "na" liṅgaliṅginorasambandho na ceti sambadhyate | tathā nāsamudāyasādhanamiti | kintu liṅgaliṅginorasambandha evāsamudāyasādhanameva ca evamapi bruvataḥ | kutaḥ? | pradeśādereva dharmitayāvasthāpyamānasyānyabhāvatvādanyabhāvalakṣaṇaliṅgatvāt | etadeva darśayati- yatraiva hi pradeśādau dharmitayā tvayā kalpyamāne yad ghaṭādikaṃ nāsītyucyate lokena sa eva pradeśādistena ghaṭādināsaṃsṛṣṭassaṃsargarahitaḥ "anyabhāvo" liṅgatayeṣṭo nāparaḥ kaścit yataḥ "taddarśanādeva" ghaṭāsaṃsṛṣṭapradeśādidarśanādevāsya pratipattuḥ ‘ghaṭo nāsti'; iti vikalpo liṅgijñānatayopagato bhavati | tataḥ sa evānyabhāvaḥ | yadeva hi dṛśyamānaṃ liṅgijñānaṃ janayati tadeva liṅgamucyate | ghaṭāsaṃsṛṣṭaśca pradeśādirevam | tasmāt tadevānyabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ liṅgamupeyam | tataḥ kathaṃ tasyaivānyabhāvasya vyāvṛttito 'pi bhedamananubhavato liṅgaliṅgibhāvo liṅgatvaṃ liṅgitvaṃ vā? | nahi liṅgameva dharmī bhavitumarhati, dharmipratipattāveva sādhyapratipatteranvayādyanusaraṇāyogāt | tataścānyasya dharmiṇo 'bhāvāt kathamanyabhāvātmano liṅgasya tatsambandhaḥ, samudāyasādhyatā vā? | śabdakṛtakatvayostu paramārthatastādātmye 'pi vyāvṛttibhedanibandhano 'styeva bhedaḥ | tataḥ śabdādidharmipratipattāvapyanityatvādyapratītau kṛtakatvādinā tat sādhyata iti yuktam |
body.translated_text: But the proponent of the thesis, thinking that the absence of relation stated earlier was between the inferential mark called the existence of another and the thing marked called the absence of the pot — which is the nature of the property to be proved — and not with the property-bearer, and therefore this response is not relevant — showing the absence of relation between the inferential mark called the existence of another and the property-bearer too, says: "Not" — the absence of a relation between the inferential mark and what is marked — 'not' connects with [the previous statement]. Likewise, it is not a proof of the non-aggregate. Rather, the very absence of relation between the inferential mark and what is marked is [the reason for] the non-aggregate [not being provable].

body.text: syānmatam- sāmānyaviśeṣakalpanayā liṅgaliṅgitaikasyāpi bhaviṣyatītyata āha- "na cātra" prakṛte 'nyabhāve "sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvakalpanā sambhavati", yena sāmānyaviśeṣavikalpena sāmānyaṃ heturbhaved viśeṣo dharmī, yataḥ samudāyasādhyatā (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 186.

children.text: ) liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandho vā syāt | kuto na sambhavatītyāha- tadviśeṣapratipattereva" ghaṭaviviktapradeśaviśeṣapratipattereva "tadabhāvasya" ghaṭābhāvasya pratīteḥ | yataśca viśeṣa eva ghaṭābhāvapratītinibandhanaṃ tataḥ kiṃ tatra sāmānyakalpanayā kriyata iti | sa eva viśeṣo 'nyatra vartamānaḥ sāmānyarūpatāṃ pratipatsyata iti cet, āha- "tasya" ghaṭaviviktapradeśaviśeṣasya "anyatra" sajātīye "anvayasya" anuvṛtterabhāvāt kutaḥ sāmānyātmatā? | na hyasau deśakālāvasthāniyato viśeṣo 'nyamanvetīti | atraivopacayahetumāha- "pratijñārthe"tyādi | yadi hi ghaṭavivikta eva pradeśaviśeṣo dharmī, tasyaiva ca hetuteṣyate, tadā pratijñāyā yo 'rtho dharmadharmisamudāyastadekadeśa eva dharmilakṣaṇo hetuḥ syāt, pratijñārthaikadeśasya ca vyāvṛttito 'pi bhedamanu(na)nubhavato hetutvamasiddhamiti | atha mā bhūt eṣa doṣa iti na ghaṭavivikta eva pradeśaviśeṣo heturiṣyate, kintu pradeśamātraṃ ghaṭaviviktatāviśeṣarahitamityata āha- "na ca yatra pradeśamātraṃ tatra ghaṭābhāvaḥ" | saghaṭe 'pi pradeśe pradeśamātrasya bhāvādanaikāntiko hetuḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: ) or the relation between the inferential mark and what is marked would exist. Why is it not possible? He says: "Because of the cognition of the absence of that" — the absence of the pot — "from the cognition of that very particular" — the cognition of that very particular location devoid of the pot. And since it is the particular alone that is the ground for the cognition of the absence of the pot, what then is accomplished by the supposition of a universal therein? If [one says:] that very particular, when occurring elsewhere, would attain the form of a universal — he says: "Of that" — of the pot —

body.translated_text: One might think: through the supposition of universal and particular, even the relation of inferential mark and what is marked for one [entity] will be [established]. To this he says: "And here" — in the present [case of] the existence of another — "the supposition of the relation of universal and particular is not possible," such that through the distinction of universal and particular, the universal would be the reason and the particular the property-bearer, whereby the provability of the aggregate (

body.text: paro 'nyathā sāmānyaviśeṣabhāvaṃ darśayannāha- tādṛśau(śe) yādṛśo ghaṭaviviktaḥ kevalaḥ pradeśo 'grataḥ sthitastādṛśe sarvatra pradeśe ghaṭasyābhāva iti kuto 'nekāntaḥ? | tathāvidhapradeśaviśeṣapratītireva ghaṭābhāvapratītistato 'nyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ liṅgaliṅgitānupapannetyupadarśayannāha- "nanu tasyaiva" ityādi | yo 'sau kevalaḥ pradeśaviśeṣo dharmitayāvasthāpitastasyaiva yat kaivalyaṃ kevala ityanena viśeṣaṇenocyate bhavatā, ta deva ghaṭaviraho ghaṭābhāva iti kathyate | sa ca ghaṭaviraho liṅgabhūtasya kevalasya pradeśasya pratipattāveva siddho na tūttarakālaṃ tato 'nya eva ākārāntareṇa dhūmādivāgniḥ sidhyati | tataḥ kasyedānīṃ "tatpratipattāveva" sādhyapratītau satyāṃ talliṅgam? | na kasyacit | (

children.text: ) jijñāsitasya ghaṭābhāvasya siddheranyasya kasyacidajijñāsitatvāt | kevalapradeśapratipattāveva ghaṭavirahapratītau ca yadetaduttarakālaṃ ‘yatra yatra kevalaḥ pradeśastatra tatra ghaṭavirahaḥ'; iti "anvayasyānugamāmanu( gamanam" anu)saraṇam, tacca nirarthakam ādāveva sādhyapratīteḥ | yata evaṃ tasmādanyabhāvaḥ kevalapradeśalakṣaṇaḥ sādhyasādhanayorbhedābhāvānna sādhanamabhāvasyeti sthitam | tadevaṃ samudāyasādhyatāṃ liṅgasya ca dharmiṇāsambandhaṃ pratipādayituṃ yaduktaṃ pareṇa- ‘pradeśādidharmiviśeṣaṇasyābhāvasya sādhanāt'; iti tadapṛthaksiddhidūṣaṇenaiva nirākṛtam |
children.translated_text: Because once the absence of the pot, which was sought to be known, is established, there is nothing else that was sought to be known. And when the separation from the pot is cognized in the very apprehension of the bare locus, then the subsequent tracing of the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) — namely, "wherever there is a bare locus, there is separation from the pot" — that tracing (<s>anugama</s>) is pointless, since what is to be proved is already cognized at the outset. Because this is so, therefore <s>anyabhāva</s> (existence of something else), characterized as a bare locus, is not a means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) of absence, since there is no distinction between what is to be proved and the means of proof. This is established. Thus, in order to demonstrate that the <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark) proves the aggregate [of properties] and that there is no connection with the property-possessor, what the opponent stated — "because absence is proved as a qualification of the property-possessor such as the locus" — that has been refuted by the very objection of non-separateness (<s>apṛthaksiddhi</s>).

body.translated_text: The opponent, showing the relation of universal and particular in a different way, says: In such [a locus] — namely, whichever bare locus (<s>kevala pradeśa</s>) stands before [us] devoid of a pot — in every such locus there is absence of the pot. So how is there any indeterminacy (<s>anekānta</s>)? The cognition of that particular kind of locus is itself the cognition of the absence of the pot. Therefore, showing that the relation of mark and marked between <s>anyabhāva</s> (existence of something else) and <s>tadabhāva</s> (absence of that) is untenable, he says: "<s>nanu tasyaiva</s>" and so forth. That very bare particular locus which has been established as the property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) — its very aloneness (<s>kaivalya</s>), which is expressed by you through the qualifier "bare" (<s>kevala</s>) — that itself is called the separation from the pot, the absence of the pot. And that separation from the pot is established in the very apprehension of the bare locus which serves as the mark (<s>liṅga</s>), not subsequently as something different from it, in the way fire is established through a different form such as smoke. Therefore, for what is there now a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of that [absence], when the cognition of what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) is already achieved "in the very apprehension of that"? For nothing whatsoever.

body.text: viṣayaviṣayibhāvena tu sambandhapratipādane niraste paro 'nyathā sambandhaṃ sādhyasādhanayorddarśayannāha- "astya"nyabhāvatadabhāvayoḥ sambandho virodhākhyaḥ | tataḥ sambandhasadbhāvādanyabhāvādabhāvasya siddhirbhaviṣyatīti | siddhāntavādī tu sādhyasādhanayorvirodhamevāsambhāvayan pṛcchati- "kena kasya virodhaḥ" iti | na hyatra sādhyasādhanayorvirodhaḥ saṃbhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ | paro virodhamabhiprāyanabhijñatayā darśayati- "anyabhāvena" kevalapradeśātmanā "pratiyogino" yasyābhāvaḥ pramātumiṣṭo ghaṭādestasyeti |
body.translated_text: When the demonstration of the connection [between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s>] through the relation of object and subject has been rejected, the opponent, showing the connection of what is to be proved and the means of proof in a different way, says: "There exists between <s>anyabhāva</s> (existence of something else) and <s>tadabhāva</s> (absence of that) a connection called <s>virodha</s> (opposition). Therefore, due to the existence of this connection, there will be the establishment of absence from the existence of something else." But the proponent (<s>siddhāntavādin</s>), not conceiving of any opposition between what is to be proved and the means of proof, asks: "What is opposed to what (<s>kena kasya virodhaḥ</s>)?" The intent is that opposition between <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> is not possible here. The opponent, displaying opposition as one who does not understand the intent, shows: "By <s>anyabhāva</s>" — i.e., having the nature of the bare locus — "of the counter-positive (<s>pratiyogin</s>)" — i.e., of that [entity] such as a pot whose absence is desired to be ascertained.

body.text: parasyaivaṃvādino asambandhābhidhāyitāmādarśayannāha- "kiṃ nu vai pratiyogī" ghaṭādiḥ pramātumiṣṭo yena pratiyoginaḥ prameyatvena liṅgaliṅginorvirodhaḥ sambandho 'bhidhīyate? | naiva pratiyogī pramātumiṣṭaḥ kintu tadabhāva iti cet, āha- "abhāvastu" pratiyogino yaḥ sādhya .........................................................................................
body.translated_text: Showing the speaker-of-non-connection character of the opponent who speaks thus, he says: "Is the counter-positive (<s>pratiyogin</s>)" — such as a pot — "desired to be ascertained, by virtue of which the opposition, i.e. connection, of mark and marked is asserted through the counter-positive being what is to be measured (<s>prameya</s>)?" The counter-positive is not at all desired to be ascertained; rather, its absence [is what is to be proved] — if so, he says: "But the absence (<s>abhāva</s>)" of the counter-positive, which is what is to be proved...

body.text: kumārilastu manyate bhavāṃśādbhinno '
body.translated_text: [<s>Kumārila</s>, however, holds: this aspect of absence (<s>abhāvāṃśa</s>) is different from the aspect of positive being (<s>bhāvāṃśa</s>); therefore, <s>anyabhāva</s> (existence of something else) is not itself <s>tadabhāva</s> (absence of that) — so how can the apprehension of the former be the apprehension of the latter? For this absence is divided into sub-types such as <s>prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) and others,

body.text: yamabhāvāṃśastato nānyabhāva eva tadabhāva iti kathaṃ tatpratipattireva tadabhāvapratipattiriti | tathā hyayamabhāvaḥ prāgabhāvādibhedabhinnaḥ, (
Hbṭ 188
) na cāvastuno bhedaḥ sambhavati ato 'yaṃ vasturūpa eva | yadāha-
body.translated_text: and distinction (<s>bheda</s>) is not possible for a non-entity (<s>avastu</s>); therefore, this [absence] is of the nature of a real entity (<s>vastu</s>). As [<s>Kumārila</s>] states:

body.text:
"na cāvastuna ete syurbhedāstenāsya vastutā ||" iti |
na ca bhāvāṃśa evābhāvāṃśo yuktaḥ, tasyendriyasaṃyogabalena pratīteḥ, itarapratīteśca tadasaṃyogahetukatvāt | yadāha-
body.translated_text: "These distinctions could not belong to a non-entity; therefore it has the nature of a real thing." And the aspect of absence cannot be identical with the aspect of positive being, because the latter is cognized through the power of sense-contact, while the cognition of the former has as its cause the absence of such contact. As [<s>Kumārila</s>] states:

body.text:
"tatsaṃyoge sadityevaṃ sadrūpatvaṃ pratīyate |
nāstyatredamitītthaṃ tu tadasaṃyogahetukam ||" iti |
body.translated_text: "When there is contact with that [object], the cognition 'this exists' — [reflecting] its real nature — arises. But [the cognition] 'this does not exist here' is caused by the absence of contact with that [object]."

body.text: tatkathaṃ tatpratipattirevāparasya vyavacchedanamiti tannirāsārthamāha | "tasyā"nyasya pradeśasya kevalasya yat tat "kaivalya" mekākikatvamasahāyatā tadeva "aparasya" pratiyogino ghaṭādeḥ "vaikalyam" abhāva "iti" tasmāt "tadanyabhāva eva" bhāvāṃśa eva tvadabhimataḥ "tadabhāvaḥ" pratiyogyabhāvāṃśo na tataḥ pṛthagbhūtaṃ dharmāntaramityucyate sugatasutaiḥ | tataśca "tatpratipattireva ca" tasyānyabhāvasya pratipattireva ca "tadapratipattiḥ" tasya pratiyogino 'pratipattirabhāvapratipattiriti yāvat | evaṃ manyate- yo 'yamabhāvāṃśo bhāvāṃśāt pṛthagbhūto vastuno dharmaḥ parikalpyate sa ghaṭādyabhāvātmakatāṃ tadrūpavaikalyādevānubhavati nānyathā | tacca tadrūpavaikalyamanyavastuno bhāvāṃśasyāpi vidyata eva | tadabhāve hi tasyānyavastutaiva hīyeta | nahi yad yadrūpavikalaṃ na bhavati tat tato 'nyatvamanubhavati, yathā tasyaiva svarūpam, tathā cābhāvāṃśo 'pi tasya na sidhyet, sarvaṃ ca viśvamekaṃ dravyaṃ prasajyeta, tataśca sahotpattyādiprasaṅgaḥ, sarvasya ca sarvatropayogaḥ syādityavaśyamanyavastuno bhāvarūpatā tadanyābhāvātmikaiva | tathā ca tatpratipattireva tadanyābhāvapratipattiḥ | tatsaṃyoga eva cendriyasya tadanyābhāvasaṃyoga iti kimucyate-
body.translated_text: Therefore, in order to refute [the view] that the apprehension of the one is itself the exclusion of the other, he says: The "aloneness" (<s>kaivalya</s>) of that other locus, the bare one — its solitary state, its being without a companion — that itself is the "deficiency" (<s>vaikalya</s>), i.e. the absence, "of the other," the counter-positive such as a pot. Therefore, "that <s>anyabhāva</s> (existence of something else) is itself" — i.e. the positive aspect itself, as you maintain — "that <s>tadabhāva</s> (absence of the counter-positive)" — the aspect of absence of the counter-positive is not a separate, distinct property from it — so say the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddhists). And therefore, "the apprehension of that" <s>anyabhāva</s> "is itself the non-apprehension of that" — i.e., the non-apprehension of the counter-positive, which amounts to the cognition of absence. [<s>Arcaṭa</s>] holds thus: the aspect of absence which is imagined as a property of a real entity, separate from the aspect of positive being, experiences its character as absence of a pot and so forth only by virtue of the deficiency of that form (<s>tadrūpavaikalya</s>), and not otherwise. And that deficiency of that form belongs also to the positive aspect of another entity. For in the absence of that [deficiency], its very otherness from the other entity would be lost. Indeed, whatever is not devoid of whatever form does not experience otherness from that, just as [a thing does not differ from] its own nature — and thus the aspect of absence too would not be established for it, and the entire universe would become a single substance, with the absurd consequence of simultaneous arising and so forth, and everything would be useful for everything. Therefore, the positive nature of another entity is necessarily of the nature of absence of what is other than it. And thus the apprehension of that is itself the apprehension of the absence of its other. And if the sense-organ's contact with that is itself the contact with the absence of what is other than it, then why is it said:

body.text: "nāstyatredamitītthaṃ tu tadasaṃyogahetukam |" iti? | vikalpāpekṣayoktamiti cet, tadetadabādhakameva | pratyakṣeṇa tadākārotpattyā tadanyabhāvātmake eva vasturūpe pratipanne pāścātyasya (

children.text: ) yathāgṛhītābhilāpino vikalpasyopagamāt | vistarataścāyamabhāvavicāraḥ pramāṇadvitvasiddhāvabhāvaṃ prameyaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca vicārayatā vihita iti tata evāvavadhārya iti |
children.translated_text: conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), which expresses [things] as apprehended, follows [accordingly]. And this investigation of absence (<s>abhāvavicāra</s>) has been set forth in detail in the <s>Pramāṇadvitvasiddhi</s> (Establishment of the Twofold Means of Knowledge), when examining absence as an object of knowledge and as a means of knowledge; therefore, it should be ascertained from that [work].

body.translated_text: "But [the cognition] 'this does not exist here' is caused by the absence of contact with that"? If it is said that this is stated with reference to conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>), then this is indeed not a valid objection. For when through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), by the arising of the form of that [object], the real nature — which is itself of the character of <s>anyabhāva</s> (otherness from the absent entity) — has been apprehended, the subsequent

body.text: avaśyaṃ ca tadanyabhāvapratipattireva tadabhāvapratipattiḥ | tato na vastvasaṅkarasidhyarthaṃ, ‘nāstyatredam'; ityabhāvavyavahārārthaṃ cābhāvapramāṇaparikalpanā yukteti darśayannāha- "anyathā" yadi tatpratipattireva tadabhāvapratipattiriti neṣyate tadā "tasya" anyavastunaḥ svarūpaparicchedena tato 'nyasyātadrūpasya "avyavacchede" anirākaraṇe tadabhāvāpratipattau "tatpariccheda eva na syāt"- tasya tadanyavastunaḥ svarūpapratipattireva na syāt | kiṃ kāraṇam?
