body.text: tasmādavaśyaṃ pratibandhaḥ sādhyasādhanayorabhyupagantavyaḥ | sa evānvayavyatirekaprayogābhyāṃ sucanīyaḥ | na cāsau vyāptyānvayavyatirekopadarśanamantareṇa khyāpayituṃ śakyata iti ‘yatra yatra'; iti sakalapadārthaparigraheṇa khyāpyate | pratibandhe hi pramāṇasiddhe satyavaśyameva yatra yatra kāryaṃ tatra tatra kāraṇam, yatra yatra tadabhāvaḥ tatra tatra ca kāryasyāpyabhāvo 'nyathā kāraṇamantareṇa kāryasya bhāve tasyāhetutaiva syāt | tataśca nityaṃ sattvādiprasaṅgaḥ | tathā yatra yatra yatsvabhāvastatra tatra tadbhāvaḥ anyathā tasya nairātmyameva syāditi vyāptyaivānvayavyatirekopadarśane pratibandhaḥ khyāpayituṃ śakyate nānyatheti prāgeva vistarato vipañcitam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, the necessary connection between what is to be proved and the means of proof must be acknowledged. That very [connection] is to be indicated through the demonstrations of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance). And since that [necessary connection] cannot be made known without demonstrating <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) through <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>, it is made known through an exhaustive inclusion of all objects with 'wherever.' For when the necessary connection has been established by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition), necessarily wherever there is an effect, there is the cause; and wherever there is absence of that [cause], there is absence of the effect as well — otherwise, if the effect existed without the cause, that [cause] would simply not be its cause. And consequently, there would be the unwanted consequence of perpetual existence and the like. Similarly, wherever there is something of a certain nature, there is the existence of that [nature] — otherwise there would simply be the selflessness of that. Thus, the necessary connection can be made known only through demonstrating <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> by means of <s>vyāpti</s>, and not otherwise — this has been elaborated in detail previously.

body.translated_text: 4. Summary regarding the triple characteristic of the reason, its threefold nature, and the status of pseudo-reasons.

body.text: evaṃ kāryasvabhāvānupalabdhilakṣaṇe eva pakṣadharme tatsādhakapramāṇasadbhāvādanvayavyatirekasadbhāvo nānyatreti pratipādyopasaṃharannāha- (

children.translated_text: ) "Thus" — this very property of the thesis-locus, characterized by intrinsic nature, effect, and non-apprehension, possesses <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) because of the existence of the necessary connection. And since it possesses <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> by reason of the existence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing the necessary connection, in the manner explained, "thus" — therefore — "pervaded by that aspect" — because the pervasion by that aspect is ascertained only through the ascertainment of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>, as stated before. And therefore, from the statement of pervasion by that aspect, the reason that possesses the triple characteristic is "triple-characterized alone" — threefold alone — the probative reason, and no other-characterized or other [reason], because any additional characteristic would be futile when the stated triple characteristic exists, and because even if an additional characteristic were postulated in the absence of the stated triple characteristic, there would be no probative force due to the absence of non-deviation. Why is the reason that is triple-characterized alone, threefold alone, probative and no other-characterized or other? He shows: "Because of non-deviation from its own provable property" — because the triple-characterized alone has non-deviation from its own provable property. And since probative force consists in non-deviation from its own provable property alone, the postulation of an additional characteristic is futile. And in the absence of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> grounded in the necessary connection, even if an additional characteristic were postulated, there would be no non-deviation from its own provable property. By this, another meaning of 'it is only threefold' has been shown: that "the reason" is triple-characterized alone, "because of the invariable" non-deviation from its own provable property, "necessarily" — because of its definite existence — and "pseudo-reasons are the others" — those that are postulated [as reasons] through the attribution of additional characteristics beyond the stated triple characteristic are pseudo-reasons, because non-deviation from the provable property — the non-deviation from its own provable property — is absent in them.

body.translated_text: Having thus demonstrated that <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) exist only in the property of the thesis-locus characterized by effect, intrinsic nature, and non-apprehension, because there exists a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) establishing them, and not elsewhere — summarizing what has been demonstrated, he says: (

body.text: 5. hetulakṣaṇe 'dhikarūpavādināṃ nirāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: 5. Refutation of those who maintain additional characteristics of the reason.

body.text: yaduktaṃ ‘trilakṣaṇa eva heturnānyalakṣaṇaḥ'; iti tatra pareṣāṃ vipratipattiṃ darśayannāha- "ṣaḍlakṣaṇo heturityapare" naiyāyika- mimāṃsakādayo manyante | kāni punaḥ ṣaḍrūpāṇi hetostairiṣyaṃte? ityāha- ‘trīṇi caitāni" pakṣadharmānvayavyatirekākhyāni | tathābādhitaviṣayatvaṃ caturthaṃ rūpam | abādhitaḥ pramāṇenānirākṛto viṣayaḥ sādhyadharmalakṣaṇo yasya sa tathoktaḥ tasya bhāvaḥ tattvamaparaṃ rūpam | tathā vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvaṃ rūpāntaraṃ, ekā saṃkhyā yasya hetudravyasya (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 206.

children.text: ) tadekasaṃkhyaṃ vivakṣitamekasaṃkhyaṃ hetudravyamāśrayatvena yasya hetusāmānyasya tadvivakṣitaikasaṃkhyaṃ tadbhāvo 'paraṃ rūpam | yadyekasaṃkhyāvyāvacchinnāyāṃ pratiheturahitāyāṃ hetuvyaktau hetutvaṃ bhavati tadā gamakatvaṃ na tu pratihetusahitāyāmapi dvisaṃkhyāyuktāyāmiti | yadi viruddhāvyabhicāryaparaṃ hetvantaraṃ nopadarśyata iti yāvat | tathā jñātatvaṃ ca jñānaviṣayatvaṃ ca | nahyajñāto hetuḥ svasattāmātreṇa gamako yuktaḥ iti | tatraiteṣu rūpāntareṣu yadetabādhitaviṣayatvaṃ nāma tat tāvat pratibandhanibandhanānvayavyatirekātmakāvinābhāvasambhave sati tataḥ pṛthaganyallakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati | tadātmakaṃ tu tadvacanenaivoktamiti na vaktavyamiti | kasmāt pṛthag lakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati? bādhāyā avinābhāvasya ca virodhāditi | tathā hi- satyapyavinābhāve yathokte bādhāsambhavaṃ manyamānairabādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaramucyate | sā ceyaṃ tatsambhāvanā na sambhavati, bādhāyā avinābhāvena "virodhāt" sahānavasthānalakṣaṇāt | tameva virodhaṃ sādhayannāha- "avinābhāvo hi" ityādi | satyeva hi sādhyadharme bhāvo hetoravinābhāva ucyate | pramāṇabādhā tu tasminnasati | yadi hi satyeva tasmiṃstadabhāvaviṣayaṃ pramāṇaṃ pravarteta tadāsya bhrāntatvādapramāṇataiva syāt iti kuto bādhā? | tataḥ "sa" hetuḥ "tallakṣaṇaḥ" sādhyāvinābhāvī "dharmiṇi syāt | atra ca sādhyadharmaḥ kathaṃ na bhavet"? yato bādhāvakāśaḥ syāt | tasmādavinābhāvasya pramāṇabādhāyāśca sahānavasthānamavinābhāvenopasthāpitasya dharmiṇi sādhyadharmabhāvasya pramāṇabādhopasthāpitasya ca tadabhāvasya parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇatayā virodhenaikatra dharmiṇyasambhavāditi |
children.translated_text: ) — that intended singular number, the substance of the reason having the number one as its support — of which reason-universal, that being of the intended singular number is another form. If reason-hood exists in a reason-instance delimited by the number one, devoid of a counter-reason, then there is indicative function, but not in one that is also accompanied by a counter-reason and endowed with the number two — that is, if no other reason that is contradictory or non-deviating is shown. Likewise, being known — being the object of cognition. For an unknown reason, by its mere existence alone, is not appropriate as an indicator. Therein, among these additional characteristics, that which is called having an uncontradicted domain — that, when invariable concomitance grounded in the necessary connection, consisting of positive and negative concomitance, is possible — is not a separate, additional defining characteristic apart from that. And that which is of that nature has been stated by that very statement [of invariable concomitance], so it need not be stated [separately]. Why is it not a separate defining characteristic? Because of the "contradiction" between sublation and invariable concomitance. For: even when invariable concomitance exists as described, those who consider sublation to be possible state having an uncontradicted domain as an additional characteristic. But this supposition is not possible, because of the "contradiction" between sublation and invariable concomitance — characterized as the impossibility of co-existence. Establishing that very contradiction, he says: "For invariable concomitance" and so on. For invariable concomitance is said to be the existence of the reason precisely when the property to be proved exists. But sublation by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition) occurs when that [property] does not exist. For if a <s>pramāṇa</s> whose object is the absence of that were to operate when that [property] actually exists, then, being erroneous, it would not be a <s>pramāṇa</s> at all — so whence sublation? Therefore, "that" reason, "characterized by that" — possessing invariable concomitance with what is to be proved — "would exist in the property-bearer. And how could the property to be proved not exist there?" — such that there would be occasion for sublation. Therefore, the impossibility of co-existence of invariable concomitance and sublation by a <s>pramāṇa</s> [is established] — because, due to the contradiction characterized by mutual exclusion between the existence of the property to be proved in the property-bearer as established by invariable concomitance, and the absence of that as established by sublation through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, they cannot co-exist in a single property-bearer.

body.translated_text: Regarding what was stated — 'the reason is triple-characterized alone, not having any other characteristic' — showing the disagreement of others on this point, he says: "The reason has six characteristics, say others" — the <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, and others think [this]. What then are the six characteristics of the reason accepted by them? He says: "These three" — namely, the property of the thesis-locus, <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance), and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance). Likewise, having an uncontradicted object is the fourth characteristic — 'uncontradicted' means having as its object the provable property that is not refuted by a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid cognition); one that is such is so called; its state, its nature, is another characteristic. Likewise, having the intended singular enumeration is yet another characteristic — [that is,] the reason-substance that has a single enumeration (

body.text: tameva virodhaṃ spaṣṭīkartuṃ paropahāsavyājenāha- "pratyakṣānumāne hi" ityādi | sādhyadharmaṃ hi bādhamāne pratyakṣānumāne, "taṃ grīvāyāṃ gṛhītvā" dharmiṇaḥ svāśrayāt "niṣkāsayataḥ" | tasmiṃśca sādhyadharme satyeva tadavinābhāvitvāddheturbhavaṃ "staṃ" sādhyadharmaṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 207.

children.text: ) niṣkāsyamānaṃ gale gṛhītvā haṭhāt "tatraiva" dharmiṇyavasthāpayatīti "paraṃ" prakṛṣṭaṃ bata "bhāvānāṃ" sādhyadharmalakṣaṇānāmasvāsthyaṃ vartate | tathā hi- yantradvayaniyantritānāṃ nirucchāvasitayā maraṇameva prāptamiti |
children.translated_text: ) — being expelled, [the reason] seizes it by the throat and forcibly "establishes it right there" in the property-bearer. And so, "supremely" — exceedingly — alas — "the distress of the entities" characterized as properties to be proved — prevails. For, being constrained by two machines [sublation and invariable concomitance], death alone has been reached through the impossibility of breathing.

body.translated_text: In order to make that very contradiction vivid, under the guise of mocking the opponent, he says: "For perception and inference" and so on. For when perception and inference sublate the property to be proved, they "seize it by the neck" and "expel it" from its own support, the property-bearer. And since the reason, by virtue of its invariable concomitance, necessarily accompanies that property to be proved when it exists, "that" property to be proved (

body.text: paro bādhāvinābhāvayorviṣayabhedādavirodhaṃ darśayannāha- "anyatra" sādhyadharmiṇaṃ parihṛtya dṛṣṭāntadharmiṇi sādhyadharmeṇāvinābhāvī heturna punaḥ sādhyadharmiṇyeva | tataḥ kuto bādhāvinābhāvayorvirodho 'nyatra bādhayā sādhyadharmābhāvasādhanādanyatra ca hetunā tadbhāvasādhanāt | tathā caivaṃvidhe satyapi avinābhāve bādhāsambhavād abādhitaviṣayatvasya rūpāntarasya sambhava iti |
body.translated_text: The opponent, showing the non-contradiction of sublation and invariable concomitance due to difference of domain, says: "Elsewhere" — setting aside the property-bearer of what is to be proved, the reason is invariably concomitant with the property to be proved in the property-bearer of the example, not in the property-bearer of what is to be proved itself. Therefore, whence the contradiction of sublation and invariable concomitance, since sublation establishes the absence of the property to be proved elsewhere [in the subject], and the reason establishes its existence elsewhere [in the example]? And thus, for such a kind [of invariable concomitance] —

body.text: evaṃvidhāvinābhāvopagame satyapyabādhitaviṣayatvādike rūpāntare "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare" rūpāntarasambhavina ityāpāditāṃ hetvābhāsatāṃ vivarītuṃ paropahāsapūrvakamāha- tat kim "ayaṃ" sādhyadharmī "tapasvī" varākaḥ "śaḍḍha(ṇḍha)mudvāhya tasmiṃn" sādhyadharmasādhanaśaktivikalaṃ hetuṃ pariṇāyya sādhyadharmalakṣaṇaṃ "putraṃ mṛgayate?" | etadeva vyanakti- "yasya" hetorddharmiṇyasatyapi "sādhyadharme bhāva" iṣyate, sādhyadharmiṇo 'nyatrāvinābhāvopagamāt | "taṃ" tathāvidhaṃ sādhyadharmiṇyupadarśya kathaṃ dharmī sādhyadharmavānityucyate? | na hy ambhastvasya samudre lavaṇatvenāvinābhāve 'pi tavdyatirikte 'mbhasi lavaṇatayā sādhyatveneṣṭe 'mbhastvabhāve 'pi lavaṇatvasiddhiriti |
body.translated_text: Even when invariable concomitance of this kind is accepted, in order to refute the charge of being a pseudo-reason due to additional characteristics such as having an uncontradicted domain — "pseudo-reasons are therefore other" — those that possess additional characteristics — preceded by mockery of the opponent, he says: "Is this" property-bearer, "poor thing," "a celibate who, having married" — having taken in the reason that lacks the power to establish the property to be proved — the property to be proved —

body.text: parasya vacanāvakāśamāśaṅkayāha- "ata eva" ityādi | etadeva vivṛṇoti- "syādetad" bhavato matam | yata eva heturanyathāpi sādhyadharmamantareṇāpi dharmiṇi bhavedambhastvādiṣu tathādarśanāt, sādhyadharmiparihāreṇa cāvinābhāvopagamāt ata eva kāraṇāt pramāṇābhyāmabādhitadharmā dharmītyucyate | yadi pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 208.

children.text: ) sādhyadharmiṇi hetorviṣayaḥ sādhyadharmo na bādhyate yathāmbhastvasya lavaṇatvam, tadā tasya gamakatvam, nānyatheti | tato 'nyatrāvinābhāvamātreṇa sādhyasiddheranabhyupagamāt na yathokto doṣa iti |
children.translated_text: ) — if, in the property-bearer of what is to be proved, the property to be proved, which is the domain of the reason, is not sublated — as the saltiness of water [is not sublated] — then there is indicative function for it; not otherwise. Therefore, since the establishment of what is to be proved is not acknowledged through invariable concomitance elsewhere alone, the fault as stated does not apply.

body.translated_text: Anticipating the opportunity for the opponent's statement, he says: "For this very reason" and so on. He elaborates on this: "This may be" your view. Since the reason could exist in the property-bearer even otherwise — even without the property to be proved — as observed in water and the like [where there is no fire despite smoke-like appearances], and since invariable concomitance is accepted only setting aside the property-bearer of what is to be proved, for this very reason it is said that the property-bearer is one whose property is not sublated by the <s>pramāṇas</s>. If [the property] by perception —

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "tat kim" idānīṃ yadā hetordharmiṇyavinābhāvitānabhyupagamāt sādhyasiddherabhāvāt tatsiddhaye rūpāntaramabādhitaviṣayatvamucyate tadā hetorna kiñcit sāmarthyam | kasmād? "abādhayaiva" hetumantareṇāpi "sādhyasiddheḥ" akiñcitkara eva hetuḥ | tathā hyatra kalpanādvayam- bādhakapramāṇavṛttau sādhyābhāvo niyato vā syād? aniyato vā? | tatra yadi pūrvo vikalpastadā sādhyābhāvo hi bādhakapramāṇasya vṛttau niyataḥ, tadaiva bhāvāt tadabhāve cābhāvāditi | tasmād "abādhāyāṃ" bādhakapramāṇavṛttyabhāve tanniyatasya sādhyābhāvasyāpyabhāvāt "sādhyasiddhiḥ" bhavatyeveti vyartha eva heturiti nopanyasanīya eva | tataḥ kasyābādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaraṃ bhavet? | syānmatam- mā bhud bādhakapramāṇavṛttyabhāve hetoḥ sāmarthyam, yadā tu sādhyasya bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ dharmiṇi vartate tadā hetoḥ sādhyasādhane sāmarthyaṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha- "bādhāyāmapi" iti | yadi bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ vartate tadā tena sādhyābhāvasya dharmiṇi sādhanāt punarbrahmaṇāpi tadbhāvasya kartumaśakyatvāt kimaṅga punaḥ śaṭhena hetuneti kutaḥ sādhanasya hetoḥ sāmarthyam? | ata eva hi bhavadbhirabādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaramucyata iti |
body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis says: "Is it then" — now, when the establishment of what is to be proved is absent because invariable concomitance of the reason in the property-bearer is not acknowledged, and having an uncontradicted domain is stated as an additional characteristic for the purpose of that establishment — then the reason has no efficacy whatsoever. Why? "Because the establishment of what is to be proved [occurs] through non-sublation alone" — even without the reason — the reason is entirely superfluous. For here there are two alternatives in this supposition: [either] the sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> —

body.text: atha bādhakapramāṇavṛttau sādhyābhāvo na niyataḥ tadabhāve 'pi bhāvāditi dvitīyaḥ pakṣa iṣyate tadāpyabādhāyāḥ sāmarthyaviraha iti darśayannāha- "aniyame" bādhakapramāṇavṛttau sādhyābhāvasyeṣyamāṇe satīdamāpatitam | na ca- bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt "sādhyābhāvasya ca sambhavaḥ"- iti "na" sādhyasādhane "sāmarthyam abādhāyāḥ" satyāmapi tasyāṃ sādhyābhāvasya sambhavāditi tadyogino 'pi hetvābhāsataiveti |
body.translated_text: If the absence of what is to be proved is not invariable upon the operation of the sublating <s>pramāṇa</s>, because [what is to be proved] can exist even in its absence — if this second position is accepted, then even so, showing the absence of efficacy of non-sublation, he says: "When non-invariability" — of the absence of what is to be proved upon the operation of the sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> — is accepted, this has resulted: there would be neither a sublating <s>pramāṇa</s> nor "the possibility of the absence of what is to be proved" — "not" in the establishment of what is to be proved —

body.text: yaduktam "abādhayaiva sādhyasiddhervyartho hetuḥ" iti tatrānyathārthamabādhāyā darśayan hetusāmarthyaṃ pratipādayannāha paraḥ- na bādhāyā abhāvo mamābādhābhimatā | kiṃ tarhi? | bādhāyā anupalabdhiḥ | sā ca tadanupalabdhiḥ puruṣasya śaktivaikalyāt kvacid deśādau bādhāyāḥ sambhave 'pi syāt | tato bādhānupalabdhimātreṇa sādhyasiddherabhāvāt tatsiddhaye 'vaśyaṃ heturabhidhānīya iti sa hetuprayogasya viṣayastadā hi hetuḥ svasādhyaṃ sādhayan kathamasamarthaḥ syāt? iti |
body.translated_text: What was said — "the reason is purposeless, since what is to be proved is established through non-sublation alone" — in response to that, the opponent, showing that non-sublation has another purpose and demonstrating the efficacy of the reason, says: the absence of sublation is not what I consider non-sublation. What then? The non-apprehension of sublation. And that non-apprehension might occur due to the deficiency of the person's capacity, even when sublation is possible in some place and the like. Therefore, sublation —

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- kiṃ nu vai heturbbādhāyā yā upalabdhistasyāḥ vibheti na punarbbādhāyā yena bādhāṃ sambhavantīmapyanādṛtya tadanupalabdhau satyāṃ prayoktavya iṣṭo bhavataḥ |
body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis says: does the reason fear the apprehension of sublation, or does it fear sublation [itself]? — such that, disregarding sublation even when it is possible, [the reason] is considered by you to be employable when there is merely the non-apprehension of that [sublation].

body.text: kadācit paro brūyāt- kiṃ kariṣyati vidyamānāpi bādhā tapasvinī, tadupalabdhireva rākṣasī | tasmāt tata eva hetorbhayaṃ tadabhāve hetuḥ prayoktavya evetyata āha- "sa tarhi" ityādi | evaṃ tarhi paramārthena bādhā kimasti nāstītyetadanapekṣya bādhāyā anupalabdhau satyāṃ prayoktavya iti kākvā pṛcchati | kadācit paro brūyāt- uktamevaitat kimarthaṃ pṛcchyate? ityāha- "kimarthaṃ prayujyata" iti | bādhānupalambhe 'pi tatsambhave sādhyasādhanāyogādityabhiprāyaḥ | paro 'navagatābhiprāya āha- "sādhyasiddhyartham" iti bādhakapratyayābhāve pramāṇyasyeṣṭatvāt tataḥ sādhyasiddhiraviruddhaiveti manyate | siddhāntavādī satyāṃ bādhāyāṃ tadanupalambhe 'pi sādhyasiddhimasambhāvayan pṛcchati "sa kiṃ kvacid" ityādi | kiṃ punarasau hetuḥ satyāmapi bādhāyāṃ sādhyaṃ sādhayediti sambhāvyate bhavatā yenāsyā bādhāyā abhāvaniścayaṃ prati yatno na kriyate hetuśca prayujyata iti | evametat iti cet; tathā satyāmapi bādhāyāṃ sādhyasādhanasāmarthopagame satyabādhitaviṣayatvaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati | kiṃ kāraṇam? | bādhāyāmapi satyāmasya hetoḥ "sāmarthyāt" sāmarthyopagamāt | taddhi hetorlakṣaṇamucyate yena vinā sādhyaṃ na sādhayediti |
body.translated_text: The opponent might say: what will sublation do, poor thing, even if it exists? It is its apprehension alone that is the demoness [to be feared]. Therefore, the reason's fear is from that [apprehension] alone; in its absence, the reason is to be employed indeed. To this he says: "Then that" and so on. If so, then — is sublation ultimately existent or not — regardless of this, when there is merely the non-apprehension of sublation, [the reason] is to be employed — thus he asks with irony.

body.text: syānmatam- anupalabhyamānabādhatvaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ paramārthena, nābādhitaviṣayatvamityata āha- "tathā ca" ityādi | evaṃ hi sati bādhāyāḥ sadbhāvasambhave 'pi tāmabhyupagamya tadanupalambhamātreṇa hetoḥ prayogaḥ prāptaḥ | yadi hi bādhāmabhyupagamya hetuprayogo nābhimataḥ syāt tadānupalambhamātreṇa bādhāyaṃ saṃśayāt- satāmapi keṣāñcit kathañcidanupalambhasambhavāt- saṃśayitasya hetuprayoge pravṛttireva na yujyeta | tasmād yo yatsaṃśaye 'pi pravartate sa tasya bhāvapakṣamabhyupetyaiva pravartate | tathā ca yathā bādhānupalabdhau tāmabhyupagamya hetuḥ prayujyate tathā tadupalabdhāvapi prayujyatām, bādhāyāḥ sadbhāvābhyupagame sati tadupalambhānupalambhayorviśeṣābhāvāditi nānupalabhyamānabādhatvamapi hetulakṣaṇaṃ yujyata iti kuto bādhakapratyayavirahe 'pyasati pratibandhe prāmāṇyasya sambhava iti |
body.translated_text: One might think: having an unapprehended sublation is the defining characteristic of the reason in the ultimate sense, not having an uncontradicted domain. To this he says: "And thus" and so on. For if this is so, even when the existence of sublation is possible, accepting that [sublation] and merely through the non-apprehension of it, the employment of the reason has been obtained. For if the employment of the reason were not accepted while acknowledging sublation, then through mere non-apprehension, sublation —

body.text: parasya vacanāvakāśamāśaṅkayāha- "na bādhāyām" ityādi | naiva hi bādhāyāṃ saṃtyāṃ hetoḥ sāmarthyamiṣyate tat kathaṃ tadupalambhe 'pi prayogaḥ syāt? | siddhāntavādyāha- "yadyevaṃ" bādhāyāṃ satyāṃ heturasamartho yadīṣyate tadānirṇīto bādhāyā asaṃbhavo yasya hetoḥ sa tathāvidhaḥ prayogaṃ bādhānupalambhamātreṇa nārhati | kiṃ kāraṇam? | mā bhūd bādhāyāḥ sambhavapakṣe "prayuktasyāpi" hetoḥ sādhyasiddhau "asāmarthyamiti" | pūrvapakṣavādyāha- bādhānupalambhe sati bādhāyā abhāvāt sadupalambhakapratyayābhāve satyavaśyamarthānāmasattvāddhetoḥ sāmarthyam iti cenmanyase siddhāntavādyāha- "kimupalambho bādhām" ityādi | upalambho hyarthānāṃ kāryam, na ca kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ vyāpnoti | na hya'vaśyaṃ kāraṇāni kāryavanti bhavanti, pratibandhavaikalyasambhavāt | tat kathamavyāpakasyopalambhasya nivṛttau bādhāyā nivṛttiḥ?, yato hetorbbādhāyāḥ sambhavakṛtamasāmarthyaṃ na sambhavediti | etacca parairapīṣyata eva; pramāṇatayopagatasyāpyudayakāle 'nupalabdhabādhasya kālāntareṇa (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 211.

children.text: ) bādhakapratyayotpāde satyaprāmāṇyopagamāt | athāvyāpakasyāpyupalambhasya nivṛttau bādhā nivartate-
children.translated_text: ) — because, upon the arising of a sublating cognition, the non-validity [of the reason] is accepted. Or if sublation ceases upon the cessation of apprehension, even of [apprehension] that is not pervasive —

body.translated_text: Anticipating the opportunity for the opponent's statement, he says: "Not when sublation" and so on. For the efficacy of the reason is not accepted when sublation exists — so how could there be employment even upon its apprehension? The proponent of the thesis says: "If so" — if the reason is accepted as lacking efficacy when sublation exists — then a reason for which the impossibility of sublation has not been ascertained — such a reason, of that kind, [should not have] employment [based on] merely the non-apprehension of sublation —

body.text: "nivartate hi mithyātvaṃ doṣājñānādayatnataḥ ||"
body.translated_text: "For falsity ceases effortlessly, from [the removal of] faults and ignorance."

body.text: iti anenaiva nyāyena jñānanivṛttyā bādhānivṛtterityāha- ta- thāpi vyartho hetuḥ | kutaḥ? | "bādhānupalambhādeva" hetuprayogarahitāt sādhyasiddheḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam? | anupalambhe bādhāyā asambhavāt | tathā hi- yatra bādhāyā anupalambhastatra paramārthata eva sā na vidyata iti manyase | yatra cāsau paramārthato nāsti tatra sādhaydharmasyābhāvo 'pi paramārthenaiva nāstyanyathā paramārthena bādhāyā abhāvāyogāt | tataśca sādhyadharmasyābhāvābhāve sati bhāva iti bhavanmatyā sādhyapratītervyarthatā hetoriti |
body.translated_text: By this very principle, since sublation ceases through the cessation of cognition, he says: even so, the reason is purposeless. Why? "From the non-apprehension of sublation alone" — because what is to be proved is established without the employment of a reason. What is the basis? Because sublation is impossible when there is its non-apprehension. For: you think that where there is non-apprehension of sublation, there it does not ultimately exist. And where it ultimately does not exist, the absence of the property to be proved also does not ultimately exist — otherwise the ultimate absence of sublation would be impossible. And therefore, in the absence of the absence of the property to be proved, there is [its] existence — so, according to your view, the reason is purposeless since what is to be proved is cognized [without it].

body.text: atha mā bhūd yuktivirodha iti nopalambhanivṛttau bādhānivṛttiriṣyate, tatrāha- upalambhasya nivṛttāvapi satyāṃ bādhāyā anivṛttāviṣyamāṇāyāṃ tadavasthaṃ hetorasasāmarthyam yadavasthaṃ bādhopalambha iti hetoraprayoga iti kasyābādhitaviṣayatvaṃ rūpāntaraṃ syāt? |
body.translated_text: Now, lest there be a contradiction with reasoning, if the cessation of sublation is not accepted upon the cessation of apprehension — to that he says: even when the cessation of apprehension obtains, if the non-cessation of sublation is accepted, then the inefficacy of the reason remains exactly as it was when the apprehension of sublation [existed] — therefore the reason is not to be employed. So for whom would having an uncontradicted domain be an additional characteristic?

body.text: etadevopasaṃharannāha- "tasmāt svasādhya" ityādi | yata evaṃ vyāptyā hetoḥ sarvatra sādhyenāvinābhāvābhyupagame bahirvyāptāviṣyamāṇāyāṃ vaiyarthyaṃ hetuprayogasyāpadyate tasmāt "svasādhyabhāvābhāvābhyāṃ anyathāpi" svasādhyabhāve 'pyabhavanna'bhāve 'pi ca bhavan heturdharmiṇi kiñcit sādhyaṃ "na bhāvayati" na sādhayati "na vibhāvayati" tadviparītaṃ na niṣedhayati "iti" tasya vidhipratiṣedhāvakurvata "upakṣepaḥ" prayogo "na samarthaḥ" ityavaśyaṃ hetuprayogamicchatā svasādhyāvinābhāvaḥ sarvatra hetorabhyupagantavyaḥ | sa ca pratibandhanibandhanaḥ | eṣa ca darśanādarśanamātrayatto yathoktaṃ prāk | tasmiṃścābhyupagate bādhāvinābhāvayorvirodhaḥ siddha ityupasaṃharannāha- "tanna" ityādi | yata evaṃ tena kāraṇenābādhā rūpāntaraṃ na bhavati |
body.translated_text: Summarizing this very point, he says: "Therefore, [by] the presence and absence of what is to be proved" and so on. Since, when invariable concomitance of the reason with what is to be proved everywhere is acknowledged through pervasion, and when external pervasion is not accepted, the purposelessness of the employment of the reason results — therefore, "by the presence and absence of what is to be proved, even otherwise" — a reason that does not exist even when what is to be proved exists, or that exists even when [what is to be proved] does not exist — in the property-bearer, "does not establish" — does not prove — anything to be proved, and "does not refute" — does not negate — the opposite. "Thus," since it neither establishes nor negates, "the employment" — the use — [of such a reason] "is not efficacious." Therefore, one who desires to employ a reason must accept the invariable concomitance of the reason with what is to be proved everywhere. And that [invariable concomitance] is grounded in a necessary connection. And that [necessary connection] depends merely on observation and non-observation, as was previously stated. And when that is accepted, the contradiction between sublation and invariable concomitance is established — thus summarizing, he says: "Therefore not" and so on. Since it is thus, for that reason, non-sublation is not an additional characteristic.

body.text: yadi nāma bādhāvinābhāvayoḥ sahāvasthānābhāvādavinābhāve (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 212.

children.text: ) satyabādhā gamyate rūpāntaraṃ tu kimiti na bhavati? iti, ata āha- "tannāma" ityādi | taddhi tasmād viśeṣaṇāntaraṃ bhaved vastusthityā | lakṣaṇakāraiśca rūpāntaratvenopādānamarhati yasya viśeṣaṇasya bhāve 'pi yasyāparasyābhāvaḥ syāt | yataḥ sambhave vyabhicāre ca viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo na sambhava eva kevale | udāharaṇamāha- "tad yathā" ityādi | satyapi hi dharmisambandhe śrāvaṇatvādeḥ sapakṣe bhāvo nāsti | satyapi ca cākṣuṣatvādeḥ sapakṣe bhāve sādhyadharmiṇi śabde sambandho nāsti | tato 'nayoḥ sambhavavyabhicārayorbhāvād viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo lakṣaṇāntaratvena copādānam | ihāpyevaṃ bhaviṣyatīti ced āha- "na caitad" anantaroditamabādhāyā avinābhāve sati sambhavati | satyavinābhāve niyamenābādhāyāḥ sambhavāvdyabhicārābhāvāt kuto viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo kṣaṇāntaratvena copādānamarhati? iti na hetoḥ sādhyāvinābhāvino viruddhasya ca sādhyaviparyayāvinābhāvino viṣaye bādhā sambhavati | uktena prakāreṇa viparyaye samyaggheturevāviṣaye tu prayogāddhetvābhāsa ucyate | yata evam "iti" tasmānna tadabhāvo bādhāvirahaḥ pṛthagavinābhāvādanvayavyatirekātmano 'nayorhetuviruddhayorlakṣaṇāntaratvena vācyaḥ, vyabhicārābhāvena rūpāntaratvāyogāt | yataścāvinābhāve sati bādhā na sambhavati virodhāt, tasmāddhetoryathoktalakṣaṇasya prayoge sati gamyārthāyā api pratijñāyā doṣāṇāṃ pratyakṣaviruddhādīnāṃ sambhavo nāsti, hetulakṣaṇenaiva teṣāṃ nirastatvāt | tat kathaṃ bādhāviraho heto rūpāntaramucyate? | asambhavināṃ ca teṣāṃ upavarṇanaṃ niṣphalamityākūtam |
children.translated_text: ) is present, non-sublation is understood — why then should it not be an additional characteristic? To this he says: "That very" and so on. For that would be an additional qualification by the nature of reality. And it deserves to be taken up as an additional characteristic by those who formulate definitions — [only] a qualification in whose presence the absence of another [qualification] would [still be possible]. Since when [two things] are [always] co-present and [always] co-deviant, the relation of qualification and qualified is simply not possible.

body.translated_text: Even if, due to the impossibility of co-existence of sublation and invariable concomitance, when invariable concomitance (

body.text: kevalāyāḥ prayoge 'sti sambhava iti cet, āha- "nāpi" ityādi | hetuprayoge hyasati kevalā pratijñaiva na prayujyate, hetuviṣayatvena tadabhyupagamāt | tataśca śāstrakārairna pratijñādoṣāḥ pratyakṣaviruddhādayo vācyā iti | diṅnāgapādaistu sādhyāsādhyaviparyayeṇa (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 213.

children.text: ) vipratipattidarśanādaprayogārhasyāpi pakṣasya lakṣaṇavidhāne nyāyaprāptamevāpakṣatva na ni(tvaṃ ni)rākṛtapadena pramāṇaviruddhasyākhyānam, na tvatiprasaktaṃ pakṣalakṣaṇam vyavacchinnam, sandigdhasyaiva sādhyatvāt, pramāṇabādhite sādhakapramāṇāvṛtteiriti |
children.translated_text: ) — through the display of conflicting views by reversing what is to be proved and what is not to be proved, when defining the characteristics of a thesis that is not even worthy of employment — the disqualification from being a thesis that is established by reasoning alone [is noted], and the mention of what is contradicted by a <s>pramāṇa</s> by the word 'excluded' [in the definition] does not excessively restrict the definition of the thesis, since only what is doubtful is what is to be proved, and because when [something is] sublated by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, no establishing <s>pramāṇa</s> operates.

body.translated_text: If [one says:] there is possibility [of additional characterization] in the employment of the bare [proposition] — he says: "Nor" and so on. For in the absence of the employment of a reason, the bare proposition alone is not employed [as an independent proof], since that [proposition] is acknowledged as being the domain of the reason. And therefore, the authors of treatises need not state defects of the proposition such as being contradicted by perception and the like. But by <s>Dignāga</s>, (

body.text: tadevamabādhitaviṣayatvaṃ nirākṛtya rūpāntaraṃ nirākurvannāha- "etena" avinābhāve sati bādhāyā asambhavadarśanena "ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣāpi" viruddhāvyabhicāridoṣavipakṣeṇocyamānā "pratyuktā" pratyākhyātā |
body.translated_text: Having thus refuted having an uncontradicted domain, refuting another additional characteristic, he says: "By this" — by the demonstration that sublation is impossible when invariable concomitance obtains — "the intention regarding singular number" — stated with respect to the defect of the contradictory non-deviating [counter-reason] — "has been answered" — refuted.

body.text: paraḥ pṛcchati- "katham" iti kena prakāreṇa- yathā bādhāvinābhāvayoḥ sahānavasthānaṃ tathā pratihetvavinābhāvayorapi?, yenaikasaṃkhyāvivakṣā tadvadeva pratyākhyāyeta iti |
body.translated_text: The opponent asks: "How" — in what manner? — just as there is the impossibility of co-existence of sublation and invariable concomitance, so too of a counter-reason and invariable concomitance? — such that the intention regarding singular number would be refuted in just the same way.

body.text: siddhāntavādī sāmyaṃ darśayannāha- "eka" ityādi | eko hi heturlakṣaṇayuktaḥ | svasādhyāvyabhicārī kathaṃ bhavati? | yadi svasādhyabhāva eva bhavet, anyathā tallakṣaṇamavinābhāvo nāma hīyeta | yatraiva dharmiṇi sa tallakṣaṇa eko bhavati tatraiva dharmiṇi tasmādanyo 'pi pratiheturviruddhastena hetulakṣaṇayuktaḥ kathaṃ bhavati? | ekasya hetoryat sādhyaṃ tabdādhakasya tadviruddhasyāparasya dharmasya bhāva eva nābhāve bhāvādavinābhāvāditi bādhayā samānaṃ bādhāsambhavena samānaḥ pratiheturiti tannirāsenaiva nirasta iti |
body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis, showing the parity, says: "One" and so on. For one reason that possesses the [proper] characteristics — how does it become non-deviating from what it is to prove? Only if it exists precisely where what is to be proved exists; otherwise, its defining characteristic — namely invariable concomitance — would be lost. In whatever property-bearer it, possessing that characteristic, exists as one — in that very property-bearer, another [reason] too, a counter-reason that contradicts [it], possessing that reason-characteristic —

body.text: atraiva dūṣaṇāntaramabhidhātuṃ vikalpayannāha- "api ca" ityādi | "vastutaḥ" paramārthato yasya pratiheturna sambhavati kimasau samyagjñānasya viparyasya vopanyastasādhyaviparītajñānasya vā heturiṣṭo yato vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvaṃ tallakṣaṇamucyate, āhosvid yasya pratihetustatsādhyaviparītasādhako na pradarśitaḥ paramārthataḥ sannapīti | paro doṣamapaśyannāha- "kiñcātaḥ" ityādi | yadi nāma purvo vikalpa uttaro vā tataḥ ko doṣaḥ? iti |
body.translated_text: In order to state another refutation at this point, he hypothesizes and says: "Moreover" and so on. "In reality" — ultimately — for one in whom a counter-reason is impossible — is this accepted as a reason for correct knowledge, for error, or for knowledge contrary to what is to be proved? — such that having the intended singular number is stated as its defining characteristic. Or is it one whose counter-reason — establishing the opposite of what is to be proved — is not [possible]?

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- yadyasambhavan pratiheturyasya sa samyagjñānādiheturiṣyate, tadālakṣaṇametad vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvam | kasmāt? | aśakyo niścayo yasya vastuto 'sambhavatpratihetutvasya sa tathoktaḥ | paramatāpekṣayā caitaducyate | paro hi darśanādarśanābhyāmasatyapi pratibandhe 'vinābhāvamicchati | tatastasya pratihetorevaṃvidhasya sambhavo 'sti | sa cānupalabhyamāno 'pi kadācit syāditi vastutastadabhāvo niścīyate | pratibandhanibandhanāvinābhāvavādināṃ tvasmākaṃ pratihetvasambhavaḥ suniścita eva | nahi tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇe pratibandhe pramāṇataḥ siddhe tannimittāvinābhāvitayā ekena hetunā svasādhye sādhite punastatraiva dharmiṇi tallakṣaṇasya tadviruddhārthasādhakasya pratihetoḥ sambhavaḥ śaṅkayate, bhāvānāṃ viruddhasvabhāvadvayāyogād, viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedalakṣaṇatvāt | viruddhadharmasādhakasambhave ca tasyaiva svasādhyāvinābhāvinaḥ prathamasya tatra pramāṇato bhāvasiddhayayogāditi |
body.translated_text: The proponent of the thesis says: if one for whom a counter-reason is impossible is accepted as a reason for correct knowledge and the like — then this is not a [proper] defining characteristic — the intended singular number. Why? Because no ascertainment is possible of being without a counter-reason in reality. And this is stated with reference to the opponent's view. For the opponent accepts invariable concomitance through observation and non-observation alone, even in the absence of a necessary connection.

body.text: syānmatam- yadi nāma prastutaḥ pratihetvasambhavo 'smābhirniścetumaśakyastathāpyasambhavatpratihetutvaṃ vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvapratipāditaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ kasmānna bhavati? ityāha- "na hyaniścitātmanaḥ" ityādi | pratipādako yo dharmo hetostasyāniścitasvabhāvasya yasmāt tallakṣaṇatvaṃ pratipādakadharmatā na bhavati | yathā saṃdigdhasya pakṣadharmatvasyeti pūrvakasya sādhanam | nāpi sandhigdhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yasya sa heturbhavatīti na kaściddheturbhavediti hetvabhāvo vā ityasya samarthanam | tataśca "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare" ityatrāpi yojitamiti |
body.translated_text: One might think: even if the impossibility of a counter-reason under discussion cannot be ascertained by us, why should the defining characteristic of a reason, indicated by having the intended singular number — the impossibility of a counter-reason — not be [valid]? He says: "For of what has an unascertained nature" and so on. Since the defining characteristic — the status of being the defining property — of a property that indicates [the nature of] the reason, when the intrinsic nature [of that property] is unascertained,

body.text: syānmatam- yasya pratiyogī dṛśyate tasyaiva pratihetubhāvāt ahetutvaṃ bhavatu, yasya tu pratiyogī heturna dṛśyate sa vastuta evāsambhavatpratihetuḥ | na hi tatra vastutaḥ pratihetusambhavaḥ śaṅkayate, bādhakapratyayamantareṇa bādhāśaṅkāyā ayogāt | taduktam-
body.translated_text: One might think: let there be non-reason-hood only for one whose counter-positive [i.e., counter-reason] is observed; but for one whose counter-positive reason is not observed — that one is in reality without a possible counter-reason. For no suspicion of the possibility of a counter-reason arises there in reality, since without a sublating cognition, the suspicion of sublation is inappropriate. As stated:

body.text: "bādhājñāne tvanutpanne nāśaṅkā niṣpramāṇikā" iti |
body.translated_text: "When the cognition of sublation has not arisen, a suspicion without a <s>pramāṇa</s> [has no basis]."

body.text: atra āha- "tulye lakṣaṇe hi" ityādi | śaṅkayamānapratihetunā tulyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ darśanādarśanamātranimittāvinābhāvarūpaṃ yasya tasmin dṛṣṭaḥ pratiyoginaḥ pratihetorbbādhakasya sambhavaḥ sa yeṣāmapi tattulyalakṣaṇānāṃ pratiyogī na dṛśyate teṣvapi śaṅkāṃ pratihetusambhavaviṣayāmutpādayati | kiṃ kāraṇam? | adṛṣṭapratiyogino dṛṣṭapratiyogino viśeṣābhāvāt | nahi tasyetareṇa kaścidviśeṣo 'sti, yatastatsambhavo na śaṅkayeta | pruṣaśaktivaikalyādinā tu tadadarśanaṃ sambhāvyeteti kimucyate ‘nāśaṅkā niḥpra(ṣpra)māṇikā'; iti | atha viśeṣaḥ pratibandhalakṣaṇo 'vinābhāvaniścāyako dṛṣṭapratihetoradṛṣṭapratiyogina iṣyate yataḥ pratiyogisambhavāśaṅkāstamupaiti | tadā sati vā viśeṣe sa viśeṣo hetorlakṣaṇam | kiṃ kāraṇam? | yatastato viśeṣāddheturekāntena niścayena nirastapratipakṣastathāvidhe dharmiṇi pratihetvasambhavāt svasādhyaṃ niścāyayatīti | yastathāvidho na bhavati tadviśeṣavirahāt dṛṣṭapratihetuḥ so 'tallakṣaṇo na hetuḥ syāt | tathā ca yadi nāmāhetau pratiheturdṛṣṭo, hetoḥ kimāyātam, yena tannivṛttaye tatraikasaṃkhyāvivakṣā kriyate, yathoktāvinābhāvavacanenaiva tannivṛtterityāha- "tathā ca hetau" tadviśeṣayogini "pratihetvasambhave" sati "vyarthā" niṣprayojanā "ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣeti" | yathoktaviśeṣāṅgīkarane tallakṣaṇasya pratihetorasambhavāt kasyaikasaṃkhyāvivakṣayā vyavacchedaḥ kriyate? yato 'sya sārthakatvaṃ syāditi |
body.translated_text: Here he says: "For when the defining characteristic is the same" and so on. When the defining characteristic — in the form of invariable concomitance grounded merely in observation and non-observation — is the same as [that of one] with a suspected counter-reason, and for that [reason-type] the possibility of the counter-positive — the counter-reason, the sublator — has been observed, then for those too — those of the same defining characteristic — whose counter-positive is not observed, it [the observation of a counter-reason in the similar case] raises the suspicion regarding the possibility of a counter-reason. What is the basis?

body.text: viruddhāvyabhicāriṇaśca hetvābhāsasya vyavacchedārthamekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā hetulakṣaṇe kriyate | vastuto 'sambhavatpratihetutvasiddhaye ca pratibandhalakṣaṇe viśeṣe hetāviṣyamāṇe viruddhāvyabhicāryapi hetvābhāso na bhavati | tato vyavacchedyābhāvāt kimekasaṃkhyāvivakṣayā? iti darśayannāha- "ataḥ" pratibandhalakṣaṇaviśeṣopagamāt "viruddhāvyabhicāriṇo hetvābhāsasya yallakṣaṇaṃ taddhīyeta" na sambhavet | kiṃ punastadviruddhāvyabhicāriṇo lakṣaṇam? ityāha- "svalakṣaṇa" ityādi | hetoryadātmīyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tadyuktayorhetvorekatra (

children.translated_text: <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> 216.

children.text: ) dharmiṇi virodhena parasparaviruddhasādhyasādhakatvenopanipāte sati viruddhāvyabhicārīti viruddhāvyabhicāriṇo lakṣaṇam | na ca tat pratibandhāṅgīkaraṇe sati sambhavati | nahi tādātmyatadutpattibhyāṃ svasādhyapratībandhavatyekatra hetau kvaciddharmiṇi saṃbhavati dvitīyastallakṣastatraiva hetuḥ sambhavet, bhāvānāṃ viruddhasvabhāvadvayāsambhavāt, viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedalakṣaṇatvāt | tadavyabhicāriṇo hetordvitīyasya tatra kutaḥ sambhavāvakāśa iti |
children.translated_text: ) — when there is co-occurrence in a property-bearer through the capacity to prove mutually contradictory things to be proved — this is the definition of the contradictory non-deviating [pseudo-reason]. And that is not possible when a necessary connection is acknowledged. For in a single reason that has a necessary connection with what is to be proved through identity or origination from it, it is not possible that a second reason with that characteristic [of being a counter-reason] exists in that very [property-bearer] —

body.translated_text: And the intention regarding singular number is made in the definition of the reason for the purpose of excluding the pseudo-reason [called] the contradictory non-deviating. But when a special feature characterized as a necessary connection is accepted in the reason — and [thereby] the impossibility of a counter-reason in reality is established — the contradictory non-deviating too does not qualify as a pseudo-reason. Therefore, since what is to be excluded does not exist, what is the use of the intention regarding singular number? Showing this, he says: "Therefore" — the counter-reason —

body.text: nanu yadi tathavidhāviśeṣasambhave sati viruddhāvyabhicārilakṣaṇaṃ hīyate, ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā vā vyarthā, tathāpi naiva hetvabhāvaparasaṅgaḥ, tat kimuktaṃ hetvabhāvo vetyata āha- "na ca" naiva "tasya" viśeṣasya pratibandhalakṣaṇasya, yato vastuto 'sambhavatpratihetutvaṃ niścīyate | "svarūpaṃ" tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇaṃ nirddiśyate bhavadbhiḥ yathāsmābhirnirdiṣṭaṃ yadrūpaṃ "pratītya" pratipadya pratiyoginaḥ ambhavāsambhavāvutpaśyāmaḥ | yatra sa viśeṣo nāsti tatra pratiyoginaḥ sambhavaḥ kalpita āgamāśraye 'numāne | yatra tvasti sa viśeṣo vastubalapravṛtte 'numāne tatra pratiyogino 'sambhava iti | yata evaṃ tasmānnāstyeva bhavatāṃ sa viśeṣaḥ- bhavadbhirna jñāyata eva sa viśeṣa iti | tasmāt sarvatra yatrāpi pratiyogī na dṛśyate tatrāpi śaṅkayā pratiyogiviṣayayā bhavitavyam | tāmeva śaṅkāṃ draḍhayannāha- "dṛṣṭapratihetorapi" ityādi | yasyāpi hi pratiheturdṛṣṭasyāpi prāk praityogidarśanāditareṇa sarvakālamadṛṣṭapratiyoginā na kaścid viśeṣo lakṣyate yaddarśanājjñāyeta ‘atra pratiyogī sambhavati nyānyatra'; iti darśanādarśanamātranibandhanayoranvayavyatirekayoḥ sarvatra samānatvāt | tathāpi paścāttatra pratiyogī dṛṣṭa iti sarvatra tattulyalakṣaṇe pratiyogisadbhāvaśaṅkā na nivartata iti |
body.translated_text: Now, if, given the possibility of such a non-differentiator (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), the definition of <s>viruddha-avyabhicārin</s> (contradictory yet non-deviating) is undermined, or the specification of a single number (<s>ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā</s>) is rendered pointless, even so there is no unwanted consequence of the absence of a <s>hetu</s> (logical reason). To the question 'what then was meant by saying there would be an absence of a <s>hetu</s>?', he says: "<s>na ca</s>" — indeed "its" — that is, of the distinguishing feature (<s>viśeṣa</s>) characterized by <s>pratibandha</s> (necessary connection) — "the essential nature" (<s>svarūpa</s>), characterized by <s>tādātmya</s> (essential identity) and <s>tadutpatti</s> (origination from that), is indicated by you just as the form indicated by us; "having understood" (<s>pratītya</s>) that form, we ascertain the possibility or impossibility of a <s>pratiyogin</s> (counter-entity). Where that distinguishing feature does not exist, the possibility of a <s>pratiyogin</s> is merely imagined, as in inference based on <s>āgama</s> (scripture). But where that distinguishing feature does exist, in inference proceeding from the force of reality (<s>vastubalapravṛtta</s>), there the <s>pratiyogin</s> is impossible. Since this is so, therefore that distinguishing feature simply does not exist for you — you simply do not know that distinguishing feature. Therefore, everywhere, even where a <s>pratiyogin</s> is not observed, there must be a doubt regarding the <s>pratiyogin</s>. Reinforcing that very doubt, he says: "<s>dṛṣṭapratihetoḥ api</s>" and so forth. For even in the case of one whose <s>pratihetu</s> (counter-reason) has been observed, no distinguishing feature is discerned — prior to the observation of the <s>pratiyogin</s> — from one whose <s>pratiyogin</s> has never been observed at any time, by which one could know 'here a <s>pratiyogin</s> is possible but not elsewhere'; because the <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), which depend merely on observation and non-observation, are the same everywhere. Even so, since a <s>pratiyogin</s> was later observed there, the doubt about the existence of a <s>pratiyogin</s> does not cease anywhere that has similar characteristics.

body.text: syānmatam- yeṣu pratiyogī sambhavati teṣvaśyameva kadācidasāvupalabhyate | yeṣu tu puruṣāyuṣeṇāpi nopalabhyate teṣvasau nāstyeva | (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 217

children.text: ) tataḥ sa tathāvidho heturbhaviṣyati, tat kathaṃ hetvabhāvo 'smākam? ityata āha- "na ca" ityādi | yeṣāmapi hi pratihetuḥ sambhavati teṣāmapi naiva sarvadā tasya pratihetorūpalabdhiḥ pratipattṝṇām | na hyasarvadarśināmupalabdhiḥ sarvabhāvasattāṃ vyāpnoti, pratibandhavaikalyasadbhāvāt | nanu ca yatra sarvadaiva pratipatra(ttrā) pratiyogī na dṛśyate tatra tadāśaṅkākathaṃ kriyate? | tathā cāha-
children.translated_text: Therefore, such a <s>hetu</s> (logical reason) will remain valid — so how could there be an absence of a <s>hetu</s> for us? To this he says: "<s>na ca</s>" and so forth. For even in those cases where a <s>pratihetu</s> (counter-reason) is possible, the apprehension of that <s>pratihetu</s> does not always occur for all cognizers. For the apprehension by those who do not perceive everything does not encompass the existence of all entities, due to the presence of deficiency in the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>). But then, in cases where a <s>pratiyogin</s> (counter-entity) is never observed by any cognizer, how can doubt about it be entertained? And so he says:

body.translated_text: One might think: in those cases where a <s>pratiyogin</s> is possible, it is necessarily apprehended at some point. But in those cases where it is not apprehended even within a person's lifetime, it simply does not exist there.

body.text: "bādha(dhā)jñāne tvanutpanne nāśaṅkā niṣpramāṇikā" iti |
body.translated_text: "But when the cognition of refutation (<s>bādha</s>) has not arisen, the doubt is not without valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>)."

body.text: tathāparam-
body.translated_text: And further:

body.text: "utprekṣeta hi yo mohādajātamapi bādhakam |
body.translated_text: "For one who, out of delusion, would imagine a refuting factor that has not even arisen,

body.text: sa sarvavyavahāreṣu saṃśayātmā kṣayaṃ vrajet ||" iti |
body.translated_text: that person, being of a doubting nature in all practical affairs, would come to ruin."

body.text: ata āha- "atiśayavatī tu" ityādi | tathā hi kasyacideva pramātuḥ kuśāgrīyamateratiśayavatī prajñā pratihetūtprekṣiṇī dṛṣṭāsmābhiḥ yathā vedaprāmāṇyanirākartṛṣu [hetuṣu] saugataiḥ śiṣyaparamparayā kumārilotpādātprāgadṛṣṭapratiyogiṣūpanyasteṣu, tenaiva prajñātiśayaśālinā pratihetava utprekṣitāḥ tatastaddarśanāt yāvajjīvaṃ adṛṣṭapratihetuṣvapi tadāśaṅkā na nivartate | tataḥ kathamāśaṅkā niṣpramāṇikocyate? | "tulyalakṣaṇe hi" ityādikamapi pratiyogisambhavāśaṅkākāraṇamuktameva | na ca pratiyogisambhavamāśaṅkamānastannimittasaṃbhavāt ‘utprekṣeta hi'; ityādyākrośamātreṇa nivartayituṃ śakyate | tenāsya pratiyogyāśaṅkāpanodakṣamaṃ kiñcit kāraṇamabhidhānīyam yathāsmābhirabhihitaṃ ‘svabhāvahetorviparyeye bādhakapramāṇavaśāttādātmyaniścaye satyanvayavyatirekayostatra nirṇayaḥ; kāryahetau ca yathoktapratyakṣānupalambhataḥ kāryakāraṇasiddhestaniścaya'; iti | yata evaṃ sarvatra pratiyogyāśaṅkā na nivartate bhavaddarśane tena kāraṇenāniścayaḥ pratiyoginaḥ sambhavāsambhavayoḥ ‘iha pratiyogī sambhavati iha tu na sambhavati'; ityevaṃrūpa iti | tasmādvastuto 'sambhavatpratihetutvaṃ yallakṣaṇaṃ (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 218

children.text: ) hetoḥ tasyāniścitatvādekasaṃkhyāvivakṣāvādināṃ na kaściddhetuḥ syāt | na hyaniścitalakṣaṇo heturbhavatītyupasaṃhāra iti |
children.translated_text: since that is unascertained, for those who maintain the view of specifying a single number (<s>ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā</s>), no <s>hetu</s> whatsoever would exist. For a <s>hetu</s> whose defining characteristic is unascertained cannot be a valid <s>hetu</s> — this is the conclusion.

body.translated_text: Therefore he says: "<s>atiśayavatī tu</s>" and so forth. For indeed, we have observed the extraordinary intellect (<s>prajñā</s>) of a certain cognizer of sharp mind, capable of conceiving counter-reasons — as when the <s>Saugatas</s> (Buddhists) presented arguments against the authoritativeness of the <s>Vedas</s>, arguments whose <s>pratiyogin</s> had not been observed through the succession of disciples prior to the arising of <s>Kumārila</s>, and that very person, endowed with extraordinary intellect, conceived the counter-reasons. Therefore, from observing that, even in cases where a <s>pratihetu</s> has never been observed throughout one's life, the doubt about it does not cease. So how can the doubt be called 'without valid means of knowledge'? The passage "<s>tulyalakṣaṇe hi</s>" and so forth has also been stated as a reason for doubting the possibility of a <s>pratiyogin</s>. And one who entertains doubt about the possibility of a <s>pratiyogin</s> cannot be turned away merely by the reproach 'one who would imagine' and so forth, since the basis for such imagination exists. Therefore, some reason capable of removing the doubt about a <s>pratiyogin</s> must be stated, as we have stated: 'In the case of a <s>svabhāvahetu</s> (nature-based reason), the determination of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) and <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance) is made regarding the opposite through the force of a <s>bādhaka-pramāṇa</s> (invalidating means of knowledge), once <s>tādātmya</s> (essential identity) is ascertained; and in the case of a <s>kāryahetu</s> (effect-based reason), the ascertainment of that is through the establishment of the cause-effect relation by the stated direct perception and non-apprehension.' Since in this way, according to your view, the doubt about a <s>pratiyogin</s> does not cease anywhere, for that reason there is uncertainty regarding the possibility and impossibility of a <s>pratiyogin</s> — of the form 'here a <s>pratiyogin</s> is possible, but here it is not possible.' Therefore, the definition of a <s>hetu</s> as that whose counter-reason is in reality impossible —

body.text: tadevaṃ ‘kiṃ yo vastuto 'sambhavatpratihetuḥ sa samyagjñānaviparyayaheturiṣṭaḥ'; iti amuṃ vikalpaṃ nirākṛtya dvitīyaṃ vikalpaṃ nirācikīrṣurāha- "athāpradarśitapratihetuḥ" samyagjñānaviparyaheturiṣṭa iti sambandhaḥ | ayaṃ ca pakṣaḥ kila diṅnāgācāryasyāpyabhimata iti para upadarśayannāha- "yathāha diṅnāgācāryaḥ" | kimāha?"yadā tarhi" ityādi | "śrāvaṇatvasya hi na kathañcivdyavacchedahetutvam" iti diṅnāgācāryeṇokte pareṇābhihitam- "yadā tarhi vaiyākaraṇaḥ śabdatvaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣaṃ nityamabhyupagacchati tadāyaṃ śrāvaṇatvalakṣaṇaḥ pakṣadharmaḥ hetureva syāt | nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāt śabdatvavat" ityevaṃ pareṇokte satyācāryeṇoktam- "yadyatra śabdākhye dharmiṇyanityatvahetuṃ kṛtakatvaprayatnānatarīyakatvādilakṣaṇaṃ kaścid vaiśeṣikādirna darśayet tadāyamapradarśitapratiheturhetureva bhavet" iti | tadevāmācāryapādaiḥ sākṣitve datte bhujamutkṣipya śāstrakāraḥ pūtkurvannāha- "idamidānīm" ityādi | yadā hyācāryasyāpyetadabhimatamiti kaiścivdyākhyāyate tadidaṃ sumahavdyasanamāyātam- gurubhirabhihitatvādaprakāśyam, nahi gurūṇāṃ doṣaḥ prakāśayituṃ yuktaḥ, "nyāyamanupālayadbhiḥ asaṃvaraṇīyam" apracchādanīyam | tat kiṃ gurūn dūṣayāma uta nyāyamapyupekṣāmahe ityubhayamapyaśakyamiti "kaṣṭataraṃ vyasanaṃ kathaṃ nirvoḍhuṃ śakyeta?" | na kathaṃciditi | kaḥ punaratra doṣo yenedaṃ kaṣṭataramityāha- "sa tāvadayaṃ" śrāvaṇatvalakṣaṇo "heturvastūni" śabdādīni svasādhyaṃ tattvaṃ nityatvaṃ "tatprakṛtīni" tadātmakāni "kṛtvā" tacchrāvaṇatvaṃ pramāṇaṃ yeṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ mīmāṃsakavaiyākaraṇādīnāṃ tān "abhyudayena" (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 219

children.text: ) svargeṇa "niḥśreyasena" cāpavargeṇa "yojayitvā" | tathā hi- vastutattvaṃ bhāvayan yāvat kleśānn prajahāti tāvat svargamāsādayati, kleśāṃstu prajahannirvāṇaparāyaṇo bhavati | athāvā śabdanityatvapratītau vedaprāmāṇyāt tadvihitāgnihotrānuṣṭhānāt svargo vedāntaniṣevaṇādaparvaggaḥ | punaruttarakālaṃ "pratibhāvatā" prajñājātīyena vaiśeṣikādinā puruṣeṇa "hetvantarasya" pratihetoḥ "nidarśanena" yadasya "nityatvasādhanasāmarthyaṃ" pratihetvanupadarśane satyāsīt ttatadupadarśanena "utkīlitam" apanītamiti | tāni vastūni nityatvasampadaḥ pracyāvya, tāṃśca tatpramāṇakān puruṣān svargāpavargasampadaḥ pracyāvya śrāvaṇatvalakṣaṇo hetuḥ śaktivaikalyāt paritrātumaśakto bhraṣṭarājya ieva rājā tapovanaṃ gacchati svaireva duścaritairiti kimatra vayaṃ brūmaḥ? |
children.translated_text: that is, heaven (<s>svarga</s>), and with "final liberation" (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), that is, <s>apavarga</s> (release). For indeed, one who contemplates the true nature of reality, as long as he does not abandon the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), attains heaven; but one who abandons the afflictions becomes devoted to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Alternatively, upon the cognition of the eternality of sound, through the authoritativeness of the <s>Vedas</s>, from the performance of <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-ritual) prescribed therein comes heaven, and from devotion to <s>Vedānta</s> comes liberation. Then, at a later time, "by a brilliant person" (<s>pratibhāvatā</s>), a <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> or the like, possessing the quality of extraordinary intellect, "by the demonstration of another reason" — a counter-reason — "the capacity to establish eternality" which existed when no counter-reason had been demonstrated, "is uprooted" (<s>utkīlita</s>), that is, removed. Having dislodged those real entities from the attainment of eternality, and having dislodged those persons who relied on that as their means of knowledge from the attainment of heaven and liberation, the <s>hetu</s> characterized by <s>śrāvaṇatva</s>, unable to protect them due to the deficiency of its power, goes to the forest of austerities like a king who has lost his kingdom through his own misdeeds — so what can we say here?

body.translated_text: Thus, having refuted this alternative — 'Is that which has a counter-reason impossible in reality the one intended as the cause of correct cognition and its opposite?' — wishing to refute the second alternative, he says: "<s>athāpradarśitapratihetuḥ</s>" — that which has an undemonstrated counter-reason is intended as the cause of correct cognition and its opposite — this is the syntactic connection. And this position is reportedly also accepted by master <s>Dignāga</s>, and the opponent shows this by saying: "as master <s>Dignāga</s> has said." What did he say? "<s>yadā tarhi</s>" and so forth. When master <s>Dignāga</s> stated "for <s>śrāvaṇatva</s> (audibility) is in no way a reason for exclusion," the opponent replied: "When then the grammarian (<s>vaiyākaraṇa</s>) accepts <s>śabdatva</s> (sound-nature), both general and specific, as eternal, then this inferential mark (<s>pakṣadharma</s>) characterized by <s>śrāvaṇatva</s> (audibility) would indeed be a valid reason: 'Sound is eternal, because of audibility, like sound-nature.'" When the opponent thus spoke, the master said: "If, regarding this property-possessor (<s>dharmin</s>) called sound, no one — <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> or otherwise — were to show a reason for impermanence such as being produced, being dependent on effort, and so forth, then this, having an undemonstrated counter-reason, would indeed be a valid reason." And when the master's own testimony is thus given, the author of the treatise, raising his arm and exclaiming in dismay, says: "<s>idamidānīm</s>" and so forth. For when it is explained by some that this is also accepted by the master, this has become a very great calamity — since it was stated by the teachers, it should not be exposed, for it is not proper to expose the faults of teachers; yet "for those who uphold the correct method (<s>nyāya</s>), it cannot be concealed." So should we fault the teachers, or should we also disregard the correct method? Both are impossible — "How can this most grievous calamity be endured?" It cannot, in any way. What then is the fault here, that makes this so grievous? He says: "<s>sa tāvadayam</s>" — this <s>hetu</s> characterized by <s>śrāvaṇatva</s> (audibility), "having made the real entities" such as sound "of that nature" — that is, having their essence as eternal —  for those persons — <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>, grammarians, and others — for whom that audibility is the means of knowledge, "connecting them" with "prosperity" (<s>abhyudaya</s>),

body.text: tadevamupahasyaitasmin pakṣe doṣamupadarśayannāha- "puruṣapratibhā" ityādi | yada hyapradarśitapratiheturheturheturiṣyate tadā puruṣapratibhākṛtaṃ sādhanatvamabhyupagataṃ bhavati | tataśca vastuto na kiñcit sādhanamasādhanaṃ vā prāptam | tathā hi- yadā pratiheturnopadarśyate tadā sādhanam, yadā tūpadarśyate tadā na sādhanamiti puruṣapratibhākṛtaṃ sādhanatvamāyātamiti |
body.translated_text: Thus, having ridiculed this, showing the fault in this position, he says: "<s>puruṣapratibhā</s>" and so forth. For when a <s>hetu</s> with an undemonstrated counter-reason is accepted as a valid reason, then the status of being a proof (<s>sādhana</s>) is acknowledged as being dependent on human ingenuity (<s>puruṣapratibhā</s>). Consequently, in reality, nothing would be established as either a proof or a non-proof. For thus: when a counter-reason is not demonstrated, it is a proof; but when one is demonstrated, it is not a proof — thus the status of being a proof comes to depend on human ingenuity.

body.text: api ca- apradarśitapratihetorhetorhetutve 'ṅgikriyamāṇe vikalpadvayam- kiṃ paramārthato hetustaddharmabhāvī, utātaddharmabhāvīti? | tatrādyaṃ vikalpamadhikṛtyāha- "sa ca" heturyo 'sau prathamaṃ upādīyate | sa "yadi svabhāvata" eva "tasmin" sādhyadharme "satyeva bhavati" ityevaṃśīlo 'smadupavarṇitapratibandhopagamāt yadīṣyate "tadā kathamanyathā kriyeta" hetvantareṇātaddharmabhāvī kathaṃ kriyeta? | na kathañcit | kiṃ kāraṇam? | vastūnāṃ hetulakṣaṇānāṃ yaḥsvabhāvaḥ- ‘satyameva sādhyadharme bhavanātmakaḥ'- "tadanyathābhāvasya" tadviparyayasya "abhāvād" ubhayośca svasādhyadharmāvinābhāvitve (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 220

children.text: ) svabhāvata eva dharmiṇyekatra tayorbhāve viruddhāvubhau svabhāvāvekasya syātām | na caikasya viruddhau svabhāvau sambhavataḥ, viruddhadharmādhyāsena tasyaikatvahāniprasaṅgāt | atha dvitīyo vikalpastadā "ataddharmabhāvī ca" asatyapi sādhyadharme bhavanaśīlaḥ pratibandhānabhyupagamāt "kathamanyadāpi" apradarśitapratihetvavasthāyāmapi "sādhanaṃ" kasyacit? | naiva tadāpi sādhanam, na kevalaṃ pradarśitapratihetvavasthāyāmiti |
children.translated_text: if both existed by nature in a single <s>dharmin</s> (property-possessor), both contradictory natures would belong to a single entity. But two contradictory natures cannot belong to a single entity, because the superimposition of contradictory properties would entail the loss of its unity. Now, if the second alternative is taken, then one that "does not possess the property to be proved" (<s>ataddharmabhāvin</s>) — one whose nature is to exist even when the <s>sādhyadharma</s> is absent, due to the non-acceptance of <s>pratibandha</s> — "how could it be a proof at any other time either" — even in the condition where no counter-reason has been demonstrated? It would not be a proof even then, not merely in the condition where a counter-reason has been demonstrated.

body.translated_text: Moreover, if the status of a <s>hetu</s> is accepted for one whose counter-reason has not been demonstrated, there is a two-fold alternative: is the <s>hetu</s> ultimately one that exists only when the property to be proved (<s>sādhyadharma</s>) is present, or one that exists even when it is absent? Regarding the first alternative, he says: "<s>sa ca</s>" — that <s>hetu</s> which is initially adopted — if it is "by its own nature" (<s>svabhāvataḥ</s>) such that it "exists only when that" <s>sādhyadharma</s> "truly exists" — that is, if this is its character, accepted through the acknowledgment of <s>pratibandha</s> (necessary connection) as we have described — "then how could it be made otherwise" — how could it be made into one that does not possess that property by another reason? It cannot, in any way. For what reason? Because there is "no existence of its being otherwise" (<s>tadanyathābhāvasya abhāvāt</s>), that is, the absence of the opposite of the essential nature of real things characterized as <s>hetus</s> — whose nature is 'existing only when the property to be proved truly exists' — since both [the <s>hetu</s> and its counter-reason] are inseparable from their respective properties to be proved,

body.text: upasaṃharannāha- "tasmāt svabhāvataḥ" ityādi | yata evaṃ bhāvānāṃ svabhāvo 'nyathā kartuṃ na śakyate, viruddhobhayasvabhāvaścaiko na sambhavati tasmāt paramārthataḥ svena svena sādhyenāvinābhāvinoryathoktalakṣaṇayoḥ kāryasvabhāvahetvoḥ tallakṣaṇasya kāryasvabhāvalakṣaṇasya pratihetorasambhavād "alakṣaṇamekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā" vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati | kiṃ kāraṇam? ityāha- "vyavacchedyābhāvāditi" | pratiheturhi vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvasya vyavacchedyo varṇyate | sa ca pratihetuḥ svalakṣaṇayuktayoḥ kāryasvabhāvayorna bhavatyeveti kathaṃ taddhetulakṣaṇaṃ syāditi | tadevamanayordvayo rūpayoryaḥ sambhavo yathoktāvinābhāvāsambhave satīti rūpāntaropagame 'pi hetvābhāsataiveti "hetvābhāsāstato 'pare iti" ityasyārtho vivṛta iti |
body.translated_text: Concluding, he says: "<s>tasmāt svabhāvataḥ</s>" and so forth. Since the essential nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of entities cannot be made otherwise, and since a single entity cannot have two contradictory natures, therefore, since the counter-reason bearing the characteristics of <s>kārya</s> (effect) and <s>svabhāva</s> (nature) — of these two, which are inseparable from their respective properties to be proved as described — is in reality impossible, "the specification of a single number is not the defining characteristic" (<s>alakṣaṇam ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā</s>) — the specified singularity does not constitute the definition. For what reason? He says: "because of the absence of what is to be excluded" (<s>vyavacchedyābhāvāt</s>). For the <s>pratihetu</s> (counter-reason) is described as that which is to be excluded by the specified singularity. And that <s>pratihetu</s> simply does not exist for <s>kārya</s> (effect) and <s>svabhāva</s> (nature) types that possess their proper defining characteristics — so how could it be the definition of a <s>hetu</s>? Thus, the possibility of these two forms, given the impossibility of the stated inseparability — even if an alternative form is adopted, it would still be a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) — this is the meaning of "<s>hetvābhāsāstato 'pare iti</s>" ('therefore the others are pseudo-reasons') that has been elucidated.

body.text: jñātatvanirākaraṇāyāha- "jñānaṃ punaḥ" ityādi | avādhitaviṣayatvaṃ vivakṣitaikasaṃkhyatvaṃ ca kārya- svabhāvahetvorevāvinābhāve sati bādhāpratihetvorasambhavāt vyavacchedyābhāvatvena satyapi liṅgadharmatve tallakṣaṇaṃ na bhavatītyuktam | jñānaṃ tu jñātatvam, tasyaiva bhāvapratyayenābhidhānāt | tathā hi- jñānaśabdapravṛttinimittaṃ jñātatvamucyate, tacca jñānameva, tadutpāde sati jñāta iti vyavahārāt | na ca tat liṅgasyātmarūpamiti kathaṃ liṅgalakṣaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati? | yadyapi vikalpapratibhāsī sāmānyākāro liṅgatayāvasthāpyate tathāpi na jñānasya liṅgadharmatā | na hyasau svatantra eva liṅgam | yadāha- "vikalpabhedāna svatantrāṇāmanvarthāśrayaṇāt (

children.translated_text: Hbṭ 221

children.text: ) tatkalpitaviṣayāda'rthapratipattāvanarthapratilambha eva syāt" iti | tasmād vāhyavastūpādānasyaivāsya liṅgatāvasthāpyate | sādhyasādhanasaṃkalpe vastudarśanahāneḥ svalakṣaṇasya kvacidananvayācca taddharmatāmeva tvanusmaranto vikalpā nānaikavyatirekān saṃdarśayanto vastuni paramparayā pratibandhādavisaṃvādakāḥ kāryādiliṅgavyapadeśanibandhanaṃ cetyuktaprāyam |
children.translated_text: from the object constructed by that [conceptual cognition], in the apprehension of the real object, there would be only the attainment of what is not the [real] object." Therefore, the status of being an inferential mark is established only for this [reason] insofar as it is based on external reality. Since in the construction of what is to be proved and the means of proof, the direct perception of the real thing is lost, and since the unique particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) does not have positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) with anything, the conceptual cognitions, while recollecting precisely its property-hood, displaying the manifold exclusions (<s>vyatirekas</s>) in relation to the real thing, are non-deceptive due to the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) through a chain of intermediaries — and this is the basis for the designation as inferential marks such as effect and so forth — this has been mostly stated already.

body.translated_text: To refute the [definition in terms of] being known (<s>jñātatva</s>), he says: "<s>jñānaṃ punaḥ</s>" and so forth. It has been stated that non-contradicted object-hood (<s>avādhitaviṣayatva</s>) and the specification of a single number (<s>ekasaṃkhyāvivakṣā</s>) do not constitute the definition — since, given the inseparability of the <s>kārya-svabhāva</s> type reasons alone, due to the impossibility of refutation and counter-reasons, and due to the absence of what is to be excluded, even though they possess the property of being an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), they do not bear that definition. But <s>jñāna</s> (cognition) means <s>jñātatva</s> (the state of being known), since it is denoted by the abstract nominal form. For thus: the cause of the application of the word <s>jñāna</s> is called <s>jñātatva</s>, and that is nothing other than cognition itself, since the conventional usage 'known' arises when cognition has occurred. And since that is not the essential nature of the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>), how could it be the definition of an inferential mark? Even though the general aspect (<s>sāmānyākāra</s>) appearing in conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is established as the inferential mark, still there is no property of being an inferential mark belonging to cognition. For that [general aspect] is not independently an inferential mark. As he says: "Since the divisions of conceptual cognition, being not independent, follow the meaning [of real objects],

body.text: na ca tasya kāryāderātmarūpaṃ jñānam | vikalpāvabhāsī ca sāmānyākāro naiva vikalpasyātmabhūtaḥ, tasya nīrūpasya vasturūpavirodhāt | tadrūpasya ca vikalpapratibimbacakrasya sāmānyātmatāvirahāt | yasmādabādhyasyāpi bāhyatayā vyavasitasyānanuyāyino 'pyanuyāyitayā sāmānyātmakatvaṃ tathātve cāsya vikalparūpatā kutaḥ? yadāha-
body.translated_text: And cognition is not the essential nature of that effect and so forth. The general aspect appearing in conceptual cognition (<s>vikalpa</s>) is not at all the essence of the <s>vikalpa</s> itself, because of the contradiction between the formless nature (<s>nīrūpa</s>) of that [<s>vikalpa</s>] and the form of a real thing. And the reflection-circle (<s>pratibimbacakra</s>) of <s>vikalpa</s>, which has that form, is devoid of the nature of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>). Since even what is non-contradicted, determined as external, and non-conforming yet [treated as] conforming, has the nature of a universal — and if it had such a nature, then whence would its character as a <s>vikalpa</s>-form arise? As he says:

body.text: "jñānādavyatiriktaṃ ca kathamarthāntaraṃ vrajet? ||
body.translated_text: "And how could what is not different from cognition become another object?

body.text: tasmānmithyāvabhāso 'yamartheṣvekātmatāgrahaḥ |" iti |
body.translated_text: Therefore, this false appearance is the apprehension of unity in [diverse] objects."

body.text: na jñānasya liṅgadharmatā | etadeva sādhayannāha- "kiṃrūpād" ityādi | kimātmakāt "hetoranumeyo 'rtho jñātavyaḥ iti cintāyāṃ" prakṛtāyāṃ "pratipattuḥ" puṃso yadavisaṃvādakaṃ liṅgaṃ tasya svarūpamabhidhīyate śāstrakāraiḥ yasya rūpasya darśanādayaṃ pratipattā ‘yatra tadrūpasambhavaḥ tat sādhanam tadrūpavikalamasādhanam'; iti pravibhāgena vyavasthāpya yattatra sādhanatvena vyavasthāpitaṃ tasyeṣṭārthasannidhānasampratyayāt pravṛttimavalambate | tathā, etasmiṃśca nyāye vyavasthite yadasya liṅgasyātmarūpaṃ tallakṣaṇaṃ bhavitumarhati pakṣadharmādivat na tu yat pararūpam |
body.translated_text: Knowledge does not have the property of being a logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>). Establishing this very point, he says 'of what nature' (<s>kiṃrūpāt</s>) and so forth. 'Of what nature'—i.e., from a reason (<s>hetu</s>) of what character—'the inferable object is to be known'—when this inquiry is undertaken, [the answer is:] the inherent nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) of that non-deceptive mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for the cognizer (<s>pratipattu</s>) is stated by the treatise-authors [as follows]: from seeing a particular form [in a mark], this cognizer [determines:] 'Where that form occurs, that is a proof (<s>sādhana</s>); what lacks that form is a non-proof'—having established [the mark] by this division, what is therein established as the proof, he depends upon for his activity because of the conviction of the proximity of the desired object. Thus, when this method is established, that which is the mark's own nature (<s>ātma-rūpa</s>)—that is fit to be its definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), like being a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa-dharma</s>) and so forth—but not what is of another's nature.

body.text: syādetat- jñātasya liṅgasya sādhakatvād yuktaiva sādhyasiddhyupayogino jñānasya liṅgalakṣaṇatetyata āha- "pratipattijanmani" ityādi | yadyanumeyapratītijanmanyupayujyate jñānamiti tanmātreṇa liṅgasya lakṣaṇamiṣyate tadātiprasaṅgaḥ prāpnoti | tamevāha- "evaṃ pratipattijanmanyupayogamātrālliṅgalakṣaṇatve prameyasya" arthasya "puruṣasya" pramātuḥ (

children.translated_text: [Hbṭ page 222]

children.text: ) "ādi" śabdāt saṃyogasamavāyādīnāmālokamanaskārādīnāṃ liṅgalakṣaṇatvaṃ bhavet | atra kāraṇamāha- "nahi teṣvapi" prameyādiṣu asatsu liṅgini jñānaṃ bhavatīti kṛtvā | atra paro 'niṣṭamāpādayannāha- "niścitagrahaṇaṃ tarhi" ityādi | yadi pararūpatvājjñānaṃ liṅgalakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati tadā ca yadetadācāryeṇa-
children.translated_text: )—from the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), contact (<s>saṃyoga</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and so forth, [as well as] light, mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), and the like would have the character of the definition of a mark. He states the reason for this: 'For not even in those'—because even when those [factors] such as the knowable and so forth are absent in the possessor of the mark, knowledge does not arise. Here the opponent raises an unwanted consequence and says: 'The inclusion of the word "ascertained" (<s>niścita</s>), then' and so forth. If, because it is of another's nature, knowledge is not the definition of the mark, then what was stated by the master—

body.translated_text: [Objection:] It might be [argued]: Since a known mark is the prover, it is quite appropriate that the knowledge which serves the establishment of what is to be proved should have the definition of a mark. To this he says 'in the arising of understanding' (<s>pratipatti-janmani</s>) and so forth. If—merely because knowledge is useful in the arising of the cognition of the inferable—[that] alone is accepted as the definition of the mark, then over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>) would follow. He states that very [over-extension]: 'Thus, if the definition of a mark [consists] merely in usefulness for the arising of understanding, then for the knowable object (<s>prameya</s>), [and] for the person (<s>puruṣa</s>), the knower (

body.text:
"anumeye 'tha tattulye sadbhāvo nāstitāsati |
niścite" ti-
body.translated_text: 'In the inferable, and in what is similar to it, existence; non-existence in what is absent—[when] ascertained (<s>niścita</s>)'—

body.text: niścitagrahaṇaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavataścābhimataṃ tanna kartavyayam | tathā hi- niścayo hi liṅgasya pararūpameva | sa cet tallakṣaṇam, jñānaṃ kimiti neṣyate yato niścayo vijñānameva tadviśeṣatvādasyeti |
body.translated_text: the inclusion of the word 'ascertained' was made, and is accepted by you—that should not be done. For indeed, ascertainment is itself of another's nature with respect to the mark. If that [ascertainment] is [included in] its definition, then why is knowledge not accepted [as such]?—since ascertainment is nothing but cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>), being a particular form of it.

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "na na kartavyaṃ" kintu kartavyameva tasya niścitagrahaṇasya liṅgarūpapratipādanyārthatvāt | tāmevānyārthatāṃ darśayannāha- "sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ" ityādi | pare hi sapakṣe darśanamātreṇāsapakṣe cādarśanamātrato gamakaṃ hetumicchanti | teṣāṃ naiva darśanamātreṇa sādhyasiddhau samartho heturbhavatīti jñāpanārthaṃ niścitagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam | yataḥ satorvidyamānayorapi darśanādarśanayoragamakatvaṃ hetordṛśyate ‘sa śyāmaḥ, tatputratvāt'; ityādau | yata evaṃ tena kāraṇena sapakṣe bhāvena vipakṣe sarvatrābhāvaviśiṣṭenāsapakṣe ca sarvatrābhāvena sapakṣe tādātmyatadutpattilakṣaṇabhāvaviśiṣṭena gamako heturityasyārthasya jñāpanārthaṃ lakṣaṇavākye niścitagrahaṇaṃ kṛtaṃ boddhavyam | etaduktaṃ bhavati- yāveva sapakṣavipakṣayoḥ bhāvābhāvau pratibandhasādhakapramāṇavṛttyā niścitau tābhyāmeva heturgamako bhavati, na tu yathākathañciddarśanamātreṇetyasyārthasya jñāpanāya niścitagrahaṇaṃ kṛtamiti |
body.translated_text: The proponent (<s>siddhānta-vādin</s>) says: 'It is not that it should not be done'—rather, it should indeed be done, that inclusion of 'ascertained' (<s>niścita</s>), because it serves a different purpose, namely the establishment of the nature of the mark. Showing that very different purpose, he says 'in the similar and dissimilar instances' (<s>sapakṣa-vipakṣa</s>) and so forth. For opponents hold that a reason is a prover merely from being observed in the similar instance and merely from non-observation in the dissimilar instance. To communicate that a reason is not capable of establishing what is to be proved merely from observation—for that purpose, the word 'ascertained' was included. Because even when observation and non-observation are [merely] present, the non-proving character of the reason is seen [in cases like] 'He is dark-complexioned, because he is his son' and the like. Because it is thus, for that reason, [what is needed is] existence in the similar instance with

body.text: prakṛtamupasaṃharannāha- "tena" ityādi | yena viśiṣṭayorbhāvābhāvayoreva khyāpanāya niścitagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam, na rūpāntarābhidhānāya, anātmarūpasya ca lakṣaṇatā na yujyate, tena pararūpaṃ liṅgasya lakṣaṇaṃ na bhavati | yataḥ tena jñānādinā pararūpeṇa liṅgasya na kaścid rūpaviśeṣo 'bhidhīyata iti |
body.translated_text: Concluding the topic under discussion, he says 'therefore' (<s>tena</s>) and so forth. Since the word 'ascertained' was included for the purpose of indicating distinguished existence and non-existence [only], and not for the purpose of designating another form—and since what is not of [the mark's] own nature is not appropriate as its definition—therefore another's nature is not the definition of the mark. Because no particular form of the mark is designated by that external nature such as knowledge and so forth.
