body.text: nanu ca pare 'pi sapakṣavipakṣayorbhāvābhāvābhyāṃ gamakaṃ hetumicchanti, darśanādarśane tu tayoreva sādhake, tat kimarthaṃ niścitagrahaṇam? iti, ata āha- "tau hi" ityādi | yadyapi pare bhāvābhāvābhyāmeva gamakaṃ hetumicchanti tathāpi sapakṣa eva bhāvo 'sapakṣe cābhāva eveti bhāvābhāvau darśanādarśanamātrato vyavasthāpayanti | na ca tatastau tathāvidhau sidhyataḥ, pratibandhavikalānāmapyarthānāṃ kvacid bhāvābhāvayoḥ kathañciddarśanādarśanasambhavāt | tasmād yau ‘hetoḥ sapakṣe eva bhāvo 'sapakṣe cābhāva eva'; ityevamātmakau bhāvābhāvau tau tadbhāvasya sādhakaṃ yat pramāṇaṃ tādātmyatadutpattisādhanaviṣayaṃ taddhṛttyā voddhavyau | kutaḥ? upāyāntarasyābhāvāt | tadanabhyupagame hi hetoḥ sapakṣa eva bhāvaḥ sarveṣāṃ hetumatāṃ bhāvānāṃ sādhyenānugamadarśane sati vipakṣe cābhāva eva sādhyavikalānāṃ sarvārthānāṃ hetuviviktānāṃ upalambhe sati syāt | na caitadasarvadarśinaḥ sambhavatīti | yata upāyāntaraṃ nāsti tena kāraṇena tayorviśiṣṭayorbhāvābhāvayoḥ pratipādanāya niścitaśabdaḥ prayukto lakṣaṇe lakṣaṇakāreṇeti |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But opponents too hold that a reason is a prover through existence and non-existence in the similar and dissimilar instances; and observation and non-observation are indeed the provers of those [existence and non-existence]. So for what purpose [is the word] 'ascertained' [included]? To this he says 'those two indeed' (<s>tau hi</s>) and so forth. Although opponents hold that a reason is a prover through existence and non-existence alone, nevertheless they establish existence and non-existence merely from observation and non-observation in the similar instance alone and the dissimilar instance alone [respectively]. But those two [existence and non-existence] of such a kind are not established merely from that [observation/non-observation], because even for things lacking a necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), existence and non-existence may somehow be observed and not-observed somewhere. Therefore, those 'existence in the similar instance alone and non-existence in the dissimilar instance alone' of the reason—the positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) [constituted by them]—

body.text: nanu ca bhāvābhāvavacanamātrādeva pramāṇato niścayo labhyate anyathā tayoreva sattā na prasidhyediti, ata āha- "yadyapi" ityādi |
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But merely from the statement of existence and non-existence, ascertainment is obtained through a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>); otherwise, the very existence of those two would not be established. To this he says 'even if' (<s>yadyapi</s>) and so forth.

body.text: "anumeye 'tha tattulye sadbhāvo nāstitāsati |"
body.translated_text: 'In the inferable and in what is similar to it, existence; non-existence in what is absent'—

body.text: ityanenaiva sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ bhāvābhāvavacanamātreṇā niścitagrahaṇanirapekṣeṇa tayorbhāvābhāvayoryat sādhanaṃ pramāṇaṃ tasya vṛttiryadyapyākṣipyate | kathaṃ punarniścitagrahaṇamantareṇa bhāvābhāvavacanamātratastaddhṛtteḥ ākṣepaḥ? ityāha- "anyathā" yadi tatsādhanapramāṇavṛttirnākṣipyeta, tadā "tayoreva" sapakṣavipakṣayoreva bhāvābhāvayoryā sattā svarūpavyavasthā tasyā "aprasiddheḥ" | kasmādaprasiddhiḥ? ityāha- "jñānasya" upalabdheryā sattā utpattiḥ tannibandhanatvājjñeyasya bhāvābhāvalakṣaṇasya sattāvyavasthāyāḥ svarūpavyavasthiteḥ | na hyupalambhamantareṇa svata evārthāḥ (

children.translated_text: [Hbṭ page 224]

children.text: ) sidhyanti, sarvasya sarvasiddhiprasaṅgāt | tasmādidamevaṃrūpaṃ naivaṃrūpamiti tadākārajñānodayādeva vyavasthāpyate | yata evaṃ tasmāt sarvatra śāstre loke vā jñeyasattāvyavasthaiva niścitagrahaṇaṃ vināpi "tatsādhanaṃ" tatsattāsādhanaṃ pramāṇam "ākarṣati" ākṣipatīti | kiñca, parārthatvācca śāstrapraṇayanasya tatsādhanapramāṇavṛttirākṣipyate iti sambandhaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ punastacchāstrapraṇayanaṃ yat parārtharūpatayā svavyavasthāpitajñeyasattāsādhanaṃ pramāṇamākṣipati? ityāha- " trirūpaṃ liṅgaṃ vaḥ saṃvādakaṃ prāpakaṃ" vāñchitasyārthasyeti | yadi nāmaivaṃrūpaṃ parārthaṃ śāstrapraṇayanaṃ tathāpi kathaṃ tat sādhanapramāṇavṛttimākṣipatītyāha- "tadrūpaṃ" tasya liṅgasya trirūpasya rūpaṃ svabhāvaṃ śāstroktaṃ ye pratipattāro na vidanti, na teṣāṃ tatastrirūpālliṅgācchāstroktād vāñchite 'rthe pravṛttirbhavati, ajñātasyārthasya jñāpakasya svasattāmātreṇa pravartakatvābhāvāt | yata evam "iti" tasmāt paropalakṣaṇatvādeva pareṣāṃ jñāpakatvādeva pravartake trirūpaliṅge jñānaṃ siddhamiti yadyapi niścitagrahaṇamatiricyate tathāpi tāveva liṅgasya sapakṣāsapakṣayorbhāvābhāvau viśiṣṭau śāstroktau ‘sapakṣa eva bhāvo 'sapakṣe cābhāva eva'; ityevaṃrūpau kecinnaiyāyikaprabhṛtayaḥ, pare darśanādarśanamātreṇa- ye darśanādarśane pratibandhasādhake na bhavataḥ- tanmātreṇa vyavasthāpayanti "yata eva iti" tasmātteṣāṃ vādināṃ niṣedhārtho 'yaṃ lakṣaṇe niścitaśabdaḥ prayukta ācāryeṇāsmābhiścābhyupagata iti | yadi tu paravipratipattiḥ na syāt tadā naivāsau prayujyeteti |
children.translated_text: )—[if that were not the case, everything] would be established [in relation to everything], due to the unwanted consequence that everything would be established of everything. Therefore, 'this is of such a form, and not of such a form'—this is determined only from the arising of knowledge having that form. Since it is thus, therefore everywhere—in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) or in the world—the very determination of the existence of the knowable, even without the word 'ascertained,' 'draws in' (implies) 'the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that establishes that [existence].' Furthermore, because the composition of the treatise is for the sake of others (<s>parārthatva</s>), the operation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing that is implied—this is the connection. What kind of treatise-composition is it that, through its being for the sake of others, implies the <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing the existence of the knowable that it has itself determined? He says: 'The triple-formed mark (<s>trirūpa liṅga</s>) [is stated] for you—'

body.translated_text: merely by this statement of existence and non-existence in the similar and dissimilar instances, without depending on the word 'ascertained'—although the operation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that establishes those [two, i.e.,] their existence and non-existence, is indeed implied. But how is there implication of the operation [of a <s>pramāṇa</s>] from the mere statement of existence and non-existence without the word 'ascertained'? To this he says: 'otherwise' (<s>anyathā</s>)—if the operation of the <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing that were not implied, then [there would be] 'non-establishment' of the reality (<s>sattā</s>), i.e., the proper determination of the actual nature, of those very existence and non-existence in the similar and dissimilar instances. Why would there be non-establishment? He says: because the reality, i.e., the arising, of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), i.e., apprehension (<s>upalabdhi</s>)—since the knowable's character of existence and non-existence depends upon that [knowledge]—

body.text: kimiti punarddarśanādarśanābhyāṃ bhāvābhāvaviṣayābhyāṃ sapakṣā [sa]pakṣayoḥ viśiṣṭau bhāvābhāvāvanvayavyatirekātmakau neṣyete ityāha- "satorapi" ityādi | satyapi kvacit sapakṣe bhāvadarśane hetoḥ kvaciccāsapakṣe 'bhāvadarśane ‘sa śyāmaḥ, tatputratvāt'; ityādāvanvayavyatirekayoḥ saṃśayāt | tathā hi- anvayo nāma sarvatra satyeva sādhye hetorbhāvo (

children.translated_text: [Hbṭ page 225]

children.text: ) vyāptyā cāsati sādhye hetorabhāvo vyatirekaḥ | na ca kvacit sati sādhye hetorbhāvadarśane 'pi tanmātreṇa tathābhāvaḥ sarvatra bhavati, apratibaddhasvabhāvānāṃ sahabhāvaniyamābhāvāt | tathā kvacit sādhyābhimatasyābhāve satyabhāvadarśane 'pi hetoḥ sarvatra tadabhāve 'vaśyamabhāvaḥ, tadanāyattasya tannivṛttau niyamena nivṛttyabhāvāt | tasmāt pratibandhaprasādhakapramāṇavṛttyaiva yathoktau sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ bhāvābhāvau sidhyataḥ nānyatheti vipratipattinirāsārthameva niścitagrahaṇaṃ kṛtamityupadarśayannāha- "tasmāt" ityādi | "asmābhiḥ" ityācāryakṛte niścitagrahaṇe 'nyatrāsmākamabhimatatvāt "asmābhiḥ" ityāha |
children.translated_text: )—and by [necessary] pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), the absence of the reason when the <s>sādhya</s> is absent is the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>). But merely from observing the existence of the reason somewhere where the <s>sādhya</s> exists, it does not follow that such [existence obtains] everywhere—because there is no invariable rule of co-occurrence for things whose natures are not connected (<s>apratibaddha-svabhāva</s>). Likewise, even from observing the absence of the reason somewhere where what is claimed as the <s>sādhya</s> is absent, it does not [follow] that there is necessarily absence [of the reason] everywhere in the absence of that—because, for what does not depend upon that [<s>sādhya</s>], there is no invariable rule of cessation upon the cessation of that. Therefore, the existence and non-existence in the similar and dissimilar instances as stated are established only through the operation of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) that proves the necessary connection (<s>pratibandha</s>), and not otherwise—this is shown [to be the purpose of] the word 'ascertained,' for the removal of the dispute.

body.translated_text: Why, then, are the distinguished existence and non-existence—of the nature of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) and negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)—pertaining to the objects of observation and non-observation, not accepted [as distinct] in the similar and dissimilar instances? He says 'even when existing' (<s>satorapi</s>) and so forth. Even when there is sometimes observation of the existence of the reason in the similar instance and sometimes observation of non-existence in the dissimilar instance—as in [the case] 'He is dark-complexioned, because he is his son' and the like—there is doubt regarding the positive and negative concomitance. For indeed, positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) means the existence of the reason everywhere where the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) exists (

body.text: tadevaṃ vipratipattinirāsārthaṃ niścitagrahaṇam, asatyāṃ tu vipratipattau tanna kartavyameveti pratipādya ata eva nyāyāt jñātatvaṃ rūpāntaraṃ na bhavatīti darśayannāha- "yato 'pi"ityādi | "pṛthagataḥ" iti pakṣadharmatvādestrairūpyāt | kutaḥ? "tenaiva"trairūpyavacanenaiva tatsādhanapramāṇākṣepataḥ "avagatatvāt" pratipannatvāditi | kiṃvat? "upanayārthavat pakṣadharmatvāt" iti | yathā pakṣadharmatvavacanenaiva hetorupanayasyārtho 'vagatastasya dharmiṇi hetoḥ sadbhāvapradarśanātmakatvāt, pakṣadharmavacanasya ca tadrūpatvāt tataḥ pṛthagupanayo rūpāntaraṃ na bhavati; tathā trairūpyāt jñānaṃ, tadvacanenaivāvagatatvāditi |
body.translated_text: Thus, the word 'ascertained' is for the purpose of removing the dispute; but when there is no dispute, it need not be included. Having established this, he now shows that, for this very reason, 'being known' is not a separate form [of the mark]. He says 'because of which also' (<s>yato'pi</s>) and so forth. 'Separately' means from the triple-form (<s>trairūpya</s>)—being a property of the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa-dharmatva</s>) and [the other two]. From what [is this separate form excluded]? Because 'by that very' statement of triple-form, through the implication of the <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes that, it is 'understood' (<s>avagata</s>), i.e., comprehended. Like what? 'Like the purpose of the application (<s>upanaya</s>) [being understood] from [the statement of] being a property of the thesis-subject.' Just as, from the very statement of being a property of the thesis-subject, the purpose of the application (<s>upanaya</s>) of the reason is understood—because its nature is showing the existence of the reason in the thesis-subject—[so too] the property of the thesis-subject

body.text: atra paro 'niṣṭamāpādayannāha- "anvayavyatirekayorapi" ityādi | yadi trairūpyavacanenaiva sāmarthyājjñānaṃ labhyata iti tat tataḥ pṛthag na vaktavyam "hantaḥ" tarhi anvayāt pṛthag vyatireko na vaktavyaḥ vyatirekācca pṛthaganvayaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam? | ekasyānvayasya vyatirekasya vā prayogādubhayasya gateḥ | kṛtaṃ ca tayoḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ, tathā jñātatvasyāpi trairūpyād gamyamānasyāpi pṛthagvacanaṃ kartavyamiti |
body.translated_text: Here the opponent raises an unwanted consequence: 'Of positive and negative concomitance also' (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) and so forth. If knowledge is obtained by implication from the very statement of triple-form, and therefore need not be stated separately—'well then,' positive concomitance need not be stated separately from negative concomitance, and negative concomitance need not be stated separately from positive concomitance. For what reason? Because from the statement of one—either positive or negative concomitance—both are understood. And [yet] a separate statement of those two has been made; likewise, even though 'being known' is understood from the triple-form, a separate statement should be made.

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "na, hetoḥ" ityādi | nānvayavyatirekayorna pṛthaktvaṃ kintu bhinnarūpataiva | tathā hi- anvayo hetoḥ (

children.translated_text: [Hbṭ page 226]

children.text: ) sapakṣe bhāva ucyate, vyatirekaḥ punarabhāvo 'sapakṣe | na ca tau parasparamākṣipataḥ parasparamantarbhavato vidhipratiṣedharūpayorbhinnasvabhāvatvāt | na ca yo yato bhinnasvabhāvaḥ sa tatrāntarbhūto yukto | nanu ca yadyanvayavyatirekayorbhinnarūpatā kathaṃ tarhi trirūpaṃ liṅgamucyate? | nahi parasparabhinnāvātmānāvevāsya yujyete, svabhāvabhedalakṣaṇatvād vastubhedasya | naiṣa doṣaḥ, yato yathānvayavyatirekau vyavasthāpyete na vā nayo (pyete tathā tayo)ranantarbhāva ucyate nānyathā | kathaṃ cetau vyavasthāpyete? | vyāvṛttikṛtaṃ bhedamupādāya | tathā cānayorbhinnarūpataiva | vyāvṛttibhede 'pi ca paramārthato bhedo nāstītyekaṃ liṅgaṃ trirūpamityucyate iti |
children.translated_text: ) in the similar instance; negative concomitance, however, is the non-existence [of the reason] in the dissimilar instance. And those two do not imply each other, [nor] do they include each other—because being of the nature of affirmation (<s>vidhi</s>) and negation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>), they are of different inherent natures. And what is of a different inherent nature from something is not appropriately included within it. [Objection:] But if positive and negative concomitance are of different natures, how then is the mark called 'triple-formed'? For two [forms] that are mutually different are not appropriate as the [mark's own] natures—because the distinction of real entities is defined by the distinction of inherent nature. [Reply:] This is no fault, because [their] non-inclusion in each other is stated [only] insofar as positive and negative concomitance are established [as distinct]—and not otherwise. And how

body.translated_text: The proponent says: 'No, because of the reason' (<s>na, hetoḥ</s>) and so forth. [It is] not [the case] that positive and negative concomitance are not separate—rather, they are indeed of different natures. For indeed, positive concomitance is said to be the existence of the reason (

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi prāguktam ‘nānayorarthataḥ kaścid bhedaḥ, anyatra prayogabhedād'; iti? ata āha- "ekaṃ vākyam" ityādi | anvayamukhena vyatirekamukheṇa vā prayuktamekaṃ vākyamubhayamanvayaṃ vyatirekaṃ ca bhinnalakṣaṇameva gamayatītyucyate 'smabhirnaiko 'rthaḥ svabhāvo dvitīyasyocyate, parasparabhinnayorevaikavākyārtharūpatvāt |
body.translated_text: Then how is the earlier statement 'There is no real difference between these two, apart from the difference in application' [to be understood]? To this he says "one statement" and so on. It is said by us that a single statement, whether employed in the mode of <s>anvaya</s> (positive concomitance) or in the mode of <s>vyatireka</s> (negative concomitance), conveys both — <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> — which are indeed of distinct character; it is not that one nature is identical to the second, since the two, being mutually distinct, have the form of a single sentence-meaning.

body.text: atra para āha- "na tu tatraiva" ityādi | ayamabhiprāyaḥ- lakṣaṇavākyapratipāditāvanvayavyatirekāvāśritya parasparāntarbhāvaścodyate | sa ca vidyata eva | tathā hi- ‘tatraiva bhāvaḥ'; ityatra lakṣaṇavākye tadarthatayā tadabhāve 'bhāvo gamyate; ‘atadbhāve 'vaśyamabhāvaḥ'; iti cātra ‘tadbhāve bhāvaḥ'; | na hyasati pratibandha ekābhāve 'parasyābhāvaḥ | pratibandhaśca tādātmyatadutpattibhyāṃ tadbhāve bhāvarūpa eva | tataścaikenaiva sapakṣāsapakṣayorbhāvābhāvapratipādakena prativiśiṣṭena lakṣaṇavākyenobhayagaterdvitīyavacanaṃ na kartavyamiti | tathā caikavākyārthāntarbhāvād bhinnasvabhāvatāpyanayordurllabhā | tataśca yaduktam ‘anvayavyatirekayorapi tarhi na pṛthaktvamiti'; tat tadavasthameveti |
body.translated_text: Here the opponent says "but not in that very [statement]" and so on. The intent is this: the mutual inclusion [of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>] is objected to on the basis of <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> as conveyed by the definitional statement (<s>lakṣaṇavākya</s>). And such [inclusion] does indeed exist. For in the definitional statement 'presence in that very [<s>sapakṣa</s>],' the absence in the absence of that is understood as having that as its purpose; and in 'where that is absent, there is necessarily absence,' the presence where that is present [is understood]. For without a necessary connection, from the absence of one the absence of another does not follow. And the necessary connection, being through identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) and origination (<s>tadutpatti</s>), is of the very nature of presence where there is presence. Therefore, since a single definitional statement, distinguished by establishing presence and absence in <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue) and <s>asapakṣa</s> (heterologue) respectively, conveys both aspects, a second statement need not be made. And thus, due to inclusion within the meaning of a single statement, a distinct nature for the two is also difficult to maintain. Therefore what was said — 'then <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> too should not be separate' — that remains as it stands.

body.text: siddhāntavādyāha- "vacanametat" ‘tatraiva bhāvaḥ'; ityādirūpam "ubhayamākṣipati" pratipādayati | kutaḥ? | sāmarthyādubhayapratipādanaśaktatvāt | katham? iti cet, āha- "ekasyāpi vākyasya" kīdṛśasya? | "niyamakhyāpakasya" ‘sapakṣa eva bhāvo 'sapakṣe cābhāva eva'; iti sāvadhāraṇasya "dvitīyākṣepanāntarīyakatvāt" dvitīyapratipādananāntarīyakatvāt | "na ca tāvataikavākyapratipādanamātreṇobhayorekasvabhāvatā" bhinnasvabhāvānāmapyarthānāmekavākyena pratipādanāt | ekenaiva ca lakṣaṇavākyenobhayagatāvapi yat "pṛthagabhidhānaṃ" tat "prayoganiyamārtham" | sādharmyaprayoge vaidharma(rmya)vacanaṃ na kartavyam, vaidharmyaprayoge ca sādharmyavacanamiti na punarekābhidhānenānavagatasya rūpāntarasya pratipādanārtham | na ca tathā trairūpyavacanena jñānanibandhanena jñeyasattāvyavasthāyāḥ propalakṣaṇārthena ca śāstrapraṇayanenāśritajñānasyaiva trairūpyasya pratipādanāllabdhasya jñānasya punarvacane na kiñcit prayojanamastīti nāsya pṛthagvacanaṃ yuktamiti |
body.translated_text: The proponent says: "This statement" of the form 'presence in that very [<s>sapakṣa</s>]' and so forth "draws in both" — that is, conveys [both]. Why? Because of its capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) to convey both. How so? He says: "even a single statement" — of what kind? — "one that declares a restriction" (<s>niyamakhyāpaka</s>), that is, one containing a determination such as 'presence only in <s>sapakṣa</s> and absence only in <s>asapakṣa</s>,' "because it necessarily entails the drawing in of the second" — that is, because it necessarily entails the conveying of the second. "But the mere conveying by a single statement does not make both of one nature," since even things of distinct nature can be conveyed by a single statement. And though both aspects are covered by a single definitional statement, the "separate expression" of each is "for the purpose of regulating application" (<s>prayoganiyama</s>): in an inference by agreement (<s>sādharmyaprayoga</s>), the statement of disagreement need not be made, and in an inference by disagreement (<s>vaidharmyaprayoga</s>), the statement of agreement need not be made — but it is not for the purpose of conveying a second form not already understood from the single expression. Nor is it proper to make a separate statement for it, since through the statement of the triple characteristic (<s>trairūpya</s>) — which is grounded in cognition, serves to establish the status of the knowable, and has the purpose of indicating [to others] through the composition of the treatise — the triple characteristic as grounded in cognition has already been conveyed, and there is no purpose in restating what has already been cognized.

body.text: syānmatam- kevalāvapi tarhyekavākyārthānantarbhūtau parasparama'bhinnasvabhāvau bhaviṣyataḥ tata evaivakavākyārthāntarbhāvādityata āha- "na punaḥ kevalau" ekavākyārthānapekṣau tadantarbhāvamātreṇa sapakṣāsapakṣayoḥ bhāvābhāvau parasparamākṣipato 'ntarbhavataḥ bhinnarūpāṇāmapyarthānāmekavākyāntarbhāvadarśanāt | nanu ca niyamavantāvapi bhāvābhāvau kevalāveva, tayoḥ parasparākṣepe kevalayorapi tatprasaṅga ityata āha- "niyamavantau ca" sāvadhāraṇavākyapratipāditau "na kevalau" kintu sahitāveva | kutaḥ? | "niyamasya" sāvadhāraṇasya vākyasya "ubhayarūpatvāt" bhāvābhāvapratipādanātmakatvāt |
body.translated_text: One might think: even taken independently, not included within a single sentence-meaning, [<s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>] will be of mutually non-distinct nature, precisely because of their inclusion within a single sentence-meaning. To this he says: "Not, however, the two taken independently" — that is, without reference to the single sentence-meaning; by mere inclusion within it, presence and absence in <s>sapakṣa</s> and <s>asapakṣa</s> do not mutually draw in and include one another, since even things of distinct form are seen to be included within a single sentence. But are not presence and absence, even when possessing restriction, simply independent? And if there is mutual drawing-in of the two, the same would apply to independent ones too. To this he says: "And [when] possessing restriction" — that is, conveyed by a statement with determination — "they are not independent" but rather conjoined. Why? "Because the restriction" — that is, the statement with determination — "has the nature of both" — that is, because it has the nature of conveying both presence and absence.

body.text: tadevaṃ sāvadhāraṇena vākyena naiva kevalo 'nvayo vyatireko vābhidhīyate | tadantarbhāvāttu dvitīyagatiḥ kintu parasparāntarbhūtāveva sahitāvekena vākyenābhidhīyete iti pratipādyopasaṃharannāha- "tasmāt" tatraiva sapakṣa eva bhāva (

children.text: ) ityanena vākyena na sapakṣe bhāva evocyate | kiṃ tarhi? | asapakṣe 'bhāvo 'pi, tathā cetareṇāpyasapakṣe 'bhāva eveti vacanena nābhāva eva kevala ucyate kintu sapakṣe bhāvo 'pi, yena kevalavacanena bhāvo 'bhāvo vā tadātmakatayā dvitīyamākṣiped yato 'nayoḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ na syāt | tasmād yadānvayavyatirekau bhavābhāvāvabhipretau tadā tau bhinnarūpāveveti kathaṃ tayoḥ na pṛthaktvam? | atha niyamavatā vākyenābhihitau tadaikavākyādevobhayagateḥ pṛthagvacanaṃ na kartavyameva | tattu kṛtaṃ nāpratipannapratipattaye kintu prayoganiyamārthamityuktametaditi |
children.translated_text: it is not the case that only presence in <s>sapakṣa</s> is stated. What then? Absence in <s>asapakṣa</s> is also [conveyed]. And likewise, by the other [statement] 'absence only in <s>asapakṣa</s>,' not mere absence alone is stated, but also presence in <s>sapakṣa</s> — [this is] so that a mere independent statement of presence or absence would, by virtue of being identical with [the other], draw in the second, whereby there would be no separate statement of the two. Therefore, when <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s> are intended as presence and absence, the two are indeed of distinct form — so how can there be no separateness of the two? But if they are expressed by a statement possessing restriction, then precisely because both aspects are obtained from that single statement, a separate statement need not be made at all. But that [separate statement] is made not for the purpose of conveying what has not been understood, but for the purpose of regulating application — this has already been stated.

body.translated_text: Thus, by a statement with determination, neither <s>anvaya</s> alone nor <s>vyatireka</s> alone is expressed. But due to inclusion within it, the second aspect [follows]. Rather, the two, mutually included, are expressed together by a single statement. Concluding the topic to be established, he says: "Therefore," by that very statement 'presence only in <s>sapakṣa</s>'

body.text: syānmatam- yathānvayavyatirekau bhāvābhāvalakṣaṇau na parasparātmakau tataśca tayoḥ parasparato rūpāntaratvam, evaṃ paropalakṣaṇaśāstrapratipāditāt trailakṣaṇyād bhidyata eva jñānam, na tatrāntarbhatam, tato rūpāntaraṃ bhaviṣyatītyata āha- "naivam", yathānvayavyatirekau bhāvābhāvalakṣaṇau parasparamanantarbhūtau, na tathā jñānaṃ paropalakṣaṇaśāstrapratipādite trailakṣaṇye 'nantarbhūtam | kutaḥ? | "paropalakṣaṇāt"- pare upalakṣyante upalakṣaṇa(ṇaṃ) trairūpyaviṣayāṃ pratītiṃ kāryante yena śāstreṇa tato yat trailakṣaṇyaṃ pratīyate āgṛhītajñānaṃ tasmādavyatirekādāgṛhītajñāne trailakṣaṇye 'ntarbhāvāditi yāvat, "iti" tasmānna lakṣaṇāntaraṃ trairūpyāditi | tadayamatra samudāyārthaḥ- yadi jñātatvaṃ jñānaśabdapravṛttinimittaṃ uktena prakāreṇa jñānamevocyate tadā talliṃgasyānātmabhūtamiti na tallakṣaṇam | athāvi(pi) jñānāpekṣaḥ karmabhāvo jñātatvamucyate tadāpi jñeyasattāvyavasthāyā jñānasattānibandhanatvāt trairūpyavyavasthaiva tatsattāvyavasthāpakaṃ jñānamākṣipati | tatastadapekṣo 'pi karmabhāvo 'nuktasiddha iti na tadvacanaṃ pṛthakkartavyam | tathā paropalakṣaṇārthaśāstrapratipāditāgṛhītajñānāt trailakṣaṇyādavyatirekāditi |
body.translated_text: One might think: just as <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>, characterized as presence and absence, are not of each other's nature, and hence each is a distinct form from the other, so too cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) is indeed different from the triple characteristic (<s>trailakṣaṇya</s>) as conveyed by the treatise intended for indicating [to others] (<s>paropalakṣaṇa</s>), and is not included therein, and therefore will be a distinct form. To this he says: "Not so" — <s>jñāna</s> is not unincluded in the triple characteristic conveyed by the treatise intended for indicating to others, in the way that <s>anvaya</s> and <s>vyatireka</s>, characterized as presence and absence, are mutually unincluded. Why? "Because of [the treatise] for indicating to others" — the treatise by which others are indicated, i.e., caused to have cognition regarding the triple characteristic — from the triple characteristic understood through that, [cognition] is not different, since it is included in the triple characteristic that encompasses cognition. "Therefore" the triple characteristic is not a separate <s>lakṣaṇa</s> [i.e., there is no fourth characteristic beyond the three]. The overall meaning here is this: if 'being cognized' (<s>jñātatva</s>), the ground for the application of the word 'cognition,' is in the manner explained simply cognition itself being stated, then that is not intrinsic to the <s>liṅga</s> (logical mark) and hence is not its characteristic. But even if 'being cognized' is said to be the objective status dependent on cognition, still, since the establishment of the status of the knowable is grounded in the existence of cognition, the very establishment of the triple characteristic draws in the cognition that establishes its status. Therefore, even the objective status dependent on it is established without being stated, and a separate statement for it need not be made. And this is because there is no difference from the triple characteristic that encompasses cognition, as conveyed by the treatise composed for the purpose of indicating to others.

body.text: tadevamabādhitaviṣayatvādikaṃ rūpatrayaṃ nirākṛtya nigamayannāha- "tasmānna hetuḥ ṣaḍlakṣaṇaḥ |" kiṃ tarhi? | trailakṣaṇya eveti |
body.translated_text: Having thus refuted the triple form [of the reason] beginning with having an uncontradicted domain, he concludes: "Therefore the <s>hetu</s> (reason) does not have six characteristics." What then? It has the triple characteristic alone.

children.translated_text: This [work], which has destroyed all paths of specious reasoning,
a lamp of the doctrinal system of the lord of sages (<s>Munīśa</s>),
having spread [it forth], whatever merit has been earned thereby,
may it bring about the supreme purification of the world.

body.text: hetubinduṭīkā samāptā |
body.translated_text: The <s>Hetubinduṭīkā</s> is concluded.

children.text: mā yatata imā yā tadrūpā vala (?) tribhuvanasya hitāya śasvat |
children.translated_text: May [this work (?)] of that very form always [be] for the welfare of the three worlds.
The guide of the doctrine of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [...] of the bridge of mankind. || 2 ||

body.text: ........75 māgra(rga)sira vādi 7 ravau | maṃgalaṃ mahāśrīḥ ||
body.translated_text: [......] 75, <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> <s>vādi</s> 7, Sunday. Auspiciousness! Great glory!

body.text:
na gurorupadeśamagrahīt bubudhe vastu tato.............dhīḥ |
yatate sma na tasya vṛddhaye na parispanditumapyapārayat || [1 ||] ||
body.translated_text: He did not receive the teacher's instruction, yet understood reality through [...] intellect; he strove but not for its increase — he was unable even to stir. [|| 1 ||]

children.text: jīvātmakaṃ cāndramasaṃ ca tejaḥ kṛtāspadaṃ tasya tai .......t |
children.translated_text: And the vital (<s>jīvātmaka</s>) and lunar radiance, having taken its abode in that [...]

children.text: tadeva śaktā.....thā paratra citrā hi viśvaprakṛti.....nāḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: That very power [...] and elsewhere — for the nature of the universe is variegated [...] || 2 ||
O beloved of <s>Rohiṇī</s>! Abode of all arts!
O lord of the stars! O sovereign of the night! O repository of nectar!
Among the virtues of <s>kādambarī</s>-nectar [...]
one should remember the self as having surrendered the body, of the moon. || 3 ||

body.text: śrībrahmāṇagacche paṃ. abhayakumārasya hetubindutarkaḥ ||
body.translated_text: In the illustrious <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>gaccha</s> (lineage), [this is] the <s>Hetubindutarka</s> of <s>Paṇḍita Abhayakumāra</s>.
